HOMEOPATHIC - Carb-an., or animal charcoal, is made from charred ox hide, it contains Calc-p. in small quantity. The Carbon group all have putriddischargesandexhalations. All act on the skin, causing interrigo and excoriations and Carb-tcl. is said to cause fatty liver (Phos., Kreos., Chlf.). Carb-an. is often indicated in the last stage of cancer, pneumonia, bronchitis, tuberculosis. Breast cancer with burning, drawing pains through breast. Right chest is most affected. Uterine cancer, burning pains down thigh. Tendency to malignancy. Glands enlarge slowly and painfully, burning. Glandular enlargements with catarrhal states, flatulency and asphyxiation. Painful swelling, lancinating, cutting and burning (Con., Merc-i-f.). Glands are indurated, veins distended, skin blue. Glands are stony hard. Neglected buboes. Marked tendency to induration of glands and tissues. Indurations after inflammations. Ulceration and decomposition. Hemorrhages. Gangrene. Offensive secretions. Discharges are acrid and foul. Slow, hard, painful processes. Sensations of looseness, crawling as of bugs. Stitch remaining after pleurisy (Bry.). Venous stasis, blue skin. Local congestions without heat. Copper- colored eruptions. Constitutional syphilis. Gummae. Paralysis of muscles of feet and hands. Patients are susceptible to colds and easy sprains. Easily strained from lifting. Hookworm disease (Thymol.). Especially adapted to scrofulous and venous constitutions. Suited to weak, broken- down constitutions and to the infirmities of old age or those prematurely aged. After debilitating disease with feeble circulation and lowered vitality. Weakness of nursing women, they weep while eating, unable to walk even across the room. MIND - Alternations of mood and overexcitability, alternating with fretful sadness. Sadness in morning. Aversion to company. Desire to be alone, sad and reflective. Avoids conversation. Weeps during meals. Whining. Cheerfulness alternating with sadness. Homesickness, longing for the past. Homesickness in morning. Forsaken feeling in morning. Anger about former vexations, about past events. Easily frightened. Fear of the dark, worse on closing eyes. Anxiety at night with orgasm of blood. Fearofsuffocation on closing eyes. Frightful images before sleep. Starting on falling asleep. Stupefaction, with vertigo, has to close eyes, when rising after stool. Confusion better epistaxis. Confusion in morning, did not know whether he had been asleep or awake. Difficulty in expressing ideas when writing. Hastiness. Irritability in morning, with heavy and dull head.

Head - Rush of blood with confusion. Headache, As if skull had been split or blown to pieces, must press it with both hands, better eating. Brain feels loose, worse motion and coughing. Throbbing headache after menses. Sensation as if something lay above eyes so that she could not look up.

Eyes - Pains down through (right) eyeball. Sensation as if something lay above eyes, so that she could not look up. As if eyeball were loose in the socket. Objects seem to be far off. Dimness of vision when reading. better rubbing eyes. Senile cataract.

Ears - Parotid gland swollen. Otorrhea with swelling of mastoid. Sharp pain. Hearing confused, cannot tell direction of sound. Ringing in ears, when blowing the nose.

Nose - Hard, red, swollen, hot with itchin pimples and desquamation. Brown strip across the nose. Nose swollen, tip bluisl small tumor on it. Fluent coryza with los of smell with yawning and sneezing.

Face - Bluish cheeks and lips. Copper colored eruptions. Acne, large number of pimples.

Mouth - Salty or sour water runs from th mouth. Knotty indurations in the tongue Bites cheeks while eating. Teeth loose worse chewing and least cold. Toothach better eating salty things.

Throat - Raw feeling like heartburn, better eating. Vertigo - Vertigo after shaving, better reeling. Vertigo followed by nosebleed. COMMENTS - Carb-an. is animal charcoal (Carb-v. is plant ash) and has similar affects as Bufo. Swollen glands with suppuration. Glands become indurated, have bluish color. Often used in the last stages of cancer with decomposition of tissue and sloughing off of tissue. Swollen inguinal glands that suppurate. Inflamed axillary glands. Buboes. Affections from loss of animal fluids, especially nursing women. Weakness of nursing women, can hardly walk across the room. “Gone” feeling from loss of fluids. Too weak to eat. Weeps when eating. Aversion to dark. Aversion to cold (Carb- v. to heat). Sensations of coldness, particularly in chest, about stomach. Coldness of the stomach, better pressure from hand. Nausea at night. Hunger in early morning. Emptiness, not better by eating (Carb-v. bettereating). Constipation where patient thinks bowels will be moved but only wind passes. Discharges are ichorous, but the discharge from hemorrhoids is odorless. Secretions stain yellow, particularly sweat and leucorrhea. Ichorous otorrhea and swelling of the periosteum over the mastoid bone. Hearing is confused, cannot tell the direction from which sounds come. Carb-an. 3x trituration has been used for ear polyps. Hoarse, suffocating cough producing a shaking of the brain as if it were loose. Expectoration is greenish, purulent offensive (Carb-v. yellow, more fetid). Tip of nose red or blue. Disagreeable smoothness of the teeth. Smothering feeling on closing eyes. Feeling of looseness of eyes in sockets, on motion or coughing. Far- sighted (Carb-v. is near-sighted). Objects seem farther apart and brighter. Neuralgia of the bone. Injured coccyx, with a dragging, bruised pain, burning when touched. Gnawing pains in tibia (during the night), such as usually followed cold feet. Lumbago when walking, standing and lying, feels as if the back were broken. A. W. K. Choudhury reports a case of cough of two years' duration in an unhealthy boy of twelve, cured by Carb-an. The symptoms were: “Cough evening and morning or after lying down, especially at night, thick or frothy whitish or yellowish sputa, sweetish when thick, worse lying on right side, worse from exposure to air to which he is very sensitive. Great tendency to catch cold.” RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Ars., Camph., Nux-v. Vinegar. Antidote to: Effects of Quinine. Compare: (1) Thymol., Badiaga, Sep., Sulph., Plb. iod. (2) Calc-p. - nearest analog, Carb-an. contains Calc-p. (3) in indurations, suppurations etc., Bad., Brom. (4) loss of fluids. Chin. (5 ) Graph., nostrils adhere to sepmm. (6) Phos., gone feeling, loss of fluids induration of cervix, pressure on back, groins and thighs during menses. (6) Cocc. has similar weakness and prostration as Carb-an. (7) Puls., Sil. (8) in vertigo with nosebleed. Sulph. (9) aversion to darkness, Am-m., Bar-c. Calc., Stroph., Stram. (10) hunger in early morning, Ant-c„ Asar., Calc.. Sabad. (11) swelling behind ear, Caps., Aur. (12) burning pains, Caps. (13) weakness of nursing women, Olnd. Complementary: Calc-p. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Stomach - All food distresses the stomach. Repugnance to fat food. Eating tires patient. Weak, empty feeling in stomach. Burning and griping. Weak digestion, flatulence. Heartburn. Retching, vomiting, hiccough with stomach cancer. Sensation of coldness around the stomach better rubbing and pressure. Nausea from smoking, whichcauses aversion to tobacco. Nausea, worse at night, of pregnancy. Faint gone feeling in stomach not better by eating in nursing women. Ptomaine poisoning.

Abdomen - Great distention after a operation. As of a hard body in groin (left) worse sitting, better pressure and passing flatus. Feeling of coldness rising into the throat. Induration of pancreas. Neglected bubo.

Rectum - Anus sore. Moisture, oozing froi anus and on perineum.

Male - Syphilis. Bubo.

Female - Menses too early, frequent, long lasting, dark, clotted, putrid, followed by great exhaustion. So weak can hardly speak (Cocc.). Flow only in the morning (Bor., Sep.). Leucorrhea, watery, burning, biting. Worse walking or standing, stains linen yellow. Nausea of pregnancy, worse at night. Offensive lochia (Kreos., Rhus-t., Sec.), thin, long lasting, with numb limbs. Right ovary seems a heavy ball. Burning in vagina and labia. Indurated os with burning. Uterine hemorrhage with disorders of glands. Cancer of uterus, burning pain down thighs, pelvic bones pain on sitting.

Heart - Palpitations when hearing singing in church or in public places. Coldness in precordial region with goose bumps.

Back - Coccyx feels bruised, burns when touched, worse sitting or lying. Coldness and aching in lumbar region with cough. Breasts - Weakness of nursing women. Darting in breast, painful indurations in breast, especially right, while nursing, arresting breathing. Hard painful nodes in breast. Last stages of breast cancer. Causations - Ill effects of eating spoiled fish or decayed vegetables. They are over affected by small vital losses. Sprains. Constitutions - Constitutional syphilis. Suited to old persons, greatly debilitated, especially when there is venous plethora and blueness of skin. Persons whose vitality becomes low on account of some serious or deep seated diseased condition or loss of fluids.

Limbs - Axillary glands, swollen, indurated. Night sweat fetid and profuse. Wrist pain. Hands numb with chest disorders. Joints weak, easy dislocation. Ankles turn easily. Pain in hip joints at night. Pain in coccyx, burns when touched. Straining and over-lifting produces a great debility Easy discoloration. Lungs - Nervous dyspnea. Suffocation or closing eyes. Pleurisy, typhoid character with remaining stitch. Ulceration of lung: with feeling of coldness in lungs. Cougl with discharge of greenish pus. Sputum dark, brown tough, syrup-like.

Sleep - Full of vivid fancies. Talks, groans, sheds tears in sleep. Talking and weeping in sleep.

Skin - Unsightly scars from eruption Spongy ulcers, copper-colored erut tion. Acne rosacea. Chilblains, worse i evening in bed and from cold. Warts c hands and face of elderly people, wil bluish color of limbs. Burning, rawne: and fissures, moisture. Bubo. Carbo animalis

Modalities - Better in warm room. Bette from laying hand on affected part. Worsi from slight causes. Worse losses of vita fluids. Worse after or during menses Worse from sprains. Worse lifting. Wors, touch. Worse taking cold. Worse dry, coli air. Worse after shaving. Worse while eat ing. Cough is worse lying on right side Throbbing headache worse in open ait Weakness worse during menses.

Temperature - Hot flushes. Sweat, foul, exhausting, at night, staining yellow.

name: Carbo Vegetabilis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from belchings. Better elevating feet. Better cool air. Betterfrom fanning. Worse from high living, rich food. Worse decayed food. Worse from poultry, fat food, butter, coffee, milk, Worse wine. Worse icy drinks. Worse from warmth, warm, damp weather, humid, cooling off. Worse walking in open air. Worse cold night air, frosty, wind on head. Worse extremes of temperature. Worse from depletions. Worse exhausting diseases. Worse dissipation. Worse suppressions. Worse over lifting. Worse pressure of clothes. Worse old age. Worse reading aloud, singing..

full:
ARMACY - carb-v. Carbo vegetabilis. 'egetable charcoal. Carbo ligni. Contains npure carbon. Trituration. Historical dose: nturation and all potencies. .INICAL - Acidity, Acne. Air hunger. anemia. Angina Pectoris. Aortitis. Apho- iia. Asphyxiation. Asthenopia. Asthma, lelching. Body, cold. Breast, erysipelas. Hood, loss. Breathing, labored. Bronchitis. Sums. Carbuncle. Catarrh. Chilblains. Chilis. Cholera. Coldness. Colds. Collapse. Coma. Constipation. Cough. Deafness. Debility. 'dehydration. Diarrhea. Digestion, weak. Distention. Dysentery. Dyspepsia. Em- rhysema. Erysipelas. Fainting. Feet, cold. Flatulence. Gangrene. Hair, loss. Headache. Heart, diseases. Heartburn. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Hypothermia. Influenza. Intermittents. Intertrigo. Irritation. Laryn- gitis. Lungs, congested. Measles. Mumps. Nosebleeds. Esophagitis. Orchitis. Otorrhea. Pneumonia. Pregnancy, disorders. Purpura. Scabies. Scurvy. Shiverings. Shock. Sleep, disorders. Stomach, disordered. Stomatitis. Trachea, dryness.Tympanites.Typhus. Ulcers. Vitality, low. Yellow fever. Weakness. 1OMEOPATHIC - Carb-v„ or vegetable charcoal, is itself a product of imperfect oxidation and disintegration, which are the keynotes of this remedy. It contains small quantity of Kali-carb., potassium carbonate. Provings with the crude Carb-v. and the potentized substances showed that the latter were much more powerful in their effect on the organism. These brought out the fact that there is an exact correspondence between the effect of crude charcoal and potentized Carb-v. Both are anti-septic and deodorant. The deodorant and disinfectant properties of charcoal in bulk had already been discovered when Hahnemann was at work on the Materia Medica. Its a deodorant, disinfectant and anti-septic properties are more enhanced in potencies. The signs and symptoms of decay and putrefaction are the leading indication for its medicinal use. Carb-v. antidotes the effects of putrid meats or fish, rancid fats, salt or salt meats, and also the pathogenic actions of Chin., Lach, and Merc. Decomposition of food in the stomach, putrid diseases and ulcerations, symptoms of imperfect oxygenation of the blood. Carb-v. acts upon the venous circulation and capillaries. Hemorrhage, blood dark, oozing from shock after surgical operations, persistent for hours or days. Hemorrhage from any mucus surface. The blood seems to stagnate, causing blueness, coldness and ecchymoses. Body becomes blue, icy-cold. Vitality becomes low from loss of vital fluids. Bacteria find a rich soil in the nearly lifeless blood stream and sepsis and typhoid states ensue. Putrid (septic) condition of all its affections, coupled with a burning sensation. Very debilitated. Almost lifeless, but the head is hot, coldness, breath cool, pulse imperceptible, oppressed and quickened respiration. Must have air, must be fanned hard, must have all the windowsopen. Cold, but wants air to be fanned or thirst for cold water. Faints easily, is worn out. Tremulous. Always weak, sick and exhausted, but those states may occur suddenly. State of collapse in cholera, typhoid or other grave diseases. When the patient is almost lifeless, cold body, breath cold, pulse imperceptible, respiration quickened. Lack of reaction after some violent attack, violent shock, violent suffering. Never well since. Patient seems to be too weak to hold out. Persons who have neverfully recovered from the effects of some previous illness. Weakness from grave or serious diseases, from effects of drug and disease, or from obstinate complications. Septic conditions. Lymphatic glands, are swollen, indurated or suppurating. Gangrene, humid, senile. Thick, acrid discharges. Ulcerations, aphthous. Blueness and decomposition. Flatulence, fetor. Sensation of fullness. Sense of weight, as in the head (occiput), eyes and eyelids, before the ears in the stomach and elsewhere in the body. General bruised soreness, old catarrhs. Bedwetting, which is worse in morning after the first sleep. Burning itching on skin. Frozen limbs. Chilblains, excoriations between toes. Numbness of parts lain on. Burning, sense of weight or heavy aching in bones, ulcers etc. Tinea capitis or scald-head. Scalp very sensitive, feels as if bruised. Whooping cough with pain at base of brain. Excessive gagging cough in the morning, compelling him to vomit everything, immediately after breakfast (Dros.). MIND - Confusion, which makes thinking difficult. Confusion better mental exertion. Torpor and indolence. Slow thinking, worse in morning on waking. Sudden loss of memory. Indifference to everything he hears or sees. Indifference, hears everything without pleasure or pain. Indifference to music which he loves. Sluggish, slow, lazy. Peevish, irritable and inclined to anger. Anxiety in evening, could scarcely remain lying still. Anxiety in morning on waking. Anxiety on closing eyes. Restlessness in company. Indolent. Irritable. Dejected. Child wishes to vent itself in rage, strikes, kicks, bites, in worm affections. Oversensitive to noise. Timidity about appearing in public. Aversion to presence of strangers. Fear of people. Easily frightened or startled. Aversion to darkness. Fear of ghosts. Fear of accidents. Sees frightful images in the dark.

Head - Cold sweat on forehead. Head hot with cold limbs. Takes cold in head easily. Dull, compressive, heavy. Headaches, worse occiput, worse overheating, lying or pressure of hat,over-indulgence. Pimples on forehead and face. Hair, sore, falls off easily in handfuls, after severe illness, after childbirth. Scalp itches when warm in bed. Hat pressed upon head like a heavy weight.

Eyes - As of heavy weight on eyes. Hemorrhages from eyes with congestion to head. Vision of floating black spots. Burning in eyes. Muscles of eyes painful when looking up. Pupils do not react to light. Asthenopia.

Ears - Deafness or otorrhea, following exanthemata. Ears dry. Something heavy seems to lie before the ears. Deficient or badly smelling yellow wax. Mumps with metastases.

Nose - Nosebleed in daily attacks with pale face. Bleeding after straining, with pale face. Tip of nose red and scabby, itching around nostrils. Eruption in corner of nose. Varicose veins on nose. Descending colds. Nose cold, hay asthma. Coryza with cough, especially in moist, warm weather. Sneezing from irritation in larynx, worse blowing nose. Ineffectual effort to sneeze.

Face - Face blue, cold with cold sweat. Puffy, cyanotic, pale, hippocratic, pinched (Cupr., Op.). Mottled cheeks and red nose. Twitching upper lip. Brown or black looking, cracked lips. F emale - Too early and too copious menses, pale blood. During menstruation, burning in hands and soles. Menorrhagia, burning across sacrum, passive flow. Leucorrhea, thick, greenish, milky, causing itching and burning, worse before menses. Feels best with a free leucorrhea. Sore, hot, itching, swollen, vulva. Vulva swollen, aphthae. Varicose veins on pudendum and yulva with burning, bluish ulcers. Vaginal fistula, burning pains. Food - Aversion to fat things, meat and milk, which causes flatulence. Aversion to the most digestible and the best kind of food. Desire for salty, sour things or sweet things, coffee. Worse from brandy.

Mouth - Breath cold. Bad smell from mouth. Bitter, sour, taste. Increased saliva. Tongue, cold, black, swollen, covered with white, yellow-brown mucus. Aphthae, bluish, black ulcers with burning. Loose teeth. Tooth pain while eating hot or cold things. Teeth very sensitive when chewing. Scorbutic gums. Blood oozes from gums when cleaning teeth. Gums retracted and bleed easily, painful while chewing. Gums black. Pyorrhea.

Throat - Sensation as if closed. Aphthous, sore. Hawking of bloody, black mucus. Painful on swallowing food. Vertigo - Vertigo with nausea and tinnitus. COMMENTS - Suited to conditions where there is lack of reaction (Op.) to low states of the vital powers, where the venous system is engorged. Lack of reaction in pupils (Op.). For near death states. “The corpse reviver.” In India, they say it pulls back souls from the jaws of death. Comas (Op., Chin.). Diabetic comas. Usually given for the last stage of processes. Last stage of pneumonia, cyanotic, weak, debilitated, faint. Shock from heart failure (Arn. first). Never well since a traumatic accident where they feel weak and sluggish. Hypo-oxygenation, with shortness of breath, varicose veins, hemorrhoids, gas and bloating. Weakness after hemorrhage. Listless and indifferent. Feebleness. Collapse (Camph.), with short, shallow breathing. Collapse with cold knees. The patient sinks and breaks out in a cold sweat, faints and collapses from weakness and lack of air (Aeon., Ign., or Gels, if from emotional trauma). Debility of greater intensity than Carbo an. in children or old people after exhausting diseases. Great debility as soon as he makes the least effort. Debility following childbirth, causing falling out of hair. Cannot be aroused, cannot think, so weak they cannot lift their head off the pillow (Stann. is weak in the chest, can barely speak). Frequent hemorrhages. Nosebleeds or hemorrhage from throat in dysentery. Hemorrhage from the bowels, lungs. Dyspnea, from chronic aortitis. Congestive symptoms like those of poisoning by carbonic acid. Pulse thready, face pale, covered with cold sweat, desire to be fanned, anxiety without restlessness. Fever, intermittent, hectic, typhoid, yellow fever and cholera. In intermittents of long standing where quinine has been abused. Thirst only during chill. Feet ice-cold up to knees. Heat in burning flushes. Sweat sour or offensive. Weak, befogged mind. Characteristic coldness. Worse from warmth. Great desire for air, must be fanned. Cold breath (cholera), cold knees, cold, but wants to be fanned. Dull headache in occiput with confusion of mind, proceeding from occiput to forehead, dull, heavy aching over eyes in warm room, buzzing in ears, very sensitive to pressure of hat. Hippocratic countenance. Vertigo from stomach with fainting, especially at meals. Burning pains (Carb-an.), especially in the limbs, with varicose veins. Numbness of limbs. Lividity, mottled skin. Round ulcers. Indolent gangrene. Varicose veins of arms, legs, vulva. Catarrh from warm, moist atmosphere. Cough is worse on entering cold air from a warm room. Hoarseness from damp air, worse morning or evening. Cough caused by a sensation as if sulphur fumes were in larynx. Menorrhagia and metrorrhagia with burning pains across sacrum and spine. Corrosive menstrual discharge, strong pungent odor. Premature and profuse menses. Headache during menses. Preceded and followed by leucorrhea. Greenish yellow leucorrhea, worse in morning. Leucorrhea excoriates. Perineum moist, raw, oozing. Itching, burning soreness and smarting at vulva and anus. Hemorrhoids. Excessive accumulation of gas in stomach and intestines. “Stomach feels full and tense from flatulence. Great pain in stomach on account of flatulence, worse especially on lying down.” Weak digestion with much flatulence, better by eructation. Flatulence accompanies many other complaints, including asthma and heart disorders. Heaviness in the stomach, full feeling and burning. Aversion to fat, meat, and milk, which causes flatulence. Desire for coffee (which does not relieve), for acids, for sweet and salt things. Guernsey considered Carb-v. especially suited to cachectic individuals whose vital powers has become weakened. In cases where disease seems to have been engrafted on the system by reason of the depressing influence of some prior derangement. A. H. Birdsall recorded a typical case of Carb-v. intermittent. “A man, 36, had fever eight months, partially suppressed by Arsenic and Quinine. Type, tertian. Headache for one or two hours before chill. “Chill always from 9 to 10 a.m., beginning in feet and hands, spreading over body, nails very blue. Thirst with chill. Cold stage lasts two to three hours, followed immediately by hot stage, much heat in head and face, which is flushed red, thirstlessness. Sweating stage short, sweat sour. “Apyrexia: Sweats easily, especially from least warmth, awakens in morning always with slight sour-smelling sweat. Weak, dispirited, flatulent. A single dose of Carb-v. cured. There were only three more attacks, each of diminished intensity.” A carbon ointment made by carbonizing a wine cork by plunging it into a clear fire and then, in its still glowing state, into Vaseline and mixing thoroughly is regarded as a sovereign remedy in anal irritation and hemorrhoid troubles. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Ars., Ambra, Camph., Coff., Lach., Nit-s-d., Ferr. (Teste). It antidotes: Effects of putrid meats of fish, rancid fats, salt or salt meats. Chin., Lach., Merc. Compare: (1) Raph. in flatulence. Caust., Lach., Eup-per., Phos. and Rumex in hoarseness, Rumex is worse 4 a.m. and 11 p.m. Caust. worse in morning from dry cold. Carb-v. worse evening from damp evening air. (2) Camph., China in hemorrhages intermittents, hectic disorders of alcoholics, Ip. in hemorrhages and intermittents, Meny. in intermittents with coldness of legs. (3) Op., Sulph. and Psor. in deficient reaction. (4) Sul- ac. in dyspepsia of alcoholics. Carb-v. has more putridity, Sul-ac. more sourness. (5) Phos. in easily bleeding ulcers, Puls., bad effect from fat food and pastry, Sulph. in acrid-smelling menses, erysipelas of breasts, Ars. and Bellis in effects of ice-cream and ice-water in hot weather. (6) Nux-v. in dyspepsia, easily angered, effects of debauchery. Nux- v. is thin, spare, yellow, wiry, Carb-v sluggish, stout, lazy. (7) Sec. in hemorrhages, cold breath, coldness worse by warmth. Calc., Carb-an. and Stram. in aversion to darkness. (8) Lach, in weak digestion. Lach, craves milk, Carb-v. has aversion to it. Intolerance of clothing around waist intermittent fever, flashes of burning heat without thirst. (9) Sep. in bearing-down in rectum and vagina. Carb-v. has strong odor of menses which Sep. has not. (10) Rhus-t. in strains in typhus, Colch. in cholera, coldbreath, prostration. Cupr. (11) Carboneum - Spasms commencing in tongue, down trachea and limbs. Tingling sensation. (12) Lyc., Ars., Chin., Carb-v. contains potash. Complementary: Chin., Dros., Kali-c. - stitches in heart. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Stomach - Burning in stomach, extending to back along spine, with coldness. Contractive pains extending to chest with distention of abdomen. Epigastric region is very sensitive. Faint empty feeling in stomach, not relieved by eating. Loathes even the thought of food. Crampy pains forcing patient to bend double. Digestion slow, food putrefies before it digests. The simplest food distresses. Distress comes on a half-hour after eating. Rancid, sour orputridbelchings. Belchings after eating and drinking, temporary relief from belch ing. Heartburn. Water brash, asthmatic breathing from flatulence. Heaviness, fullness and sleepiness, tense from flatulence, with pain, worse lying down. Stomach ulcers, cancer. Vomiting of blood. Nausea in the morning. Stomach pain of nursing women.

Abdomen - Greatly distended, especially upper part, worse lying down, better passing wind. Flatulent colic, forcing the patient to bend double. Obstructed flatulence, giving rise to complaints. Pain as from lifting a weight. Abdomen feels as if hanging down, walks bent. Cannot bear tight clothing around waist and abdomen. Epigastric region very tender. Ailments from intestinal fistulae. Abdominal sufferings, worse from the smallest portion of food.

Rectum - Hot, moist offensive flatus. Itching, gnawing and burning in rectum and anus. Acrid, corrosive moisture from rectum. A musty, glutinous moisture exudes. Excoriation of anus. Soreness, itching, moisture of perineum, especially at night. Discharge of blood from rectum. Burning varicose veins (Mur-ac.). Bluish, white, burning hemorrhoids, pain after stools. Ineffectual urging, even soft stool passed with difficulty. Frequent, involuntary, putrid, cadaverous smelling stools, followed by burning. Feces escape with flatus. Painful diarrhea of old people.

Male - Discharge of prostatic fluid, while straining at stool. Itching and moisture at thigh near scrotum. Seminal discharge too soon during sex, followed by roaring in head. Swelling of testes from metastasis of mumps.

Chest - Heavy sore or weak chest, on awakening. Burning in chest with hemoptysis. Brown yellow spots on chest. Sore ribs. Constitutions - Suited to atonic conditions where there is lack of reaction. The typical Carb-v, patient is fat, sluggish, lazy and has a tendency to chronicity of complaints. Complaints of old people. Persons who have never fully recovered from the effects of some previous illness. School girls and boys are sluggish, slow to learn, suffer from night terrors, will not sleep alone or go to bed in the dark.

Heart - Continuous anxious palpitation, worse eating, sitting. Thread-like, weak and small, intermittent pulse. Burning around the heart. Pulsation throughout the body.

Back - Severe pain in small of back, with a sensation of a plug, unable to sit down, had to put a pillow under it when lying. Burning behind shoulder. Breasts - Lumps in breasts with indurations of axillary glands. Breasts, hard, swollen with impending abscess. Prostration after nursing. Causations - Carbon monoxide poisoning. Blood loss. Shock. Surgery. Effects of alcohol, meat, fish, especially if tainted, ice-water, vegetables, salt or salt meats. Disorders from high living and especially butter- eating.

Limbs - Heavy, stiff, feel paralyzed. Limbs go to sleep. Want of muscular energy, joints weak. Burning pain in bones and limbs. Numbness when lying on limbs. Pain in shins. Cold from knees down. Cramp in soles. Feet numb and sweaty. Foul foot sweat, worse walking. Toes red, swollen. Senile gangrene of fingers and toes with fiery burning vesicles, oozing bloody water. Paralytic weakness of the wrists and of the fingers, when seizing anything. Arms weary when writing.

Sleep - Unrefreshing. Awakes often from cold limbs especially cold knees. Comatose sleep with rattling in throat. Frequent yawning and stretching which seems to agree. Horror during sleep.

Skin - Blue, cold and bruised. Purpura. Wounds heal and break out again. Marbled with venous over- distention. Moist skin, hot perspiration. Fine moist rash with burning. Burning in various places. Itching, worse on evening, when warm in bed. Bedsores, bleed easily. Foul ulcers, indolent, burning and bleeding. Varicose ulcers, bleeding easily, pus smells like asafetida. Ulcers heal and break out again. Ichorous, offensive discharge. Tendency to gangrene of the margins. Senile gangrene beginning in the toes. Carbuncles (Ars., Anthr.). Varicose veins during pregnancy. Falling out of hair from a general weakened condition.

Modalities - Better from belchings. Better elevating feet. Better cool air. Betterfrom fanning. Worse from high living, rich food. Worse decayed food. Worse from poultry, fat food, butter, coffee, milk, Worse wine. Worse icy drinks. Worse from warmth, warm, damp weather, humid, cooling off. Worse walking in open air. Worse cold night air, frosty, wind on head. Worse extremes of temperature. Worse from depletions. Worse exhausting diseases. Worse dissipation. Worse suppressions. Worse over lifting. Worse pressure of clothes. Worse old age. Worse reading aloud, singing.

Liver - Pain in liver. Jaundice from over eating or eating too rich food. Lungs -Asphyxiation. Breathing, laborious, quick and short, worse walking. Wants to take a deep breath. Breath cold, must be fanned. Cheyne-Stokes breathing in organic heart disease. Destructive lung diseases. Cough with itching in larynx, spasmodic with gagging and vomiting of mucus. Cough with burning in chest. worse in evening, in open air, after eating and talking. Spasmodic cough, bluish face, offensive expectoration. Occasional Carbo vegetabilis spells of long coughing attacks. Wheezing and rattling of mucus in chest. Expectoration with retching. Expectoration is very thick, sticky, yellow and profuse. Hemorrhage from lungs. Neglected pneumonia. Whooping cough, especially in the beginning, with bluish face, and its complications. Asthma in aged with blue skin. Hoarseness, worse evenings, talking, evening oppression of breathing, sore and raw chest. Roughness in larynx with deep rough voice.

Kidneys - Albumin, protein in the urine. Nephritis, septic or from alcohol. Urine, copious, clear yellow or thick and whitish. Diabetes. Bedwetting at night. Urine, suppressed in cholera and retained from standing on the cold pavements.

Temperature - Icy coldness, unilateral of tongue, knees, legs, foot, at night. Coldness with thirst. Chill begins in forearm. Cold worse coughing. Alternate chill and heat. Warm head and cold limbs. Internal burning heat, at heart, chest with cold icy skin and cold sweat. Burning in various places. Yellow fever. Hectic fever, ex- hausting sweats. Sweats easily, on eating. Sweat sour on face.

full:
PHARMACY - carb-ac. Carbolicum acidum. Carbolic acid. Phenolum. Phenol. Monoxy benzine. Phenic acid. Phenyl alcohol. Solution in rectified spirit. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Allergic, reactions. Anaphylactic, shock. Backache. Bee stings. Belchings.Burns. Carbuncles. Cholera. Colds. Constipation. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Dyspepsia. Eczema. Erysipelas. Flatulence. Gangrene. Heartburn. Hydrocephalus. Influenza. Intermittent, fever. Irritation. Leprosy. Leucorrhea. Meningitis. Neuralgias. Pneumonia. Psoriasis. Pityriasis, versicolor. Prostration . Scarlatina. Smallpox. Smell, disordered. Stomach, disorders. Toothaches. Ulcers. Uremia. Uterus, displacements. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Carb-ac., like the Carbons, is a powerful anti-septic and its use as such in surgery has led, incidentally, to the poisoning of both patients and surgeons. These experienceshave provided a number of the symptoms indicating its medicinal use. Carb-ac. is a languid, painless, foul and destructive remedy. Acts primarily on the central nervous system. It affects the mucus membranes, heart, blood and respiration. Stomach symptoms are also important. Marked prostration, even paralytic with loss of sensation and motion. Collapse. Stupor. Paralysis of sensation and motion. Feeble pulse and depressed breathing. Death due to paralysis of respiratory centers. Malignant and septic conditions. Physical exertion brings on abscess somewhere. Discharges are foul, burning. Putrid discharges (Bapt.). Bloody discharges. Scarlet fever with marked tendency to destruction of tissue internally and fetid odor. Terrible pains coming and going suddenly. Pricking, burning sensation. Trembling with an uncertain, staggering walk. Arthritis. Mental and bodily languor, disinclination to study with headache like a band. Very marked acuteness of smell. Increased olfactory sensibility. Spasmodic coughs. Allergic reactions to bee stings (Apis). In cholera when Verat. is indicated but fails. MIND - Mental and bodily languor. Disinclination to do any mental or physical work. Unfit for study, as reading aggravates all symptoms. Periods of mental abstraction. Mental exertion aggravates. Unconsciousness. Absent minded, starts when spoken to. Difficulty of remembering passed events. Forgetful, can't remember anything, becomes easily confused. Starts to do something and forgets it. Entire disinclination to study, what he had accomplished seemed very trifling. Very irritable. Fear of impending disease at night in bed. Sense of bewilderment. Mental and physical exhilaration. Constantly agitated, moaning continuously and occasionally uttering a piercing cry. recognizes no one, acute hydrocephalus.

Head - Orbital neuralgia over right eye. Headache, better from green tea, while smoking. Headaches appearing at the time of menses. Tight feeling as if compressed by a rubber band (Gels.). As of a hot ball in forehead. Tender scalp.

Eyes - Severe orbital neuralgia over right eye. Contraction alternating with dilatation of pupils in hydrocephalus. Neuralgic twitching in eyeballs. Photophobia during headache.

Nose - Smell very acute. Putrid discharge. Ozaena with fetor and ulceration. Influenza and resulting debility.

Face - Dusky face. Pale about nose and mouth. Face pale, pinched, with cold sweat. Face cyanotic. Lips covered with a white membrane. Swelling of face and tongue from bee stings. Twitching in cheeks and temples. Lupus.

Mouth - Intensely foul breath with constipation. Burning in mouth to stomach. Lips dry, cracked, painful or black.

Throat - Glazed. Fauces red and covered with exudation. Uvula whitened and shriveled. Ulcerated patches on inside of lips and cheeks. Burning in mouth to stomach. Putrid discharge. Almost impossible to swallow. Diphtheria, fetid breath, regurgitation on swallowing liquids, but little pain (Bapt.). Face dusky red, white about mouth and nose. Rapid sinking of vital forces. Vertigo - Vertigo, felt as if staggering, like a drunken man. Giddiness, not better closing eyes. Vertigo on going up and down stairs, better walking fast in open air, worse sitting down. Vertigo with fear of falling, trembling. COMMENTS - Anaphylactic shock from bee stings (Apis, Hist.). The skin is inflamed, and other symptoms appear with burning, tingling, itching and numbness. Pains come suddenly. Burning, pricking, sticking pains. Numbness and twitching. Profound prostration and fatigue, convulsions, collapse, cold, clammy sweat. Constant yawning. Palpitations of the heart at night. Putrid discharges. The urine is very dark, black or black olivegreen, grass or olive-green. Great flatulent distention of the abdomen with belching of wind. Desire for stimulants. Vomiting in alcoholic, in pregnant women, with violent frontal headache. Many poisoning cases show pneumonia. single or double, affecting the bases principally. Gangrene has been caused by the application of 2 to 5 percent solutions, prescribed by Dr. Streintz. Fahnestock observed a case of poisoning from inhaling the fumes. The patient, a woman, feeling ill, ran across the street to a neighbor's. Before reaching the house she fell prostrate, pale, gasping for breath. When taken in, she had to be propped up in order to breathe, trembled all over, wanted her hands held, “pricking like needles,” all over body, unable to raise right arm. Cold hands and feet. Wanted a drink of water every few minutes, nausea but no vomiting, pain in lumbar region. Symptoms lasted four hours. Allen noted that it relieved cases of cancer of the stomach, and epithelioma of the cheek and nose with hemorrhages. Deschere found Carb-ac. 30c of great service in uterine displacements with or without discharges but these, if present, are always offensive. The symptoms first relieved are the agonizing backache across the loins with a dragging sensation down the buttocks into the thighs. Cooper regarded it as specific in influenza in the 3x for the attack and 30c for resulting debility. Dr. Proctor recorded a brilliant cure of a double basal pneumonia with drop doses of the B. P. solution after failure of more commonly used remedies. Nervous dyspepsia of intensely painful character has frequently been cured by it. R. K. Ghosh found it admirable in cases of cholera where V erat. seems indicated and fails. There is intolerance of warm room, but also sensitiveness to cold air which aggravates many symptoms. Ghosh also reported great improvement in a case of diabetes when the remedy was given for something else. Proell recorded his own case of idiopathic erysipelas affecting the back of the right hand, first three fingers and arm with violetcolored swelling and roughness. Rhus-t. removed the fever, but did nothing to stop the erysipelas. Carb-ac. 30c did so promptly. RELATIONS - Antidote: Alcohol, Vinegar, Chalk, Iodine. Glauber’s Salt in watery solution. Compare: (1) Apis, Gels. Merc, and Sulph. (2) In band-like headache, Ars., Carb-v., Chin, and Kreos. (3) in bums, ulcers, unhealthy offensive discharges, Pic-ac. (4) Ant-t. and Vario, in smallpox. (5) Chrysarobin, locally in ringworm of the scalp, 5-10 per cent, in glycerin and alcohol. Equal parts. (6) Ars., Kreos., Carbo, Guano. - Violent headache as from a band around head. Itching of nostrils, back, thighs, genitals. (6) Symptoms like hay fever, All-c, Ars. Incompatible: Glycerin and vegetable oils. In bums from carbolic acid, Elias Price found milk give immediate relief. He suggests A draft of milk in poisoning cases. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Stomach - Fermentative dyspepsia with bad taste and breath. Heat rises up esophagus. Constant belching, nausea, vomiting. heartburn. Flatulent distention of stomach and abdomen. Painful flatulence often marked in one part of the bowel. Nausea and vomiting during pregnancy, from seasickness, cancer. Dark, olive green vomit. Sore stomach.

Abdomen - Flatulence. Colic of nursing infants. Soreness of hypochondria worse motion. Abdominal muscles sore.

Rectum - Constipation with retraction of abdomen. Constipation with very offensive breath. Passes mucus from anus while urinating. Fetid, rice water diarrhea. Thin, black, putrid diarrhea. Bloody, like scrapings of intestines. Shreddy stools. Great tenesmus.

Female - Discharges always offensive (Nit- ac., Nux-v., Sep.). Pustules about vulva containing bloody pus. Severe backache across loins with dragging down thighs, from uterine displacement. Painful swelling of left ovary, worse walking in open air. Induration of cervix. Erosions of cervix, fetid, acrid discharge. Thick, irritating leucorrhea, causing itching and burning (Kreos.). Leucorrhea in children (Cann-s., Merc., Puls., Sep.). Puerperal fever with offensive discharge. Food - Appetite lost. Cheerful while eating. Desire for stimulants and tobacco. Desire for whiskey. Nausea from cold water. Hiccough after dinner.

Heart - Heart worse after indiscretion in eating. Stitches in region of heart. Palpitation. or violent action of heart at night. Bellows murmur over mitral valves. Organic valvular heart disease. Thready pulse. Pulse rapid, weak or intermittent, irregular.

Back - Aching between scapula. Pains in loins, worse straightening up and better pressure. Stitching pain, in right side of neck. Drawing in muscles of neck. Severe pain, in lumbosacral region. Soreness of muscles of back and limbs.

Limbs - Cramps in fore part of leg, close to tibia, during walking. Stiffness of limbs, hydrocephaloid. Cold hands and feet. Gnawing pains in shin bones. Arthritis.

Sleep - Very sleepy.

Skin - Burning, itching vesicles and pustules. Bloody vesicles or pustules. Burns tend to ulcerate. Erysipelas.

Modalities - Better from smoking. Better strong tea. Better rubbing, binding. There is intolerance of a warm room, but also sensitiveness to cold air which aggravate many symptoms. Worse from jar. Worse reading. Worse pregnancy. Worse combing hair.

Kidneys - Tired sensation in renal region. Urine, scanty, green. Urine alkaline. Urine scanty and red, in scarlatina. Urine dark, almost black. Albuminuria. Urine contained albumen in meningitis. Urinated freely an excessive quantity of saccharine urine. Diabetes.

Bladder - Frequent urination. Irritable bladder in old men. with frequent urination at night, of prostatic nature. Straining on passing urine.

Perspiration - Profuse, cold sweat. Profoundprostration, collapse and bathed in cold sweat. Clammy sweat on head, face and hands. Profuse sweat with restlessness. Sweats at night

Temperature - General chilliness and coldness of surface. Chills runs from head downward. Chilly sensation while in a warm room. Chilly in open air.

HOMEOPATHIC - Carbon tetrachloride is a worm antiparasite remedy of great potency. It has shown itself to be the best vermifuge for treatment of hookworm in a country where this disease predominates. It gives little discomfort to the patient, is palatable, requires no preparation of the patient and, when pure, is apparently not toxic in homeopathic doses, all of which features are of advantage in a popular campaign. COMMENTS - Dr. Lambert, in Suva, Fiji, noted the usefulness of Carb-tcl. for hookworms, he employed it in 50,000 cases. W. G. Smillie and S. B. Pessoa of Sao Paulo, Brazil, also found Carb-tcl. to be extremely efficient in removing hookworms. A small dose given to adults has been proved to remove 95 percent of all the hookworms harbored. REFERENCES Boericke.

full:
PHARMACY - carbn. Carboneum. Lamp- black. Amorphous carbon obtained from the chimney of a coal-oil lamp. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Convulsions. Sore throats. Tetanus. Tongue, spasms.

HOMEOPATHIC - This substance was proved by Dr. Burt in the lx trituration. Carbn. produced sore throat, a great craving for acids, and a peculiar convulsive attack. The attack began with spasms, commencing on the tongue, passing down the trachea to the lungs which prevented him from breathing for about two moments, then gradually left and went to the stomach, arms, hands and legs. It took four persons to hold him, two at his hands and two at his feet. Spasms both tonic and clonic. Lasted two hours then gradually ceased. The hands had no feeling in them, they were closed and could not be opened. Wrists perfectly pulseless, hands shriveled and cold. At 2 p.m., the spasms came on very suddenly, the same as the first time, but not so violent. The spasms did not affect the lungs this time, but were much harder in the stomach. Lasted three hours then gradually ceased. He seemed at the point of death. The spasms left him so weak that he could not lift his hand to his head nor sit up. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Carb-an., Carb-v., Carb-h., Carb-o., Nux-v., Aeth., Oena. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - carbn-h. Carboneum hydrogeni- satum. Carburetted hydrogen. Ethylene. Olefiant gas. Solution in alcohol. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Eyes, convulsions. Strokes. Tetanus. Whooping cough.

HOMEOPATHIC - This carbon gas, which was experimented with by Sir Humphrey Davy, produces a condition almost resembling a stroke attack. Illuminating gas is a complex gas, carburetted hydrogen being the leading ingredient. It was a popular custom to take children suffering from whooping cough to breathe the air at a gas-works. A case has been recorded in which an accidental escape of gas in a child's bedroom affected a prompt cure of its whooping cough. Stupefaction, comatose, surface cold and completely insensible. Spasm as in lock-jaw. Arms flexed at elbows. Trismus. Involuntary stools and urine. Steady and extreme oscillation of the eyeballs. Eyes distorted. Lids half closed. Dark bodies moving before eyes. Pupils insensible to light. MIND - Stupefaction. Extraordinary sensation of contentment. All thoughts appear in a moment as if seen in an inner mirror.

Head - Pressure in brain. Excruciating pain in forehead and between eyes.

Eyes - Eyes distorted, half closed. Eyeballs oscillate steadily, synchronously with breathing. Dark bodies moving before eyes.

Face - Staring look. Face turgid. Cheeks flap. Some degree of trismus, interrupted by yawning.

Stomach - Violent cramps in stomach. Nausea and vomiting. Vertigo - Vertigo, worse going into open air. Vertigo with nausea, loss of memory and sensation. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Chloroform, Ether, Amyl-n., Carboneum. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Rectum - Involuntary passage of stool and urine. Stools rice-water, thin feces mixed with dark blood and mucus.

Heart - Beating of the heart scarcely perceptible. Pulse strong, rapid, regular, or small and extremely weak.

Back - Violent spasm in the extensors of the back.

Limbs - Spasmodic stitching and trembling of limbs, felt paralyzed. Lungs - Voice feeble and indistinct. Paroxysms of cough. Dyspnea. Violent tearing pains in thorax.

Sleep - Sleep prolonged and very deep, interrupted by cramps in jaws and toes.

Skin - Skin icy cold. Sweating copiously, sweat smells of gas.

Modalities - Better by open air (convulsions).

PHARMACY - carbn-s. Carboneum sulphu- ratum. Carbon bisulphide. Alcohol sulphuris. Alcohol lampadii. Solution in rectified spirit. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Amblyopia. Anemia. Bums. Clergyman's sore throat. Coal gas, effects. Color-blindness. Glandular, swellings. Goiter. Gout. Heartbum. Hemiplegia. Hernia. Herpes. Impetigo. Impotency. Lead, poisoning. Liver, disorders. Memory, lost. Meniere's disease. Muscular, atrophy. Noises, head. Rheumatism. Scabies. Scalds. Sciatica. Spinal sclerosis. Strokes. Tetanus. Tinnitus. Toothache.

HOMEOPATHIC - Carbn-s. combines many characters of its two elements. It was first brought into notice by its effects on workers in rubber works. This remedy has a deep and disorganizing action and an immense range of action and symptomatology. Lack of vital heat. Sensitive to warm, damp weather. Worse from warmth. Sensitive patients, worse cold, wasted muscles Carboneum sulphuratum and skin and mucus membranes anesthetic. Tabes. Anesthesia of skin and mucus membranes. Chronic rheumatism. Sciatica. Paralysis with intense congestion of nerve centers. Sensory difficulties in limbs. Diminished sensibility of arms, hands and feet. Peripheral neuritis. Tremor. Muscular weakness Ataxia. Strong increase of mechanical muscular irritability. A feeling of vibration and trembling in whole body, particularly in hands. Burning, tearing, jerking, and stitching pains, apt to return at regular intervals for a long time. Pains come and go quickly. Special affinity for eyes. Disturbance of sight and sensibility. Vision better in evening, in twilight, after eating. “Toothache brought on by warm food” (Caib-v., Sulph.). Ringing in the ears with poor hearing. Eruptions of herpes and impetigo, discharges excoriating and producing violent itching. Herpetic diathesis. Flatulency (Carb-v.) and abdominal soreness (Sulph.). Diarrhea every four to six weeks. Digestive disorders of extreme severity. Periodic diarrhea, comes every six weeks. Incontinence of urine. Inability to sleep. Sleep is restless with tossing in bed. Giddiness. Impotence. Chronic lead poisoning. Useful in patients broken down by abuse of alcohol. MIND - Irritable, anxious intolerant, stupor. Sluggishness of mind. Confusion during headache. Memory lost. Dullness in children. Childish behavior. Idiocy and childishness. Anxiety in morning, on waking. Anxiety in bed. Anxiety at night. Oversensitive to noise. Fear while walking in the dark. Changeable mood. Extravagant gaiety or destructive anger. Dementia alternating with excitement. Great excitement at night has to be confined. Doesn't know what to do with things in the hands. Hallucination of sight and hearing. Visions of magnificent grandeur. Delirium, with incoherent talking. Singing. Delusions, surrounded by enemies. Delusions he is about to receive an injury. Delirium talks Carboneum sulphuratum of money. Violent, vehement. Desire to strike. Biting. Sought for things lying before them. Cheerful, free from care, after wind passed. Suicidal disposition, throwing himself from a window.

Head - Headache as from a tight cap. Dull muddled feeling in forehead. Noises in head. Constriction of forehead and occiput. Pressure pain in forehead. Violent pain, increasing till it causes confusion of mind. Brushing hair is painful. Itching on head. Head sinks forward in walking. Single nodules on head, sore to touch. Headache and dizziness.

Eyes - Eyes sunken, fixed, expressionless. Sunken eyes, with gray rings. Itching. Inflammation, followed by atrophy of optic nerve. Asthenopia and dyschromotopsia. Myopia. Cloudiness and atrophy of optic disc. Central scotoma. Retinal congestion, optic disc pale. Optic neuritis advancing toward atrophy. Arteries and veins con- gested. Reading causes lachrymation. Lids heavy. Lids sore on moving, quivering.

Ears - Sharp pain in ears after stool. Pain in left ear on swallowing. Sharp pain in right ear. Ears feel obstructed. Deafness, as if ears were obstructed by a fixed substance. Hearing impaired. iVoises in head. Tinnitus aurium. Meniere's disease. Buzzing and singing noises like an Aeolian harp.

Nose - Eruptions on nose. Sneezing with sensitiveness in chest. Tip of nose burns, as if raw, and is quite red. Tickling in point of nose with irritation to sneeze. Nosebleed. Smell is lost.

Face - Face pale, with clammy sweat. Face pale, with flushes of heat. Expression bewildered and as of one demented. Eruption on nose and cheeks similar to acne of drunkards. Tetter-like eruption on left cheek, from scratching with fingernails; spreads and is covered with yellowish- brown scabs, disfiguring the face; almost unbearable on account of continued itching. Pushes the lower jaw far forward, and gnashes with it against the upper one. Lips dry and burning.

Mouth - Anesthesia of mouth and tongue. Sweetish, foul, bitter, sour, pappy, metallic taste. Neuralgia of teeth. Toothache brought on by warm food. Hawking of salty mucus. Tongue cold. Tongue burning, stiff. Lisping, stammering speech like that of a child. Ulceration of the lips. Lips blue, moist, with convulsive movements.

Throat - Burning in throat extending to stomach. Tickling in back of palate after lying down, causes violent, dry cough. Sensation as if a hair has lodged in throat. As if a piece of bone has lodged in esophagus. Sharp, contracting pain. Scraping feeling in throat with fine stitches. Goitre. Voice feeble, of a deep tone. Hoarseness. Irritation to hawk. Heat in larynx, scratching and scraped feeling. Clergyman's sore throat. Vertigo - Sudden attacks of vertigo while sitting. Vision - Dim vision, objects fade away. Myopia. Loss of vision, progressive with central scotoma. Vision greatly impaired. Everything seems in a fog. Color blindness, red and green, not for white. Vision better evening, twilight, after eating. COMMENTS - In the Medical Argus, H. H. Crippen collected, from several sources, instances of workers intoxicated with Carbn-s. Carb-s. combines many characteristics of its two elements. It was brought to notice by its effects on workers in rubber works. Pains come and go quickly. The periodicity shows itself, as in diarrhea, which comes every six weeks. The worse from warmth common to Carb-v. and Sulph. shows itself in Carb-s. A feeling of vibration and trembling in whole body, particularly in hands. Carb-s. has the flatulence of Carb-v. and the abdominal soreness of Sulph. In many cases, the action on vision was very marked. Myopia, asthenopia, achromatopsia, dyschromatopsia. Cloudiness and atrophy of optic disc. Optic discs pale. Central scotoma for light and colors. Retinal congestion. Arteries and veins tortuous. Veins are distended and arteries contracted. Everything seemed in a fog, as if a spider's web over objects, green or red. One patient had complete right side hemiplegia, following sudden loss of consciousness, blindness of right eye and great impairment of vision of left. Loss of memory, especially for words, was a very frequent symptom. Delusions were common: “Heard voices and believed he had committed a robbery,” “sensation of a hole close by into which he was in danger of falling.” One acute case concerned a girl, aged 15, who was employed in vulcanizing works, and was exposed to the fumes one whole day. Before this, she had, from smaller exposures to the fumes, frontal pains and heaviness of the head. After this, the pains became more violent and were accompanied by painful contraction of masseters, then by stiffness of neck and vertebral column, finally of legs and arms. The contracture was generalized, but nowhere complete, though the jaws could not be separated. Ulcerative stomatitis ensued and tartar accumulated on the teeth. E. Case cured with Carb-s. 30c in a slender, nervous woman, a “Sensation, as of a weight between the scapulae, compelling her to bend forward. Throbbing in the dorsal spine as if a heart were beating there. Constipation with ineffectual urging to stool, hemorrhage of bright blood from rectum after stool. Itching of anus after stool, also in the night. Feet swollen, hot and throbbing in the evening.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kali xantate - Similar in action. Acts on cortical substance, loss of memory, marked blood degeneration, impotence and senility. (2) Tuberculinum, Radium, Carbo-v., Sulph., Caust., Salicyl, ac., Chin. HERBAL - Indigenous to the Mediterranean region and brought to Central Europe as a medicine as early as the M iddle Ages, where it is still cultivated. The Carline thistle has an enormous root and purple composite flowers surrounded by radical spinous leaves. Flourishes on dry stony ground and wasteland. This thistle was used externally for wounds, especially burns. It is said to have obtained its name ‘benedictus' from its high reputation as a heal-all, being supposed even to cure the plague. It is a basic ingredient of the Benedictine Liqueur and other bitter tonics, stomach bitters.

Hemoptysis. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Hepatitis. Influenza. Intermittents. Jaundice. Kidney, stones. Liver, disorders. Melaena. Metrorrhagia. Nausea. Neuralgias. Nosebleeds. Pleurisy. Rheumatism. Salivation. Sciatica. Spleen, disorders. Tuberculosis. Typhlitis. Ulcers. Varicose, ulcers. Varicose, veins. Vomiting. Waterbrash.

HERBAL - Rademacher, the medical alchemist, found Card-m. to be a primarily liver remedy, all its manifestations originating in some disorder of the liver. Burnett agreed, noting that it is primarily a liver and spleen remedy.

HOMEOPATHIC - The action of this remedy is centered in the liver and portal system. causing soreness, pain, and jaundice. It has a specific relation to the vascular system. Useful for a history of a toxic liver. It establishes a healthy flow of bile, and helps reduce the tendency for reformation of gallstones. Chronic liver weakness and cirrhosis of the liver, especially with ascites, a water- filled abdomen, and edema. Cirrhosis with swollen legs and varicose veins. Liver enlargement in the transverse direction (Chel. is more vertical). Gallstone colic. Jaundice. Hepatitis with hot flashes, flushing of heat. Damaged liver (Nux-v.). May help liver cancer. Dropsical conditions depending on liver disease and when due to pelvic congestion. Hemorrhages, especially connected with hepatic disease. Bilious fever. Infection of the gallbladder. Liver headaches (Sang., Chel.), migraines, often worse on the right side. Liver disorders associated with lung disorders. Influenza when liver is affected. Low blood sugar. Never well since mononucleosis or hepatitis. For the abuse of alcoholic beverages, especially beer. Characteristic bitter taste in the back of the mouth. The tongue has white down the center with a red tip. Portal stasis. Hemorrhoids with itching, burning in the rectum, dark urine. Spleen disease (Cean.). Associated with digestion problems and with a bitter taste in the mouth. Vomiting of bile-like substances. Chronic heartburn, fatigue after eating. Drawing pain up the abdomen, from the umbilicus to the solar plexus. Rumbling in the abdomen, clay-colored stools, blood in the stool. Diseases of miners associated with difficult breathing, asthma (Sil.). Debility, fatigue, worse eating and riding with frequent yawning. Varicose veins and ulcers. Stitching, drawing, burning pains. MIND - Melancholy with liver disorders. Joyless, apathetic. Despondency. Disposition to become angry. Hypochondriacal. Forgets what he has just intended to do.

Head - Headache better eating. Headache shortly before meals, disappearing after eating. Dull frontal headache with foul tongue. Liver headaches. Bilious headaches. Burning and pressure in head. Constriction, contractive feeling skull, over eyebrows. Pain in left parietal bone.

Eyes - Pressure as if eyeballs were pressed against side of orbits. Burning and pressure in eyeballs and lids.

Nose - Burning in right nostril. Tickling, first in right, then left nostril, with watery discharge- Habitual nosebleed. Sudden profuse nosebleed, relieving vertigo.

Face - Earthy, yellowish-gray, dirty or florid complexion. Heat in face. Weak upper lip.

Throat - Irritation in posterior part of larynx causing cough. Fauces as if rough and dry, with scraping, causes coughing. Swallowing painful. Larynx as if dry. Pressing pain on speaking and swallowing.

Stomach - Bitter taste. Sour eructations. Repeated belchings of air with burning in esophagus. Burning as of acidity. Sensation of emptiness. Pressure in the stomach. Griping pain. Colicky pain with waterbrash. Stitches in left side of stomach, near spleen (Cean.). Sour contents of stomach and intestines. Nausea, retching and vomiting of green acid fluid or blood. Nausea with salivation. Hematemesis. Tendency to attacks of bilious vomiting. Continual nausea with desire to vomit. Vomiting of pregnancy.

Abdomen - Sluggish peristalsis in colon. Fullness and soreness in hepatic region, with moist skin. Distention with rumbling, cutting pains. Painless flatulence in small intestine. Pain in region of liver. Cutting pain in bowels, changing from place to place. Stitches in spleen, worse on inspiration, stooping. Stitches in small intestine, better pressure. Sensation of motion in intestines on expiration, around navel. Pressure with sensation of warmth in small intestine, on left side of abdomen. Pulsation in abdomen.

Female - Menses too profuse or suppressed. Metrorrhagia. Chronic uterine hemorrhage with portal derangement. Food - Poor appetite. Voracious appetite. Aversion to salt meat. Abuse of beer. Great fatigue after eating. Low blood sugar. Soups salted as usual tasted insipid, at other times well salted food is repugnant.

Chest - Pain in chest going to shoulders, back, loins and abdomen with urging to urinate. Stitching pains in lower right ribs and front, worse moving, walking. Pain during breathing. Stitches in chest, from left nipple to right downward. Diaphragm high. Constitutions - Choleric constitutions.

Heart - Pain, pressure, and stitches in region of heart. Oppression on deep breathing.

Back - Sensitiveness in dorsal and cervical vertebrae. Drawing pains in back. Drawing, tearing, burning in left shoulder blade.

Sleep - Restless sleep with frequent awakening and many dreams. Nightmares from lying on back. Fatigue with yawning. Uncontrollable yawning.

Skin - Varicose veins and ulcers. Broken or hard thrombosed veins. Itching on lying down at night. Eruption on lower part of sternum.

Modalities - Better from bleeding. Worse frorn lying on left side. Worse motion. Worse touch. Worse eating. Worse beer. Worse cellars. Mouth ' Bitter taste. Collection of water in mouth- Smooth sensation of mucus membrane °f palate, as though covered with fat-

Tongue - Tongue furred. Tongue white, white center, red tip and edges. Tongue white-coated on side, and weak. Vertigo - Vertigo with tendency to fall forward, better by nosebleed. COMMENTS - G. F. Laidlaw gave acondensed translation of Rademacher's remarks about Card-m.: “He regards hematemesis as most frequently due to chronic disease of the spleen, less frequently to disease of the liver. People who have long suffered from pains in the left hypochondrium are apt to vomit blood after which they are relieved. “Rademacher regards the bleeding as often beneficial and says it should not be checked too soon. In the treatment of hematemesis he says it is best to use a remedy that acts on the epigastric region without irritating the stomach and interfering with the healing of the lesion. Such a remedv he found in a decoction of the seeds of Card-m. “He used to give Opium before, but this, he says in some people ‘produces an array of symptoms similar to those seen in severe hemorrhage and might aggravate and condition.'” Rademacher added: “It is probable that many small hemorrhages of the stomach escape notice because there is no vomiting and that it is in this manner that obscure abdominal complaints are sometimes suddenly relieved or cured.” Burnett related the case of a girl of sixteen who had severe attacks of vomiting for three months with pains in abdomen. The vomiting was relieved by remedies symptomatically related, but the pains were not. An examination showed the “liver and spleen both very much enlarged so that they seem to fill the abdomen.” Card-m. tincture in 5 drop doses, night and morning soon cured the patient. Dudgeon gave an account of Windelband and Kunze's experience with the remedy. Windelband, in treating a woman forchronic swelling of the liver with Card-m., incidentally cured at the same time some “colossal varicose ulcers.” This experience led Dudgeon to cure a large number of similar cases with the same remedy. He also cured cases of gastrointestinal catarrh, nosebleeds, metrorrhagia, hemorrhoidal flux, dependent on portal congestion. Tenderness of the liver, bilious fever, symptoms resembling peritonitis and stitch-in-the-side have been cured by it. Kunze commended the remedy in cases of stomach spasms, contractive pains, vomiting occurring at the climax, cold rising from precordium to throat, feeling of spasmodic constriction, pressive, shooting pain in right side of abdomen spreading to back or shoulder. Kunze cured with it pains in the hepatic and splenic regions accompanied with hemoptysis, or expectoration of viscid, lumpy mucus, and evening fever. Even tuberculosis pituitosa has been cured by it. Local muscular rheumatisms dependent on liver disease. E. A. Cook gave Card-m. 1c to a patient suffering from liver congestion, swollen veins of legs, hemorrhoids and headache with great benefit to all the symptoms. On the second day the patient developed new symptoms, which she had never had before and which alarmed her greatly : “Great giddiness with inclination to fall forward and a sudden and profuse nosebleed followed by great relief.” A striking cure by Card-m. in “Miner's Disease" is recorded by Proell.: “An old miner in the gold minesof Bockstein suffered from the so-called “Bergsucht" (miner's disease). His chief symptoms were: earthy complexion, eyes dim, hardness of hearing, mucus coating on tongue, loss of appetite even for his favorite food and tobacco. “Great dyspnea and palpitations on going up-hill, spleen and stomach distended, with much gas eructated, constant borborygmus, constipation alternating with diarrhea, but the latter more frequent, evacuations gray, urine scanty and pale, skin dry as if withered, great weakness, pulse slow and weak. “Especially remarkable was the disposition of this man. Formerly cheerful, he is now joyless and apathetic, the most important events he took no notice. “He was given the tincture of Card-m., a few drops four times a day. Unable to effect any alteration in his food, drink or regimen. “A month after this he returned looking much better. On asking him how he was, he replied: ‘You have made a new man of me.' Almost all the former symptoms had disappeared and given place to the opposite. “His complexion was fresh, his eyes sparkled, he was cheerful, wished to live and work, had good appetite, motions brown, more urine passed, pulse normal. He said for the first time he knew what it was to be well and he remained so for many years.” Proell also recommended it in disorders of the liver, spleen and kidneys caused by abuse of alcoholic beverages, especially beer. He related two cases, one in a cook who had symptoms of cirrhosis of the liver and general dropsy which made her features unrecognizable, and one in a worker in a brewery who developed dropsy. Both were cured by the tincture. The brewery man, thinking the remedy was intended to be purgative and thinking the 4 drops prescribed would not be sufficient took the whole amount, 2 1/2 drachms, at one dose, without markedly bad effects and was quickly cured. Proell added that Card-m. is indicated where there is a relaxed state of the mucus membrane of the stomach. Evidenced by flatulence and diarrhea, especially when the stools are clay-colored. Much fatigue is experienced, worse after eating, when riding, on awaking, frequently accompanied by yawning. Chilliness is prominent, on awaking, at night, worse uncovering. Coldness of knees. Head very sensitive to cold. Sweating of forehead and back after meals. Stitches, drawing pressure are prominent, also radiating paints, constriction, band-sensation and cramps. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lyc., Chel. Chion., Nux-v., Podo. (2) Card, benedictus - strong action on eyes and sensation of contraction in many parts, stomach symptoms similar. (3) Merc., Bry., Aloe. (4) Bry. - nosebleed. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Liver - L*ver, engorged, swollen laterally, painful to pressure. Hyperemia of liver. Pains in region of liver, with dizziness, ba(j taste in mouth and jaundiced skin. Cirrhosis of liver with general edema. Jaunie with dull headache, bitter taste in mouth, and white tongue. Left lobe is very sensitive. Gallstones. Gallstone diseases with an enlarged liver. Terrible attacks of gallst°ne colic. Swelling of gallbladder with painful tenderness. Stitches in liver, worse lying on left side. Liver disorders cause lung diseases, causing hemoptysis. Tens>on *n Hver when lying on right side, worse pressure. Crawling sensation. Lungs ' Asthmatic respiration. Asthma of miners. Cough with stitches in sides of chest with bloody sputum. Expectoration of pure blood, mucus mixed with blood. Splenic or hepatic cough.

Kidneys - Urging to urinate. Pressure on bladder, producing dribbling of urine after unavailing urging to stool. Strangury. Burning at meatus, in urethra. Urine, cloudy, golden-colored, turbid. Kidney stones. Limbs rheumatic pains in right deltoid. right arm. Pain in hip joint spreading through buttocks down the thighs, worse stoop*n8’ with difficult rising. Weakness fe|t jn feet, especially after sitting. Drawing Pæn *n muscles. Cramp-like pain in muscles of arms, hands, calves, and feet.

Perspiration - Sweat on forehead and back after meals. Sweats over whole body, with lassitude, on awakening. Rectum ’ Burning pain in the rectum and anus, which interferes with sitting. Itching. paste-like, clay stools. Bright yellow stools- Constipation. Stools hard, difficult, knotty, alternates with diarrhea. Bleeding hemorrhoids. Prolapse of rectum. Profuse diarrhea due to rectal cancer. Melaena. Stools either bileless or black.

Temperature - Chill and fever with jaundice. Chilliness at night, worse uncovering. Chilliness on awakening with strong urge to urinate. Epidemic influenza. Bilious fever.

full:
PHARMACY - carl. Carlsbad aqua. Carlsbad Springs. Karlsbad. The Waters of the Sprudel Springs and Muhlbriinnen Springs. It is a very complicated solution containing the sulphite, bicarbonate and chloride of sodium in preponderating quantity with carbonates, sulfates, phosphates, fluoride and oxides of calcium, magnesium, strontium, ferrum, manganum, potassium, aluminum, silicon and carbon, with traces of iodide and bromide of sodium of caesium, rubidium, lithium and boric oxide. Karlsbad, Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Blushing. Constipation. Cramp. Debility. Diabetes. Gout. Hot,flashes. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Sprains. Urination, urgings. Weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Carl, is famous for its action on the liver and in the treatment of obesity, diabetes and gout. Clarke found Carlsbad in the potencies responded admirably to its indications. General weakness with discomfort. General anxious sensation as if blood in artery would stagnate, with constant flushes of heat. Pains are dislocated and spraining, drawing, tearing, stitching, burning, dull shocks and jerks. Sensation of weakness, prostration, so that she trembled and could hold nothing securely. Tired, dejected, sluggish, anxious trembling. Great liability to take cold. Hot flashes. Flushes ofheatallover. Periodicity, effects repeated after from two to four weeks (Ox-ac., Sulph.). Itching on various parts. In homeopathic doses, Carl, is useful in weakness of all organs. Weakness of all organs of organs of speech. Weakness of bladder, stream weak and slow, only passed with assistance of abdominal muscles. Weakness of rectum, stool slow and only passed with help of distant parts of intestinal canal. Constipation. MIND - General anxious state. Excited and peevish. Feels weak and incapable. Poor self confidence. Discouraged and anxious about domestic duties. Discouraged before menses. Homesickness. Irritability. Absorbed, buried in thought. Anxiety in the house, better open air. Confusion better walking in open air. Excitement over trifles. Sympathetic, weeping from sympathy with others. Sensitive, affected to tears by the sorrows of others. Difficult thinking, indisposition to all mental exertions. Absent-minded, forgets names. Aversion to reading. Difficulty writing, often omits letters.

Eyes - Heat streams from eyes with burning and pressing in them. Violent pressure above orbits. Twitching, quivering in upper lids. Excessive lachrymation, worse using eyes. Eyes weak, water, lids agglutinated. Cannot do fine, near work. Objects swim before sight. Appearance of black spots swimming about.

Ears - Increased warmth in ear, which itches. Fine twitching from Eustachian tube to tympanum. Humming, roaring, ringing. Transient loss of hearing.

Nose - Catarrh of nose and throat, with hoarseness. Frequent sneezing, blowing out thick mucus. Swelling of nasal veins. Habitual bleeding of nose. Nosebleed on suppression of menses. Loss of smell after stoppage of nose.

Face - Face yellow, sallow, changes color. Red and hot. Pain in zygomatic process, feels as if cobwebs were on it.

Mouth - Offensive smell from mouth. Sour or salty taste. Clayey, pappy taste with salivation. Flow of saliva and frequent spitting. Dryness of whole mouth, especially roof, as if dried up, with increased thirst.

Throat - Hoarseness and roughness of voice. Constantly hawking up of much mucus.

Stomach - Sensation of emptiness. Pressure and heaviness after eating. Heartburn (Carb-v.). Frequent belching, sometimes smelling and tasting of the food, sometimes very bitter. Hiccough and yawning at same time, worse after drinking and eating. Nausea with salivation and shuddering.

Abdomen - Pressing, pinching in the hypochondria. Twitching in jerks. Burning pain in spleen. Sensation of ring stretched around abdomen.

Rectum - Burning in rectum with constant pressure. Feces held back. Stool slow and only passed by much abdominal pressure. Mucus diarrhea. Stools green, or dark green. Discharge of bloody mucus, with itching. Bleeding from hemorrhoids. Shooting pain. Gallstones passed.

Male - Testicles swollen without sign of inflammation, pressive pain.

Female - Three days aftercessation of menstruation, discharge of lumps of tenacious black blood. Hot flashes. Leucorrhea. Food - Appetite and thirst much increased. Head - Aches with swollen temporal veins (Sang.), better motion in open air. Rush of blood to head, with heaviness and confusion. Pressing, stupefying, tearing headache. Throbbing and beating in head. Hair falls out.

Chest - Heaviness, fullness, oppression, anxiety. Peculiar sensation of oppression in lower part of chest, as if lung had not room enough to expand. Stitching in chest. Weakness in the chest while writing.

Heart - Painfulness in heart, frequent transient stitching and painful drawing. Tension and contraction in heart region.

Back - Drawing pain in nape of neck and shoulder blade. Stiffness, paralysis, pressure. Heat and burning and at times a shudder over back. Tensive and pressing pains from small of back.

Limbs - Cracking in all the joints. Trembling and crawling. Restlessness of limbs, with yawning. Sensation of falling asleep, stiffness. Going-to-sleep sensation in fingertips. Heaviness of the arms after writing, with coldness. Varicoses of superficial veins of lower limbs. Lungs - Frequent hawking of mucus. Sensation of soreness, sensitiveness, scraping and tickling. Difficult breathing on ascending steps.

Sleep - Constant yawning and sleepiness, worse after a meal. Frightful dreams with tossing. Dreams are not remembered.

Modalities - Better in open air. Better on motion. Even the headaches are better by motion. Worse morning and evening. Worse after lying down in bed. Worse after eating and drinking. Worse on ascending.

Teeth - Thick, pappy mucus coating on teeth. Gums painfully swollen. Teeth loosen and fall out. Prominent teeth. Tearing in roots of upper molars, worse after every meal. Toothache, worse cold or warmth.

Tongue - Tongue coated white, with offensive smell from mouth. Vertigo - Dizzy confusion and heaviness, worse after eating, better open air. Momentary attacks of vertigo, had to hold himself up. Vertigo with turning as if in a circle, better open air. COMMENTS - The action of Carl, has been observed on some healthy persons, but the bulk of the symptoms, many of which are strikingly peculiar, have been obtained from patients under treatment. They are. however, characteristic and have furnished the indications for many homeopathic cures. W. J. Guernsey cured with it sciatica in an old man with a cramp in his left ankle. About a month after ceasing the remedy the patient complained that he felt paralyzed in the loins for several hours after rising from bed, better as the day advanced. This was a new symptom very like the Carlsbad effects. Noted periodicity, effects repeated after two to four weeks. The skin has red spots and streaks, frequently burning like fire. Pimples and pustules. Crawling and prickling on various parts with sweat breaking out. Itching on various parts. Much itching and increased sweat of genitals. Increased sensitiveness of the skin. Sensitiveness to cold air, great liability to take cold. Frequent alternations of shuddering, chilliness and heat. Flushes of heat all over, especially in face with sweat on forehead. Heat of head with redness of face and creeping shudders. Sweats more easily. Sweat stains linen yellow. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1) Nat-s. - sensitive to cold. (2) Carb-an. - sweat staining yellow. (3) All-c. - lachrymation, Nux-v. - worse after eating, Puls., Carb-v. - better in open air. (4) Bell., Glon. - headache. (5) Anae., Apis, Nux- m., Ph-ac. - absent-minded. Aloe. - cracking in head. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Kidneys - Stream weak and slow, only passed by pressing abdominal muscles. Frequent urging with discharge of copious, watery urine. Brick red sediment. Tenacious, like frog-spawn. Urine stains linen dark yellow.

Perspiration - Sweats more easily. Stains linen yellow.
