PHARMACY - chin-b. China boliviana. Cinchona boliviana. A variety of Cinchona calisaya growing furthernorth. N. O. Rubiacae. Tincture of bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aphthae. Corns. Coryza. Flatulence. Mouth, ulcerated. Pneumonia. Wry-neck. .

HOMEOPATHIC - China boliviana has the main features of Chin, off., but some are peculiar and deserve separate mention. Chin-b. was proved by Modiedo. Chin-b. has ulceration of commissures of mouth. Cough with dagger-like pains in base Of right lung. Rigidity of nape of neck. Hands red hot or cold and sticky. Sticky sweat about the anus. Flatulence. Disturbed and dream-filled sleep. Sensitiveness to touch. MIND - Gloom alternating with serenity. Alternation of bad and good humor. Fits of rage, blasphemes. Cowardice.

Head - Headache in morning on awaking, leaves during the day or lasts all day and leaves during sleep.

Eyes - Violent pains like a stab in left eyes, followed by itching and tears.

Ears - Detonation as of a cannon in right ear. Ringing, humming, whistling sounds.

Face - Aphthae on inner surface of lips, ulceration of commissures. Food - Hunger or lack of appetite, repugnance to meat. After eating, feels a weight in stomach. Cold, sneezing, sleepy and desire to sleep in evening.

Mouth - Mouth bitter in morning on waking. Nose - Much sneezing on awaking with smell of fresh pus. Sensation of incipient cold with tight feeling and pain in throat. Violent cold in head. Mucus from posterior sinuses.

Stomach - Much gas rises from stomach. Throat - Constriction and burning in throat. Vertigo - Vertigo as after a drunken fit, voracious appetite. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Abdomen - Pain in both hypochondria and under ribs on waking in the morning. Pain in splenic region.

Rectum - Biting in anus as from worms, excoriated sensation. Viscous sweat on anus.

Male - Pollutions exceedingly weakening. Excoriation on inner and lower part of prepuce. Gleet and ulceration of prepuce.

Back - Nape of neck rigid, cannot turn head to right, any sudden movement causes a snap or crack. Wry- neck. Pain in left shoulder, left buttock and also in right hip bone on sitting up in bed.

Limbs - Legs and feet icy cold, as if blown on by wintry wind. Painful corns. Lungs - Cough with pain in right lung, as from a dagger buried there, at times makes breathing laborious, burning in eyes, limbs cold. Unbearable pain in right lung, extends to region of liver, sensitive to touch.

Sleep - Dreams of the sea, of fishes, swimming, bathing. Dreams of journeys by land and sea, Dreams of vomiting of worms.

full:
PHARMACY - chin. China officinalis. Peruvian bark. China regia. Kina-Kina. Cinchona calisaya. Cinchona rubra. Cinchona succirubra. N. O. Rubiacae. Central and South America. Tincture of the dried bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Albuminuria. Alcoholism. Amaurosis. Amblyopia. Anasarca. Anemia. Aphthae. Asthma. Back, weakness. Bedwetting. Bilious, attack. Blood, loss. Breast-feeding, disorders. Cachexia. Candida. Catarrhal, disorders. Chills. Chorea. Cirrhosis. Colic. Colitis. Coma, Constipation. Coughs. Debility. Dehydration. Delirium. Dermatitis. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Digestive, disorders. Dropsy. Dyspepsia. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Ears, deafness. Ears, noises. Edema. Emaciation. Emissions. Empyema. Epilepsy. Erysipelas. Eye, disorders. Facial, neuralgia. Fainting. Fatigue. Fermentation. Fevers. Flatulence. Food, poisoning. Gallstone, colic. Gallstones. Gangrene. Headaches. Hectic, fever. Hematuria. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Hepatitis. Hip, joint, disease. Ichthyosis, Impotency. Indigestion. Infertility. Influenza. Insomnia. Intermittent, fever. Jaundice. Labor, pains. Leucorrhea. Lienteria. Liver, diseases. Malaria. Masturbation. Meniere's disease. Menstruation. Mercury, poisoning. Muscae, volitantes. Nausea. Neuralgia. Night blindness. Ovaritis. Paralysis. Parasites. Pemphigus. Pneumonia. Peritonitis. Perspiration. Pleurisy. Psoriasis. Pylorus. Rheumatism. Sleep, disorders. Spermatorrhea. Spleen, disorders. Stomach, disorders. Strokes. Suffocation, fits. Taste, disordered. Tea, effects. Thirst. Tinnitus. Tobacco, habit. Traumatic, fever. Traveler's diarrhea. Tropical, fever. Tuberculosis. Tympanitis. Ulcers. Varicose, veins. Vertigo. Vomiting. Weakness. Worms.

HERBAL - Kina is the Peruvian name for “bark,” and “Kina-Kina” is the “Bark of barks. ” The story of its introduction into European medical practice is one of the romances of the Healing Art, as the story of its frightful abuse is one of its many tragedies. The tincture of Chin., Cinchona rubra, is useful in removing the craving for alcohol in alcoholics who wish to reform. Ten to thirty drops two or three times a day is the usual dose for this. Where the general symptoms correspond, the potencies would probably do better.

HOMEOPATHIC - Cinchona bark was to Hahnemann what the falling was to Newton and the swinging lamp to Galileo. Dissatisfied with the explanations of the action of Bark in curing ague that were current in his time, Hahnemann took the powdered Bark himself, being in health and behold, a malaria attack ensured. A repetition of the experiment produced the same result. Further experiments revealed that action of Bark which is the opposite of “tonic,” positively debilitating in fact, already referred to. China affects the blood, making it thinner and impoverished. It weakens the heart and impairs the circulation, producing congestion and hemorrhages, anemia, relaxation and collapse. Gallbladder disorders. Gallstones. Worse since gallbladder surgery. Debility due to profuse, exhausting discharges, loss of vital fluids, excessive suppuration, diarrhea, hemorrhages etc. Dropsy after loss of fluids, hemorrhages. Blood loss with weakness. Inflammation of bleeding organ after hemorrhages. Convulsions during the hemorrhages. Profuse hemorrhages, with loss of sight, faintness and ringing in ears. Weak digestion, fermentation, gas and diarrhea. Gas and bloating of the abdomen. Post-operative gas pains, no relief from passing it. Gout. Chronic suppurative pyelitis. Traveler's diarrhea or tropical diseases. Hepatitis and severe diarrheas. Foodpoisonings, worse from bad water or fruit, from eating bad fruit, unripe fruit, bad meat, decomposing meat (Ars.). Marked periodicity. Intermittent periodicity is very marked in fever and neuralgias. The patient becomes very weak, oversensitive and nervous, everything upsets him, light, noise, odors, drafts, pain etc. bursting pain. Neuralgia. Wounds become black and gangrenous. Psoas abscess. Epilepsy, chorea, paralysis from loss of fluids. Keynote gas and bloating, diarrhea, indigestion, irritability. Very sensitive to touch and pressure, especially around the abdomen. Intestinal candida. Fermentation in the bowels. Failure to thrive, malabsorption in babies (Aeth., Mag-c.). Emaciation, especially of children. Anemia. Hard swelling. Rheumatism. Sepsis. MIND - Apathetic, indifferent, disobedient, taciturn, despondent. Lack of self-confidence. Dislike of all mental and physical work. Reluctant to speak. Unable to think. Slow flow of ideas, can't arrange his thoughts. Mental exhaustion (Sil.). Makes mistakes in speech or writing. Mind constantly changing from one thing to another. Ideas crowd in mind, prevent sleep. Abundant ideas and clearness of mind in evening. Full of plans and projects, in evening and at night and reflects upon their execution. Insomnia from fantasies, builds air castles. Loss of control over mind. Anxiety in morning on waking. Excessively anxious about trifles. Inconsolable anxiety. Oversensitive to noise. Fearful and apprehensive. Fear of dogs and other animals, at night. Excessive vividness of mind and imagination during headache. Sudden crying and tossing about, when cheerful. Excitement after hearing horrible things. Dwells on past disagreeable occurrences at night. Cheerfulness alternating with gloom. Weeping about a fancied need. Discontented mood. Disobedient, stubborn. Irritable, sensitive and very touchy. Irritability, even if looked at. Irritability after sex. Contempt for everything. Peevish, ill- humored, easily angered. Ill humor, worse hugging and caressing. Reproaches others. Disposition to hurt other people's feelings. Aversion to be looked at. Deliriumfrom the loss of fluids. Sees faces and objects on closing eyes. Indifference, sad, no desire to live. Fixed ideas, that he is unhappy, persecuted by enemies. Runs about. Desire for suicide but lacks courage. “Intolerable anxiety about 8 p.m. and2 a.m.. springs out of bed and wishes to take his own life, but does not go near the window or take a knife (Alum.) with heat of the body without thirst.”

Head - Bursting, throbbing pain with throbbing of carotids. Intense throbbing of head and carotids. Congestion of blood to head during menses. As if skull would burst. Sensation as if brain were swashing to and fro, causing pain. Bruised pain in brain, worse temples. Congestive headaches. Head heavy. Dullness and confusion of head. Spasmodic headache in vertex. Headaches after hemorrhage. Headaches, worse in open air, current of air, sun, by contact, stepping. Headaches, better by hard pressure, rubbing, warm room, moving head up and down. Nosebleed relieves headaches. Sharp pains from temple to temple. Headaches from suppressed coryza. Burning in forehead with sweat on it. Supraorbital neuralgia. Sweats when walking in open air. Sore, sensitive scalp, worse touching or combing hair.

Eyes - Inflammation and itching of eyes and eyelids in persons debilitated by loss of vital fluids. Blue color around eyes. Hollow eyes. Yellowish sclerotica. Iritis from loss of blood after confinement. Night blindness, due to anemic retina. Amaurosis, scalding lachrymation. Lachrymation, with crawling pain in eyes. Photophobia, eyes sensitive to bright light. Distortion of eyeballs. Pressure in eyes as from drowsiness. Pressive, burning pains in eyes, much heat, redness of eyes. Eyes painful on reading and writing. Eyes smart as from salt. Motion of eyes painful. Stitching as from sand. Eyes as if filled with smoke. Sensation of foreign body in eye, with inflammation and heat, worse evening. Pupils dilated or contracted. Involuntary closing of eyelids from mere weakness. Intermittent ciliary neuralgia. Ulcers in course of pannus, with much pain in morning. Ulceration of cornea.

Ears - External ear, sensitive to touch. Lobules red and swollen. Stitches in ears. Tearing pain worse least touch. Foul, purulent, bloody discharge. Hemorrhage from ears after prolonged suppuration. Hemorrhage from ear, offensive, bloody, purulent discharge. Tinnitus, then vertigo. Humming, roaring, or tickling. Meniere's disease. Ringing in ears with headache. Ringing in ears with debility. Noises in ears, with faintness, great weakness, trembling debility, aftermenses. Hardness of hearing. Hearing sensitive to noise.

Nose - Ill effects from suppressed coryza, headache. Checked catarrh causes headache. Pressive pain in root of nose. Hay fever, watery coryza with pain in temples. Violent, dry sneezing. Sneezing, water discharge, coryza. Smell too acute. Sensitive to odor of flowers, cooking and tobacco. Cold sweat about nose. Nose, hot, red. Easily bleeding from nose, especially on rising. Nosebleed with paleness of face, fainting. Nosebleed with congestion of blood to head.

Face - Sallow, pale complexion. Red, hot face, with cold hands. Earthy, sickly, pale, hippocratic, bluish around the eyes. Lips, dry, black and shriveled. Lips deep blue. Bloated face. Swelling of veins. Face hot, when entering room from open air. Face flushed after hemorrhage, sexual excess or loss of vital fluids. Facial neuralgia. Faceache nervous or rheumatic. Prosopalgia worse touch or motion. Needle-like pains, in left face, left chest and left hand. Violent tearing, burning pains in face. Submaxillary glands swollen. Erysipelas of face and hairy portion of scalp.

Mouth - Dryness of mouth. Food, water tastes bitter, acute, or too salty, even water. Bitter taste in mouth for a while after eating. Gums swollen. Putrid taste in morning. Painful sensitive swelling of uvula. Salivation day and night, years after mercury.

Throat - Difficult swallowing, as from contraction of esophagus. Enlarged tonsils. Throat feels rough, scraped, producing a sore sensation on swallowing. Gangrene of throat. Larynx and trachea as if sore. Hoarse, rough voice. Deep, husky voice when talking or singing. Sensation as if something adhering to larynx.

Stomach - Flatulence. Flatulence in stomach for a long time after a meal, as if he had just eaten. Bloated stomach. Fermentation after eating fruits. Indigestion. Digestion, weak and slow. Cold feeling in stomach. Pulsations and rumbling in epigastrium. Stomach sore, as if ulcerated. Gastric disorders from eating fish, tea, sour wine, new beer, impure water, fruit, milk. Weight after eating small quantity of food. Spasmodic pain in stomach. Belching of bitter fluid. Eructations, taste of food. Regurgitation of food, gives no relief, worse eating fruit. Pulsations and rumbling in pit. Hiccoughs. Hematemesis. Darting pain crosswise in hypogastric region. Frequent vomiting of undigested food. Vomiting worse at night. Sour vomiting of water, mucus and food. Vomiting of food, in debilitated persons. Stools - Involuntary stools. Very weakening stools, with much flatulence. Stools loose, brownish, painless with a feeling China officinalis of debility. Stools, worse at night, after meals. Stools, very weakening with much flatulence. Stools with undigested food. Stools, frothy, yellow, dark, foul, watery. Stools bloody, painless. Stools, worse during hot weather. Stools, worse from fruit, milk, or beer. White stools with dark urine. Stool loose and green in children, with great flatulence.

Abdomen - Liver and spleen swollen and enlarged. Tympanitic abdomen. Abdomen distended, wants to belch, eructations afford no relief. Flatulent bloating, better motion. Muchflatulentcolic, better bending double. Dysentery with dehydration and weakness. Abdominal colic with hunger. Colic better bending double. Colic with shivering. Colitis. Constrictive pains from incarcerated flatulence. Post-operative gas pains, no relief from passing it. Fermentation in instestines from eating fruit. Heat in abdomen as if hot water running down. Pain from rectum to genitals. Pain in right hypochondrium. Internal coldness of stomach and abdomen. Gastro-duodenal catarrh. Parasites, worms. Swelling, inflammation, induration of spleen. Strangulated hernia.

Rectum - Involuntary stools. Traveler's diarrhea. Difficult stools even when soft (Alum., Plat.). Diarrhea and dehydration. Diarrhea after weaning in children. Chronic diarrhea in children, who become drowsy, pupils dilated, body becomes cold especially chin and nose, with rapid respiration. Dysentery with dehydration and weakness. Constipation, large accumulation of feces. Sharp pain in rectum during stool. Accumulation of much flatus, which will pass neither up nor down. Bleeding hemorrhoids, burning and itching. Mucus discharge from rectum. Tingling in anus. Worm troubles, worse at night, fullness in abdomen, with heartburn and waterbrash.

Male - Swelling of testes and spermatic cord, after gonorrhea. Orchitis. Swelling of epididymis. Tearing pain in left testis and left side of prepuce. Cramplike, contractive pain in testes, evenings. Frequent emissions, followed by great weakness. Impotence from overindulgence. Lost of vital fluids. Morbid sexual desire with lascivious fancies. Sexual desire with craving for dainties.

Female - Dysmenorrhea. Menstrual colic. Menses dark, profuse. Profuse menses with anemia and pain. Menses too early. Menses clotted with abdominal distention. Suppression of menses from chagrin. Metrorrhagia, blood dark with fainting, convulsions. Painful heaviness in pelvis. Painful induration in the vagina. Dropsy of ovaries, uterus. Ovaritis from sexual excess. Ovaritis from hemorrhage. Leucorrhea, instead or before menses with spasmodic uterine contraction. Bloody leucorrhea, seems to take the place of the usual menstrual discharge. Leucorrhea with painful bearing down to vulva and anus. Discharge of bloody serum, alternating with pus. Congestion to uterus, fullness, pressing and heaviness, worse walking. Uterine spasms. Uterine hemorrhage, with ringing in ears, fainting. Desire too strong in lying-in women. Labor pains cease from hemorrhage. Anemia, exhaustion, blood loss since childbirth. Promotes expulsion of moles. Long- lasting lochia sometimes fetid, cheesy or purulent. Food - Voracious appetite in emaciated children. Hunger and yet want of ap- petite, only while eating some appetite and natural taste for food return. Quick satiety. Anorexia, feels satiated all the time. Complete loss of appetite in people suffering from malaria. Aversion to all food. Aversion to food or canine hunger, during fever. Aversion to hot food, fats and rich food, fruit, meat. Aversion to bread, butter, coffee. Aversion to beer, coffee, milk. Craving, for dainties, sour or sweet things. Desires various things without knowing what, especially children. Desires highly seasoned food, sour fruit, fruit, Desires wine, salt, coffee. Desires sour, cooling things, roasted coffee. Food poisoningfrom bad meat, impure water. Ill effects of tea. Milk disagrees. Bitter or sour eructations after milk, heartburn after milk. Diarrhea from fruit, milk, beer. Food tastes bitter, even water. Food tastes too salty. Fruit, tea causes flatulence. Warm drinks impede digestion. Thirst for cold water, worsens diarrhea. Thirst during abdominal colic. Thirst during apyrexia, before chill. Thirstlessness or thirst for cold drink only, during fever.

Chest - Painful, sore chest with soreness between scapulae, cannot bear percussion or auscultation. Pressing, stinging pains in chest and trachea. Pressive drawing pains, across lower portion of chest while sitting, causes anxiety, disappearing while standing and walking. Oppression in chest as if from a lump. Sides of chest feel as if beaten. Sticking pain in small spot below last right ribs, worse slightest pressure or walking. Boils on chest. Constitutions - Suited to persons of thin, dry, bilious constitutions. Leuco- phlegmatic persons with a disposition to dropsical disorders, catarrhs or diarrhea, to disorders of women.

Heart - Movement excites palpitations. Irregular, with weak, rapid beats followed by strong heartbeats. Suffocative attacks, syncope, anemia and dropsy. As if blood China officinalis flowed warm from the heart. Melancholy feeling about heart, with desire to take a deep breath. Pulse small, hard, rapid and irregular. Palpitations with distension of veins. Strong, violent palpitations with feeble pulse and cold skin. Pulse more quiet after meals.

Back - Pressure as of a stone between scapulae. Inter-scapular spine painful. Sharp pains across kidneys, worse movement, at night. Knife-like pains around the back. Heavy pressure on sacrum. Backache as from sitting bent for long time. Intolerable pain in lumbar region. Lumbago, worse slight motion. Spinal affections with diminished sexual desire. Sweat on back and neck from least motion. Sharp pains in spine and shoulders. Causations - Ill effects of dehydration, loss of vital fluids. Masturbation. Blood loss. Ill effects of vexation, anger, cold, mercury, onanism, and suppressed coryza. Food poisoning. Ill effects of eating fish, fruit, bad meat or fish, impure water, milk, tea, beer, beer, sour wine, or alcohol.

Limbs - Great debility, trembling with numbness of limbs. Pain in marrow. Decay of bones with profuse sweat. Sensation as of a string around limb. Pains in limbs and joints. Paralytic stiffness in all joints on rising after sleeping. Pain as if sprained, worse slight touch, hard pressure relieves. Averse to exercise, sensitive to touch. Weariness of joints, worse mornings and when sitting. Joints as if bruised, worse rest, better motion. Joints swollen, very sensitive with dread of open air. Twitching in knees. As if heavy load on shoulders. Spasmodic stretching of arms with clenched fingers. Hands tremble while writing. As of a band about legs or arms. Cold hands and feet. One hand is icy cold other is warm. Emaciation of hands and feet. Swelling of veins of the hands. Nails blue.

Sleep - Drowsiness. Overpowering sleepiness during day, when sitting and after eating. Heavy, snoring sleep, especially in children. Snoring, blowing expiration moaning, whining, during sleep. Protracted sleeplessness. Sleeplessness from an overactive mind. Sleeplessness from hunger. Sleeplessness frompressive pain in head. Waking from pains, noise and when feet get cold. Unrefreshing or constant stupor. Wakens early. Unre- freshed sleep, wakes confused. Dreamy kind of reverie as soon as he falls asleep. Anxious, or frightful dreams with confused consciousness on waking, so that the dream cannot be rid of and fear of dream remains.

Skin - Skin dry, flaccid. Waxy pale or yellow skin. Jaundice. Yellow color. Itching, bleeding after scratching. Cold and blue skin. Extreme sensitiveness to touch, but hard pressure relieves. One hand ice cold, the other warm. Coldness, with much sweat. Anasarca (Ars., Apis). Dermatitis, erysipelas. Indurated glands, scrofulous ulcers and decay. Psoriasis and ichthyosis. Pemphigus. Humid gangrene. Ulcers flat, shallow, copious discharge.

Modalities - Better from hard pressure. Better bending double. Better open air. Better warmth. Better loose clothes. Worse from jar. Worse slightest touch. Worse bending over. Worse during and after stool. Worse loss of vital fluids. Worse noise. Worse cold, winds, drafts, open air. Worse mental exertion. Worse after eating. Worse fruits, fish, milk. Worse impure water, spoiled meat. Worse tea, smoking. Worse at night, midnight. Worse increase of moon. Worse every other day, every fourteen days, every three months. Worse periodically. Worse from 1 a.m. to 10 a.m. Worse 12 p.m. or 1 p.m. Worse from 8 a.m. to 2 or 3 p.m. Worse in autumn, summer.

Teeth - Teeth loose and painful only when chewing. Black coating of teeth covered with dark sordes. Painful numbness in decayed teeth. Gums swollen. Toothache, better by pressing teeth firmly together and warmth. Toothache during sweat. Toothache while infant sucks the breast. Toothache with sweat. Pressure as if blood were forced into teeth. Throbbing pain, better external warmth.

Tongue - Burning stitches on tongue. Cracked, black or yellow coated tongue. Burning as from pepper on tip of tongue, followed by salivation. Tongue, thick, dirty coated. Painful swelling posteriorly on side of tongue. Tongue parched or raw as if burnt. Tongue dotted here and there with yellowish vesicles, some of them broken and looking sore. Vertigo - Vertigo, falls backwards. Dizzy when walking. Vertigoon waking at night. Vertigo can't sit upright. Head inclined to sink backward, wc rse motion and walking, better lying. Vertigo on waking at night. Vertigo from anemia. Vertigo on raising head. Vertigo after loss of vital fluids. Vertigo on rising as if he would fall backward. Vertigo in occiput, when sitting. Vertigo with heat in head, worse when lying. Vision - Shortsightedness after typhus, with diarrhea. Letters run together and look like black spots on a white ground. Vision better in morning. Sudden blindness with violent pain in occiput extending into eyes. Night blindness in anemic retina. Amaurosis, scalding lachrymation. Transient blindness, with flickering before eyes. Focal distance of eyes unequal for near and far points. Amblyopia in alcoholics. Amblyopia after masturbation, surging of blood to head. Black specks, bright dazzling illusions. Weakness of vision and neuralgia above eye. Dimness and weakness of vision, can only distinguish outlines of distant objects. Letters pale, surrounded by white borders. Flame of candle seems to be of a dazzling sulphur color. Sees spots. COMMENTS - Teste wrote, “According to Humboldt about 500,000 pounds of this bark are annually exported to Europe for the purpose of being converted into sulphate of quinine.” Well could Teste add the exclamation. “Poor patients !” As with almost every other good thing that comes into its hands, allopathy has contrived to do an infinity of harm with quinine to make up for the good. Ip. (as well as Gali, and Mit.) belongs to the same natural order of plants as Chin., and the relation of the two to intermittent fever, hemorrhages and gastro-enteric disturbances is very similar. Coff. also belongs to the Rubiacae and is nearly allied in many of its nervous symptoms to Chin. The tincture is anti-septic, destroying ameboid motion and retarding tissue change. It weakens the heart and impairs the circulation. Chin, helps with congestions and hemorrhages, anemia and complete relaxation and collapse. The result of suppression is thus sketched by Hahnemann's master-hand: “True, he (the patient) can no longer complain that the paroxysms of his original disease occurs any more on regular days and at regular hours, but behold his earthy complexion, his bloated countenance, his languishing looks ! “Behold how difficult it is for him to breathe, see his hard and distended abdomen the swelling of the hypochondria, see how his stomach is oppressed and pained by everything he eats, how his appetite is diminished, how his taste is altered, how loose his bowels are and how unnatural and contrary to what they should be, how his sleep is restless, unrefreshing and full of dreams. “Behold him weak, out of humor and prostrated, his sensibility morbidly excited, his intellectual faculties weakened, how much more does he suffer than when he was a prey to his fever ! “The number of patients who have been consigned to an early grave by quinine probably falls short only of the number that mercury can claim. When first introduced it was (as chloral and hundreds of other poisons have been since) declared on the highest authority to be incapable of harm “in whatever dose it may be taken.” Debility caused by an excessive drain of animal fluids, such as loss of blood, excessive suppuration, loss of semen, and after prolonged strain of overwork, mental or bodily. A “pumped-out” condition, and the sensitive, irritable state of mind that accompanies such. Never well since blood loss, surgery, loss of fluids, especially if the liver, the colon, or the digestive tract has shut down or been weakened since the blood loss. Hemorrhages occur from every orifice of the body. Rectal bleeding, nosebleeds, menstrual blood, birthing. Perspiration, dehydration from high fevers, from heat stroke. Loss of fluids from diarrhea, a history of dysentery or parasites with exhausting, debilitative diarrhea. Weakness from breast-feeding. Terrible irritability, always worse at night. Sense of unhappiness. Believes he is pursued by enemies in business. Intermittent fever from marsh miasm, tertian or quartan in type. Chill and heat without thirst, thirst occurring either before or after chill. Chill followed by long-lasting heat, generally with desire to uncover, face fiery red, often delirium, profuse and debilitating, followed by sweat. In the apyrexial period, the face is a sallow, dingy yellow, the spleen is enlarged and painful, the appetite is totally lost, or else there is canine hunger, the feet swell and as soon as the patient closes his eyes for sleep he sees figures. Typhoid and gastric fever. Hectic fever. Lung conditions which are attended with hectic. Suppuration of the lungs, especially in alcoholics. Weakening night-sweats. Prostration, chilly, wants to be wrapped up but cannot bear the fire. Periodicity in fever and in neuralgias. Characteristic worse every other day. Neuralgia is generally infra-orbital. Weak eyes and ringing in ears, such as follow depletion. Loss of sight, deafness, ringing in the ears. Humming, throbbing in ears. The nose, ears and chin are cold, complexion sallow, dingy, yellow. Headache, congestive, throbbing like many hammers hammering on temples, ringing in the ears, worse from drought of air, open air, slightest contact, better by hard pressure. Scalp sensitive. Asthma, wheezing, suffocative catarrh and paralysis of lungs in oldpeople. Respiration labored, loud and stertorous with puffing, blowing out of cheeks on each expiration. Rheumatism, characterized by soft swelling, pale red, very tender to touch. Great sensitiveness to touch. Flesh sore to touch. Even a current of air blowing on the part causes great pain (Plb.). Cannot get wide awake, head remains confused and stupid. Cannot get rid of dreams, even after waking the impression continues. Saliva found on the pillow in the morning. Thick, dirty yellow coating on tongue, bitter taste on waking. Aphthae of weakly people. Thirst for cold water. Everything tastes bitter, even water (everything except water, Aeon.). Canine hunger, especially at night. Hunger after meals with feeling of emptiness. If a meal is late, he is sure to suffer from it. Total loss of appetite. Craves spicy (Nux- v.) and wine. Full feeling after the least food, but belching only better temporarily. After eating, a lump under mid-stemum. Stomach so weak it cannot tolerate any food at all. Very sour stomach. Slow digestion. Diarrhea after fruit. Dyspepsia after loss of fluids. Nausea, worse on sitting up. Stomach sore to touch. Very flatulent. Guernsey described it as an uncomfortable distention of abdomen with a wish to belch up or a sensation as if the abdomen were packed full, not in the least better by eructation. Gastric troubles of children who are always wanting dainties, irritable on waking, bad taste, white tongue. Tympany coming on early in a case. Spleen aching, sore. Liver swollen, sensitive. Feeling of subcutaneous ulceration. Gallstone colic, duodenal, catarrh, jaundice. Fermentation in bowels, frothy, sour diarrhea. Yellow, watery, undigested diarrhea, with much flatus and no pain. Diarrhea of dark inky fluid, stools frequent at night, only after food during the day. Useful in cases where purgatives have been abused (Nux-v.). Excessive seminal losses. Menorrhagia, metrorrhagia, post-partum hemorrhage. Leucorrhea before period, painful pressure towards groins and anus, fetid or bloody leucorrhea before period with contractions in inner parts. Koch and others have attributed the hematuria of African intermittents to quinine. Hering said Chin, is useful after abuse of chamomile tea when hemorrhage from uterus results. Nash cured a case of acute rheumatism with Chin, on the modality “worse every other day.” E. Carleton related the cure of a case of spasm of the glottis in a middle-aged man. Sudden attacks. 3 a.m., suffocation seemed imminent. At length with one tremendous effort, while sitting bent forward, a little air would be forced into the lungs in spite of the epiglottis with a noise audible at a distance. After each succeeding expiration the inspiration would become less difficult. Chin. 200c cured. A. Villers cured with Chin. 30c a girl, 20, who, after a chill, had a pain in her right hip worse by every movement and which she could only describe as being like the pain in the legs which occurred before the menses. She was pale and had much hard nursing work. The menses were scanty and she was weak. Three days after taking Chin., the pain was gone after having persisted for five months. Clarke removed with Chin, the dropsy and relieved all the other symptoms of a case of cirrhosis of the liver in a hard drinker. He remained at his work for many months, but in the end, his old habits proved too much for him and he died from an acute illness following a cold. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Ferr., Ars., Nairn., Carb-v., Aran., Eup-per., Ip., Merc., Nux- v., Puls., Rhus, Sep., Sulph.. Verat. Antidote to: Ars., Calc., Cham., Coff., Ferr., Hell., lod., Merc., Sulph., Verat. Is useful in bad effects of tea-drinking and after abuse of chamomile tea, with uterine hemorrhage. Compare: (1) Are. - prostration without pain, black stools. (2) Carb-v. - flatulence, diarrhea, great weakness, Chin, stool is caused by every attempt to eat and drink. (3) Coloc. - beer intoxicates easily. (4) Cedr., Caps., Cupr-ac. - black, thin stools. (5) Psor. - rapid exhaustion following acute diseases, Psor. has despair of recovery. (6) Puls. - bitter taste, worse eating at night. (7) Meniere's disease, Sal-ac. (8) Ph-ac. - li- entery, seminal emissions, diarrhea, but this China officinalis does not exhaust with Ph-ac. (9) worse from brandy - Are., Carb-v., Nux-v. (10) diarrhea immediately after eating - Are., Aloe., Lyc., Podo., Staph.,Trom. (ll)hepatitis with great tenderness - Phos., Aeon., Are., Lyc. (12) Cephalanthus - intermittent fever, sore throat, rheumatic symptoms, vivid dreams. (14) Are., Cedr., Nat-s. Complementary: Ferr., Calc-p. Incompatible: after Dig., Sei. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Liver - Liver and spleen swollen and enlarged. Gallstone colic. Gallstones. Obstruction in gallbladder with colic, periodic recurrence, yellow skin and conjunctiva, constipation. Worse since gallbladder removed. Jaundice after leucorrhea, masturbation, sexual excess, diarrhea. Hepatitis with exhaustion. Swelling and induration of liver. Periodical liver symptoms. Cirrhosis and edema. Liver weakness due to alcohol orpoordiet. Pain in hepatic region, as from subcutaneous ulceration, very sensitive to touch. Lungs - Asthma, worse damp weather, autumn or after depletion. Wheezing, whistling inspiration, crowing, rattling, oppressed and painful breathing. Asphyxia of newborn, after great loss of blood by the mother. Dyspnea, sharp pain in left lung. Cannot breathe with head low. Suffocative catarrh, rattling in lungs. Puffy, rattling, breathing. Every motion excites palpitation and takes his breath. Inclination to take a deep breath. Wants to be fanned but not too hard, for it takes her breath. Rattling in lungs, loud sounds through nose. Pneumonia after hemorrhages or with bilious symptoms. Pneumonia, and other lung affections, symptoms being worse every other day. Pleurisy in persons who have lost much blood. Pleuro-pneumonia with profuse exudation, prostration, emaciation and pallor during confinement. Suppurative tuberculosis. Tuberculosis in alcoholics. Hemoptysis. Hemorrhage from lungs. Asphyxia of newborn due to great blood loss by the mother.

Kidneys - Sharp pains across kidneys, worse movement and at night. Burning at meatus, worse rubbing of clothes. Urine turbid, dark, scanty. Pinkish sediment. Hematuria. Bedwetting of weakly children. Pressure in bladder follows frequent and ineffectual efforts to urinate. Frequent urination with pressure in bladder. Urine turbid, dark, scanty. Urine pale, becoming cloudy or depositing a dingy, yellow, loose sediment. Scanty, greenish-yellow, brickdust sediment. Albuminuria. Diabetes.

Cough - Asthmatic cough, at 3 a.m., followed by frothy, badly tasting expectoration. Violent, hacking cough after every meal. Paroxysms, after eating or laughing, worse evening, night. Spasmodic coughs from irritation of larynx. Spasmodic coughs as from fumes of sulphur, at night and in mornings. Spasmodic coughs with bilious vomit. Cough causes cutting pain in lower abdomen, expectoration difficult, black. Cough with pain in larynx and sternum. Cough with pain throughout whole cavity of chest. Dry cough, with taste of blood. Cough during or after measles. Coughs worse talking, lying with head low or on left side. Cough worse lightly touching larynx. Coughs from draft of air, loss of fluids. Cough from laughing. Cough after eating, drinking.

Perspiration - Debilitating night sweats. Debilitating sweats from weakness, depletions. Profuse sweats, caused by every little exertion. Profuse sweat during sleep, or on being covered up. Drenching sweats, at night, worse least motion. Greasy oroily sweat on side lain on. Cold and clammy sweat with hemorrhages. Copious sweat, exhausting, at night. Suppressed sweat. Debilitating sweatsfrom malaria, fevers. Sweats after waking at 3 a.m., with thirst. Sweats on face and hands. Sweats on side lain on. Sweats after meals.

Temperature - Chills on alternate days. Chill, then thirst, then fever, then thirst. Chill generally in forenoon. Chill alternating with fever, in afternoon. Chill begins in the breast. Internal chills, violent, with icy cold hands and feet, and congestion of blood to head. Chills with headache, congestion of head, paleness of face, pain in liver. Can't get warm in evening in bed. Influenza with debility. Malaria. Stages of chill, heat and sweat well marked. Intermittent fever. Typhoid and gastric fever. Periodic fever and chils. Fever returns every week. Hectic fever. Tropicalfevers. Sepsis. Red hot face, with cold hands with cold body. General heat with distended veins. Fever with dryness of mouth and lips.

name: Chininum Arsenicosum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better by motion (vertigo). Better by eating (gastralgia). Better yawning. Better pressure. Better bending forwards. Better open air. Better sitting up. Worse rest, morning, forenoon. Worse when stomach is empty. Worse looking up. Worse motion. Worse on ascending..

Intermittent, fever. Keratitis. Malaria. Nausea. Neuralgias. Ophthalmia. Palpitations. Prostration. Rheumatism. Scarlatina. Sleeplessness. Sorethroat, malignant. Spinal, irritation. Syphilis. Tobacco, effects. Tuberculosi

full:
PHARMACY - chin-ar. Chininum arsenicosum. Quinine arsenite. Trituration or solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Anorexia. Asthma. Bright's disease. Chills. Coryza. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dyspnea. Epilepsy. Fever. Gastralgia. Headache. Hectic fever. Hemicrania. Hyperacidity. Intermittent, fever. Keratitis. Malaria. Nausea. Neuralgias. Ophthalmia. Palpitations. Prostration. Rheumatism. Scarlatina. Sleeplessness. Sorethroat, malignant. Spinal, irritation. Syphilis. Tobacco, effects. Tuberculosis. Vertigo. Vomiting. Weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - This is one of the salts of Chin, that combines the Chin, physical symptoms and Ars. mental symptoms. The Arsenite of Quinine combines many of the properties of its components, but having been proved, it can be treated as a separate medicine. Useful in diphtheria with great prostration, especially cases that are prolonged, and in malarial affections, neuralgia, etc. Weariness and prostration, useful as a general tonic, often with very marked beneficial and prompt effect. Continuous fever with oscillating temperature. Profuse, exhaustive sweat, at night. Stomach pain, pressure in solar plexus with tender spine just at back of it. Hyperacidity alternating with decrease of acidity. Anorexia. Eggs and fish produce diarrhea. Nausea and vomiting, followed by sleep. Sleeplessness due to nervous causes. Periodic asthmatic attacks with great prostration. Shortness of breath on ascend- ing. Palpitations. Sensation as if heart had stopped. Icy skin. Coldness of hands and feet, knees and limbs. The periodicity is intensified and this is especially noted in the neuralgias. An irritable mood precedes the headache, which is worse by mental and bodily exercise. MIND - Great anxiety and nightly delirium. Anxiety, with unquenchable thirst, must sit up bent forward, if possible at open window. Fears at night. Fear of evil. Fear of ghosts. Child sits up when lamenting. Prostration and disinclinationformentalwork. Believes he can't long endure such utter prostration. Weakness and weariness. Desire to sit or lie in one place and not be disturbed. Great irritability. Irritability precedes headache. Censorious with friends. Depressed spirits, wishes to be quiet and let alone. Thinking of complaints aggravates, chills brought on by thinking of them. Mental dullness with inclination to vomit. Memory impaired. Hemicrania from fright.

Head - Headache, worse mental and physical exertion. Tired feeling. Head feels too full. Throbbing. Dull, heavy headache, frontal and occipital. Darting pains running up into head. Bruised feeling all over head after fever and sleep. Hemicrania from fright, physical and mental exertion. Periodical headache in occiput, from noise or excitement. Neuralgic headache, in right temple and above eye. Furuncles and abscesses which relieve head.

Eyes - Flickering with pain and lachrymation. Keratitis. Intense photophobia and spasms of orbital muscles, gushing of hot tears. Scrofulous ophthalmia, worse after midnight.

Ears - Ringing in ears like bells, with congestion towards head. Noise in ears and dullness of hearing.

Nose - Profuse coryza, better erect position and out of doors. Post-nasal catarrh, worse left side. Copious nosebleed. Fluent coryza, profuse limpid and watery discharge. Nose stopped up with a purulent and bloody substance, diphtheria. Corners of nose excoriated, diphtheria. Yellow Chinum arsenicosum discharge. Left nostril fills up when lying on that side. Nose clearer when in an erect posture and in open air.

Face - Pale, sallow and bloated face, intermittent fever. Trembling of facial muscles, especially orbicularis palpebrum. Swelling of submaxillary and parotid glands, in diphtheria. Dull pain in left temporal region at articulation of lower jaw. Face pale, sallow bloated. Blueness of lips, in tuberculosis. Food - Anorexia. Appetite gone. Ravenous appetite. Aversion to meat. Desire for sweets. Indigestion from unripe fruit. Eggs or fish cause painless diarrhea at once. Gastralgia from ill-baked bread. Diarrhea after eating. Violent thirst for cold water, yet it disturbs. No thirst with fever. Aversion to cold water, during rheumatic headache. Water tastes bitter.

Mouth - Burning canker spot on inside of left upper lip. Fetid breath, in diphtheria and scarlatina. Tongue thickly furred. Yellow, slimy coating on tongue. Dryness in roof of mouth, gnawing and nausea. Sweetish taste after clearing throat and coughing. Metallic bitter taste in mouth. Tongue black, sore and swollen. Tongue coated thick and brown, diphtheria. Soreness and redness of tip of tongue.

Throat - Throat feels sore and raw, worse coughing and sneezing. Constant hacking and clearing of throat. Malignant angina during scarlatina, with paleness of skin, and exhaustion. Hoarseness, with diphtheria. Diphtheria with great fetor oris, submaxillary glands swollen and painful. Tonsils covered with a grey exudation. Swallowing of liquids very difficult. Vertigo - Sudden attacks of vertigo. V ertigo is worse looking up. COMMENTS - Bonino, who gave it aprolonged proving, found the chief effects were manifested on the stomach, solar plexus, ligaments and skin. According to him, it corresponds to tobacco intoxication and its effects, indigestion from unripe fruits, and stomach pain from coarse food or ill-baked bread. Marked weakness, prostration and disinclination for mental exertion. Effects of severe and depressing influences on the mind to convalescence from long-lasting sickness. Slow circulation, relaxed limbs. Chronic rheumatism of the joints without swelling. Tertiary syphilis of periosteum. Colic from incarcerated flatus intermittent fever with predominating chills. Little thirst and continuous almost convulsive yawning. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Chin., also Ferr- citric. in nephritis with great anemia, acid dyspepsia in chlorosis. (2) Chin-m. - in severe neuralgic pains around eyes with chills, exaggerated sensitiveness to alcohol and tobacco, prostration and restlessness. (3) Enothera - effortless diarrhea with nervous exhaustion incipient hydrocephaloid. (4) Macrozamia spiralis - extreme debility after illness, collapse. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Stomach - Burning, sore feeling in stomach, worse motion, going up stairs, better expanding chest. Hyperacidity (Rob., Arg-n.). Alternation of hyperacidity and decrease of acid. Sour bitter eructations. Regurgitation of food. Hiccough and belching, followed by urging to stool. Empty sensation. Nausea with waning strength, especially of lower limbs. Nausea and vomiting followed by sleep. Sensation from stomach through entire intestinal canal as if diarrhea would set in. Nausea and vomiting, followed by sleep, with hemicrania.

Abdomen - Paininepigastrium,as from foul stomach. Pain as from flatus wedged into flexure of colon. Pressure in solar plexus. Aching around navel and in ilium. Colic from incarceratedflatus. Severe colicky pains in evening, better by pressure. Soreness, in a small spot, below and to right of umbilicus. Distension and rumbling in abdomen. Left hypochondriac region enlarged. Abdomen bloated, in intermittent fever.

Rectum - Burning in anus after stool. Violent urging to stool. Diarrhea, in the morning, hardly had time to dress. Bad-smelling flatus. Diarrhea at night and after eating. Diarrhea from malaria. Stools thin, watery, offensive, with pain in bowels. Stool pappy, watery, fetid. Stool thin, brown, painless. Stool with mucus and blood, preceded and followed by tenesmus. Brown, liquid jelly-like lumps.

Male - Peculiar burning ache about bladder sphincter and throughout urethra.

Chest - Severe stitching pains in chest, later in précordia, worse on inspiration. Tightening sensation in mediastinum, in front at left of breastbone. Intercostal neuralgia. Aching in intercostal muscles, right side. Peculiar pain, dull with pressure, as if caused by flatulence, coming and going rapidly. Chest as if hollow or full. Paralysis of respiratory muscles on left side.

Heart - Cardiac dyspnea, circulatory weakness after acute infections, early myocardial degeneration. Short of breath on ascending, cardiac dyspnea. Palpitations. Sensation as if heart stopped. Suffocative attacks, occurring in periodical paroxysms. Must have open air. Circulatory weakness after acute infections, early myocardial degeneration. Trembling of heart, palpitations, on leaning against back. Pulse small, very frequent. Pulse irregular. Pulse can't be felt on left side.

Back - Pain in muscles between left shoulder and neck, as if sprained, on rising from sleep, 4 p.m. Back feels weak as after a long journey. Causations - Ill effects of tobacco. Fright. Eggs and fish produce diarrhea.

Limbs - Weak limbs. Coldness of limbs. Tearing pains. Pain in left wrist, stiffness of left arm. Pain of fatigue in right wrist. Burning pain as in periosteum of left elbow. Annoying feeling of fatigue in right shoulder. Sore, tired aching in joints, bones and muscles. Tearing pains. Coldness of hands and feet, knees and limbs. Limbs icy cold, tuberculosis. Lungs - Periodic asthma attacks, with great prostration. Asthmatic breathing on ascending. Dyspnea on ascending. Suffocative attacks beginning in morning and lasting till noon. Must sit bent forward and, if possible, at an open window during attack of suffocation, worse any otherposi- tion. Breathing unsatisfactory, wants more air than can take into his lungs. Respiration very free, as if thorax were hollow. Bronchial catarrh with periodical fever, worse at night. Cough with little expectoration. Slight cough, at long intervals, seems to come from full feeling in chest. Dyspnea with anxiety, in tuberculosis.

Sleep - Sleeplessness due to nervous causes. Deep sleep after suffocative attacks. Goes to sleep after tea and sleeps heavily all night. Sleep frequently interrupted. Restless sleep. Restless until 3 a.m., constantly changing position, particularly as soon as pillow becomes warm. Awakes from sleep exhausted and bathed in sweat after attack of dyspnea. Nervous restlessness, anxious dreams. Night full of visions, heavy sleep till morning.

Skin - Goose bumps, especially of lower extremities. Dry skin, pallor of skin, with rapid exhaustion. Periodical furuncles and abscesses. Burning, erysipelatous redness and violent itching, worse by warmth, better by cold.

Modalities - Better by motion (vertigo). Better by eating (gastralgia). Better yawning. Better pressure. Better bending forwards. Better open air. Better sitting up. Worse rest, morning, forenoon. Worse when stomach is empty. Worse looking up. Worse motion. Worse on ascending.

Kidneys - Frequent, tiresome urging. Spasmodic retention of urine, better application of hot cloths to chest. Urine scanty or increased.

Perspiration - Cold, clammy sweat. No sweat after fever, but weak, broken-up feeling in morning and no appetite for breakfast. Cold, clammy sweat, all over. Cold sweat after epileptic attack.

Temperature - General chill and cold. Chill comes in waves in evening, with Chinum arsenicosum restlessness, gooseflesh, worse moving hands and feet to a cool place in bed, also on motion, and by thinking of it. After the feverish cough in the chill, no reaction of warmth. Heat with nausea. Continuous fever with weakness. After chill, fever toward midnight, pulse full and strong, with inclination to throw off covers.

name: Chininum Muriaticum
author: Murphy
constitution: Alcoholism. Eyes, neuralgia. Gastritis. Headaches. Intermittents. Iritis. Keratitis. Neuralgia. Pannus. Sclerotitis. Tobacco, effects. Trachoma.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Eyes, neuralgia. Gastritis. Headaches. Intermittents. Iritis. Keratitis. Neuralgia. Pannus. Sclerotitis. Tobacco, effects.…

PHARMACY - chin-m. Chininummuriaticum. Quinine muriate. Trituration or solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Eyes, neuralgia. Gastritis. Headaches. Intermittents. Iritis. Keratitis. Neuralgia. Pannus. Sclerotitis. Tobacco, effects. Trachoma.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chin-m. resembles Chin-ar. very closely. An excellent proving by old-school authorities was published in Virchow's Archives. Chin-m. has been used for eye affections, especially when accompanied by severe intermitting neuralgic pains in and around the eyes. Eye affections with chills. Lachrymation. Photophobia. Ulceration of cornea of malarial origin. Intermittent fever following bronchopneumonia, shaking chill 5 a.m. accompanied by fatiguing cough, rattling in bronchi without expectoration. In one prover it caused an exaggerated sensitiveness to alcohol and tobacco. Two glasses of beer make him tipsy. Prostration and weakness are marked in all provers and accompany the headaches and other symptoms. Feeling of enlargement in eyeballs in tongue, head symptoms are better after a walk. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Ferr-o-r. Compare: (1) Chin-s., Chin-a. (2) Nat-m. - headaches. REFERENCES - Clarke.

author: Murphy
constitution: Ear, disorders. Deafness. Hearing, impaired. Meniere's disease. Tinnitus.

CLINICAL - Ear, disorders. Deafness. Hearing, impaired. Meniere's disease. Tinnitus.

HOMEOPATHIC - Cozzolino stated “Of all the preparations of Quinine the Salicylate is the most injurious to the structures of the internal ear and, therefore in all likelihood, the most powerful homeopathic curative.” REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Chininum Sulphuricum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from yawning. Better pressure. Better bending forwards. Worse from exact periodicity (Cedr.). Worse 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. Worse touch, cold. Motion causes chilliness. Stooping causes giddiness..
constitution: Angina pectoris. Anorexia. Asthma. Black-water, fever. Brow, ague. Cachexia. Cancerous, ulcers. Cholera. Concussion. Deafness. Delirium. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Ear, disorders. Gangrenous, suppurations. Gravel. Headaches. Hearing, impaired. Hematuria. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Intermittent, fever. Malaria. Meniere's disease. Nephritis. Neuralgia. Noises, in head. Parotiditis. Pr

PHARMACY - chin-s. Chininum sulphuricum. Quinine sulphate. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Anorexia. Asthma. Black-water, fever. Brow, ague. Cachexia. Cancerous, ulcers. Cholera. Concussion. Deafness. Delirium. Diarrhea.…
full:
PHARMACY - chin-s. Chininum sulphuricum. Quinine sulphate. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Anorexia. Asthma. Black-water, fever. Brow, ague. Cachexia. Cancerous, ulcers. Cholera. Concussion. Deafness. Delirium. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Ear, disorders. Gangrenous, suppurations. Gravel. Headaches. Hearing, impaired. Hematuria. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Intermittent, fever. Malaria. Meniere's disease. Nephritis. Neuralgia. Noises, in head. Parotiditis. Pruritus vulva. Puerperal, convulsions. Pyemia. Rectum, prolapsed. Remittent, fever. Rheumatism. Scarlatina. Spinal, irritation. Spleen, enlarged. Tinnitus. Typhus, fever. Urticaria. Varicose, veins. Variola.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chin-s. closely resembles Chin, in its effects, but as it has been proved separately and as observations of the effects of over-dosing have supplied many additional symptoms, there is plenty of guidance in the selection of one in preference to the other. In old-school practice, the Sulphate of Quinine has almost entirely taken the place of the crude bark as a remedy. A dose of Chin-s. in high potency sometimes arouses suppressed malaria and brings back the paroxysm. Aside from its undoubted influence over malaria, it is indicated whenever there is a marked periodicity and spinal sensitiveness. Chin-s. acts on the nerves causing great sensitiveness to external influences. Perin odical neuralgia (Cedr.). Tinnitus. Violent ringing, buzzing and roaring in ears. Deafness. Tinkling in the ears. Meniere’s disease. Buzzing, especially in left ear, sometimes occasioning deafness on that side. Hardness of hearing, sometimes with violent headache. Rapid decrease of red blood cells and reduction of hemoglobin with tendency to leucocytosis. Thready vessels. Weak and nervous, little exertion causes palpitations. Inability to remain standing. Falling in street. Wants to lie down. Deathly sick and faint, felt as if she would sink through bed. Acute Joint rheumatism. Gout. Itching and congested conditions of the rectum. Symptoms of chronic interstitial nephritis. Retro-bulbar neuritis with sudden loss of sight. Hiccough. MIND - Memory weak, thoughts not clear. Indolence on waking in morning. Indolence with lassitude. Indifference, stupid expression, vacant stare, aversion to answering questions. Discouragement, inclination tocry. Slowness of reflection. Lost power of naming objects. Speechless. Despair. Melancholy. Morose, depression and ill-humor. Anxiety with fear. Anxiety about future. Nervous. Fits of anxiety. Fear of impending evil. Great anguish. Fear of misfortune. Loud sobbing and weeping. Buoyancy, excited state, later despondency. Clearness of mind, abundant ideas, at night. Making many plans in evening. Semiconsciousness, partly insensible to pain. Decrease of imaginative faculty with inability to remain standing. Delirium during fever. Delirium with great restlessness, followed by stupor in morning. Delirium with humming in ears. Delirium with screaming andjumping out of bed. Delirium all night while lying quietly on back. Delirium as if from intoxication.

Head - Confusion feeling in head. Intermittent neuralgia at regular hours. Dull headache with debility or numbness. Violent headache, throbbing, pressive, or tearing pains in forehead and temples. Violent throbbing, with vertigo and heat in face and prostration. Beating, throbbing in vertex. Pain in forehead and temples, increasing gradually at noon, of malarial origin, with vertigo and pulsation, worse left side. Head as if enlarged. Sensitiveness and tightness of scalp. Soreness of roots of hair.

Eyes - Dryness of eyes. Eyes staring and lustreless. Eyes close from weariness. Conjunctiva injected. Lachrymation and conjunctivitis. Squint on alternating days (children). Sensibility of the eyes with lachrymation. Extreme photophobia. Violent stitching, throbbing pains. Orbital neuralgia. Pupils dilated or contracted. Twitching of eyelids. Lids red and swollen. Disc and retina very anemic.

Ears - Meniere's disease. Noises in ears, worse during a chill. Noises in ears, worse during vertigo. Violent ringing, buzzing and roaring in ears. Tinkling in the ears. Tinnitus. Deafness. Deafness from concussion of brain. Hardness of hearing, sometimes with violent headache. Buzzing, especially in left ear, sometimes occasioning deafness on that side.

Nose - Frequent bleeding at the nose. Severe nosebleed in young people. Frequent sneezing.

Face - Flushed face. Redness of the face. Heat of the face. Pale anxious face. Earthcolored face. Dull and stupid expression. Complexion yellow. Sickly look, air of suffering with sunken eyes. Neuralgia under eye. Neuralgia pains return with great regularity, better by pressure. Brow ague. Bluish-colored lips. Eruption on the upper lip.

Mouth - Aphthae in weakly persons. Dryness with heat, thirst. Sensation of constriction in the mouth. Great paleness of the buccal cavity. Erosion of the gums. Accumulation of mucus in the mouth. Saliva increased. Nocturnal angina. Taste pasty, flat or bitter. Speech disturbed or difficult.

Throat - Pains in the throat. Burning in the throat. Tickling in the larynx. Scraping in the throat. Sensation of dryness in the pit of the throat. Feeling as though a foreign body were lodged there.

Stomach - Dyspepsia or heartburn, with nausea, loathing of food, eructations, bitter taste, vomiting of bile. Heartburn or burning in stomach and esophagus, and feeling of constriction and pulling sensation. Cramp in the stomach. Fullness in the stomach, and tension of the abdomen. Risings after a meal. Bitter hiccough and retching. Nausea with risings. Nausea, with inclination to vomit. Vomiting during an intermittent fever. Pressure, heat in the stomach.

Abdomen - Distension of abdomen, with much rumbling and discharge of flatus. Flatulent colic of an intermittent type. Movement in the abdomen and emission of wind, after a meal, with violent risings. Pain in region ofliver and spleen on bending, taking a deep breath, or coughing. Violent cutting, colicky pains in region of transverse colon, after eating. Pains in liver shortly before going to bed. Dull pain in region of spleen, disappearing on pressure. Painful enlargement of spleen after intermittent fever. StiuAies'vn spleen.

Rectum - Obstinate constipation. Constipation or soft stools, followed by weakness. Dysentery. Diarrhea. Evacuations exhale a gangrenous odor. Stools are white and pap- like. Stools hard, insufficient, indolent, sometimes in small fragments. Nightly diarrhea. Urgent inclination to evacuate. Involuntary stools. Many stools during the day. Hemorrhoids.

Male - Suppression or diminution of sexual desire. Forcing pain in the direction of the groins.

Female - Passive metrorrhagia, with diminished irritability. Violent uterine contractions sufficient to produce miscarriage. Labor pains appearing like tonic spasms. Labor pains with convulsive twitches, unconsciousness after childbirth. Violent uterine neuralgia, returning at same hour every afternoon, worse after confinement. Food - Want of appetite, for many days. Anorexia. Indifference for food and drink. Hungry at night. Bulimia, sometimes at night. Hunger with faintness, as from fasting. Excessive repugnance to all food. Disagreeable taste of food. Bread appears bitter. Thirst, mostly only during sweat. Thirst during chill and apyrexia.

Chest - Oppression of chest, can scarcely breathe from weakness. Pain across the chest. Painful sense of pressure and weight on chest. Pressure on the left side of the chest. Intercostal neuralgia.

Heart - Precordial anxiety. Palpitations. Palpitation from slight exertion. Angina pectoris with marasmus. Heart weak and feeble, with prostration. Pulse full and large. Pulse weak, trembling, scarcely perceptible.

Back - Periodical pains in back. Periodical cervical neuralgia. Cervical, dorsal spine aches or very tender with oppression of breath. Spine, great sensitiveness of the dorsal vertebrae, pain on pressure. Spine painful on pressure in all stages of fever paroxysm. Last cervical sensitive. Pain extends to head and neck.

Limbs - Acute joint rheumatism. Joints very sensitive. Heaviness and aching in all limbs andjoints. Paralysis of the limbs. Weakness, trembling of the limbs. Cracking of the shoulder joint. Tearings in the legs. Painful sensitiveness in the malleoli. Edematous swelling of the feet. Lungs - Increased breathing. Slow, irregular breathing. [11] Dyspnea and anxiety with intercostal pain. Accelerated breathing, with abnormal rising and falling of thorax. Tickling at bifurcation of trachea. Irritation in the throat. Violent cough during the day. Dry, loose cough. Cough caused by a small, painful spot in the throat. On coughing, expectoration of gelatinous mucus. Hemorrhage from lungs with diarrhea, fever, cold sweat and prostration.

Sleep - Frequent yawning. Drowsiness during the day. Sleep profound and unrefreshing. Agitated, with debilitating sweats, tossings. Insomnia from fever and chills. Sleeplessness from overstimulation of nervous system. Extravagant dreams.

Skin - Itching, erythema. Jaundice. Vesication, pustules, purpura. Skin is flaccid or Chininum sulphuricum sensitive to the touch. Shrivelled skin. Petechiae. Urticaria. Red rash over whole body with severe stinging, followed by desquamation. Sudamina and red spots. Gangrenous inflammations. Formation of a thick scurf.

Modalities - Better from yawning. Better pressure. Better bending forwards. Worse from exact periodicity (Cedr.). Worse 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. Worse touch, cold. Motion causes chilliness. Stooping causes giddiness.

Tongue - Bitter taste with clean tongue. Tongue white. Tongue thick yellow fur. Tongue yellow at root. Tongue white or yellow in centre, pale at margin. Dryness of tongue. Vertigo-Vertigo with tinnitus. Vertigowith twitching of the eyelids, and throbbing headache. Vertigo on stooping. Whirling, as if the head were falling backwards. As if intoxicated with buzzing in the ear and giddiness. Falling in street, inability to remain standing. Vision - Can see objects only when looking sideways. Transient amaurosis. Amaurosis. Sparks before the eyes. Sight dimmed as by a fog with dryness of the eyes. Black spots. Obscuration of the sight, when booking Exeûïy aï an object. COMMENTS - Chin-s. is even more powerful as an anti-septic than Chin., and it is probable that it is in virtue of its property of antagonizing the malarial poison that it suppresses intermittent fever when it does not cure. It only cures when the fever corresponds to its own type. “Black-water fever” has been developed by Chin-s. in intermittents. Koch deserves much credit for showing that the worst features of African fevers are due to over-dosing with Quinine and not to the disease. When a fever is “suppressed” there is generally an unholy alliance between diseaseforce and drug-force, which is expended on some part of the organism, resulting at times in lifelong ill-health. The “Quinine cachexia” is well-known, including a sallow complexion, emaciation, deafness and singing in the ears, enlarged spleen, disposition to shiver and great debility. Extremely well marked intermittents, the attacks returning at the same hour each day. The onset may anticipate. Great sensitiveness to external influences. Sleeplessness and over-stimulation of nervous system. Skin flaccid and sensitive to touch. Red rash over whole body with severe stinging, followed by desquamation. Twitching of left eyelid, worse in the evening. Aphthae in weakly people. Tartar on teeth. Debilitating discharges. Weak and nervous, a little exercise causes sweat from least exertion. Head gradually breaks into sweat when perfectly quiet. Headache extending from occiput to forehead. Whirling in the head like a mill-wheel. Hunger at night. Prolapsed rectum, especially in children. Hematuria and hemoglobinuria. Arrhythmia. Palpitations. Pain fit/ness and swelling of varicose veins during a chill. Julius E. Schmitt cured a case on this last indication. E. W. Sawyer related this instructive history. He learned from his cook that her brother (age 16), could not take a particle of quinine without causing a profuse flow of blood with the urine, sometimes within halt anhoMï, ai'oa^'s'AtaVpai'a.Trástai followed every time his doctors had tried to break his ague with quinine. A year later a farmer's wife, age 60, came to Dr. Sawyer to be treated for bloody urine unattended with pain or uneasiness. She attributed it to strain from walking two miles on a slippery road. She had been for months under Hygienic treatment without benefit and was alarmingly weak from loss of blood. Rhus-t. 200c, Ham. lx. Erig. lx, Chin, lx, Ferr-m. 2x were given in succession in vain. At last, calling to mind the case of the youth, he gave Chin-s. in 1/16 grains doses three times a day and a prompt cure was effected. Tyrrell had a patient in whom in any potency it caused her to become “deathly sick and faint, thought she would die, could not raise her head, felt she would sink through the bed.” Sinking sensation. Sac-alb. produced in her the same symptoms and she accused the doctor of having given her quinine (Ars. has “sinking sensation, as if bed had gone from under her and she had alighted on the floor.” Bell., Dulc., Rhus-t., Lach., have “sinking through the bed.”). RELATIONS - Antidotes: Parthenum, Nairn., Lach., Am., Puls. Compare: (1) Chin., Chin-sal. - deafness, tinnitus and Meniere's disease. (2) Ars., Eupat., Methyl blue. (3) Camph-br. is said to intensify the action of Quinine and render it more permanent. (4) Baja, an East Indian drug, said to be almost infallible in intermittent fever, quartan type, pulsating headache injected eyes, flushed face. Liver and spleen enlarged. Edema. (5) Also Pambotano, a Mexican remedy for intermittent and tropical fevers. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Kidneys - Burning in urethra during urination. Small amount of urea and phosphoric acid with excess or uric acid and abundance of chlorides. Excessive flow. Albuminuria. Deposit of straw yellow, granular or brick red sediment. Diminution of urine. Frothy urine. Sediment yellowish-white of a strong odor. Brick-dust sediment. Gravel. Profuse hemorrhage. Urine, bloody, turbid, slimy, clay-colored, greasy sediment. Hematuria and hemoglobinuria.

Blood - An immediate and rapid decrease in red blood cells and reduction in hemoglobin with increase in elimination of chlorides. Tendency to polynucleated leucocytosis.

Perspiration - Profuse sweat, worse but exhausts. Sweats with thirst. Sweats profuse, even while quiet. Sweats improves all symptoms but headache, which is aggravated. Sweats coming on gradually after heat. Sweats on least motion. Sweats in mornings in bed. Profuse, exhausting sweats with nightly diarrhea. Profuse sweat on back and neck, during sleep.

Temperature - Malaria. Anticipating chills. Subnormal temperature. Painful swelling of veins during a chill. Shivering even in a warm room. Chill daily at 3 p.m. Clear apy- rexia. Delirium during fever. Increasing fever and prostration with profuse night sweats. Thirst in all stages. Anguish with fever and chills. Stages of chill, fever and sweat well marked and distinct. Tertian or quartan fever with trembling of limbs, pain in spleen, spine sensitive, face pale, thirst, lips blue, ringing in ears. Typhus with great prostration.

full:
PHARMACY - chion. Chionanthus virginica. Fringe-tree bark. Chionanthus americana. N. O. Oleacee. The bark, which is the part employed, contains Saponin. Tincture.Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cholecystitis. Constipation. Debility. Diabetes. Emaciation. Gallstone, colic. Gallstones. Headaches. Jaundice. Liver, diseases. Malaria. Migraines. Neurasthenia. Nursing women, complaints. Pancreatic, disease.

HERBAL - Chionanthus is useful for neurasthenia, periodical, sick, menstrual or bilious headaches. It has a powerful action on the Ever and on the head. Taken for several weeks, in drop doses, will often break up the sick headache habit. Pain in the forehead, chiefly over eyes. Eyeballs very painful with pressure over root of nose.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chion. acts powerfully on the liver and is indicated in hypertrophy, obstructed liver in malaria districts. Enlarged liver, constipation, clay-colored stool with jaundice and high-colored urine. Liver region sore. Liver derangement. Gallstones (Berb., Cholest., Calc.). Chronic jaundice. Jaundice, recurring every summer. Jaundice with arrest of menses. Enlarged spleen (Cean.). Diabetes mel- litus. Paroxysmal, abdominal pain. Bruise, soreness is felt in various organs, liver, eyeballs etc. Pains ascend upwards from forehead, stomach etc. Sensation of contraction of stomach as if something alive moving in it with uneasy sensation in liver and spleen. Rheumatic pains in left ankle and tarsal bone. MIND - Listless, apathetic. Feels worn out. No desire to do anything. Wants to be let alone. Hypochondriacal, inclined to look on the dark side.

Head - Severe bilious, sick headaches, worse stooping, motion, jarring. Dull frontal headache, over root of nose, over eyes, through temples. Feels sore and bruised. Heavy, dull feeling in forehead. Forehead very hot and dry. Perspiration on head during fever, while asleep.

Eyes - Eyeballs feel bruised and sore. Yellow conjunctiva. Whites of eyes have a yellowish cast all over. Blood vessels of sclerotic very much enlarged.

Nose - Pressing at the root of nose or squeezing on bridge. Drawing or pressing at root of nose during headache.

Face - Face has a yellowish appearance. Perspiration on face during fever, while asleep. Food - Complete loss of appetite. Tried to eat, but food nauseated. Eating and drinking relieved empty, weak feeling in stomach to some extent.

Mouth - Tongue heavily coated. Tongue, broad with thick greenish yellow fur, feels drawn up. Dry sensation not relieved by water, also profuse saliva.

Stomach - Belching, nausea, and vomiting. Great nausea and retching with desire for stool. Bitter, sour, hot, bilious, ropy, gushing vomiting, sets the teeth on edge. Vomiting with colic and cold sweat on forehead and back of hands. Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy.

Abdomen - Abdominal pains somewhat better by lying on stomach and abdomen. Cutting and twisting pains all through the abdomen. Sore abdomen, enlarged with jaundice and constipation. Gripping at navel. Aching in umbilical region, grip- Chionanthus virginica ing. Feels as if a string were tied in a “slip-knot” around intestines which was suddenly drawn tight and then gradually loosened. Pancreatic disease. Weakness in hypogastrium. Passage of offensive flatus. Back - Sore, weak, bruised feeling all over small of back. Small of back exceedingly weak. Pain from seventh to tenth dorsal vertebra, on waking. Constitutions - Suited to the bilious temperaments.

Rectum - Constipation. Diarrhea. Claycolored stool, tarry, also soft, yellow and pasty. Stool copious, watery, dark brown. Stools undigested and showing an absence of bile. Stools terribly offensive, like carrion. Emission of flatus during stool. Hot, scalding sensation in anus during stool. Cold sweat on forehead and back of hand during stool.

Limbs - Cold sweat on the back of hands during stool. Rheumatic pain in left ankle and tarsal bones. Rheumatic pain in articulations of left thumb. Sore, aching, tired feeling in lower limbs.

Sleep - Could not go to sleep before midnight. Nervous and restless after going to bed. Feels very badly and sick all over on waking in the morning. Sleepy during the day, could hardly keep awake. Perspiration on head and face during sleep.

Skin - Marked moisture of skin. Yellow, sallow, greenish, itching. Chronic jaundice, recurring every summer, caused by drinking too much cider.

Modalities - Better from lying on abdomen. Worse from jarring. Worse motion. Worse cold.

Liver - Hypertrophy of liver. Hepatic region tender. Cholecystitis. Bilious colic. Gallstones. Obstruction of liver in malaria districts. Enormous liver, constipation, stools clay-colored, skin very yellow. Soreness in region of liver. Chronic cases of jaundice. Jaundice recurring every summer. Jaundice with arrest of menses. Lungs - Astringent expectoration.

Kidneys - Bile and sugar in urine. Large amount of high specific gravity, frequent urination. Urine very dark, orange-yellow color, thick, black, syrupy.

Temperature - Cold sweat on back of hands. Chill at noon. Chilly sensations darting through body from front to back. Aching in back or limbs before and during fever. Wants to be covered during chill and fever. No thirst during chill or fever. Headache and backache during fever, eyeballs very sore. COMMENTS - A proving of Chion. was made by Dr. John Z. Lawshe and was communicated with additions to the Southern Journal of Homeopathy by H. C. Morrow. One observer, who gave Chion. to a nursing woman who had liver disorder with jaundiced tint, noticed that while rapid improvement of the liver symptoms occurred, at the same time the milk disappeared and the menses returned. The medicine was stopped and Sabal. given and the milk returned. Six weeks later Chion. was again given and identically the same result took place.” Jaundice with arrest of menses” should be a strong indication. Sherbino cured a case of neurasthenia in a clergyman who had complained of perspiration all summer. Weakness in arms and legs. Prostrated after preaching, mind ran on sermon and kept him awake. Stupid, drowsy all the time, appetite poor, all food gave distress. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bry., Card-m., Cean., Chin., Euon., Chel., Lept., Merc., Podo. (2) In bilious vomiting, Bry., Eup-per., Iris. (3) Nux-v., in green frothy stools, Elat., Grat., Kali-bi., Mag-c., Iris., Merc. (4) in weakness, bruised and sore feelings, Arn., Bapt., Bry., Eup-per., Gels., Nux-v., Rhus-t. in headache, Bell., Bry., Caps., Gels., Nux-v. (5) sensation of something alive. Croc., Thuj. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

author: Murphy

PHARMACY - chlol. Chloralum hydratum. Choral hydrate. This gas is proved in the form of Chlorine water. Solution, trituration. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Angina pectoris. Asthma. Bedsores. Bedwetting. Bronchitis. Chorea. Conjunctivitis. Coughs. Dermatitis. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspnea. Emaciation. Erysipelas. Eye, disorders. Hay, fever. Hemorrhagic, diathesis. Heart, disorders. Hydrophobia. Keratitis. Labor, abnormal. Laryngitis. Laryngismus, stridulous. Leucorrhea. Night-terrors. Palpitations. Paralysis. Ptosis. Puerperal, convulsions. Purpura. Spasms. Strokes. Urticaria.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chloralum hydratum was used in physiological doses is a powerful hypnotic and cardiac depressant. Introduced as hypnotic, Chlol. soon showed that it possessed wide powers of disturbing the organism and many people (including the late Professor Tyndall) were fatally poisoned by overdosing. A person under the influence of Chlol. hears voices, sees visions of arches, etc., when in the dark or when the eyes are shut. Emotional excitability, hallucinations. Night-terrors in children. Marked effect on the skin, producing rashes, erythema, ecchymosis, purpura etc. These symptoms have been used homeopathically with much success, especially in the treatment of allergic hives. Marked action on respiratory organs. The brain, eyes, urinary and sexual organs and skin are most affected. Inflamed and ulcerated mucus membranes. Muscular prostration. Spasms of the glottis. Marked sensation of constriction. Patients rapidly emaciate. MIND - Fears insanity or losing senses. Forgets names and persons. Night-terrors. Constitution - Hemorrhagic diathesis.

Head - Morning headache, worse in forehead, also in occiput, on motion, better in open air. Passive cerebral hyperemia. Feeling as if hot band were drawn from temple to temple. Lungs - Sudden dyspnea from spasms of the vocal cords, with protruding eyes, blue face, cold sweat. Extreme dyspnea with sensation of weight and constriction of chest. Inspiration free but cannot exhale. Asthma or hay fever with sleeplessness. As if air were forced into upper chest.

Eyes - Protruding eyes, blood-shot and watery. Conjunctivitis, burning in eye and lids, eyeball feels too large, everything looks white. Circles of light, black spots. Illusions of sight where eyes are closed or at night. Dim vision.

Ears - Hears voices.

Nose - Smoky or sooty. Coryza, acrid with headache, suddenly running in drops with lachrymation.

Face - Swollen with protruding eyes.

Mouth - Putrid odor from mouth. Putrid aphthae. Tongue, dry, black.

Throat - Choking sensation inability to swallow. Laryngitis. Laryngismus stridu- lous. Aching tickling or whistling in throat pit. COMMENTS - W. S. Gee cured with it a terrific headache of several days’ duration. Dull, heavy aching in forehead, coming on each morning 8 a.m., worse sudden motion, lying down, better in open air. The 6c gave great relief, though it aggravated at first, the aggravation occurring ten minutes after each dose. One dose of the 25x cured permanently. The brain is congested, hard, full, pressing pains in head. Eyes injected, the eyeballs feel too large, lids swollen, heavy, can hardly lift them. Asthma and wheezing respirations, probably due to an urticaria condition of the lung tissue. Insomnia due to over-fatigue. Snoring in sleep. When lying on back inspiration was through the nose, while expiration was blown from the lips as in a stroke. The heart's action is increased with oppression. Palpitation, hypertrophy. Paralysis of heart. Heart dilated or weakened with peculiar fullness and lightness of chest and sense of emptiness in stomach. Marked sense of sinking and oppression at the pit of the stomach, and shows a profound action on the solar plexus. RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Am-c., Atro., Dig. (heart), Mosch., Electricity. Compare: ( 1 ) Bell, and Op. in stertorous breathing and puffing out cheeks, Gels., Nux-v. (2) in urticaria, Astac. Bell., Chlf., Chin., Op., Apis. (3) Veronal - a dangerous drug made by the action of alcohol upon urea and contains the same radical that alcohol does. Makes a man just as drunk as pure alcohol. Staggers, cannot stand up. (Varney.) Confluent, reddish spots, dermatitis, itching of glans and prepuce, circumscribed dermatitis patch on first metacarpal phalangeal joint. (4) Luminal - sleeplessness with skin symptoms, migraine headaches and lethargy like epidemic encephalitis. (Royal). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Sleep - Insomnia, hallucinations, horrid dreams. Somnolence.

Skin - Sensitive, dry, yellow, shriveled.

Modalities - Wants fanning, open air. Better from open air. Better motion. Worse from expiration. Worse evening, night, after midnight. Worse lying down. Worse after hot drinks. Worse stimulants. Worse eating.

Temperature - Easy sweat.
