full:
PHARMACY - cortiso. Cortisone. Cortisone is used in an acetate form and is prepared today by synthesis. It is a cortico-suprarenal hormone, belonging to the groupof 11 steroids or 11-oxycorticosteroid hormones. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Addison's disease. Allergic, rhinitis. Amenorrhea. Cataract. Conjunctivitis. Constipation. Cushing's syndrome. Depression. Dyspepsia. Edema. Goiter. Hay fever. Heatstroke. Hyperten- sion. Hypothyroidism. Lupus, erythematosis. Memory weak. Moon-faced. Muscular, atrophy. Obesity. Ophthalmic, migraine. Osteoporosis. Osteo-necrosis. Psoriasis. Styes. Sunstroke. Ulcers. Virilism.

HOMEOPATHIC - The Corticoid are a group of synthetic bodies whose action is analogous to that of Cortisone, but with greater power at equal weight and theoretically with greater tolerance. All corticoids can have side effects including the perforation of gastric and duodenal ulcers, gastric and duodenal hemorrhaging, psychological complaints, virilism, acne, osteoporosis, diminution of resistance to infections and to tuberculosis, amenorrhea and Cushing's syndrome. Prednisone and prednisolone cause less retention of water and salt and less potassium reduction in the blood than cortisone, but on the other hand, can be the cause of myopathy. The homeopathic proving of cortisone was carried out during May and June 1963 by W. L. Templeton on eight provers and five controls, using the potencies 6c, 12c and 30c, prepared by A. Nelson and Co. Ltd. Symptoms included a general lack of reaction and decrease of the organic reactional capacity. Slowness of the body and of the mind with irritability. Bradycardia torpor. Rhythmic disorders of glands, especially the pituitary, adrenal, pancreas. Dysthy- roidism with tendency to hypothyroidism. Inhibition of secretion of ACTH. Goiter. Hypercorticism, moon-faced. Virilism. Polydipsia. Morbid hunger. Tendency to obesity with retention of water. Acrid dyspepsia, which can lead to gastric ulcers. Vomiting. Headache. Intra-cranial hypertension. Right frontal and orbital pain, aggravated by the heat in a room, by pressure and in the afternoon. Impaired vision. Dryness of nasal and pharyngeal mucus membranes with coughing and dry, sticky eyes. Vertigo. Convulsions, the back of the eye reveals papillary edema. Skin discolored, vesicular eruption, dryness and cracking of the skin on the face and hands with exfoliation of the nail beds. Face round, puffy, moon-faced. Legs swollen with edema. Sacroiliac pain, as if the back were about to break. MIND - Unstable mood, alternating between euphoria, melancholy and excitement. Excitability with increased activity. Action calms him. Fatigue with weariness. Loss of willpower. Heavy, confused, irritable, impatient. Memory weak, mental effort arduous, aggravating the general condition. Difficulty in concentrating. Melancholic state. Thoughts of death. Depressive conditions.

Head - Headache, as from a band around the head. Pulsating headache around the right eye, the vertex and the left side of the occiput. Sensation of frontal and occipital rending. Pain stronger around the right eye and forehead. Pain aggravated by pressure, heat, movement, sun. Ameliorated in the open air.

Eyes - Tension behind the eyeballs. Eyeballs painful, dry, edges of the eyelids agglutinated. Inflammation of the inner canthus. Allergic conjunctivitis. Styes. Cataract. Accommodation difficult. Foggy vision.

Ears - Ringing in the ears.

Nose - Allergic rhinitis. Hay fever. Sneezing, worse in the morning, better by washing.

Face - Acne of the face, shoulders, and back.

Mouth - Dryness of the mouth, especially in the morning. Dryness of the throat and pharynx, worse with swallowing, ameliorated by eating warm honey. Uvula red.

Stomach - Amelioration by empty swallowing, aggravated in the morning and by hot drinks. Gastric ulcer.

Abdomen - Hepatic deficiency. Spasmodic entero-colitis.

Rectum - Diarrhea on rising in the morning, after breakfast, after a meal. Constipation and incomplete evacuation of hard stools in balls.

Urine - Loss of potassium, calcium, phosphorus. Diminution of ascorbic acid. Retention of chloride and sodium. Increase of creatinine, cholesterol, uric acid. Glycosuria. Proteinuria. Tubular casts in the urine. Vertigo - Vertigo, aggravated in a warm room. COMMENTS - Its fundamental properties are promotion of the formation of glycogen, diminution of the use of glucide by the tissues, negation of the nitrogen balance, elevation of urinary elimination of uric acid of creatine (without any change in the level of creatinine in the urine) and of potassium, sodium retention, varying action on the urinary elimination of phosphorous and calcium. Degeneration of the lymphoid organs with lymphocytopenia. Increase of globulins in the plasma and inhibition of conjunctival inflammatory reactions. Inhibits the production of ACTH and produces atrophy of the suprarenal cortex. It gives the impression of well being and euphoria, but there is the possibility of maniacal or depressive psychological complaints. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Ars., Sep., Sulph. - Impatient, quarrelsome, has grandiose ideas, pain and burning eruptions. (2) Psor. - Sad, periodic migraines, anxious, scabby, weeping eruptions, weakness of the back and limbs as if dislocated. (3) Puls. - changing, variable, weeps at the slightest trifle, alternation of smiles and tears. Erratic pains, dry cough, congestion of the veins. REFERENCES - Julian.

Male - Diminution of sexual desire.

Female - Amenorrhea in young girls. Menses copious, blood thick. Pelvic congestion. Heaviness in the lower abdomen. Sensation of repletion in the stomach, ameliorated by menstrual flow and by walking. Vulvar eczema. Food - Insatiable appetite, has butterflies if he does not eat. Milk and fats provoke nausea.

Chest - Skin of the thorax discolored. Red rash on the lower part of the sternum. Constitutions - Psoric and allergic constitutions. Slow, irritable subjects with a dull mind. Suitable especially, but not exclusively, for carbonic type and for Bernard's fat Sulphur types. Subjects fleshy with round face, sad, weeping for no reason.

Heart - Arterial hypertension. Purpura. Ecchymosis.

Back - Dorsal pain, under the ribs on the left side, spreading to the anterior sacroiliac, ameliorated by movement and pressure, as if broken, aggravated in a sitting position, by bending down and in the morning. Pain between the bones.

Limbs - Osteoporosis. Painful post-traumatic osteoporosis. Osteo-necrosis of the hip in particular. Painful joints. Muscular atrophy of the quadriceps of the lower limbs. Legs restless, not ameliorated by movement in bed. Drawing pain behind the knees. Pain in the loin, worse when seated or lying down. Sacroiliac pain, as if it were about to break. Vesicular eruption on the backs of the hands, itching with round marks, worse with the heat. Dryness and irritation of the back of the hands. Lungs - Dyspnea, aggravated in a warm room. Heaviness behind the sternum, respiration difficult. Short of breath, from nervous irritation, from warming himself and when in a hot room. Respiratory allergies, hay fever. Bronchitis with much sputum. Gray, gelatinous sputum. Laryngeal cough with sneezing in the morning. Cough aggravated by laughing, becoming excited, by walking, by physical fatigue, worse by undressing and by shaving.

Sleep - Sleep light. Agitated, easily disturbed, cannot sleep. Does not refresh, wakes tired.

Skin - Eczema with puffiness of the face. Round, raised marks, slightly hard, on the hands, ankle, cheek and left side of the neck. Itching rash on the legs, feet and hands. Red rash at the nail beds and on the backs of the fingers. Rash worse with heat. Red streaks on the skin, streaked with weals. Face and hands rough, chapping. Slow healing of wounds. Increased growth of hair in the usual places.

Modalities - Better from menstrual flow. Better walking. Better in the evening. Worse in the morning. Worse from external heat. Worse immobility. Worse scratching. Worse coughing. Worse pressure. Worse predominantly on the left side.

Kidneys - Nephrotic syndrome. Frequent, pressing urination. Urination at night, oliguria. Edema.

Blood - Increased production of the thrombocyte. Erythroid hyperplasia. Polymorphism of the leukocytes.

In massive doses it has cured, according to herbal authorities, “A derangement of the stomach, attended with profuse morbid secretion of mucus, there being always a coated tongue with fetor of the breath and loss of appetite and digestion.” Cory, is therefore indicated, as Hale remarked, in gastric catarrh, being an analog in this respect of Hydr. It has not been used in the potencies, a usual dose has been ten drops of the tincture four times a day.

HOMEOPATHIC - It is an unproved remedy, but clinical experience has revealed a specific relation of the manifestation of syphilis, including Hunterian chancre, syphilitic nodes, falling of the hair, and syphilitic ulcerations of scalp. Dry, scaly scabs on the faces of old people. Swollen lymphatic glands. Pronounced cancer cachexia. Gum- mata and night-pains. Chronic diseases with atony. Tongue clean, broad and full. Tissues flabby, doughy, cold. Gastric catarrh (Hydr. ) Syphilitic and non-syphilitic ulcerations of fauces. Ulcers of mouth and fauces. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Nit-ac., Kali-i., Fl-ac. HOMEOPATHIC - Cotyledon has had aconsid- erable proving. Cooper considered it a cancer remedy. He cured with it sinuses in buttock. A patient to whom he gave it for polyps said it made him stagger as if drunk. Marked action on the heart, oppression of the chest, and fullness in the throat. Oppressed breathing, disturbed heart. Catarrh of larynx and trachea. Well-marked pains through the breast to scapula. Pains in the region of the spleen. Rheumatic symptoms. Sciatica. Hysterical joint. Numb aching in muscular and fibrous tissue. Weak, faint feeling. Stitching, pricking, jerking pains are predominant sensations. A feeling as if some part of the body, like a foot or the head, were absent. The senses of sight and hearing are dulled. A yellow patch follows the eyesight. Disagreeable surging in ears, ears feel stuffed. Pressing vertex headache. Epilepsy. MIND - Lost and confused feeling. Could not articulate for some time on awaking. Feeling as if a part of the body were absent. Ailments from suppressed emotion.

Head - Headache, causing desire for open air, which ameliorates. Dull headache with cold feet. Dull, heavy, stupefying pain in forehead and vertex, shifting suddenly between them.

Throat - Constant choking in throat, feeling as if he would burst into tears. Back of throat feels as if covered with thick mucus. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ambr., Asaf., Hepat., Ign., Lach., Sedum acre. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Pain at epigastrium through to shoulder, with nausea. On swallowing, the morsel seems to pass and press against some swelling in cardiac region.

Abdomen - Long stitching in left hypochondrium. Dull pains in left hypochondrium. Dull pushing in region of spleen recurring at intervals.

Rectum - Bowels freely opened, later, constipation.

Chest - Full, bursting feeling, as if from obstruction at heart.

Heart - Heat about heart. Uneasiness. Clawing, dragging pain on riding, better by compressing side.

Back - Pain through to scapula from region of left breast. Pain at angles of scapulae. Breasts - Pain under left nipple and aching in right breast.

Limbs - Aching in back and thighs. Aching in all joints. Skin sensitive, rubbing of trousers causes an acute sting. Aching in left thigh followed by numbness. Stinging pain under left gluteus maximus in region of sciatic nerve. Legs and arms feel heavy and sore. Between attacks of headache, gnawing, rheumatic pain in right shoulder. Aching, bruised pain in wrists. Aching, tingling in hands, especially at night, preventing sleep, tingling down arm when the nerve is struck. Lungs - Oppressed breathing. Tickling in larynx with dry cough. Shooting in all directions in chest, particularly under right scapula and left nipple during evening. Stitches below both nipples.

Modalities - Worse morning and evening.

Kidneys - Calls to urinate frequent. Increased flow of clear urine.

full:
PHARMACY - crb-a-b. Crab apple. Malus pumila. Pyrus malus. Small twigs with whole clusters of flowers are boiled for half an hour. The water is strained and used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle, (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.

HOMEOPATHIC - The remedy Crab Apple, together with Oak-b., Will-b., Star-b-b., Sw- ch-b., Elm-b., Pine- b., and Lar-b., belongs to the group of For Despondency or Despair, as classified by Bach. States of severity. Burdening condition, without sufficient power or possibility to grow above. Unclean skin, acne. Accumulated wastes in the blood stream. Cleansing of digestive tract. Long-lasting viral infections. Chronic poisoning due toenvironmental hazards. Helps draw out impurities from a wound, if applied to the bandage. Chronic diarrhea. Feelings of disgust or repulsion. Strong repulsion toward the food consumed with the urge to vomit. Vomiting, nausea and emaciation (Chic-b., Must-b.). Anorexia and bulimia, tendency to obsess with weight problems. MIND - Self-centered. Concentrates on the unclean, shameful, bothering and burdensome. Obsessive preoccupation with beauty flaws or states of sickness considered unclean and unbecoming. Fear of contamination, by germs or unclean surroundings. Obsessive-compulsive disorder with deep shame (Cher-p-b., Pine-b.). Shame about appearance or inner guilt and uncleanness. Regrets sinful or shameful behavior. Feels soiled or dirty after abuse or molestation. Intense craving or desire to be cleansed and purified. Feels helpless in regard to the problem. Unable to shake off or overcome the condition. Minor problems assume disproportionate importance. Despair. REFERENCES Bach.

PHARMACY - crat. Crataegus oxyacantha. Hawthorn berries. Crataegus monogyna. Crataegus laevigata. N. O. Rosacea. The fresh berries are pounded to a pulp and macerated in two times their weight of alcohol. Tincture of the ripe fruit. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, fluid extract or tincture, one to fifteen drops.

CLINICAL - Anasarca. Anemia. Aneurysm. Angina pectoris. Arteriosclerosis. Dropsy. Dyspnea. Dyspepsia. Dyspnea. Edema. Heart, disorders. Heart, failure. Heart, hypertrophy. Heart, weakness. Hemorrhages. High bloodpressure. Insomnia. Myocarditis. Nausea. Weakness.

HERBAL - Crat is a great positive heart tonic. It has produced some heart symptoms and doubtless has a homeopathic relation, but it is not a heart-poison like digitalis and has no cumulative action. In tonic, it works very slowly, may palliate long term. For recovery from heart attacks. Increases heart strength. Congestive heart failure, heart weakness, enlarged heart. Chronic heart disease with extreme weakness. Heart-failure threatened from slightest exertion. Irregularity of heart.

HOMEOPATHIC - Produces giddiness. Shortness of breath with a slow pulse. Weak, rapid, and lowered pulse. Slow and irregular pulse. Air hunger. High blood pressure, also useful for low blood pressure. Very feeble and irregular heart action. Weakness in the valves, regurgitation, valve prolapse. Dyspnea and dropsy, from failure of heart-power whether from valvular affection or from anemia. Hypertrophy, dilation, nervous palpitation, arrhythmia. Insomnia. Aortic anemia, edema, cutaneous chilliness. Myocarditis. General anasarca. Arteriosclerosis, said to have a solvent power upon crustaceous and calcareous deposits in arteries. Cardio-hemorrhagic or lithemic cases. Dyspepsia and nervous prostration with heart failure. Heart problems after rheumatism. Alcoholic heart. A sedative in cross, irritable patients with cardiac symptoms. Oppression of the chest. Pain under the collarbone, chest pain in general. Stitching pain. Nervous with pain in back of head and neck. Weakness, exhaustion. Sudden weakness. Cold limbs. Pallor. Nervous palpitations. Collapse from typhoid. Hemorrhages from bowels. MIND - Irritable, cross and melancholic. Apprehensive, despondent. Despair, feels weak and fragile. Mental dullness. Makes mistakes. Confused feeling, followed by a feeling of quiet and calmness mentally. Anxiety with palpitations. Hurried feeling with rapid action of heat. Very nervous and irritable, with pain in back of head and neck. Irritable, cross and despondent. Morose and sulky. Ailments from grief. Despair about recovery. Irritability with heart disease. Cross, ill-humor, peevish. Sadness, depression.

Head - Very nervous and irritable with pain in back of head and neck.

Eyes - Conjunctival irritation, with nasal discharge.

Nose - Nasal discharges.

Stomach - Nausea. Dyspepsia and nervous prostration with heart failure.

Chest - Painful sensation of pressure in left side of chest below the clavicle.

Heart - Circulatory weakness. Angina pectoris. Anxiety with palpitations. Palpitations, tumultuous, violent, vehement. Heart muscles seem flabby, worn out. Heart weakness with oppression, stitches and insomnia. Fatty degeneration. Hypertrophy of heart. Aortic disease. Aneurysm of the aorta. Aortitis. Cardiac dropsy. Cardiac dyspnea. Pain in region of heart, under left clavicle, and under left scapula. Heart dilated, first sound weak. Incompetent valves. Valvular murmurs. Valvular incompetence. Myocarditis. Pericarditis. Sustains the heart in infectious diseases. Neurosis cordis. Fatty degeneration of heart.

Limbs - Limbs cold and edematous. Coldness of fingers. Blueness of limbs. Swelling of lower limbs. Swelling of feet. Lungs - Cough with an albuminous expectoration. Extreme dyspnea on least exertion without much increase of pulse.

Sleep - Insomnia of heart patients. Sleeplessness in aortic disease.

Skin - Skin eruptions. Burning, smarting eruptions on back of neck, axillae and chin, worse heat and sweating, better washing. Excessive perspiration. Fingers and toes blue. Coldness of skin. Blueness of fingers and toes, worse exertion or excitement. Great pallor of skin, with rush of blood to head.

Modalities - Better fresh air. Better quiet and rest. Worse in warm room. Worse least exertion. Worse at night. Worse from rheumatic affections.

Kidneys - Diabetes, especially in children. Urine diminished. Urine contains traces of albumen and an excess of phosphates.

Perspiration - Excessive sweat. Palms sweaty. Perspiration of limbs.

Pulse - Pulse accelerated. Pulse irregular, feeble, intermittent.

Temperature - Cutaneous chilliness. Blueness of fingers and toes, all aggravated by exertion or excitement. Chilliness in heart disease. Vertigo - Faintness and collapse. COMMENTS - Crat. was introduced into medicine as a heart remedy by Dr. Greene of Ennis, Ireland, and it has been used empirically with much success in cases of heart failure. It has usually been given in drop doses of the tincture. Dr. Green had a reputation for the cure of heart disease that caused patients to flock to him from all parts of the United Kingdom. He cured the majority of them and amassed considerable wealth by means of his secret medicine. Contrary to the code, he, though a physician in good standing, refused to reveal the remedy to his professional brethren. After his death, his daughter, a Mrs. Graham, revealed that the remedy her father had used so successfully was crataegus oxyacantha. Halbert in Clinique, March, 1899, recorded the case of “Mr. S., a young man sixteen years of age, had worked hard at manual labor since his twelfth year to support a widowed mother. He had in fact, done a man's work before his physical maturity would permit it. For some time he has shown signs of cardiac hypertrophy and had been cautioned by physicians to take good care as to his heart. “About a year ago during some gymnastic extreme in the nature of sport, he was suddenly admonished that something had ‘given way,' and for relief was obliged to take to his bed. When I first saw him he was obliged to lie down, respiration was labored and irregular and the heart's action was greatly exaggerated and erratic. “There was decided precordial bulging, the apex beat was considerably displaced, downward and to the left and the whole cardiac dullness was greatly extended, the impulse was heaving in character with considerable mitral systolic blowing and the corresponding diastolic intensification, there were also signs of considerable pulmonary engorgement and some pain in the chest region. “The patient was put into a warm bath for twenty minutes and then carefully returned to bed. Aconite 3x was administered every half-hour and continued hourly for a day or two afterward until he was somewhat relieved. “Crataegus, five-drop doses of the tincture, was then administered five times daily for a long time. The effects of this remedy were most remarkable, the cardiac irritation gradually lessened, the area of dullness decreased and the rhythm improved, at the same time all the general symptoms improved rapidly. “He has now been using the remedy for several months and the result is most satisfactory. I have every reason to expect a cure of the extreme symptoms and believe the heart will be reduced to a safe hypertrophy, will virtually be a cure.” A girl of twelve had a sudden collapse in Crataegus oxyacantha the third week of typhoid. Crat. five drops, every two hours was given on the indications ofagreatpallor with irregular breathing, cold limbs, pulse 120, very weak and irregular. Strychnia, Dig. and Cact. had failed to give more than temporary relief. Under Crat. she rallied at once. T. C. Duncan gave complete relief in a case of angina pectoris, the pain being above and to the left of the stomach. Strong pulse and forcible indications of hypertrophy were found. A very tender spot on the left side of the spine. Crat. removed at the same time “a hurried feeling” and the anxious expression on her face. Dr. Duncan produced a “hurried feeling” in himself when proving Crat., which he attributed to the rapid action of the stimulated heart. Anshutz reported that Dr. Jennings procured for himself some of the remedy and his experience with it explains Dr. Green's national reputation. Dr. Jennings wrote of the case of a Mr. B., aged seventy-three years. “I found him gasping for breath when I entered the room with a pulse-rate of 15 8 and very feeble, great edema of lower limbs and abdomen. “A more desperate case could hardly be found. I gave him fifteen drops of Crataegus in half a wineglass of water. In fifteen minutes the pulse beat was 126 and stronger and breathing was not so labored. In twenty- five minutes pulse beat 110 and the force was still increasing, breathing much easier. “He now got ten drops in same quantity of water and in one hour from the time I entered the house he was, for the first time in ten days, able to lie horizontally. I made an examination of the heart and found mitral regurgitation from valvular deficiency with great enlargement.” For the edema, he prescribed Hydrargyrum cum creta, Squill and Digitalis. “He received ten drops four times a day of the Crataegus and was permitted to use some light beer to which he had become accustomed at meal time. He made a rapid and apparently full recovery until in three months, he felt as well as any man of his age in Chicago. “He occasionally, particularly in the change of weather takes some of the Crataegus which, he says, quickly stops shortness of breath or pain in the heart. His father and 'a brother died of heart disease.” In another case, a woman “was suffering from a compensatory enlargement of the heart from mitral insufficiency,” was taken with dyspnea when Dr. Jennings was called and was nearly dead. Under Crataegus, and some other indicated remedies, she made an excellent recovery. “In a letter from her, three months afterward, she said she was feeling well, but that she would not feel fully secure without some of the Crataegus.” “The forty other cases ran courses somewhat similar...all having been apparently cured. Yet I am not satisfied beyond a doubt, that any of those patients were completely cured except those whose troubles of the heart were functional. And it is possible and even probable that in weather of a heavy atmosphere or when it is surcharged with electricity or if the patient be subjected • to great excitement or sudden or violent commotion or exercise he may suffer again therewith. “Cardiac impulse after a few days' use of the Crataegus is greatly strengthened and yields that low soft tone so characteristic of the first sound, as shown by the cardiograph. The entire central nervous system seems to be influenced favorably by its use, the appetite increases and assimilation and nutrition improve. “Also a sense of quietude and well-being rests on the patient and he who before its use was çross, melancholic and irritable after a few days of its use shows marked signs of improvement in his mental state. “I doubt if it is indicated in fatty enlargement. The dose which I have found to be the most available is from ten to fifteen drops after meals or food. If taken before it may in very susceptible patients, cause nausea. I find also that after its use for a month it may be well to discontinue for a week or two, when it should be renewed for another month or so. “Usually three months seem to be the proper time for actual treatment and after that only at such times as a warning pain of the heart or dyspnea may point out.” Dr. T. C. Duncan contributed the case of Mrs. A., a printer, who “came to me complaining of some pain in the side as if it would take her life. She did not have it all the time, only at times, usually the last of the week, when tired. “I prescribed Bryonia, then Belladonna without prompt relief. One Saturday she came with a severe attack, locating the pain with her right hand above and to the left of the stomach. The pulse was strong and forcible. “On careful examination I found the heart beat below normal indicating hypertrophy. I examined the spine and to the left of the vertebra about two inches I found a very tender spot (spinal hyperemia). She told me that when a girl she had several attacks and that her own family physician gave her a remedy that relieved her at once. “She had tried several physicians, among them an allopath, who gave hypodermic injections of morphine without relief. Hot applications sometimes relieved. I now recognized that I had a case of angina pectoris and that her early attacks were due, I thought to carrying her heavy brother. Now the attacks come when she becomes tired holding her composing stick, at the same time she became very much flurried, so much so that she had stop work because she was confused. “I now gave her a prescription for Cactus, but told her I would like to try first a new remedy, giving her Crataegus, saturating some disks with tincture. I directed her to take two disks every hour until relieved and then less often. If not relieved to take the Cactus. “She returned in a week reporting that she was relieved after the first dose of Crataegus. More, that hurried, flurried feeling had not troubled her this week. Her face has a parchment skin and the expression of anxiety so significant of heart disease was certainly relieved. I have not seen her since.” The proving of this remedy produced a flurried feeling due, to the rapid action of the stimulated heart. A nervous female medical student who also proved it had “an unusual rush of blood to the head with confused feeling,” followed later by “a feeling of quiet and calmness mentally.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aven., Heliant., Alfa., (2) Stroph., Dig., Iber., Naja, Cact. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

full:
PHARMACY - cresol. Cresylolum. Cresol. The cresols are phenols (ortho, meta, para) derived from toluene. They are extracted from tar, coal-tar, wood-tar. They are also prepared synthetically. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Anemia. Anorexia. Atherosclerosis. Emaciation. Maniac, depression. Muscular, atrophy. Paralysis. Premature, senility. Schizophrenia.

HOMEOPATHIC - The word “cresol” is derived from “creosote” and the suffix “-ol,” which means phenol. The cresols are powerful antiseptics, soluble in soap, but their use is restricted, owing to their strong odor. They are used, however, as primary material in the manufacture of bakelites, they form cresolins. The homeopathic proving was established by O. A. Julian in 1958 on five provers, three men. two women and a dog, as well as by the study of cases of chronic poisoning. The potencies 5c, 7c and 9c were used. Sclerosis of the cerebral, nervous and vas- cularsystems. Muscular atrophy, especially of the small muscles in the hands. Paresis or atrophic paralysis of the lower limbs. Quivering beneath the skin of the entire body. Pigmentation disorders, melanosis. Papular erythema. Hypertensive kidney sclerosis. Allergic conditions from a cancerous evolution. Anemia with thrombocytopenia and leucopenia. Asthenia, anorexia and emaciation. MIND - Schizophrenia with euphoria and volubility. Manic depressive psychosis. Euphoria, with abundant gesticulation, can lead to ecstasy. Loquacious mood. Schizophrenia in children. Anguish in the evening. Indifference. Distracted, gives the impression of being deep in thought. Unhappy visions. Hears bells. Irritable. Often repeats himself, trembling of upper limbs. COMMENTS - A long-standing experiment and numerous clinical observations by O. A. Julian and several of his colleagues allow the confirmation that Cresol, is a very valuable remedy, especially with regard to neuro- psychological, cardiovascular and cutaneous infections. It is almost a homeopathic phenobarbital in cases of epilepsy. It's particularly effective in a large number of epileptic cases if one is the first doctor to see the patient. If, on the other hand, allopathic treatment has already been prescribed, it is essential to know how to combine homeopathic remedies with a slow and progressive reduction of the previously prescribed classical remedies. Clinical observation, plus electro-encephalogram readings are used to direct this reduction of the allopathic dosage. By contrast, the number of Cresol, drops of 7c can be increased, which results in a better sedation of cortical irritability. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Arg-m. - Subject thin, sad, agitated and loquacious. Loss of memory, paretic state of lower limbs with trembling. (2) Plb. - Rapid emaciation, cortical and somatic weakness, gradual paralysis of the limbs. Abdomen hard retracted. (3) Caust. - Mental failing, melancholic, critical, paretic weakness. REFERENCES-Julian.

PHARMACY - croc. Crocus sativus. Saffron. N. O. Iridaceae. Tincture of dried stigmas. Tincture of the fresh young shoots. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abortion, threatened. After- pains. Anger. Asthenopia. Blepharospasm. Brain, congestion. Chorea. Constipation. Dysmenorrhea. Fainting. Gastric disorders. Hemoptysis. Hemorrhages. Headaches. Heart disorders. Hysteria. Lachrymation. Leucorrhea. Mania. Menorrhagia. Menstruation, heavy. Metrorrhagia. Miscarriage. Nosebleeds. Ophthalmia. Pregnancy, disorders. Surgery, after effects. Tumors. Ulceration. Uterine, hemorrhage. Wounds.

HOMEOPATHIC - Characteristic hemorrhage from various parts when the blood is black, stringy, clotting, forming itself into long black strings hanging from the bleeding orifice. Viscidblood,dark. Clotting. Tumors. Lipoma. Encephaloma. Symptoms rapidly change sides or mental and physical symptoms alternate. Rapid alternation of mental conditions. Jerking or spasmodic contraction of single sets of muscles. Chorea and hysteria. Chorea every seven days with hilarity, singing and dancing. Sensation as if something alive were moving internally in abdomen, chest etc. with nausea, faintness and shivering or jumping about various parts. Drowsiness, better by literary occupation. Prostration, weariness, fainting with nosebleed, metrorrhagia. MIND - Mind very much distracted. Forgetful. Impressionable, affectionate and moody. Loss of ideas on attempting to write anything down. Childish behavior. Confusion, better open air. Industrious. Irritability, takes everything in bad part. Mistakes in time, confounds present with past. Uneasy, anxious, sorrowful mood. Happy and affectionate, then angry. Changeable disposition. Rapidly changing or alternating mental disposition, opposite to each other. Anger with violence, rapidly followed by abject repentance. Remorse, repents quickly. Laughter quickly followed by tears. Cheerful at night. Cheerful, alternating with sadness, violence. Hysterical laughter, laughing mania. Involuntary laughter and weeping, worse music. Jesting. Loquacious. Vivid recollection from music heard (Lyc.). Singing in sleep. Sings on hearing a single note sung. Jumping, dancing, laughing, whistling, wants to kiss everybody. Delusion he is unfit for business.

Head - Throbbing, pulsating headache at menopausal period, during menses, or instead of menses, better pressure.

Eyes - Dry. burning, as after weeping. Asthenopia with extreme photophobia. Pupils enlarged and react slowly. Threatened glaucoma, embolism of central retinal artery. Ciliary neuralgia, pain from eyes to top of head. Lachrymation when reading. Must wipe eyes as if mucus or water were in them. Sensation as if she had been looking through too sharp spectacles. Feels as if smoke in eyes. Sensation as if cold air was rushing through eye (Fl- ac., Syph.). Electric sparks or jumping spots before eyes. Twitching of the upper eyelid. Lids heavy.

Ears - Noises in ears with hardness of hearing, worse stooping.

Nose - Nosebleed, strings of dark blood hanging down the nose, with faintness and cold sweat on forehead. Nosebleed at puberty of young girls »

Face - Hot, red, or alternating with paleness.

Mouth - Unusual warmth in mouth. Sour taste. Foul, offensive, sickly breath.

Throat - Feeling as if uvula were elongated, during and when not swallowing Crocus sativus in hysteria. Feeling of nausea in throat and chest. COMMENTS - Cooper and Culpepper agreed in thinking that Croc, is very similar to Calen, in its action. It is a vulnerary and corresponds to the effects of blows (deafness, tumors, etc.). Dark hemorrhage. Uterine hemorrhage of dark, black, stringy blood, often'associated with miscarriages or cancer of the uterus (Sec.). Painful suppuration of bruised parts, old scars re-open and suppurate. Lipoma and encephaloma of scalp. Used externally to scatter indolent tumors and ecchymosis. Tumor with ulceration and characteristic bleeding. A warm sensation ascending to the heart, impeding breathing, better by yawning. Tingling, crawling, pricking and itching occur in the skin. Scarlet redness of the whole body or scarlet spots on the skin. A domestic remedy for bringing out measles eruptions. Stitches, shocks, throbbings, broad thrusts. Cuttings and jerkings. Twitchings of single sets of muscles (chorea). Sensitive to music, involuntarily joins in on hearing anyone sing. Croc, has been successfully given to pregnant women who have complained of violent fetal movements, as well as in cases of imaginary pregnancy. Clarke once cured a young artist who had become subject to violent outbursts of rage. He would take up a knife to throw at his mother, with whom he lived, and almost immediately after would be abjectly repentant. The household was on the point of being broken up when the trouble was completely removed by Croc. On one occasion in a hospital, Clarke happened to see a young girl who was desperately ill with heart failure and valvular disease in a fit of hysterical laughter. This made him think of Croc. The only definite sensation she complained of in the heart region was a “jumping” sensation. Croc. 30c was given and very soon she was able to lie down flat (after having been propped up for weeks) and from that time she made a rapid recovery. Cooper gave single doses of the tincture in a case of malignant disease of the side following extirpation ofacancerous kidney. The result was an arrest of progress after an initial aggravation and complete relief of pain. The patient was a woman, who had formerly had hemorrhages with dark clots during her periods and feeling of weight towards womb. She had also the sensation of something moving in the abdomen. Teste cited from Murray the case of several children “who were seized with an extraordinary laughing mania from having, smelled of leather bottles that hadcontained essence of saffron.” RELATIONS-Antidote: Op., Bell. Compare: (1) Ip., Trill., Plat., Chin., Phos., Ust., Sabin. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Gastric troubles, bloatedness, belchings, vomiting etc.

Abdomen - Abdomen swollen, feeling of something heavy. Sensation as if something living were jumping about in the stomach and abdomen (left side) (Thuj.).

Rectum - Obstinate constipation due to portal stagnation. Constipation in infants. Stools contain dark stringy blood. Crawling and stitches in anus. Useful after operations for hemorrhoids.

Male - Excitement of sexual desire.

Female - Menses dark, viscid, too frequent and copious, black and slimy. Urging of blood to genitals. Uterine hemorrhage, clots with long strings, worse from least movement, worse during full or new moon. Threatened miscarriage, especially when hemorrhage is dark and stringy. False pregnancy. Movements of fetus are violent and painful. Food - Great thirst for cold drinks.

Heart - Sensation of heat ascending to the heart impeding breathing, better yawning. Dull stitches in the left chest. Anxious palpitation, worse ascending stairs.

Back - Sudden feeling of coldness in back, as if cold water were thrown over him, with icy-cold limbs. Breasts - Jumping pain in left breast, as if drawn towards the back, as if jumping alive in right breast. Jerking pain in interior of left breast, as if drawn toward back by means of thread (Crot-t.). Causations - Effects of blows. Constitutions - Suited to women and hysterical men.

Limbs - Spasmodic contractions and twitch- ings of single set of muscles. Chorea and hysteria with great alteration of feeling. Upper limbs fall asleep. Weakness in knees and legs. Cracking in hip joint and knees, worse stooping. Pain in ankles and soles. Cold as ice with metrorrhagia, nosebleed. Lungs - Heaviness in chest, must take deep breath. Dry cough, better laying the hand on the pit of the stomach. Wheezy cough with frothy expectoration, containing threads like fine twine, worse lying down. Expectoration stringy like thread.

Sleep - Deep sleep. Sings in sleep.

Skin - Prickling and crawling. Scarlet redness or spots on the skin. Old scars open and suppurate. Lipoma. Encephaloma. Disperses tumors.

Modalities - Better after breakfast. Better in open air. Better yawning, desire to take a long breath. Worse from motion. Worse lyingdown. Worse reading. Worse looking fixedly at an object. Worse from puberty. Worse pregnancy. Worse fasting. Worse during new and full moon. Worse hot weather. Worse heat, warm room. Worse in morning.

Temperature - Flushes of internal heat with prickling andcrawling in skin. Sweat only on the lower half of the body. Continuous, foul smelling sweat, worse debility, hemorrhages after childbirth.

HOMEOPATHIC - The poison of Cascavella is an deadly as that of the other Crotalide and the general symptoms are like those of the other members of the group, but the mental symptoms are more pronounced and peculiar. The proving was done by Mure, with additional effects reported by Higgins. Crot-c. has frequent sharp pains, worse by cold washing. Symptoms are worse at night. Pains in bones. Paralysis of articulation. Embarrassed, stertorous breathing and semiconsciousness. Hallucinations, a magnetic state is induced, with a cutting sensation all around the eyeball. Thoughts and dreams of death. Headache after sleep (Lach.). MIND - Restlessness worse drinking. Answers monosyllabic, “no” to all questions. Clairvoyance. Fear at night. Fear of being alone. Fear that someone is behind him. Thoughts of death when alone. Hurried. Loquacity. Moaning during sleep. Starting during sleep. • Delusions that the eyes were falling out. Delusions hears footsteps behind him. Fancies he hears groans. Sees spectres, ghosts, spirits. Death appears as a gigantic black skeleton. Hears voices that he must follow. Insanity alternating with metrorrhagia. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Crot-h., Lach., Naja, Vip. REFERENCES - Clarke.

White-leg. Whooping cough. Yellow, fever.

HOMEOPATHIC - Crotalus horridus, the rattlesnake venom, affects the blood, heart and liver. It produces profound nervous shock with deathly sickness, trembling and prostration. Easily tired by slight exertion. Profound nutritional action, nutritional troubles in old age. Low septic states. General disorganization of the blood, hemorrhages and jaundice. Hemorrhages from every part of the body. Hemorrhages are slow, oozing dark thin blood, not clots. Hemorrhages from all the orifices and surfaces, especially from the pharynx. Hemorrhages from the pores of the skin. Bloody pus, sweat. Tissues rapidly decompose producing putrid and malignant conditions. Dark or bluish parts. Septic conditions in the tonsils, goiter, ulcers, abscesses, blood boils. Moldy odors of secretions. Fetor of evacuations and discharges. Tendency to carbuncles. Pete- chiae. Neuralgia as a sequel to sepsis. Gangrene. Malignant scarlatina, yellow fever. Bubonic plague. Cholera. Stroke victims with bloody eyes. Chronic biliousness. Metastasis of erysipelas to brain. Menopausal conditions. Fainting. Easily tired by slight exertion. Paralysis, post-diphtheria of the insane. Progressive muscular atrophy. Convulsions, epilepsy with trembling of the limbs, foaming at the mouth, violent cries, delirium. In epilepsy, the average rate is far greater than in normal conditions. Sleeps into his symptoms. Pains alternate rapidly with each other and frequently recur, also appear and disappear suddenly after lasting some time (except headache). General burning. Swelling of whole body. Edema in general or of affected part. More right-sided in its action. Great periodicity. MIND - Clouded perception, impaired memory. Timid. Aversion to hisfamily. Weak memory, cannot express himself correctly. Loss of memory, for words and figures. Mistakes in writing. Connected thoughts difficult. Senile dementia incipient, forgets figures, names and places or suspicious about his friends. Weeping mood, agony, despair. Melancholy. Sadness during headache. Readily moved to tears. Weeping, tearful mood, while reading. Marked indifference. Thoughts dwell on death continually. Fears of evil. Sensitive to certain persons. Nervous agitation, anxious, pale, with cold sweat. Irritable, cross. Impatient. Irritable, cross, infuriated by least annoyance. Suspicion and snappishness, or quiet indifference. Plaintive speech. Intense restlessness, twitching and nervous agitation. Loquacious with desire to escape. Delusions of cerebral decay. Feels as if surrounded by foes or hideous animals. Delirium, with wide open eyes. Delirium, muttering, mumbles, jumbles and stumbles over his words. Delusions awakes struggling with imaginary foes. Delirium tremens with constant drowsiness, but with inability to sleep. Mania in zymotic diseases and when connected with puerperal or ovario-uterine disease. Insanity with coldness of skin. Abdomen - Burning pain in abdomen. Swollen, hot, tender. Inguinal glands enlarged. Bubo. Intestinal hemorrhage. Violent pain in left side near last ribs as if in diaphragm. Heat and tenderness of abdomen, can scarcely bear clothes on. Coldness in the stomach or abdomen as from a piece of ice. Violent pains in colon. Violent pain in region of appendix. Appendix feels large. Peritonitis. Typhlitis.

Head - Dull, heavy occipital pain, on right side and right eye. Pain in occiput, as of a blow. Headache in waves from spine. Severe pain at the center of forehead. Headache with pain in heart, on lying on left side. Sick headache with vertigo. Headache worse jarring, must walk on tiptoe. Dull headache before attack of uremic coma. Bilious headache every few days. Throbbing headache with nausea before menses. Meningitis. Violentitching of scalp, eruptions, pustules. Falling off of hair, as a result of toxemia. Soreness in back of head on pressure.

Eyes - Dry and burning sensation. Yellow color of eyes. Burning, red with lachrymation. Ciliary neuralgia, tearing, boring pain, as if a cut had been made around eyes. Retinal hemorrhages. Bleeding eyes after strokes. Blood exudes from eyes. For absorption of eye hemorrhages into the vitreous. Photophobia, worse during menses. Very sensitive to light, especially lamp light. Ptosis. Keratitis. Exopthalmic goitre.

Ears - Otorrhea after scarlatina, offensive and bloody, with deafness. Otorrhea, result of alcoholism. Blood oozes from ears. Feeling of stoppage in right ear. Full sensation in ears. Erysipelas of external ear. Deafness, illusions of hearing. Auditory vertigo. Sensitive to noises.

Nose - Nosebleed especially during diphtheria or other septic diseases. Nosebleed, blood black and stringy. Ozaena after exanthemata or syphilis. Nosebleed with flushes of face, vertigo or fainting. Bloody discharge. Tip of nose swollen and cold. Tip of nose, blue and red.

Face - Sallow. Dark, besotted face. Face yellow, death like pallor. Distorted on waking. Lips, swollen, stiff and numb. Lockjaw. Acne of masturbators. Small blisters around eyes. Eruption around mouth. Frequently recurring erysipelas of face. Face swollen and red during delirium tremens and fever. Swelling of submaxillary and parotid glands.

Mouth - Complete loss of taste. Fills up with saliva. Saliva bloody, frothy. Salivation at night. Stiff palate. Cannot speak on account of sensation of constriction around tongue and throat. Fetid breath. Putrid, sore mouth. Moldy smell of breath.

Throat - Dry, swollen, dark red with thirst. Spasm of esophagus, cannot swallow any solid substance. Gangrenous with much swelling. Tickling from a dry spot in larynx. Tight constriction of throat. Hoarseness, with weak, rough voice. Sore throat. Fauces sensitive to dry or cold air. Quinsy with much venous congestion. Tonsils bulge and are tender. Laryngismus stridulus. Edema glottidis. Paralytic aphonia. Ulceration from necrosis of cartilages of larynx. Acute laryngitis from burns. Laryngitis from stings of insects.

Stomach - Atonic dyspepsia. Trembling, fluttering below the epigastrium. Heartburn. Intolerance of clothing about epigastrium. Faintness and sinking at stomach. Ulceration of the stomach. Gastritis in chronic alcoholism. Cancer of stomach with vomiting of bloody, slimy mucus. Constriction of pylorus. Nausea on movement. Unable to retain anything. Violent vomiting of food. Constant nausea and vomiting every month after menstruation. Cannot lie on right side without vomiting dark-green matter. Black or coffee- grounds vomiting. Bilious vomiting. Vomiting of blood. Ulceration of stomach. Vomiting on ¡east exertion.

Rectum - Constipation with headache. Shuddering with diarrhea, aphonia. Diarrhea with nausea, thirst and anxiety. Diarrhea from septic matter in food or drink. Dysentery, septic. Hemorrhoids in pregnant women, and with menstrual irregularities. Hemorrhoids connected with heart disease or liver disease. Rectal hemorrhage, blood dark, fluid, non-coagu- lable. Rectal hemorrhage when of hepatic, splenic or cardiac origin. Bleeding from anus when standing and walking. Violent purging, with disagreeable sensation through whole body and nauseous taste. Perineal abscess. Sensations - As from a blow on occiput. As if tongue and all around throat were tied up. As of a plug in throat to be swallowed, of choking. As if the heart turned over like a tumbler pigeon.

Stool - White stools. Stools, black, dark green, thin, offensive, like coffee-grounds. Stools followed by debility. Liquid stools, with colic. Involuntary stool.

Male - Prostate cancer, painful (Con.). Sexual instinct increased with entire relaxations of penis. Sharp cutting in glans.

Female - Uterine hemorrhage with faintness at stomcch. Sensation as if the uterus would drop out. Prolonged menses. Dysmenorrhea with pain in hy pogastrium, down the thighs with aching in the region of the heart. Painful drawing in uterine ligaments. Puerperal fever. Offensive lochia. Phlegmasia alba dolens, worse touch. Alcoholics with delayed menses. Ovarian neuralgia. Ovarian abscess. Vicarious menses. Menopausal flushings, sweat. Fungoid cancer of uterus. Cauliflower excrescences. Miscarriage during course of septic or zymotic disease. Miscarriage from other blood- poisoning causes. Food - Hunger with trembling, weakness, and occipital headache. Aversion to meat. Craves pork. Desires stimulants, sugar. Diseases caused by abuse of alcohol. Unquenchable burning thirst.

Chest - Excessive oppression of chest. Burning in chest with heat in forehead. Stitches in right chest near sternum. Oppression in old people. Hydrothorax in fever and ague. Left axillary glands swollen and tender. Constitutions - Broken-down constitutions. Chronic bilious, menopausal or albuminuric conditions. Hemorrhagic diathesis. Septic toxemic or even miasmatic disease.

Heart - Aching in region of heart. Weak, trembles, action feeble. Heart beats rapidly, but feebly. Trembling feeling of heart. Heart tender when lying on leftside.Much pain in heart, through left shoulder and down left arm. Palpitations with sore pain in and about heart. Palpitations as if heart tumbled about. Palpitation during menses. Pulse rapid and weak, scarcely perceptible. Pulse feeble and quick, then slow. Pulse fluttering, frequent. Pulse small, quick, threadlike. Pulse wavy, or slow.

Back - Tearing pains from right shoulder to neck, worse on moving arm. Pain on top of shoulder and in ascending aorta. Aching in right kidney and in stomach. Drawing, tensive pain from right shoulder along neck, as from a tense tendon, worse pressure and moving arm. Softening of spinal cord. Carbuncles, boils, pustules, pimples or bed sores. Breasts - Inflamed breasts. Causations - Ill effects of fright, alcohol, sun. lightning, foul water, insect stings, noxious effluvia, or vaccinations.

Limbs - Phlebitis, varicose veins and varicocele. Right-sided paralysis. Paralysis of left hand and leg. Arms and legs become numb, first one and then the other. Lower limbs go to sleep easily. Cannot keep legs still. Pain in top of shoulders. Hands tremble, swollen. Hands feel dead when sewing. Heaviness as if bones were made of heavy wood. Bruised pain in joints and bones. Numb pain as after cramp, in anterior of fingers and in toes. Right-sided paralysis. Limbs inflamed, swollen and gangrenous. Contraction of flexors. Gonorrheal rheumatism. Cannot keep legs still.

Sleep - Drowsy, but cannot sleep. Sleeplessness from nervous and mental distress. Sleepless from nervous agitation. Starting in sleep. Smothering sensation when awaking. Symptoms worse after sleep. Dreams of dead persons. Travelling dreams. Dreams of quarrels. Horrible dreams. Yawning.

Skin - Skin cold and dry. Skin dry, stiff, like thin parchment. Lymphangitis and septicemia, from dissecting wounds. Skin, cold and dry. Yellow color of the whole body. Jaundice. Purpura hemorrhagica. Great sensitiveness of skin of right half of body. Sore sensation relieved by pressure. Pustular eruptions. Blood boils, carbuncles, felons. Hemorrhagesfrom every part of body. Chilblains, felons. Boils, carbuncles and eruptions are surrounded by purplish, mottled skin and edema. Anthrax. Vesication. Dissecting wounds. Edema about the affected part. Petechial spots. Old scars break open again. Old ulcers. Bloody sweat. Post- vaccination eruptions. Stings of insects. Gangrene with diarrhea. Pemphigus.

Modalities - Better from rest, motion, light. Head and stomach symptoms better from open air. Worse in morning, on waking or wakes the patient up in the night. Worse right side. Worse lying. Worse falling asleep. Worse jar. Worse exertion. Worse from alcohol. Worse open. air. Worse damp, wet. Worse evening and morning. Worse in spring. Worse changing to warm weather. Worse yearly. Cold air aggravates the throat and respiratory symptoms. Dry air aggravates cough.

Teeth - Gums white. Bleeding of gums. Gums swollen, painful, borders reddened. Grinding of teeth during sleep.

Tongue - Glossitis. Tongue numb and stiff. Tongue, yellow, enormously swollen, protruded to the right. Tongue red and small, but feels swollen. Tongue fiery red, dry in center, smooth and polished. Cancer of tongue with hemorrhage. Tongue very foul, with red tip. Tongue swollen to nearly twice the normal size. Edema of tongue after sting of insects. Vertigo - Vertigo with pale face. Auditory vertigo. Menière's disease. Vertigo with faintness, weakness and trembling. Fainting on assuming upright position. Dizziness and fainting with occipital headache. Anemic vertigo, better resting head. Vertigo from fright. Vertigo with dilated pupils. Vertigo from lightning or sunstroke. Vision - Amblyopia from hemorrhage, debility and exhaustion. Amblyopia from grief or from over use of vision. Diplopia. Illusions, blue colors. Dim vision for distant objects. Dim vision when reading. Lost vision with lethargy and coldness. Momentary disappearance of vision with profuse lachrymation. Muscae volitantes and various colored flames. Weak vision after an attack of keratitis or kerato-iritis. COMMENTS - Crot-h. produces profound nervous shock and prostration with trembling, mental alienation and disorganization of the fluids and tissues. Bleeding from all orifices and surfaces. Hemorrhagic diathesis caused by previous low states of system, by zymotic or septic poisoning, by abuse of alcohol, etc. Low, typhoid states with oppressed nervous system and degraded blood-supply. Neuralgia occurring as a sequel of septic toxemic or even miasmatic disease or çhronic bilious, menopausal or albuminuric conditions. Broken-down constitutions. Sleepy, but cannot sleep. Grinds teeth. Predominantly a right-side medicine (Lach, is left). Acts strongly on the liver and corresponds to jaundice and yellow fever. Used as a prophylactic against yellow fever. For this inoculation with diluted virus has been practiced. The cobra poison (Naja.) coagulates blood into long strings. Crotalus poison is acid, the Viper neutral. The Rotton-snake (“Birri”) causes more sloughing than any other. Hering wrote that Crot-h. is preferable in fluid hemorrhages, with yellow skin, hence in yellow fever with black vomit, and nosebleed of diphtheria. Naja, has more nervous phenomena. Lach, has cold, clammy skin, rather than cold and dry, hemorrhage with charred-straw sediment, and more markedly ailments of the left side. Elaps is preferable in otorrhea and in disorders of the right lung. Hayward observed that sloughing is a strong indication for Crot-h. and the cure with this remedy of his own daughter of scarlatina maligna with gangrenous-looking sore-throat was a dramatic outcome of his researches. Symptoms of Crotalus Durissus as well as Crotalus Horridus are included in the pathogenesis. A case of rattlesnake bite and its isopathic cure, related by Dr. J. S. M. Chaffee in Hom. News, Sept., 1892, gives a good general idea of the action of the venom. “I was called to see James Wright, aged 54 years, who, while binding wheat, was bitten on third finger of right hand by a rattlesnake. I found him bleeding from the bitten finger and from eyes, nose, ears, mouth, rectum and urethra, pulse 110, small, wiry, respiration 40, temperature 105, haggard expression, whole body bathed in hot perspiration, delirium. “This patient had the regular routine treatment of whisky, quinine and carbonate ammonia for ninety-six hours, when the attendants withdrew and pronounced the case beyond the reach of medical aid. A marked characteristic symptom was a moldy smell of breath with scarlet red tongue and difficult swallowing. Great sensitiveness of skin of right half of body, so much so that the slightest touch would produce twitching of muscles of that side. “I prescribed Crot-h. 30c trituration, 30 grains in four ounces of water, a teaspoonful every hour, until my return visit, twenty- four hours later, when I found marked improvement. Temperature normal, pulse full, soft and regular, delirium gone, saliva and urine slightly tinged with blood, appetite returning, he having asked for food for the first time since the accident. The medicine was continued for two more days, when recovery was practically complete.” RELATIONS-Antidote: Lach., Alcohol. Radiant heat. Camphor. Compare: (1) Both., Naja - more nervous phenomena. (2) Lach. - more markedly worse on left side. (3) Elaps - preferable in otorrhea and disorders of right lung. (4) Crotalus cascavella - poliomyelitis. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Liver - Jaundice, malignant with hemorrhage. Stitches in region of liver on drawing a long breath, worse by pressure. Aching in liver, vomiting, coldness. Pain in region of liver and top of shoulders. Lungs - Asthma with cardiac disease. Asthma, with great debility and prostration, blue, puffy countenance, cold sweat. Anxious, labored breathing. Oppression in old people. Tickling from a dry spot in larynx. Difficult breathing, as if lungs would not expand. Embarrassed breathing with constriction of throat. Quick, labored breathing with weak pulse and nervous agitation. Bronchiectasis, putrid bronchitis, chronic bronchorrhea. Edema or gangrene of lungs. Pneumonia with tendency to gangrene or haemorrhage.

Kidneys - Nephritis. Inflamed kidney. Suppression or painful retention of urine. Urine scanty, dark and red with blood. Nephritis albuminosa in pregnancy. Albuminuria in course of typhoid, diphtheria. Albuminous, dark, scanty (Merc-c.). Dark, bloody urine, green-yellow. Casts. Hematuria with bronchitis. Hematuria with bladder or prostate cancer. Hemorrhage from kidney after scarlet fever. Hemorrhage from urethra. Urine copious and light colored. Yellow or reddish-yellow urine, from much bile.

Cough - Cough from external pressure on larynx. Cough as if from salt or pepper. Cough on awaking from sleep. Cough with stitch in left side. Dry cough on speaking, worse in dry or cold air. Nervous cough. Whooping cough, with blueness or pallor which is long in passing off. Cough with bloody sputum of moldy odor. Cough from tickling in throat. Cough with stitch in left side and bloody expectoration.

Perspiration - Bloody sweat. Sudden attacks of cold sweat. Colored sweat.

Temperature - Chill alternating with heat. Severe chills. Malignant fevers of a hemorrhagic or putrescent character. Low bilious remittents. Plague fever. Black water fever. Yellow fever. Cerebrospinal meningitis (Cic., Cup-a.). High fever. Bloody sweat, cold sweats. Pyemia. Hectic fever with burns, compound fractures, lacerated wounds, dissection wounds, cellulitis, erysipelas, stings of insects.

name: Croton Tiglium
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better after sleep. Better gentle rubbing. Many symptoms are worse at night. Worse least food or drink. Worse Croton tiglium during summer. Worse night, morning. Worse receding eruptions. Worse washing. Worse touch, pressure. Worse motion, and when sitting or crouching. Dizziness and faintness are worse in open air. Drinking cold water while heated causes complete loss of voice. Colic worse hot milk. Diarrhea is worse in summer..

full:
PHARMACY - croto-t. Croton tiglium. Croton oil seeds. Tiglium officinale. N. O. Euphor- biacae. Tincture of the oil from the seeds. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Blisters. Cholera, infantum. Colic. Diarrhea. Eczema. Eruptions. Herpes, zoster. Neuralgias. Ophthalmia. Otorrhea. Poison ivy. Pustules. Rashes. Rhus,poisoning. Skin, disorders. Vesicles.

HOMEOPATHIC - Croton Tiglium was used as a powerful purgative and irritant of the skin in ordinary practice, therefore causing watery discharges. Croto-t. has a strong affinity for skin, face and external genitals. It is one of the antidotes to rhus poisoning, as is evident from its wide and intense action upon the skin and mucus surface, causing irritation and inflammation with formation of vesicles and mucus discharges. Croto-t. is a valuable remedy in diarrhea, summer complaints and skin disorders. Skin symptoms alternating with internal symptoms, diarrhea etc. Many symptoms spread from below upwards. Peculiar feeling as if parts were drawn backwards, eyes, nipples, etc. Skin feels hide-bound, tight all over. Burning in the esophagus. Marked eye symptoms include purulent ophthalmia, ulceration and hypopion. Croton tiglium Affects the mucus membranes of the intestines. Colic before stool, constant urging, worse from eating, drinking, and every movement. Stool is yellowish or yellowish green. Characteristic sudden evacuation in one gush, like a shot, followed by great prostration. MIND - Morose, dissatisfied. Cannot think outside himself. Feels all spent up. Feeling of anxiety, as though some personal misfortune would befall him. Not disposed to work.

Head - Pressing pain in forehead, especially orbits. Weight of hat causes headache.

Eyes - Purulent ophthalmia, red and raw appearance. Pustules on cornea with eruptions around eyes. Granular lids, pustules of cornea. Eyes feel drawn backward. Tensive pain above right orbit.

Ears - Otorrhea, with great itching.

Face - Pustular eruptions on the face. As though insects were creeping.

Mouth - Neuralgia of the tongue. Burning in esophagus.

Stomach - Excessive nausea with vanishing of sight. Vertigo - Vertigo, worse drinking. COMMENTS - On the skin, Croto-t. produces erythema, erysipelas, eczema, and herpes pustules. Large, copper-colored spots almost like liver-spots. Small, red blotches that are not very apparent in thighs, abdomen and genitals, all accompanied with intolerable itching. Useful to antidote poison ivy and poison oak, particularly on the face and groin. Croto-t. antidotes Rhus-t. and the antidote to Croto-t. is Ant-t. Guernsey gave the skin indications as “in any skin disease which itches very much, but the patient cannot bear to scratch very hard as it hurts, a very slight scratch, a mere rub suffices to allay the itching. Erysipelas that itches exceedingly.” He also gives “otorrhea when there is much itching.” Teste, who was among the first to use Croto-t. homeopathically, gave a very interesting account of it. He quoted Trousseau and Pidoux as saying that it often happens that eruptions are developed on parts not touched by the remedy in those who have been engaged in making Croto-t. ointments on patients. The face and the scrotum especially have been thus attacked. The itching which it causes, according to Teste, is at first more tingling than burning (the contrary taking place with Rhus-t.). The itching changes to burning (like Rhus-t.). Teste recorded the case of a delicate, cachectic, psoric girl of four who had suffered for two years without interruption from a fetid discharge from the nose, less in winter, more in summer. Before this, she had a vesicular eruption on chest and neck, which disappeared by itself, followed in three or four days by the discharge. After the failure of Sulph., Merc., Calc., on the indication of the previous eruption. Teste gave Croto-t., and in less than a fortnight the disease lost three-fourths of its intensity, although it was in mid-summer. Six months completed the cure, the only other remedies given during the time were Lob. and Kreos. A second case from Teste records a man of forty, very fleshy, who for fifteen years had been subject to attacks of gout returning every spring, except on two occasions when a most fatiguing and obstinate rash appeared instead. This consisted of an intense redness of the whole body, accompanied with a burning itching, especially in the hollow of the hands, at the chest, and behind the ears. These parts were the seat of a yellowish, plastic exudation, emanating from a multitude of small vesicles in close contact with each other. They were only distinctly •perceived in places where they were less numerous and where a greater degree of resistance on the part of the epidermis imparted to them a certain persistence. Each time this eruption broke out, it lasted three months in spite of purgatives and the baths of Bareges and Aix les Bains. When Teste saw the patient, he had neither gout nor eczema, butadry, racking, almost convulsive and unceasing cough. Skin was rather hot, there was thirst, a little headache, heat in the chest, no dyspnea. Sometimes, especially in the evening, but only for a few days, he showed a tendency to syncope. At the end of three weeks, having received no benefit from Teste's treatment, the patient took of his own accord three tablespoonfuls of the “Syrup of White Poppy,” at bedtime. The cough ceased entirely for some hours and then returned in its old intensity. But during the intermission the malady had come out on the skin, and at daybreak the patient found himself covered from head to foot with his old horrible eczema. He was almost unrecognizable and in a state of the deepest anxiety and despair. He expected three or four months of it. Teste then gave Croto-t. The itching disappeared the same day. Within five or six days there remained not a trace of either cough or eruption. As the patient left Paris, Teste was not able to follow the case in subsequent years. Conrad Wesselheft cured a case of proctalgia in a woman of thirty with Croto-t. 3x. The attacks came on after stool, lasting half a day and preventing her from fulfilling her duties as a teacher. There were no hemorrhoids, only sensitiveness of rectum to touch. He was led to the remedy by having previously had another patient who suffered from a similar pain after using Croton pills. Pain in the rectum came on with extreme intensity after straining at stool and the patient (also a woman) was in agony for three hours afterwards with frequent tenesmus. The pills were stopped and Nux-v. given, and she was well in a week. RELATIONS - Antidote: Ant-t. Compare: (1) Rhus-t., Anagallis, Anae., Sepia. (2) Momordica charantia - has marked drastic properties, producing colic, nausea, vomiting, cholera-like symptoms, abdomen seems full of fluid discharged explosively, thin, watery, yellow. Great thirst. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Abdomen - Pressure on the navel causes pain in the rectum or urging for stool. Colic, better hot milk. Breasts - Nodes in breasts with pain from nipple to scapula. Breast hard, swollen. Inflamed breasts. Nipples very sore to touch. Pain from nipple to back when child nurses.

Rectum - Swashing sensation in intestines. Pain in the anus as if a plug were forcing outwards. Constant urging to stool, followed by sudden evacuations. Copious, watery stools with much urging, then profuse sudden gushing stools of yellow water. Diarrhea worse drinking the least quantity or while eating, followed by prostration. Summer diarrhea. Cholera infantum. Sensations - As if the skin were hide-bound. Mentally hide-bound, can't think outside of himself. As of a string pulling from one part to another, from eyeball to back of head, from nipple to back, with pain in nipple when the child nurses. Cutting, sticking, stinging, stitching pains and burning stitches. Writhing in transverse colon. As if a plug were forcing outwards at anus.

Male - Eczema of scrotum. Vesicular eruptions on scrotum and penis. Left testes retracted, right pendent.

Female - Intense itching of genitals, better by gentle rubbing.

Chest - Drawing-pain through the left chest into the back. Constitutions - Psoric and allergic constitutions.

Limbs - Neck and shoulders painful. Lungs - Asthma with cough, as soon as he touches the pillow, must sit up. Could not expand the lungs. Feels as though he could not inhale deeply enough. Sensitive to deep breathing.

Skin - Rhus poisoning, poison ivy and oak. Eczema. Herpes zoster, stinging, smarting pains of the eruption. Vesicular erysipelas. Confluent, oozing, vesicles. Pustular eruptions, clustered blisters, which burst and form crusts, especially on face and genitals with fearful itching, followed by painful burning. Intense itching, but scratching is painful. Violently itching, burning, red skin, sore if scratched, better gentle rubbing. Feels hide- bound.

Modalities - Better after sleep. Better gentle rubbing. Many symptoms are worse at night. Worse least food or drink. Worse Croton tiglium during summer. Worse night, morning. Worse receding eruptions. Worse washing. Worse touch, pressure. Worse motion, and when sitting or crouching. Dizziness and faintness are worse in open air. Drinking cold water while heated causes complete loss of voice. Colic worse hot milk. Diarrhea is worse in summer.

Kidneys - Night urine, foaming, dark orange colored, turbid on standing, greasy particles floating on top. Day urine is pale with white sediment.

name: Cubeba Officinalis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from getting up and walking about. Worse from night, in bed..
constitution: Albuminuria. Aphthae. Bedwetting. Catarrh. Croup. Cystitis. Diarrhea. Dysr entery. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Hernia. Leucorrhea. Orchitis. Prostatitis. Rheumatism. Roseola. Urethritis. Urticaria.

full:
PHARMACY - cub. Cubeba officinalis. Cubebs. Pipercubeba. N. O. Piperaceae. Tincture of dried unripe fruit. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Aphthae. Bedwetting. Catarrh. Croup. Cystitis. Diarrhea. Dysr entery. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Hernia. Leucorrhea. Orchitis. Prostatitis. Rheumatism. Roseola. Urethritis. Urticaria.

HOMEOPATHIC - Cubeba is an old-world remedy for gonorrhea and gleet. It affects the mucus membrane of the nose, air passages, intestines, and the uro-genital tract. It acts well in persons of bilious temperament with tendency to constipation. Burning, rawness is felt in the throat in stomach, abdomen, rectum, urethra, fossa navicularis. Catarrh. Discharges are thick, acrid, yellow, pus like, green, offensive after violent inflammation. Frequent urination of a nervous origin. Leucorrhea in young girls. MIND - Weakness of intellect. Frequent absence of mind. Loss of memory. Is unable to accomplish anything. Waking reveries. All his ideas are confused and wandering. Cannot find words to express himself. Exaltation of temper and mental faculties. Starting from noises. Uneasiness, anxiety, can't remain in bed. Madness, with sorts of beastly extravagances. Impatient, irritable, a mere trifle provokes him. Furious insanity, with wickedness. Breaks everything within his reach, out of sheer malice. Mania, desire to strike and to kill. Impulse to swear at people. Im- Cubeba officinalis pulse to strike them and spit in their faces, even to bite them. Proneness to debauchery and every species of excess. Shamelessly indecent in thoughts, words, and gestures, especially towards evening. Delirium. Lascivious words and thoughts, with violent priapism. Lewd talk. Incoherent speech during sleep. Paroxysms of foolish gaiety, with great loquacity, or silent weeping, towards evening. Want of decision and will-power. Fits of dejection, apathy, insensibility. Indifferent to everything. Regards himself as more of an invalid than be really is. Delusion he is unfortunate. Disturbed about his health and social position. Paroxysms of anxiety, suffocation and fainting. Excessive nervous excitement; he is very easily frightened.

Head - Veins of the forehead and temples are distended. Contractive and pressive pains with drowsiness, but without sleep. Deep-seated pains. The hairs becomes white. Falling off the hair, especially in the evening. Pustules on the scalp, forming scabs like those of small-pox. Intolerable itching of the head, with burning ulcers.

Eyes - Rheumatic or gonorrheal ophthalmia. Fullness in eyes, turgid and watery.

Ears - Obstinate otorrhea. Offensive discharge.

Nose - Post-nasal catarrh. Mucus trickles from nose into throat with rawness of throat and hoarseness. Nasal catarrh, with fetid odor and catarrh of throat. Nasal catarrhwith greenish-yellow expectoration.

Face - Fullness of face or red and pale by turns. Lips puffed, dry and shining. Twist of mouth to one side.

Mouth - Aphthae of lips and gums. On attempting to smile or speak his mouth seems to twist to one side. Mouth as if dry, though moistened with an oily saliva, great thirst. Tongue furred and moist or very white.

Throat - Swallows saliva constantly to relieve burning and dryness of the throat. Catarrh. Vertigo - Frequent giddiness, so that he is afraid of falling. COMMENTS - Burning in throat with dryness, constant need to swallow saliva. Burning in stomach, abdomen, rectum, urethra and fossa navicularis. Prickling in soles of feet. Sensation of downward weight and pressure in region of femoral ring, worse on walking, riding or lifting. Stools and colic are worse at night in bed, better getting up and walking about. Urine foaming. Albuminous, bloody. Acrid leucorrhea in children. Skin diseases with kidney disorders. Nash defined its place in gonorrhea as “After the inflammatory stage is passed under the usual remedies for that stage, if there still remains burning in the urethra after urination and the discharge remains thick, yellow or pus-like (with Puls, the discharge is bland with Merc, all symptoms are Worse at night). Thin (gleety) discharge does not correspond to any of the three.” RELATIONS - Cop. with which it is compatible. Compare: ( 1 ) Cucúrbitas. (2) Cop.. Santa. (3) Pipermethyst. Pi per nigrum and Matico. Caps, Canth. (4) irritable bladder in females. Terebe., Cann-s. (5) lod. - membranous croup. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Burning in stomach and abdomen. Uneasiness, heat at pit with fever. Sour eructations. Nausea and vomiting.

Abdomen - Distended and very sensitive. Burning in stomach and abdomen. Burning and pressure about navel. Cutting pain in hypogastrium before stools. Sensation of weight, pressure and pain. Constitutions - Suitable to persons of bilious constitution with tendency to constipation.

Rectum - Constipation with hemorrhoids and tenderness of perineum. Burning and itching of anus. Relief of pains after stool. Loud flatus during stool. Long-continued tenesmus. Gelatinous stools of transparent mucus mixed with whitish, shining particles like rice, worse night, in bed, better getting up and walking about. Diarrhea with rumbling and cutting in abdomen and burning in rectum. Stools cold.

Male - Pale, copious, slimy discharge from urethra after use of alcohol. Prostatitis with thick yellow discharge. Pressure and heaviness in penis. Sexual excitement. Gonorrhea with profuse discharge and scalding pain during urination. Pale, copious, slimy discharge, causing soiled linen to become stiff. Thick, yellowish- green discharge with frequent obstruction of urethra.

Female - Urethritis. Vaginitis, chronic with profuse discharge. Acrid leucorrhea in young girls. Leucorrhea, profuse, acrid, offensive, yellow or green, with pruritus. Leucorrhea with erythema at inner surface of thighs. Menses too soon, often preceded and followed by leucorrhea. Menses scanty, and consisting mostly of leucorrhea. Food - Increased appetite. Craving for oranges, onions, almonds and nuts. Desires delicacies, acid fruits. Desires brandy, spirits, fresh bread. Mucus diarrhea worse fruit, acids. Unquenchable thirst with feeling of dryness of mouth and burning in throat.

Limbs - Sensation of heat in palms and soles. Numbness of fingers and toes. Wrists stiff and thickeraboutjoints. Acute, deep-seated pains. Lungs - Dyspnea. Catarrh of nose and throat with fetid odor and expectoration. Mucus trickles from posterior sinuses. Rawness of throat and hoarseness. False membrane in larynx, danger of suffocation. Hurried and noisy breathing. Impeded breathing with crepitant rales. Dyspnea and sense of suffocation.

Skin - Eruption all over body like urticaria. Roseolous papules without fever or itching. Intense itching. Skin diseases with kidney affections. Skin diseases with catarrh of bladder and urethra.

Modalities - Better from getting up and walking about. Worse from night, in bed.

Kidneys - Burning and itching in fossa navicularis. Hematuria. Cystitis. Urethritis with much mucus, especially in women. Cramp, cutting, burning in urethra after urination, with constriction. Stringy gonorrhea. Sensation as if bladder still contained water. Last drops of urine passed with pain. Urine frothy. Urine copious, dark. Urine, odor of violets. Nocturnal enuresis.

Cough - Cough seems totear bronchi. Cough in bronchitis. Incessant cough, bronchial. Barking and croupy cough with feeling as of a foreign body in larynx. During and after cough cold sweat upon breast and back, burning in abdomen. Cough with coryza and hoarseness.
