full:
PHARMACY - lie. Ficus religiosa. Ashwathya. Bo-tree. Pakur. N. O. Moraceae. India. Tincture of juice of fresh leaves mixed with equal parts of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bloody, discharges. Dysentery. Hematemesis. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Menorrhagia. Nosebleed. Typhoid. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Sarat Chandra Ghose of Midnapore made the first proving and thereby discovered its power to cause and cure hemorrhages of many kinds. Ghose related some striking cases cured with the remedy in cases of dysentery, hematemesis, hemorrhage of typhoid, bleeding hemorrhoids and nosebleed. General hemorrhages. Vomiting of a bright red blood. Hemoptysis. Menorrhagia. Profuse discharge of bright red blood, bearingdown pains in lower abdomen. Bloody urine. Very weak and restless. Headache, burning at the top of the head. Sight dim. MIND - Quiet and disinclined to move. Sad and melancholic.

Head - Burning at vertex, vertigo and slight headache.

Eyes - Sight dim.

Nose - Nosebleed.

Face - Face became yellow.

Stomach - Pain and sick feeling in stomach. Nausea, vomiting of bright red blood. COMMENTS - Dr. Ghose participated in his own proving, along with his wife and a dog. The dog, which was perfectly strong and healthy, received 40 drops of the tincture one morning. No result followed that day and the dose was repeated the next morning. The animal commenced and continued to vomit blood of a bright red color. It kept very quiet and was unwilling to move. After three doses of five drops of the tincture given in quick succession, the vomiting ceased. The same treatment (minute doses of the remedy) was effectual in arresting the effects of the drug throughout the provings. Mrs. Ghose took the tincture in 20-drop doses repeatedly throughout two days. On the third day dysentery and menorrhagia set in simultaneously. The blood was bright red. Other symptoms included a headache, very weak and restless, sight dim, burning at the top of the head. The face became yellowish, breathing difficult. She became sad and melancholic. With the profuse discharge of bright red blood there were bearing-down pains in the lower abdomen. Dr. Ghose took 40 drops in one dose. The result was a frequent desire to pass water, which gradually became bloody, containing much blood. Inclination to cough, causing him to spit blood. Slight headache, giddiness and nausea. Sight dim. Very weak and restless. The tincture was taken three drops every two hours, and after the third dose the symptoms vanished. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Acalypha, Ip., Am., Mill., Phos., Hirudo, Cact., Ferr. Thlaspi. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Abdomen - Bearing-down pains in lower part of abdomen.

Rectum - Dysentery with menorrhagia. Dysentery, bright red blood.

Female - Menorrhagia, bright red blood, bearing-down pains in lower abdomen.

Kidneys - Frequent desire to urinate. Urine contains much blood. Lungs - Difficult breathing, cough with vomiting of blood, pulse very weak.

name: Filix Mas
author: Murphy
constitution: Abdomen, bloated. Abortion. Blindness. Infertility. Miscarriage. Tapeworm. Worms.
keynote:
PHARMACY - fil. Filix mas. Male fern. Aspidium filix-mas. N. O. Filices. Dryopteri- daceae. Tincture of fresh root or fresh root grated. Maceration of fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abdomen, bloated. Abortion. Blindness. Infertility.…
full:
PHARMACY - fil. Filix mas. Male fern. Aspidium filix-mas. N. O. Filices. Dryopteri- daceae. Tincture of fresh root or fresh root grated. Maceration of fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abdomen, bloated. Abortion. Blindness. Infertility. Miscarriage. Tapeworm. Worms.

HERBAL - The male fem has been recognized as a vermifuge from the time of Galen. For worm symptoms, especially with constipation. Dioscorides credits it with the power of causing infertility and abortion.

HOMEOPATHIC - A fragmentary proving in Allen's Appendix records a case in which 15 to 20 drops of the tincture given three times a day to a woman suffering from bloated abdomen with more or less pain caused diminution of the bloating. Also, severe prolapse of vagina. Pain and tenesmus of bladder with copious and frequent emission of urine, with intense pain. Filix was then discontinued and Chim. relieved the symptoms. They did not return afterwards, except after much walking or standing. The leading symptoms include a pale face with blue rings around the eyes, and blindness from atrophy of the optic nerve. Torpid inflammations of lymphatic glands. Pulmonary tuberculosis in young patients, no fever with limited, ulcerated lesions. Gnawing, boring pains in abdomen, worse after sweet things. Tapeworms. Soporific conditions.

Eyes - Blindness, monocular amblyopia. Blindness, first mydriasis and amaurosis with normal fundus, eight days later, atrophy of optic nerve. Immobility of pupil.

Nose - Itching of nose.

Face - Pale face, blue rings around eyes. Female - Menstruation stimulated. Prolapse of vagina with pains and tenesmus of bladder and copious frequent emission of urine with internal pains. Abortion. Sterility.

Stomach - Nausea. Sick after taking food. Temperature - Violent rigor, fever, great pain in abdomen with diarrhea and constant vomiting. COMMENTS - C. S. Spencer recorded this effect from taking capsules each containing ten minims of the oil of male fem for tapeworm: “A feeling of nausea, abdomen became painfully distended with colicky pains. Menses returned after only one week's absence and continued profusely for three weeks. Very sick after taking her food. The worm was got rid of and the capsules stopped when these symptoms passed away.” Hering said the best time to give the drug for expulsion of tapeworm is in the summer when the fresh root can be obtained. If an ounce of the grated root is given in the forenoon, usually the tapeworm comes away in the afternoon. Teste used it successfully in a case of violent dyspnea without cough, with stitches in region of heart and obscure symptoms of pericarditis. The patient was a young woman of lymphatico-nervous temperament and was much weakened by long sickness. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aspidium alha- manticum. Panna - 3 doses, 2 grams each, all in half hour, fasting in a glass of milk. Tasteless and will remove tapeworm. (2) Ciña, Gran., Kousso. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Abdomen - Bloated. Gnawing and boring in bowels, worse eating sweet things. Great pain in abdomen with diarrhea and constant vomiting. Worm colic with itching of nose, pale face, blue rings around eyes. Painless hiccough.

Rectum - Violent vomiting and diarrhea. Ineffectual urging to stool. Pappy stools. Worm symptoms with constipation. Worm colic.

Limbs - Numbness of right wrist.

Sleep - Soporific condition. Restless and sleepless at night.

name: Flavus Bacillus
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better in the autumn. Better spring. Better from hot baths. Worse from cold. Worse heat. Worse at night. Worse in the morning. Worse on the left side. Worse after drinking wine..
constitution: Arthritis. Arthrosis. Brachial, neuralgia. Coughs. Dysmenorrhea. Dysphagia. Dyspnea. Endometriosis. Headaches. Intoxication. Otitis. Palpitations. Premenstrual syndrome. Rhinitis. Sciatica. Sinusitis. Thyroid, problems.
keynote:
PHARMACY - flav. Flavus bacillus. Neisseria pharingis Hava. Neissericeae. Micrococ- cales. A non-pathogenic bacterium found in the upper respiratory passages but was also found in cerebrospinal fluid during meningitis. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis.…
full:
PHARMACY - flav. Flavus bacillus. Neisseria pharingis Hava. Neissericeae. Micrococ- cales. A non-pathogenic bacterium found in the upper respiratory passages but was also found in cerebrospinal fluid during meningitis. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis. Arthrosis. Brachial, neuralgia. Coughs. Dysmenorrhea. Dysphagia. Dyspnea. Endometriosis. Headaches. Intoxication. Otitis. Palpitations. Premenstrual syndrome. Rhinitis. Sciatica. Sinusitis. Thyroid, problems.

HOMEOPATHIC - Flavusisabacteriumcalled Neisseria Phringis Flava, belonging to the Neisseriafamily of the Micrococcales order. These microbes are in the shape of shells arranged in pairs like coffee beans. They are Gram-positive. Neisseria Flava is an aerobic saprophyte found in the upper respiratory passages. Flavus is not considered to be pathogenic. Nevertheless, it was isolated from the cerebrospinal fluid of several children suffering from meningitis. It owes its name to the formation of a yellow pigment in the middle of the culture colony. Flav. shows signs of irritation in the eyes, nose and pharynx which can lead to spasmodic rhinitis. Sensation of a lump in the throat. Feeling like feathers in the throat (Kali-bi.). Feeling of gravel in the larynx after speaking for a long time. Thyroid problems. Headaches. Peri-orbital headaches, localized on the right side (Sang.). Pain at the level of the frontal and maxillary sinuses. Discharge from the eyes and nose. Tendency tocolds, coughs and expectorates. Slight localized trembling, particularly in the fingers. Intoxication. MIND - Low morale, exaggerates difficulties. Sensitive to others' emotions and being contradicted.

Head - Peri-orbital headaches, localized on the right side (Sang.).

Eyes - Per-orbital headache, localized on the right side. Eyes red in the evening, when tired. Eye fatigue. Eyes swollen in the morning, on waking, eyelids heavy. Conjunctivitis.

Ears - Frequent attacks of otitis, recurring. Pain in the right ear.

Nose - Nose dry with dry scabs. Nasal discharge of greenish pus (Kali-bi.). Sinusitis. Sneezes easily. Spasmodic coryza. Nasal congestion at night, one nostril becomes blocked. Bleeding from the nose in the morning on waking.

Mouth - Arthritis of the jaw with loose teeth.

Throat - Red, sore throat. Sore throat after having had wet feet. Throat dry with slight discomfort at night. Throat inflamed. Fre quent loss of voice. Dysphagia. Tickling sensation in the right side of the larynx. Dry cough, aggravated in the morning. Feeling that the hard palate is touching the tongue. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kali-bi. - Coryza and sinusitis with sensation of blocked nose and tickling in the nostrils. Thick yellow or greenish discharge, viscous or running, forming greenish elastic lumps, sticky, which leave the mucus membranes raw and burning. (2) Zinc - Also shows aggravation from wine, but the depressive condition is infinitely more accentuated. General weakness. Cannot keep his legs still. REFERENCES -Julian.

Stomach - Digestion bad. Digestive complaints after moist food. Frequent nausea after meals.

Female - Menses irregular, too early, of varying quantities with pale blood. Menses too frequent. Menses late with premenstrual syndrome. Loss of blood at ovulation. Dysmenorrhea. Endometriosis. Hot flushes, worse at night. Food - Complaints aggravated by wine (Zinc, Nux-v.).

Heart - Palpitations at night with feeling of fever, worse after drinking wine.

Back - Arthrosis of the cervical column with cracking. Neck pains. Cervical-brachial neuralgia. Pain in the back, spreading to both arms. Constitutions - Psoric, sycotic and tubercular constitutions.

Limbs - Arthrosis, rheumatic arthritis. Sciatica. Pain in the joints with cracking situated at the knees, wrists, shoulders and fingers. Pain in the left hip, left arm. Slight localized trembling, particularly in the fingers. Lungs - Dyspnea, worse at night, worse around 2 a.m., with waking and suffocation. Coughing in the morning for 1 hour, on waking.

Skin - Perspiration from the palms. Dry eczema of the palms. Ecchymosis occurring regularly from the slightest shock.

Modalities - Better in the autumn. Better spring. Better from hot baths. Worse from cold. Worse heat. Worse at night. Worse in the morning. Worse on the left side. Worse after drinking wine.

name: Flor De Piedra
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from open air, Better heat. Worse in the evening. Worse from exertion..
constitution: Cholecystitis. Colic. Colitis. Diabetes. Dysthyroidism. Emaciation, Epilepsy. Exophthalmus. Goiter. Headache. Hyperthyroidism. Hypothyroidism. Rickets. Vertigo.
keynote:
PHARMACY - flor-p. Flor de piedra. Lopho- phytum leandri. Balanophoraceae. South America. Tincture of whole dried plant Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cholecystitis. Colic. Colitis. Diabetes. Dysthyroidism. Emaciation, Epilepsy. Exophthalmus. Goiter.…
full:
PHARMACY - flor-p. Flor de piedra. Lopho- phytum leandri. Balanophoraceae. South America. Tincture of whole dried plant Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cholecystitis. Colic. Colitis. Diabetes. Dysthyroidism. Emaciation, Epilepsy. Exophthalmus. Goiter. Headache. Hyperthyroidism. Hypothyroidism. Rickets. Vertigo.

HERBAL - Flor de Piedra grows in the tropical forests of Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil. This plant is used by the natives for stomach and liver disturbances. In Pio Carrera's book on Brazilian phototherapy, rickets and epilepsy are also indicated.

HOMEOPATHIC - W. Schwabe brought back the plant from Brazil. In collaboration with others, he carried out a proving on sixteen provers (10 women and 6 men), using the 6x, 4x, 3x, and 2x potencies, on February 21. 1964. J. R. Reside undertook another proving in 1966-67. Finally, Juliette Fourmon undertook an extremely thorough clinical proving. Emaciation from the pituitary or the thyroid gland. Neuro-endocrine complaints. Congestion of the thyroid with vago-sym- pathetic disharmony. Pituitary diabetes. Cardiac complication of hyperthyroidism. Pain in the heart and liver. General nausea. Distention and spasmodic diarrhea. Constriction of the neck. Feeling of tightness around the neck. Headache, vertigo. Sudden tiredness, especially in the morning. MIND - Increase in general activity. Mentally alert, clear-headed. Bright, then slow. Confused, lacking focus. Depressed.

Head - Left frontal or temporal headache, ameliorated in the open air, increased in the evening. Headaches, as though the brain would burst with visual disturbances and zigzags at the edge of the field of vision.

Eyes - Eyes bloodshot. Stye on the lower right eyelid. Orbital pain of a pressing type, when reading. Diminution in visual activity.

Ears - Pruritus of the auditory canal.

Nose - Dryness in the nose. Fits of sneezing.

Mouth - Mouth dry with difficulty in swallowing. Ulcers in the mouth and on the lips and tongue. Heartburn. Diminution in sense of taste.

Throat - Throat dry, empty swallowing to clear the throat. Feeling of a lump in the back of the throat. Stabbing pain in the throat, worse during the morning. Vertigo - Vertigo and tendency to fall to the left. COMMENTS - Freiwald reported favorable results in thyroid infections, using the potencies 3x and 6x and in infections of the liver and bladder, using 4x and 6x. Juliette Fourmon reported some clinical successes in goiter cases, hyperthyroidism, and in a case of bilateral degenerative labyrinthitis. M. Tetau made a general review of thyroid disorders and their homeopathic and biotherapeutic treatment, noting the value of Lophophytum Leandri. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) lodum - Anxious, cannot stay still, emaciation, hoarseness, diarrhea. Precordial anxiety with palpitation at the slightestexertion. (2) HederaHelix. (3)Nat-m. - Emaciation of the upper part of the body, headache, dryness of the mouth and fissure on the middle of the lower lip. Abnormal desire for salt. (4)Tuberculinum - Asthenia, emaciation, erratic pains, constant need to move, diarrhea in the morning, sweating at the least physical or mental effort. REFERENCES-Julian.

Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Nausea and epigastric discomfort.

Abdomen - Wakes at 2 a.m. with abdominal pains, ameliorated by going to stool. Heavy, full feeling and abdominal distention. Pressure in the right iliac region. Cannot bear the pressure of underclothes.

Rectum - Tendency to diarrhea with grayish or pale yellow stools.

Female - Menses infrequent, abundant, but late by five days. Greenish vaginal discharge. Food - Extreme thirst.

Chest - Right subcostal pain. Feeling of oppression in the thorax, rather more to the right that the left side. Thoracic pain, worse by movement and deep respiration. Constitutions - Suited to tubercular, nervous, phosphoric or phospho-fluoric types.

Heart - Palpitations.

Back - Pain in the right shoulder on lifting the right arm.

Limbs - Painful drawing and pricking feeling in the left arm, elbow and hand, with formication in the left hand. Drawing pain in the right thigh down to the calf and heel. Sharp, cutting pain in the left knee, worse when walking. Heaviness in the legs. Right foot slightly edematous and sensitive to pressure. Feet cold. Lungs - Irritating, dry, hacking cough.

Sleep - Sleep disturbed. Fiery, hot feeling in bed.

Skin - Generalized pruritus, but particularly the ears, scalp, arms and face, abdomen and anal region. Marks on the thighs and lower limbs. Perspiration.

Modalities - Better from open air, Better heat. Worse in the evening. Worse from exertion.

Kidneys - Abundant urine.

Blood - Disorders of the basal metabolism. Hypo-cholesterolemia.

Temperature - Profuse sweating and hot flushes.

name: Fluoricum Acidum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better cold. Bending open air. Better cool bathing. Better walking. Better rapid motion. Better bending head back. Better short sleep. Better sitting. Better eating. Worse heat of room. Worse night. Worse morning. Worse warmth. Worse warm drinks. Worse alcohol, red wine. Worse sour foods. Worse rest. Worse rising. Worse coffee. Worse standing..
constitution: Abscess. Alcoholism. Alopecia. Bedsores. Birthmarks. Bone disorders. Brain, atrophy. Coccyx.pain. Dental, fistula. Dropsy.Edema. Exostosis. Eyes, disorders. Felon. Fistula. Fluoride, poisoning. Gleet. Goiter. Gonorrhea. Hair, loss. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Hydrocele. Keloids. Liver, induration. Locomotor ataxia. Nevi. Nose, inflammation. Nymphomania. Otorrhea. Peritonitis. Perspiration. Pityriasis.
keynote:
PHARMACY - fl-ac. Fluoricum acidum. Fluoric acid. Hydrofluoric acid. Made by distilling pure fluorspar (Calcium fluoride) in a state of fine powder with sulphuric acid. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscess. Alcoholism. Alopecia. Bedsores. Birthmarks.…
full:
PHARMACY - fl-ac. Fluoricum acidum. Fluoric acid. Hydrofluoric acid. Made by distilling pure fluorspar (Calcium fluoride) in a state of fine powder with sulphuric acid. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscess. Alcoholism. Alopecia. Bedsores. Birthmarks. Bone disorders. Brain, atrophy. Coccyx.pain. Dental, fistula. Dropsy.Edema. Exostosis. Eyes, disorders. Felon. Fistula. Fluoride, poisoning. Gleet. Goiter. Gonorrhea. Hair, loss. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Hydrocele. Keloids. Liver, induration. Locomotor ataxia. Nevi. Nose, inflammation. Nymphomania. Otorrhea. Peritonitis. Perspiration. Pityriasis. Satyriasis. Scars. Spleen, pains. Strokes. Suppuration. Syphilis. Teeth, decayed. Toothaches. Tongue, ulceration. Ulcers. Varicocele. Varicose, ulcers. Varicose, veins. Veins, diseased. Whitlow.

HOMEOPATHIC - Fl-ac. acts on the lowertis- sues of the body much like Sil., which it follows and precedes well, although their modalities differ, Fl-ac. is better from cold applications. Useful after the abuse of Sil. Slow, deeply destructive effects. Decay of long bones, ulcerations, bedsores, varicose veins. Necrosis of the bones, favors the expulsion of the necrosed part. Acts especially upon lower tissues. Teeth are deficient in enamel, black, rough, unsightly-looking. Early decay of teeth. Calcareous degeneration. Nails grow rapidly. Felon. Nevus, flat. Edema. Tissues are puffy indurated and fistulous. Dropsy with numbness or without. Old scars, scars become redder and itch. Red blotches on body which tend to desquamate. Small red spots here and there, worse by warmth, better in cool place. Discharges are thin, foul, acrid or salty, causing itching. Increased sensitiveness of vision and hearing. Glabella region bloated. Numbness of the part not lain on in brain diseases, spinal disorders. Goiter. Affinity for rectal, dental and lachrymal fistulas. Suffering if the call for evacuation is not immediately attended to. Old cases of nightly fevers, coming on periodically. Always feels too hot, wants to bathe in cold water. Patient is compelled to move about energetically. Hob-nailed liver of the alcoholics. Complaints of old age or the prematurely aged with weak, distended blood vessels. Especially adapted to chronic diseases with syphilitic and mercurial history. Secondary syphilis. MIND - Absent-mindedness. Forgetful in evening, better morning. Great loss of memory. Forgets almost everything. Forgets dates. Mistakes right for left. Opinionated, strong-minded. Domineering behavior. Irritability, sends the nurse home. Abuses and reproaches others. Irritability with absent persons. Sensitive to noise. Conversation aggravates. Depression of mind. Aversion to his own family. Aversion to those loved best (Sep.). Sits silently, does not utter a single word, nor answers anyone when questioned. Inability to realize responsibility. Shuns responsibilities. Indifference to business affairs. Indifference to loved ones, to relations. Anxious ideas. Apprehensive, causes sweat, better morning than evening. Fear of having a stroke. Sensation as if danger menaced him, but without fear. Impulse to walk fast, necessity to be always on the move. Becomes interested and converses pleasantly with strangers. Buoyancy of mind. Mentally elated and excited. Fears nothing and is self-satisfied. Cheerful during menses. Cheerful when walking in open air. Delusion, marriage must be broken. Thinks he must drive children out of the house, must dissolve marriage. Thinks he must get rid of servants. Stands on the street looking at women as they pass by, so great is his lust. Nymphomania.

Head - Atrophy of brain. Stunning headache, better urinating. Pressure on sides of head from within outward. Compressing pain in temples. Pressure in occiput. Pain along the sutures. Numb sensation in forehead. Puffy glabella. Congestion of blood to head during pregnancy. Decay of ossicles and mastoid with copious discharge, worse warmth (Sil.). Decay of skull bones. Exostosis. Decay of skin. Itching of head. Brittle hair. New hair dry and breaks off. Falling out of hair after fevers. Alopecia areata. Baldness. Scaly eruptions on head.

Eyes - Burning in eyes. Increased lachrymation. Chronic inflammation of lachrymal sac, worse cold air. Lachrymal fistula, worse] cold air. Violent itching of inner canthus. As if sand in eyes. As if something in the eyes, that could not be rubbed off, must wink. Sensation as of a cold wind blowing through the eyes. Left eye smaller than right.

Ears - Intolerable itching in ears. Itching momentarily better scratching, but followed by burning. Profuse otorrhea. Otitis externa. Great sensitiveness in morning to little noises. Difficulty in hearing human voices, with numbness of bones around ear. Deafness, better bending head back. Singing, ringing.

Nose - Red, swollen, inflamed nose. Fluent coryza during sleep. Sneezing with salivation. Chronic nasal catarrh with ulceration of the septum. Sudden copious watery discharge from eyes, nose and mouth. Nose obstructed and dull heavy pain in forehead. Itching on right side of nose. Cold water causes coryza. Posterior nares feel expanded, during a walk.

Face - Heat in face, wants to wash it in cold water. Pale. Exostoses of bones of face. Heat in face, wants to wash it in cold water. Crusta lactea, dry, scaly, itches very much. Suppurating tubercles in skin of forehead and face. Sweats on face. Right lower jaw swollen.

Mouth - Mouth coated with mucus in morning. Painful ulcer in right angle of jaw. Affects teeth and bones of upper jaw. Increased flow of saliva, with sneezing. Viscid, tasteless saliva in mouth. Syphilitic ulceration of mouth, which is very sensitive to cold.

Throat - Excessive pain, when swallowing or talking. Sore throat, worse inspiring cold air. Throat sensitive to cold, slightest exposure resulting in sore throat, with increase of pain and impeded swallowing. Constriction in throat, with difficult swallowing. Hawking of phlegm, mixed with blood. Red blotches, over palate and sides of cheek, bleeding easily. Throat intensely red and much swollen, with fetid breath, nasal voice. Goitre. Trachea sore and raw. Weak voice. Dryness in larynx and trachea. Itching in larynx, causes hawking and swallowing. Soreness and increased irritability in larynx with impeded respiration and wheezing. Syphilitic ulceration of throat.

Stomach - Frequent eructations and discharge of flatulence. Sour eructations. Stale eructations. Burning, pinching pain in stomach, before stool. Heaviness and weight in stomach. Heat in stomach before meals. Gnawing hunger, is always eating which temporarily relieves. Sour or stale belchings. Bilious vomiting on slightest errors in diet. Stomach symptoms, better tight clothes.

Abdomen - Ascites from hepatic disorders. Induration, enlargement and portal congestion. Flatus and belchings. Sensation of emptiness at the region of navel with a desire to draw a deep breath, better bandaging. Burning, pinching, about navel.

Rectum - Flatus and eructations with constriction of anus. Constipation. Itching and burning at anus. Bilious diarrhea with aversion to coffee. Diarrhea worse on alternate days. Warm drinks and salmon produce diarrhea. Itching in perineum. Very loose, bright yellow stools, with much mucus, preceded by considerable griping. Stools frequent and hard. Stools pappy, yellowish brown, fetid, with tenesmus and prolapsed anus. Sensations - Sensation as of a cold wind blowing under lids, even in warm room, as of air passing down from shoulder joint to fingers. Numbness of limbs even when not lain on. Increased ability to exercise his muscles without fatigue. Less affected by excessive heat in summer or cold in winter.

Male - Burning in urethra. Oily pungent smelling sweat on genitals. Dropsical swelling on penis. Gleety discharge at night, staining linen yellow. Varicocele. Swollen scrotum. Violent erections at night. Increased sexual desire in old men. Overwhelming sexual desire, keeping him awake at night. Enjoyment excessive. Gonorrhea. Sensation of fullness in spermatic cords. Sudden loss of sexual power. Impotence. Yellow drop from urethra in morning.

Female - Menses, blood thick and coagulated. Menses too early, copious, frequent, too long. Feels distressed if the flow is slightly delayed. Metrorrhagia with difficulty of breathing. Copious and excoriating leucorrhea, itching. Acrid leucorrhea. causes itching. Ulceration of uterus and os. Nymphomania. Food - Hungry. Averse to coffee. Desire for pungent, spicy, highly seasoned food. Desire for fancy dishes. Craves refreshing drinks. Craving for cold things. Craves cold water. Warm drinks produce diarrhea. Desire for wine. Worse from sweet things. Worse from coffee.

Chest - Oppression in chest, difficult breathing, great dyspnea, better bending backwards. Hydrothorax. Upper part of chest seems most affected. Scaly eruption on chest and arms. Itching under ribs left side. Constitutions - Suited to complaints of old age or the prematurely aged. Suited to the weakly constitutions, sallow skin, emaciation. Pale, miserable, cachectic, flabby and broken down patients. Dropsy of limbs in old, feeble constitutions.

Heart - Sore pain in heart. Pulse somewhat accelerated, only during exercise. Small, frequent pulse.

Back - Pain in third cervical vertebra. Coccyx pain worse motion and exercise. Bruised, in sacrum. Aching in sacrum and lumbar region, better stretching and bending backwards, esp. by pressure. Stiffness of nape. Lameness in back, hips and legs. Breasts - Nipples sore, cracked, itching. Itching on left breast.

Limbs - Dropsy of limbs in old feeble constitutions. Limbs go to sleep. Osteitis. Decay and necrosis, especially of long bones. Constant redness of the hands, especially the palms. Hot, sweaty palms. Inflammation of joints of fingers. Feeling of hair on back of fingers. Soreness between toes. Nails distorted. Nails crumble. Nails grow rapidly. Felon. As of a splinter under the nail. Nails corrugated lengthwise. Corns are sore. Necrotic bones. Ulcer over tibia.

Sleep - Sudden sleepiness. Drowsy and sleepy in early evening. Sleeplessness without inclination to sleep. A short sleep suffices and refreshes him. Sleep disturbed by accumulation of mucus in fauces. Sensation as if sleeping on side not lain on. Sleeplessness in evening from crowding of thoughts. Dreams towards morning. Dreams of fire. Dreams with amaurosis.

Skin - Dry, harsh, itching or cracked skin. Burning pains on small spots of skin. Itching, especially of the orifices. Itching in spots, worse warmth. Itching of scars. Keloids. Scars, surrounded by pimples, become red around the edges. Bedsores, worse warmth. Varicose veins. Atony of capillary and venous system. Tissues bloated. Nevus or birthmarks on children. Nails grow rapidly. Ulcers, red edges and vesicles. Ulcers on ankles. Syphilitic tubercles. Syphilitic rupia. Periosteal abscess. Hard, dry warts. Frequent small boils, carbuncles.

Modalities - Better cold. Bending open air. Better cool bathing. Better walking. Better rapid motion. Better bending head back. Better short sleep. Better sitting. Better eating. Worse heat of room. Worse night. Worse morning. Worse warmth. Worse warm drinks. Worse alcohol, red wine. Worse sour foods. Worse rest. Worse rising. Worse coffee. Worse standing.

Teeth - Affects teeth and bones of upper jaw. Great sensitiveness of teeth. Late dentition. Teeth, décay rapidly, worse at roots. Thin enamel. Teeth feel warm, heavy, rough. Dental fistula with bloody, salty discharge. Acrid, foul tasterfrom roots of teeth. Teeth coated with mucus in morning. Wisdom teeth come late. Toothache worse cold drinks. Toothache better until water becomes warm in mouth.

Tongue - Tongue, fissured in all directions, painful when talking. Ulcer on and under tongue. Tongue as if stiff, with restricted mobility. Tongue vivid red at tip and edges. Tongue coated yellow in centre. Tongue whitish and dry. Numbness and tingling of tongue. Pricking sensation of tongue. Vertigo - Vertigo with nausea, must sit down. Feeling as if in an earthquake. Vision - Amaurosis. Dark spot before eye, worse reading. Flashes like lightning. Red photopsia. due to retinal excitement. COMMENTS - Severe bone diseases and ulcers, where the bones decompose instead of healing. Necrosis of the bones, bone abscesses. Bone pains (Merc.. Calc-f.). For syphilis, when it causes ulcers and goes to the bones. Tendency to form ulcers on the skin and in the mouth that do not heal well, particularly in the elderly. Ulcers can have a red edge. Bedsores. Keloids that ulcerate or don't heal well (Sil.). Varicose veins that swell and ulcerate with severe burning pain, worse heat (Sec., Lach.). Varicose veins with itching, swelling and burning pains. Varicose veins or ulcers aggravated after each childbirth. Hot blooded. Worse heat. Better from cold washing and walking in the open air (opposite Sil.). Constant desire to walk in the open air, and does not fatigue. Hungry. Symptoms seem to move from below upward. For children with weak tooth enamel (Sil., Calc-f.), or whose teeth erupt rotten and abscessed (Kreo., Calc-f.). Generally a woman's remedy. Hate between spouses. Guernsey noted that it tends to affect the right ear, the left teeth, left hypochondrium, left side of the abdomen, right side and nape of the neck, and the right side of the back. McLachlan added that the left hand is affected rather than the right, and the pus tends to point on the dorsum of the finger. T. F. Allen noted its use for whitlow. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Thiosin. - action on scar tissues, adhesions, strictures, tumors. Calc-f., Sil. (2) Coca - fatigue, Coffea - toothache. (3) Cit-ac. and Sep. - aversion to one's family. (4) Ox-ac. - diarrhea worse from coffee. (5) Rhus-t. and Ruta - Coccyx, pain. (6) Sil. - fistula, onychia, bone diseases. Coccyx, pain. (7) Brom.. lod., Spong, and Kali-c. - goiter. (8) Staph. - teeth. Complementary: Sil. Compatible: after Ars. in ascites from gin-drinker's liver after Kali-c. in hip disease after Ph-ac. in diabetes. Followed well by: Sulph.. Nit-ac. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Liver - Ascites from hepatic disorders. Degeneration of liver in consequence of alcoholism. Soreness over liver. Hepatic disorders with ascites. Lungs - Difficulty of breathing with, or alternating with, metrorrhagia. Great dyspnea, better bending backwards. Wheezing. Difficult breathing, in afternoon and evening. Great dyspnea, has to be propped up in bed.

Kidneys - Involuntary urination at night. Increases urine in dropsy, with great relief. Burning in urethra during and after urination. Upward drawing in the urethra. Whitish or purple colored sediment. Urine pungent and fetid. Urine alkaline. Urine, scanty, dark.

Perspiration - Profuse and sour, offensive perspiration. Feels as if hot vapor were emitted from all the pores. Acrid, eroding sweat, excites itching. Sweat on diseased part. Sweats on hands and feet. One-sided sweat (left). Sweats in afternoon. Sweats during exercise. Sweat relieves. Excessive sweat on feet. Sweat promotes excoriation Fluoricum acidum and bedsores.

Temperature - Nightly fevers coming on periodically. Ebullitions of heat with pain in bones. Feels as if burning vapor were emitted from pores. General heat with nausea, with inclination to uncover. Face constantly hot, wants to bathe it continually in cold water.

Here the villagers and their livestock are chronically ill, while neighboring villages with no fluoride have no such illnesses. Premature aging is the overall effect. Children have brown decaying teeth; young adults often have none. Young men are bent over and crippled with pain in their joints and hips. Their skin is wrinkled and they look 60 at age 30 to 40. There is premature hardening of the arteries. Loss of appetite and sex drive by age 30. The rate of stillborn miscarriages by 4 months is extremely high. Fluoride damages enzymes which results in a wide range of chronic diseases. Fluoride causes breakdown of collagen. It also leads to irregular formation of collagen which serves as a major structural component of skin, ligaments, tendons, muscles, cartilage, bones and teeth.

full:
PHARMACY - foen. Foeniculum sativum. Fennel. Foeniculum vulgare. N. O. Umbel- liferae. Tincture of seed. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HERBAL - The fruit (seeds) are quite fragrant, and are among the most relaxing and least pungent of all the aromatics. They are eminently carminative, and quite diffusive; and are usually better received by the stomach than are cummin or dill seeds, being also more relaxing than these, but more stimulating than anise seed. Their principal use is in combination with senna, rhubarb, juglans, rhamnus, and other cathartics. The oil may be made into essence. From a very early period of medical history, fennel seed has been credited with the power of increasing the secretion of milk, (galactagogue.) Its use for this purpose is most extensive in Germany; but leading physicians of many countries ascribe to it excellent power in this direction. The infusion of the seed may be used without limitation. Huefeland employed it in the following combination: Fennel seeds, one drachm; sweet orange-peel, half a drachm; carbonate of magnesia, three drachms; sugar, two drachms. Mix the powders, and give a teaspoonful three times a day. This preparation is greatly extolled through Germany. Others have given formulas combining the fennel with anise seed, parsley root, licorice root, etc., and using an infusion freely. HOMEOPATHIC The whole plant has an aromatic odor and taste, owing to a volatile oil by which it is pervaded.lt is cultivated largely in Italy and Sicily for the sake of the shoots, which are eaten raw, or in salad, or boiled as pot-herbs. The odor of fennel-seed is fragrant, its taste warm, sweet and agreeably aromatic. It is among our most grateful aromatics, and in this country much employed in the old school as a carminative and as corrigent of other less pleasant medicines, especially senna and rhubarb. In infants it is employed as a tea, or injection, to produce the expulsion of flatus. In most of the ancient books on the practice of medicine we find it in common use as a modifier and corrective of cathartic infusions, to prevent griping, and to obviate flatulence. As far back as Hippocrates can its employment be traced. Pressure in the left upper jawbone, which soon ceases. Pungent pain in the right elbow joint, it recurs often during several days. Diarrhea. Increased secretion of urine. Excites the vascular system and the respiratory organs. REFERENCES - Murphy.

HOMEOPATHIC - A female remedy, affecting primarily the female hormonal system. Foil, in a homeopathic dilution could be indicated in premenstrual syndrome, as well as for all the functional symptoms present in a patient. Premenstrual syndrome. Weight gain without excessive eating, worse before menses or during ovulation. Premenstrual migraines. Congestive headaches, either with redness of the face or the opposite with pallor, but still with the sensation of chilliness at the limbs. Frequent ecchymosis, bruises very easily. Acne on the face and seborrhea of the nostrils. Hypersensitive to heat, noise and contact. Foil, in low potencies of 3x and 4c is an arouser to be given in cases of amenorrhea and insufficient menstruation. In 7c, it is a regulator. In 9c, it is a restrainer and a dose should be given either towards the tenth day of the cycle, when the pains predominate on the 14th day or 5 days before the beginning of menstruation, when the discomforts are predominant before the arrival of menses. MIND - Alternation of excitability and depression, worse before menses. Irritable and sensitive before the menses. Extreme instability with anguish, worse at nightfall. Sexual hyper-excitability. Fixed ideas of a sexual nature.

Head - Alopecia in women.

Eyes - Swelling with edema of the conjunctiva tissue.

Nose - Coryza with headache and profuse discharge. Hay fever.

Face - Acne on the face and seborrhea of the nostrils.

Throat - Swallowing of liquids very painful. Cannot bear pressure on the pharynx. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) The closest remedy is Lach. Like this remedy, it has: Alternating excitability and depression, extreme sensitivity to contact, amelioration by menstrual flow. But, unlike Lachesis, we do not find: Laterality or aggravation from sleep, but, on the contrary, aggravation during ovulation. (2) Sepia, Lac-c., Puls., Kali-c. REFERENCES - Julian.

Female - Congestion, uterine, and premenstrual pains. Vaginal, vulvar pruritus, worse before menses. Menses prolonged, blood bright red with clotting. Menses painful for the first few days. Leucorrhea. Yellow or brownish discharge, sometimes blood streaked, between menses, especially during ovulation. Small losses of blood during ovulation. Uterus is fibrous with metrorrhagia.

Lungs - Need for fresh air, takes large breaths of air and sighs deeply. Fitful cough, worse when in company, with sensation of constriction around the heart.

Back - Lumbar pains, worse during ovulation. Backache before menses.

Skin - Dry eczema, worse during ovulation, before menses. Dry eruption of the fingers with splitting and chapping of the skin.

Modalities - Better after the third day of menses. Better with movement. Better fresh air. Worse before menses. Worse during ovulation. Worse from heat and resting.

Bladder - Recurring cystitis in women. Breasts - Breasts enormous, swollen, cannot bear being constricted or touched. The pain is ameliorated or disappears with menses. Congestive mastitis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Formica rufa causes many rheumatic and gouty pains. Pains appear suddenly and dart from place to place: left, then right, then left. Pains are worse from motion, better pressure. Arthritis with sudden rheumatic or gouty pains. Chronic gout and stiffness in joints. Acute outbursts of gouty poisons, especially when assuming the neuralgic forms. The spinal cord is affected, paralyzes and spasms occurring. It affects the liver, kidneys and right side. Influence on theformation of polyps. Tuberculosis. Carcinoma, cancer. Apoplectic diseases. Lupus. Chronic nephritis. Atrophy of wounds. Takes cold easily. Clammy skin, disagreeable sweat during night, sweat without relief. Chorea from checked foot sweat. Complaints from over lifting. MIND - Indisposed, morose. Fearful, apprehensive. Exhilarated after pain. Remarkable and unexpected activity of the mind during the day with absence of usual dullness and sleepiness. Forgetful in the evening.

Head - Brain feels too heavy and large. As if bubbles bursting in forehead. Headache with cracking in left ear. Headache better after combing hair. Vertigo.

Eyes - Pain in the eyes on waking, better washing. Rheumatic iritis. Rheumatic ophthalmia. Macule and ulcers on cornea. Dim sight. Flickering before eyes. Pterygium. Spasmodic twitching of upper eyelid.

Ears - Ringing and buzzing. Deafness. Cracking in left ear with headache. Polyps. External sensitiveness of right ear and temple. Parts around ear feel swollen.

Nose - Nasal polyps. Coryza and stopped up feeling.

Face - Entire left side of face and cheek feel as if paralyzed.

Mouth - Water tastes sweetish.

Throat - Sore throat in morning with much mucus, worse left side. Hoarseness with sore throat. Pain in neck when hawking or gargling. Vertigo - Vertigo, all things seem to move to and fro, reeling of body. Pain in left supra-orbital region when going to bed with dizziness, blackness before eyes, better by sitting down. COMMENTS - Sensation as if brain too heavy and large. Sensation as if a bubble burst in forehead. Hering noted its use “in all kinds of apoplectic diseases. It strengthens the brain.” Cooper gave the 3x with success in cases of weakness of the lower limbs. J. W. Thomson reported the case of a man, aged 84, who had severe neuralgic pains between posterior of right ear and center of occiput. He apparently recovered, but returned eighteen months later with a steady, sore and burning pain in the same region, swollen and tender around, but especially behind right ear. He could only sleep in one comfortable position, which he could not describe, but only knew when he found it and he must be covered up warmly behind right ear and between that and occiput and neck. All on the right side. Better from taking right hand and rubbing gently behind right ear. Sweat afforded no relief, the whole head seemed to sympathize with the distress. He had dribbling of urine. Form, was given, six doses, one before each meal. On the second day towards evening, he felt worse, and on the third day there were twinges and spasms of severe pain in addition to the sore pain that he had experienced before. These gradually got better and on the fourth day even the soreness was much better. The main thing, however, was that he felt mentally better, said his mind and head felt stronger and from feeling depressed he had become cheerful and life did not seem the burden it had for some time past. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Formic acid, Ars., Bry. (2) Dulc. - Rheumatism. (3) Urt-u. - nettle-rash, gout, rheumatism. (4) Frag-v. - lack of breast secretion. (5) Trom. - Diarrhea. (6) Caps. - Burning pains worse by cold water. Compatible: after Cham. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Constant pressure at the cardiac end of the stomach, with burning pain. Pains shifts from stomach to vertex. Gas cannot be passed. Nausea with headache and vomiting of a yellowish bitter mucus.

Abdomen - Flatulence. Drawing pain around navel before stools. Dull pain in region of spleen. Hardening of mesenteric glands.

Rectum - Constriction in the anus. Drawing pain around navel before stool. Pain in bowels before stool with shuddering chilliness. In the morning, difficult passages of small quantities of flatus, afterwards diarrhea-like urging in the rectum. Light, foaming stools.

Male - Seminal emissions, weakness. Long- lasting erections after urinating in morning. Scanty ejaculation with incomplete erection. “Slothful to venery.”

Female - Menses scanty and pale with bearing-down pain in back. Menses appear eight days too soon. Ovarian cysts containing water or blood.

Heart - Uneasy pain in region of heart. Fluttering palpitations.

Back - Soreness in neck and up into head. Severe pain in left side of neck while chewing. Severe pain across sacrum and dorsum of each hand. Affection of spinal cord. Breasts - Violent penetrating pain in region of right nipple. Lack of milk in nursing women. Causations - Complaints from over-lifting. Checked foot-sweat. Wounds. Great liability to take cold, consequences of cold and wet. cold bathing, damp weather. Chests - Pleuritic pains. Coughs - Cough tedious and long-lasting, worse at night and worse motion. Cough with aching in forehead and constrictive pain in chest. Cough, mostly at night. Violent attacks of cough with vomiting, day and night.

Neck - Pain in neck when chewing, especially on closing jaws.

Limbs - Rheumatic pains, stiff and contracted joints. Rheumatism comes on with suddenness and restlessness. Muscles feel strained and torn from their attachment. Stiffness and contraction of joints. Hard nodes around joints in and out. Weakness of lower limbs. Paraplegia. Pain in hips. Itching in armpits in morning. Hands numb. Lungs - Nervous asthma. Hoarseness with dry, sore throat, with aching in forehead and constrictive pain in chest, pleuritic pains.

Sleep - Could get to sleep if she could get the right position. All night dry throat, woke her out of sleep. Disagreeable sweat during night, awoke with clammy skin. Wakes early and feels she has had sufficient sleep. On awaking, headache, vomiting with headache, pain in eyes, stitches in ears.

Skin - Red, itching and burning. Nettlerash. Hives in flat plaques. Nodes around joints. Wounds that atrophy. Profuse sweat without relief.

Modalities - Better warmth. Better pressure. Better rubbing. Better combing hair. Better after midnight. Worse motion. Worse sitting. Worse dampness. Worse cold washing. Worse cold. Worse before snowstorms.

Kidneys - Paralysis of bladder. Quantity of urine increased, urates. Urine like saffron, bright yellow, no sediment, passed frequently. Bloody, albuminous urine with much urging.

Temperature - Profuse sweat without relief.

PHARMACY - form-ac. Formicicum acidum. Formic acid. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis. Catarrh. Gout. Polyps. Tremors. Varicose veins. Vision, weak.

HOMEOPATHIC - Form-ac. is known to the homeopathic Materia Medica only in the preparation of Formica rufa, a tincture made of ants that contain the acid. Apis and other insects contain formic acid, as well as Urtica urens and many other plants. Form-ac. in small doses increases muscular strength and resistance to fatigue. Feels stronger and more fit in ordinary walking. Chronic muscular pains and soreness. Tremors. Gout and joint rheumatism, which appear suddenly. Pains usually worse on right side, motion and better from pressure. Chronic arthritis following an attack of acute rheumatic fever. Chronic arthritis in connection with gouty diathesis. Marked diuretic effect, greater elimination of products of disassimilation, particularly urea. Failing vision. Hering gave as an indication for Form-ac.: “Burning pain, burning from washing, renewed burning from cold washing.” In prescribing it for varicose veins, polyps, catarrh, Clarke ordered an ounce or two of a solution of formic acid to the proportion of one part of the acid to eleven of distilled water. Of this, one teaspoonful is taken in a tablespoonful of water after food once or twice daily. COMMENTS - Mr. R. Wallace Ellison of Richmond, sent three letters to Anshutz concerning his experiences with formic acid. “About two years and nine months ago I added to my daily diet from one to two grains of Formic Acid with the result that it has produced the following results in my body: Polyps and fibrous matter absorbed from my nose. Nose tongue, lips and some other parts greatly reduced in thickness. “Chronic catarrh of nose, throat and intestines practically cured. Stiff joints throughout the whole body have become loose. Short sight diminished by fifty percent. Eyes have changed in color from light slate gray to a darker shade. “Varicose veins in left leg and others at base of neck now of no consequence. Facial and bodily appearance so altered that even my mother is puzzled and I can meet and converse with people who formerly knew me very intimately without my identity being discovered. “I have also tried its effects upon a sickly and scabby pony and found it quickly restored the animal to health as well as giving it a beautiful, healthy crop of hair. Anyone who cares can produce this result in the case of an old pony. I hasten to add what I would have mentioned before, that the quantity taken during the last two years was not much over 1 grains daily. “I found that 2 grs. daily was too much for regular use, though it served the purpose. If my theory be correct, perhaps 1 grains daily would be the proper thing and best to be taken in the form of honey, raw juice of sugar cane, etc. “When I first commenced I used to drink about a pint of water with it, but now I just put the teaspoonful of acid into a very small quantity of water and drink it. It has a pleasant, 'fruity' sort of taste. I add a little citric acid and sugar to it and I believe this improves the effect. “Chronic arthritis of traumatic nature can be cured by formic acid. In the latter case Formic acid 6x showed quicker and better results than 12x or 30x which are indicated in the previous cases. In general the disappearance of the stiffness of the joint is the first sign of improvement. Then the pain and swelling cease gradually in 1-6 months time.” In the Homeopathic World of April, 1902, Dr. Dudgeon gave an account of the work of Dr. Edward Krull of Gustrow, who was led to think of formic acid as a remedy from its constant occurrence in the internal organs and soft parts of the body. He found it constantly present in the sweat of healthy persons, but very much diminished in or entirely absent from the sweat of persons affected with tuberculosis. He thought to supply the defect in tubercular subjects by introducing it into the system in material doses. He found no benefit when he gave considerable doses by the mouth, so he used hypodermic injections of the watery solution. After two years of experiments he found to his surprise that the more dilute his injections were, the more powerful the effects and he ended by giving injections of a dilution which corresponds to our 3c or 4c and waiting five or six months before repeating the injection. Dudgeon noted “He treated in this way with success externar and internal tuberculosis, chronic nephritis and malignant tumors. It was necessary for the success of the treatment that the nutrition of the body should be well maintained. In cachectic states the treatment is not indicated. It will be remembered that Hering mentions the case of an anemic woman who died from the effects of an ant-vapor bath. “The general effects which were observed in all the cases treated by Krull's method were: Immediate increase of nutrition, the appetite improved, the weight increased, all this without any material change in the diet. “In all the patients during the first months, sometimes every two or three days, sometimes at an interval of weeks, there occurred slight transient attacks of pain in the abdomen, on the right and left of the umbilicus, sometimes accompanied by urging to stool. “If several copious fecal evacuations occurred, this had no bad effect on the patient, they seemed to have a critical character. After the injection the menses came on earlier and were more copious, all diseased organs and parts showed greater activity. “In the first and second stages of tuberculosis cure is the rule. In the third stage the treatment only does harm, rapidly diminishing the strength. “The action is most remarkable in lupus. During the first days after the injection the effected part commences to grow vividly red, rises up somewhat and discharges moderately and is the seat of shooting pains occasionally. Curative action usually begins in the third week. “In carcinoma of the breast and stomach, the tumor first increases in size and becomes very sensitive and the skin over it feels warmer. The shorter the term the tumor has existed and the stronger the constitution, the sooner does reaction occur and the consequent cure of the disease.” In the concluding words of Dudgeon’s article, “Tuberculosis, chronic nephritis and carcinoma are not diseases in which we can claim a great amount of success. So where other remedies fail or cannot be discovered we may take Solomon's advice and ‘Go to the ant!'” RELATIONS - Compare: Formica rufa., Apis., Urtica urens. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.

HERBAL - An infusion of the root diminishes the size of the breasts and dries up the milk, useful in women who wish to wean their children. In ancient medicine, Fragaria vesca was used in decoctions of leaves, roots or fruit, ripe or unripe, or combinations of these. Fragaria vesca is commended by W. Salmon as a wash for sore-mouth, as a hemostatic arresting the menses and stopping “bloody- flux,” swelling of the spleen, many forms of skin eruption and for “clearing the complexion.” HOMEOPATHIC The allergic effects from those who are sensitive to strawberries have been utilized in homeopathy. The well-known “strawberry tongue” is an indication for its use. Dr. Burnett gave it as “pippy tongue.” Faintness, suffocation like a stroke, convulsions and death have resulted, general anasarca and especially swollen tongue. Profuse viscid sweat. Lippe mentioned “Tapeworm. Pain in chilblains in hot weather.” In two instances Clarke noted the indulgence in strawberries to revive symptoms of gonorrhea in men who thought themselves cured. A number of cases of sprue or pilosis have been cured by a diet of strawberries ad libitum. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Hydr-ac., Apis, Ars. Crat. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

HERBAL - Frankincense remedies appear in the Syriac Book of Medicine, ancient Arabic texts, and in Ayurveda and Chinese medical writings. Greek and Roman physicians used Frankincense in the treatment of a great variety of diseases. It is stimulant, but seldom used now internally, though formerly was in great repute. Pliny mentions it as an antidote to hemlock. The famous eleventh-century Arabian physician, Avicenna, recommended its cooling effects as a remedy for infections and illnesses that increase the body's temperature. Avicenna used it fortumors, ulcers, vomiting, dysentery and fevers. In China it is used for leprosy. Recently, the Frankincense boswellic acids that are a part of the resin it produces have shown some promise as a treatment for asthma and various inflamatory conditions. The inhalation of steam laden with the volatile portion of the drug is said to relieve bronchitis and laryngitis. The essential oil of Frankincense has been used for anxiety, stress, asthma, bronchitis, severe coughing, scars and stretch marks. This oil is rejuvenating to the skin, treating acne, bacterial and fungal infections, and to treat wounds and scars. Thus, it is used in cosmetics, soaps, and perfumes. The anti-inflammatory properties of frankincense very effective as a treatment for joint pain and arthritis. COMMENTS - Frankincense is used in incense and perfumes. Its principal use now is in the manufacture of incense and pastilles. It is used in plasters and might be substituted for Balsam of Peru or Balsam or Tolu. It is also a natural insecticide and was used ‘ in ancient Egypt to fumigate wheat silos and repel wheat moths. In Arabia, the smoke of burning frankincense resin is used to repel mosquitoes and sand flies. Researchers have found that burning frankincense indoors improves the acoustic properties of the room. In ancient Egypt the resin was a key ingredient for embalming the dead. RELATIONS - Compare: Myrrh, Camphor. REFERENCES - Murphy.

The womb is somewhat large, the pain in the feet considerable, depriving her of sleep.” “On condition that she abjures sleeping draughts once and for all, I undertake her case. This is an invariable condition with me, as it is quite impossible to really cure people who take hypnotics.” “I gave Fraxinus Americanus tincture. Ten drops in water at bedtime. March 3rd. Has done her much good, womb is lighter, and she is better able to do her work. HERBAL - Ash leaves were highly recommended by the medical alchemist Dr. Rademacher and were extensively used in Germany on his suggestion. In the Union Medical for Nov. 27, 1852, two French physicians, Drs. Pouget and Peyraud. detailed several case of gout and rheumatism cured by an infusion of ash-leaves in boiling water. Dr. Peyraud himself was one of those relieved. A commercial traveler, who had been gouty for twenty years and had saturated himself with the syrup of Boubee and other vaunted specifics, consulted Dr. Pouget. At this time he was almost constant prisoner in his room successive attacks. After eleven days' use of the infusion he was able to walk two kilometers (one and a quarter miles), in fifteen days he resumed his journeys and was able to travel without suffering from Bordeaux to Quimper. Acute and chronice painful gout and rheumatism. Joint rheumatism in numerous instances. COMMENTS - Anshutz recorded the case of Dr. Peyraud. In 1842, Peyraud had his first attack of gout, which was severe and lasted for twenty-five days. During the three following years the attacks increased in frequency and severity. Having derived little benefit from the remedial means that he had resorted to, he listened to the suggestion of one of his patients, an inhabitant of the department of Dordogne in France, who advised him to try an infusion of ash leaves. Informing Peyraud, at the same time, that his forefathers had been cured by this prescription and that many of the country people got rid of “their pains” by employing it. Dr. Peyraud took the infusion of ash leaves and from 1845 to 1849 had no fit of gout. He then had an attack, which yielded in five days to the infusion of ash leaves, used under the observation of Dr. Pouget. Dr. Pouget recalled that when he was a physician at Soreze in 1824, the peasants of that place had spoken to him of the great power which an infusion of ash leaves had in driving away pains. He afterwards discovered that it had been used forty years ago as a gout specific by the peasants of Auvergne. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Colch., Rhus-t. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Clarke.

HERBAL - In the American Eclectic Dispensatory, John King stated “Fucus vesiculosus, sea wrack or bladder- wrack, has a peculiar odor and a nauseous saline taste. The charcoal of this plant has long had the reputation of the deobstruent and been given in goiter and scrofulous swelling. “The dose is a teaspoonful of the tincture twice or three times daily in a well-developed case. Half a teaspoonful twice a day will answer in recent cases. Smaller doses seem not to produce any effect. The medicine is very unpleasant to the taste, but causes no disturbance after it has been taken. It ought to be taken, each dose in a few ounces of water and preferably between meals.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Fuc. is a tissue remedy of great power and must be compared with lod., of which it contains a large proportion. Digestion is improved and flatulence diminished. Obstinate constipation, forehead feels as if compressed by an iron ring. Very weak and restless. Thyroid enlargement in obese subjects. Obesity and nontoxic goiter, also exophthalmic. Goiter has been cured with it in teaspoonful doses of the tincture given two or three times a day.

Head - Intolerable headache, forehead felt as if compressed by an iron ring. Headache with hemorrhages. Burning at vertex. Nausea, vertigo, and slight headache.

Nose - Nosebleed.

Face - Face became yellow.

Stomach - Vomiting of bright red blood. COMMENTS - Anshutz wrote “The following letter, by Dr. J. Herbert Knapp to the Homeopathic Recorder, was publishedin 1896: ‘After treating many cases of exophthalmic goiter, I have come to the conclusion that I have found a specific for that disease in Fucus vesiculosus, (sea-wrack). I might record one case. “ ‘Mrs. Mary B., age 24 years, German, came into my clinic at the Brooklyn E. D. Homeopathic Dispensary to be treated for swelling of the neck of several years duration. I gave her the tincture of Fucus ves., thirty drops three times a day. The treatment began December 1, 1895 and patient was discharged cured, on October 2, 1896. Would be pleased to hear from any others who have had any experience with Fucus vesiculosus.' “So far as I now remember, this is the only hint I ever receive which led me to try in goiter. At the same time, I do not feel sure of this. I had met in some medical journal a statement respecting the relation of this drug to goiter, which fact led me to look it up in the ‘Eclectic Dispensatory.' But if so, I cannot recall the authority. “At all events, I was led to try the remedy in a pronounced case of goiter with such goods results that I have never since given any other remedy for that disease either in the exophthalmic or in the uncomplicated form. “What is more, I have never known it to fail to cure when the patient was under thirty years of age. After that time of life or about that period, it seems to be no longer efficacious. “I have now used it on more than twenty- four cases with the same unvarying result and never with any other result-that is, no unpleasant consequences have ever accompanied or followed its use. “I published this fact in the medical investigator after I had used it in a few case and again announced it in the Chicago Homeopathic Medical Society still later and again have frequently repeated it with growing confidence and of greater numbers of cases in medical societies in colleges and in private conversation with physicians. “And yet the fact is so utterly unknown that your journal published Dr. Knapp’s inquiry respecting it, which shows how easily a good thing may be forgotten. Also how readily a genuine specific may be superseded by a host of abortive procedures right under the eyes of the profession. It is most probable that more real good remedies have been forgotten or cast aside in medicine. “Respecting this Fucus vesiculosus and its use in goiter, I would like to add a few words. The drug is of variable quality. If one specimen fails to give satisfaction it ought to be discarded and another tried. The pharmacist must be importuned to make special efforts to give us an article that is not inert, but contains all the activity that belongs to the drug. “Time is required for effecting a cure. This varies according to the age and size of the goiter. Three months may suffice for a small goiter of one year's growth. Six months may be required for one twice as large and of longer standing. A year and a half is the longest period during which I have had to continue the medicine. But during all that time the goiter was manifestly diminishing.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Phyt., Thyr., Bad., lod. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke.

The keynote is nutrition, and this nosode might suitably be named “the children nosode.” Clinically useful for the nutritional disorders common to children. For children fed on artificial food who have poor digestion. Affects the digestive tract. Inability to digest fat, celiac disease, ketosis intestinal infantilism. Malnutrition, either from lack of adequate diet or failure to metabolize, e.g. in steatorrhea, celiac disease or following gastric operations and in some cases of colitis. Indicated by marked emaciation, marasmus, especially in children, the elderly, or with malignant disease. Growth disorders. Poorly nourished bodies and poor muscular development, but with active minds. Restless, lack of attention. Hypersensitive to physical or psychological impressions. Fear of the dark and of being alone. Urticaria. MIND - Hypersensitive to all impressions. Restless. Mental uneasiness. Pessimistic, lack of confidence. Fear of heights, of the dark and of being alone.

Eyes - White sclerotics. Styes.

Ears - Otorrhea, worse when teething.

Nose - Polyps. Catarrh.

Mouth - Herpes. Dry, scaly eruption. Salivation. Deep fissures in tongue. Teeth black.

Stomach - Pain in stomach. Dilated stomach. Vomits everything, worse after sweets. Headache and vomiting. Acidosis attacks. COMMENTS - Ghosh noted “Gaertner in 30c potency may be used in extensive suppuration with intestinal disorders in small-pox.” E. Paterson thought that Gaert. may help in teething troubles where Cham, fails. Defective digestion of fat as of Puls, has a worthy trial of this remedy. “In all varietiés of neurasthenia, I know of no single remedy to compare with the Gaertner nosode.” Wheeler noted: “For cases of children who get a discharging ear every time they cut a tooth, give one dose of Gaertner 30, followed the next day by the dose of Silica 30c and repeat the Gaertner as soon as there is any ■'ign of a further out break of this ear discharge.” Griggs indicated that “it is helpful to make a comparison and to remember the Dys-co. child whose nervous tension expressed itself by an uneasiness of the muscular system. Although fidgety and uneasy, the shyness of his temperament would prevent him from leaving his chair while you are taking the preliminary notes in your consulting room. “The Gaertner child has mental uneasiness. He must know the reason for everything you do and for what purpose you use this or that article lying on you desk or somewhere in the room. Furthermore, he will proceed to make close inspection of it, but you will notice that his attention is not held long on any subject.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) The remedies most closely associated with this nosode are Dys-co., Phos., Sil. and Merc. REFERENCES - Bach. Boericke. Paterson.

Abdomen - Chronic gastro-enteritis, tabes mesenterica.

Rectum - Constipation. Blood and mucus in stool. Diarrhea offensive, attacks every few weeks. Itching of anus. Worms, threadworms (Cina).

Male - Hydrocele.

Female - Profuse, offensive leucorrhea. Pruritus vulvae. Food - Desires oatmeal, cheese, eggs, milk, pudding, sugar and sweets. Averse to bread, butter, butcher meat, and fish.

Chest - Bronchial colds. Nocturnal coughs. Constitutions - Fair hair, blue eyes, freckles. Pale, thin. Long, black eyelashes.

Back - Severe pain in hip and back.

Limbs - Fibrositis. Sciatica. Shoulder rheumatism, worse at night. Rheumatism hands and feet. Chilblains on hands in winter. Bites nails. Pes planus. Soles of feet covered with blisters, itch and are worse at night.

Sleep - Desires light in room. Desires company, especially mother. Late in falling to sleep. Sleep walking. Restless sleep, night terrors.

Skin - Urticaria, heat spots. Circinate eruption on sternum. Eruption on back, head and neck. Boils on arms and legs. Perspiration, worse at night.

Kidneys - Blood and mucus with urine. Burning in urethra.

Increases the quantity and quality of the milk in nursing women, it also improves the appetite. An excellent tonic in cases of anemia and impaired nutrition. Backache and debility. Dorretta gave Galeg., in liquid extract of the leaves, for a common form of backache, which he located in the kidney though it is unaccompanied by any sign of kidney disease. Carron de la Carriere tested its action on the milk glands of nursing women. He found it rapidly increased the quantity and quality of the milk and increased the woman's appetite. HOMEOPATHIC - Gallic acid is the well- known astringent, derivative of tannic acid, obtained from galls or oak-apples. It is used in old-school practice as a local application to arrest hemorrhages and in popular practice to check excessive menstruation. A case is recorded in which the application of an ointment containing gallic acid or the insertion of a tannin suppository for hemorrhoids caused an attack resembling hay asthma with an eruption of urticaria. The experience was repeated several times before the cause was discovered. This is sufficient to show that Gall-ac. is homeopathic to pulmonary cases in which it has been largely used by the old school as well as the new. Pulmonary hemorrhage, excessive expectoration, and the nightsweats of tuberculosis. Tuberculosis. Weakness with irritability. Excessive dryness of mouth and throat. Sense of contraction of anus. Jerking of limbs. Itching of skin. MIND - Wild delirium at night, very restless, jumps out of bed, sweats. Rude, abuses every one. Cursing. Strange speech. Jealousy. Afraid to be alone.

Eyes - Photophobia with burning of lids. Head - Pain in back of head and neck.

Nose - Thick, stringy discharge from nose.

Throat - Much mucus in throat in morning. Dry throat at night. COMMENTS-Marcy, of New York, recorded the case of a young woman who had a cavity in the left lung with purulent expectoration, night-sweats, evening fever, pulse 130. Under the prolonged use of Gall-ac. lx she recovered her normal health except that the left lung remained dull and she had great shortness of breath on the slightest exertion. Her flesh, strength and general appearance were as when she was in perfect health. Bayles said Gall-ac. rapidly checks secretions, give general tone to the stomach, increases appetite, and removes constipation. Heartburn. Hematuria. Hemophilia. Passive hemorrhages when pulse is feeble and capillaries relaxed, cold skin. RELATIONS-Compare: ( l)Querc.,Tann-ac., Bac., Ars-i., (2) Phos. relieved pain in right lung. (3) Ars., lod. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Rectum - Copious stool, anus feels constricted. Chronic mucus discharges. Faint feeling after stool.

Kidneys - Kidneys painful. Distress along ureters into bladder. Dull heavy pain in bladder, directly over pubis. Urine loaded with thick, cream-colored mucus. Hematuria. Lungs - Pain in lungs. Pulmonary hemorrhage. Excessive expectoration. Much mucus in throat in the morning, dry at night.

HOMEOPATHIC - Affects the stomach and bowels, chiefly known as a remedy for a diarrhea similar to Crot- t. Burning in anus after stool, anus sore and excoriated. Profuse watery diarrhea, particularly with elderly people. Stool preceded by excessive cutting about navel. Stool is expelled all at once after considerable urging and is followed by a feeling of great relief. Stools are yellow, green, bloody, lienteric. Frightful vomiting and purging with fainting. Burning in the liver. Pain in small of back, as if bruised or sprained. Pain in sacrum, resulting from a blow. Gnawing pains in the coccyx. Burning pains. General soreness. Rheumatic symptoms. Periodic symptoms. MIND - Irritable in morning on waking. Despondency, sadness. Cheerful and talkative. Feeling of ease, great lightness of all his motions.

Head - Gastric headaches. Head hot, face red, during attacks of diarrhea. Heat rises to head, with sweat. Heavy sensation with inertia and drowsiness. Sensation of great coldness in left temple as from a wet cloth. Vertex as if bruised, in forenoon, better open air. Oppressive pain with heaviness in forehead. Compressive pain. Pain in coronal suture.

Eyes - Burning in eyes. Itching and burning in eyes. Itching of eyelids, he rubs them. Eyelids stick together with sneezing. Eyes as if sticky and dry. Nightly agglutination of lids, burning in morning. Violent burning of eyes with photophobia. Smarting of eyes with lachrymation. Very severe pain in eyeballs.

Ears - Ringing in left ear all the time. Lancination pain in ears.

Face - Swelling of face. Swelling of eyelids, nose and lips. Upper lip swollen. Itching, smarting on right cheek, chin and upper lip.

Mouth - Aphthae. Deep ulcers in mouth, inner side of lips and cheeks. Bitter taste in mouth. Feeling of coldness at the edge of teeth. Burning vesicles on inner side of lips. Dryness of mouth. Clammy, adhesive state of mouth. fióse-Violent chronic sneezing, in daytime only. Smarting as if a sore pimple existed immediately below right nostril. Dryness of right nostril. Much mucus in nose, smelling like pus. Tendency to hemorrhages from nose and lungs.

Throat - Swollen sensation. Violent stitches in right side of throat. Pain as from soreness in throat. Rawness and burning in throat, causes constant hawking. Sore, in throat. Scratching sensation in larynx. Tickling in larynx and trachea from epiglottis to pit of throat.

Stomach - Frequent violent empty eructations. Gulping up of sour water. Gnawing pain in stomach. Emptiness in stomach and abdomen. Great irritability of the stomach. Pain in the stomach after food. Acute dart ing, stitching pain in stomach. Nausea, inclination to vomit with accumulation of saliva in mouth. Frightful vomiting and purging, with fainting. Ulcerative pain in stomach, better after eating. Vomiting and purging with fainting.

Abdomen - Gurgling in abdomen, as of fluid running from a bottle. Rushing sounds in abdomen as from motions of air. Tenderness in epigastrium. Pain and distention of abdomen from flatulence after stool. Rumbling and rolling. Ileo-cecal region sensitive to pressure. Pinching pain in abdomen immediately after eating.

Rectum - Burning and heat in anus during stool. Tenesmus after stool with burning in anus. Pinching, gurgling in bowels, then sudden yellow or green. Diarrhea alternating with constipation. Hard, insufficient stool, with strong urging. Dysentery, with retained stool, with pain in sacral region. Frequent emission of flatulence. Thin stools coming out in prolonged gushes with burning at anus. Diarrhea with sudden and forcible ejection of bilious stools. Diarrhea after drinking ale. Profuse, watery diarrhea in hot weather, particularly old people. Yellow and green diarrheic stool, mixed with mucus. Stools of dark green mucus, offensive, corrosive. Infantile diarrhea.

Male - Gleety discharge agglutinating orifice of urethra.

Female - Menses too early and too profuse. Menses long-lasting. Congestion to sexual organs. Leucorrhea. Food - Aversion to food. Violent thirst in evening. Appetite good, but a little food satisfies. Thirst after dinner. Thirst during chill. Great thirst, in chronic diarrhea. Worse after drinking ale.

Chest - Congestion of blood to chest. Chest, sore and raw. Pressure and weight in chest. Pressure pain in middle of chest. Sharp pains in sternum. Sharp pains going from both sides of chest towards each other.

Back - Pain in coccyx. Small of back as if bruised or sprained. Gnawing pain in coccyx. Pain and itching between scapula. Cutting pain across top of sacrum and in left hip. Cutting pain in muscles just above sacroiliac symphysis on left side.

Limbs - Stinging and numb feeling in ball of right thumb. Tearing pain in shoulders. Sharp pain, in upper limbs. Itching blisters on both hands, at first pale, afterwards red. Severe aching deep in hip, and severe cutting pain about trochanter major. Aching pain in knees. Cramp in calf with contraction of toes. Heaviness and languor of feet.

Sleep - Sleepiness, great inclination to sleep. Sleeplessness from weight on chest. Anxious, vexatious dreams. Dreams with broken sleep.

Skin - Violent itching in various parts of body, burning after scratching, worse evening and night. After scratching, burning and ulcerative pain, with swelling and redness of parts, worse evening and night. Biting as of ants over whole body, worse 1 evening and night. Itching on various parts of surface pleasantly better gentle friction. Itching and formication here and there all night. Pemphigus.

Modalities - Better by motion. Better in open air. Better after stools. Better sitting up. Worse evening and at night. Worse motion. Worse in open air. Worse after stools. Most symptoms come on while sitting, and go off during motion in open air.

Tongue - Burning, smarting and dryness of tongue and throat. Burning of anterior half or only tip of tongue, which feels hard. Raw, rough feeling in fauces and at root of tongue. Vertigo - Vertigo during rest or motion. Vertigo in morning. Vertigo on rising. Confusion of head with feeling of reeling or motion from side to side. COMMENTS - Gamb. painted on the chest in lung tuberculosis was considered by Abrams a specific. Also incipient diarrhea cases were symptomatically cured in several weeks. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Coff., Coloc., Kali-c., Op. Compare: (1) Crot-t., Aloes, Podo., Puls. - cough better sitting up, better open air. (2) Apoc. - stool expelled all one, but Gamb. has cutting before and better after stool. (3) Crot-t. has stool in one gush, but Gamb. is not worse from least food or drink like Crot. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Liver - Burning in liver. Lungs - Expectoration of blood.

Kidneys - Sharp pain in left kidney. Infrequent urination. Increased secretion of urine. Urine smells like onions. Urine diminished in dropsy.

Cough - Dry, with hoarseness and hawking of mucus. Severe cough, at night, compelling him to sit up, with easy expectoration of mucus. Cough better sitting up.

Perspiration - Sweats all over, at night. Sweats on awaking at 4 a.m. Cold sweats on limbs, during stool.

Temperature - Violent chill, beginning in back. Chill with empty eructations. Internal and external coldness from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m. Violent shaking chill at 7 p.m., beginning in back. Sudden shaking chill at night, waking him from sleep, and suddenly disappearing. Chill with chattering of teeth and violent thirst. Increased heat with anxiety.
