HOMEOPATHIC - The hot springs of Wildbad Gasterin in Salzburg. Austria, contain sodium sulphate predominantly, but also silicic acid, potassium sulphate and carbonate, lithium chloride, magnesium carbonate, ferrum carbonate, aluminium phosphate and traces of calcium fluoride, strontium, arsenicum, titanic acid, rubidium, cesium, also free carbonic acid. Lapis albus is a kind of gneiss found in the spring. It is a silicofluoride of calcium. Constantin James described the effects of the baths as a “General unpleasant sensation. Instead of expanding (as would be expected in a warm bath) the skin is drawn up upon itself as if by a tight astringent. There is slight dyspnea, the abdominal walls draw together, the testicles rise to the inguinal rings. “Soon an unusual warmth, accompanied by shocks and tremors, spreads throughout all the limbs. The pulse becomes hard and vibrating, the face becomes suffused, there is humming in the ears. It is now time to leave the bath to stay longer is attended with danger. “Then after the seventh to the fourteenth bath the thermal influence tends to concentrate itself entirely on the nervous system. Thus it seems to the patient that an increase of vitality spreads through his whole being, he feels more active then before, the longest walks cause hardly any fatigue and that is promptly repaired by sleep. “Among individual symptoms noted are diminished secretions. Activity of all the veins, excitement of the circulation. Weakness and weariness with dragging sensation in the abdomen, as if it were too heavy. Exhaustion and inclination to sleep. “Takes cold very easily, which was caused then cured. Pulsation in the body, especially in the arms with jumping in them. Contractive sensations predominate. Scar tissues and callosities are affected. Worse before a storm.” COMMENTS - The baths affect phlegmatic patients in an increase of force and tone, causing the disappearance of involuntary losses of semen. In irritable temperaments it will provoke erotic dreams and unwanted excitement, in such cases the waters are aphrodisiac. Sensation of indescribable mental and physical comfort runs through all the tissues during the bath. Predominantly influences the sexual system. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lap-a., Fl-ac. Sil., Canth., Phos. REFERENCES - Clarke.

HERBAL - An evergreen trailing vine found in cool, damp woods. The oil contains methyl salicylate and is one of the sources of salicine.

HOMEOPATHIC - Several cases of poisoning with the oil have been recorded in which symptoms of acute gastritis appeared. Prolonged vomiting, set up afresh by the least thing taken, as a cup of water. Severe pain in epigastrium. Slow, laborious breathing. Insensibility and hot skin. Inflammatory arthritis, rheumatism, sciatica and other neuralgias. Pleurodynia. Bladder and prostatic irritation. Kidney inflammation. Undue sexual excitement.

Head - Neuralgia of head and face.

Ears - Marked dullness of hearing. Food - Inordinate, uncontrollable appetite for food. Irritability of the stomach, everything, even cold water, is immediately rejected.

Stomach - Acute gastritis, severe pain in epigastrium. Prolonged vomiting. Uncontrollable appetite, with irritable stomach. Stomach pain from nervous depression.

Abdomen - Very severe pain in epigastrium and inferior part of the hypochondria, greatly worse by pressure of finger.

Chest - Pleurodynia with pain in anterior mediastinum.

Skin - Smarting and burning. Intense erythema, worse cold bathing, better olive oil and cool air blowing on part.

Tongue - Tongue dry, smooth and slightly swollen. Speech rather indistinct from the swelling. COMMENTS - B. F. Lang related his experience with material does in ciliary neuralgia, facial neuralgia, gastric, ovarian, uterine and menstrual neuralgias, sciatica and inflammatory rheumatism. Anshutz wrote on the action of Gaultheria: “My attention was first called to its use about ten years ago southern Ohio, where I received most pleasing results in the treatment of inflammatory rheumatism. Afterwards to complaints in form of neuralgia.” “While I am not a champion of any specific, I want to say that this drug has given me the quickest and most satisfactory results of any remedy in the Materia Medica. If there is anything that a person wants relief from quick and now, it is from these excruciating pains.” “Often was I called to treat some obstinate cases of ciliary neuralgia or facial or in fact nearly every form of neuralgia and found my skill taxed to its utmost to bring out the balm. Did I find it in the homeopathic indicated remedy? I trust so, but not in any Materia Medica. I don't say but what I got some results from them, but I found it in this a “helper”, it came to my relief immediately and to the great comfort of the patient.” “In severest cases of neuralgia of the head and face it would do its work quick and well. Equally well has it served me in very severe cases of neuralgia of stomach and bowels, while for the past few years it has done faithful work in ovarian and uterine neuralgia following or preceding difficult menstruation. I have many a dear friend today whose relief from suffering was found in this remedy. I am satisfied that it should be given a prominent place in our Materia Medica.” “Lest this article should become tedious, I will cite a few cases. Mr. A., traveling man from Chicago, a few years ago called on me for temporary relief of a severe case of ciliary neuralgia. He had suffered for many years with it, every spring especially and that he had consulted great numbers of physicians of Chicago, Milwaukee and Cincinnati. He said, “had taken bushels of drugs, both old and new school,” with only temporary relief.” “So he expected nothing more, as he was told he must wear it out. I told him I thought I could give him relief. I furnished him one- half ounce of Gaultheria with directions to take, did not see him again for two years.” “When he came into my office one day and greeted me by saying I was the only man that could ever give him any permanent relief from his sufferings, that he never had any return after first day taking medicine.” “Miss B., dressmaker, came to me suffering terribly with facial neuralgia and greeted me similar to No. 1, that she expected nothing but temporary relief, as she had been afflicted for a long time. Gave her 2 drachms of oil of Wintergreen told her to take one dose immediately and another in two hours if the pain did not quiet down.” “She was careful to ask if it was an opiate, as she objected to that. I assured her it was not, saw her next day, said that pain disappeared and had not returned. I was acquainted with the lady for three and one- half years and she only had one return of the disease, which the same remedy relieved immediately. Many cases more could I cite in which it never has failed me.” “Another case: Mrs. G., 1 was called to relieve a severe case of neuralgia of stomach and bowels this last summer, who had been under the care of two of my worthy competitors. They had exhausted their pill case and for about three weeks the poor woman had suffered everything but death itself.” “After diagnosing the case I put her on this remedy and in two hours she was relieved. After two days was able to be about and cured shortly by no other remedy than it. I want to say you will find a true friend in this remedy in all forms of neuralgia and only give a few suggestions now, but if it should be necessary could give scores to prove its value. I mentioned in the beginning that it had been of great value in inflammatory rheumatism.” “A word as to the best way of giving the drug. I have found that the dose should never be less than five drops and if pain is severe fifteen drops repeated in half hour afterwards two hours apart. For adult it may be necessary to give twenty drops at first. It always should be dropped on sugar and taken.” “One suggestion: I would like to have it put in a tablet of about two to five drops pure oil, as 1 think it could be taken more satisfactorily. While the crude oil is very pleasant to take at first, yet, on account of its strong odor, will nauseate after awhile if not removed from room. I am confident that if you make this into a tablet and place it among your remedies you would have a weapon that you could place into the hands of doctors of untold value in these troubles.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bry., Rhus-t., Salol., Nat-sal., Kalm., Led.. Spirae. (2) Gaultheria contains Arbin., Sal-ac. (3) Methy-sal. - an artificial Gaultheria oil for rheumatism, especially when the salicylates cannot be used. Itching and epididymitis, locally. (4) after Canth. in bums. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Clarke.

PHARMACY - gels. Gelsemium sempervirens. Yellow jasmine. Gelsemium lucidum. Yellow jessamine. Gelsemium nitidum. Bignonia sempervirens. N. O. Loganiacee. Tincture of the bark of the root. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Anxiety. Aphonia. Astigmatism. Bad, news. Bilious fever. Brain, disorders. Chills. Choroiditis. Chronic, fatigue. Colds. Coma. Constipation. Convulsions, Deafness. Debility. Dengue, fever. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Diplopia. Drug, overdose. Dupuytren'scontraction. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Emotional, shock. Epilepsy. Esophagus, stricture. Eyes, disorders. Fatigue. Fevers. Menstruation, disorders. Metrorrhagia. Multiple sclerosis. Muscle pain. Muscular, weakness. Neuralgias. Nystagmus. Paralysis. Parkinson's disease. Paraplegia. Pregnancy, toxemia. Ptosis. Puerperal, convulsions. Remittent, fever. Retina, disorders. Rheumatism. Salpingitis. Sexual, excesses. Sleep, disordered. Spasms. Sun, headaches. Sunstroke. Teething. Tic douloureux. Tobacco, effects. Tongue, disorders. Toothache. Tremors. Uterus, disorders. Ver- tigo. Viral infections. Voice, loss. Weakness. Writers' cramp.

HOMEOPATHIC - First introduced by Hale, Gelsemium belongs to the same order of plants as Nux-v. and Cur., and ranks among the vegetable polycrests. Like its botanical relatives. Gels, is a great paralyzer. Mental and bodily paresis. Sluggish mind. Relaxed muscular system, limbs feel so heavy he can hardly move them. Functional paralysis of all descriptions, of various groups of muscles. Various degrees of motor paralysis. Ptosis in the eye muscles and diplopia. Loss of the ability to swallow. Diarrhea from depressing emotions or bad news. Post-diphtheria paralysis. Muscular weakness, lack of muscular coordination. In muscles, especially in the limbs, it causes overpowering aching, tiredness, heaviness, weakness and soreness. General prostration and complete relaxation. Dizziness, drowsiness and trembling. Tremors or twitchings of single muscles, face, chin tongue etc. Hysterical convulsions. Chorea of pregnancy. Parkinson’s disease. Body feels light in nervous, hysterical subjects. Mental prostration, anxiety. Lassitude (Mur-ac.), but the patient does not express it. Slow pulse, tired feeling. Apathetic and dull. Circulation becomes sluggish, causing arterial or venous congestion with sense of fullness and heaviness in different organs. Coma and strokes. Alternate pelvic organ symptoms with head symptoms. Debility after seminal discharges, great prostration from irritability of seminal vesicles. Catarrh of mucus membranes with watery discharges. Influenza with malaise. Never well since influenza. Measles. Pellagra. Wants to lie down quietly, half reclined, wants to be held. Children have a fear of falling, they can grab the nurse or crib (Bor.). General depression from heat of sun. Cold and dampness brings on many complaints. Effects of bad news, anger, grief when accompanied by trembling and fatigue. Drug overdose. Nervous disorders from tobacco. MIND - Mental dullness, dizzy, drowsy and droopy. Dazed mind. Answers slowly. Weak, tired, delicate, timid. Desire to be quiet, to be left alone. Apathy, regarding their illness. Mental exertion cause a sense of helplessness and weakness. Mental exhaustion. Dullness, languor, listless. Incapacity to think or fix the attention. Vacant feeling on attempting to concentrate. Stupefaction during vertigo. Vanishing of thoughts on mental exertion. Great depression with confusion of mind and exhaustion. Depression of spirits. Desire for be alone. Apathy and indolence. Indifference to business affairs. Inability to attend to anything requiring thought. Wants to be quiet. Irritability, doesn't wish to be spoken to. Nervous, irritable, easily angered. Excitable, easy to anger, especially in children and adolescents. Bad effectsfrom fright, fear, badnews. Fear of falling, especially in children (Bor.). Fear of doctors anddentists. Stage fright. Emotional excitement, fear, etc., lead to bodily ailments. Effects of grief, cannot cry, broods over her loss. Ailments from anticipation. Nervous dread of appearing in public. Fear of upcoming ordeals. Dread of ordeals, pain. Lack of courage. Anticipation of any unusual ordeal, preparing for church, theatre, or to meet an engagement, brings on diarrhea. Fear of going to doctor or dentist. Anxiety about present and future. Anxiety about health. Anxiety during thunderstorm. Apprehensive feeling at approach of thunderstorm. Overpowering fear, with fatigue, exhaustion and drowsiness. Fear from traumatic shock. Fear of losing self-control. Fear that unless on the move the heart will cease beating. Fear of falling. Child starts and grasps the nurse, and screams as if afraid of falling (Bor. ). Fear of death. Fear of pain. Fear of injury. Confusion, acts as if crazy. Delirious on falling to sleep. Delirium with incoherent talk. Sensation of intoxication during diarrhea. Acute mania after melancholy. Absolute lack of fear. High places aggravates. Impulse to jump from a height, from window. Cataleptic immobility with dilated pupils, closed eyes but conscious.

Head - Dull headache with influenza. Headache coming on suddenly, with dimness of sight or diplopia. Sensation as if a band around head with occipital headache. Dull, heavy ache with heaviness of eyelids. Bruised sensation. Sick headache. Headache worse mental exertion, heat of sun, lying with head low. Nervous headaches from emotional excitement. Headache better pressure and lying with head high. Wants to have head raised on pillow. Pain in temple, extending into ear and nose, chin. Headache with muscular soreness of neck and shoulders. Headache preceded by blindness. Headache better profuse urination. Headache with faintness. Hemicrania preceded by great sensitiveness to noise. Occipital headaches. Delirious on falling asleep. Meningitis, congestive stage, pain at the back of head and dilated pupils. Fontanels pulsate strongly. Swollen feeling in head. Scalp sore to touch. Threatened or actual stroke, with stupor, coma and paralysis.

Eyes - Dullness, sleepy look of eyes. Eyes, red sore aching, suffused. Eyes red and watery. Heavy, drooping eyelids. Ptosis, can hardly open eyes. Ptosis due to congestion of brain, exhaustion. Orbital neuralgia with contraction and twitching of muscles. Bruised pain back of orbits. Disturbedeye muscular apparatus. Serous inflammations. Eyeballs sore when moving them. Eyeballs oscillate laterally when using them. Deep inflammations with haziness of vitreous. Photophobia worse sun or gaslight. Asthenopia. Glaucoma. Blepharitis and conjunctival hyperemia. Descemetitis. Retinitis. Detached retina from injury or myopia. Serous choroiditis. One pupil dilated, the other contracted. Yellow color of eyes.

Ears - Catarrhal inflammation, at beginning of head cold and closure of eustachian tube. Ear pain while swallowing. Earache from cold. Earache and sore throat. Neuralgic otalgia. Great sensitiveness to all sounds. Impaired hearing from cold. Sudden loss of hearing for a short time, rushing and roaring in ears. Catarrhal deafness with pain from throat into middle ear. Deafness and loss of speech from quinine.

Nose - Disposition to catch colds and influenza, with every change of weather. Spring and summer colds. Acute coryza with dull headache and fever. Coryza with thin acrid watery discharge. Stuffed nose. Coryza with influenza. Sneezing, fullness at root of nose. Sneezing, early morning. Swelling of turbinates. Nosebleed with suppressed menses. Sensation as if hot water flowing from the nostrils. Hay fever. Watery, excoriating discharge. Nasal catarrh, with prostration, with sore throat. Nasal voice. Coryza in changeable weather. Itching and tickling in soft palate and naso-pharynx. Dryness of nose.

Face - Face looks fatigued, droopy. Hot, heavy, flushed, besotted-looking (Bapt., Op.). Dusky hue of face with vertigo and dim vision. Neuralgia of face. Facial muscles contracted, especially around the mouth. Trigeminal neuralgia after exposure on a cold damp day. Chin quivers. Lower jaw dropped, wags sideways. Shooting pains in jaws. Facial paralysis. Erythema of face and neck. Sore, acute, red pimples on face.

Mouth - Dryness of mouth, must swallow frequently. Putrid taste and breath. Bitter taste. Taste, clammy and feverish during the sweat. Saliva yellow as from blood. Muscles of mouth seem contracted. Speech thick, as if drunk, he can hardly speak. Sore mouth, with febrile and catarrhal states, intermittent or remittent type. Roof of mouth feels, as if swollen.

Throat - Throat feels rough, burning. Pain from throat to ear. Swallowing causes pain in ear (Hep., Nux-v.). Difficult swallowing. Inability to swallow or speak. Feeling of a painful lump in throat that cannot be swallowed. Sore throat during menses. Tonsils swollen and very red. Tonsillitis from acute catarrh. Tonsillitis, shooting pain into ears. Post-diphtheria paralysis. Paralytic dysphagia, especially worse from warm food. Spasms of glottis, long crowing inspiration, sudden and forcible expiration. Dryness of throat with hoarseness. Hoarseness after depressing emotions. Hoarseness during menses. Burning pain in larynx and chest, when coughing. Larynx raw, as if ulcerated. Aphonia. Loss of voice from fright. Loss of voice, with dryness and burning in throat.

Stomach - Sour eructations. Feeling of emptiness or weakness in the stomach. Flatulence of stomach. Rumbling and dull pain. Cramps in stomach, worse riding or sitting erect. Hiccough, worse evening. Tenderness of stomach with vomiting.

Abdomen - Rumbling in abdomen with discharge of wind above and below. Acute catarrhal enteritis during damp weather. Gnawing pain in the transverse colon. Sudden spasmodic pains in upper part of abdomen, compelling him to cry, leaving a sensation of contraction. Soreness in abdominal walls. Tenderness in right iliac region during typhus. Periodic colic with diarrhea, yellow discharges. Neuralgia of intestines periodic, malarial. Intestinal obstructions. Strangulated hernia.

Rectum - Partial paralysis of rectum and sphincter. Paralysis of the anal sphincter. Prolapse rectum. Rectal pains after labor. Passage of flatus before stool. Diarrhea, painless in nervous persons. Diarrhea after sudden emotions as grief, fright, bad news. Diarrhea during dentition. Urging to stool caused by exciting news. Disposition to go to stool whenever anything startles her. Diarrheafrom anticipation of an unusual ordeal (Arg-n., Ph-ac.). Painlessor involuntary stools. Copious yellow stools. Stools, cream colored. Stool papescent, dark yellow. Stools, tea-green. Stools yellow, bilious, clay-colored. Sensations - Lightness of head or body. As if the head were enlarged. As if there were a tape around the head. As if the skin were contracted in the middle of the forehead. As if a lump were in throat which could not be swallowed. As if a lump were in the esophagus. Load in stomach. As if stomach were quite gone. As if the uterus were squeezed by a hand. As if he would die, as if the blood ceased to circulate, as if the heart would stop unless he kept moving. As if a knife were thrust through from occiput to forehead. As if eyes were jumping out of head.

Male - Genitals cold, relaxed (Ph-ac.). Continually profuse warm sweat on scrotum. Dragging pain in testes. Gonorrhea, in first stage, discharge scanty, tendency to corrode, much heat, smarting at meatus. Whitish discharge in gonorrhea. Suppressed gonorrhea, with fever, rheumatism, orchitis. Excitable sexual desire. Spermatorrhea without erections. Spermatorrhea during stool. Too early ejaculation during sex. Sexual power exhausted, slightest caress causes an emission.

Female - Menses retarded, pain extends to back and hips. Dysmenorrhea with scanty flow. Dysmenorrhea preceded by sick headache, vomiting, bearing down in abdomen. Menorrhagia, almost continuous flow, without any pain. Suppressed menses with nosebleeds. Epileptiform convulsions at menstrual period or from suppressed menses (Oean.). Uterus heavy sore, feels as if squeezed (Cham., Nux-v., Ust.). Cramps in abdomen and legs during pregnancy. Threatened miscarriage from sudden depressing emotions. False laborpains, painspass trpback. Inefficient labor pains or none at all. Labor pains go up, backward or down the thighs. Nervous chills during first stage of labor. Rigidity of os during labor (Bell.). As if a wave from uterus to throat with choking feeling, impedes labor. Severe after-pains. Twitching of muscles of the whole body with drowsiness, before puerperal convulsions. Deep yellow leucorrhea with aching across lower part of the back. White leucorrhea, with fullness in uterine region. White leucorrhea with aching across lower part of back. Leucorrhea in gushes, day and night. Leucorrhea with constipation. Sex difficult from contraction of the vaginal muscles. Vaginismus. Food - Low appetite and thirst. Thirstless- ness with trembling. Thirst with sweat, but not with fever. Difficult swallowing of warm food. Vertigo worse smoking. Sleeplessness from smoking. Headache worse wine. Eye symptoms worse wine.

Chest - Oppression about chest. Heaviness in middle of chest. As if a lump behind the chest. Burning in chest, when coughing. Periodical pain in pectoral muscles. Constrictive pain around lower part of chest. Stitches in chest from above downward. Constitutions - Suited to children and young people, to persons of a nervous, weak, hysterical temperament. Suitable to irritable, sensitive, excitable people.

Heart - Feeble heart, slow heart's action with cold hands and feet. As if blood had ceased to circulate. A feeling as if it were necessary to keep in motion or else heart's action would cease. Pain in heart on rising from seat. Palpitations and oppression of heart, worse when thinking of it. Hysterical palpitations. Sore pain in heart. Sharp pains in region of heart. Pulse soft, weak, full and flowing. Slow pulse (Dig., Kalm., Apoc.), greatly accelerated on motion. Weak, slow pulse of old age. Pulse slow, full, soft, compressible.

Back - Backache with occipital pains. Backache day before appearance of menses. Complete relaxation of the whole muscular system. Chilliness up and the down back. Languor, muscles feel bruised. Every exertion causes fatigue. Dull aches, heavy pains, up and down in spine, better walking. Pain in muscles of back, hips and lower limbs, mostly deep-seated. Dull aching in lumbar and sacral region, passing upward. Pains under scapula. Pain in neck, especially upper sternocleido muscles. Lameness and stiffness of neck. Neck feels bruised, unable to hold the head. Spinal congestion, with incipient aphasia. Paralytic condition of lumbar and sacral muscles.

Limbs - Fatigue of limbs after slight exercise. Deep-seated, aching, in bones and joints. Myalgia from overexertion. Loss of power of muscular control. Excessive trembling and weakness of all the limbs. Heavy sensation in lower limbs. Knees weak worse descending tottering gait, cannot direct his legs. Muscleaches, chills and fatigue with influenza. Hard aching in humerus (right). Feeling of partial luxation of patella when walking. Numbness and weakness of limbs. Wandering, rheumatic pains. Cramps in muscles of the forearm. Coldness of wrists and hands. Hot, dry, numb hands, especially palms. Wants hands in cool water. Neuralgic pains in limbs, after scarlatina. Professional neurosis. Writer's cramp.

Sleep - Sleepless from nervous irritation (Coff.). Insomnia from mental excitement, uncontrollable thinking or tobacco. Insomnia from exhaustion. Sleepless from itching. Sleeplessness during dentition. Sleeplessness in delirium tremens. Heavy, stupid sleep. Cannot get fully to sleep. Restless sleep, worse toward morning. Starts on falling to sleep. Drowsiness with influenza. Delirious on falling asleep. Incoherent talking during half awake state. Sleepiness of students. Languor and drowsiness when trying to study. Sudden shrill cries on awaking in meningitis. Awakens from sleep with headache or colic. Yawning. Night terrors from nose being stopped up and dry. Unpleasant dreams after midnight. Sexual dreams with nocturnal emissions. Dreams followed next day by great languor and irritability. Dreams with pain at base of brain.

Skin - Papular eruption, like measles. Itching of skin, without eruption, worse at night and from warmth. Hot dry, moist, yellow, itching, measles-like eruption. Erysipelas. Measles, catarrhal symptoms, aids in bringing out eruption. Measles with cerebral symptoms. Retrocedent measles, with livid spots. Livid spots. Scarlet fever with stupor and flushed face. Erythema of face and neck. Pimples on forehead and neck. Pimples like small cutaneous indurations. Rubeola.

Modalities - Better from profuse urination. Better alcoholic drinks, stimulants. Better mental efforts. Better open air. Better sweating. Better shaking. Better bending forwards. Better continued motion. Better reclining. Better with head held high. Better in afternoon. Worse emotions or excitement. Worse surprise, anxiety. Worse shocks, ordeals. Worse bad news. Worse from tobacco smoking. Worse dentition. Worse motion. Worse from anticipation. Worse thinking of his ailments. Worse damp weather. Worse humid weather, spring. Worse fog. Worse before a thunderstorm. Worse heat of sun. Worse summer. Worse at 10 a.m. Worse periodically.

Teeth - Toothache from a cold. Toothache with nervous excitement. Toothache with a weak and trembling condition. Toothache. purely nervous. Pains from teeth extend to temple. Pains come in paroxysms. Neuralgic pains and darts through jaws and face. Toothache with congestion of head and face. Dentition, child frantic, awakens with sudden screams. Gums swollen and tender. Child frantic at times, when gums are examined.

Tongue - Thick, yellow coating on tongue. Tongue numb and trembles while protruding. Edges of tongue red, centre white. Tongue inflamed in middle. Tongue brown, nearly clear. Tongue thick, coated, yellowish, paralysed. Vertigo - Vertigo on rising, lightheaded, worse by sudden movement of the head and walking. Dizziness and blurred vision. Vertigo spreads from occiput, as if drunk with visual symptoms. Staggering as if intoxicated when trying to move, worse from smoking. Vertigo with loss of sight, chilliness, accelerated pulse, dullness of vision, double vision. Vertigo Gelsemium sempervirens of child on being carried. Vision -Dim vision. Dim vision during pregnancy. Blurring and discomfort in eyes even after accurately adjusted glasses. Slow accommodation of vision. Vision blurred, smoky (Cycl., Phos.). Blurred vision with pain above eyes. Obscured vision on stooping. Blind spells. Blindness with dilated pupils. Double vision, when looking sideways. Diplopia during headache. Diplopia during pregnancy. Diplopia with multiple sclerosis. Affections of vision before migraine. Pupils dilated and insensible to light. Hysterical amblyopia. Amaurosis after stroke. Amaurosis from masturbation. Astigmatism. Vision dim, can neither read nor write, words run together. Sees swimming black specks. Misty or glimmering appearance. Distant objects seem indistinct, when riding or walking. COMMENTS - Overall fatigue with a sense of fright. Ailments due to bad news and fright (Op.), fright causes weakness. Acute shock, shaking and trembling. Trembling with fear. Incontinence with fear. Fear of failure, acute fear or panic (Aeon.). Anticipatory anxiety. Convalescence. Chronic fatigue ever since a viral infection (Ph-ac.), especially if the limbs feel heavy, exhaustion. Ailments from flu shots. For the elderly who become weak, frail, and lose confidence after infections. Viral infections, particularly influenza, mono, meningitis, and hepatitis, with tiredness and weakness. Sore throats, worse swallowing. Coryza and hay fever with early morning sneezing and streaming colds. Catarrh generally occurs in warm, moist, relaxing weather. Major influenza remedy. Influenza epidemics and for prevention. Dizzy drowsy, droopy and dumb. Slow onset of flu symptoms. Influenza infections with tiredness and weakness. Apathy and indifférance during the flu. Wants to be alone and quiet when sick. Sore throats and colds. Fever without thirst. Muscle aches and weakness. Influenza with dull headaches. Never well since influenza, chronic fatigue. Worse since flu vaccinations. Paralysis. Excessive weakness and trembling. Weakness and paralysis of the limbs, the limbs feel heavy, with trembling. Keynote tremors. Multiple sclerosis. Neuralgic problems. Epileptic attacks beginning with a throbbing headache. Headaches with a heavy feeling, dizziness. Sensation of a band around their head. Throbbing headaches, particularly in the occiput and forehead. Nondescript headache with dullness. Headache begins in the occiput and spreads over the whole head, settling down over the eyes. Migraine headaches with double vision, weakness, and nausea. Violent headache may occur if needing to urinate at night and not doing so. Headache with stiff neck, worse morning, better urinating, with irregular action of the eye muscles. Double vision, dimness of vision. Ptosis of the eyelids. Vertigo. Dizziness from weakness, especially during viral infections, flus, and colds. Drowsy. Sense of dullness, apathy. Low stamina. Aversion to the least effort. Neurotic symptoms in cigar-makers, with impotence, palpitations. Drug overdose resulting in a stupor or coma. Paralysis of the tongue, trembling of the tongue, particularly in typhoid cases. The tongue is thinly coated. Dry lips. Face is flushed (less that Bapt.). Itching of the skin, measles-like eruptions. Measles and eruptive disorders with drowsy state, suffused face, and convulsions. Thirstlessness with low fevers. Cold extremities. Chills up and down the spine. Trembling and shaking, can be from extreme exhaustion. Euphoria followed by weakness. Generally a slow onset, with aches and pains, especially after exerting themselves. Nervous diarrhea due to stress, worry and anxiety. Stools generally yellow, whether diarrhea or constipation. Nervous heartburn and colic. Hysterical dysphagia or aphonia after emotions. Dysmenorrhea, epileptiform convulsions during menstrual period, rigid os in labor, chill, beginning in hands or feet and running up back. Aggravation before, during, and after menses. Aversion to noise and light, desire to be left alone. Desires fresh air (Bry., Lyc., Ars.).Wants to lie down and rest. Wants to be held, that he may not shake. Must be covered in all stages of the paroxysm. Worse thinking about their symptoms. Complaints from sudden changes of weather, particularly from hot or dry to damp air. Worse sunlight, heat of the sun, summer, damp weather, cold, damp atmosphere, fog. Great distress and apprehensive feeling at approach of a thunderstorm. Symptoms may be better urinating. Better from stimulants, especially alcoholic. Cold drinks are vomited immediately, but warm or spirituous drinks can be swallowed. Pain at the back of the head is better from hot applications. Motion aggravates most symptoms, but alleviates muscular heart pains. Rising from a seat causes pain in the heart. Heaviness of the head is better from shaking the head. Lifting the arms causes trembling of the hands. Playing the piano causes a tired sensation in the arms. J. H. Nankivell drank two ounces of tincture of Gels, instead of a glass of sherry. He walked a few feet with assistance and in another minute his legs were paralyzed. He dragged himself to the bedside with his arms, but they were unable to help him to bed into which he had to be lifted. As long as he lay quiet there was no trouble, but on the least exertion there were excessive tremors. Vomiting occurred during the next twenty-four hours. Temperature rose to 101.5° F. Heart's action very violent and intermittent. All the muscles of the eyes were affected, but, of voluntary muscles, those of the right side suffered most. Prolonged conversation involved paralysis of upper lip. There was somnolence, absence of mental excitement and good appetite. The effects passed away in the order of occurrence from below upwards, but after the arms had recovered, vision was not perfect for twenty-four hours. A patient of Clarke once took a drachm of the tincture for a headache. On going out, he could not tell which side of the street he was on. He was near St. Paul's Cathedral and saw two cathedrals instead of one. J. G. Blackley pointed out the suitability of Gels, to writer's cramp and professional paralyzes. Clarke relieved with it cases of Dupuytren's contraction. Erskine White cured an infant born in convulsions three weeks after its mother had been terribly frightened by seeing her little brother nearly burnt to death. The only guiding symptom was “the child's chin quiveredincessantly.” In thirty seconds after the dose the quivering ceased, in three minutes the convulsions were at an end. White had to ride twelve miles over mountains to reach the patient after receiving the summons, so the convulsions must have lasted a considerable time. RELATIONS -Antidotes: Atrop, Chin., Coff., Dig., Nux-m. Coff., Dig., Alcoholic stimulants relieve all complaints where Gels, is useful. In cases of poisoning, artificial respiration and faradization of respiratory muscles. Foy found Nitro-glycerine a perfect antidote in one case. Jephson antidoted his case with Strychnine. It antidotes: Mag-p. It antagonizes: Atrop., Op. Compare: (1) Bell - labor, Caul., Caust. - complaints of women, Cocc., Con., Cur. - paralysis. (2) Ferr-p. - fever, Phos. - effect of thunderstorms. Ol-an., Verat. - headache. Bor. - sense of falling. (3) Bry. - typhoid, dreads movement. Gels, because he is so weak, Bry. because movement worse pains. (4) Hyper, worse from fog. Ign. - gastric disorders of cigar makers, Bapt., Ip., Aeon., Cimic., Mag-p. (5) Culx. - vertigo on blowing the nose with fullness of the ears. Compatible: Bap. (in typhoid influenza). Ip. (in dumb ague). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Hale. Murphy. Phatak.

Liver - Hepatitis with chronic fatigue. Passive congestion of liver with vertigo, dim sight and fullness of head. Griping pain in gall bladder. Deficient secretion of bile. Jaundice with prostration and clay-colored stools. Lungs - Heavy, labored breathing. Tiresome, slow breathing. Slow breathing with great prostration. Acute bronchitis. Dyspnea and great chilliness. Respiration quickened. Spasmodic disorders of lungs and diaphragm. Spasmodic asthma. Oppressed breathing with cold hands and feet. Sudden sensation of suffocation. Extreme restlessness from threatened suffocation, demands for fresh air. Sudden and severe attacks of dyspnea, with crowing noise, profuse sweat and dark flushed face. Scanty expectoration of mucus.

Kidneys - Pain in region of kidneys, as if produced by pressure of a blunt instrument. Kidney pain during fever. Constant urination, hysterical. Spasmodic affection of ureters from passage of calculi. Urine profuse, clear, watery, with chilliness and trembling. Urine much increased in quantity. Urine stream intermittent. Albuminuria.

Bladder - Partial paralysis of bladder, intermittent flow (Clem.). Bladder paralysis following diphtheria. Bladder paralysis in elderly people. Retention of urine. Dysuria. Frequent urging, with scanty emission and tenesmus of bladder. Incontinence from excitement. Incontinence from paralysis of sphincter. Constant dribbling of urine, but not a drop flows on making the greatest effort. Alternate dysuria and bedwetting. Bedwetting in nervous children at night. Bladder spasm in women, often combined with uterine spasms. Bladder spasm in men, with colic. Bladder distended up to navel. Causations - Ill effects of fright, depressing emotions, anger, bad news, unpleasant surprise, traumatic shock. Sun, heat, warm or cold damp weather. Alcohol, drugs. Masturbation.

Cough - Dry cough, with sore chest and fluent coryza. Cough from tickling in eustachian tube. Cough from tickling or roughness of fauces. Croupy cough in measles. Convulsive, spasmodic cough. Spasmodic cough in hysterical women. Irritative cough without expectoration. Coughs a good deal during the night.

Perspiration - Sweats freely from slight exertion. Cold sweat. Sweat coming gradually and moderately, always relieves pains. Sometimes profuse, with languor and prostration. Sweats at night. Night sweats of tuberculosis. Most profuse sweat on genitals. Sticky sweat.

Temperature - Chills, without thirst, along spine. Influenza with chills, muscular soreness, great prostration and headache. Chill with aching and languor, mixed with heat or alternating with heat. Chills Gelsemium sempervirens up and down back. Wave-like chills, extending upward from sacrum to occiput. Wants to be held, because he shakes so much. Cold hands and feet. Coldness so severe as to be painful. Nervous chills. Nervous, shuddering, chills, preceded by visual disturbances. Nervous chills during labor. Heat and sweat stages, long and exhausting. Fever with drowsiness. Bilious remittent, malarial, typhoid, cerebrospinal fevers. Fever and thirstlessness. Measles, influenza and colds. Fever with a stupor, dizziness, faintness, and weakness. Fever with nervous restlessness. Fever with intense burning. Wants to lie still and rest with influenza.

full:
PHARMACY - gent-c. Gentiana cruciata. Cross-leaved gentian. Kreutz-Enzian. N. O. Gentianacae. Tincture of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Belching. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Dysphagia. Hernia. Hoarseness. Stiff neck. Stomach, affection. Throat, sore.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany stated “Gent, cruciata has been invested with imaginary virtues, because its leaves grow in the form of a cross, it has been recommended in hydrophobia.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Gentiana cruciata's reputation as a remedy for hydrophobia is partly justified in the provings. It also has throat and stomach symptoms. Dysphagia, vertigo with headache, pressing inward sensation in eyes. Constricted of the throat, head and abdomen. Distention, fullness and tightness in abdomen. Creeping over body as from fleas. MIND - Weeping mood with disinclination to talk. Very peculiar anxiety, acceleration and difficulty ofbreathing, swelling of the temporal veins and feeling of pressure in the temporal region. On reading, print seemed indistinct and as if covered with a veil.

Head - Sensitiveness of whole head and brain after dinner, worse by violent motion of the head. Swelling of temporal veins and feeling of pressure in temporal region. Sudden stitch through left temple. Distressing tension and at times transient jerking in region of vertex, tension soon became a very acute constant pressure, worse by exerting eyes or constant thought.

Eyes - Sensation as though eyes were lying deep in orbit, piercing inward sensation in right eye. Print indistinct, as if covered with a veil.

Mouth - Two aphthous ulcers on margin of lower lip on either side of frenum. Increased flow of saliva.

Throat - Frequent attacks of hoarseness and sensitiveness of the throat. Weak voice. Slight redness and distressing sensation of constriction within the throat, swallowing is very difficult. Rawness and scrapings, causing frequent hawking with constriction when swallowing. Intermittent, deep redness of fauces. Stitches in tonsils. Vertigo - Confusion and whirling. COMMENTS - The proving developed a number of striking symptoms in the throat and digestive tract. Movings about in stomach and abdomen. Pressure in the stomach as if a stone was in it with inclination to vomit. All the symptoms of right inguinal hernia occurred in one prover. A peculiar sense of anxiety, faintness, uneasiness. One prover felt as if all the nerves were tense, so that walking was difficult. Creeping over the body as from fleas in the evening. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Gent-1., Lyc. - better from warm drink. (2) Bry., Puls. (3) Abies-n., - pressure in stomach as from a stone. (4) Kali-bi. - tenacious mucus in throat. (5) Gent-q. (6) Hydr., Nux-v. (7) Epip. - thick saliva. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Burning, fullness, pressure in stomach. Pressure in stomach as if a stone were in it with inclination to vomit. Sensation of pressing inward in pit of stomach. Acid belchings, watery vomiting. Great nausea with inclination to lie down. Vomiting with some difficulty, a small quantity of mucus of an acid odor intensely bitter, leaving a scraping and rawness in throat.

Abdomen - Sensitive, griping, sore sensation in umbilical region, better sitting and lying, worse after dinner or smoking, standing, or walking, obliging him to bend forward, therewith umbilicus seemed to be drawn inward. Distention, fullness, tightness and constriction. Dragging in right inguinal region with feeling of protrusion, very sensitive.

Rectum - Movings about in intestines with slight headache, followed by copious pasty evacuation. Constant violent urging, followed by watery evacuations. Pasty diarrhea and stools without the usual itching in anus.

Female - Menstruation three days earlier than usual, during which there was a headache as if head too full with feeling of distention in the skull, better during rest and worse by motion, preventing sleep for a long time. Food - Appetite increased or lost.

Back - Drawing and jerking along right side of neck, extending to shoulder. Drawing in cervical muscles, extending to ears, worse by turning head, an uneasiness so that he could not remain long in one position. Tension in lumber region.

Limbs - Distressing drawing in right shoulder lasting several minutes. Cramp-like pains in soles of feet.

Modalities - Better from drinking fresh water. Better warm soup. Better open air. Worse after eating.

full:
PHARMACY - gent-1. Gentiana lútea. Yellow gentian. N. O. Gentianacae. Tincture of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anorexia. Biliousness. Colic. Debility. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Fever. Gout. Headaches. Stomach, disorders. Throat, constriction.

HERBAL - The yellow gentian is the source of the well-known tonic of herbal practice; it may cause increased the appetite in the healthy.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chief symptoms from the provings were in the alimentary sphere, including ravenous hunger as well as a diminished appetite. Marked stomach symptoms. Aching in the eyes and throat. Dry, thick saliva. Dry mouth, bitter or earthy taste, nausea, vomiting, colic. Diarrhea with yellow stools, rheumatic pains, sensations of constriction are marked and common. Febrile conditions. MIND - Dull feeling of whole body. Morose mood, general dejection. Confusion while writing.

Head - Frontal headache, better eating and open air. Brain feels loose, head tender.

Eyes - Pressure in eyeballs. Frequent aching in the eyes. Redness of the conjunctiva. Obscuration of the sight for some moments, so that objects immediately before the eyes cannot be distinguished, could not see the person with whom he was talking for a few moments.

Nose - Irritation in nose, as in coryza, followed by a watery discharge.

Mouth - Dryness of the month and throat, saliva thicker than usual. Intensely bitter, earthy taste. Swelling, fine sticking in throat, mostly in posterior portion of plate.

Throat - Frequent hawking of mucus, which is difficult to loose. Rawness, roughness of the throat. Hoarseness. Vertigo - Vertigo is worse from rising or motion. Vertigo better in the open air. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Gent-q. (2) Gent. 1 ., Hydr., Nux-v., Epip. - thick saliva. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Acid risings, ravenous hunger, nausea, weight and aching in stomach.

Abdomen - Inflation and tension of stomach and abdomen (Poth.). Colic, umbilical region sensitive to touch. Flatulence.

Rectum - Urgent inflation to evacuate, sometimes sudden, with abundant stools, followed by painful sensitiveness of the abdomen, pressure on the anus while wanting to go to stool. Dragging towards anus with tenesmus. Sudden urging with copious evacuation.

Stool - Stool soft, yellow, preceded by colicky pains, which become so severe after the stool that they force the patient to bend double. Soft stools, immediately after rising. Bilious diarrhea in afternoon.

Chest - Oppression of the chest, fullness in the chest, sometimes with pressure and difficulty of respiration. Pressure on left side near the throat.

Back - Pain in the back and bowels, much worse by motion, better by sitting. Sensation of a cord or pressure and weight around the loins.

Limbs - Rheumatic tension and dragging in the right hand, with inflammatory redness of two articulations of the fingers, spasmodic symptoms and pain of the part during movement.

Sleep - Y awning. Inclination to sleep without power to go to sleep. Uneasy sleep disturbed by abdominal symptoms and fever. Sleep impeded by colic, which obliges the patient to turn in bed, sometimes on one side and sometimes on the other.

Modalities - Worse in the afternoon. Worse after eating. Worse on motion.

Temperature - Febrile shuddering, as from electric shocks, followed by lassitude, depression and tension in the limbs. Increase of natural heat in head, cheeks and whole body. Heat originating in the lumber vertebrae. Pulse accelerated.

PHARMACY - gent-q. Gentianaquinquefolia. Five-flowered gentian. Gall of the earth. N. O. Gentianacae. Decoction of the herb. Tincture of fresh plant in flower September, October. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anorexia. Cholera infantum. Dyspepsia. Intermittent fever. Weakness.

HERBAL - Gent-q. is a pleasant bitter and appears, like the other Gentians, to be a positive tonic. It has a popular reputation in Ohio and other parts of the United States as an anti-periodic and tonic. Valuable tonic for old cases of dyspepsia and torpid liver. Dr. Yelvington of Susquehanna, who said he learned its value from a tribe of Native Americans, said it has succeeded in obstinate intermittents where quinine and other anti-periodics had failed. He used the decoction of the herb, but a fluid extract or the saturated tincture is a better form for administration in fever. Y elvington also used it in cases of infantile fever and cholera infantum. “As a tonic in enfeebled patients and in chronic diseases, it is a remedy par excellence, appearing to exert an action over organs of nutrition and assimilation, as well as being a stimulant to the excretory organs.” REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

PHARMACY - ger. Geranium maculatum. Wild cranesbill. N. O. Geraniaceae. Tincture and triturations of root. Infusion of the plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Diplopia. Dysentery. Headaches. Hemorrhages. Leucorrhea. Migraines. Ptosis. Stool, ineffectual. Throat, sore. Ulcers. Vomiting.

HERBAL - Geranium maculatum. in the herbal tinctures and lower potencies, has been used successfully in cases of hemorrhage from various parts, nose, stomach and lungs. It has also been used for chronic diarrhea and leucorrhea. Locally in ulcers, it will destroy the pyogenic membrane.

HOMEOPATHIC - Under the use of the drug, the blood in hemorrhages becomes darker, clots more easily and is much less in quantity. The root contains both tannic and gallic acids. There are two fragmentary provings of Ger. one made with root preparations, one with infusion of the plant. The chief symptoms observed have been diplopia and other disorders of vision and a constant and ineffectual desire for stool. Migraines, habitual sick headaches. Profuse, hemorrhages, pulmonary and from different organs. Vomiting of blood. Ulceration of stomach. Atonic and foul ulcers. Summer complaints. Breasts - Sore nipples (Eup-a.).

Head - Giddiness with diplopia, better closing eyes. Sick headache. Slight pain in occiput, low down.

Eyes - Ptosis and dilated pupils. Fullness in the eyes. Great difficulty in walking with eyes open, though he could walk with them closed.

Mouth - Dry mouth. Tip of tongue dry and burning.

Throat - Pharyngitis. Vertigo - Vertigo with diplopia. Vertigo better closing eyes. Vertigo with blurred vision and constant ineffectual urging to stool. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ger. - Constant hawking and spitting in elderly people. (2) Erod. - a popular hemostatic in Russia and especially used for metrorrhagia and menorrhagia. (3) Hydrin., Cinch.. Sabin. (4) Ham., Hydr., Hematoxylin., Rat., Fic., Erod. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Catarrhal gastritis with profuse secretion. Lessens the vomiting in gastric ulcers. Tendency to ulceration and passive hemorrhage.

Rectum - Constant desire to go to stool with inability to pass anything for some time. Chronic diarrhea with offensive mucus. Constipation.

Female - Menses too profuse. Post-partum hemorrhage.

full:
PHARMACY - germ. Germanium metal- licum. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Amyloidosis. Anemia. Arthritis. Bronchitis. Cancer. Diabetes. Headaches. Hypertension. Kidney, failure. Malaria. Palpitations. Paralysis. Pneumonia.

HOMEOPATHIC - Severe illnesses with dysfunction of nerves, liver, kidney. Démyélinisation of the nerves. Numbness. Ataxia, cerebellum. Chronic fatigue. Extreme weakness, as if the vitalforce is leaving the body. Feeling of heaviness, present throughout the pathogenesis. MIND - Absent minded. Mentally slow and confused. Forgetful. Cannot adapt. Inept. Incapability. Makes mistakes in writing and speaking. Dyslexia. Difficulties with concentration, confusion. The answer is there but it can not come out. Moody. Feels weak, dull, empty, flat. Indifferent. Everything appears unreal. Lack of romantic feelings. Hopeless. Feels helpless. Guiltyfeelings. Self reproach, hates himself. Disgusted with himself. Gloomy. Doomed feelings. Restlessness. Fear of responsibilities. Fear of being criticized. Fear of being a total failure. Fear of being unmasked. Fear of falling. Fear of paralysis. Irritable when having to answer questions. Feeling of isolation. Feels like a stranger in society. Does not feel connected. Feels invaded, somebody has entered their territory. Feels trapped. Emotions are strong but cannot come out or are kept under strict control. Suppressed anger or outburst of anger. Holding anger inside, aggravates. Such outburts are very quickly forgotten with no feeling of remorse. Delusion, that he is a prisoner. Delusion that the world is shabby. Delusion that she estranged, isolated. Delusion, everything looks smaller or lower. Time going more slowly. Hearing voices. Delusions, hands don't belong to him.

Head - Headache with sharp, stabbing pains. Headache, worse moving. Head feels loose inside. Headache over left eye better cold bathing on waking. Head congestion with catarrhal symptoms. Heaviness sensation, occiput. Pressing pain in temples. Dull pain between the temples. Crawling sensation, right side of head. Light- headed, better eating. Slight dizziness in head with throbbing pain in temples. Dandruff and itchy scalp.

Eyes - Burning pain with lachrymation and discharge from nose. Dry, gritty eyes. Burning and itching of eyelids. Cold sensation of the eyes. Eyes cold and watery as if exposed to a cold draft. Stiffness with swelling upper eyelids and below eyebrows. Cannot open eyes properly.

Ears - Aching pain moved into ear with pressure in both ear drums. Cracking in the ears from yawning. Pain, throbbing behind the ears. Sharp pain in right ear. Tightness in ear drum. Noises in ear. Ringing noise. Low, whispering sounds. Humming vibrating sound in head. Sensitive to noises.

Nose - Itching of nose, external and internal, better rubbing. Abundant sneezing during coryza. Sneezing with watery coryza. Sneezing with mucus on waking. Head congestion with catarrhal' symptoms. Nasal discharge clear and bland. Clear discharge following chest cough. Discharge thin watery pale and yellow. Nasal discharge salty.

Face - Whole face swollen. Rash then extends behind ears. Face more greasy than usual. Purulent eruptions. Pain on cheekbone and above gum like sinusitis. Submaxillary glands swollen and sore to touch.

Mouth - Dry mouth. Metallic taste in mouth, better glass of water. Greenish-white coating on the tongue and inside of upper lip. Salivation increased. Pain aching in jaw as if chewing something. Tingling in the middle of lower lip.

Throat - Sore throats, with much mucus. Sore and prickling throat on waking. Rasping, grating feeling in trachea while coughing and sneezing. Sore throat started in top of pharynx, worse eating oranges. Difficulty speaking. Vertigo - Vertigo on turning head. Vertigo on writing and studying. Vertigo on going to bed, as soon as head hit the pillow. Vertigo worse closing eyes and opening again. Dizziness after massage. Vision - Black in front of eyes on rising up from lying in the evening. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Gallium., Ferr. REFERENCES Sherr.

Stomach - Eructations while eating. Eructations very bitter and sour. Stomach feels cold, better warm drinks. Stomach feels bloated and full of air during and after eating. Tightness in the stomach. Heaviness and bubbling pain in stomach after eating. Sore pain if pressed. Nausea, wobbly queasy feeling worse after eating. Nausea after drinking beer. Nausea better lying down. Vomits suddenly with extra salivation. Vomitinginmorning. Vomiting after alcohol. Stools - Stool yellow, loose and offensive, alternating with hard stool. Stool scanty, dry dark brown, with mucus. Loose stools. Stools frequent. Stools, frequent.

Abdomen - Feels as if a lump in the solar plexus.

Rectum - Itching of the anus. Constipation, difficult stool. Stools on alternate days. Stools alternating between hard and soft. Explosive flatulence. Flatulence offensive. Diarrhea and flatulence. Diarrhea with thirstlessness. Diarrhea, followed by increased energy. Intense pain in rectum from sexual excitement. Pressing tearing in rectum after stool, extending towards genitals. Sharp pain in rectum extends to ovaries, worse stool.

Male - Coldness in the whole penis with formication in the prepuce. Desire for sex with strong erection which remained long after emission. No sexual interest. Desire absent. Shooting pain in right testicle. Intense sharp pain in the tip of the prepuce of very short duration. Emissions smelling of fish. Emissions profuse.

Female - Menses early. Pain-free menses. Menses started with brown-black discharge followed by red blood. Menses with protracted heavy flow. Dark clotting flow. Bright heavy clots on rising. Tiredness with ovulation. Tiredness during and after period. Leucorrhea thick and yellow. Vaginal discharge offensive. Internal itching with slight yellow discharge turning slightly pink. Itching in vulva. Irresistible itching around vagina. Itching bump on clitoris. White discharge from bump on clitoris. Flatus from vagina. Intense, tearing, bearing down pains in vagina and anal before menses. Sharp pain like hot needles lower abdomen and ovaries. Cramp-like labor pains. Pain before the flow starts, pacing and restlessness. Bleeding very scanty but clotted. Sudden stabbing pain right ovary. Twinge of pain in left ovary. Soreness in opening of vagina, worse by touch. Sexual desire increased. Heightened sexual sensations. Food - Appetite increased.

Chest - Constriction in chest on coughing with clear expectoration. Pain on left side when coughing. Twinge, both breasts, lateral. Aching pain in lateral side of left breast. Aching pain in right breast. Aching on inspiration, worse bending, moving forward, lifting arm. Cramping lateral side right breast. Sensation of a lump in chest on waking. Tightness in the chest in a small spot. Tickling behind sternum.

Heart - Palpitations. Palpitations could start at any moment, as if with anxiety in the chest.

Back - Back spasms. Ache lower sacrum, left side, better stretching and deep pressure. Tension in neck as if nerve was trapped. Aching back of neck extending to right side of occiput, tender to touch, better massage. On waking, intense pain between last cervical and first thoracic vertebrae. Twinges of pain. Muscles feel sore on pressure. Sudden sharp pains appear and disappear quickly. Sharp pain on waking, like a sharp point in shoulder, worse turning head to right. Sharp pain, left scapula. Spasm, left lumbar region, extending to leg.

Limbs - Paralysis. Legs trembling. Inflammation of joints. Cold hands. Cold, wet, clammy feet. Feet very sweaty, odorless. Warm sensation of arms. Incoordination. Hands very dry rough and papery, palms red. Blood blister on finger, sore to touch. Itchy eruptions on shins, better in hot water. Rash slightly raised and a bit itchy, extending down arms. Itchy eruptions on right shin after shower or bath. Pimples on right buttock and thigh. Pain, aching in right shoulder as if bone is sensitive. Pain, aching, left hand near bone. Sciatic pain, leg, right, while standing. Aching in thigh muscles in bed. Knee pains, when walking, worse descending. Dragging pain in knee. Tension in knees when sitting. Stiffness, and soreness calves. Cramping pain in the right big toe. Prickling sensation in arms and hands.

Sleep - Sleepy, must lie down and sleep. Waking 3.30 a.m. Wakes at 5 a.m. Couldn't sleep. Sleep interrupted by cold feeling in the stomach. Stays awake in spite of sleepiness because of pain in the head and eyes. Sleep interrupted by splattering sound inside head. Sleeping on right side impossible with aching in kidney. Yawning constantly with sleepiness. Yawning, paroxysmal. Yawning, which provokes crackling in the ears. Y awning throughout day. Dreams of being pursued. Dreams of accidents. Dreams of war. Dreams of being raped. Dreams of burglars. Dreams of invasion.

Skin - Rash on chest. Very fine itchy rash, behind ears, worse left side. Inflamed pimples on skin of back. Molloscum contagiousum. Eruption red, soft, tender. Right palm very dry and flaky. Skin feels as if an ant were rapidly crawling, then biting. Tingling. Itching on the right side of the chin. Biting, prickling and itching after bath or shower. Swelling, on waking. Eyes swollen virtually shut, rash and swelling now extending to right side of face with red blotches and terrible burning, worse water, worse scratching and rubbing. Skin very oily all over. Skin greasy, and sticky, better washing.

Teeth - Sharp cutting pain in all gums. Pain in teeth from cold water. Sharp pain in teeth. Sudden nerve pains in teeth and gums.

Liver - Liver injuries. Lungs - Pneumonia. Bronchitis. Soreness with slight wheeze in bronchi. Slow, deep respiration. Out of breath on climbing one flight of stairs. Sighing. Restriction in lungs with coughing. Funny sensation on breathing. Once the air passed through the throat felt fluttering sensation in chest and bronchi. Can't breathe deeply, air can't get through properly.

Kidneys - Sudden stabbing pain, right kidney while sitting. Kidney injuries. Kidney failure. Diabetes. Frequent urination. Frequent urging for small amounts. Feeling of heat while passing urine. Stabbing sudden pain right kidney while sitting. Aromatic odor of urine. Powerful stream. Copious urine. Very dark urine with reddish hue and very strong smell. Concentrated, urine, with acid quality.

Bladder - Cutting, pressing pain in the right side of the bladder.

Blood - Hemolysis. Anemia. High blood pressure. Amyloidosis. Breasts - Tenderness in breasts. Wart on right breast with cheesy discharge. Sharp pain in right nipple. Sharp pain in right breast pulling from inside to outside. Sharp pain in left lower breast while walking in the open air. Sensation in right breast as if something is trying to come out through the duct.

Cough - Cough in evening. Cough better hot drinks. Dry cough, with tickle in throat while lying in bed, worse cold water. Dry cough in pairs, with irritation in throat. Dry, racking cough better lying down, with no expectoration. Dry, tickling cough. Hard, dry cough waking from sleep at night. Hollow, barking cough in bed. Sharp, tickling, barking cough, worse evening, cold drinks, better warm drinks. Spasm across lower abdomen with cough.

Perspiration - Perspiration absent at night. Sweats during eating. Sweats with hot flushes. Perspiration from smelling soap.

Contains lithium and silica, which it is similar to. Gettysburg aqua is indicated in the decay of vertebrae or the hip, ulceration of joints, when the discharge excoriates. Scrofulous children. Sub-acute and chronic rheumatism. Sensation of rigidity. Ligaments rigid. Worse stiffness of muscles on moving. Cannot remain long in one position. Stiffness of muscles on moving. Joints weak. Cannot lift things. Pain not perceived when quiet. Pain in ligaments relieved by rest. Stringy mucus from throat and posterior sinuses. Rawness. Neck muscles rigid. Subacute gouty state. White coated tongue. High colored urine with red sandy sediment.

Modalities - Better rest. Worse in the morning. Worse from moving, especially in lumbar region and joints of hips, shoulders and wrists. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1) Lyc., Phos. Rhus- t. (2) Puls., but modalities differ. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - gins. Ginseng. Wild ginseng. Panax quinquefolia. Panax ginseng. Aralia quinquefolia. Schinseng. N. O. Araliacee. Trituration and tincture of the root. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Appendicitis. Backache. Borbo- rygmi. Debility. Flatus. Headaches. Hiccough. Lumbago. Memory, weak. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Sexual excitement. Typhlitis.

HERBAL - The symptoms of the Chinese and the American Ginseng are taken together, as the two are probably identical. The root is forked like that of the mandrake. The name ginseng is said to signify “the resemblance of a man” or a man's thigh. The shape of the root might indicate an action on the pelvis and lower limbs.

HOMEOPATHIC - Lembke and others have proved it. It is an aromatic stimulant and removes feelings of fatigue, imparting a joyous sense of vigor and elasticity to the limbs, especially the upper limbs, and clearness of mind. Malaise. Y awning. Drowsiness with headache. Feeling of extreme heat and intense coldness, longing to expose the body to cool air. Stimulates the secretory glands, especially salivary. Dry mouth, tongue and lips. Mouth and throat are sensitive to the ordinary air of room. Hiccoughs. Affects the respiratory organs. Acts on the lower part of the spinal cord, lumbago, sciatica and rheumatism. Paralytic weakness. Skin symptoms, itching pimples on neck and chest. The right side of the body is most affected. Pain in right side of hypogastrium, extending into groin. MIND - Mood quiet and contented with good courage. Calm, but impatient impulses. Disposition to weep. Anxious about the future. Fear of misfortunes. Fear of accidents. Thinking is difficult. Memory weak.

Head - Head seems at times enlarged and to sway to one side. Pressure in longitudinal sinuses. Drawing pains. Painful sensitiveness of the head. One-sided head pain. Lancinations from right side of the forehead as far as the orbit with heaviness of the eyelids. Sudden shock in occiput, followed by pains, as of a bruise.

Eyes - Pressure on the eyes. Pupils alternately large and small. Unpleasant sensation of coldness on surface of eyeball. Great difficulty in opening the eyelids, which are heavy and painful, itching of the eyelids. Biting and itching in margins of lids. Vision indistinct. Sensation of fatigue when exposed to the light. Objects appear double when looked at fixedly in reading, the characters become confused.

Ears - Buzzing noises.

Face - Alternation of redness and paleness. Burning erythematous redness on right cheek, alae nasi, chin. Lips red, dry, rough, thick, cracked and bleeding, especially the lower lip. Drawing in jaws and bones of face.

Mouth - Tongue red and smarting with thirst. Tongue white, dry with large glistening papilla. Green saliva. Swallowing of saliva, very difficult on account of dryness. Mouth, lips and teeth very dry, voice rough and scraping.

Throat - Tonsillitis (Bell.), in dark-complexioned people. Vertigo - Vertigo, cloudiness, confusion, giddiness and heaviness of the head. Vertigo on going down winding stairs. Vertigo while standing, the ground seems to waver. Vertigo with gray spots before eyes. Vertigo with semi-lateral headache, occipital. Vertigo difficult opening of eyelids, objects appear double. COMMENTS - Very valuable herb in China, the wild ginseng of Siberia is said to be the best. Natives along the Ussuri river use it boiled for headaches, colds, fevers, and stomach pains. In America, it is a domestic remedy for the after pains of labor. J. H. Henry said it acts on the lower part of the spinal marrow. He noted that it is also useful for “bruised pains in small of back and thighs (on rising from bed). Great languor with paralytic, rheumatic pains in lower limbs. Arthritic swelling of the foot, which had been exerted a long time. Violent pain in big toe.” Henry also mentioned a “nightly digging in right lower limb from hip to big toe, cramp, pains from right hip to toes, lancinating, tearing in right tarsal joint.” He considered it specific in lumbago, sciatica and chronic rheumatism that are accompanied by a frequent desire to urinate and sexual excitement. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aral., Coca. (2) Hed. - depression and skin irritation antidoted by Gunpowder. (3) In “Drowsiness with head- ache”Bruce., Hera., Gels., Nat-s. (4) Nux-m. and Sulph. in dry lips, Bry. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Stomach - Pressure on the stomach. Oppression and pressure of clothing intolerable. Painful drawings in the stomach, as from hunger. Swelling and pulsation of the stomach. Contractive pain in the stomach with anguish, difficulty of respiration. Drawing pains in the stomach and lancinations in right side, which stop respiration. Inclination to vomit.

Abdomen - Tense, painful, rumbling. Pain in right side. Loud gurgling in ileo-cecal region. Dull borborygmi in the abdomen, tension and feeling of inflation, emission of wind, uneasiness and yawning. Peri-typhlitis.

Rectum - Evacuation difficult. Sticking in rectum. Tenesmus and lancinations. Hard stool, which is not emitted without efforts, followed by burning in the anus. Thin stools preceded by short violent pain, extending from within the pelvis to the thighs, as though one must sink to the ground. Liquid stools in the evening, preceded by colic.

Male - Voluptuous tickling at end of urethra. Pressure in testicles. Weakness of genital organs. Sexual excitement. Nocturnal erections without pollutions. Painful erections while sitting at engrossing business. Rheumatic pains after frequent emissions.

Female - Premature menses. Premenstrual lumbar pains. Leucorrhea.

Chest - Aching and oppression in the chest with great difficulty of respiration. Oppression of the chest with anxiety and lancinations in pit of stomach and lumbar region. Prostration of strength and lassitude in the limbs.

Heart - Severe pain, cutting, dagger-like lancinations and stitches in précordia. Some violent beats while sitting and followed by sensation of floundering of heart with rapid, small indistinct pulse. Pulse very irregular.

Back - Stiffness in back. Coldness in back and spine. Pressure in dorsal vertebrae. Frequent cracking in upper cervical vertebrae on moving head. Heaviness and stiffness in nape. Drawings in neck muscles. Weight in nape of neck with contusive pain along back of sacrum. Pulsation in vessels of right side of neck. Painful lassitude along back with bruised feeling down to and in sacrum. Deep lancinations around loins, between the shoulder blades, extending to right shoulder.

Limbs - Skin feels tight, contracted. Stiff, contracted joints. Much cracking in joints on moving. Bruised pain in limbs alternating in different parts. Heaviness of lower limbs. Bruised pain in small of back and thighs, nightly digging in right lower limb to toes. Eruption on upper inner thighs. Hands feel swollen. Violent burning heat in fingertips. Lungs - Short anxious respiration or slow and deep with exertion. Frequent deep inspiration and tightness of chest as if he could not get enough air, better while walking. Contractive pain across lower thorax. Dry cough in paroxysms. Voice rough and hoarse.

Sleep - Much yawning and drowsiness. Vivid, lascivious dreams, of which the recollection remains. Awakens with difficulty or else with a start.

Skin - Itching pimples on the skin of the neck and of the chest. Itching below right foot.

Modalities - Better at dinner. Worse in open air. Worse night. Worse from talking. Worse bending, turning. Worse descending stairs. Worse sitting.

Kidneys - Sticking and voluptuous twitching in navicular fossa. Pruritus and burning in urethra with frequent urging to urinate. Yellowish lemon-colored urine, depositing a red sediment.

Temperature - Coldness, numbness, trembling of hands, fingers white. Chilliness through the back extending into arms, into bones of back, cold hands, blue nails.

name: Glonoinum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from open air. Better cold things, cold application. Better elevating head. Better lying still (opposite Bell.). Worse bending head backward. Worse stooping. Worse left side. Worse motion, shakingjarring. Worse stimulants, wine. Worse fruits, peaches. Worse gaslight. Worse cutting hair. Worse weight of hat. Worse suppressed menses. Worse lying down. Worse from 6 a.m. to noon. Worse in sun. Worse open fire. Worse heat on head. Worse becoming overheated. Worse hot weather. Worse from injury..
