full:
PHARMACY - guai. Guaiacum officinale. Lignum vite resin. Lignum sanctum resin. Gum guaiacum. N. O. Zygophyllaceae. The gum resin of a large tree growing in West Indies. Tincture of the gum resin. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscess. Amenorrhea. Aneurysm. Bones disorders. Bronchitis. Decay. Cholera, infantum. Constipation. Contraction. Cough. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dysmenorrhea. Earache. Emaciation. Fever. Gout. Growing, pains. Headache. Hernia. Membranous, dysmenorrhea. Mercury, effects. Neuralgia. Osteomalacia. Otitis. Ovaries inflammation. Pleurisy. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Stomach disorders. Syphilis. Throat, disorders. Tonsillitis. Toothaches. Torticollis. Tuberculosis. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Guai., which is one of Hahnemann's anti-psorics, is best known as a remedy in govt and rheumatism and as a diuretic, but it has also taken a place in old-school therapeutics as a remedy for tuberculosis. Guai. was first recommended by Brinton in the Lancet in 1857 for quinsy, was given in full doses and produced a crisis of sweat and profuse urination. Homeopathic provings developed and defined the sphere of its utility in these respects and many more. It acts on mucus membranes, muscles, fibrous tissue, joints and bones. Arthritic diathesis. Acute rheumatism. Gouty nodosities on joints. Nodes. Exostosis. Growing pains. Tonsillitis with rheumatism. Secondary syphilis. Contraction of limbs, stiffness and immobility. Muscles and tendons are contracted, resulting in pain, rigidity and swelling of the joints, and deformity. Muscles and tendons seem too short or feel sore. Contractions between scapulae, palms etc., causing distortions and immobility. Unclean odor from whole body. Promotes suppuration of abscesses. Free foul, secretions, expectoration, sweat, etc. Bones become spongy or suppurate. Burning heat in affected part. Sensitiveness and aggravation from local heat. Gnawing or sticking pains in chest. Pains often end in stitch, especially head. Contractive pain between scapula. Violent pains in limbs after a cold. Feeling that he must yawn, stretch with uneasy feeling in the whole body. Violent, spasmodic inflammatory disorders of windpipe and larynx with palpitation, preventing motion or calling for help, feels suffocating. Cough dry or with copious bloody or purulent expectoration of very offensive odor. Heat, swelling and blotchiness of face. Prosopalgia every day from 6 p.m. to 4 a.m. Toothache when biting jaws together. Progressive emaciation. Desire for apples, which helps the gastric symptoms, and a general aversion to milk and food. “Violent hunger afternoon and evening,” similar to the “sinking” sensations of Sulph. and the anti- psorics. Nausea from sensation of phlegm in throat. Marked flatulence. “Every morning vomits a mass of watery phlegm with great exertion, followed by great exhaustion.” Morning diarrhea with dry skin and chilliness. Cholera infantum, the face is like that of an old person. Constipation, dry, hard, crumbling and very offensive stool. Continuous urging even after urination with profuse fetid urine. Stitches in neck of bladder after ineffectual pressure to urinate. Cutting while urinating. General ill feeling, better yawning and stretching, worse from the least motion. Clothes feel damp. Perspiration on head on walking in open air. Chilly crawls over breasts. Chilliness in back. Cannot bear heat with pains in limbs. Marked periodicity. Stomach illness returns every summer. MIND - Indolent, obstinate, fretful. Disinclina- tion to labor. Sadanddepressed. Weakmemory. Forgetful, thoughtless, staring. Forgetful of names. Slow to comprehend. Delusion everything seems narrow. Strong desire to criticize and despise everything. Inclination to blame everybody and scold. Defiant. Disobedience. Shrieking during sleep. Weeping after nightmare.

Head - Gouty and rheumatic pain in head and face, extending to neck. Tearing pain in skull, worse cold, wet weather. Pains often end in a stitch, especially in head. Head feels swollen and blood vessels distended. Brain feels loose. Headache better walking and pressure, worse sitting and standing.

Eyes - Exophthalmos. Pupils dilated. Eyeballs seem too big to be covered by the eyelids, or eyelids appear too short. Hard pimples around the eyes.

Ears - Aching in left ear.

Nose - Pains in bones of nose. Nose swollen. Fluent coryza.

Face - Neuralgia of the left side of the face, daily from 6 p.m. to 4 a.m. Face like an old person.

Mouth - Tongue furred.

Throat - Dry. burning, swollen. Sharp stitches towards the ear on swallowing, cannot swallow without a drink. Acute tonsillitis, painful to touch. Recurrent tonsillitis followed by rheumati sm. Syphilitic sore throat. Rheumatic sore throat with weak throat muscles. Vertigo - Vertigo on rising. COMMENTS - Affected parts are very sensitive to touch, worse from heat. Offensive secretions. Rheumatism in syphilitic and mercurial patients. Growing pains in children. Acute tonsillitis, simple or rheumatic. Syphilitic sore throat. “Burning in the throat.” Erythematous or inflammatory angina with bright redness (Bell.). Edema (Apis.). Phlegmon with tendency to suppuration of tonsils (Bar-c., Apis.). Burning sensations in mouth, throat and stomach. Stitches in chest going from front to back or from below upward in region of apex, worse from motion and deep inspiration. “Sharp pain about mid-day under right breast to shoulder.” Neuralgia of left side of head and face, extending to neck. Sharp stitches in brain. Sensation as if the brain were loose. External headache with sensation as if blood vessels were over-filled, extending to face and neck. Tearing pains in skull. Swelling and sensation of swelling in eyes and nose. Eyes feel protruded. Ozanam gave it in the 1c, 2c and 3c dilutions and found that he got the curative effects without crisis, which was an unnecessary effect of the drug. Guai., said Ozanam, seems to combine the properties of Bell., Apis and Bar-c. Houghton cured with Guai. 3x a case of gouty inflammation of the meatus of the ear and tympanum after failure with Ferr-p. Concomitant rheumatic lameness and soreness led him to Guai. Verwey treated a woman, who for several years had a frequently recurring gouty inflammation of the knees. After Chin. 30c had failed to relieve, Guai. 30c was given without obvious benefit. Guai. 1c was then given, and after a few hours the swelling broke and the pains quickly subsided. A short time after, the same patient accidentally injured the same knee. Under Guai. 1c the swelling soon broke and the pain was relieved, but an abscess formed at the same time on the upper thigh. The pain became unbearable and the patient's husband “begged for more of the drops that had twice before made the swelling break.” It was again given and in six hours the abscess evacuated. On two later occasions Dr. Verwey saw Guai. act in the same way on scrofulous and gouty abscesses. This is probably analogous to its action in quinsy. RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Nwi-v. Antidote to: Caust., Rhus-t. Compare: (1 ) Merc., Caust., Rhus-t., Mez., Rhod. (2) Ph-ac. - growing pains. (3) Cimic. - pleurodynia and tuberculosis. (4) Bry. - chronic rheumatism when the joints are distorted, worse motion, pleurisy in second stage of tuberculosis. (5) Coloc. - contractions after rheumatism. (6) Caust. - Guai. is better than Caust., which it follows well, when either gout or rheumatism causes distortion of limbs. (7) Araceae - late tuberculosis, pleuritic pains left apex. (8) Kali-i., Phyt., Still. Compatible: After Merc. - Rheumatism, gout and syphilis, after Sulph. in cholera infantum, after Caust. in torticollis. Follows: Sep. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Thick, white fur on tongue. Constricted epigastric region. Burning in stomach. Vomits a mass of watery mucus, then exhaustion. Stomach disorders return in summer.

Abdomen - Distention, flatulent. Intestinal fermentation. Sensation of constriction or stoppage in epigastrium, causing cough, dyspnea.

Rectum - Cholera infantum, face like an old person, emaciation. Diarrhea.

Male - Seminal emissions without dreams. Discharge from urethra.

Female - Ovaritis in the rheumatism, with irregular menstruation, dysmenorrhea and irritable bladder. Food - Aversion to milk, to all food, could not eat anything. Desire for apples and other fruits, which relieve gastric symptoms.

Chest - Pleuritic stitches. Chest pains in articulations of ribs, with shortness of breathing until expectoration sets in. Pain in the chest while riding in the open air, better pressure and walking, worse sitting and standing.

Back - Pain from head to neck. Aching in nape. Stiffneck and sore shoulders. Contractive pain between scapulae. Stitches between scapulae to occiput. One-sided stiffness of back from neck to sacrum. Breasts - Cold crawling over breasts. Shuddering in breasts with goose bumps.

Limbs - Growing pains (Calc-p.). Arthritis deformans. Arthritic lancinations fol- lov/ed by contraction of limbs. Sciatica and lumbago. Gouty tearing pains with contractions. Immovable stiffness. Joints swollen, painful and intolerant of pressure, can bearno heat. Stinging pain in the limbs. Feeling of heat in the affected limbs. Rheumatic pain in shoulders, arms and hands. Rheumaticpain in wrists. Pricking in buttocks, as if sitting on needles. Hamstrings too short. Ankle pain extending up the leg, causing lameness. Lungs - Feels suffocated. Recurrent pleurisy. Pleuritic stitches, worse deep breathing. Stitching in apex of (left) lung. Tuberculosis. Dry. tight cough. Fetid breath after coughing.

Sleep - Yawns and stretches for relief of general ill feeling. Frequent waking from sleep, as if from falling.

Modalities - Better external pressure. Better apples. Better yawning and stretching. Better from cold locally. Worsefrom heat. Worse cold, wet weather. Worse touch. Worse motion. Worse exertion. Worse rapid growth. Worse mercury. Worse puberty. Worse 6 p.m. to 4 a.m.

Kidneys - Continuous urging, even after urination. Sharp stitches during or after urination.

Perspiration - Profuse sweat on single parts, face, etc. Sweats at night. Much sweat, especially on head and face. Sweats on walking in open air. Sweat is usually offensive.

Temperature - Sweat profuse on single parts, face etc. Night sweats. Burning of body. Hot palms. Burning fever with hot face and dry cough. Fever with chill in the evening.

HERBAL - Guaraña is a climbing shrub of Brazil, the seeds of which contain caffeine and are used by the natives for making a stimulating beverage.

HOMEOPATHIC - Guar, is used in conditions of nervous exhaustion, sick headache in those who have abused tea and coffee. Headache followed by vomiting and excited by any error in diet or depression of mind. Throbbing, congestive headache after excessive use of liquor. Neuralgia. Persistent twitching of eyelids. Paralysis. Restlessness, nervousness, weariness. Reduced vital powers, with grief, depression of spirits, loss of appetite. Debility after prostrating diseases. Chlorosis. Diarrhea. MIND - Intellectual excitement, mental hyperesthesia. Extravagant behavior. Grief, depression of spirits.

Head - Sick headache from excess of tea or coffee. Throbbing, congestive headache after excessive use of alcohol.

Eyes - Persistent twitching of eyelids.

Rectum - Cholera infantum. Stools profuse, bloody, bright green, mucus, flakes intermixed, odorless. Diarrhea of tuberculosis.

Sleep - Uncontrollable sleepiness and heaviness of head, with flushed face after eating. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Agar. - Twitching of eyelids. (2) Ign., Nux-v. (3) in sick headache, Coff., Coca., Thea. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Skin - Chloasma on temples and arms. Urticaria (Dulc., Apis, Chlol.). Prurigo.

Bladder - Spasm of bladder. Causations - Ill effects of alcohol or coffee.

HOMEOPATHIC - Petroz is the authority for this remedy, which produces a number of symptoms in the eyes. R. K. Ghosh cured a number of cases of chemosis and pterygium. He found a lotion of Guarea tincture of great assistance. Lupus of an ochre-red color. Eye symptoms alternate with diminished hearing. A number of symptoms were experienced in the umbilicus and inguinal rings. Flow of blood between menses. On the skin there were liver spots and an eruption with burning vesicles. Aromatic- smelling sweat. Sweat during or after eat ing. Suppuration of glands. Steatoma, hot swelling, swelling of affected parts. Sensation of constriction. Sudden shocks of whole body. Bruised pains. Pains in periosteum. In the head there is a sensation as if the brain were falling forward and a sensation as of a blow on the head leaving numbness and diminished thinking power. MIND - Anxiety during fever. Irresolution. Loquacity. Indifference. Fear of losing reason.

Head - Sensation as if brain were falling forwards, as from a blow on head.

Eyes - Conjunctiva inflamed, swollen. Tearing pain in eyeballs, tension, forced-out feeling. Objects appear gray, upside down. Eye symptoms alternate with diminished hearing.

Ears - Swelling of periosteum behind ears. Sensation in ears as of a peg of a worm, pushing-out feeling. Roaring in ears.

Nose - Coryza with hardened secretion with heat. Nose stuffed, ineffectual desire to sneeze, constriction at root of nose.

Face - Suppurating swellings on face. Swelling of upper lip.

Mouth - Mouth smells of cheese. Sweet taste, food tastes insipid.

Throat - Tonsils swollen. Esophagus has raw pain, sensation of contraction and burning heat. Swallowing difficult.

Stomach - Constriction in stomach, bruised. Sour belchings with tension and pressure at stomach. Inclination to vomit during fever. Vomiting, sour, green.

Abdomen - Hardness at umbilicus. Abdomen distended with lancination in groins and inguinal ring. Bruised pain externally.

Rectum - Constriction of anus and rectum. Urging to stool. Constipation.

Female - Fetid leucorrhea after menses. Flow of blood between menstrual periods. Itching of pudenda. Labor pains suppressed. Lochia is scanty. Food - Canine hunger in evening, speedy satiety. Aversion to milk, fish and hot, greasy, cooked food.

Chest - Sensation of hollowness and dilatation of chest.

Limbs - Jactitation of limbs. Cracking in joints. Nightly pains in bones. Bruised pain in bones. Caries. Lungs - Cough with sweat, pain and tightness of chest, larynx irritated. Cough dry barking, violent, deep- seated. Breathing, sobbing, difficult during chill. Respiratory symptoms worse from putting hand to throat.

Sleep - Sleepy in open air. Dreams, anxious, melancholy, full of strife.

Skin - Yellow spots on temples! Liver spots on arms. Eruptions behind ears. Herpes. Itching. Lupus of ochre- red color.

Modalities - Better hot drinks. Better wrapping warmly. Acids and cold water aggravates. Bone pains worse at night.

Tongue - Tongue coated during the fever, grayish yellow, swollen, paralyzed, bleeding. Tongue feels cold and dry. Lancinations in tongue. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bov. - flow of blood between menses. (2) Crot-h. - as if had a blow on the head. Anae. - peg in ear. Gels - vertigo, ptosis. Aza., Apis - chemosis, asthmamillari. Am. - injuries. Phos. - steatoma. Ign. - nerves. Merc, and Sil. - Bone-pains, suppuration. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Temperature - Coldness followed by heat with sweat. Heat of upper part of body, coldness of bones. Sweat chiefly during and after eating. Sweat aromatic.

HOMEOPATHIC - Described in 1790 by J. B. Guatteria and in 1906 by G. F. Gaumer. The symptomatology was established by Castro on seventeen adults of both sexes, using 3x and 6x, in 1944. There are grounds for thinking that Guat. will take one of the first places among the homeotherapeutic remedies for liver conditions, alongside Chlorpr. Guat. acts on the liver, gallbladder, kidneys and pancreas. Digestive complaints with liver and biliary manifestation. Predominantly on the right side, lungs, scapulae, shoulders, kidneys. MIND - Irresolute, weak memory. Sad. Obsessive ideas.

Head - Occipital pain, aggravated in a warm room and by lying down. Frontal pulsating headache.

Eyes - Conjunctival jaundice 'vith photophobia, myosis and itching, ameliorated by rubbing.

Mouth - Tongue dirty, yellow, furred, especially at the root. Bad breath, mouth tastes bitter. Excessive, thick salivation.

Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Bilious yellow and green vomiting, aggravated by hot food, movement. Burning in the esophagus and stomach, aggravated by condiments and sweets. Vertigo - Vertigo with headaches, heavy head. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Chel. - Same side and located on the right, stools golden yellow. (2) Chin. - Extreme abdominal distentions, aggravation from loss of fluids, diarrhea. (3) Lyc. - Melancholy, irritable, dyspepsia, hepatic disorders, aggravated ffom4 p.m. to 8 p.m. (4) Lac-c. - Perspiration stains the underwear yellow, symptoms move from right to left. REFERENCES - Julian.

Abdomen - Epigastric pain, spreading towards the right hypochondrium, right kidney and the base of the right lung. Abdominal distention, ameliorated by belching. Constitutions - Allergic, psoric or sycotic constitutions.

Rectum - Diarrhea with cramping colic or constipation, followed by burning and tenesmus after stools passed. Stools bright green or bright yellow, hard or liquid, mucous, with a nauseating odor.

Female - Excoriating, white leucorrheal discharge. Food - Extreme thirst. Anorexia, nausea. Aggravated by hot foods, condiments and sweets.

Heart - Palpitationsand tachycardia, worse after eating.

Limbs - Pain and joint aching, especially of the fingers, knees and shoulders, predominantly on the right, with stiffness.

Skin - Skin dirty, especially on the face, discolored, pigmented with brown spots on the forehead and cheeks. Brownish stains on the arms and backs of the hands. Perspiration stains underwear yellow. Eruptions with itching, yellowness, aggravated by eating, ameliorated by prolonged rest. Vesicular tension disorders.

Modalities - Better from rest. Better food, if administered in small, repeated quantities. Worse in a warm room. Worse movement. Worse on right side. Worse after meals.

Liver - Congestion of the liver. Liver deficiency. Jaundice from hepatitis or gallstones. Gallstones. Inflammation of the gallbladder. Lungs - Lung infections on the right side, bronchitis. Viral pneumonia. Dry cough with blockage in the base of the right lung, linked with congestion of the liver, aggravated by lying on the right side. Painful cough, with palpitations and tachycardia, worse after eating.

Kidneys - Hematuria, urine thick with muddy deposits of calcium oxalate. Urinary density increased. Urinary urea diminished.

Ulcers. Vaccinosis. Worms. Wounds.

HOMEOPATHIC - Gunpowder was first published in the Homeopathic World, London in 1914 by Clarke. A combination remedy of carbon, sulphur and potassium nitrate. Useful for all kinds of blood poisoning, for septic wounds and ptomaine poisoning. Strong history of use in wartime, particularly useful in World War I and II. Gunshot wounds, surgical septicemia, boils. Methane poisoning. Wartime ailments. Blood disorders. Blood poisoning from pyorrhea alveolaris. Septic suppurations. Infected wounds. Wounds that refuse to heal. Abscessed bites, infections and wounds, antiseptic. Swollen and abscessed glands. Osteomyelitis. Poisoning from bad food or water. Poisoning from meats that have been unsuccessfully tinned. Acute infections, boils, abscesses, carbuncles, and bites. Antidote to ivy and primula rash. Antidoting the ill effects of vaccinations. Preventative for various kinds of inoculations. Gonorrhea and syphilis. Shingles of the face and eyes. In some country districts a decoction of gunpowder is given to children for worms with much success.

Mouth - Sores, boils. Gum abscesses. Pyorrhea.

Male - Gonorrhea and syphilis.

Skin - Boils, abscesses, carbuncles and bites. Fistula. Infected wounds. Shingles. COMMENTS - Dr. Clarke referred to the old fashioned gunpowder that was in use before the era of high explosives and smokeless powder. Black gunpowder is a mixture and not a chemical compound. It contains three remedies, two of them polycrests. Gunpowder Nitre with sulphur and charcoal forms gunpowder. A teaspoonful of this in hot water was a favorite remedy for gonorrhea among soldiers when black powder was used. In the lower triturations, gunpowder has cured ascarides in adults. The London Police Force also knew it as a boil remedy. “Get six-penny worth of gunpowder from an oil store and take as much as would lie on a sixpence night and morning for four days and then leave it off for the same time and resume if necessary” is one such prescription. Canon Roland Upcher noted that Norfolk shepherds rubbed gunpowder onto the sheep's wounds made during sheep-shearing, and took it to cure or prevent ill effects from handling sheep who suffered from “foot-rot.” Upcher published cases of skin eruption mistaken for scabies, actually caused by handling ivy. Cured with Gunp. 3x. Clarke experimented with Gunp. 2x and developed severe herpes facialis involving the right eyebrow and the right side of the nose. Clarke confirmed the proving by curing shingles. He heard of a case of lumbrici cured with an infusion of Gunpowder by the patient. A woman, who had a very sensitive skin, was bitten by a gnat on the foot, resulting in swelling inflammation and suppuration. There was a ring of inflammation around the bite, constantly spreading and detaching the epidermis as it spread. After the failure of several remedies, Gunpowder 3x rapidly cured. A man had a bad cut with a knife on the left index finger. The wound refused to heal. An inflammatory ring stripped off the epidermis and spread more and more. Lachesis and other remedies failed to make any impres- sion. Gunp. 3x rapidly cured. Another woman was very severely poisoned by sewer-gas. There followed swelling of the right arm and axillary glands of the right side. Three months after the accident the right arm was almost fixed at the elbowjoint with swelling. 11 threatened suppuration Gunpowder above and below. The axillary glands were as large as a hen's egg. Gunp. 3x gradually resolved the trouble and, though the cure was interrupted by an attack of measles, the motility of the arm was fully restored. Canon Upcher found that occasional doses of Hep. highly increase its effects. RELATIONS - Calen, externally is also complementary. Compare: Thuja, Sil., Bar-c. - septic tonsils. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Blood - Blood disorders. Blood poisoning. Causations - Bites. Blood poisoning. Vaccinations. Wounds. Gonorrhea. Herpes zoster. Worms. Glands - Swollen and inflamed. Swollen axillary glands. Abscessed glands.

HOMEOPATHIC - Gymn. causes numbness and blueness, especially of the tongue. Bluish-white coating of tongue. Sore throat, dark livid redness of fauces. “Erysipelatous swelling of face and head, hot face, it feels swollen is compelled to rub the eyes.” Hives. Headache, throbbing in forehead, temples and over eyes. Full, tight headache, with sensation as if the eyes were pushed forward. Burning in eyes. Full sensations and burning pains. Desire for heat and quiet. C. T. Bingham cured a man of headache following influenza “a constant severe pain in front part of head, especially under eyebrows and upper part of nose.” It lasted over two weeks, ne ver ceasing and at times intolerable. Bones of eye-sockets were sore to touch. Tongue was covered all over with bluish-white coat, did not enjoy food. Very weak. Gym. 2x cured. Epidemic fevers of typhoid character have been cured by it. MIND - Forgets everything. Slow grasp, cannot think, comprehend or study. Indifference to what happens around him.

Head - Tight feeling, as if bound.

Eyes - As if were pushed forward, wants to rub them. Pain under brows into the nose.

Face - Erysipelatous swelling. Crawling as of flies over the face.

Mouth - Great sensibility of teeth, especially to cold air. Toothache from slightest cold air or drink. Lungs - Tickling with dry, hard, racking cough. Tickling in throat in morning causing cough, increasing through day.

Throat - Sore throat, dark livid redness of fauces and tonsils. Smarting in larynx. Sticking pain. Mucus in throat and hawking.

Stomach - Hot, sour belchings. Burning spot in stomach.

Abdomen - Pain in left side as if spleen were swollen. Soreness and tenderness of abdomen. Stitches in bowels and umbilical region.

Stool - Constipation with ineffectual desire. Aching fullness in rectum after stool.

Male - Itching of gland and prepuce.

Chest - Pressure on chest and sternum.

Limbs - Violent pain in left forearm, in radius, as if bones were crushed and broken. Pulsation in left index finger, as if panaritium were forming.

HOMEOPATHIC - Logwood is a well- known dye of commerce. The tincture was proved by Jouve in 1939 and some very distinctive symptoms were produced including general uneasiness with anxiety arising from the stomach, and colic. Weak digestion accompanies and complicates most other conditions. General sensitiveness. Painful sensibility of the limbs with lassitude. Constriction in many parts, culminating in the stomach and abdomen. Colic with chest symptoms like angina pectoris. Sensation as if a bar lay across chest. Chilliness predominates, but the symptoms are better in open air. MIND - Ill humor, sadness, melancholy. Inclination to repose, desire to weep. Difficulty when reflectingandexpressingone'sideas. Vexation. Anxiety at night. Anxiety arising from the stomach. Mistakes in speaking.

Head - Head feels constricted, heavy, hot, painful. Constriction in the forehead and in the occiput with burning heat in the head. Headache at night, as from indigestion, with swelling of the stomach and abdomen, anxiety, inclination to vomit, sour risings of food. Headache in the forehead with inclination to vomit on stooping. Pain in left forehead, spreading over face and affecting left teeth.

Eyes - Redness of the conjunctiva. Redness of the eyes with blue margins. Eyes downcast and surrounded by a livid circle. Heaviness in the eyes. Heaviness of the eyelids, compels them to close. Painful pressure on the eyes with sensation of constriction. Sensation as if sand were introduced into the eyes. Pupils contracted and sight confused. Mist before the eyes, on reading, the letters vanish. Amelioration of the symptoms when in open air.

Ears - Violent pain in right ear, extending to throat.

Face - Face pale, dejected and changed, discomposed. Pain in face.

Throat - Lower jaw with stinging in teeth and cheek. Throat feels contracted with burning pain during swallowing. Sore throat with difficult swallowing, inclination to swallow, salivation and smarting. Sensation of a-foreign substance in the throat with yawning and stretching. Vertigo - Vertigo, so as to occasion falling and dullness of ideas. COMMENTS - Sensation as if a bar lay transversely across from region of heart to right side with acute pain in left upper portion of chest. Haem. cured a case of herpes zoster with agonizing pain as if a bar lay across the chest, arresting the breathing. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. Compare: ( 1 ) Cact. (2) in compressive pains, Cact., Lil-t., Coloc., Aur., Naja. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Painful digging from abdomen to throat, causing pain in region of heart with oppression. Painful swelling in the stomach with pressure at the epigastrium and risings of flatus. Colic, tympanitis. Borborygmi and diarrhea. Inclination to vomit, sour risings of food.

Abdomen - Tympanitic distention of the abdomen and rising of air. Tension and digging in the abdomen. Pain in the abdomen with yawning inclination to vomit and stretch. Borborygmi. Colic with painful sensibility of the abdomen to the touch, inflation. Colic and diarrhea in morning. After the colic, general cold with burning heat in the palms of he hands.

Rectum - Borborygmi. Colic and diarrhea in morning.

Heart - Con vulsi ve pain in heart region with oppression. Great soreness in the region of the heart with anguish, redoubled throbbing, small pulse, burning in the hands and shivering of the body. Palpitations of the heart with diminished perspiration of the feet.

Back - Pain and chilliness between the shoulders.

Sleep - Irresistible drowsiness. Frequent yawning.

Skin - Dry skin. Herpes zoster.

Modalities - Worse at night. Worse on stooping. Worse pressure. Worse touch.

Kidneys - Urine red, scanty and burning. Limbs - The limbs are painful and languid. Pain in left shoulder, as if inflamed. Suppression of the habitual sweat of the feet.

Temperature - Chilliness predominates, shuddering, goose flesh.

HOMEOPATHIC - Halcion is a drug used for short-term treatment of insomnia. It is a member of the benzodiazepine class of drugs, many of which are used as tranquilizers. It's homeopathic used can be surmised from the side effects of this medication. Coordination problems. Dizziness, drowsiness. Nervousness. Changes in sexual drive. Chest pain. Congestion. Cramping pains. Dreaming and sleep abnormalities. Tendency to fall, stumble. Chronic fatigue. Impaired urination. Morning “hangover” effects. Tiredness and weakness. MIND - Mental confusion. Perceptual problems. Loss of sense of reality. Disorientation. Anxiety and depression. Increased anxiety during the daytime. Inappropriate behavior. Irritability. Aggressiveness, agita- tion. Behavior problems. Restlessness. Memory impairment, memory loss. Traveler's amnesia has been reported by patients who took Halcion to induce sleep while traveling. Anterograde amnesia, forgetting events after an injury. Nervousness. Sense of well-being, excitement. Hallucinations and delusions. Coma.

Eyes - Visual disturbances. Yellowing of the whites of the eyes.

Ears - Ringing in the ears.

Mouth - Dry mouth. Burning tongue. Inflammation of the tongue and mouth. Slurred or difficult speech. Taste changes.

Stomach - Nausea and vomiting. Vertigo - Fainting. Dizziness and impaired coordination. COMMENTS - The drug Halcion has been associated with the following withdrawal symptoms: Convulsions, cramps, tremors, vomiting, sweating, feeling ill, perceptual problems, and insomnia. Symptoms of the Halcion overdose may include: Apnea (temporary cessation of breathing), coma, confusion, excessive sleepiness, problems in coordination, seizures, shallow or difficult breathing, slurred speech RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cocc., Coff. REFERENCES - Murphy.

Sleep - Sleep disturbances including insomnia, sleepwalking. Drowsiness during the daytime. Insomnia. Rebound insomnia in patients who have stopped taking the Halcion drug. Sleep apnea. Nightmares.

Skin - Skin inflammation. Itching. Yellowing of the skin.

Kidneys - Incontinence.

HOMEOPATHIC - The salt springs of Hall contains chlorides, iodides, bromides, carbonates of the alkalies and alkaline earths and iron, but by far the largest ingredient is chloride of sodium. Provings have been made of this water, many of them on patients suffering from goiter. In the provings, many marked symptoms appeared in the breast glands. Great weakness and exhausting night- sweats were produced, and all the symptoms of cold in the head and chest. A number of symptoms occured after sleep and some of them woke the provers in the night. One prover had a sensation as if her stomach would fall out and as if her breasts would fall off. In many cases the pains were transient, acute and returned after a short interval. PHARMACY - halo. Haloperidol. Haldol. An allopathic drug. Halo, is a butyrophenon used as an anti-psychotic. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Backache. Catatonia. Conjunctivitis. Dermatitis. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hypotension. Impotency. Liver, disorders. Memory, weak. Nausea. Neurosis. Paresthesia. Parkinson's disease. Pseudo-bulbar, syndrome. Raynaud's syndrome. Sclerosis. Schizophrenia. Tachycardia. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - A butyrophenone drug used as an antipsychotic, also used in Huntington's chorea and Gilles de la Tourette's disease. The present symptomatology is the result of the examination of the toxicology record of the side effects of Haloperidol, and of a homeopathic proving. The proving was done by O. A. Julian who used Haloperidol in 30c, 7c, 3x and placebo, with twenty-eight collaborators in 1974-75. Out of twenty-eight provers, there were six women, and most of the provers were also doctors or students of medicine. Instability of the mind and body. Weariness, fidgets in the lower limbs, buzzing in the ears, dizzy feeling on rising. Constant need to move when in bed, resulting from sensation of formication in all the joints of the body. Physiological slowness. Disturbances of synthetic processes of the mind. Sensation of constant stress. Dawdles. Mumbles. Sensation of unreality, of being outside self, particularly in morning. Loss of notion of time. Frequent forgetfulness of everyday tasks. Confused. Difficult concentration. Desire to stay lying down and do nothing. Strong need to sleep. Talkative, especially in the evening after 9 p.m., with need to relate stories. Excited. Tendency to philosophical speculation. Sensation of constricted throat, of chest being in a vice, respiration difficult, thorax painful. Tachycardia. Respiratory rhythm disorders. Excess salivation. Nausea in the Haloperidol morning. Desires salty foods. Empty urging and constipation. General sweating. Legs give way. MIND - Extreme difficulty in concentrating and in intellectual thought. Forgetfulness and loss of sense of time. Impression of being behind acloud. Great waves of pessimism for no reason. Depression. Neurosis from anguish. Anxious, restless. Very talkative. Depersonalization of the self. Impression of disintegration of personality, especially after 9 p.m. Catatonia with attitudes, gestures, words, all strange and stereotyped. Schizophrenia and schizophrenic conditions. Euphoric state in the evening. Feeling of living “outside of myself,” and returns to himself a few hours later.

Head - Headache in the morning, localized at the frontal region.

Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Cataract. Vision misty. Deep, burning sensation in the eyes, rising to the surface with tingling in the eyelids, appearing slowly, gradually between 11 a.m. and noon.

Ears - Earache in the left ear.

Face - Face expressionless of fixed expression. Fixed gaze.

Mouth - Excessive salivation. Bad breath in the morning and after each meal.

Throat - Constricted throat. Vertigo - Vertigo with stumbling gait. Dizzy sensation with visual fog, on rising. COMMENTS - Difficult concentrating, feeling as if in a fog, as if dead. Headache in the morning. Short headaches localized in the frontal region. Headache behind the right eye, better by closing eyes, lasting only a few seconds. Heaviness of the head, starting at the nape of the neck and spreading to the occiput and rising to the top of the head, ameliorated by lying down, closing the eyes and placing the hands over the eyes. Difficulty in moving, grimacing and protrusion of the tongue. Very severe spasms of the ocular rotary muscles. Muscular stiffness and contracture. Painful contractions of the abdominal, brachial and lumbar muscles. Fleeting torticollis when stretching. Constant restlessness of the lower limbs, cannot stay sitting or lying down. Extreme trembling, stumbling gait. Raynaud's syndrome. Hysterical stitch. Paresthesia. Extreme sensitivity to touch. Symptoms better by stretching out the hands perpendicularly to the axis of the body and by bending the legs. Sleeps lying on stomach. Tachycardia. Faintness and syncope. Hypotension. Rapid pulse. Circulatory complaints including formication of the ankle, knee, wrist, elbow, scapular and humeral regions. Proliferation of hair. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Phos. Lyc. Puls. Zinc. Med. Cocc. Hydrog. (2) Anh. - Hyperesthesia of the cortex, thalamus and organs, visual hallucinations, loss of contact with surroundings, accommodation difficult and perception disorders. ( 3 ) Chlorpr. - Melancholy, difficulty in concentrating, loss of memory, had to make great effort for intellectual work, trembles, hypertonia, stiffness. (4) Agar. - Vertigo in the morning, clumsy hand movements, frontal headache, spreading to the nose with pains as if pricked by icy needles, head moves constantly, spasmodic jerking in the limbs. REFERENCES - Julian.

Stomach - Quickly satisfied. Acrid dyspepsia. Nausea, vomiting, digestive discomfort. Nausea in the morning or during the day.

Abdomen - Rumbling and belching. Painful contractions of the abdominal muscles.

Rectum - Frequent desire to go to stool, then expelling nothing. Persistent constipation, slightly ameliorated by eating prunes. Spasmodic constipation. Fecal incontinence. Anal pruritus, lasting for four days.

Male - Total impotence. Diminished or disturbed libido.

Female - Disturbed libido. Food - Hypoglycemia. Desires salty foods, which relieve. Loss of appetite, especially at midday.

Heart - Tachycardia. Faintness and syncope. Hypotension. Rapid pulse. Circulatory complaints, formication of the ankle, knee, wrist, elbow, scapular and humeral regions.

Back - Backache. Stiffness at the nape of the neck, trembling, shaky walk.

Limbs - Arthralgia. Muscle pain. Raynaud's syndrome. Pains in the bones, especially left metatarsal bone, wrists, elbows, and knees. Painful cramps in the afternoon in both thighs. Cramps in the calves. Pain in the right elbow with appearance of a few red spots. Pains in the wrists and right Haloperidol thumb. Hands hot, fingertips freezing. Lungs - Asthmatic wheezing. Irregular respiration, either rapid and superficial or short inhalation following very slow exhalation followed by an arrest of pulmonary ventilation for a few seconds.

Sleep - Insomnia. Sleep disturbed. Fear of cancer-type dreams. Sleeps better on the stomach. Frequent desire to sleep. Rises with feeling of not having slept enough, even after a good night's sleep. Difficulty getting started in the morning. Sleepy during the day.

Skin - Skin yellowish, blotchy, pink cheeks. Abnormal hair growth. Hyperhidrosis. Dermatitis in brown patches on the legs.

Modalities - Better from closing the eyes. Better hot water. Better walking in company. Better salty food. Worse in the morning.

Bladder - Retention in the bladder. Dysuria. Urinary and fecal incontinence. Constitutions - Allergic, cancerous conditions with psychopathic tendency.

Perspiration - Profuse perspiration. Sweating from the hands, more intense between 1 p.m. and 3 p.m. Fairly intense sweating from the whole body. Hands and axilla extremely wet. Palms of hands very hot, despite the fingertips being frozen.

Temperature - Fever and chilliness. Overheated.

full:
PHARMACY - ham. Hamamelis virginiana. Witch-hazel. Hamamelis macrophylla. Hamamelis dioica. N. O. Hamamelidacee. A shrub growing in all parts of U. S. in damp woods or along streams, flowers in autumn, flowers yellow, the seeds ripen the year following. Tincture of fresh bark of twigs and root. A resinoid, Hamamelin is also prepared. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aching, pains. Ankles, weak. Black eye. Bruises. Burns. Cancer. Chilblains. Edema. Enteric, fever. Gastric, ulcers. Hematemesis. Hematocele. Hematuria. Hemoptysis. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Leucorrhea. Menstruation, disorders. Miscarriage, threatened. Nipples, sore. Noises, head. Nosebleeds. Orchitis. Ovaries, disorders. Ovaritis. Phlebitis. Phimosis. Phlegmasia alba dolens. Purpura. Rheumatism. Scurvy. Smallpox. Sore, pains. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Uterus, disorders. Vaginismus. Varicocele. Varicose, ulcers. Varicose, veins. Wounds.

HERBAL - The deep red color of the tincture may be taken as thesignature of its therapeutic action. No remedy has a wider sphere of usefulness in cases of hemorrhage and disordered blood vessels. It has also a decided relation to the effects of mechanical injuries including first-degree burns. As a local application it takes rank with Arn. and Calen, in the materia medica.

HOMEOPATHIC - The principle action of this remedy is on the veins especially of rectum, genitals, limbs and throat, producing venous congestion, varicose veins, hemorrhoids and hemorrhages. Acts upon the coats of the veins causing relaxation with consequent engorgement. Passive venous hemorrhages from any part. Phlebitis. Veins, painful, varicose, sore, cutting, swollen inflamed. Painful, hard, knotty. Hemorrhages cause great exhaustion, out of proportion to the amount of loss. Hemorrhages, capillary, dark, fluid, relieves or ca ses undue weakness. Hemorrhoids with much bleeding and marked soreness of the part, the back feels as if it would break (Aesc. has little or no bleeding). Tense, bursting feeling in hemorrhoids, joints or lower limbs. Bruised, soreness of the affected part from which blood flows, in blood vessels, abdomen etc. Great value in open, painful wounds with weakness from blood loss. Relieves the pain after surgery (Calen.), supercedes the use of morphine. Prickling, stinging pain in veins, muscles, skin. MIND - Forgetful of words when talking. No desire to study or work. Averse to being spoken to. Irritable, gloomy, depressed, stupid. Feels unappreciated. Wants respect due to him. Hemorrhages with tranquil mind. Reverence for those around him. Anxiety at night. Sadness better evening. Depressed after emissions with regretful mind. Sadness from masturbation. Felt as if he was going out of his mind during headache over left eye. Thinks constantly of his ailment. Wandering thoughts while studying.

Head - Feeling as of a bolt from temple to temple. Numbness over frontal bone. Hammering headache, over left eye, left temple, as if he would go out of his mind. Stupid feeling in head. Stupor, dullness, headache, crowding fullness in head and neck, also in forehead. Fullness of head, followed by a nosebleed. Bursting headache on waking. Headache after an emission.

Eyes - Traumatic effects. Sore pain in eyes, eyes painful under slight pressure. Painful weakness. Black eye. Iritis, conjunctivitis. Blood shot eyes. Hastens absorption of intra-occular hemorrhage. Eyes feel forced out, better pressure of finger. Eyes inflamed, vessels greatly injected, caused by a foreign substance. Intense soreness after operations.

Ears - Deafness in right ear, passes off by noon. Buzzing, ringing in ears. Bleeding at right ear, also nosebleed, which clears her head, relieving her.

Nose - Over-sensitive sense of smell. Bad smell from the nose. Nose feels stopped up. Sneezing spells, watery, excoriating, burning discharge. Nosebleeds, flow passive, non-coagulable, with tightness at the bridge of the nose. Profuse nosebleed, idiopathic or vicarious. Nosebleeds with hemiplegia in old men. The nosebleed clears head and relieves.

Face - Burning in right cheek. Muscles feel sore and stiff. Occasional shooting pains along right superior maxillary to malar bone. Lips are dry, sore, cracked.

Mouth - Burns of tongue and lips, or feels burnt. Blisters on sides of tongue, canker spots near the tip. Tongue coated white. Bloody, metallic taste. Passive hemorrhage from gums after tooth extraction with soreness.

Throat - Hoarse on waking. Sore throat, worse right side, right tonsil more swollen, reddened, with distended veins. Sore throat in those predisposed to fullness of the veins, worse in warm, moist air. Mucous membrane distended and bluish, varicosis of throat. Stinging, breaking pain in uvula, while coughing. Hawks considerably. Vertigo - Swimming sensation on rising. Vertigo when stooping. Nausea and vertigo with desire to lie down. COMMENTS - Hering, who learned its properties from Mr. Pond of “Pond's Extract” fame (Pond was a patient of Hering’s), made the first provings and introduced the remedy into homeopathy. He defines its position as being between Aeon, and Arn. “Pond's Extract” is an aqueous distillate prepared from the leaves. A number of interesting superstitions are associated with the shrub, and shoots of it are used as “divining rods” for discovering water and metals. It is tonic, astringent, sedative and hemostatic. Applied topically to varicose veins. May help relieve the pain from burns (Canth.). It has been used as a mouthwash with spongy, bleeding gums. Hale gave a very full account of the remedy, noting that conditions likely to require Ham. include phlebitis and varicose veins, hemorrhoids, venous hemorrhages. The local application of Ham. to a sprained knee has been known to set up inflammation in the veins of the part and the provers who had varicose veins experienced increased sensitiveness and unusual sensations in them, a number were cured. Passive hemorrhages (Chin.), with intense soreness. The part from which the flow of blood proceeds feels sore and bruised. Fullness, soreness, and a bruised feeling. Hemorrhages are mostly dark and may occur from any orifice. Bruising and bleeding under the skin (Arn., Sul-ac.). Ecchymosis. Bruising from a puncture wound. Lack of ligament tone. Laxed ligaments, tendons, or tissues. Tired, aching, feeling in the back and lower limbs. Rheumatic symptoms with characteristic soreness. Congestion, inflammation and bleeding of hemorrhoidal vessels, with marked action in the throat (Aesc.). Phlebitis and varicose veins with soreness. Varicose angina, where the veins of the pharynx are large and blue. Taste of blood in the mouth. Headache, chiefly in the temples, throbbing, hammering, especially over left eye. Black eye (Symph., Led.). History of use in painful tumors, especially ulcerated malignant tumors where there is bruised, dark bluish or purplish color. Pricking pain in the rectum, anal itching. Dysentery, when the amount of blood is unusually large, dark, small clots or patches through the mucus. Constipation. Hemorrhoids. Metrorrhagia, menorrhagia, vicarious menstruation and hemorrhages between the period, particularly if it's dark red blood. Stagnant blood in the uterus. Ovulatory bleeding. Orchitis, ovarian disorders, phlebitis and varicose veins. Venous stasis (Bell-p., Sep.), particularly after childbirth. Ovarian disorders, orchitis, with soreness Thirst. Toothache worse in warm room, from touch. Takes cold easily from every exposure, but especially to warm, moist air. Dr. Ward noted a case in which he cured inter-menstrual pain. Allen mentioned in the provings an inter- menstrual flow and Dr. Ward observed that if his patient has had the flow, the soreness so distinctly felt might not have been realized. Hughes gave Ham. to a young woman suffering from a daily nosebleed and throbbing headache. The first dose was followed by a flushing of the face and most distressing throbbing, aching and sense of fullness in the head. The second dose brought back all the symptoms in the head and a feeling as if it would burst. Some days later, the 3x was given and again the dilatation of the cerebral vessels occurred, through the symptoms were not so severe. The scapular pain bears on the experience of Dr. Koech, who cured with Ham. many cases of scapular rheumatism. He regarded it as a specific in disorders of the last five cervical nerves. Bree said it will relieve the excessive thirst that most patients with heart troubles complain. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Arn., Camph., Chin., Puls. - toothache. Compare: (1) Arn., Calen, is better than either in hastening the absorption of intra-ocular hemorrhage. (2) Chlor., Sec., - purpura. (3) Fl-ac., Lach., Puls., Nux-v., Aesc, Nit-ac. - in varicose veins and hemorrhoids. (4) Spong., Puls. - orchitis. Ham. has more soreness. (5) Cimic. - abdominal sore- ness after labor. Ham. is an excellent external application. (6) Bry - vicarious menstruation. (7) hemorrhage in typhoid, Nit-ac. light. Ham. dark. (8) Bell., Euphor., Rhus-t., Tereb., - as an application in bums of first degree. (9) Hirudo - hemorrhages. (10) in hemorrhoids: Fl-ac., Aloe, Mur-ac. (11) in varicose veins, Mangifera indica. Complementary to: Ferrum in hemorrhages. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Blisters on side. Pain and heaviness at the back of stomach. Throbbing and pain in stomach. Cramp in stomach after eating. Belchings after a meal, taste of the food. Nausea, headache in frontal bone on awaking. Nausea and inclination to vomit after a meal. Vomiting of black blood. Hematemesis, black blood.

Abdomen - Burning in the epigastrium and umbilicus. Pain all around lower abdomen. Cramps in stomach and transverse colon two hours after a hearty dinner. Varicose veins of abdomen. Flatulence. Inguinal glands tender and enlarged.

Rectum - Anus feels sore and raw. Itching at the anus. Pulsation in rectum. Hemorrhoids, bleeding profusely with soreness. Costive, hard stools, coated with mucus. Large quantities of a tar-like blood in stools, particularly with typhoid or dysentery.

Male - Severe neuralgic pains in testicles. Pain running down the spermatic cords into the testes. Orchitis, intense soreness and swelling, worse touch. Testicles enlarged, hot and painful. Epididymitis. Varicocele. Hematocele. Emission at night without being aware of it. Profuse cold sweat on scrotum, capillary stasis.

Female - Vicarious menstruation. Menses dark, profuse with soreness in abdomen. Jolting brings on menses. Bleeding, midway between menstrual periods, only in daytime. Inter-menstrual pain. Leucor- rhea, bloody with soreness of vagina. Uterine hemorrhage, bearing-down pain in back. Ovarian congestion and neuralgia, feel very sore. Ovaritis after a blow or after abortion with soreness over the whole abdomen. Vagina very tender, sore. Vulva itches. Vaginismus. During pregnancy, legs become painful, can neither stand nor walk. Milk leg. Food - Appetite good. No appetite for breakfast. Nausea from pork. Considerable thirst, better by small quantities of water. Very thirsty in afternoon and evening, throat dry. Averse to water, makes him sick to think of it.

Chest - Chest feels sore and constricted, worse by a long or deep breath. Stitches in lower part of lungs. Dull, aching pain constantly in muscles of left chest, worse using arms afternoon and evening. Constitutions - Venous constitutions. Coughs - Tickling, with taste of blood on awakening. Dry cough, severe stinging in the uvula, as if it would break. Hemoptysis, tickling cough with taste of blood. Dry, short, with sensation of dryness in throat. Cough from a varicose condition of throat.

Heart - Pulse accelerated, full. Palpitations. Pricking pain in region of heart and superficial veins of both arms.

Back - Sore pain down cervical vertebrae. Breaking backache. Painful scapulae. Severe pain in lumbar and hypogastric region, extending down legs. Rheumatism of scapula. Chilliness in back and hips, extending down legs. Breasts - Sore nipples, bleeding. Causations - Bums. Injuries.

Limbs - Great lassitude and weariness of the limbs and elsewhere. Tense, bursting feeling in limbs and joints. Very sore muscles and joints. Rheumatism with great soreness of the muscles. Tired feeling in arms and legs. Phlebitis. Varicose veins. Varicose ulcers with bloody bases. Neuralgia of internal saphenous nerve. Milk- leg, hemorrhoids and sore nipples after childbirth. Lungs - Smothering sensation when lying. Expectoration thick, yellowish or greenish gray, tasting putrid. Hemoptysis, tickling cough with taste of blood.

Sleep - Restlessness at night. Uneasy, restless morning sleep. Emissions of semen during sleep.

Skin - Burns. Ecchymosis. Purpura. Bruises, traumatic inflammations (Arn.). Bluish chilblains. Varicose veins and ulcers, very sore. Varicose ulcers with bloody bases.

Modalities - Worse from injuries. Worse bruises. Worse pressure. Worse jar, touch. Worse motion. Worse exertion. Worse warm, moist air. Worse open air. Worse humid, rainy weather. Worse cold. Worse during day (pains).

Teeth - Sharp pain along the molar teeth, extending to the malar bone, also in temporal region. Teeth ache, can scarcely sleep, yet not decayed. Pains worse in warm room. Gums sore, painful, swollen, bleed easily, dark fluid. Passive venous hemorrhage after extraction of teeth.

Kidneys - Dull aehe about kidneys. Hematuria with increased desire for urination. Hematuria, passive congestion of the kidneys, dull pain in kidney region. Dull ache about kidneys. Urine clear copious. Scanty high-colored urine. Irritation of the urethra, followed by a discharge and ardor urine.

Perspiration - Sweats freely at night, after lying down.

Temperature - Cold creeps in the open air, chills run up the legs, head stopped up, dull pain over orbit. Chilliness over back and hips, extending down the limbs. Chilly on going to bed, dreading an attack of fever. Fever at night, hands hot, burning in the eyelids on closing them.

Sleep-like disorders (see Chic-b., Ch-bd-b.) or obsessively fixated ideas (Wh-ch- b.). Feigning or unconscious production of sickness, urge to talk about symptoms. MIN

full:
PHARMACY - heath-b. Heather. Calluna vulgaris. The flowering stems are placed in a bowl of water and allowed to sit in the sun for several hours. The water is strained and used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.

HOMEOPATHIC - Heath-b., with Wat-v-b. and Imp-b., belongs toBach's group of Loneliness. For suffering from inner loneliness as a result of being too centered within their own selves and losing the connection with others. Overbearing and agitated. Sleep-like disorders (see Chic-b., Ch-bd-b.) or obsessively fixated ideas (Wh-ch- b.). Feigning or unconscious production of sickness, urge to talk about symptoms. MIND- Self-centered. Worry over self. Feeling that one deserves sympathy and regard. Stuck on personal affairs. Attaches importance to experienced hardships and dilemmas. Craves attention and sympathy. Attentiongetting behavior. Talkative over seemingly unimportant details, to get attention, feel special or show self-pity. Feigning sickness, hypochondriasis (Chic-b., Mimul-b.). REFERENCES - Bach.

full:
PHARMACY - hecla. Hecla lava. Volcanic ash. Lava Heclae. Volcanic ash from Mount Hecla in Iceland. The finer ash falling in distant localities. The ash of this volcano contains silica, alumina, lime, magnesia with some oxide of iron. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies, lower triturations.

CLINICAL - Abscess, gums. AntrumofHigh- more, tumor. Arthritis deformans. Arthritic nodosities. Boils, gums. Bone, deformities. Bones, disorders. Bones, spurs. Bone, tumors. Breast, tumors. Dentition, difficult. Exostoses. Facial, neuralgia. Glands, disorders. Hallux vulgus. Hipjoint, arthritis. Jaw, pain. Jaw, tumors. Milk, deficient. Neuralgias. Nodosities. Osteitis. Osteomalacia. Osteosarcoma. Paget's disease. Periostitis. Rickets. Syphilis, bones. Teeth, decay. Toothaches. Tumors. Varicose, veins. Warts. White, swellings. Whitlow.

HOMEOPATHIC - When traveling in Iceland, Garth Wilkinson noticed that the sheep in the vicinity of Hecla had immense bony growths on the jaws. Another effect noticed was the drying up of the milk both in sheep and cows. The finer ash which feel on pastures at a distance was the most deleterious, the gross ash near the mountain was inert. Wilkinson added that he used Hecla, with excellent effect in toothache, gum abscess, swellings about the jaws and in difficult dentition. Hecla, affects mostly the bones of the head, jaws, jawbones, teeth and legs. Osteosarcoma, exostosis and osteitis, arrests development and prevents recurrence. Clinical experience has shown the power of Hecla, to arrest many forms of bone disease including osteosarcoma, scrofulous and syphilitic osteitis and exostoses. Painful swellings, sensitive to touch, worse from touch and pressure. Exostosis, gum abscess, toothaches, difficult teething. Nodosities, decay of bone, etc. Bone necrosis. Necrosis and sinus after mastoid operation. Facial neuralgia from decayed teeth and after extraction. Induration and infiltration of cervical glands, studding the neck like a row of pearls. Tumors in general. White swellings. Whitlow and gumboils. Syphilis. Predominantly affects the right side. Mind - Irritability. Nervousness in the morning. Sensitive to criticisms. Outburst of violent anger and feeling of helplessness. Indignation. Suppression of anger. Ailments from shock.

Head - Chronic headache, from dental or bone disease. Headache from injury of dental nerves. Tumors of the skull. Jaws - Abscess or enlargement of bone remaining after a tooth extraction. Violent pain in upperjaw. Enlargement of maxillary bone, from injury to jaw. Painful to touch, upper jaw, swelling under right alae nasi sensitive. Right cuspid of upper jaw sensitive to slight pressure.

Ears - Caries of mastoid bone. Exostosis in external meatus of ear.

Nose - Nasal polyps or tumors. Ulceration. Destructive, syphilitic ulceration of nasal bones.

Face - Facial neuralgia from decayed teeth and after extraction. Polyps, commencing in Antrum of Highmore. Tumor, deforming face, forcing eyeball upward, obstructing nostrils, extending downward into the mouth, impeding breathing and chewing, nosebleed, headache.

Mouth - Neuralgia from decayed tooth in cavity from which tooth has been extracted. Pain in wound, where tooth has been extracted. Abscess of gums. Difficult dentition in scrofulous and rickety children.

Chest - Muscle pain, especially of intercostal muscles.

Back - Induration and infiltration of the glands. Neck glands are enlarged and indurated, like a row of pearls Bones - Necrosis and destruction of bone. Bone inflammation. Bone spurs, tumors or exostoses, especially of the head, jaws, leg. Benign bone cysts, tumors. Painful bone tumors or nodosities after injury. Exostoses of fingers. Tumors of the tibia with severe continuous pain. Osteomalacia, rickets. Osteitis, periostitis. Osteitis deformans. Osteosarcoma. Breasts - Breast tumors or nodules. Diminished milk while nursing. Dried up, no breast milk. Causations - Injury to bone.

Neck - Swollen cervical glands, like a string of pearls.

Limbs - Severe, continuous pain in lower limbs. Swollen and bulging thighs and legs. Varicose veins. Arthritic nodosities. Exostoses of tibia, severe continuous pain incapacitating from work. Hip joint disease. Hallux vulgus. Deformity or nodules of the fingers, toes.

Skin - Black warts. Actinomycosis. White swellings.

Modalities - Worse from touch. Worse pressure. Worse beginning of motion. Worse sitting, rest. Worse left side.

Teeth - Toothaches, especially of teeth that are very sensitive to pressure with swelling about jaws.Dental abscess with swelling, pus worse pressure on teeth. Decay of teeth. Pain or neuralgia after extraction. Chronic dental or jaw abscess. Chronic gingivitis. Fistula. Gumboil. Delayed or difficult dentition in malnourished children. Vertigo - Vertigo everything goes up, down and sidewise. COMMENTS - Affinity for bone deformities, bone spurs and tumors (Calc-f.), bone diseases. Calcium deposits in the joints that cause deformities, deforming or rheumatoid arthritis. Spinal curvatures. Hypertrophied bone. Bone cancer. Osgood-Schlatter. Bone lesions, osteitis, periostitis, exostosis, tumor, often follow an injury to the bone. Painful and tender lesions. Enlarged and indurated cervical nodes, sometimes likened to “a string of pearls.” Decomposition and necrosis of the sinus and nasal bones, or for a history of damage or surgery in the area. Severe toothache, where the jawbone aches, boring and digging pains in the bone. Bony lesion after a dental abscess. Late state syphilis where the nasal bones deteriorate. Facial neuralgias after tooth extractions. Damage to the jawbone from dental surgery. Ulcerations of the bone. Burnett noted “On July 3, 1880, a young lady, age 15, came under my observation with an exostosis on her right os caléis, somewhat smaller an a little flatter than half a walnut shell. It was at times painful. “Patient was in other respects in good health and well nourished, but her teeth were not very sound. She goes blue in winter, and suffers also very badly from chilblains both on hands and feet, worse on hand. “Hecla lava 2c given six grains three times a day. July 17th. The exostosis is decidedly smaller; it never pains now. September 25. The exostosis has entirely disappeared; the two heels being compared, no difference between them now can be discovered.” Burnett stated “I have cured several bony tumours of the jaws with the same remedy, and that very promptly: they were all of recent origin.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Calc-f., Calc., Merc., Phos., Sil. Still., Sulph., Kali-i., Symph., Ruta. (2) Conch. - diaphysis of bone affected, parts extremely sensitive to touch. (3) Amph. - great affinity for the jaw bones, worse by air and dampness. (4) Slag - great itching of parts. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

full:
PHARMACY - hedeo. Hedeoma pulegioides. Pennyroyal. American pennyroyal. N. O. Labiate. The British Pennyroyal is Mentha pulegium. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Gastritis. Flatulent, colic. Leucorrhea. Miscarriages. Nausea. Poison oak. Vertigo. Vomiting.

HERBAL - Hedeoma puleg. is also known as the common English Pennyroyal, the German Poley, the Arabic Alnam, and the ancient Greek Glachon. Hedeoma belongs to that large class of mints and common herbs that have been cast aside by the medical profession as worthless. Hedeoma is one of the oldest remedies known, a common household herb long before the time of Hippocrates. Hippocrates and the ancient physicians used it as a tea for increasing the flow of urine, for kidney stones, and as a uterine stimulant. Popularly believed to be valuable for treating miscar1 riage in weak, cachectic women.

HOMEOPATHIC - Marked female symptoms, often associated with nervous disturbances. Bearing-down pains, worse by any movement and accompanied by almost paralytic weakness of the legs. Nervous symptoms, jerkings and twitch- ings. Weak, faint, better lying down, inability to sit up. Pains in abdomen, worse after eating or drinking, touch and pressure. Flatulent colic. Pain along ureter. Red sand ih urine. Antidotes effects of poison oak (Grin.). Abdomen - Distended, sore and sensitive. Flatulent colic.

Head - Dull, heavy feeling in morning. Sore pain, as from a cut. Weak, faint, better lying down.

Stomach - Gastritis. Everything taken into stomach causes pain. Tongue coated thin white. Nausea. COMMENTS - Anshutz wrote “Hedeoma contains three bodies peculiar to the plant, three different oils, also formic and acetic acid and likewise ischeptoic acid. There are on record seven cases of poisoning. Two provings have been made by my self. Several of the poisoning cases are very meagre and of little value. “One teaspoonful of the oil, three drachms of the essence, seems to be almost a fatal dose in one case only was abortion produced and that from one ounce of the oil, followed by collapse and death. “The leading symptoms of the cases of poisoning are briefly: Vertigo. Dimness of vision. Dilated pupils. Nausea and vomiting. Persistent severe bearing-down pains from the upper part of the sacrum and the region of the kidney to the uterus like true laborpaints. Frequent painful, scanty, burning urination. Small, rapid pulse. Nervous weakness. Cold clammy limbs.” Dr. Toothaker reported a case in which the bearing-down labor-like pains and the scanty, painful urination lasted for many days and were very severe. Clarke prescribed this remedy in two cases. In the first, a woman of gouty, rheumatic tendency, who had dragging burning pains in the left ureter going to the bladder and was passing quantities of “red sand.” The pain lasted for ten days. Hedeo. 1c, on discs, was given, one disc every two hours. Complete relief was obtained after two doses. The second case concerned a man of 60, very fond of champagne, who was bothered by constant burning irritation at the neck of the bladder, which caused frequent, intense desire to urinate and an inability to retain his urine for more than a few minutes. He always had marked relief on urinating. Urine retained in the bladder increased this irritation at the neck of the bladder and also caused an uneasy pain in the right testicle. These symptoms had been more or less persistent for months and the attacks always lasted days at a time. Complete relief was obtained after one or two doses of Hedeo. 1c. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Menth., Sep., Lil-t. (2) Oci. - uric acid diathesis, pain in ureters. (3) Hed. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Female - Leucorrhea with itching and burning. Ovaries congested and painful, bearing-down spasmodic contractions. Bearing-down pains with much backache, worse least movement.

Limbs - Pain, coldness and paretic conditions. Twitchings, jerkings, soreness. Pain in thumb joint. Achilles tendon painful, as if sprained and swollen, walking painful. ,

Kidneys - Dragging pain from kidney to bladder. Dull burning pain over left kidney. Frequent urging, cutting pains. Pain along left ureter. Burning irritation at neck of bladder causing frequent, intense desire to urinate and inability to retain urine for more than a few minutes, better urinating.

Hay fever. Hemor- rhoids. Herpes. Hydrocephalus. Insomnia. Leucorrhea. Menorrhagia. Myocarditis. Raynaud's syndrome. Rhinorrhea. Rickets. Sinusitis. Tachycardia. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - Hederá helix, or Ivy, is a shrub that grows all over Europe. It is a creeper, which fixes itself by clinging roots. The leaves are cadiform at the base and more separated in the higher parts of the plant. The fruit is bluish-black in color, equal to a pea in size. Historically, the wood was used for coughs as an anti- spasmodicl; the leaf was used internally as an emmenagogue and externally as a topical anti-neuralgic. The fruit was used for intoxication, digestive and nervous complaints, delirium, and convulsions. The mother tincture is used for coughs and is prepared from the flowering twigs.

HOMEOPATHIC - The symptomatology was established by Mezgerin 1932 on seventeen people, using the lx, 6x, and 15x potencies, for a period of twelve weeks. Easily tired, ameliorated by fresh air or noticeable increase in physical ability. Dr. Cooper's experience has shown it to have a relation to rickets and rickety conditions. Rhinorrhea cerebro- spinalis. Hed. has been used for “clearing the sight” and Cooper said it has cured cases of cataract. Joint pains and circulatory complaints, especially in the middle of the night. Cardiac palpitations. Acts on blood vessels, menorrhagia. Menses reduced, vesicular eruption on the face and body. Swelling of the thyroid glands. Glándula sub-mentalis inflamed. Extreme anxiety with the feeling of constriction of the throat. Cough with laryngeal and tracheal irritation. Morbid hunger, gastric cramps. Diarrhea. Anus feels raw and sore. Hemorrhoids with rectal irritation and bleeding. Delirium and convulsions. Chronic hydrocephalus, rhinorrhea, and cerebro-spinalis. General improvement in fresh air. but extreme sensibility to catching cold and to chills. Symptoms start on the left side and spread towards the right. MIND - Constant state of unrest and worry. Anxiety, which grows all the more as he feels incapable of mastering it. Insomnia. Psychological symptoms improve in fresh air.

Head - Catarrhal inflammation of the frontal sinuses with headache. Headache, especially in the left side of the forehead and nape of the neck. Neuralgic pains in the head, ameliorated by fresh air.

Eyes - Feeling of sand in the eyelids. Cataract. Muscae volitantes.

Ears - Pain and buzzing.

Nose - Hay fever. Acute and chronic rhinitis. Sinusitis (frontal, ethmoidal). Pharyngitis. Nasal discharge, worse in a warm room. Pain in the ethmoid and frontal sinuses. Chronic tracheitis, caused by a lesion in the nasal mucous membrane.

Mouth - Transparent vesicles on the lips and on inside of cheeks in a group, circumscribed by ared ring. Toothache from hot and cold. Dental neuralgia.

Throat - Chronic tracheitis. Pain around the tonsils and throat on swallowing. Hoarseness and inflammation of the larynx. Cough with a cold and inflammation of the pharynx, aggravated by heat and by speaking. Vertigo - Vertigoon bending down and from rapid movement of the head. COMMENTS - Cooper published case of a woman of twenty, who was cured of chronic hydrocephalus with a single dose. When she was brought to Cooper, the circumference of her head was 27.5 inches, rendering her an object of wonder and ridicule and reacting on her disposition and nervous state. The condition had existed from childhood and was apparently growing much worse. There were two large edematous swellings on the nape of the neck, one on either side and immediately below the occiput, evidently the result of intra-hydrocephalic pressure. One drop of Hed. tincture was placed on her tongue. The next morning, clear fluid began dripping from the nostrils, a “cerebrospinal rhinorrhea” in face. This continued for three weeks, between twenty and thirty pocket-handkerchiefs were used in a day. Simultaneously the swellings began to diminish and had completely disappeared when the discharge ceased. Thirteen months later, when being measured for a hat, it was found that the size of the head was reduced to 25 inches and no longer occasioned remark. When, later on, some symptoms of brain pressure seemed to threaten, a second dose of Hed. completely dispelled them. The disposition of the patient was completely changed from being nervous, unhappy and diffident, she became lively, cheerful and active. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aral-r., Gins., Sil., Nat-m. (2) lodum - is the remedy, whose symptomatology is very similar. lodum shows more emaciation inflammation and hardening • of the lymphatic glands. Ovarian pain on the right and menses more abundant. (3) Calc- fl - Fear that his way of life will collapse. Pains aggravated by humid or cold weather. Menses copious. Hardening of the breasts, ovary or uterus. (4) Nat-m. - Depressed and sad, prefers solitude. Emaciation. Fissure in the middle of the lower lip. Chronic, periodic headaches with strong pulsating, as though the head would burst. Dryness of the mouth with extreme thirst. REFERENCES - Clarke. Julian.

Stomach - Pain on empty stomach, ameliorated by eating. Nausea, gastric heaviness, stomach cramps. Gastritis. Stomach and duodenal ulcers.

Abdomen - Pancreatitis. Constitutions - Tubercular conditions, especially in phosphoric types.

Rectum - Stools copious, either diarrhea or constipation.

Female - Premenstrual leucorrhea. Acrid, scorching discharge. Menses late, shorter and less copious. Infrequent menses. Feels better during menses. Amenorrhea in young girls. Pain in the Fallopian tubes and left ovary. Sclera-cystic ovaritis, especially on the left side. Genital tuberculosis. Food - Lack of appetite or strong hunger pangs.

Heart - Angina pectoris. Needle-like pains in the precordial region. Palpitations and anguish with swelling of the thyroid gland. Myocarditis. Arterial sclerosis. Rhythmic anomaly, accompanied by tachycardia. Thyrotoxic tachycardia. Extrasystole or paroxysmal tachycardia, in a young subject with a normal heart.

Limbs - Pain in the arms, legs, back and sacral region, sometimes ameliorated, sometimes aggravated by movement. Muscular rheumatism. Joint rheuma tism. Tubercular inflammatory dislocating rheumatism. Arthrosis deformans. Nocturnal paresthesia pains in the arms. Raynaud's syndrome.

Sleep - Wakes around 3 a.m., falls asleep again after eating a little.

Skin - Pruritus. Eruption of small pustules on the skin of the face and body. Prurigo. Urticaria. Labial and genital herpes.

Modalities - Better from fresh air. Better cold baths. Better in a room. Better movement. Better friction, massage. Better in the afternoon and evening. Worse in the middle of the night. Worse 3 a.m.

Liver - Inflammation of the gallbladder. Gallstones. Pain in the region of the gallbladder. Cirrhosis of the liver with cardiac decompensation. Lungs - Irritated cough with grayish or yellow sputum. Whooping cough. Bronchial asthma in children. Emphysema.

Kidneys - Frequent, abundant urination.

Temperature - Peripheral circulatory complaints. Feet and hands icy, red. Shivering and chilliness with bouts of perspiration and palpitations. Shivering and nausea in the evening until 4 a.m.

HOMEOPATHIC - Helia. is a spleen remedy (Cean.). Spleen disorders. Chronic cases of intermittent fever. Coryza, catarrh, nasal hemorrhage and thick scabs in nose. Rheumatic pain in left knee. Externally, used as a vulnerary like Arn. and Calen. In the pro vers there were marked effects on stomach, with nausea and vomiting. Congestion and dryness of mouth and pharynx. Dry mouth. Redness and heat of skin, worseexternal warmth. Black stools (Lept.), soft, with an emission of semen; stools become black, hard, occurring every other day. Hemorrhoids.

Head - Headache.

Eyes - Slight redness on margin of left upper lid with smarting in inner canthus. Eyes suffused. Weakness of the eyes.

Nose - Coryza, catarrh. Nosebleeds and thick scabs in nose.

Face - Anxious, countenance. Face deeply flushed. Food - Thirst, nausea.

Mouth - Tongue and fauces very red and inclined to dryness. Unusually hot taste when eating. Difficulty in articulation. Sticking in upper back teeth.

Throat - Voice hoarse. Stiffness and dryness of the throat. Sensation of glowing in the throat and stomach. Severe burning in fauces, esophagus and epigastrium. COMMENTS - Dr. Cessoles proved the expressed juice of the flowers, some observations have also been made on the effects of eating the seeds. In some parts of America the Native Americans use the seeds as an article of food. Hansen said it equals Arn. and Calen., also yellow-flowered composites, as an application to wounds. Burnett regarded Helianthus as a great spleen remedy. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lept. - black stools. (2) Arn., Calen., Hyper. - wounds. (3) Cean. - spleen. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Vomiting, increasing in severity-

Abdomen - Spleen enlarged and painful.

Rectum - Hemorrhoids. Stools soft, black, hard, every other day, with emission of semen.

Limbs - Rheumatic pain in left knee on descending stairs. Lungs - Cough in forenoon with gelatinous expectoration streaked with blood. Breath rather difficult and hurried.

Skin - Skin generally of scarlet redness and very hot. Tingling of skin. Many urticarialike pimples. Groups of red pimples on inner side of knee with slight itching. Small red tetter to right of navel. Measles.

Modalities - Better after vomiting. Worse from external heat, especially the skin.

HOMEOPATHIC - Helio, has been slightly proved. Cooper used this remedy clinically and considered hoarseness and “thick voice” a great indication. He cured clergyman's sore throat with it. Helio, has an action in uterine displacement, leucorrhea, backache. There is a bearing down from heavy, waterlogged condition of the uterus. , Symptoms of pressure and tension were produced in many parts: pressure on the sternum impeding breathing, pressure on the head, on mons veneries, pain as if beaten in leg muscles.

Head - Headache in forehead like a pressure and drawing pressing pain, better walking in open air.

Eyes - Feeling of tension in left inner canthus extending down into nasal bone. As if a swelling were there. Eye seems drawn together and smaller.

Throat - Voice thick, clergyman's sore throat. COMMENTS - Cooper gave Helio, to a woman who had been advised by several surgeons to have various organs either braced up surgically or removed. She described the effect as having made her “feel just as if braced up” six hours after taking the dose. Helio, is especially indicated if there is also a tendency to loss of voice. It has also cured membranous dysmenorrhea. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bor. - membranous dysmenorrhea., (2) Symph. - bruised pain in leg. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Stomach - Pressure in pit of stomach, worse on inspiration. Epigastric region is sore to touch, most violent after eating and in evening.

Female - Membranous dysmenorrhea. Leucorrhea. Pressure on mons veneries only when sitting. Uterine displacements with backache, especially if subject to loss of voice.

Chest - Pressure and oppression of external parts of chest, without affecting breathing.

Limbs - Pain, as if beaten above ankle, extending up the muscles, even when sitting. Itching on tibia, with sensations as if there was an eruption.

Modalities - Head symptoms better on walking in the open air. Other symptoms were worse after resting. Worse on inspiration.

HOMEOPATHIC - Snails have a tradition for curing tuberculosis. COMMENTS - W. H. Leonard reported two cases cured with Helix 100,000c. In the first, a man had frequent hemoptysis. Continuous hoarseness with a dry tickling cough, worse at night, preventing sleep. Dyspnea, worse from ascending stairs. He had already had all the usual remedies. Helix 100,000c., three powders were given. There was no more hemorrhage. A few weeks later a return was feared and a few more doses were given. Four months later the patient was greatly improved in health and remained well. In the second case, a woman of tubercular diathesis developed the disease after confinement. Several well- indicated remedies failed to check its progress. At length, hemorrhage set in. Helix was given, as in the other case, with prompt effect. Hemorrhage ceased, cough and expectoration gradually improved, and in eight months the patient was well and remained so. REFERENCES - Clarke.
