full:
PHARMACY - hippoz. Hippozaeninum. Glanders nosode. Glanderinum malleinum. Farcin. The nosode of glanders or farcy. Triturations of sugar of milk saturated with the virus. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Bedsores. Boils. Bronchitis. Cancer. Carbuncles. Decay. Catarrh, chronic. Cold, chronic. Diphtheria. Elephantiasis. Erysipelas. Glanders. Glands, inflamed. Hip-disease. Liver, enlarged. Lupus. Nasal, cartilages, ulceration. Edema. Ozaena. Parotiditis. Phlegmasia alba dolens. Phlegmon. Plague. Pustules. Putrid, fever. Pyemia. Scrofula. Smallpox. Syphilis. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Whooping cough.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hippoz. is a powerful nosode introduced by Dr. Garth Wilkinson. The disease is called “Glanders” when the catarrhal symptoms are pronounced, “Farcy,” when these are not noticeable, the skin being chiefly affected with deposits in the lungs. Homeopathic preparations of both have been made. In horses, glanders affects the lungs and the upper respiratory tract, causing coughs and disseminated ulcerations and deposits throughout the lungs. Mallein, a toxin prepared from glanders, was used in veterinary practice as a test injection for deciding whether a horse suspected of glanders actually has the disease or not. Hippozaeninum If the horse reacts it is concluded there is glanders. In a number of cases in which animals reacted to the first injections, repetition of the test has failed to elicit reaction, thus suggesting that Mallein is curative as well as diagnostic. The nosode has been used by homeopaths, at the suggestion of Wilkinson, on the phenomena of the disease as guides. It has been used in a large number of cases involving low forms of suppuration and catarrh. Ma- lignant ulcerations and swellings, abscesses and enlarged glands and also in conditions similar in kind, but less in severity. Weakness, fatigue, general discomfort. General prostration with considerable emaciation. Numerous ecchymoses in internal organs. Inflammation of lymphatic vessels and swelling of glands. Phlegmasia alba dolens. Pyemia, erysipelas. Chronic rhinitis, bloody secretion. Symptoms suggesting tuberculosis, cancer, syphilis, etc. It promises useful service in the treatment of ozaena, scrofulous swellings.

Head - Fainting turns with headache. Inflammation of membranes of brain. Scattered abscesses in brain substance. Purulent collections between bones of skull and dura mater. Tubercles may appear in periosteum of skull in dura mater in plexus choroides. A diffused myelitis malleolus, attributable to infiltration. Bones of skull and face (frontal most) decayed. Hair loses its glisten.

Eyes - Full of tears or slime. Pupils dilated with collapse. Papules on choroid coat of eye.

Ears - Tinkling sounds in ears. Hoarse and deafness. Inflammation of parotid gland.

Nose - Cartilage exposed and decayed. Decay of nasal bones. Nose and mouth ulcerated. Swelling and redness of nose and adjacent parts, with severe pain. Discharge often one-sided, albuminous tough, viscous, discolored, gray, greenish. Bloody Hippozaeninum and offensive, acrid, corroding discharge. Obstinate catarrh. Chronic ozaena.

Face - Maxillary gland swollen, firmly attached to the maxilla, uneven, rugged, mostly painless, burning at times. Submaxillary and sublingual glands swollen and painful at times, abscesses are formed which open externally.

Mouth - Difficulty speaking. Tongue dry, thickly covered with a black, sooty deposit. Gums covered with a black, sooty deposit. Bleeding gums. Breath putrid. Ulcers in mouth. Buccal passages filled with tenacious lymph and mucus. Scrofulous swelling of left parotid gland in a child.

Throat - Hoarseness. Swollen tonsils closing posterior channels. Ulcerations on velum of palate. Upon mucous membrane of pharynx ecchymoses, redness, swelling, eruptions and foul ulcers. COMMENTS - Clarke used Hippoz. with excellent effects in cases of inveterate nasal catarrh and of glandular enlargement. The nasal affection may go on to ozaena, ulceration of nasal cartilages and bones. Papules and ulcerations in frontal sinuses, pharynx, larynx and trachea. Hoarseness. Old cases of bronchitis, especially in old persons where suffocation from excessive secretion seemed imminent. Bronchial asthma. Whooping cough. Long-lasting coughs. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bacil., Syph., Variol. (2) The serpent poisons. (3) Aur.. Cadm-s., Kali-bi„ Hep., Psor. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Abdomen - Gastro-intestinal catarrh, indigestion, constipation in later stage, diarrhea. Spleen enlarged, filled with blood, softened and liquefied, of a grayish or dark color. Wedge-shaped abscess in spleen. Swollen inguinal glands. Coughs - Cough and obstructed respiration, resulting from scar contraction of mucous membrane of nose and larynx. Whooping cough. Severe cough with profuse expectoration.

Rectum - Colliquative diarrhea with a general cachexia and exhaustion precede the fatal termination. Constipation.

Male - Tubercles and abscesses of glans penis, testicles.

Female - Slimy discharge from vagina. Uterine phlebitis. Miscarriage. Hippozaeninum Food - Loss of appetite. Thirst excessive, especially with diarrhea.

Limbs - Obscure pain in limbs, mostly in muscles and joints. Swollen arm with sore finger. Phlegmonous and erysipelatous with pustules and ulcers. Hip-disease. Psoas and lumbar abscesses. Old. bad leg ulcers. Anasarca of lower limbs.

Sleep - Insomnia and great restlessness. Nocturnal delirium.

Skin - Erysipelatous erythema. Malignant erysipelas, particularly if attended by large formations of pus and destruction of parts. Confluent smallpox. Abscesses, pustules and ulcers over all of body. Ulcers have no disposition to heal, livid appearance.

Liver - Enlarged liver, signs of fatty degeneration. Hepatitis with gangrenous and ulcerative inflammation of gall-ducts. Lungs - Papules and ulcerations in frontal sinuses, pharynx, larynx and trachea. Bronchitis, especially in elderly persons, where suffocation from excessive secretion is imminent. Noisy breathing. Loud, snoring respiration before fatal termination, breath fetid. Tubercles, size of millet seed to a pea, of a gray, yellowish or reddish color. Tuberculosis, diminishes expectoration and recurring aggravations and checks liability to catarrhal disorders. Lung disease of cattle.

Kidneys - Tubercles and abscesses in kidneys. Albumen in urine, also leucine and tyrosine.

Pulse - Frequent and small pulse, 110 to 120. Retarded pulse.

Temperature - Frequent chilliness. Chills and fever in cases of abscesses and ulcers. Skin becomes cool with collapse. Fever when a series of abscesses follow in rapid succession. Putrid fever. Plague. May be tried in scarlatina, where odor of breath is putrid, mouth filled with tenacious lymph and mucus tonsils greatly swollen.

author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better in the open air. Better with pressure. Worse in a warm room, heat. Worse with movement. Worse in late afternoon or at night..
constitution: Arthritic pains. Backaches. Blepharitis. Chemosis. Cirrhosis. Dacryocystitis. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Gastritis. Headaches. Jaundice. Laryngitis. Menorrhagia. Migraine. Pimples. Premenstrual syndrome. Vincent's angina.

CLINICAL - Arthritic pains. Backaches. Blepharitis. Chemosis. Cirrhosis. Dacryocystitis. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Gastritis. Headaches. Jaundice. Laryngitis. Menorrhagia. Migraine. Pimples.…
full:
PHARMACY - hip-ac. Hippuricum acidum. Hippuric acid. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritic pains. Backaches. Blepharitis. Chemosis. Cirrhosis. Dacryocystitis. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Gastritis. Headaches. Jaundice. Laryngitis. Menorrhagia. Migraine. Pimples. Premenstrual syndrome. Vincent's angina.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hippuric acid is present in urine, very rarely as an amorphous and crystalline deposit. The proving was carried out in 1952-53 by Dr. W. B. Griggs on seven men and three women over a period of forty- five days using potencies ranging from lx to 6x. Its chief action is on the external tissues of the eyes and naso-pharynx, joint surfaces, liver and mucous membranes. Nasal secretion viscous, yellow evil-smelling. Inflammation of the throat with a dry cough, especially at night. Pain in the liver with bouts of nausea and ajaundiced complexion. Hyper-productivity of the ovarian follicles. Eruption of pimples on back, chest, legs. Severe headache on the right side, aggravated by heat and amelio- rated in the open air. General muscular soreness and tenderness. Muscular and joint pains in the shoulders, back, lower limbs. Right side is especially affected. Rheumatic and poisoned subjects. Allergic mesenchymatic with arthritic ten- dencies. Arthritic and tubercular conditions in elderly patients. Weak exhausted types. MIND - Concealed anxiety. Irritability.

Head - Dull, constant pain over right eye, worse in warm room. Dull aching, aggravated in warm room, ameliorated by fresh air. Occipital headaches, vertigo. Migraine.

Eyes - Eyelids inflamed and swollen, edema. Jaundiced, yellow conjunctiva. Painful inflammation, especially of the lower lid, on the right side. Dacryocystitis. Blepharitis. Chemosis. Visual complaints.

Ears - Buzzing in the ears.

Nose - Sensation of a blocked nose. Swelling over lower ethmoid bone. Sinusitis. Secretion thick, viscous, yellow, evil-smelling. Acute rhinitis. Adenoids. Nasal polyps.

Mouth - Offensive breath.

Throat - Acute laryngitis. Dry throat. Pain and difficulty in swallowing. Sore, raw, dry. foul odor, gummy exudate, thickness and infiltration of tissues around throat. Eructation with a lump in the throat. Exudation thick and membranous around the tonsils and the back of the throat. Gangrenous inflammation of throat. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Benzoic acid seems to be an analog. Benz-ac. - A uremic type with brown, strong urine, whitish, fetid diarrhea, joint pains especially in the big toe and Achilles' tendon. (2) Merc-cy. - Infectious, weak conditions. Diphtheria. Inflammation of the anus and rectum. Bad breath and cervical inflammation. (3) Guai. - Red, burning tonsillitis. Pleurodynia with a dry cough. Diarrhea resembling that of cholera. Joint pains. (4) Rhus-t. - Erythematous and vesicular rash. Muscular and joint pains, worse during rest, ameliorated by a change of position or by continued movement. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Julian.

Stomach - Feeling of a lump in the pit of the stomach. Lump in pit of stomach. Soreness and pressure over liver. Acid rising. Acrid belching. Nausea, vomiting, hepatic pains, especially when pressure is applied.

Abdomen - Pain and heaviness in the liver. Entero-colitis. Abscess beneath the diaphragm. Infectious epidemic jaundice. Cirrhosis. Acute cholecystitis.

Rectum - Diarrhea with watery, fetid stools.

Female - Premenstrual syndrome. Menstruation prolonged yet scanty. Menstrual flow for three weeks with complete relief of muscular and joint pains. Menorrhagia. Hyper-productivity of the ovarian follicle.

Chest - Pain on the right side of the chest when coughing.

Back - Lumbar aching, especially at the end of the day. Backache extending down hips. Breasts - Breasts painful during menses.

Limbs - Pain in shoulders and limbs. Pain in middle of thigh posteriorly shooting down right leg. Sore, swollen joints. Tired, grating sensation in the joints. Lungs - Cough dry, irregular, gasping, worse at the end of the day. Dry rightsided pleurisy.

Skin - Itching, burning, tingling and shuddering sensations. Yellow coloring of the skin. Eruption of spots and pimples, on the back, chest and legs. Papules looking like goose flesh on chest. Erythema.

Modalities - Better in the open air. Better with pressure. Worse in a warm room, heat. Worse with movement. Worse in late afternoon or at night.

Kidneys - Hot, pungent urine, smelling strongly.

name: Hirudo Medicinalis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from sitting. Better coughing. Worse after defecation. Worse left side, but not exclusively..
constitution: Aerophagy. Alcoholism. Angina. Anal, bleeding. Aneurysms. Cervicitis. Colic. Conjunctivitis. Headaches. Hemiplegia. Hemoptysis. Hemorrhages. Hepatitis. Jaundice. Leucorrhea. Myelitis. Ovarian, cysts. Paraplegia. Thrombophlebitis.
keynote:
PHARMACY - hir. Hirudo medicinalis. Leech. Sanguisuga officinalis. N. O. Hirudinea. Tincture of the animal. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Aerophagy. Alcoholism. Angina. Anal, bleeding. Aneurysms. Cervicitis. Colic. Conjunctivitis. Headaches. Hemiplegia. Hemoptysis.…
full:
PHARMACY - hir. Hirudo medicinalis. Leech. Sanguisuga officinalis. N. O. Hirudinea. Tincture of the animal. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Aerophagy. Alcoholism. Angina. Anal, bleeding. Aneurysms. Cervicitis. Colic. Conjunctivitis. Headaches. Hemiplegia. Hemoptysis. Hemorrhages. Hepatitis. Jaundice. Leucorrhea. Myelitis. Ovarian, cysts. Paraplegia. Thrombophlebitis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Burnett was the first to use Sanguisuga or Hirudo medicinalis as ahomeo- pathic remedy for hemorrhages. Dangerous hemorrhageshave frequently followed the application of leeches and it has been ascertained that the leech does not merely bite, it poisons the bitten part in such a way as to render the blood in it watery. The symptomatology was established by members of the International Homeopathic League, following the Congress in Amsterdam in 1961-62. Members of the British, American and Chilean leagues participated in the proving. The group from London, whose report was made by Reside, was made up of eighteen people, nine men and nine women. Hir. caused the provers to feel lively and energetic, then exhausted suddenly, shivers, felt depressed. Alternating well being and depression. Throbbing frontal or occipital headache. Progressive lacunar cerebral sclerosis. Syphilitic hemiplegia and paraplegia. Myelitis, tabes. Transverse, myelitis, preceded by intermittent claudication. Tendency to bleed. Bleeds easily from all the orifices. Irregular heartbeat and congestion of the veins. Menses irregular and burning leucorrhea. Gastro-intestinal malfunctioning with nausea, vertigo, diarrhea or constipation (stools streaked with bright red blood). MIND - Lively spirit, alert, animated with sense of well being. Condition alternates with lack of energy, sleepiness and tires easily. Depressed, sad, sluggish. Weary with a heavy head and difficulty in concentrating. Irritable, angry or tearful. Fear of falling backwards when looking up.

Head - Hot, heavy head, with pulsations going from the occiput towards the forehead, with dizziness. Headache at the vertex, accompanied by nausea. Pulsating frontal and occipital headache, especially in the evening. Feeling as though the head were in a vice. Wakes during the night from a constrictive headache located around the occiput.

Eyes - Red, painful photophobia. Difficulty focusing. Nervous twitching of the lower eyelid. Conjunctivitis.

Ears - Outer ear hot. Left ear red and burning. Boil in the auditory canal.

Nose - Nosebleed, slight bleeding on wiping nose. Pimples and boils on the nose. Pustule on the left side of the nose. Swelling on the nose.

Face - Neuralgic pains on the left or right of the face.

Mouth - Mouth painful with bleeding gums. Small ulcerous swelling on the uvula. Ulcerations on the soft palate, roof of the mouth and tongue.

Throat - Swallowing painful. Throat painful with sensation of a ball stuck in it. Tonsils, neck glands swollen. Tonsillitis, glandular fever, infectious mononucleosis. Vertigo - Vertigo after exertion or when sitting down. Fear of falling backwards when looking up. COMMENTS - Burnett had a case of persistent bleeding from the rectum, the blood was watery and all the usual hemorrhagic remedies failed to arrest it. Burnett thought that Hir. might prove a similar remedy. He had a tincture made and attenuated, gave the 5c potency and cured the case. To make Hir., macerate the end of aleech's head for twenty minutes in a mixture of sand and a physiological serum. Centrifuge the liquid and agreen liquid residue is obtained, which is dried after the addition of thymol. The substance obtained forms the stock for the preparation of the potencies. W. Schwabe of Stuttgart, who prepared this stock, called it -‘Hirudin.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lat-m. (2) Naja - Weakness and cardiac complaints with coughing and choking. Left-sided ovarian pain. Sudden desire to commit suicide. (3) Crot-h. - Skin or cellulitic inflammations. Hemor- rhaging of black, clot less blood. Infectious or adynamic conditions. REFERENCES - Clarke. Julian.

Stomach - Nausea, flatulence, general weakness, worse in the morning. Alcoholic gastritis. Discomfort in the stomach after lunch with nausea and burning acridity and a tart taste. Nausea before eating with diarrhea. Vomiting around 4 a.m. Gastric and duodenal ulcer (hemorrhaging type).

Abdomen - Severe abdominal distention. Acute pain in the epigastric region and hypochondrium. Wakes at 2 a.m. from abdominal colic, worse after defecation. Colic with nausea and diarrhea around 10 a.m. Alcoholic hepatitis. Aerophagy, accumulation of air in the colon.

Rectum - Proctitis. Anal pruritus. Rectal pain after passing stool. Bright red blood seen in stools, caused by painful constipation. Bacillary or protozoic dysentery.

Female - Left-sided ovarian pain like being stabbed. Brownish leucorrhea two days before menses. Menses, too early or late, heavy or light, painful or less painful than usual. Feeling in the pelvis as if menses would come on two weeks before due. Cervicitis. Endometriosis. Incoordination of the hypophysis, thalamus and ovary. Ovarian cysts. Pre-cancerous condition of the neck and body of the uterus. Food - Thirst for cold drinks in large quantities. Indigestion from fatty foods with consequent anorexia.

Chest - Angina pectoris. Constitutions - Allergic and psoric constitutions. Phosphoric, syphilitic and neuro- biliary types. Hemophiliac types.

Heart - Extra systolic rhythm anomaly. Irregular heartbeats when lying down. Heart irregular with dull, diffuse pain in the precordial region when going to bed. Pain in the region of the heart when sitting, when bent forwards, ameliorated by sitting up straight. Rheumatic endocarditis. Aneurysm of the aorta. Syphilitic aortitis.

Limbs - Pain in the left arm. Sharp pain in the joints of the hands, elbows and shoulders. Transient pains in the legs. Hands and feet cold in a warm room. Swelling of the left ankle. Feet swollen and painful. Lungs - Hemoptysis.

Sleep - Sleep disturbed by disordered dreams or nightmares, thinks he is being followed.

Skin - Spots on the nose and face with pustules and boils, small wounds. Rough patch on chin. Burning spot on upper lip. Boils. Anthrax. Axillary adenitis of sweat glands. Sycosis of the beard.

Modalities - Better from sitting. Better coughing. Worse after defecation. Worse left side, but not exclusively.

Blood - Hemorrhage. Jaundice caused by destruction of red corpuscles. Disease due to a change in the quality of blood platelets, prothrombin deficiency, thrombocyte dystrophy and capillary weakness. Skin and mucous purpura. Thrombophlebitis.

Temperature - Cold shivers coming suddenly without apparent cause.

name: Histaminum Muriaticum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from pressure. Better fanning. Worse from heat. Worse movement. Worse nervous irritation, and deep breathing..
constitution: Allergic, reactions. Angina pectoris. Arteritis. Asthenia. Asthma. Bee stings. Blepharitis. Bronchitis. Cancer. Cervicitis. Colitis. Conjunctivitis. Cystitis. Dysthyroid- ism. Edema. Emphysema. Gastric, duodenal ulcers. Headaches. Hives. Insomnia. Itching. Ovaritis. Pericarditis. Pruritus. Pyelonephri- tis.Rashes. Typhoidfever. Urticaria. Vertigo. Whooping cough.
keynote:
PHARMACY - hist. Histaminum muriaticum. Histamine. Imidazolethylamine. Histamine hydrochloricum. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergic, reactions. Angina pectoris. Arteritis. Asthenia. Asthma. Bee stings. Blepharitis. Bronchitis. Cancer. Cervicitis. Colitis.…
full:
PHARMACY - hist. Histaminum muriaticum. Histamine. Imidazolethylamine. Histamine hydrochloricum. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergic, reactions. Angina pectoris. Arteritis. Asthenia. Asthma. Bee stings. Blepharitis. Bronchitis. Cancer. Cervicitis. Colitis. Conjunctivitis. Cystitis. Dysthyroid- ism. Edema. Emphysema. Gastric, duodenal ulcers. Headaches. Hives. Insomnia. Itching. Ovaritis. Pericarditis. Pruritus. Pyelonephri- tis.Rashes. Typhoidfever. Urticaria. Vertigo. Whooping cough.

HOMEOPATHIC - Histamine is a capillary vessel dilator, an arteriole vessel constrictor, and a hypertensive. It constricts the bronchi and stimulates the tissues of the intestine, the uterus, and the gastric and pancreatic salivary secretions. It is normally used in the form of histamine bi-chlorhydrate, which serves as the stock for homeopathic preparations. The symptomatology was established in 1950 by J. Gringuaz of Buenos Aires, on thirty-nine provers, using the potencies 30c, 200c, 1000c, then 12c, 6c and 3c. Hist, has general asthenia as after physical exertion. Feeling of constriction in different parts of the heart. Quivering and cramping contracture of the muscles. Irritable, susceptible, impatient, with need to walk up and down. All symptoms of the skin and mucous membranes in allergic types. Dryness of the mucous membranes. Redness and burning sensation in circumscribed areas of the skin. Red, itching papules. Burning, cramping, spasmodic pains in the joints and muscles. Headaches and vertigo with sensation of heat and burning on the head and face. Loss of sense of taste. Feeling that the teeth are loose. Pruritus and burning in the nose, throat, ears and vagina. Burning pains in the scrotum and left ovary. Oliguria with burning and pain on urination. Burning epigastric and abdominal pains. Burning precordial pain. Burning thoracic pain, fitful coughing. MIND - Sensitive to the slightest trifles. Impatient, restless with need to move from place to place aimlessly. Nervous when waiting. Quarrelsome. Slowness and difficulty in understanding. Cannot find correct words, forgets proper nouns. Melancholic with anguish and reduction of mental faculties. Sad. prostration which disappears by forced walking. Pain and gastric constriction when receiving news or remembering a painful experience. Psychogenic allergy.

Head - Frontal pain, at the temples and nape of the neck, spreading towards the front and back of the head. Heavy, compressive headaches, better by cold, pressure and fresh air, aggravated by movement, bending the head, and sun. Sensation of tension of tightness at the scalp with pruritus. Sensation of heat and itching in localized places.

Eyes - Contracture and muscular twitching of the eyelids and around the eyes. Spasmodic closing of the eyelids. Allergic conjunctivitis. Blepharitis. Feeling of a foreign body in the eyes. Stinging pain, as if a nail were being driven into the eye, better from cold, aggravated by a draft. Edge of the eyelids red, edematous. Feeling of heat and pruritus at the edge of the eyelids. Yellowish secretion from the eyelids or dryness of the mucous membranes.

Ears - Pain in one or other of the ears, spreading to all the sense organs. Pain in the mastoid. Feeling of blocked ears with ringing and heaviness in the ears. Alternating sensation that the ear is blocked, then clear.

Nose - Pruritus in the nose with feeling that the skin on the nose is shrinking. Feeling that nasal orifices are enlarged. Feeling of painful dryness in the nostrils. Inspiration difficult and painful in cold air. Nose blocked on one or both sides. Head cold with blocked nostril on one side and feeling of heat and prickling. Spasmodic rhinitis.

Face - Facial pains on one side of the face, spreading towards the upper and lower maxilla and the teeth. Unilateral heat on the face.

Mouth - Mouth dry. Loss of sense of taste. Wine smells of perfume. Salivary secretion sometimes profuse, sometimes dried-up. Heat and itching in the mouth. Dares not open mouth too wide, as a result of pains arising from the passing .of cold air. Accompanying dental and precordial pains.

Throat - Painful dryness of the pharynx, worse swallowing or heat, better from cold. Dry throat. Feeling of a lump or a foreign body in the throat. Feeling of pressure, constriction in the throat, as if tied by a band. Vertigo - Vertigo, as if on a swing with nausea and misty vision. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Apis - Acute inflammations with rosy edema, prickling, burning pains, as if produced by red-hot needles. (2) Ars. - Anxiety, agitation. Burning pains. Cadaverous odor of the secretions. (3) Sec. - Tendency to hemorrhage. Burning pains and chilliness all over the body, putrid diarrhea, cramps, especially in the lower limbs, chilliness, pallor and burning pains at the limbs, worse in the cold. REFERENCES - Julian.

Stomach - Nausea when eating or thinking about eating. Stomach heavy, distended, as though it would burst. Stomachache, as if he had eaten indigestible food. Tense, anguishing pain, caused by a weak feeling in the pit of the stomach, worse when recalling unpleasant memories or receiving news. Sensation of fire in the stomach.

Abdomen - Acrid dyspepsia. Gastric and duodenal ulcers. Painful contractions. Sensation of constriction at belt-level. Spasmodic enterocolitis. Hemorrhagic rectocolitis. Ulcerous membranous colitis. Typhoid fever and paratyphoid fever.

Rectum - Painful contractions, followed by diarrhea. Black stools with a nauseating odor. Tenesmus and feeling of not having finished, when expelling stools.

Male - Hydrocele. Epididymitis and orchitis. Prostatic adenoma. Burning, stinging, drawing pains. Pain travels from one side to the other. Pain moves in the scrotum with occipital headache.

Female - Left-sided ovarian pain, spreading to the leg and left hypochondrium. Menses too early or late. Diminution in quantity of menstrual flow. Menses extremely foul-smelling. Leucorrhea with smell of “burnt” blood. Cystitis. Ovaritis and salpingitis. Cervicitis. Cervical cancer.

Chest - Stinging pains in various parts of the thorax. Thoracic pain, as if caused by contusion or crushing. Angina pectoris. Feeling of anguish in the chest, which necessitates deep breathing. Constitutions - Allergic and psoric constitutions. Tubercular types with dys- thyroidism.

Heart - Precordial pain as if produced by a needle. Pericarditis. The heartbeat is irregular with an extra systole with compensatory intervals. Pain in the heart region with constrictive feeling, drawing, dull pains. Heart pain that alternates with or accompanies a toothache. Feeling of heart “caught up,” and need to hold it with the hand. Heart feels too large. Feeling as if drops of icy water were flowing through the heart.

Limbs - Arteritis of the lower limbs. Allergic rheumatism. Muscular and joint pains, burning, stinging, drawing, dull, crushing pains. Involuntary spasms and muscular contractions. Feeling of exhaustion, does not want to make the slightest movement. Formication, tickling, pruritus in the muscles. Feeling of heat, as if he had been burned. Sensation of an electric current across the arms. Sensation as if band were tied around the stomach and around the limbs. Lungs - Lack of air, feeling of oppression, constriction in the chest. Coughing fits which almost choke him with tickling in the throat preventing speech. Persistent, dry, fitful cough, coming from the throat or the supra-sternal cavity. Yellowish, white-yellow, orgreenish-yellow sputum, tasting of cheese. Dilatation of the bronchi. Chronic bronchitis. Asthma. Emphysema. Whooping cough.

Sleep - Insomnia until 2 to 3 a.m. Insomnia with abundance of ideas. Dreams of insects.

Skin - Urticaria. Red, itching papules, the size of a pea, all over the body, better scratching, worse bathing. Redness and heat on the skin of the face, as after a first degree burn. Sensation of heat and burning, hyperasesthesia. Formication and tickling with numbness on different areas of the skin. Lichen planus. Prurigo strophulus. Hair becomes dry. Alopecia, hair loss from the head and body.

Modalities - Better from pressure. Better fanning. Worse from heat. Worse movement. Worse nervous irritation, and deep breathing.

Teeth - Dull or drawing pains in the teeth and cavities of extracted teeth. Alveolar, dental pyorrhea. Teeth feel loose, dares not chew for fear of losing teeth.

Kidneys - Cystitis. Pyelonephritis. Unbearable feeling of heat in the bladder, all the time, needs to urinate, but can only pass a few drops at a time. Urinary retention with urination only in drops, feeling of having to strain and accompanying the hemorrhoid congestion. Despair at inability to urinate. Urine burns like fire. Needle-like pain in the bladder towards the urethral canal.

Temperature - General chills, shivering, alternating with feeling of heat. Feeling of great heat with sweating and weakness.

name: Hoitzia Coccinea
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better lying in a curled-up position. Worse from movement..
constitution: Aching. Blepharitis. Chickenpox. Conjunctivitis. Diphtheria. Encephalitis. Eye, disorders. Gastric, typhus. Hematuria. Iritis. Keratitis. Measles. Meningitis. Miliary, fever. Myocardia. Paratyphoid, fever. Pericarditis. Photophobia. Scarlet fever. Smallpox. Typhoid fever. Typhus. Vaccinations, effects. Valvulitis.
keynote:
PHARMACY - hoit. Hoitzia coccinea. Colibri flower. Loeselia coccinea. N. O. Polimo- niaceae. Mexico. The tincture is obtained from the entire fresh plant. Tincture of the dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aching. Blepharitis. Chickenpox.…
full:
PHARMACY - hoit. Hoitzia coccinea. Colibri flower. Loeselia coccinea. N. O. Polimo- niaceae. Mexico. The tincture is obtained from the entire fresh plant. Tincture of the dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aching. Blepharitis. Chickenpox. Conjunctivitis. Diphtheria. Encephalitis. Eye, disorders. Gastric, typhus. Hematuria. Iritis. Keratitis. Measles. Meningitis. Miliary, fever. Myocardia. Paratyphoid, fever. Pericarditis. Photophobia. Scarlet fever. Smallpox. Typhoid fever. Typhus. Vaccinations, effects. Valvulitis.

HERBAL - Hoitzia coccinea grows in the valley of Mexico. Its common name Colibri flower comes from the feeling on touching it. It seems to be covered with small thorns.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hoit. has high temperature from the start and increases in intensity. Stifling feeling of heat, general aching. Shivers at every movement. Red appearance, high and steady temperature. Acute infectious conditions. Nervous and circulatory over-excitability. Uneasiness, fear, exaltation. Heavy sleep. Congestion of the head, eyes, stomach intestines and genital organs. Pains in the throat, neck and ears. Thirsty, anorexia, frequent and scanty urination. Scarlet fever, anasarca-type and urticarial eruptions. Post-vaccination encephalitis. Anti-smallpox and anti- diphtheria. Encephalitis following measles, chickenpox. Serous meningitis in young subjects. MIND - Fearful, anguished state of mind. Nervous excitability, groaning. Hallucinations. Abdomen - Pains in the epigastric and intestinal regions. Acute inflammation of the gallbladder and biliary passages. Acute enterocolitis. Crohn's disease, terminal ileitis. Abdominal muscles painful.

Head - Head heavy with sensation of fullness. Congestive beating in the temples with dizziness. Acute frontal headache, stupefying, soothed by holding the painful area tightly.

Eyes - Bloodshot and burning, conjunctiva red. Blepharitis. Conjunctivitis. Iritis. Keratitis. Edges of eyelids red, edematous. Eyelids heavy, swollen, tend to close, half closed. Gaze is fixed and vague. Photophobia, weeping.

Ears - Sensation of blocking in the auditory canal. Crackling noises with dryness of the ear. Acute congestive otitis.

Nose - Nose swollen, painful. Vesicles and scabs on the edges of the nostrils. Nosebleed frequent, but lasts only a short time. Maxillary and frontal sinusitis. Ethmoiditis.

Face - Face red, swollen.

Mouth - Mouth dry, burning. Swollen gums and tongue. Saliva thick, sticky, difficult to spit. Breath fetid.

Throat - Throat red, swollen, burning. COMMENTS - Hoitzia is a voracious plant belonging to the Polimoniaceae family. It grows up to 1 meter in height with a tap-root, gnarled with fine isolated rootlets, which in turn give out other smaller rootlets. It has a straight, cylindrical stem, “sub-ligneous,” covered with small whitish hairs, alternated, oval, spear-shaped leaves and axillary flowers. In herbal medicine, it is used as a sudorific remedy. The Mexican cowherds use it for fevers and eruptions in their cattle. The women use a decoction of the plant for washing their hair as it prevents hair from falling out. Twenty drops of the mother tincture in a half-liter of boiled water can be used as a compress for irritations of the scalp resulting from the use of hair dyes. The mother tincture is obtained from the entire fresh plant and it was Manuel De. Legarreta who established its homeopathic proving. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bell. - Active congestion with nervous and vascular excitability. Dryness of the mucous membranes. Photophobia. Hyperthermia. (2) Euphr. - Irritating, excoriating weeping from the eyes. Non-irritating coryza. Amenorrhea. Frequent urination. (3) Ars. - Agitation with fear of death. Burning pains. Cadaverous odor of secretions. (4) Rhus-t. - Agitation of the body. Stiffness of the limbs. Skin red, swollen with vesicular, burning, itching eruptions. REFERENCES Julian.

Stomach - Acute pain in the stomach with vomiting of mucus and bile. Phlegmonic gastritis.

Rectum - Stools hard, dry, round, burning, followedbyadysentery-like pressingneed to evacuate with tenesmus.

Male - Prostatic adenoma.

Female - Copious menstruation, which improves the general condition. Menses late by two to three months, then menorrhagia with intense bilateral ovarian pains. Profuse metrorrhagia with acute, burning pains, tearing pains, black blood with clotting and a putrid odor. Lochia, very copious. Burning and itching leucorrhea. Heat in the low abdomen, painful with feeling of a foreign body in the abdomen. Food - Thirst for water, which repulses, followed by vomiting.

Chest - Constrictive oppression as after running a race. Sensation of tightness in the thorax, as if in a breast- plate.

Heart - Strong and rapid heartbeats, resounding in the head and audible. Pericarditis. Myocardia. Valvulitis.

Limbs - Acute joint rheumatism. Muscular rheumatism. Limbs are painful, aching. Ameliorated by lying in a curled-up position. Lungs - Frequent, deep inhalation, provoking a slight cough. Frequent, short, persistent coughing. Sputum like eggwhite, foamy, profuse. Pneumonia. Bronchopneumonia.

Skin - First and second degree burns. Erythema. Solar erythema (phlyctena). Scarlet fever-type and anasarca- type eruption with itching and burning. Urticaria eruptions on the feet, hands and face with a bluish complexion. Edema. Seborrheic alopecia. Anthrax.

Modalities - Better lying in a curled-up position. Worse from movement.

Kidneys - Urine red, frothy, blood-streaked. Pain and burning in the urethra. Tenesmus of the bladder. Slow difficult, painful urination, as a result of prostatic congestion.

Temperature - Congestive fever, high, steady, even after appearance of eruption.

PHARMACY - holly-b. Holly. Ilex aquifolium. Flowering twigs are boiled for half an hour, the water strained and used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.

HOMEOPATHIC - The remedy Holly-b. belongs to the group of Oversensitivity to Influences and Ideas, as classified by Bach. Additional remedies in this group are Agri- b.. Cent-b. and Waln-b., all helping those suffering from vulnerability to disturbances from outside. The Holly-b. state can be a state of exhaustion, frazzled nerves and over stimulation by environmental impact. Urge to “fight” oneself free of excessive noise and turmoil. Internal suffering and agony, stifled feeling. Nervousness, physical irritability. Tension headaches or migraines after annoying experiences. Suppressed anger. Psychosomatic illness (Will-b.). Antisocial personality disorders (Ch-bd-b., Vine-b.). Disorders with aggressive or jealous features. Prone to outbursts of anger, rage or violence which can also lead to injuries for oneself and others. Impulse control, when rage isnot bridled (Ch-p-b., Imp-b., Verv-b.). Persecutory or paranoid delusions, heightened accusation and antagonism against the imagined threat of others (Beech-b, Will-b.). MIND - Over sensitivity to minor occurrences. Irritable, easily annoyed. Prone to vexation. Strong emotions. Agitated, aggressive state. Overly suspicious, envious, jealous. Revengeful, angry, wounded pride. Perceives disturbances or other people as threats to peace and well-being. Urge to be free of the annoyance. even to the point of violence. REFERENCES - Bach.

full:
PHARMACY - horn. Homarus gammarus. Lobster digestive fluid. N. O. Crustacea. Triturations of sugar of milk saturated with the digesting fluid of the lobster, a thick, reddish offensive liquid contained in a sac situated at the back of the mouth. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, sixth potency.

CLINICAL - Back, pains. Bones, pains. Coryza. Diaphragm, pain. Dyspepsia. Eyes, disorders. Flatulence. Granular, throat. Headaches. Liver, pains. Edema. Paralysis, nervous. Pruritus. Sleep, disordered. Spleen, pains. Throat, sore. Wrist, pain.

HOMEOPATHIC - A. M. Cushing studied the affect of lobster poison, noting the specific affect eating lobster has shown on specific occasions. Noting that persons have been known to die after eating lobster and then drinking milk, Cushing put a little of the poison into warm milk. In ten minutes it was a hard mass. Cushing found that milk aggravated his symptoms during the proving. “Worse from milk.” Other prominent symptoms from his proving included a severe sore throat, dry, inflamed throat with large, granulated blood vessels. Throat burns with tough mucus. Headaches, chiefly frontal and temporal pain, with soreness in eyes. Pain in stomach and abdomen, better after eating. Deranged digestion. Belching. Disturbed sleep, waking at night with flatulence. Chilliness. Itching of the skin. Sharp and sudden pains, all day and after retiring. Back pains. Strange, dull feeling all over, not dizzy. Sick feeling, unable to move, but better moving. Nervous feeling, restlessness, but dread of moving. Sexual excitement. MIND - Frightened feeling. Dullness of mind. Nervous, but with dread of moving.

Head - Headache in morning, sharp at times, mostly in temporal region, worse left. Dizziness.

Eyes - Aching, smarting in eyes. Aching pain in left ball. Profuse lachrymation. Lids stuck together in the morning. Edema of lids.

Ears - Frequent stabbing through lower lobe of left ear, had to pinch it.

Nose - Stinging and burning in nasal passages extending to throat after rising. Sensation of mucus in left nostril. Nose stopped in morning. Discharge from the nose, watery from left nostril. Sneezing often.

Mouth - Profuse salivation.

Throat - Pain near left ear, sharp, sudden, transient. Burning in throat, right side and in esophagus, stomach and bowels. Edema of throat, can hardly breathe. COMMENTS - During the proving, Cushing noted that he “Felt as though could not move, on moving no pain, felt better by moving.” On this indication with others, he cured a case with Hom. 4x. The patient had headache, sore throat, loss of appetite and when she awoke in the morning felt as if she could not move at all. On receiving Hom., there was a speedy restoration of keen appetite, both for food and work and loss of headache and sore throat. Another cured case had “No appetite, distress in stomach, restless sleep, very tired in morning.” A case of frequent “bilious spells” was also cured in a man who had Nux-v. and Dios, with only temporary relief. L. H. Hallock related a personal experience in which, an hour after eating a small amount of lobster salad, general pruritus commenced, worse in lower limbs, especially the calves. The itching was of a biting, burning character, not better by rubbing or scratching, almost unendurable. It lasted two hours in spite of bathing with hot and cold water, fresh and salt. No sooner had the itching abated than his lips, nose, eyes began to swell, until the eyes were closed and lips almost completely inverted. Throat swollen and edematous so that it was almost impossible to breathe, profuse salivation. Eight hours after the meal he had the appearance of a severe and protracted debauch. In twenty-four hours was as well as ever. Once subsequently he had a similar experience after eating lobster. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sep., Murx., Aster., Astac. (2) in cold damp feet, Calc. (3) Lach. - worse after sleep. (4) Hydr., Phyt., Pic- ac. (5) Worse from milk. Calc., Chin., Con., Nit-ac.. Sulph., Mag-c., Aeth. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Belching tasteless wind in the morning. Pain in morning with occasional hot flashes. Sharp pain after a light breakfast. Burning in stomach.

Abdomen - Pain in diaphragm and hypochondria. Pain in liver and spleen.

Rectum - Frequent inclination to stool during the day. Alternate diarrhea and constipation, changing every three or four days. Large, long tenacious stool after much effort.

Male - Long-continued excitement every morning and in night.

Chest - Sharp pain in back side of left lung. Burning distress at right of lower end of sternum in both sides, with difficult breathing.

Back - Aching just below diaphragm in center of right scapula, in morning, inside of scapula, worse right. Sharp pain at superior spinous process of left ilium. Sharp pain, transient, sudden in right side near kidney, forcing him to sit down. Causations - Milk.

Limbs - Grinding pain just above elbows. Pain in left wrist in afternoon. Pain in right thigh and leg. Knees weak and trembling, worse right, worse afternoon. Lame pain in right knee. Left foot lame through toe joints at times.

Sleep - Restless at night. Sleepless. Woke early and could not go to sleep on account of pains all over, worse epigastric region, back, arms and legs.

Skin - Sore pimple on left thigh, outside. Itching in various parts, frequently, day and night, before and after retiring, better scratching, but appearing in anotherplace. Itching sudden, worse night, in limbs, frequent sudden darting, on various parts, worse legs.

Modalities - Better from motion. Better inhaling cold air. Better eating. Better passing wind. Weakness worse walking. Worse from drinking milk. Worse after sleep. Worse at night. Worse on drawing a long breath.

Liver - Pain in lower part of liver. Sharp pain in region of left lobe of liver, worse drawing a long breath. Lungs - Intense edema of throat rendering breathing almost impossible. Difficult breathing after retiring.

Pulse - Pulse full, rolling.

Temperature - Chilliness all over with trembling. Feet cold and damp, afterwards burning.

full:
PHARMACY - home. Hornería collina. Cape tulip. N. O. Iridaceae. Tincture of bulbs. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Collapse. Constipation. Nausea. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hornería is a violent narcotic-acrid poison very like Colchicum in its effects. Collapse, almost insensible, cold limbs. Severe nausea and vomiting. Obstinate constipation. Pulse is irregular and the pupils are dilated. In one case of toxic poisoning, a Malay woman with her three grandchildren, ages 12, 8 and 6, ate a small basinful of the bulbs with their supper (between 7 p.m. and 8 p.m.). About 1 a.m. the woman woke with severe nausea and vomiting and found the children similarly affected. She tried to call for help, but found herself too weak to leave her bed and when, by five o'clock, assistance arrived the eldest girl was found moribund and expired almost immediately. The boy of 8 died an hour later. The youngest child was found in collapse, almost insensible, cold limbs, pulse scarcely 50 and irregular, pupils much dilated. The grandmother's symptoms were similar, but lesser in degree, accompanied by constant efforts at vomiting. By using stimulants she and the child eventually recovered. REFERENCES -. Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - hura. Hurabrasiliensis. Assaku. N. O. Euphorbiacae. Tincture of milky juice. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Blindness. Hysteria. Leucorrhea. Leprosy. Sinuses disorders. Skin disorders. Spine, pains.

HOMEOPATHIC - The milky juice called Assaku by the Brazilians of Hura is as powerful as that of the better- known Euphorbians. Hura, has been used in leprosy when the skin feels as if it were hide bound. Two of the pro vers had been affected with leprosy, but under homeopathic treatment they seemed to have recovered. During the proving, one of them had symptoms of compression of the spinal marrow with very great suffering. Skin of forehead feels drawn tight. Tense vesicles. Stiff neck, pain in back. Throbbing in fingertips. Sensation of splinter under thumbnails. Itching, pimples on all projecting portions of bone, malar bones, etc. MIND - Excited and oppressed as if by some misfortune. Causeless weeping followed by laughter. Laughing followed by chilliness. Laughing from every paroxysm of pain. Flow of sad thoughts. Imagines she will lose some one dear to her. Thinks he is about to lose a friend. Exaggerated conscientiousness. Irritable. Indisposed to work. Fear of fever on going to bed. Weeping when singing. Biting hands, himself. Desire to break things. Forsaken feeling, Sensation ofisolation. Impatience from pain. Mistakes in localities. Mistakes in time. Reproaches himself. Weeping in open air. Delusions that she is alone in the world. Delusions that he is despised. Delusions has lost the affection of friends. Delusions his friends have lost all confidence in him. Delusions floating in air. Delusions that he is unfortunate. Delusions on falling asleep. Abdomen - Frightful colic with diarrhea and shivering. Throbbing in left side of abdomen. Twisting pain in left side with very painful, shooting, extorting cries. Stitch in ileo-cecal region, worse on movement.

Head - Rush of blood to the head. Heaviness, numbness of the head. Painful lancinations through head. Constriction in back of head. Skin of forehead feels drawn tight.

Eyes - Prickling and burning in eyes, sensation as if sand in them. Eyelids red. Vision dim. Blindness. Sparks and zigzags before the sight when walking.

Ears - Pain behind and in right ear. Stoppage in ears. Loud whizzing and whistling sound in ears.

Nose - Redness of (left) wing of nose. Constriction, throbbing at root of nose. Coryza, nosebleed. Sense of smell very acute.

Face - Face weary-looking as after a debauch, rings around eyes. Face dull and dark-looking with paleness mottled with red. Face scarlet and bloated. Heat rising to face. Swellings on upper part of right cheek. Lips red. Small pimples inside lower lip.

Mouth - Tongue white, pain at tip. Fleshy excrescence on inside of lips. Clammy mouth, foul smell. Taste of copper, blood, clammy, smoky.

Throat - Irritation of throat with dryness. Spitting of blood in morning. Vertigo - Confusion. Dizziness. COMMENTS - Mure's provings were made with single doses of the 5c potency. All the provers had symptoms of nervous excitement, twitching and irritability. The gastrointestinal irritation of the other Euphorbians was marked. Farrington noted that the vesicles are so tense that when pricked they eject their contents. Sensation of a splinter under thumbnails. Eruptions tend to occur on the skin covering projecting portions of bone or the malar bones. He compared it with Canth. A case of leprosy was reported cured with Assaku, which led to its extensive use in this disease, though Mure noted it had not cured any others. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Op. Compare: (1 )Crot-t., Ric., Euphor., Hura-c. (3) Calo. - Leprosy, livid and gangrenous tubercles, thickening of the skin. (3) Urin. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Great hunger with pain in stomach, satisfied immediately on eating. Qualmishness. Stomachache, as from hunger.

Rectum - Constriction at anus. Frequent, ineffectual urging to stool. Diarrhea succeeded by great weakness of chest. Stools are liquid, painless, flowing constantly, offensive containing thread-worms. Constipation, hard, difficult stools.

Male - Intolerable erections. Amorous dreams with erections, lemon-colored semen. Weight in testicles when walking.

Female - Pain in uterus as if compressed, as if a sharp instrument were thrust into it, followed by lancinations in vagina. Menses scanty, eight days too early, profuse with leucorrhea. Food - Hunger, sometimes immediately after a meal.

Chest - Lancinations in chest preventing deep breathing. Throbbings in chest. Nervous shivering all over chest. Suffocative sensation, especially when thinking of anything that has gone wrong.

Heart - Constant pain at heart, sometimes very sharp, arresting breathing.

Back - Stiff-neck, right side, least motion is painfully felt in nape. Dislocated and tearing pain in dorsal region, on sitting down. Severe pains in lumber region, weakness. Excruciating pain in lumbo-sacral region, when trying to lift a weight. Breasts - Sensation of small ball under right breast. Sharp pain shifting from shoulderto left breast. Stitches, throbbing in breasts.

Limbs - Weariness of limbs. Lancinations, throbbing, rheumatic pains, numbness in upper and lower limbs. Dislocated pains in joints. Throbbing in fingertips. Heat in nails, sensation as if part of nail had been torn off. Pain as from splinter under thumbnail. Lungs - Feeling of suffocation. Sighs and yawns much. Dryness of glottis causing cough. Considerable yellow, thick, frothy sputa. Expectoration rusty-colored, foul, bloody, like milk-chocolate.

Sleep - Yawning and drowsiness. Nightly restlessness. Dreams of traveling, swimming, yellow water, corpses, or assassins.

Skin - Large pimples, itching, painful to touch on face. Cluster of pimples or vesicles on various parts. Red vesicular pimples, the vesicles break on pressure and water squirts out with great force. Small vesicular pimples with itching. Itching on forehead, eyelids, chin, beard, back, legs, sleep disturbed by it.

Teeth - Lancinations in teeth and gums, passing to ear. Pimples on gums.

Kidneys - Acute pain in right kidney while walking, with great urging to urinate. Urine light green, clear, deposits a white sediment.

Temperature - Feet and body constantly cold and damp. Heat and transient perspiration. Flushes of heat in face. Cold sweat on face and all over body.

PHARMACY - hura-c. Hura crepitans. Monkey's dinner-bell. Sand-box. N. O. Eu- phorbiacae.Tinctureofseeds.//¿vtoncaZrfose: Tincture and all potencies.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany only recognizes one species of Hura, H. crepitans. But Mure compared his Hura with H. crepitans and they are probably varieties of the same species as the properties of the milk are the same. The rounded, hard-shelled fruits are about the size of an orange and have as many deep furrows as there are cells, each cell containing a single flattened seed. When the fruit is ripe and exposed to a dry atmosphere, it bursts with great force, accompanied by a loud, sharp crack like the report of a pistol, for which reason it is often called the Monkey's Dinner-bell.

HOMEOPATHIC - The Hura-c. seeds are emetic, in a green state violently purgative, but when dry, according to Lunan, they lose this property. An oil is extracted from them and sometimes used as a purgative, about twenty drops of it equal in action to a tablespoonful of castor oil. A venomous milky juice is abundant in all parts of the plant and causes almost immediate blindness if applied to the eye. The observed effects of Hura-c. were found from eating the seeds. Burning in throat, vomiting and purging, suffocation, headache, were the main symptoms complained. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph.. Op.

Compare - (1) Hur-br., Ric., Crot-t. (2) Caps. - burning in throat not better by water. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - hydrang. Hydrangea arbore - scens. Seven-barks. N. O. Hydrangeacee or Saxifragaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves and young shoots. Fluid extract. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, catarrh. Bladder, stones. Cystitis. Diabetes. Dizziness. Gravel. Gout. Kidney, colic. Kidney, stones. Nephritis. Prostatic, disorders. Prostate, enlarged. Pyelitis. Rheumatism. Urinary, incontinence.

HERBAL - Like some other members of the Saxifragaceae, Hydrangea has a traditional reputation as a “stone-breaking ” remedy as it was used in calculous diseases for many years. Hansen noted that Hydrang. arrested the tendency to formation of calculus in the bladder and relieved distress from renal calculus, with soreness over the region of the kidneys and bloody urine.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hydrang. is a remedy for gravel, profuse deposit of white amorphous salts in urine. Kidney stones, kidney colic, bloody urine. It appears to act strongly on the neck of the bladder and on the ureters. Gout and rheumatism. Oppression of the chest. Pain in lumbar region. Dizziness. Mind - Nervous and worried. Violent attacks of anger. Outbursts of anger due to pains.

Abdomen - Colic. Abdominal symptoms and enlarged prostate .Sharp pain in loins, especially left side.

Urine - Profuse deposit of white amorphous salts. Gravel deposits. Yellow sand. Bloody urine. Heavy deposit of mucus. COMMENTS - Dr. Nottingham of Lansing said that in physiological doses it produces giddiness, oppression of the chest and acts as a cathartic, diuretic, sialogogue and narcotic. Nottingham used it with brilliant results in the case of Mr. B., 71, tall, slender, dark. He was exceedingly irritable and frequently subject to violent paroxysms of anger. For many years he had been accustomed to make the most reckless use of drugs and was always requesting his homeopathic doctor to give him “something stronger. ” For eight years he had suffered from bladder sphincter irritation with dribbling of urine, severe spasms of prostate, kidney catarrh, yellow sand in urine and even small stones. After persistent use of the best indicated remedies with no effect, the fluid extract of Hydrangea was given, a teaspoonful every three or four hours. The symptoms disappeared in a very short time. Cooper has also used this remedy (which, he says is the thirstiest plant known) with good effect in diabetes in cases presenting great thirst with abdominal symptoms and in enlarged prostate. Hansen added that it is particularly useful for profuse deposits of white amorphous salts in the urine. Hydrang. has arrested the tendency to formation of stones, relieves distress from kidney stones with soreness over region of kidneys and bloody urine. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lyc., Chim., Berb., Pareir., Uva., Sabal., Oxyd., (2) Geum. (3) Polytr. - according to Dr. Cushing in tincture or infusion for enlarged prostate or prostatitis. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Male - Prostate hypertrophy. Enlarged prostate (Ferr-pic., Sabal.).

Kidneys - Pyelitis. Nephritis. Calculus in the ureter with prostate enlargement. Kidney stones, kidney colic. Sore kidneys. Pain in left kidney, ureter. Radiating pains (Berb.).

Bladder - Bladder catarrh, stones. Urinary incontinence. Frequent urination. Spasmodic stricture. Cystitis. Burning in urethra and frequent desire, but hard to start. Stitching pain during urination. Food - Great thirst with abdominal symptoms.

HOMEOPATHIC - The alkaloids of Hydrastis have been largely used in the allopathic school for internal hemorrhage. Hydr-m. was found to be inconvenient by reason of its irritant properties. Its use in fibroid tumors was advocated by Dr. Burford and others in the homeopathic school. Locally used in aphthous sore mouth, ulcers, ulcerated sore throat, ozaena, etc. Hydr-m. is a uterine hemostatic and also a vaso-constrictor. Hemorrhages in dilatation of the stomach and chronic digestive disorders. Metrorrhagia, especially from fibroid tumors. COMMENTS - A case of central uterine fibroid tumor, about the size of a large orange, and pressing on the bladder, causing bladder symptoms, was quickly reduced in size with the disappearance of all symptoms by Hydr-m. 3x. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
