full:
PHARMACY - kali-m. Kali muriaticum. Potassium chloride. Kali chloratum. Not to be confounded with Chlorate of potash. Kali chloricum. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Allergies. Aphthae. Breasts, cysts. Bubo. Bunion. Bums. Cataract. Chilblains. Colds. Constipation. Coryza. Croup. Cystitis. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dropsy. Dysentery. Ear, disorders. Eczema. Embolisms. Eustachian, congestion. Eye, disorders. Glands, swollen. Hay ieser. Hemorrhoids. Hodgkin's disease. Ingrown, toenails. Jaundice. Joints, stiff. Leucorrhea. Measles. Morning, sickness. Mumps. Nasal, congestion. Rheumatism. Scorbutus. Shingles. Sinusitis. Smallpox. Sycosis. Tendons, creaking. Thread- worms. Vaccination, effects. Warts.

HOMEOPATHIC - Schiissler introduced Kali-m. into homeopathy. His account of it is “it is contained in nearly all the cells and is chemically related to fibrin. It will dissolve white or grayish-white secretions of the mucus membrane and plastic exudations.” When the cells of the epidermis lose molecules of Kali-m. due to a morbid irritation, the fibrin comes to the surface as a white or whitish-gray mass. When dried, this forms a mealy covering. If the irritation affects the tissues under the epidermis, then fibrin and serum are exuded, causing the affected spot on the epidermis to rise in blisters. Similar processes may take place in and below epithelial cells. Useful in catarrhal disorders in the subacute inflammatory states, fibrinous exudations and glandular swellings. Whiteness of secretions, exudations, eruptions of tissues. Tough, fibrinous exudations and discharges. Milky white, viscid, sticky, thick, slimy or lumpy discharges. White or gray coating of base of tongue and expectoration of thick, white phlegm. Blood clots too readily. Embolism, indurations, hard swellings. Hard deposits, glandular swelling. Sore, cutting or sticking, shifting pains. Bursitis, patellar. Crawling and numbness. Crosswise symptoms. Slow reaction. Stubborn infiltration. MIND - Discontent, discouraged. Sadness alternating with cheerfulness. Fears evil. Sits in silence. Imagines he must starve. Irritable and angry, at trifles.

Head - Confusion in head, also in occiput, with peculiar sensation in cervical muscles. Sick headache with white-coated tongue. Headache with vomiting of white phlegm. Sinus headache with thick white discharge. Headache with sneezing and coryza. Catarrh of frontal sinuses. Aching pain in temple. Stunning shock in or a leaden load holds down occiput, better letting hair down and warmth. Brain feels loose. Meningitis. Crusta lactea. Copious white dandruff. Perspiration on head.

Eyes - Trachoma. Cataract. Corneal opacities, pustules. Exudation in retina. Scintillations on coughing. White mucus, purulent scabs. Superficial ulcer. Congestion to eyes, irritated. Redness with some pain. Sensation of sand in eye. Edges of eyelids scabby. Yellow crusts of pus on edges.

Ears - Otitis media. Swimmer's ear infection. Earache with swelling of glands. Eustachian tube blocked. Soreness of Eustachian tube. Glue ear. Great effusion about the auricle. Catarrhal conditions of the middle ear. Deafness from catarrhal condition and occlusion of Eustachian tubes. Deafness from swelling of internal ear. Sensation of a plug in ears. Snapping. popping noises in ear. Crackling noises on blowing nose or swallowing. Swollen glands about the ear. Threatened mastoiditis.

Nose - Nasal catarrh. Stuffy cold in head. Hawking of mucus from posterior si- nuses. Phlegm or catarrh, white and thick discharges. Vault of pharynx covered with adherent crust. Nosebleeds (Arn., Phos.).

Face - Bluish, sunken. Cheeks swollen and painful. Lips hot, swollen. Chapped lips from cold. Eruptions around mouth. Pimples on forehead, face, lips and chin. Barber's itch. Swollen glands about jaw and neck. Face aches with swelling of gums or cheek. Mumps without fever. Paralysis, following pain in face. Paralysis of right facial nerve. Muscles of face twitch and tremble, worse eating, speaking or coughing. Lightning-like attacks of pain in face.

Mouth - Aphthae. Thrush, white ulcers in the mouth. Eruptions around the mouth. Breath excessively fetid, in ulceration and diphtheria. Profuse and acid saliva. Accumulation of mucus. Salty, bitter taste, with coldness of tongue. Heat and dryness in mouth. Swollen glands about jaw and neck. Scorbutic gums. Gumboil before matter forms. Toothache with swelling of the gums and cheeks.

Throat - Chronic sore throat. “Hospital” sore throat. Croup, membranous exudation. Loss of voice, hoarseness. Follicular tonsillitis. Tonsils swollen, inflamed, swallowing excessively painful. Tonsils enlarged, can hardly breathe. Grayish- white, ulcerated throat. Adherent crusts in vault of pharynx. Pharynx feels cold. Eustachian catarrh. Hawks out thick, white mucus, cheesy.

Stomach - Dyspepsia and indigestion, with a whitish-gray tongue. Cutting pain in stomach. Eructations alternating with pains in chest and abdomen. Empty, sour eructations. Empty feeling in stomach. Pain in the stomach with constipation. Bulimia, hunger disappears by drinking water. Sick feeling after taking fat. Fatty or rich food causes indigestion. Morning sickness with vomiting of white phlegm. Nausea with eructations. Nausea with shivers. Stomach heavy, at night. Vomits food. Vomiting of white, opaque mucus, blood. Stools - Pale, light-colored, hard or flocculent stools. Stools clay-colored, white, or slimy. Painful stools, passing nothing but mucus. Bloody stools, or bloody mucus. Stools so dry it almost crumbles.

Abdomen - Abdominal tenderness and swelling, fullness after eating. Flatulence. Tensive pressure in region of liver, better emission of flatus. Pressing pain in region of spleen. Colic with shifting of flatulence. Colic with diarrhea. Colic in pelvic region. Catarrh of duodenum from chill. Peritonitis. Suppurating buboes.

Rectum - Constipation, light-colored stools. Diarrhea after fatty food. Dysentery, purging with slimy stools. Hemorrhoids, bleeding, blood dark and thick, fibrinous, clotted. Anus sore, worse walking or after stools. Itching or crawling in anus after stools. Threadworms, causing itching at anus.

Male - Chronic syphilis. Gonorrhea. Gleet combined with eczema, visible or latent. Soft swelling of buboes, soft chancre. Condylomata. Hydrocele. Itching of scrotum. Orchitis from suppressed gonorrhea. Violent emissions with voluptuous dreams. Violent erections with emissions. Sexual desire diminished, with chilliness and apathy.

Female - Menses too late or suppressed, checked or too early. Excessive discharge, dark, clotted or tough. Menses black blood like tar (Plat.). Leucorrhea, discharge of milky-white mucus, thick, non-irritating, bland. Morning sickness with vomiting of white phlegm. Threatened miscarriage. Food - Habitual loss of appetite or refuses food. Fatty or rich food causes indigestion. Worse cold drinks.

Chest - Rawness in chest. Flushes of heat in chest. Constriction of chest as from vapors of sulphur. Oppression of chest with violent palpitations.

Heart - Heart disease causing dropsy. Coldness in region of heart. Pericarditis. Palpitations from excessive flow of blood to heart. Pulse accelerated, or soft and sluggish. Pulse not synchronous with beats of heart.

Back - Heaviness under right shoulder. Buzzing under right scapula. Lightning pains from small of back to feet. Backache better lying down. Must get out of bed and sit up.

Limbs - Rheumatic fever. Swelling around joints. Exudation and swelling around the joints. Rheumatic pains felt only during motion or increased by it. Nightly rheumatic pains, worse from warmth of bed. Lightning-like pains from small of back to feet, must get out of bed and sit up. Cramps in limbs. Twitching thighs. Tension in leg alternating with tension in arm. Cutting in bones. Bursitis. Cold foot sweat. Cold hands and feet. Chilblains on hands or feet or any part. Cracking of tendons in the back of the hand. Hands get stiff while writing or knitting.

Sleep - Restless sleep, startled at least noise. Anxious dreams, towards morning. Somnolence.

Skin - Chickenpox. Smallpox. Blisters arising from burns. Acne. Pimples on face, neck, etc. Erythema. Herpes zoster. Vesicular erysipelas and shingles. Eczema from suppressed or deranged uterine functions. Vesicles containing thick, white contents. Itching of whole body, in bed. Dry, flourlike scales on the skin (Ars.). Greenish, brownish, yellow crusts. Branny. Proud flesh. Carbuncles. Condylomata. Warty excrescences. Eruptions connected with stomach or menstrual disorders.

Modalities - Better from cold drinks, rubbing, letting hair down. Worse from open air, drafts, dampness, night. Worse cold drinks, fatty, rich food or pastry. Worse motion, sprains, lying, during menses. Rheumatic symptoms worse from warmth of bed.

Tongue - Grayish-white, sticky, thick, slimy, or dry coating on tongue. Tongue mapped, gray dr white at base. Tongue white, or only in middle. Coating of tongue after diarrhea. Coldness of tongue. Sensation as if a tumor were growing on the tongue. Glossitis. Burning, stinging blisters on tongue. Vertigo - Vertigo after violent exercise. Vertigo with congestion to head. Vertigo during headache. Vision - Scintillations on coughing or sneezing. Smoky and misty vision. Letters appear smaller when reading. COMMENTS - Chronic catarrhal condition of the middle ear. Eustachian tube catarrh (Merc-d.). Closed Eustachian tubes. Pain in ears during pressure changes. Snapping and noises in the ear. Common cold with yellow or watery mucus. A milky, white, thick discharge, can be lumpy or stringy. Grayish white, dry or slimy tongue. Bleeding hemorrhoids, dark, fibrous, clotted blood. Diphtheria. Rheumatic fever with exudation and swelling around the joints. Better from cold drinks. It is said to have cured cataracts after Calcfl. helped. Clarke cured with it rheumatism affecting mostly the left shoulder and the elbow, worse in the morning on rising. There is some clinical evidence of helping breast cysts. Boericke and Dewey noted the “protruded appearance of eyes, white tongue, croupy, hard cough, harsh barking.” Hering added “cough, noisy with protruded appearance of eyes.” In one case, it caused a severe aggravation in which the patient felt “as if eyes would be forced out of head with cough.” Similar to Kali-chl, which has the keynote symptom “tendency to rush of blood to both eyes and light before both eyes on coughing and sneezing.” RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Bell., Calc-s., Hydr. .Puls. Compare: ( 1 ) Bell., which Kali-m. follows well in the catarrhal and hypertrophic conditions. (2) Kino - otorrhea with stitches in right ear. (3) Bry., Merc., Puls., Sulph. (4) Kali-chl. in tough secretions, Kali-bi., Kali-c., Hydr. (5) in rheumatic affections, Bry., Rhus-t., Sulph. (6) Merc-d. in the Eustachian tube and in inflammations of ear. (7) Graph., Nat-m., Nit-ac., Sil., Apis, Thuj. (8) Puls, in worse from fatty food, worse from warmth. It follows well: Calc-p. Calc-fl., Ferr-p. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Liver - Liver disease with dropsy. Jaundice, caused by a chill, resulting in catarrh of duodenum. Sluggish action or complete torpidity of liver. Pain in right side. Lungs - Difficult or oppressed breathing. ■ Asthma with gastric derangements, mucus white and hard to cough up. Rattling sounds of air passing through thick, tenacious mucus in the bronchi, difficult to cough up. Catarrhal pneumonia. Bronchitis. Croupy inflammation of lungs. Mucus white, thick and hard to cough up. Yellowish green mucus. Expectoration sticky, milky or flies from the mouth. Hemorrhage from lungs.

Kidneys - Kidney disease with dropsy. Catarrhal nephritis. Dribbling urine. Discharge white thick mucus. Turbid urine, with dirty yellow sediment. Diabetes. Albuminuria during pregnancy.

Bladder - Cystitis. Inflammation of bladder with violent fever. Acute cases of inflammation of bladder, when swelling has set in and discharge is thick, white mucus. Acute and chronic catarrh of bladder. Dribbling urination. Discharge of white, thick mucus. Itching in urethra. Breasts - Breasts cysts. Soft, tender nodes or growths in breasts. Painful breasts before or at menses. Causations - Ill effects of vaccination, sprains, burns, blows, cuts.

Cough - Loud, noisy stomach cough. Cough short, acute, and spasmodic. Whooping cough. Sputum thick and white. Violent cough during coryza.

Perspiration - Sweating of head.

Temperature - Shivering all over, or over back and neck, with warm feet. Continual chilliness with stiffness of hands, with vomiting of white (not transparent) mucus, in open air.

name: Kali Nitricum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better lying down, lying on right side, uncovering head, gentle motion, drinking water in sips. Worse cold, damp, taking cold, morning, afternoon. Worse lying with head low, walking, breathing, eating veal, coffee, wine, beer..
constitution: Asthma. Bedwetting. Chest, pain. Colic. Debility. Diabetes, insipidus. Dropsy. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Gastritis. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hemorrhages. Herpes. Meniere's disease. Menorrhagia. Nephritis. Nosebleeds. Peritonitis. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Polyps. Rheumatism. Tuberculosis. Vertigo.
keynote:
PHARMACY - kali-n. Kali nitricum. Potassium nitrate. Saltpetre. Nitre. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Bedwetting. Chest, pain. Colic. Debility. Diabetes, insipidus. Dropsy. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Gastritis. Headaches.…
full:
PHARMACY - kali-n. Kali nitricum. Potassium nitrate. Saltpetre. Nitre. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Bedwetting. Chest, pain. Colic. Debility. Diabetes, insipidus. Dropsy. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Gastritis. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hemorrhages. Herpes. Meniere's disease. Menorrhagia. Nephritis. Nosebleeds. Peritonitis. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Polyps. Rheumatism. Tuberculosis. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - The Saltpetre of the Alchemists, Kali-n. is known in old-school practice principally as a “refrigerant diuretic” and as the active agent in the well known “nitre papers,” which are burnt, producing fumes to allay attacks of asthma. A solution of saltpetre as an application was an old remedy for inveterate mange in cats. Nitre with sulphur and charcoal forms gunpowder. A teaspoonful of this in hot water was a favorite remedy for gonorrhea among soldiers in the days when black powder was used. Affects the respiratory organs, kidneys, heart and blood vessels. Secretions are increased into cavities. Sudden dropsical swellings over the whole body. Pains are dull stitching, throbbing. Wooden, numbness. Very weak. Asthma and cardiac asthma. Relapsing tuberculosis. Hemorrhagic tendency. Rheumatism. Gastro-intestinal inflammation with much debility and relapse in tuberculosis. Suppurative nephritis. Incontinence of urine in children. MIND - Peevish, fretful. Bored. Mental weariness from lack of occupation or interest. Discouragement. Sadness when alone. Aversion to thinking in morning. Fear of death. Anxiety and congestion to chest. Anxiety during headache.

Head - Headache with vertigo, as if falling to right side and backwards, worse stooping. Head pain, better motion of carriage. Pains in occiput, better letting hair down. Scalp very sensitive.

Eyes - Burning in eyes, with lachrymation and photophobia. External angle of right eye twitches, worse chewing. Vision becomes clouded. Turbid corpus vitreum (Arn., Ham., Phos.). Transient blindness. Colored circles before eyes. In evening, candles appear surrounded by a rainbowlike halo.

Ears - Shooting in ears. Inflammation and swelling of lobe of right ear. Chronic deafness from paralysis of auditory nerve. Vertigo and tinnitus. Tinkling and ringing in ears.

Nose - Violent coryza with obstruction of nose, and loss of smell. Sneezing. Swollen feeling, worse in the right nostril. Burning in nose with digging and clawing pain. The nasal bones are painful, especially to the touch. Swelling of interior of nose. Ulcers in the nostrils covered by a scurf. Nosebleed with acrid blood. Polyps (Thuj., Sang-n.). Point red and itching.

Mouth - Tongue loaded with a white coating. Tongue red with burning pimples. Burning blister at tip of tongue. Crawling on tongue. Taste disagreeable, nauseous, disgusting, sour. Fetid breath. Throat constricted and sore.

Throat - Laryngeal diphtheria. Sore throat with shooting pain. Nocturnal pain in throat, as if it were contracting. Impeded swallowing from tension and cutting in the larynx. Hoarseness. Loss of speech. Vertigo - Fainting fits with vertigo in morning, worse on standing, better sitting down. Vertigo and tinnitus. COMMENTS - Kali-n. has been extensively proved by homeopaths and symptoms have been added from cases of poisoning, so that its characteristics are well defined. It is almost equal to Kali-c. in producing stitching pains and it is similar to it in having a cough at 3 a.m. Severe stitching, cutting, lancinating, tearing and pressing pains. As with many other Kalis, there is external sensitiveness of scalp, of abdomen, of testes. Kali nitricum Diabetes insipidus. Bedwetting. Painful colic. Diarrhea and dysentery. Sexual excitement. Pain in testes and cords. Menorrhagia with flow of ink-like blackness. “The pain-like contraction in the eyes, forehead and face concentrates in the tip of the nose. Swollen feeling in right nostril, which is painful on pressure, sore pain in upper part of right nostril with external sensitiveness,” these two last symptoms led to the cure of large nasal polyps in a girl. In a poisoning case, during the recovery there was intense vertigo with tinnitus, which should indicate Kali-n. in some cases of Meniere's disease. Easy intoxication by wine or beer was noted by several provers. A peculiar symptom is a sour taste in the throat. In the asthmatic state the breathlessness is so great that the patient, though thirsty, can only drink a sip at a time between the breaths. Allen defined the asthma of Kali-n. as asthma with excessive dyspnea, faintness and nausea with dull stitches or with burning pain in chest, rather free expectoration. RELATIONS - Antidotes: Op., Nit-s-d. It antidotes opium or morphine poisoning, 8 to 10 grains to glass of water. Compare: ( 1 ) Cann-s. which contains a large amount of Kali-n. (2) Lyc., Sang., All-s., Ant-i. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Faint-like weakness at stomach pit. Epigastric or sub-sternal pains go towards axilla. Gnawing, spasmodic weakness, and pressure on epigastrium. Burning in stomach. Severe pain after every meal. Nausea, as if about to vomit worse at night. Ineffectual retching. Vomiting of mucus, mixed with blood.

Abdomen - Excessive distention of abdomen. Griping about umbilicus. Stitching and sticking pains. Violent pain in right side after eating veal. Peritonitis. Incarceration of flatus, especially in afternoon and evening. Very loud rumbling in abdomen.

Rectum - Frequent pressing in rectum. Urgent want to evacuate with tenesmus. Dysentery with much cutting pain, great thirst and icy coldness of feet. Diarrhea from eating veal. Membranous shreds with tenesmus. Thin, watery dark, bloody stools. Feces difficult, and retarded, evacuated with much effort. Hard like sheep's dung.

Female - Profuse menses, black like ink. Menses too early, profuse, preceded and with violent backache. Burning pains in the ovarian region only during menses (Zinc, after menses). Leucorrhea. Food - Better hot food. Aversion to beef, eggs, meat, veal. Worse from eating veal, causing headache, diarrhea. Worse from cold food, fats, rich food, milk. Worse from beef, fish, lobster, oysters. Worse from beer, wine, bread, coffee, rice, soup, watery fruits and vegetables.

Chest - Chest feels constricted. Oppression on chest, when ascending. Contractive pain in chest. Sticking in left side near sternum. Inflammation of lungs. Constitutions - Suited to asthmatic constitutions and chest complaints.

Heart - Violent stitch in précordia and beating of heart. Palpitations, worse lying. Pulse is weak, small and thready.

Back - Aching in lumbar region. Pains in back on stooping. Shootings in and between scapula. Pains extend into the chest. Shooting pains in sacral region. Violent pains in loins on waking. Feeling in back as if kidneys engorged.

Limbs - Drawing in limbs with paralytic weakness. Rheumatic pains and stitches in limbs and joints. Stitches between shoulder blades. Tearing and sticking in shoulders and joints. Hands and fingers seem swollen. Lungs - Rapid gasping breathing, sits upright. Congestion of right lung. Dyspnea so great that breath cannot be held long enough to drink, though thirsty. Asthma with excessive dyspnea, nausea, dull stitches and burning in chest. Spasmodic croup, paroxysm of crowing. Bronchitis with sharp, short, dry, hacking cough. Acute exacerbations in tuberculosis. Dry, morning cough with pain in the chest and bloody expectoration. Sour- smelling expectoration. Expectoration of clotted blood after hawking mucus.

Sleep - Drowsiness during day. Disturbed sleep at night, constant dreaming, with frequent awakening. Anxious and uneasy dreams about dangerous situations. Nightmare. Coma.

Skin - Lancinations in skin. Pricking like needles, followed by burning. Tubercles, size of a pea. Burning vesicles filled with yellowish serum, which break when scratched. Sudden dropsical swelling.

Modalities - Better lying down, lying on right side, uncovering head, gentle motion, drinking water in sips. Worse cold, damp, taking cold, morning, afternoon. Worse lying with head low, walking, breathing, eating veal, coffee, wine, beer.

Teeth - Toothache, with sharp drawing, or tearing pains in teeth and head. Shooting in carious teeth, when touched. Pulsative toothache, at night, worse by cold things. Swelling of gums, of an inflammatory or scorbutic character, they bleed readily.

Kidneys - Diabetes insipidus. Dull kidney pains. Burning in urethra while urinating and greatly diminished urine. Frequentand profuse emission of clear urine.

Perspiration - Profuse perspiration every alternate night (Nit-ac.).

Temperature - External coldness, chin, skin. Extraordinary shiverings not better by hot drinks or coverings. Coldness in afternoon with thirst, or coldness, preceded by headache. Quotidian fever, with drawing pains in limbs. Profuse and colliquative sweat. Sweat in morning, especially on chest. Internal burning.

name: Kali Oxalicum
author: Murphy
constitution: Convulsions. Cramps. Eyes inflamed. Lumbago. Vomiting.
keynote:
PHARMACY - kali-ox. Kali oxalicum. Potassium bioxalate. Kali oxalas. Salts of sorrel. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Convulsions. Cramps. Eyes inflamed. Lumbago. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Only cases of poisoning have been observed with this…
full:
PHARMACY - kali-ox. Kali oxalicum. Potassium bioxalate. Kali oxalas. Salts of sorrel. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Convulsions. Cramps. Eyes inflamed. Lumbago. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Only cases of poisoning have been observed with this salt. The main symptoms of Kali-ox. are those of violent irritation. Convulsions. Violent and continuous vomiting. Throbbing in the head with great thirst. Cramps. Severe pains in the back (Ox-ac., Rumx-a.). Coldness and collapse. One patient became insane. MIND - Extreme depression. Insanity.

Head - Swimming in head, heaviness, throbbing pain and great thirst.

Eyes - Great soreness of eyes with dim vision. Conjunctive injected, pupils dilated.

Face - Countenance flushed. Face pale, anxious-looking and covered with a cold sweat. Face and lips pale with continual riggers over whole body. Food - Great thirst and throbbing pain in head.

Mouth - Tongue and fauces red and irritable. Very strong acid taste of poison lasting two days.

Throat - Scalding sensation in throat and stomach. REFERENCES-Clarke.

Stomach - Vomiting and faintness. Vomiting, continuing at intervals of ten minutes to an hour for nearly a week. Very severe burning pain in stomach and bowels. Excruciating pain, followed by violent convulsions and death.

Abdomen - Violent pains in abdomen and convulsions. Scalding sensation extended over abdomen with tenderness on tolerably firm pressure.

Back - Pain in back. Severe lumbar pain.

Limbs - Spasmodic contractions in hands. Great weakness in lower limbs. Cramps in legs. Muscular weakness. Falls and utters loud cries. Tendency to faint. Lying on the floor quite faint. Nails and fingers blue.

Skin - Cold and clammy.

Kidneys - Urination accompanied by a sensation of scalding.

Bladder - Urination accompanied by a sensation of scalding.

Temperature - Sensations of coldness, succeeded by burning heat in chest and stomach and general muscular weakness. Continued rigors affecting whole body.

PHARMACY - kali-perm. Kali permanganicum. Potassium permanganate. Permanganate of potash. Kali manganicum. Kali hypermanganicum. Solution in distilled water. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bites. Cough. Diphtheria. Gastritis. Opium poisoning. Ozaena. Salivation. Snakebites. Throat, sore. Uvula, swollen. Warts.

HOMEOPATHIC - Kali-perm, is a well-known disinfectant and has been chiefly used in medicine as a local application in diphtheria and other conditions where there are fetid discharges. Kali-perm, counteracts the effects of alkaloids of many poisonous plants owing to its oxidizing powers, if given before the alkaloid has been absorbed. A case of opium poisoning is reported in which an ounce of laudanum had been swallowed by mistake. Kali- perm, in dilute solution (2 grains to the pint) was given repeatedly and acted promptly. The next day, only dryness of mouth and throat was felt. Intense irritation of nose, throat and larynx. Kraft, who used it largely in diphtheria, dissolved a few grains in a tumbler of water, sufficient to make it very red. A teaspoonful of this was put into another tumbler of water and a teaspoonful out of the second tumbler was given every hour or two. Various septic conditions, the tissues are infiltrated with tendency to sloughing. Bites of snakes and for other animal poisons (Led.). Dysmenorrhea. Diphtheria, with extreme fetor of the breath and bloody discharges from the nose and intense prostration. Intense irritation of nose, throat and larynx with bloody and bloody discharges and constant inclination and constant flow of ropy mucus from the stomach. The uvula was swollen and red. Back - Muscles of neck feel sore.

Head - Head feels full.

Eyes - Profuse lachrymation.

Ears - Sharp pricking pains extending from throat to left mastoid process, apparently along Eustachian tube.

Nose - Posterior sinuses painful. Nasal discharge smart and irritates. Bloody discharge, nose feels stuffed and full as in catarrh. Profuse bleeding from nose.

Face - Face hot. Food - Appetite lost. Thirst, inability to drink.

Mouth - Fetor of breath. Mouth and lips very dry, lips smart when exposed to cold air. Increased flow of saliva runs constantly out of the mouth. Swollen uvula. Speech painful, difficult, hoarse.

Throat - Constrictive, smarting sensation in throat. Swollen and painful. Larynx feels raw. Everything hawked up streaked with blood. Constant inclination to swallow. COMMENTS - Potassium permanganate is recognized as being the most effective chemical antidote in cases of morphine or opium poisoning, acting directly on the morphine and oxidizing it to less toxic substances. To be effective, the permanganate must come in direct contact with the opium or morphine in the stomach. The treatment is administration of two to five grains of potassium permanganate in dilute aqueous solution as soon as possible after the poison is taken, this amount to be increased if very large doses of the poison have been taken. Washing out the stomach with a quantity of 1 to 500 solution of permanganate is also recommended, using at least a pint of this solution either by a stomach pump or by enforced vomiting. RELATIONS - Kali-perm, antidotes opium. Compare: (1) Other oxidizing salts, especially Kah-bi., also Mang., Caust., Kali-c. (2) in edematous uvula, Mur-ac., Apis. (3) in diphtheria, Diph., Merc-cy., Arum-t., Kali-bi., Kali- m., (4) in thick, ropy mucus, Kali-bi. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Hot, burning pain in stomach. Sickening pain in stomach. Nausea and constant inclination to swallow. Nausea and vomiting.

Rectum - Obstinate constipation.

Chest - Aching in region of cricoid cartilage, worse every attempt to swallow.

Limbs - Legs feel as though he could not move them, tremble on attempting to stand. Lungs - Short, hacking cough, with a constant, painful urging to swallow, with blood-streaked sputa.

Sleep - Restless at night. Sleepless.

Skin - Profuse sweat.

Kidneys - Compelled to urinate frequently. Urine copious, clear, watery.

Nosebleeds. Nymphomania. Ozaena. Palpitations. Paralysis. Pemphigus. Pneumonia. Ptosis. Puerperal fever. Puerperal mania. Pulmonary, edema. Seasickness. Sciatica. Scurvy. Stomach, ulcer. Typhoid fever. Typhus fever. Ulcers. Urticaria. Vertigo. Weakness. Whitlow. Whooping cough.

HOMEOPATHIC - Schiissler used this remedy for conditions arising from want of nerve power. According to Schiissler, Kali-p. is contained in the cells of the brains, nerves, muscles, blood (corpuscles and plasma) and intercellular fluids. A disturbance in the motions of its molecules produces despondency, anxiety, fearfulness, fearfulness, homesickness, suspiciousness, agoraphobia, and weak memory. There is Kali phosphoricum at first a small and frequent pulse, later it is retarded. Pain with sensation of paralysis in sensory nerves. Weakness of muscles and nerves even to paralysis. Retarded nutrition, even total arrest in a limited area of cells and then a softening. Cases in which there is increased sensitivity to all impressions from a weakness of the vital resistance or control. In weakened states from mental or physical shock, from over strain or over drain of the system. H. T. Doge noted that it is indicated for worn-out nursing mothers, tired to distraction by nervous babies. Wom- out business and professional men or women, or students. Doge recommended the higher potencies where indications are close. Characteristic low, nervous condition. Generally nervous, sensitive, weak and easily fagged by slight causes like pain, worry, mental fatigue etc. Conditions arising from lack of nerve power, neurasthenia, and mental and physical depression. Nervous prostration. Weak and tired. Marked disturbance of the sympathetic nervous system, usually from excitement, overwork and wony. Convalescence after exhausting diseases. Muscular weakness after acute diseases. States of weakness and decay, gangrenous conditions. Suspected malignant tumors. Delayed labor. Putrid, carrion like odor of secretions, foul odor of the body. Foul breath, with brownish mustard-like coat on the tongue. Secretions are golden yellow. Emaciation, wasting diseases. After surgery, when in the healing process the skin is drawn tight over the wound, especially cancer. Stitching pains. Dull, heavy ache between the shoulders. Paralytic weakness or pain with sensation of paralysis. Paralysis infantile during dentition. Nervous, restless, fidgety feeling in feet, trembling sensation in muscles of legs. Numb sensations. Sexual excitement from indulgence or suppression. Irregular, menses, pulse, etc. Seasickness without nausea. Especially adapted to the young. MIND - Mental and physical prostration caused by a combination of overworking and psychological factors like excitement, worry and vexation. Mental fatigue from over study or overwork. Brain fatigue. Mental exertion aggravates. Ailments from strong emotions, fright, grief, care. Extreme lassitude and depression, lethargy, gloom. Morose. Great despondency about business. Slightest labor seems a heavy task. Dullness of mind. Weak memory. Forgetful, loss of memory. Shyness, disinclined to converse. Indisposition to meet people or to talk with them. Sighing ormoaning. Homesickness. Sadness on waking. Weariness of life and fear of death. Negative, dark forebodings. Very nervous, starts easily. Anxiety and worry. Anxiety with nervous dread. Apprehensive about future. Fear of being alone, open spaces, crowds. Fear about his health, of death. Angry. Irritability when spoken to. Impatience about trifles. Gloomy moods. Dwelling upon grievances. Suspicious. Obstinate. Perverted affections. Aversion to own family, cruel to husband, baby. Easily frightened. Starting from noise, when touched. Sensitive to light and noise, especially during menses. Disposition to feel bodily pains too acutely. Oversensitive children. Children cry and scream, fly into passion, can hardly articulate. Night terrors. Shyness, excessive blushing, from undue sensitiveness. Hysterical fits of laughter and crying. Weeping about trifles. Religious melancholy, believes she is eternally and irretrievably damned. Continually weeping and crying. Wringing hands. Tears things. Pulling to pieces and tearing her clothing, as well as bed covering. Doesn't recognize her surroundings.

Head - Excruciating nervous headache with great sensitiveness to noise. Headache of students, worse mental exertion. Occipital pain, better after rising. Pains and weight at back of head, with feeling of weariness and exhaustion. Cerebral anemia. Headache with weary, empty, gone feeling at stomach (Ign., Sep.), with hunger. Headaches worse before and during menses. Headache are relieved by gentle motion.

Eyes - Burn, sting, with a lot of tears. Yellowgray milky secretion. Retinitis. Drooping of eyelids, especially the left (Caust.). Squint after brain diseases. Weakness of vision. Loss of perceptive power, after diphtheria from exhaustion. Black spots before eyes.

Ears - Ulceration of the eardrum and middle ear suppurations, with foul discharge. Sensitive hearing, cannot endure noise. Noises in ears from nervous exhaustion. Noises in head on falling asleep. Humming and buzzing in the ears. Deafness from atrophic condition of nerve.

Nose - Hay fever with nervous irritability. Hay fever, as a prophylactic. Itching in posterior sinuses. Violent sneezing with symptoms of fresh cold, at 2 a.m. Ozaena. Nasal disease with offensive odor. Fetid discharge. Nosebleeds.

Face - Sad, careworn look. Livid and sunken with hollow eyes. Neuralgia of face followed by great weakness. Right-sided neuralgia, relieved by cold applications. Sharp pains from riding in cold air. Brown stripe at the edge of hair.

Mouth - Aphthae. Breath offensive, fetid. Palate feels greasy. Mouth excessively dry. in morning. Gums, spongy, receding, with bright-red seam. Noma. Slow speech, becoming inarticulate. Nervous, chattering of teeth.

Throat - Aphonia. Paralysis of vocal cords. Hoarseness from overexertion of voice. Croup, last stage. Sensation as if a ball rising in throat. Gangrenous sore throat.

Stomach - Indigestion with great nervous depression. Gastritis with failing strength. Nervous, gone sensation at the pit of stomach, bettereating (Ign., Sep., Sulph.). Hungry soon after eating. Feels seasick without nausea. Nausea, better belchings, worse coughing.

Abdomen - Abdomen feels cold, better covering. Cutting pain in abdomen. Affections of spleen. Splenic leukemia. Enterocolitis. Hernia. Flatulence with distress about heart.

Rectum - Diarrhea, foul, putrid odor. Diarrhea caused by fright. Diarrhea with depression and exhaustion. Brain affection with diarrhea smelling like carrion. Diarrhea, at night and after eating. Dysentery, stools consist of pure blood, patient becomes delirious, abdomen swells. Cholera, rice water stools (Verat., Ars., Jatr.). Hot, golden yellow stools. Painless stools. Prolapse rectum (Ign., Podo.). Paretic condition of rectum and colon after removal of hemorrhoids. Sensations - As if tongue would cleave to root of mouth, as if a ball were rising in throat, as if a rocket had passed through head.

Male - Nocturnal emissions. Sexual excitement. Impotency. Sexual power diminished. Prostration and weak vision after sex or after nightly emissions (Kali-c.).

Female - Delayed menses with depression. Menses irregular. Menses too late or too scanty in pale, initable. sensitive, lachrymose females. Menses, too profuse discharge. Menses, deep-red or black- red, thin and not coagulating. Menses, sometimes with offensive odor. Horribly foul leucorrhea. Periodical discharge of copious orange colored fluid from vagina and rectum. Intense sexual desire for days afterthe menses. Tired, worn out, nervous women, subject to miscarriage. Feeble and ineffectual labor pains. Puerperal fever with absurd notions or mania. Food - Hungry soon after eating. Wants to eat almost every hour. No appetite except for sweets. Craves ice cold water, cold drinks, vinegar, sweets. Aversion to food, bread and meat.

Chest - Pain in lower part of left chest, worse coughing. Axillary sweat smells of onions.

Heart - Sluggish circulation in sensitive, nervous subjects. Weak action of heart causes fainting. Palpitations with shortness of breath, with nervousness, anxiety, sleeplessness Palpitations, worse slightest motion or ascending stairs. Intermittent action of heart from violent emotions, fright, grief, care. Pulse irregular.

Back - Stiffness of back after rest, better gentle motion. Paralytic lameness of back, must lean on a chair. Rheumatic pains and weakness. Spinal irritation. Creeping sensation and intense pain along spine, relieves the headache. Constitutions - Weak nervous system and brain. Suited to pale, sensitive, irritable persons. Causations - Ill effects of mechanical injuries, grief, or vexation. Mental overwork.

Limbs - Paralytic lameness in back and limbs. Paralyzing pain in limbs, better motion and external warmth, worse during rest. Exertion aggravates. Pains with depression and subsequent exhaustion. Prickling in hands and feet. Numb fingertips. Feet fidgety. Chilblains. Foot feels frostbitten. Pains in soles. Lungs - Nervous asthma, least food aggravates. Short breath, worse going upstairs. Cough with yellow expectoration. Whooping cough in highly nervous patients with great exhaustion. Frothy, expectoration with pulmonary edema.

Sleep - Drowsy. Yawning. Sleeplessness from worry, over study, business troubles. Sleeplessness from overactive mind. Restlessness and heat during sleep. Sleepwalking. Sighing and moaning during sleep. Amorous dreams. Night terrors. Awakening with fright and screaming. Loss of sleep.

Skin - Skin diseases with bad smelling discharge. Greasy, offensive smelling crusts or scales. Ulcers, ichorous, bad smelling. Vesicles with bloody, ichorous contents. Pemphigus. Urticaria. Erysipelas bordering on gangrene. Gangrene. Blue spots on skin. Skin inactive. Cold skin. Jaundiced.

Modalities - Better from warmth, rest, sleep, gentle motion, leaning against something. Better from nourishment, eating, when menses comes. Worse mental and physical exertion, anxiety and worry. Worse from slight causes. Worse from cold, dry air, cold drinks, eating. Worse puberty, sex, excitement, touch, pain, early morning.

Teeth - Nervous chattering of teeth. Toothache, with easily-bleeding gums. Gums spongy andreceding (Caps., Ham., Lach.). Toothache of highly nervous, delicate, pale, irritable, sensitive persons.

Tongue - Tongue coated brownish, yellow like liquid mustard. Sensation as if tongue would adhere to roof of mouth from dryness of mouth. Creeping paralysis of the tongue. Vertigo - Vertigo from fatigue, from lying down, when facing the sun, on standing up from sitting, when looking upward (Gran.). COMMENTS - Chronic fatigue from excessive mental work or over-exertion of the mind; the mind and nervous system become weak. Mental fatigue. Headaches from over studying. Nervous insomnia (Aven.). Memory loss and difficultly concentrating in the elderly. Pain in the back of neck and head. General irritability, great despondency. Depressed states of mind and body. Hypochondriasis, hysteria. Neurasthenia. Great lassitude, emaciation. Nervous, hot, restless, easily startled. The least touch causes starting. Trembling of hands from nervousness. Stitching pains. Numb fingertips. Spasms of irritable weakness, paralysis. Progressive muscular atrophy, around ulcer of stomach. Typhoid, typhus fever. Septic states, septic fevers and hemorrhages. Phagedenic chancre, carbuncles. Toothache alternating with headache. Alopecia areata. Scurvy. Menstrual headaches, backaches with menses. Severe vaginitis with yellow- brown, offensive discharge (Kreos.). Worse after sex and sensitiveness to touch. Aching in sacrum. Frequent urination, passing large quantities night and day, containing phosphates. H. C. Allen noted the indications of waking in the early morning, the peculiar mouth and the severe action on the skin. Characteristic golden or orange-yellow color. Urine is very yellow. Allen gave the remedy for sleeplessness, and cured an old pelvic abscess with orange colored discharge. W. T. Laird pointed out that Kali-p. cures a nervous dyspepsia almost identical with that of Anae. The Kali-p. patient is more decidedly neurasthenic than the other and the relapses, which are frequent in both, are mostly due to dietetic errors in Anae, cases and to excitement or worry in the Kali-p. cases. H. M. Rean reported cures in cases of amenorrhea. One young woman, who was very nervous, pale blonde, skin rather waxy, cross and snappish, but cried easily, had a constant dull headache, yet was very drowsy all day. Fidgety, at times could not control herself, and called her mother to hold her hands. Menses did not appear until eighteen and were scanty then and since. Kali-p. 3x four times daily caused great improvement at next menstrual period. In three months the menses were regular and normal, and in five months the patient was perfectly well. J. C. Nottingham considered a leading indication of Kali-p. “nervousness arising from excessive sexual excitement, whether indulged or suppressed.” He has cured impotence and seminal losses on these indications. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Zinc., Gels., Cimic., Lach., Mur-ac. (2) Kali-hp. (3) Mac- roz.- extreme debility after severe illness, collapse. Macroz., weariness from no assignable cause, no pains. Boring pain at vertex, vomiting and retching all night, impossible to eyes, giddiness and cold. (4) Genist. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Kidneys - Nocturnal bedwetting, in nervous, excitable children and in old people. Incontinence of urine. Very yellow urine, saffron yellow or milky. Bleeding from urethra. Urine comes in stops and starts.

Perspiration - Excessive, exhausting, strong-smelling sweats. Axillary sweat smells of onions.

Temperature - Subnormal temperature. Yellow fever.

HOMEOPATHIC - Kali-s., introduced by Schiissler, affects respiration, mucus membranes and skin where it causes desquamation. Schiissler explains that Kali-s., in reciprocal action with iron, effects the transfer of the inhaled oxygen to all the cells and is contained in all the cells containing iron. When a sulphate and any oxide of iron come into contact with decomposing organic substances they surrender their oxygen and form sulphate of iron. With more oxygen added, this may be further decomposed into sulphuric acid and an oxide of iron. A deficiency of Kali-s. causes a sensation of heaviness and weariness, vertigo, chilliness, palpitations of the heart, anxiety, sadness, toothache, headache and pain in the limbs. Symptoms are worse in a warm room and towards evening, better in open, cool air. Catarrh of larynx, bronchi, nostrils, etc., with yellow discharges. Catarrh of the stomach where the tongue has a yellowish mucus coating. Profuse and deep yellow discharges, thin or sticky. Ailments accompanied by profuse desquamation. Suppurations. Yellow, mucus and serous discharges, profuse and intermittent. Later stages of inflammation. Wandering pains, wandering rheumatism (Puls., Kali- bi.). Stitching, tearing, festering pains that shift about. Torpid processes. Lack of reaction. Warmblooded. Oxaluria. Facilitates the formation of new epithelium. Epithelial cancer. Interrupted growth of nails. Gonorrhea and ophthalmia neonatorum (Puls.). MIND-Alwayshurried. Irritable. Timid. Confusion and restlessness, worse in a warm room. Mental exertion aggravates. Desires and then rejects things. Desire to lie down, but lying aggravates so must walk for relief. . Anxiety, better in the open air. Anxiety in evening. Frightened at trifles. Fear of falling, of losing her reason. Claustrophobia with fear of suffocation.

Head - Rheumatic headache, beginning in evening. Headaches worse warm room, better open air. Headache during menses. Great pain on moving head from side to side or backwards. Dandruff yellow, moist and sticky. Scaldhead. Bald spots, after gonorrhea.

Eyes - Purulent yellow mucus in eye diseases. Sticky, watery discharge from eyes. Thin, yellow crusts on eyelids. Cataract. Ophthalmia neonatorum.

Ears - Eustachian deafness. Stinking otorrhea. Bro wn offensive secretion from right ear. Offensive discharge with polyps. Discharge of yellow matter (Hydr.). Watery, sticky, thin discharge.

Nose - Colds with ayellow,slimy discharge. Yellow, thick discharge, alternating with watery discharge. Sinusitis with thick yellow, green discharges. Nose obstructed. Loss of smell and taste (Nat-m.). Swelling of the nasal pharyngeal mucus membrane, remaining after removal of adenoids.

Face - Aches in heated room, better cool open air. Epithelioma.

Mouth - Mouth breathing, snoring. Insipid, pappy taste. Loss of taste and smell. Tongue coated yellow and slimy. Yellow mucus coating on tongue. Painful gums. Toothache, worse warm room and toward evening, better cool open air. Blistered lips and mouth. Lower lip swollen. Epithelioma on lip.

Throat - Croupy hoarseness (Hep., Spong.). Constant scraping. Sore throat and hoarseness after catching a cold. Every cold settles in larynx. Vertigo - Dreadful vertigo on rising from lying, on standing from sitting. Vertigo when looking upwards. Vertigo with a fear of falling. COMMENTS - Useful for chronic Puls, conditions, recurring earaches, asthma, respiratory problems, when Puls, doesn't cure completely. Yellow discharges, thick and bland, especially from the sinuses and lungs. Rattling mucus (Ant-t.). Wandering arthritis, worse hot applications and hot baths. Desquamation. Skin conditions with flaking and peeling. Psoriasis, eczema, dandruff. Scabs with yellow pus. Ulcers ooze yellow, watery fluid. Skin cancer. Tongue can be yellow with a slimy coating. General sluggishness. Modalities similarto Puls. Worse in warm, stuffy rooms, at twilight, better fresh air. Thirstless. Better walking in the fresh, open air. Mood changes and can weep easily. Claustrophobic with fear of suffocation. M. E. Douglass reported an asthma case with a lot of thick, yellow expectoration. Much rattling in chest, with labored breathing and talking almost impossible, this was cured with Kali-s. 3x, five grains every hour in the attack. Hansen cured with Kali-s. a case of psoriasis beginning on the right leg, later attacking the left elbow and left leg. Eruption, papular, oval and annular with paler centers, covered with whitish scales, skin beneath red and smooth. The guiding symptom was “great desquamation of the epidermis.” RELATIONS - Antidote to: Rhus poisoning. Compare: (1) Kali-s., Puls., Kali-bi., Nairn. (2) Puls., Kali-bi. (3) Hydr. - dyspepsia, epithelioma. (4) Chr-ac. 3x. - produces in the nasal passages very fine threads from the septum to external wall, disorders of nasal fosse and hay fever. Chronic colds. Sneezing, red, watery eyes, irritation of mucus membrane. Compatible: Acet- ac. (itching and redness of skin), Calc., Hep., Puls., Rhus-t., Sep., Sil., Sulph. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Stomach - Burning thirst. Pressure and feeling of fullness in stomach. Sensation as if a heavy load on stomach. Sensation of faintness in stomach with befogged feeling in head. Catarrh of stomach and duodenum. Nausea, and vomiting.

Abdomen - Colicky pains, abdomen feels cold to touch. Abdomen cold and distended after eating. Hard, ascites, in whooping cough. Empty feeling in hypogastrium, better passing flatus.

Rectum - Constipation with hemorrhoids (Sulph.). Stools large like sheep's dung. Black, thin, offensive stools. Stools light-colored and bilious. Yellow, slimy diarrhea.

Male - Gonorrhea, slimy, yellowish, green discharges. Gleet. Orchitis after suppressed gonorrhea.

Female - Menses too late, scanty. Menses with a feeling of weight in the abdomen. Metrorrhagia. Leucorrhea, yellowish, watery. Food - Burning thirst. Craves sweets, cold food, cold drinks. Dread of hot drinks. Averse to and worse from eggs.

Chest - Anxiety in chest.

Back - Pain in nape. Stiff neck, head inclined towards left. Rheumatic pains in back and limbs, worse in warm room, better cool open air. Causations - Ill effects of chill when over heated. Injuries.

Limbs - Rheumatism. Rheumatic pains, worse heat, evening, better cold weather or cold applications. Pain in back and limbs, worse in a warm room. Shifting, wanderingpains. Arthritic nodes. Cold hands and feet. Scaly eruption on arms, better hot water. Diseased condition of nails. Lungs - Asthma with yellow, slimy expectoration, easily expelled. Coarse rales in lungs. Bronchitis, mucus is distinctly yellow and slimy, thin, or watery matter and profuse. Rattling of mucus in lungs (Ant-t.). Post- influenza cough, especially in children. Cough, worse in evening and in hot atmosphere. Croupy cough (Hep., Spong.). Pneumonia with wheezing. Yellow, loose rattling mucus is coughed up with difficulty. Sputum consists of watery matter. Whooping cough.

Sleep - Sleeplessness from heat, warm room. Vivid, terrifying dreams of ghosts, death, robbers, murder. Dreams with violent struggling in their sleep.

Skin - Dry skin. Itching, worse heat. Peeling, flaking of skin. Psoriasis (Ars., Thyr.). Intertrigo. Eczema, burning, itching, papular eruption. Desquamation of skin. Promotes desquamation after erysipelas. Accelerates removal of scabs in smallpox. Nettle rash. Yellow scales. Favus. Yellow skin jaundice. Skin affections with yellow, slimy discharge. Ulcers, ooze thinyeZ/ow water. Polyps. Epithelioma. Suppressed rash of measles or other eruptive diseases, with harsh and dry skin. Seborrhea. Scabs with yellow pus. Ringworm of scalp or beard with abundant scales. Scabies. Rhus poisoning.

Modalities - Better from walking, fasting, discharge of flatus, cool, open air. Worse in evening (Puls.), noise, consolation. Cannot stand warm rooms or other forms of heat. Worse warm air, warm wraps, warm weather, heated room.

Kidneys - Albuminuria after scarlatina. Oxaluria. Pyelitis.

Perspiration - Profuse, easy sweat.

Temperature - Chilliness. Cold hands and feet. Intermittent fever. Temperature rises at night.

full:
PHARMACY - kali-t. Kali tartaricum. Potassium tartrate. Cream of tartar. Tartrate of potash. Trituration. Sohition. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Insomnia. Salivation. Tongue, swelling.

HOMEOPATHIC - A few symptoms of Kali-tel. have been observed, of which the garlicky odor of the breath was the most noticeable and persistent. Offensive breath. Tongue coated white and swollen, with salivation. Appetite increased at first, later diminished, finally lost.

Mouth - Tongue coated white and somewhat swollen. Offensive garlicky odor in mouth. Copious secretion of saliva.

Stomach - Inclination to vomit. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Tell., Phos. and Kali-p. - garlicky odor. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Abdomen - Pain in umbilical region with thirst. Flatulence and griping. Pain in loins.

Rectum - Diarrhea and violent vomiting. Feces like coffee-grounds.

Heart - Oppression in cardiac region.

Limbs - Thighs and legs paralyzed. Mouth - Tongue brown and dry.

Sleep - Sleepiness during first days.

Pulse - Pulse feeble.

author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from eating cloudy weather, continued motion, sitting, or standing upright. Worse looking down, turning eyes, stooping, bendingforward, motion, lying on left side. Worse from heat of sun, open air, becoming cold, from sunrise to sunset. Worse during leucorrhea..

keynote: PHARMACY - kalm. Kalmia latifolia. Mountain laurel. Ledum floribus bullatis. American laurel. Calico bush. Cistus chamerhododen- dros. N. O. Ericaceae. Rocky sterile hills, near water in New England States. Flowers May and June. Tincture of fresh leaves when the plant is in…
full:
PHARMACY - kalm. Kalmia latifolia. Mountain laurel. Ledum floribus bullatis. American laurel. Calico bush. Cistus chamerhododen- dros. N. O. Ericaceae. Rocky sterile hills, near water in New England States. Flowers May and June. Tincture of fresh leaves when the plant is in flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Angina, pectoris. Arthritis. Blindness. Bright's disease. Coryza. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Gastralgia. Globus hystericus. Gout. Headache. Heart, disease. Hoarseness. Locomotor, ataxia. Lumbago. Nausea. Neuralgias. Palpitations. Ptosis. Pregnancy, albuminuria. Rheumatic, fever. Rheumatism. Retinitis. Scleroderma. Sunheadaches. Syphilitic, sore throat. Tachycardia. Tinnitus. Tobacco, effects. Tobacco, heart. Vertigo. Vomiting.

HERBAL - Kalmia is the name of a genus of heath worts native to North America. Kalmia latifolia, which has large and showy flowers, is found in the northern parts of the United States. Its flowers yield a honey said to be deleterious, and its leaves and shoots certainly are so to cattle. Dr. Meadows says cattle eat Kalmia in the latter part of the winter when they are in want of something green. Kalmia latifolia K. angustifolia, probably for the same reason, has the name of lamb-kill. The powdered leaves are used as a local remedy in some skin diseases. The hard wood of K. latifolia is used in the manufacture of various articles. The Treasury of Botany noted that the Canadian partridge is said to become poisonous to humans after feeding on Kalmia berries.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hering introduced Kalm. into homeopathic practice, and he, and some friends, completed the first proving. The head, including the eyes and face, shows the majority of its action, followed by the heart. A number of skin symptoms confirm the popular use of the leaves, among them a stiffness of the skin, especially of the eyelids. A heart, nerve, circulation and rheumatic remedy. In small doses, it accelerates the heart’s action, in larger doses, it moderates it greatly. Nausea and slow pulse frequently accompany conditions. Neuralgic pains, shoot downwards with numbness, tingling, trembling or paralytic weakness. Neuralgia after the disappearance of herpetic eruptions. Great weakness with neuralgia. Pains of locomotor ataxia. Protracted and continuous fevers with tympanites. Albuminuria. Paralytic sensations, pains and achings in the limbs. Pains shift rapidly, shooting outward along the nerves with much nausea and slow pulse. Aching, bruised, stiff feeling. Dull tearing, crushing pain, moving downwards. Pain alternating with cardiac symptoms or between upper and lower limbs. Rheumatism, syphilitic. Motion brings on complaints. MIND - Confusion of brain. Memory and mental faculties are perfect in a recumbent posture, but vertigo on attempting to move. Anxiety and palpitations. Irritable, cross. Talk of others aggravates.

Head - Cracking in head, sounds like a horn blowing in the ears, frightens him. Headache worse and better with sun. Headache begins at sunrise, worse at noon and leaves at sunset. Headache worse bright sunlight. Headache better profuse urina- tion. Shooting pain from nape to vertex and face. Maddening supra-orbital pain (right). Pain in front and temporal region from head, to nape, and to teeth, from cardiac origin. Aching in forehead.

Eyes - Stiff drawing sensation when moving eyes. Pains increased by moving the eye. Pressure in and above right eye. Paralysis of upper lids. Stiff eyelids. Retinitis, albuminuria especially during pregnancy. Rheumatic iritis. Scleritis. Itching in eyes, stinging when rubbing them. Eye symptoms worse evening and in open air.

Ears - Sharp pain in and behind right ear, at night. Acute inflammation of meatus. Sound like blowing a horn after cracking in head. Meniere's disease.

Nose - Coryza, with increased sense of smell. Coryza with sneezing, dullness, headache and hoarseness. Tearing in root of nose and nasal bones, with nausea.

Face - Anxious expression. Flushing with vertigo. Redness of face during throbbing headache. Neuralgia, worse right side. Neuralgia from exposure to cold, better eating, worse from worry or mental exertion. Trigeminal neuralgia. Facial neuralgia after herpes zoster. Sharp and tearing pains in bones of jaw and face. Itching of face at night. Tired feeling in masseters. Cracked lips with dry skin.

Mouth - Tingling in salivary gland. Sublingual salivary gland inflamed. Bitter taste with nausea, better eating. Tongue white, dry. Sharp pain in tongue. Tongue, sore left side, hurts when talking. Teeth tender, during facial neuralgia. Pressing in molars, late in evening. Tired feeling in chewing muscles. Lips, stiff, dry, swollen.

Throat - Throat feels swollen. Sensation as of a ball rising. Pressure in throat, stitches in eyes and nausea. Dryness in throat with aching pains, causing cough, difficult swallowing and thirst. Chronic syphilitic sore throat. Tickling in trachea. Noise as from spasm in glottis when breathing. Hoarseness during coryza. Vertigo - Vertigo with headache, nausea, blindness, pains in the limbs and weariness. Vertigo worse from motion (Bry.), worse stooping, looking down. Vertigo with blindness. Vision - Impaired vision. Vision becomes black on looking downward. Diplopia, from paralysis of ocular muscles. Glimmering vision, with dimness. COMMENTS - For paralytic weakness and trembling. Neuralgias in almost all regions, generally on the right side. Wandering arthritis, sharp, shooting pain jumps from joint to joint. Arthritis with heart conditions or neuralgias. Wandering rheumatic pains that travel from above downwards. Rheumatic fever. Pain, followed by numbness in the joints (Naphtin. with sciatica). Joints can swell, become red, hot and throbbing (Bell. ). Pains worse sunrise to sunset (Nat-m., Spig.). Painful facial neuralgias (Spig., Mag-p.). Neuralgic pains are better from food. Pain in the back, shuns all exertion, can hardly go up stairs. Pains in the periosteum preventing sleep. Pain between shoulders coming up over the head. Pain with nausea and slow pulse. Pain during the early part of the night or soon after going to sleep. Pain from a sudden chill or exposure to a sudden wind. Tumultuous action of the heart and slow pulse. Every heartbeat has a strumming as if it would burst, along sternum to throat. Palpitations are better lying on back and breathing, worse on left side, from mental effort. Generally acts on the right side of the head, the left side of the chest and the left arm. Vertigo from least motion, worse from motion (Bry.), even motion of eyes and eyelids is painful. Vertigo is worse on stooping, on looking down, on rising from a seat. Headache comes on in the morning, worse again in evening. Headache, worse heat, better cold. Sun headache, worse or better with the sun. Headache and eye symptoms are worse in evening, from open air. Rubbing eyes causes stinging in them. Scleroderma. Cheek roughness every summer. Much external sensitiveness, face, pit of stomach, muscles of neck sore, worse by touch. Dry throat. Feeling as if a ball was rising in the throat. Dry, stiff, swollen, cracked lips. Tingling in the salivary glands immediately after eating. Stitches in the tongue. Sensation of weakness in abdomen extending to throat. Vomiting with ruminating action, without the least nausea, better with wine. Pressure on rectum after stool. Symptoms worse during leucorrhea. Vonder Luhe cured with Kalm. 200c an intercostal neuralgia of the left side, so intense that the patient could not lie down or sleep at night. The chief guiding symptom was a concomitant numb sensation of the whole left arm. Lambert recorded the case of a gatekeeper, age 54, who had smoked since he was seven years old. He suffered from “tobacco heart” palpitations, occurring on the least exertion or fright and sometimes awakening him in the night. Intermittent pulse, no valvular lesion, tingling in the left arm and leg and sensation as if the blood did not circulate in them. He could walk, but not far. The chief complaint was a sharp pain in the right temple like pins and needles, of eighteen months' duration. It was induced by touch and turning the head quickly. Kalm. 3x cured the temporal neuralgia and greatly alleviated all the other symptoms. Proell cured with Kalm. 1c, 2c and 3c headaches and weak memory in a boy of 13 that were preventing him from continuing his studies. He also had insufficiency of the mitral value. RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Aeon., Bell.Antidote to: Tab. Compare: (1) Kalm. contains Arbutin. (2) Der. of great service in neuralgic headaches of rheumatic origin). (3) Spig., Puls. Complementary: Benz-ac. Follows well: Nux-v., Thyr., Spig. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Crampy pain with eructation of gas. Pain in pit of stomach, worse by bendingforward, relieved by sitting erect. Sensation of something being pressed under the epigastrium. Warm, glowing sensation in epigastrium. Gastralgia with empty eructations. Bilious attacks with nausea, vertigo and headache. Nausea and vomiting. Wine relieves vomiting.

Abdomen - Incarcerated flatus with nausea. Sensation of weakness in abdomen extending to throat, better by eructation. Sudden pains in paroxysms, across abdomen, above umbilicus. Neuralgia of bowels.

Rectum - Diarrhea with dullness, dizziness, weariness, nausea and bellyache. Stools like mush, easily discharged. Stools as if glazed, followed by pressure on rectum. Sensations - As if something loose in head diagonally across the top. As if the body was surcharged with electricity, as shuddering without coldness. As if something was being pressed away from under sternum.

Male - Frequent, spontaneous, lasting erections without desire. Pain in the right testicle in morning, in the left testicle in afternoon.

Female - Menses too soon. Menses regular but painful. Suppressed menses, with severe neuralgic pains throughout whole body, with pain in limbs, back and inside of thighs. Leucorrhea, one week after menses, aggravating other symptoms.

Chest - Angina pectoris with dyspnea and pain. Feverish heat with great pain in chest, worse when breathing and from slightest motion. Pain in chest as from a sprain. Sharp pain in lower chest. Shooting through chest above heart into shoulder blade. Pain in left arm. False pleurisy of winter season. Rheumatism of muscles of thorax and back, worse from every motion.

Heart - Angina pectoris with empty eructations. Heart disease, after frequent attacks of rheumatism, or alternating with it. Tumultuous action, rapid and visible. Paroxysms of anguish around heart. Fluttering of heart with anxiety. Pains, sharp, burning shooting, stabbing, radiating to left scapula and arm. Sharp pains take away the breath. Tachycardia with pains (Thyr.). Severe palpitations with constriction of throat, worse motion. Palpitations, worse leaning forward, better sitting erect. Gouty and rheumatic metastasis of heart. Shooting through chest above heart into shoulder blades. Tobacco heart. Hypertrophy, valvular insufficiency. Aortic obstruction. Pulse slow, weak, tremulous (Dig., Apoc.). Frequent pulse.

Back - Pain from neck down arm, brachial- gia. Pain down back, as if it would break. Kalmia latifolia Pain in localized regions of spine, through the shoulders. Sharp pain in lower part • of left scapula. Lumbar pain of nervous origin, with heat and burning. Sensation of lameness in small of back. Drawing or sharp pain in spine.

Limbs - Pains affects a large part of a limb or several joints and pass through quickly. Weakness, numbness, pricking and sense of coldness in limbs. Joints red, hot, swollen. Pains from hips to knees and feet. Pains along ulnar nerve, goes into third or fourth fingers. Tingling and numbness of left arm (heart pains). Deltoid rheumatism, especially right.

Sleep - Sleepless. Restless sleep, turns often. Periosteal pains prevent sleep. While sleeping, stands up and walks about. Talks in sleep. Fantastic dreams. Dreams of murder. Wakes very early in morning.

Skin - Stiff, dry skin. Sensation of rigidity. Pricking sensation in skin with moderate sweat. Erysipelatous on hand with oppressed breathing. Scabies-like eruptions. Red inflamed places here and there, exceedingly painful, as if boils would form. Scleroderma.

Modalities - Better from eating cloudy weather, continued motion, sitting, or standing upright. Worse looking down, turning eyes, stooping, bendingforward, motion, lying on left side. Worse from heat of sun, open air, becoming cold, from sunrise to sunset. Worse during leucorrhea.

Liver - Pains in region of liver. Lungs - Dyspnea and pressure from epigastrium toward the heart. Short-breathed, must breathe quickly, involuntary. Difficult and oppressed breathing, throat feels swollen, nausea, with palpitations and anxiety. Noise as from spasm of glottis when breathing. Hoarseness with coryza. Tickling in trachea. Frequent cough caused by dryness or scraping in the throat. Expectoration easy, smooth, gray, tasting putrid, salty.

Kidneys - Frequent urination of large quantity of yellow urine, with sharp pains in lumbar region. Frequent urination of scanty, hot urine. Profuse urination, better headache. Post-scarlatinal nephritis. Albuminuria with pains in lower limbs, dropsy. Albuminuria during pregnancy.

Perspiration - Cold sweat.

Temperature - Shivering and coldness. Shaking chill in cold air; chills run over back. Protracted and continued fevers with tympanites. Fever with burning and pain in back and loins.

name: Kamala
author: Murphy
constitution: Leprosy. Pustules. Skin, affections. Tapeworm. Worms.
keynote: PHARMACY - kam. Kamala. Spoon wood. Croton coccineus. Rottlera tinctoria. Mallotus philippinensis. N. O. Euphorbiacae. India, South Arabia, Australia. A red mealy inflammable powder, obtained from the tri-lobed capsules of the plant. Tincture. Solution in ether. Trituration.…
full:
PHARMACY - kam. Kamala. Spoon wood. Croton coccineus. Rottlera tinctoria. Mallotus philippinensis. N. O. Euphorbiacae. India, South Arabia, Australia. A red mealy inflammable powder, obtained from the tri-lobed capsules of the plant. Tincture. Solution in ether. Trituration. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Leprosy. Pustules. Skin, affections. Tapeworm. Worms.

HERBAL - Kamala is best known in medicine as a remedy for tapeworms. It is given in doses of half to two drachms. The Treasury of Botany noted that “Among the Arabs of Aden it is given internally in leprosy, and used in solution to remove freckles and pustules, while in this country it has been used successfully in treating the eruption known as ‘wildfire’ (Strophulus volaticus) in children, by rubbing the powder over the affected part with moist lint.“Kam. appears, however, to be most valued as an anthelmintic, and has been extensively used with much success in India in cases of tapeworms, three drachms being sufficient for a robust person, and half that quantity for one of feeble habit.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kam. shows by its clinical uses it relationship with Croton and the other Euphorbians. REFERENCES-Clarke.

CLINICAL - Convulsions. Pains. Paralysis.

HOMEOPATHIC -…
full:
PHARMACY - kara. Karaka. Kopi tree. Co- rynocarpus levigatus. N. O. Myrsinacee, Allen puts it in Anacardiacae. New Zealand. Tincture or Trituration of fresh seeds. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Convulsions. Pains. Paralysis.

HOMEOPATHIC - The Treasury of Botany noted that karaka seeds contain a tasteless farinaceous substance and are eaten in times of scarcity. The raw seeds are poisonous and produce spasmodic pains, giddiness and partial paralysis. To render them edible, they are steamed for twenty-four hours and then either buried in the ground or allowed to soak in water for some days. G. Bennett recorded a few symptoms observed in the case of a Maori chief poisoned with the seeds. Spasm with pains. Violent pain lasting a week. Partial paralysis. Heat anesthesia, when warm water was applied he did not feel any warmth from it. Violent spasms and convulsions of whole body, arms and legs stretched violently and rigidly out. Permanent rigid distortion. COMMENTS - C. F. Fischer proved Kara, and used it clinically in cases of convulsions. He recorded an account of its effect from the proceedings of the New Zealand Institute. “Violent spasms and convulsions of whole body, arms and legs stretched violently and rigidly out, great flushings of heat, protrusion of eyes and tongue, gnashing of jaws. The poison proves rapidly fatal if the patient is not attended to immediately and the limbs are permanently and rigidly distorted if they are not fixed in proper positions until the crisis is passed. “The general treatment is to bind the patient (generally a child) with the limbs in right positions, dig a pit and place him in it, standing, buried up to the chin with a gag in his mouth. “The writer described a youth, age 12, who had recovered after being poisoned, but whose limbs had not been properly secured and were ever after absolutely useless. “One leg was curved up behind his loins, the other bent up with the foot outwards. One arm inclined behind his shoulder, the other slightly bent and extended forward and all, as to muscles inflexibly rigid. He could not move himself or even drive away the flies.” REFERENCES-Clarke.

author: Murphy
constitution: Acute poliomyelitis. Acute bulbar paralysis. Amyotrophy. Bedsores. Dyspnea. Encephalitis. Paralysis. Paresis.Poliomyelitis. Quadriplegia.
keynote:
PHARMACY - karw-h. Karwinskia humboldtiana. N. O. Rhamnacae. Foundin Mexico and Southern North America. The seeds, crushed and macerated are used for the preparation of the tincture. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acute poliomyelitis. Acute bulbar…
full:
PHARMACY - karw-h. Karwinskia humboldtiana. N. O. Rhamnacae. Foundin Mexico and Southern North America. The seeds, crushed and macerated are used for the preparation of the tincture. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acute poliomyelitis. Acute bulbar paralysis. Amyotrophy. Bedsores. Dyspnea. Encephalitis. Paralysis. Paresis.Poliomyelitis. Quadriplegia.

HERBAL - The plant Karwinskia belongs to the Rhamnacae family, it is found in the northern states of Mexico. It is known locally under different names including Tullidora, the “little coyote,” “wild capuli,” “little black rod,” and “cacachila.” It is a small shrub, but can grow up to 9 meters in some places. The leaves are elliptical or oblong, rounded at the end, the flowers are small, yellow-green in color. The fruits are small in clusters from 6 to 9 mm in diameter, dark violet in color, usually containing four seeds of which only two are reproductive. The seeds are toxic, causing paralysis of the limbs, which becomes generalized and can terminate in death. They contain a fatty acid, a yellow substance and a glucoside, which is the cause of the paralysis of the motor nerves.

HOMEOPATHIC - The clinical observation of the mass intoxication of one hundred and six soldiers constitutes the first Memoirs of Dr. Castillo Najeros, published in Mexico in 1918. A homeopathic proving of Karw-h. was carried out by Luis de Legarreta and published in 1961 in his Materia Medica of Mexican Plants. Karw-h. is a remedy with neurotrophic action, paralyzing the motor nerves. Flaccid paralysis, which increases, ending in quadriplegia. Ascending progressive paralysis, flaccid and painless, predominantly on the left side, with amyotrophy of the lower limbs. Acute spinal paralysis, sub-acute atrophic spinal paralysis. Chronic anterior paralysis. Loss of contractility and mobility of the leg muscles. Reduction of tendons reflexes and skin. Paresis of paralysis, rising to the upper limbs and muscles of the thorax and diaphragm. Paralysis of the lips, tongue and larynx. No diminution of reflexes of the bladder and intestines. Poliomyelitis. Acute and sub-acute, polioencephalitis. Bedsores.

Head - Severe headache. Constant headache with feeling of heaviness.

Ears - Buzzing in both ears.

Stomach - Nausea with vomiting. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Lath. - Weakness, then paralysis of the lower limbs with exaggerated reflexes and complaints of sensitivity. (2) Hydroph. - Paralysis with muscular dystrophy. (3) Plb. - Rapid emaciation, progressive paralysis of the limbs with amyotrophy and starting in the extensor muscles. REFERENCES - Julian.

Abdomen - Lack of intestinal inactivity, partial obstruction.

Rectum - Diarrhea in the first 48 hours, followed by intestinal paralysis with difficulty in evacuating.

Heart - Pulse slower with fever.

Back - Cramping pains in the back.

Limbs - Progressive paralysis. Cramping pains in the arms and legs. Loss of contractility and mobility of the leg muscles. Lungs - Dyspnea, which becomes worse and can end in respiratory paralysis. Bronchopneumonia, paralytic alveolitis, which can cause fatal asphyxia. Difficult speech.

Skin - Bedsores.

name: Kerosolenum
author: Murphy
constitution: Anesthesia. Asphyxia. Convulsions. Delirium. Ecstasy. Laughter.
keynote: PHARMACY - keroso. Kerosolenum. Kerosene. One of the lighter products, obtained by distillation from the crude oil. Kerosolene being the trade name given by the “Downer Kerosene Oil Company,” nearly identical with gasoline. Solution in rectified spirit. Historical dose: All…
full:
PHARMACY - keroso. Kerosolenum. Kerosene. One of the lighter products, obtained by distillation from the crude oil. Kerosolene being the trade name given by the “Downer Kerosene Oil Company,” nearly identical with gasoline. Solution in rectified spirit. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anesthesia. Asphyxia. Convulsions. Delirium. Ecstasy. Laughter.

HOMEOPATHIC - The effects of Keroso. have been observed on workmen, andexperi- ments have been made with it for the purpose of testing its anesthetic properties. Keroso. causes a pleasurable kind of intoxication, but too much muscular rigidity, asphyxia and intermittent pulse to render it a safe anesthetic. Moderate convulsions. Laughter was noticed in two cases and this should prove an indication in some kinds of delirium and insanity. Partially or wholly insensible, but rapidly recovers when brought into open air. Insensibility complete, though eyes not closed. MIND - Sense of complete loneliness. Insensible, with inclination to laugh. Cannot keep still Chest - Breathing checked during convulsions due to rigid contraction of chest muscles.

Head - Peculiar lightness of head. Slight headache.

Eyes - Eyes a little unnaturally open and staring.

Face - Momentary dusky redness of face at each convulsion (as in epilepsy).

Limbs - Weakness of the limbs. Modalities - Better in open air.

Pulse - Accelerated intermittent, volume diminished during insensibility.

Temperature - Some sweating. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Petr., Paraf., Benzin. REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Kissingen Aqua
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Worse in the forenoon, at night, on waking, while reading and writing. Vertigo worse while eating. Toothache worse during menstruation. COMMENTS - Constantin James, recorded in Allen, noted that the dose is from three to six glasses of the water in the morning and two glasses at 4 p.m., but the general rule is that no more it to be drunk than the stomach can digest without difficulty. In the first days, appetite and force is increase, but as the water is absorbed the effects become general. Then an elimina- tory “crisis” comes on. The stools become brownish, loose, bilious. The urine is turbid, depositing a sediment which rapidly putrefies. The secretion of the bronchial, genital, and ocular mucus membranes, as well as the skin, is increased and changed in character. Moral and physical prostration, old and long-forgotten troubles reappear. This crisis, which appears in the first or second week, soon disappears of itself and the cure proceeds. In one case, a patient vomited blood after the disappearance of a hemorrhoidal flux. Kiss, restored the latter, and the bloodvomiting ceased. Trembling, pulsation of the whole body. Weariness. Stitches here and there. Muscle volitantes. Noises in the ears. Chills, heat and perspiration. Tearful disposition, especially at 10 a.m. “If he only looks at any one he must weep.” RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Nat-m. - weeping disposition, chill at 10 a.m., catarrh, constipation. (2) Ant-c. - saburral condition. (3) Urt-u. - gout. (4) Ferr-pic. - warts and corns. REFERENCES - Clarke..

HOMEOPATHIC - Kissingen water has been proved by Carl Preu and observations have been made on its general effects. Nat-m. is the leading solid ingredient, existing in the proportion of 5.82 out of a total of 8.55 in the 1,000. It compares with Nauheim, Kreutznach and, to some extent, with Vichy. Useful for abdominal affections, especially a catarrhal condition of intestinal atony. Convalescence from typhoid and gallbladder affections. Disorders of the liver, spleen and intestinal glands. Gout where the asthmatic principle appears to be repercussed upon the abdominal viscera, for then the waters draw it out to the joints. The dosage must be managed with extreme prudence, too much can bring on a true attack of gout.

PHARMACY - kou. Kousso. Brayera anthelminthica. Hagenia abyssinica. Kuso. Cosso. N. O. Rosacee. Abyssinia. Infusion of dried flowers. Tincture of flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Miscarriage. Tapeworm. Worms.

HERBAL - The flowers of Kousso are a favorite remedy for tapeworm with the natives of Abyssinia. The use of them in European practice for that purpose has led to the observation of the few recorded symptoms, among which thirst, nausea and vomiting are prominent. In one case miscarriage was caused. To use as a vermifuge, take a quarter of an ounce of the dried flowers and boil in four ounces of distilled water. Infuse for fifteen minutes without straining. The powder is to be taken with the infusion in the morning, fasting. Two such drafts may be given. It is best to give a purgative before and an hour or two after the draft. Nausea and vomiting. Vertigo. Precordial anxiety, slowing and irregular pulse, delirium and collapse. Rapid and extreme prostration.

HOMEOPATHIC - Alexander Milne remarked “Though Kousso leads to the expulsion of the worm, it seems not to improve the morbid condition which favors its production.” The prostration caused by the treatment is so great that Milne advises a course of Cinch, and Ferr. to follow. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cuc-c„ Gran., Fil. (2) Kam., an efficient remedy for tapeworm in 30-60 minims of tincture taken in cinnamon water. REFERENCES - Clarke.
