full:
PHARMACY - oci. Ocimum canum. Brazilian alfavaca. Hoary basil. Ocimum incanescens. Ocimum fluminense. N. O. Labiate. Portuguese. Tincture of fresh leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Allergies. Arthritis. Belching. Breasts, painful. Bubo. Diarrhea. Edema. Gravel, urinary. Headaches. Herpes. Hiccoughs. Kidney, diseases. Kidney, pain. Kidney, stones. Nausea. Pyelonephritis. Salpingitis. Urine, abnormal. Vagina, prolapse. Vulvitis.

HERBAL - All the members of the Ocimum genus are aromatic. The Sweet or Common Basil, Ocimum basilicum, is one of the best known. Mure reported that it is used in Brazil as a specific for diseases of the kidneys, bladder and urethra. P. C. Majumdar added that Ocimum sanctum is the sacred tulsi of India and that the Kabirajes use it in diseases of the liver and bilious remittent fevers.

HOMEOPATHIC - Oci. is useful in diseases of kidneys, uterus, bladder and urethra. Kidney pain with violent vomiting every fifteen minutes. Wrings one's hands and moans and cries all the time. Kidney colic, especrally on the right side. Pronounced symptoms of kidney stones. Uric acid diathesis. Red sand in the urine. Red urine with brick-dust sediment after the attack. The urine may be saffron color or thick, purulent with an intolerable smell of musk. Febrile condition, shivering, sweating and with congestive headache. Vomiting, cries tossing about and wringing hands. Arthritis. Allergies. Pain in the left testicle. Prolapsed vagina. Vulvarcongestion. Breast congestion. Swelling of inguinal glands and breasts. Excessive sensitiveness of the breasts and pain on nursing. MIND - Difficulty concentrating. Confused state. Anxiety.

Head - Stinging pain in the head. Pain in the head, as if a nail were being driven in, ameliorated by pressure. Pulsating, throbbing headache. Headaches followed by shivering.

Eyes - Blurred vision.

Ears - Boil on the meatus of the right ear. Noise heard painfully in the ears.

Mouth - Lips dry, face red. Tongue furred, yellow, yellowish-white with a brown spot in the center. Toothache on the right, ame liorated by pressing the teeth together. Nose - Nasal congestion.

Abdomen - Abdomen distended, painful on the right side during menses. Glands in the groin swollen. Edema on the right side of the testes or labia. Breasts - Constrictive tension in the breasts. Breasts feel full and tense, itching. Neuralgic pains in the breast. Nipples painful and sensitive to the touch. Congestive pains in the breasts as after nursing. Puerperal mastitis.

Rectum - Constipation with dry, hard, evil-smelling, yellow or greenish stools. Diarrhea several times a day.

Urine - High acidity, formation of spike crystals of uric acid. Brick-dust red or yellow sediment. Red sand in saffron colored urine. \Jrinefoul-smelling with odor of musk. Turbid, thick, purulent, bloody urine. Urinary complaints with proteinuria. Scanty urine, which aggravates. Vertigo - Vertigo on rising and on sitting down. COMMENTS - Majumdar related the case of a medical man, 45. Majumdar was sent for at 4 a.m. one morning and found the patient in great agony, pain in upper part of region of right kidney, extending downwards and forwards to pubes. Constant vomiting, bilious, acid tossing about without any relief. After Calc., Lyc., Sep., Sars. and Berb. had been given in vain, Oci. 3x gave immediate relief and no other remedy was required. Majumdar also noted the case of a man, 50, with excruciating pain in his left kidney, for which he had received opium under allopathic treatment without relief. Majumdar saw the patient on the sixth day of the attack. The suffering was extreme, vomiting of bile, constant nausea, bowels constipated. Oci. 3x, one drop every three hours, speedily gave relief, and two days later two small uric acid stones were passed. There was no recurrence. Clarke published two cases. The first concerned a man, 27, who was seized with violent pains of a leaden character in the right side of the abdomen, every three or four weeks. The pains commenced in morning, lasted twelve to fifteen hours. For four hours from commencement of attack the pain steadily increased, culminating in vomiting, first of sour fluid, then slime, then a fluid like coffee. After the vomiting there was some relief of pain. Urine contained no sediment. The attacks had lasted seven years. At first they began in the evening. There was a history of epilepsy in the family, and as a child the patient had three fits. Oci. 200c, one dose, was given and there were no more attacks for about two years. On their recurrence Oci. failed to control them, but Dios, tincture succeeded. In the second case, a woman, 24, had severe pain in her right flank shooting around to her back. Frequent urination, sometimes depositing clots. Terebe. 3c gave some relief, but it was not permanent. Oci. 200c, a few globules in water, a teaspoonful every two days, rapidly relieved the symptoms and cleared up the case. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In kidney colic, Berb., Dios., Coloc., Calc., Lyc. (2) Berb.. Hedeo., Lyc., Urt-u. (3) Pareir., Coloc., Tab. (4) In painful breasts, Lac-c., Bor. (5) Crot-h., Phel. (6) Prolapsed vagina, Staph. Followed well by: Dios. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Julian. Phatak.

Male - Pain in the testes. Tenderness, heat and swelling of the left testicle. Increase, then diminution of sexual desire. Absence of erection.

Female - Menses late, short or abundant. Whitish-yellow leucorrhea. Vulvitis. Vulva swollen, darting pain in labia majora. Vaginal prolapse. Salpingitis. Food - Lack of appetite. Desire for cold drinks during fever.

Chest - Chest painful on right side. Dry cough in the evening and early morning. Copious sputum. Constitutions - Allergic constitutions. Psoric constitutions. Neuro-arthritic temperament.

Skin - Herpes. Eczematous eruptions. Stomach - Belching, hiccoughs. Nausea.

Modalities - Better in a room, in rainy, humid weather. Worse in the morning, from cold, right side.

Kidneys - Pyelonephritis. Cramps in kidneys. Kidney colic on the right side with vomiting ever quarter of an hour with calling out. Restlessness and groaning. Pronounced symptoms of kidney stones, especially of right side. Stones in the bladder. Tenesmus of the bladder. Sore pain in ureters. Burning pain in the urethra during urination. Urine abundant, burning.

Temperature - Shivers, fever and lack of thirst. Profuse sweating with strong odor. Fever of the tertian or quartan type.

PHARMACY - oci-s. Ocimum sanctum. Holy Basil. Tulsi. N. O. Labiate. Brazil. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aphthae. Asthma. Bites. Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia. Catarrh. Colds. Constipation. Cough. Delirium. Diarrhea. Headache. Hiccoughs. Influenza. Intermittent fevers. Leucorrhea. Memory, weak. Ophthalmia. Ozaena. Pneumonia. Ringworm. Ulcers. Urethritis.

HERBAL - Ayurvedic physicians like Cha- raka, Harita, Chakradatta, Bangasena, and others have found Ocimum sanctum very efficacious in cough, cold, catarrh, nose affections, ozaena, scorpion bites, remittent and intermittent fevers and constipation. The medicated oil is used as drops, in the ears in earache and purulent discharges, and into the nose in ozaena. The leaves, with lime juice, are rubbed over ringworm. The seeds are mucilaginous and used as a diuretic in scanty urine and cough. The leaves are expectorant, and given, sweetened with honey, in chronic cough, especially in children. The expressed juice of the herb has traditionally been administered to children who are attacked with catarrh, cough with fever and constipation, with very gratifying and beneficial results.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ocimum canum is a species of this shrub which grows abundantly in Brazil. Dr. Mure, who proved and introduced it, noted that it is largely used in Brazil “as a specific for diseases of the kidneys, bladder, and urethra.” He gave a short list of nineteen symptoms which are partly clinical and partly pathogenetic. Dr. Mure's experience was several times verified by several noted homeopaths. Drs. Pramada Prasanna Biswas of Pabna, Bengal, N. Sinha and N. C. Ghosh have made provings of this drug. MIND - Memory weak. Forgetfulness. Mistakes in talking. Difficulty concentrating. Prostration and drowsiness. Patient falls asleep while answering questions. Child is peevish and cries, does not like to lie in bed. Irregular delirium, disturbed.

Head - Headache as from a nail. Heavy, throbbing pain as if thousand nails were being driven into it, relieved by pressure. Giddiness of head, worse while walking, likes to keep quiet, relieved by wrapping up the head. Heat on the vertex, relieved by pouring cold water on the head or by fanning.

Eyes - Eyes red. Pain in the eyes, lachrymation, eye complaints due to nasal catarrh. Ophthalmia. Foggy vision. Mist before eyes, especially when fixing them on something.

Ears - Watery secretion from the ear. Offensive pus from the ears. Ears painful due to nasal catarrh. Hot flushes come out from the ears. Noises in the ears, loud sound appears to be very painful. Shortness of hearing.

Nose - Nasal obstruction. Nasal catarrh associated with frequent sneezing, white or yellow secretions. Coryza. Watery discharge from the nose. Nostrils ulcer ated. Nosebleeds.

Face - Face red or pale with reddish hue. Flushed and hot.

Mouth - Lips bright red. Lips dry and black as if burnt. Watery salivation or spitting from the mouth. Putrid and bitter taste in mouth. Ulcer, aphthae in mouth. Ulcer in mouth and tongue of children. The tongue is bright red or its edges and sides are red and the middle portion is deeply coated. Toothache, better pressing the gums together, warmth, pressure.

Throat - Pain in the throat while walking or during cough. Pain and difficulty in swallowing. Redness, ulceration of throat. Glairy phlegm. Enlargement of tonsils. Hoarseness. Voice gets changed. Vertigo - Vertigo on rising. COMMENTS - Oci-s. has an assured place in the treatment of influenza and in common nasal catarrh. Remittent fever associated with cough, cold or diarrhea, pneumonia, broncho-pneumonia, bronchitis and asthma. Typhoid fever or fever associated with delirium, comatose condition, prostration, and falls into slumber or drowsiness while answering questions (Bapt.). Fever in influenza, associated with cough, acute pains in the body, bone pains, soreness of the muscles, and terrible headache (Eup-per.). Fevers associated with cough, cold and diarrhea, especially in children. Fevers prevalent in rainy season, winter or spring. Intermittent fever. Fever with thirst or absence of thirst. Fever comes on in the afternoon with extreme chilliness, with shivering. Chilliness, even when exposed to the sun. Hands and the feet become cold and do not become warm easily. Numbness and tingling in hands and feet. Extreme heat and flushes of heat felt over the face and eyes during hot stage. Burning sensation in the palms of hands and soles of feet, relieved by cold breeze or placing cold water on the head. Sweat with heat. Heat, sweat, and chilliness may appear alternately. Sweat, delirium, drowsiness or comatose condition. Remittent fevers of children, fever during dentition period, diarrhea and worm affections (Cina.). Wormcomplaints of children, fretful and peevish, start from sleep, and do not allow the physician to examine them. The children become awfully peevish, always cry, become quiet while they are being carried (Cham.). Aching pains, in the feet and legs. Pains are felt all over the body. Offensive and filthy odor. Putrefaction. Contagious and infectious diseases caused by bacteria or bacilli. Terrible headache. Headache due to congestion, common cold, influenza or fever. Headache relieved by application of cold water on the head or by fanning the head. Better from keeping quiet or wrapping the head with a cloth, worse while walking or by motion. Face is flushed and hot. lips are red and parched, eyes are drowsy. Pain in the throat, felt while swallowing, coughing or sneezing. Redness inside the throat, both tonsils are enlarged. Offensive smell comes out of the mouth, offensive salivation. Tongue is red or reddish and shining at the edges with yellow or brown coating in the middle (Bapt.). Aphthae. Putrid ulcer in the mouth and teeth. Toothache, with terrible pains, worse at night, from touch or cold. Eyes congested, red, with lachrymation, especially in cases of the common cold. Watery discharges and sticky discharges. Ophthalmia, ophthalmia neonatorum. Earache and purulent discharges from the ear. Shortness of hearing. Difficult respiration. Asthma, the patient cannot lie on the back. Bends forward and supports the head with the hands, the elbows resting on the knees or leans forward and puts the head on the hands lain flat on such support (Aral., Lob., Blatta.). Asthma of children. Gastric and intestinal catarrh, with inflammation of the intestinal mucous membrane, fever and diarrhea. Pain in the region of liver and spleen. Abdomen distended, distension does not abate in spite of stools passed. After gurgling in the stomach, copious watery and offensive stools appear. Diarrhea with fever and cold, cough, pneumonia, broncho-pneumonia and bronchitis. Involuntary stools. Irregular, long lasting menses. Leucorrhea. Uterine complications after delivery. Terribly offensive lochia, of unnatural color, long lasting. Discharge mixed with mucus, is pus-like and like washing of fish. Ocimum sanctum is supposed to drive away mosquitoes; it may prevent malarial fevers if cultivated near a house. REFERENCES Ghose.

Stomach - Want of appetite. Thirstlessness during chill. Eructations, Hiccough.

Abdomen - Abdomen distended. Heaviness in abdomen. Griping pain in the abdomen. Pain is felt over the region of liver and spleen. Pain in the right iliac region. Hepatic pain. Gurgling sound can be felt on pressure.

Rectum - Constipation. Incomplete stools. Diarrhea with high fever. Diarrhea during rainy season and autumn. Stools liquid, copious, watery, very offensive. Yellowish or greenish liquid stools. Mucus or bloody or streaked with blood. Involuntary stools during high fever.

Male - Troublesome erections. Sexual desire increased or decreased. Impotency.

Female - Menses too late. Metrorrhagia. Leucorrhea alternating with bloody discharge. Leucorrhea offensive, profuse, white, yellow. Metritis after childbirth. Profuse bloody discharges after delivery. Lochia offensive, profuse, fetid, lasts for a long period. Sexual desire diminished or increased.

Chest - Pains are felt on both sides of the chest, worse while coughing or sneezing. Pleuritic pains in the chest. Pain is felt in the middle of sternum. Patient cannot lie quiet in bed.

Limbs - Aching pains, better from pressure. Lungs - Asthmatic attack, wheezing and rattling sound felt in the chest. Asthma better from bending head forward, rocking. Asthma of infants and children. Croupy cough. Hacking cough, profuse expectoration.

Skin - Skin disease.

Kidneys - Kidney colic. Urethritis. Desire to urinate off and on. Burning in the urethra while urinating. Yellow like saffron, urine. Discharge of mucus with urine. Involuntary urination of the children.

Perspiration - Offensive sweats.

Temperature - Chills and fever. Influenza. Remittent and intermittent fevers. Bilious, continued fever. Quartan fever, tertian fevers. Typhus, typhoid fever.

name: Oenanthe Crocata
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Worse from water, injury, sexual and menstrual disturbances. Pressure aggravates pain in throat, but ameliorates deep pain in thorax. Swallowing causes soreness of throat..
constitution: Albuminuria. Amenorrhea. Breast, pain. Coma. Convulsions. Cough. Delirium tremens. Diaphragm, spasm. Epilepsy. Esophagus, stricture. Gastroenteritis. Hysterical, epilepsy. Ichthyosis. Insanity. Leprosy. Menstrual, convulsions. Nausea. Priapism. Puerperal, convulsions. Sciatica. Speech, lost. Status, epilepticus. Stomatitis. Strokes. Tetanus. Tongue, swollen. Tongue, ulcerated. Tympanites. Vertigo.
keynote:
PHARMACY - oena. Oenanthe crocata. Water dropwort. Hemlock drop-wort. N. O. Umbel- liferae. Marshy places. Tincture of fresh root at time of flowering. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Amenorrhea. Breast, pain. Coma. Convulsions. Cough.…
full:
PHARMACY - oena. Oenanthe crocata. Water dropwort. Hemlock drop-wort. N. O. Umbel- liferae. Marshy places. Tincture of fresh root at time of flowering. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Amenorrhea. Breast, pain. Coma. Convulsions. Cough. Delirium tremens. Diaphragm, spasm. Epilepsy. Esophagus, stricture. Gastroenteritis. Hysterical, epilepsy. Ichthyosis. Insanity. Leprosy. Menstrual, convulsions. Nausea. Priapism. Puerperal, convulsions. Sciatica. Speech, lost. Status, epilepticus. Stomatitis. Strokes. Tetanus. Tongue, swollen. Tongue, ulcerated. Tympanites. Vertigo. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Oenanthe crocata is one of the most poisonous of the Umbelliferae, and many accidents have occurred from the use of the root in mistake for parsnips and of the leaves in salads and soups. These have fumishedmany of the symptoms of the pathogenesis. Epileptic convulsions, worse during menstruation and pregnancy. Epilepsy, utters a loud cry before falling backward. Status epilepticus. Face swollen, convulsive twitching of facial muscles, foaming at mouth, lockjaw. Cold as if dead during convulsions, noise in throat as if being choked. Burning heat. Numbness. Legs stretches straight out. Skin affections, especially leprosy and ichthyosis. Rosy red blotches on face and chest, arms, abdomen. Profuse, offensive sweat. Burning in throat and stomach, nausea and vomiting. Obstinate vomiting for days, not relieved by anything. MIND - Epileptic condition at periods when menses are due, in amenorrhea. Epileptic insanity. Coma after convulsions. Sudden and complete loss of consciousness. Insanity, hallucinations. Delirium tremens. Furious delirium. Tendency to cry over little things. Averse to be questioned.

Head - Hyperemia of brain, extravasation and serous exudation. Pains all over head, dizzy. Headache and giddiness. Violent pain in head. Apoplectic conditions. Suddenly falls down backward. Hair fell off.

Eyes - Sunken, full and projecting, inflamed. Redness. Pupils first contracted, then dilated. Eyes turned upward and inward, firmly fixed. Vision disturbed, obscured.

Nose - Nosebleeds.

Face - Countenance livid, rose-colored spots on face. Lips blue. Eyes fixed, pupils dilated. Rapid, convulsive twitching of facial muscles. Trismus, foaming at mouth, locked jaws. Risus sardonicus. Food - Total loss of appetite with debility. Thirst, craves cold drinks, evening. Cannot bear to drink anything hot.

Mouth - Mouth dry and parched. Foaming at mouth, bloody mucus. Excoriation inflammation, blisters. Convulsive movement of teeth. Loss of speech.

Throat - Burning and constriction in larynx. Pharyngitis. Violent constriction and burning in the throat. Pressure on throat gives pain, sore when swallowing. Power of swallowing lost.

Stomach - Tender stomach. Burning heat in stomach. Esophagitis. Distressing hiccough. Nausea, better if vomiting occurs. Vomit is clear water liquid, blood. Vomiting and diarrhea.

Abdomen - Great tenderness, slightest touch on any part of abdomen causes great pain. Distended with colic pains. Gastroenteritis with violent pain and vomiting. Tympanites with the convulsions.

Rectum - Involuntary stool, diarrhea. Sensations - As if a bug creeping under the skin about the waist, worse touch of clothes.

Male - Priapism.

Chest - Pain in right side under the ribs. Chest firmly fixed. Pleuritic exudation. Lungs hyperemic, hepatized in spots.

Heart - Pain in region of heart. Pulse is small, feeble, irregular and scarcely perceptible, accelerated before the fit.

Back - Pain along spinal column. Intense action of dorsal and lumbar muscles, opisthotonos. Breasts - Swollen breasts. Pain in breast. Nipples painful to least contact. Causations - Menstrual disturbances. Injuries.

Limbs - Numbness and feebleness of limbs. Pain along crural and sciatic nerves, commencing in back. Cold hands and feet. Numbness of hand and foot. Cramps in calves. Arms flexed at elbow in a right angle. Hands clenched during tetanus. Convulsions, opisthotonos. Lungs - Spasms of the diaphragm. Heavy, spasmodic, stertorous breathing. Tickling cough with rattling in the lower part of the chest. Cough, worse at night, excited by tickling at top of throat. Rattling in the chest, sputa thick, heavy, white and yellow. Thick, frothy expectoration, reddish, bloody, white.

Sleep - Much yawning. Drowsy. In a deep sleep, snoring loudly and moaning. Roused with difficulty.

Skin - Rose colored rash on face, chest, arms and abdomen. Loss of nails and hair.

Modalities - Worse from water, injury, sexual and menstrual disturbances. Pressure aggravates pain in throat, but ameliorates deep pain in thorax. Swallowing causes soreness of throat.

Tongue - Tongue sore, swollen and protruded. Tongue slightly furred, raw at tip, ulcerated at edges. Tongue clean, moist, trembling. Tongue half bitten through. Vertigo - Vertigo with falling. Vertigo with nausea, vomiting, syncope and convulsions. COMMENTS - Oena. is a valuable con vulsive remedy, useful in epileptiform, puerperal and uremia convulsions. Hormonal epilepsy, since or during pregnancy, in childbirth, abortion, miscarriage, menstrual period, amenorrhea, and menopause. Epileptic symptoms since birth control pills. Epilepsy after vaccinations. Epilepsy after errors in diet. Severe, violent epileptic attacks. Sudden attacks (Bell.). Grand mal, petit mal, and particularly statusepilepticus attacks. Risus sardonicus, a fixed smile. Feeling of dread and anxiety before attacks. Can hear bells ringing before. Followed by deep sleep or coma. Vomiting after epilepsy. Vertigo during the menstrual period. Toxemia during pregnancy with convulsions and protein in the urine. All symptoms are worse from water and drinking. D. A. Baldwin of Englewood, N. J., entirely controlled the convulsions in a young man of 16 with Oena. Dr. Ord reported a case of petit mal cured with Oean. 3x. In a South American homeopathic journal a Dr. Rappaz reported the cure of a case of three years' standing with increasing seizures with the remedy in doses ranging from the 6c to 12c. Henderson reported the cure of an epilepsy case of 9 years standing, where the patient was almost idiotic, the convulsions were relieved and the mental condition was greatly relieved and improved. In two other cases equally satisfactory results were had. S. H. Talcott, in the report of the Middletown Asylum. 1893, noted that Oena. possesses a marked power in epilepsy. He stated that it makes the attacks less frequent, less violent and improves the mental state of the patient. Talcott prescribed it in the tincture, 1 to 6 drops daily. F. H. Fisk reported the cure of a case that had lasted two years with the tincture. This patient was having 6 to 10 attacks daily during the last month before Fisk took the case. Dr. Garrison of Easton, Penn, reported a case of reflex uterine of hystero-epilepsy in which the Oena. 2x acted promptly. J. S. Cooper of Chillicothe, Ohio, reported the cure of a case of 25 years standing with Oena. 4x. J. Ritchie Horner reported that the Oena. 3x greatly modified the attacks in a woman who had the disease over 20 years and who, for the two months previous, had a convulsion daily. W. A. Dunn reported a cure of a young woman of 16 who had been epileptic for 7 years, having as many as 4 or 5 attacks during a night. The remedy caused these attacks to disappear entirely. The girl commenced menstruating at age 12, so the establishment of the menses had nothing to do with the cure. Charles A. Wilson of San Antonio, Texas, reported a number of cases cured with Oean. 3x, and the same potency greatly lessened the number of seizures in others. Dr. Purdon of the University of Dublin, related a case of epilepsy cured with this remedy in 1 to 6 drop doses several times a day. F. E. Howard, in a case that had 3 or 4 attacks a week, gave 5 drops of the tincture every two hours, which caused violent pains in the head, but complete recovery followed on reducing the dose. McClellan of New Jersey told of a case of his in which a young woman, 19, of a very healthy family, who had never menstruated and had become almost idiotic in consequence. At the periods when the menses should have come on there were epileptiform seizures of minor intensity. The state of mind was such that after taking the best advice in Paris and the States without avail, the patient was about to be put away. Oean. was given and the next period passed without any epileptic symptoms. But there was no sign of the flow. Bell, was given and at the next period, the flow came on and the patient's mind was entirely restored. J. S. Cooper related the case of a clergyman in attendance on one of the Federal generals at the battle of Gettysburg, who was wounded in the forehead by a fragment of shell, taken prisoner and kept in prison twenty months. On his release he was quite a wreck and soon began to have light epileptic seizures, which gradually got worse. When seen by J. S. Cooper, twenty-five years later, he was having four or five fits a day, could write his name and at time would take to his heels and run four or five miles into the country before he could be caught. Oean. 4c, five drops every four hours, was prescribed. After the first dose he had a very bad fit. The dose was then diminished. He began to improve and in less than a year was in perfect health. Oean., was not taken continuously, but when he “felt nervous” he would take a few doses. F. H. Fish cured a girl, 16, sanguine, well grown, who at eight began to have fits of absentmindedness at irregular intervals. At 12, menstruation commenced; at 14, epileptic seizures occurred, having no relation to the menstrual periods. The fits were so severe that sixty to one hundred grains of potassium bromide were required to keep them under control. Oean. tincture was given, five drops in six ounces of water, a teaspoonful every three hours, and later less often. She had not another spasm, lost her absentmindedness and became cheerful and active. W. K. Fowler reported a case of a teamster, 60, who had gotten into a fight nineteen years before from which he had three ribs broken and was struck in stomach with the butt of a gun. Two weeks later, he had pneumonia on the injured side, and after that, epileptic seizures. Before the attacks he had a pain in the stomach going through to the spine and pain in the second cervical vertebra. Attacks were induced by worry and by becoming very tired. He had severe attacks when the day's work was finished. Oean. was given on discs, four discs every three hours for a month. After this there was only one slight attack after a hard day's work during the four months he was under observation. Several cured cases of epilepsy have been reported in which Oena. alternated with Sil. or some other drug, but they need not be given as it was unclear which remedy cured. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cic., Kali-br. (2) Phel., Con. (3) In epilepsy, Bufo. (4) In priapism, Pic-ac. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Kidneys - Painful urination. Urine copious, dark, turbid, reddish, with thick yellow sediment.

Temperature - Extreme coldness, loss of animal heat. Deadly cold and pale. Face and limbs cold and blue. Burning heat that mounted to head. Slight fever with pain at pit of stomach. Profuse, offensive sweat, accompanies symptoms.

keynote:

CLINICAL - Cholera infantum. Diarrhea. Hydrocephalous. Nervous exhaustion. Paralysis.

HOMEOPATHIC -…
full:
PHARMACY - oeno. Oenothera biennis. Large evening primrose. Tree primrose. N. O. Onagracee. North America. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cholera infantum. Diarrhea. Hydrocephalous. Nervous exhaustion. Paralysis.

HOMEOPATHIC - T. Riker Nuted recorded a proving on a woman who took Oeno. twice, the first, a teaspoonful, the second, 30 drops of the liquid extract for the relief of a wearisome feeling of mental and physical oppression. On each occasion, notably the first, distinct poisoning symptoms were developed. General paralysis of mental and bodily forces, with copious and easy evacuations of bowels and bladder, followed by relief of the general symptoms. General numbness, general warm sweat with urgent desire to urinate, better after evacuation of bowels and bladder. Effortless diarrhea. Farrington gave the indication exhausting, watery diarrhea without effort with nervous exhaustion, even incipient hydrocephalous. Hurd cured a man, 65, who had “severe pains in his stomach after meals for over two years” with 25 drop doses of the tincture. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In diarrhea, Ip., Gnaph., Nuphar. (2) In better from copious urination, Ign., Gels. (3) In better after stool, Bry., Colch., Coloc., Crot., Oxyt., Rhus-t., Spig., Sulph. (4) Paralytic symptoms, Gels. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Oleander
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from looking sideways, brandy. Squinting helps headache. Worse in open air, draft, undressing after nursing. Worse rubbing, scratching, friction of clothes. Worse rest, looking sideways. Rising up aggravates headache, vertigo. Stooping causes pain over heart..
constitution: Brain, disorders. Eczema. Fainting. Headaches. Hyperesthesia. Lienteria. Memory, weakened. Numbness. Nursing, disorders. Palpitations. Paralysis. Perichondritis. Rheumatism. Scalp, eruptions. Spasms. Spine, disorders. Strabismus. Tongue, coated. Vertigo.
keynote:
PHARMACY - olnd. Oleander. Rose laurel. Nerium oleander. N. O. Apocynaceae. South Europe, North Africa, West Asia. Thrives best in moist ground. Tincture of the leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Brain, disorders. Eczema. Fainting. Headaches.…
full:
PHARMACY - olnd. Oleander. Rose laurel. Nerium oleander. N. O. Apocynaceae. South Europe, North Africa, West Asia. Thrives best in moist ground. Tincture of the leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Brain, disorders. Eczema. Fainting. Headaches. Hyperesthesia. Lienteria. Memory, weakened. Numbness. Nursing, disorders. Palpitations. Paralysis. Perichondritis. Rheumatism. Scalp, eruptions. Spasms. Spine, disorders. Strabismus. Tongue, coated. Vertigo.

HERBAL - In the Cap de Verde Islands, the petals of oleander blossoms are used with dried orange-peel in all kinds of fevers to promote perspiration and drive out the rash.

HOMEOPATHIC - Olnd., which is one of the remedies proved by Hahnemann, has been recognized as a powerful poison from antiquity. In animals poisoned by it. the heart becomes paralyzed, first the auricles, then the entire heart. Goullon referred to poisoning cases in which “anguish inflammation of the stomach, diarrhea, swoons,” and even death had occurred. “Palpitations of the heart, anxiety insomnia and unconsciousness,” were observed by Petrus de Alvano, and Morgagni noted “vomiting, thirst, slumbering, speechlessness and death.” Goullon also quoted instances of suffering from exhalations of the flowers and even from the plants when not in flower. Marked action on the skin, heart and nervous system. Paralytic conditions with cramp like contractions of upper limbs. Hemiplegia. Paralytic rigidity. Paresis after infantile paralysis. General crampings. Numbness. Sopor. Weakness with trembling in nursing women. Sense of vibrations. Difficult articulation, or unable to speak. Emptiness in stomach and chest after eating, betterbrandy. Involuntary discharges. MIND - Memory weak, slow perception. Morose. Peevish. Sadness with lack of confidence and power. Melancholy with obstinate constipation.

Head - Numb feeling. Dull, unable to think. Indolence. Pain in brain, as if head would burst. Headache better by looking crossways, sideways or squinting. Corrosive itching on forehead and edge of hair, worse heat. Eruption on scalp. Humid, fetid spots behind ears (Graph., Petr.) and occiput, with red, rough, herpetic spots in front.

Eyes - Sensation as if eyes were drawn back into the head. Lachrymation, when reading. Double vision. Can see objects only when looking at them sideways.

Face - Pale, sunken, with blue rings around eyes (Ph-ac.). Numb upper lip. Lowerjaw trembles when yawning.

Mouth - Toothache only when masticating. Tongue numb. Loss of speech.

Throat - As if a cool wind blowing on throat (left). Vertigo - Vertigo for a long time before paralysis. Vertigo, worse looking fixedly at an object or looking down, turning to either side in bed with diplopia. COMMENTS - A young man, 18, fell sick, had attacks of vertigo, suffered from great weakness of the muscles, headache better in evening, worse every morning after waking, which was a difficult process. He had a pale face, white-coated tongue, slow pulse. On leaving for change of air he soon got quite well, but ill again as soon as he returned. Some oleanders in his bedroom were then suspected by his doctor, and on their removal all the trouble vanished. The doctor recalled that when he was a student he had some oleanders before his windows and in autumn, when the nights were cold, he took them into his bedroom. On waking in the morning, he had a heavy head and sensation of weariness, could only leave his bed by great exertion. As soon as be put his foot to the ground, he was seized with vertigo and reeled. Having traced this to the oleanders, he purposely repeated the experiment, always with the same result. Weak memory and slow perception. Pres- sive and stupefying headache. Pressure as if a hundredweight were pressing brain forward and as if everything would come out at forehead. Headaches better by looking cross- eyed or looking sideways. Cloudiness of vision, worse by looking sideways. Momentary loss of sight. Eyes distorted. Strabismus. Functional paralysis. The left side is most affected, violent contraction of muscles, worse left side. Numbness of upper and lower limbs. Digestion is paralyzed, the food passes completely undigested. Gastro-enteritis. Involuntary evacuation of feces and urine. Infants soil their diapers every time they pass flatus. “Trembling after nursing” in nursing women. The skin is very sensitive and easily chafed and chapped. Olean, is in the front rank of remedies affecting the scalp, more particularly the back part of the scalp or commencing there. Clarke confirmed the symptoms “desquamation of the epidermis of the scalp,” and “violent gnawing itching on the scalp, as from lice after scratching, a smarting as if scratched raw.” Cooper reported a case of a schoolboy whose head was very sore and irritable, covered with crusts, sore to the touch. Glands in his neck were swollen and sore to the touch. Olean, was given, two drops in a powder at bedtime on November 14th. On November 27th an aggravation was reported and the eruption had spread from the head to the back. From this time rapid improvement set in. Cooper noted that a single dose of the tincture may give the best possible results in such cases. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. - acute effects, Sulph. - the chronic effects. Compare: (1) Con., Nat- m., Rhus-t„ Caust., Lath. (2) Oleander contains Oleandrin and also Nerein which is said to be closely related, if not identical with Digitalin. (3) In irritability, Staph., Hyos., Nux-v. (4) In fits of passion followed by quickrepentance,Croc. (5)disordersofnursing women, Carb-an. (7) Inlienteria, Ferr., Ars. has diarrhea from chilling stomach indigestion of cold things, stool yellow with stool great pain, burning, worse after midnight, great thirst. (8) Arg-n. - bowels act as soon as patient drinks. (9) Chin. - watery stool containing undigested food, very debilitating, stools may escape involuntarily after a meal, caused or worse by eating fruits. (10) Apis, Phos. and Ph-ac. - wide-open anus. Compatible: Con., Lyc., Nat-m., Puls., Rhus-t., Sep., Spig. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Canine hunger with hurried eating without appetite. Thirst. Empty feeling even after eating, better brandy. Extreme debility of digestive power. Throbbing in pit. Empty belching. Vomiting of food, greenish water.

Abdomen - Borborygmus with profuse, fetid flatus. Gnawing around navel.

Rectum - Ineffectual urging. Burning pain in anus. Passes food undigested in the morning. Stools, pass when emitting flatus, thin involuntary. Sensations - Peculiar sensations suggestive of paralysis. Numb or painless paralyzed feeling as if inner parts were distended. Buzzing and humming. Pulsations in outer parts. Gnawing, itching, biting or pungent pain after scratching. Numbness of skin or itching numbness.

Female - Tremors after nursi ng, so weak she can scarcely walk across the room. Food - Desires cold water. Aversion to cheese.

Chest - Oppression as from a weight, asthmatic when lying down. Obtuse stitches in chest.

Heart - Palpitations with weakness and empty feeling in chest, better brandy. Pains on stooping.

Limbs - Limbs stiff and cold. Crampy contraction of upper limbs in paralysis. Stiffness of joints. Weakness of lower limbs. Painless paralysis. Paralysis of legs and feet. Trembling knees when standing. Edema. Swelling, burning stiffness of fingers. Veins on hands swollen. Constant cold feet. Lungs - Dyspnea.

Sleep - Sopor. Yawning with trembling of lower jaw.

Skin - Very sensitive skin, slightest friction causes soreness and chapping. Nocturnal burning. Violent itching eruption, bleeding, oozing, want of perspiration. Itching, especially of scalp, which is sensitive. Itching, scurfy pimples, herpes, sensitive and numb. Eruptions with itching, biting as of lice. Skin numb.

Modalities - Better from looking sideways, brandy. Squinting helps headache. Worse in open air, draft, undressing after nursing. Worse rubbing, scratching, friction of clothes. Worse rest, looking sideways. Rising up aggravates headache, vertigo. Stooping causes pain over heart.

Kidneys - Involuntary urination.

Temperature - Heat from mental exertion.

full:
PHARMACY - ol-an. Oleum animale. Dippel's animal oil. Aethereum dippeli. Oleum cornu cervi. Bone- naphtha. Dilutions in alcohol. This volatile oil is prepared by Dippel first by distillation of stags' horn. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Breast, disorders. Cancer. Colds. Constipation. Coryza. Facial, paralysis. Faint. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Migraines. Neurasthenia. Polyuria. Prostate disorders. Spermatic cord, neuralgia. Testes, neuralgia. Testes, retraction.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ol-an. is an oil obtained from the preparation of bone-black and further distilled and rectified for medicinal use. It was discovered in 1711 by Johann Conrad Dippel, the alchemist, who was the discoverer of Prussian blue. Dippel obtained it in the first instance by a distillation of stags' horns, the deciduous horns of the stag partaking more of the nature of bone than the permanent horns of cattle. This lead to the name Oleum cornu cervi, with which the Ol-an. is at present prepared is considered identical. Sircar noted that though it is not the panacea which Dippel imagined it to be when he discovered it, Ol-an. in a very powerful medicinal substance and since it has been well proved by Nenning, Schreter and Trinks, it has a definite place in the Homeopathic Materia Medica. Grimmer indicated it in cases of breast cancer with burning or sticking and pressure radiating in all directions, relieved by rubbing and in the open air. A uterine tumor cured with several doses of Ol-an. 1000c potency given at long intervals shows its relationship to new growths. Pain in spots. Stitches, burning pains, as with red hot needles. “Pulled upward’’ and “from behind forward” pains in malar bones, testicles, breasts. Flesh feels torn from bones. Affected part feels sore. Symptoms appear here and there or in single parts. Affects the nerves, especially pneumogas- tric nerve, digestive organs. Neurasthenia. Migraine, neuralgia of spermatic cord. Tremulous weakness of hands, knees, feet etc. Shuffling gait. Icy coldness from tips of teeth in throat, stomach etc. Chilliness (and coryza) are worse in a warm room and better in open air. Sensation as if stomach were full of churning water. Urinous odor with belch- ings, leucorrhea etc. MIND - Ill-tempered. Nervous irritability. Sad introverted, absorbed in self, speaks in whispers. Indolent, inclined to sit, taciturn. Vanishing thoughts. Faintness from gastric origin.

Head - Migraine with polyuria. Pain in spots. Tearing pain with sadness and irritability, worse after dinner, relieved by rubbing. Itching, burning vesicles, better friction. Malar bones feel pulled forcibly upward.

Eyes - Smarting in eyes, misty vision. Lachrymation when eating. Short-sighted. Glistening bodies before the eyes. Twitching of lids (Agar.). A skin seems to over- hang the eyes.

Nose - Watery, excoriating discharge, worse in open air.

Face - Cramp-like pains. Feels drawn. White of an egg seems dried on lips. Twitching of lips. Malar bone feelspulled upward. Swelling beneath right lower jaw. Toothache, better from pressing teeth together.

Mouth - Bites cheek while eating (Caust.). Snow-white cottony saliva. Greasy feeling in mouth. Tongue sore as if scalded. Toothache, better pressing teeth together with sensation of coldness coming out from tips.

Throat - Sore, dry, constricted, empty swallowing difficult, though food and drink pass easily. As if cold air penetrates the throat. Acrid vapor or raw streak in throat, worse cough. Hawks out gluey, brown lumps. Vertigo - Vertigo from gastric origin, better bending head backwards. COMMENTS - Dippel's Animal Oil is “a colorless or slightly yellow, thin, oily liquid with a penetrating but not disagreeable odor and an acrid, burning taste, which changes to a cool and bitter one. It darkens and thickens on exposure to air and light and is extremely volatile. A drop on paper evaporates without leaving a greasy stain.’Tts composition is extremely complex, but it may be regarded as belonging to the group of volatile carbons. Burning pains and burning sensations in almost all parts, stitching pains, “stitches as with red-hot needles” (Kali-c., other carbons). Stitches and pressure in all directions, particularly from behind forward. Cramp-like pains indifferent parts. Sensation of part being pulled upward. The left side is predominantly affected, when direction is noted it is from before backward and from behind upward. Cracking in vertebra of neck on raising head. Twitching of lips and swelling beneath right lower jaw. Malar bone feels as if pulled forcibly upward. Greasy feeling in mouth and accumulation of quantities of saliva white as snow. Relaxation of buccal mucus membrane, patient cannot avoid biting cheek when he eats. Sensation as of white of egg dried on lips. Soreness of tongue as if scalded. Sensation as if cold air penetrated throat although the air is warm, better eating and drinking, worse empty swallowing. Desire for soft-boiled eggs or for bread, with aversion to meat. Sensation as if water were in stomach, as if a lump of ice there. Belchings taste like urine and burn. Both testicles are drawn up and very painful. “Stitches from behind forward in breasts, pressure from both sides of the back extends forward.” Menses too early and too scanty. Clarke gave great relief in a case of cancer of right breast in which the patient complained of pains darting forward out of the nipple. Dr. Leggett related the case of a very stout Dutch woman, 56, who had been under constitutional treatment for uterine tumor, engorged liver and cerebral congestion. She fancied the tumor had increased to the size it was years ago. She had the sensation as if water rushing back and forth in stomach. She had been walking, standing and shopping and had eaten many sweets. Of the remedies having “stomach as if full of water,” Ol-an. was chosen as more similar to the case than Mill, or Phell. and was given in 1000c potency, a single dose. A month later she was better in every way and a second dose brought still further improvement. A case of long-standing neuralgia of the spermatic cord was cured. There were excruciating attacks three or four times every year, pains as if testicles were seized by a hand and pulled very severely. Ol-an. 18c gave almost instant and permanent relief. Dever cured a toothache in an extremely irritable patient, pain better by pressing the teeth together. The provings had “stitches in right upper molar removed by pressure after dinner.” The cure of a case of migraine is quoted in H. M., July, 1895. Zwingenberg, after failing with Sang., gave Ol- an. 2x, five drops in warm water, morning and evening to a woman who always suffered from migraine the day after a party, at which she usually wore a heavy diadem on her head. Polyuria of clear urine accompanied the migraine and suggested the remedy. This accompaniment may indicate Ol-an. in any nervous disorder. Zwingenberg also cured a case of nervous asthma following repelled foot-sweat. RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Camph., Nux-v., Op. Compare: (1) Puls., Ars., Sil., Sep. (2) in headache with concomitant polyuria, Ign., Gels. (3) Twitching eyelids, Agar. (4) Gastric symptoms after drinking cold water, Ars., Phos., Carb-v. (5) Pains in testicles, Puls. (6) worse by noise, Graph, better by noise. (7) better by rubbing, Phos., Nat-c., Carb-ac., Canth. (8) Coryza worse in open air, All-c. (9) Numb head, Graph. Cracking in nape on moving head, Nice. (10) Dried white of egg sensation, Alum., Bar-c., Mag-c., Ph-ac., Sul-ac. (11) better eating and drinking, worse empty swallowing, Lach. (12) Belchings taste like urine, Agn., smell like old urine. ( 13) Sad. despondent, Puls. - unlike Puls., bad tempered. Follows well: Bry. Followed well by: Sep. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Sensations as if water were in stomach, of coldness, constriction, and burning, better belchings. Urinous belchings. Water brash, better chewing tobacco.

Abdomen - Flatulence and rumbling. Bruised pain in abdomen after stool.

Rectum - Ineffectual urging to stool, with burning in anus. Sensations - Sensation in scalp as if skin had been cut and reunited. As if blood were rushing to head to occiput on entering a warm room. As if red-hot needles in chest. As if testicles were seized and pulled forcibly upward. As if thumb (and toe) would ulcerate.

Male - Desire increased, ejaculation too soon. Pain along spermatic cord to testicles. Testicles feel seized and pulled forcibly upward, worse right. Pressure in the perineum. Prostate hypertrophy. Seminal losses, on straining at stool.

Female - Stitches in breast from behind forwards. Sore breasts before menses, outward stitches in nipples in scirrhus. Menses, early, scanty, black flow. Urinous leucorrhea. Food - Drinking cold water causes pressure in stomach, worse from hot drinks. Desires bread. Worse eating (sweat, lachrymation, headache). Especially worse after dinner.

Chest - Stitches at clavicle. Chest feels constricted. Oppression.

Heart - Anxious palpitations. Pulse slow.

Back - Cracking in cervical vertebrae on raising the head. Aching in right scapula, better pressure. Sprained feeling in sacrum. Unsteady gait. Breasts - Stitches in breast from behind forward. Causations - Ill effects of suppressions, especially of foot sweat.

Limbs - Sprained feeling in small of back. Cracking of vertebrae on raising head (Aloe, Nat-c., Thuj.). Rheumatic pain in shoulders. Restlessness. Fish-brine odor of sweat of heels. Lungs - Asthma from suppressed footsweat.

Skin - Excoriation in bends of joints.

Modalities - Better from rubbing, pressure. Better stretching, changing position. Better in open air. Better eructation. Worse from cold. Worse in warm room, hot drinks. Worse eating. Worse suppressions, noise. Worse from 2 p.m. to 9 p.m. Worse before, during and commencement of menses.

Kidneys - Polyuria. Frequent and urgent want to urinate with tenesmus and scanty emission. Small stream of urine. Profuse, pale urine of fish brine odor, worse hysteria, migraine. Greenish urine. Itching in urethra.

Temperature - Alternate chill and heat. Cold, foul foot-sweat, fishy smell on heels.

HOMEOPATHIC - The number of people who “cannot take cod-liver oil” is very great, which means that Ol-j. is a pathogenic as well as a curative agent. Neidhard proved it and elicited some very definite symptoms and to these have been added curative and pathogenic effects observed on patients. The oil contains a large number of proximate principles of great complexity to which its specific medicinal properties are due. Decided pains in the liver and liver region with great soreness were noted in Neidhard's provings and these symptoms give one of the keynotes of the remedy as soreness. Not only the liver, but the throat, chest, abdomen, kidneys, ovaries, joints and back are all sore. The spine is sore as in spinal irritation. Sore pains. Burning in spots. Rheumatic disorders. Pains in liver region. Yellow discharges. Scrofulous diseases. Faulty nutrition. Emaciation. Anemia, weakness. Deficiency of vital heat. Always taking cold. Lassitude. Hot hands and head. Frontal headaches, over right eye, bursting after coughing. Palpitations of the heart, with cough, short breath. The nutrition of the skin is improved and the medicinal properties of the oil are absorbed without any tax being put on the organs of digestion. Burnett said that olive oil and almond oil acts as well. Atrophy of infants, emaciation with hot handle and head, restless and feverish at night. Emaciated, dwarfish, chilly babies and children, a nightly rubbing with cod liver oil soon revolutionizes their condition. Children who cannot tolerate milk.

Face - Growth of short, thick hair on chin and upper lip in women.

Mouth - Tongue yellow. Fetid breath.

Throat - Hoarseness. COMMENTS - Ol-j. is a liver remedy, an ally of Choi., confirmed by the provings. Burnett noted that cod liver oil is a nutrient and affects the chest, liver, pancreas and tendons. Internally, a nutrient and a hepatic and pancreatic remedy. Burnett showed that ringworm generally has its constitutional basis in a tuberculosis miasm. In recent ringworm, the application of the plain oil at bedtime is at once the most innocent and most effectual of known local measures. Before the application, the part should be washed well with soft soap. “Dry, hacking cough, night-cough, cough with tough expectoration, yellow or white, soreness of chest, especially on coughing, sharp stitches here and there, through chest, burning through to back, burning in spots.” Tuberculosis, in the beginning stages. Scrofulous diathesis. Cough is worse from exposure to cold, worse in damp weather. Cough relieved by onset of fever. Marked fever symptom, both hectic and intermittent. “Fever worse towards evening with burning in palms.” Chilly, sensitive to drafts, feels as if continually taking cold. Chills running down the back. Feet constantly cold. Sensitive to chill and damp. Thirst before and during the chill. Affection of the spleen. Y ellow discharges, particularly expectoration, coating of the tongue, yellow mucus from sore throat. Increases the menstrual flow, and restores it when in abeyance. Abnormal growth of hair on the face of a woman. Yellow leucorrhea. Passage of mucus from urethra with burning during stool. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Iris v. (chill with sick stomach and diarrhea). Compare: (1) Choi., Tub., Phos., lod. (2) One liter of Ol. Jecoris contains 0.4 gram of iodine. (3) Gad., Cod, - frequent breathing with flapping of ala nasi, rush of blood to chest, pain in lungs and cough, dry heat in palms. (4) Fei. and sarcodes generally. (5) In tuberculosis, ringworm, emaciation, Bac., Phos. (6) Emaciation and ravenous appetite, lod. (7) Intolerance of milk, Aeth., Calc., Lac-v„ Mag-c. (8) Pains in head with cough, Caps., Bry., Nat-m. (9) Chilly, effects of damp localities, Nat-sulph., Aran. (10) Heavy eyelids, Gels., Op. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Abdomen - Soreness and heaviness in the region of liver, worse exercise.

Female - Establishes menses. Yellow leucor- rhea with weak back. Food - Children who cannot take milk.

Chest - Sharp, stitching pains. Burning spots. Soreness through chest. Coughing causes soreness of chest, headache.

Heart - Palpitations, accompany other symptoms.

Back - Chilly or fluttering from sacrum up back to occiput. Causations - Malnutrition.

Limbs - Chronic rheumatism with rigid muscles and tendons. Aching in elbows and knees, in sacrum. Burning in palms. Palms hot toward evening. Lungs - Dry, hacking, tickling cough, especially at night. Cough with palpitation. Soreness or stitches in chest. Yellow sputum. Hemoptysis (Acai., Mill.). Early tuberculosis. Whooping cough in miserable, scrofulous children. Dahlke indicated giving give drop doses increasing daily, one drop up to twelve, then descend in the same way for whooping cough.

Skin - Yellowness. Cold abscesses. Milk crusts. Ringworm (local application).

Modalities - Worse from milk. Worse from exposure to cold, draft of air. Worse living in cold. Worse damp localities. Worse touch, motion. Worse raising arm, bending side inwards. Worse stooping, walking. Worse riding, falling. Laughing aggravates cough. Lying down causes oppressed feeling.

Temperature - Constantly chilly towards evening. Hectic fever. Night-sweats.

CLINICAL - Constipation. Dehydration. Heart, disease. Malnutrition. Skin, disorders.

HERBAL - Olive oil is obtained from the fruit of the olive tree, now common to the shores of the Mediterranean. It is used in cooking, cosmetics, soaps and as a fuel for traditional oil lamps. Olive oil is pleasant and bland, very nutritious, and mildly laxative. It is regarded as a healthful dietary oil because of its high content of monounsaturated fat (mainly oleic acid) and polyphenols. Very well tolerated by the stomach. It's protective function has a beneficial effect on ulcers and gastritis. Activates the secretion of bile and pancreatic hormones, lowering the incidence of gallstone formation. For infants it is especially serviceable as a cathartic, being easily taken and of mild action. Suitable for adults in irritated or inflamed conditions of the bowel or stomach, and may be given after acrid poisons. As a laxative enema, one to two fluid ounces should be taken, two teaspoonfuls or less for a child one year old. Externally, it is a lubricant and is valuable for shielding irritated surfaces, relax contracted tendons, and promote healing. Olive oil massage is helpful in preventing dehydration from fever. Daily breast massage with the oil is helpful in preventing breast cancer and tumors. Olive oil foot massages are good for relaxation and will promote sleep. Olive oil is often the basis in which to incorporate other medicaments, or is compounded with dense fatty or resinous substances to give them pliancy in the formation of ointments, cerates, or plasters. RELATIONS - Compare: Alf., Mel., Aloe-v., Calen., castor oil. REFERENCES - Murphy.

HOMEOPATHIC - In Germany, Onis. has a popular reputation as a remedy for epilepsy. Hering proved a tincture and Wolf recorded the effect of swallowing three cellar-worms in a glass of brandy before an attack of fever. This experience provided the most characteristic symptoms of the remedy, showing it to be related to Canth., Apis and their cognates. The symptoms of Hering's proving showed pains in the head, over the eyes and down the nose. Constriction of gullet and stomach. Hawking up of blood-streaked mucus. Burning in anus. Many erections with disinclination to work (Canth.). Frequent yawning and desire to stretch. Asthmatic conditions with bronchial catarrh. Pale face, wild expression, constant vomiting. Very severe colic with meteor- ism and tension of abdomen. Tenesmus of bladder and rectum. Cutting burning in urethra. Dropsy.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany notes that ononis arvensis is indigenous to Britain, growing on barren pastures and on the borders of ill-cultivated fields. It owes its name, “Rest- harrow,’ ’ to its tough underground roots, which cause stoppages to harrow and plough. In some parts it is called “Cammock,” and the country people, having the idea that it communicates its nauseous, goat-like odor to cheese made from the milk of cows who have eaten it, call the cheese so tainted “Cammocky.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Nosebleed three or four times in one day, worse when washing his face. Hansen gave “chronic nephritis” as having been cured by Onon. COMMENTS - Cooper recorded the case of a brick field laborer, 45, who at 13 was prostrated for a week, apparently with sunstroke, something seemed to catch the back of his head. At 25, had similar attacks. In March, 1900, he began to have daily attacks. An aura seemed to spread over his head from the occiput, he made frightful grimaces, but did not scream out, became unconscious, turned deathlike and blue in face and fell down. After the attacks he had a violent headache, giddiness and wakeful nights. Onon. tincture in single doses at rare intervals produced improvement at once and cured in nine months. REFERENCES Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - Constriction in left side of chest. Sensation as of a stone in the chest. Characteristic heart rhythm disorders. Excessive depressive tendency. Headache better change of weather, to warm and dry weather. Stuffed sensation in ears and nose. Pain in right maxillary sinus. Increased sensory perceptions. Chilliness. Sensitiveness to cold and to drafts of air. Worse cold, damp weather. Better warmth and rest. Pains in back and limbs, better motion, and worse sitting and after sleep. Sensation of cold and the dryness of the mucous membranes of nose and throat. Dryness of mouth, lips. Better eating. Desire for sweets. Swelling and redness of the part of the abdomen where a belt is worn. Cold feeling in lower abdomen during scanty menses. As if icicles in rectum. MIND - Difficult concentration. Sensitiveness to external impressions. Euphoria, alternating with sadness. Food - Desires sweets.

Head - Headache better change of weather to warm and dry weather.

Nose - Smell more acute. REFERENCES - Murphy.

Heart - Dull pain in region of heart, extending to left arm.

Limbs - Fleeting pains in small joints. Limbs heavy like lead. While walking, feet turn frequently.

Modalities - Better warmth and rest. Better eating. Worse cold, damp weather.

full:
PHARMACY - onos. Onosmodium virginianum. False cromwell. Lithospermum virginicum. N. O. Boraginacee. Tincture of entire fresh plant including root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Aphasia. Bladder, irritation. Breasts, disorders. Colic. Colorblindness. Debility. Diarrhea. Diplopia. Eye, disorders. Eyestrain. Headaches. Locomotor ataxia. Meniere's disease. Migraines. Neurasthenia. Nose, dryness. Paralysis. Pregnancy, sickness. Presbyopia. Seminal emissions. Sexual, weakness. Spine, congestion. Throat, sore. Tinnitus. Urethra, irritation. Uterus, prolapse.

HOMEOPATHIC - Onos, is a member of an American branch of the borage family closely resembling the British Onosma. Its common name is False Cromwell, the real Cromwell being another borage, Lithospermum. It was proved in material doses by W. E. Green of Arkansas. The most remarkable feature of the proving was the want of power of concentration or coordination produced by the drug. This appears in an inability to concentrate thought, to focus eyes, to coordinate muscles, or to judge the height of impediments on stepping. General prostration, weariness. Acts and feels as if born tired. Seems to tread on cotton. Staggering. Vertigo, numbness with muscular prostration. Neuralgic pains. Aching, soreness and stiffness of muscles after a pain. Marked association of head and eye symptoms with muscular tiredness and weariness. Disturbance in the sense of proportion. Migraine headaches. Onos, has probably cured more cases of headache associated with eye-strain (Ruta), than any other remedy since it was proved. Headaches from sexual weakness. Diminution of sexual desire in both sexes, similar to sexual neurasthenia. Depressed or lost sexual life in women. MIND - Loss of concentration and coordination. Confused mind, slow thinking. Irresolution. Aphasia. Forgetful, loss of memory. Fear of falling on going up or down stairs.

Head - Migraine headache from eyestrain or sexual weakness. Dull, heavy, dizzy, pressing upward in occiput. Occipital headache as if screwed, worse eyestrain and lying down. Occipital-frontal pain in morning on waking, Chiefly on the left side. Pain up and down from occiput (left) to shoulder worse exertion. Pain in temples and mastoid (Caps.).

Eyes - Eyes heavy and dull. Eyestrain, strainedfeelingin eyes, worse using eyes. Muscular asthenopia. Ocular muscles tense. Internal eye muscles paretic. Pain in eyeballs between orbit and ball, extending to left temple. Eye symptoms with ovarian symptoms.

Ears - Fullness in ears. Hearing impaired, ringing as from quinine.

Nose - Dryness of nose, with feeling as from taking cold. Pain in nasal bones. Stuffed feeling or discharge in posterior sinuses. Sneezing in morning, left side of nose and left eye seem affected.

Mouth - Dryness of mouth, and of lips, without thirst, better cold water, with scanty saliva. Clammy, sticky, feeling in mouth. Bitter taste.

Throat - Severe dryness and tightness, all symptoms are better by cold drinks and eating. Raw, scraping. Laryngeal cough, better from drinking cold water, with expectoration of whitish, sticky phlegm. Husky voice. Vertigo - Vertigo, numbness and muscular prostration. Vertigo with headache, worse lying on left side, raising the hands above the head. Vision - Vision blurred, optic disc hyperemic and retinal vessels enlarged. Misjudges distances. Color blindness for red and green. COMMENTS - Vertigo and sensations of numbness and general muscular prostration. Neuralgic pains, dull, heavy aching, affecting the cervical and spinal nerves, pelvic organs, eyes, occiput and sacrum. These are the chief centers of pain along with the throat, bowels, breasts, heart and limbs. The left side of the body is more affected than the right. Characteristic paralyzing effects on the internal eye muscles. “Feeling of tension in the eyes, as from straining them to read small print,” and “desires to have things far off to look at them.” The eyeball aches, aggravated by reading small print. Glaucoma. Blurred or double vision. Eyestrain headaches (Ruta.). Marked “soreness and stiffness.” In the occiput there is pressure upward and the pains may go from the eye backward. Gluey expectoration with laryngeal cough. Catarrh of the Eustachian tube (Kali-m„ Merc-d.). Meniere's disease. Characteristic dryness of the nose, mouth and throat. Ameliorated by a great thirst for cold water. Strictures of the urethra where there's painful urination and there are adhesions or blockages in the urethra. Great loss of sexual desire. Fibroids. History of enlarging breasts when given in tincture (Sabad.). Equalizes the size of unequal breasts. E. S. Norton published several illustrative cases including the case of Miss C., 23, who suffered three years from a headache. Pain especially in occiput, which felt “sore and stiff,” often extending down spine, which was somewhat sensitive to touch. There was a dull, aching pain on the left side of head, with occasional darting pain through the eyes. Aching in eyes, stiff, strained feeling in them if she read a lot, worse on the left. Headache worse in the morning with some dizziness. The patient had some astigmatism that was corrected with glasses and Onos, lx at once relieved all the symptoms. Norton also noted the case of Mrs. D., who had excessive myopia and a severe headache with a constant dull, stupid ache in right occiput and right eye, worse when tired, from coughing or from any sudden motion. There was a little vertigo and a strained feeling in right eye. Onos. 3x cured. Norton suggested that neurasthenia and neurasthenic headache may be met with Onos, when connected with strains of other kinds besides eye strains. He pointed to the case of Mrs. B., who was deaf for nine years. For four years she had a constant roaring, hissing noise in both ears with constant dull, pressing pain in occiput, worse in the evening. She had some pain in the ear and sharp shooting pain in front of auricle, with slight vertigo. Chronic catarrh of both middle ears, membranes thickened. Onos, lx immediately relieved all the pains, though it did not alter the hearing or noises. H. F. Ivens cured a case of headache of ten years duration, with the modality worse in the dark. The pain was in the left temple and over the left eye, not worse by noises, light or use of eyes, but worse in the dark and on lying down. Pellets of Onos, tincture were given every twelve hours. W. A. Yingling found that the depressing action of Onos, extends to the generative sphere, desire being abolished in both men and women. He quoted S. A. Jones as suggesting that this is the primary action of the drug, thereby distinguishing it from Pic-ac. in which excitement precedes debility. Onos, will correspond to the developed consequences of sexual abuse and Pic-ac. to the initial step of sexual debility manifested in weakness. Yingling many times verified “complete loss of desire” as a leading indication. Yingling had an interesting experience in the case of a woman to whom he gave Onos, for dryness of the nose and throat. Not only did it cure this, but it also restored the breasts, which were diminutive and almost absent to their normal size. Yingling's results were from the tincture, and not marked from 30c. W. J. Guernsey greatly relieved with Onos, a man, 38, who suffered from seminal emissions, the result of masturbation. The pains were better by undressing and lying on the back. Green published some very striking cases with some pathogenic symptoms as well as cures, and also gives an interesting comparative experience with potencies. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Nat-m., Lil-t, Gels., Ruta. (2) Myos., Helio., Symph. (3) In uterine misplacement, Helio., Helon., Lil- t., Sep.. Nat-m., etc. (4) Disorder of vision, Lil-t. - astigmatism, Pic-ac. - myopia, Nat-s. - Myopia. (5) Ocular headache, Gels, more right, Onos, more left, Lil-t., Spig., Bapt. (6) Eyestrain - Ruta. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Abdomen - Distended feeling, better removing clothing, with griping and grumbling. Colic is better bending backward.

Rectum - Stools with tenesmus, yellow, mushy, hurrying him out of bed in morning. Stool is shining, bloody and stringy.

Male - Burning in urethra with itching. Sexual excitement. Constant, severe erections. Speedy emissions. Psychological impotence. Loss of sexual desire. Deficient erections.

Female - Sexual desire completely loss. Feels as if menses would appear. Menses too early and too prolonged. Leucorrhea, acrid, yellow offensive, profuse, running down the legs. Severe uterine pains, bearing down pains, old pains return. Soreness in uterine region. Pains alternate between ovaries. Soreness of ovaries with rectum. Food - Craving for ice water and cold drinks, wants to drink often. Distaste for water. Appetite and thirst diminished. Appetite increased. Hunger after siesta, nervous, all day.

Heart - Pain in heart causing fear of death. Pain in region of apex. Oppression of heart. Depressed feeling in heart, as if it would stop beating. Pulse rapid, irregular and weak, and slow. With every third or fourth beat the diastole is prolonged.

Back - Tired feeling in lower part of the back. Pain in dorsal and lumbar regions. Numbness and tingling in feet and legs. Breasts - Sore, aching in breasts, feel swollen and sore. Nipples itch. Causations - Eyestrain. Sexual excess.

Limbs - Great muscular weakness and weariness. Pain in back. Pain in left scapular region. Tired and numb feeling in legs, popliteal spaces and below knees. Staggering gait. Sidewalk seems too high. Lungs - Hacking cough with sticky, white sputum, better drinking cold water.

Sleep - Sleeplessness. Sleep is uneasy and interrupted, restless and waking early. Many, varied dreams.

Skin - Formication in calves.

Modalities - Better from cold drinks, eating, undressing. Better lying on back, rest, sleep. Worse eyestrain, sprains, jarring, motion, tight clothing. Worse sexual excess, darkness, warm, humid air.

Kidneys - Pain in prostatic urethra before and after urination. Seldom any desire to urinate. Urination frequent, scanty. Urine is high-colored, very acid, aromatic, of balsamic odor and heavily loaded with urea.

Temperature - As if would have a chill every day about twelve or one o' clock. Hushed feeling over body. No perspiration in very warm weather.

Boils and slowly suppurating abscesses. Hemorrhoids. Cholera morbus. Watery diarrhea, profuse with sinking sensation. REFERENCES - Boericke.
