PHARMACY - plb. Plumbum metallicum. Lead metal. The element (Pb. At. Wt. 206.39). Plumbum aceticum. Lead acetate. Sugar of Lead. Plumbum carbonicum. Lead carbonate. Pure White Lead. Trituration. Historicaldose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Anus, prolapsed. Anemia. Anesthesia. Aneurysm. Anidrosis. Appendicitis. Arteriosclerosis. Asthma. Atrophy. Bone, tumors. Brain, disorders. Bright’s disease. Colic. Coma. Constipation. Convulsions. Cramps. Cystitis. Depression. Diplopia. Dropsy. Dysuria. Emaciation. Epilepsy. Epulis. Esophagus, stricture. Eyes disorders. Ganglion. Glaucoma. Gout. Hemoptysis. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Hernia, strangulated. Hyperesthesia. Hypertension. Hypopion. Ichthyosis. Intermittent fever. Intestines, obstruction. Intussusception. Jaundice. Jaw, tumor. Kidneys, disorders. Lead, poisoning. Liver disorders. Lockjaw. Locomotor ataxia. Marasmus. Metrorrhagia. Multiple sclerosis. Myelitis. Nephritis. Neuritis. Numbness. Painter's colic. Paralysis. Parkinson's disease. Penchondritis. Progressive muscular atrophy. Rectal pain. Sciatica. Spasms. Spine, diseases. Spleen, disorders. Stricture. Strokes. Tabes mesenterica. Tobacco habit. Tongue, paralysis. Typhlitis. Umbilicus, disorders. Uric acid. Vaginismus. Varicose veins. Wristdrop.

HOMEOPATHIC - Plb., the Saturn of the Alchemists, has been proved by Hartlaub, Trinks, Hering and Nenning. To those symptoms have been added those of numberless cases of poisoning among workers with lead and painters, symptoms from drinking lead contaminated waters, from the use of lead in cosmetics, and from cases of suicide. Teste noted that metallic lead was seldom used in old school practice as it was considered inert, but Boerhaave gave it internally, reduced to an impalpable powder, forleucor- rhea, dysentery, syphilis and gout. The salts of lead, in the form of plaster and “Foulard water,” have been largely used as external applications in skin diseases, vaginal and urethral injections. Injury has frequently resulted, especially from repelled eruptions. Among painters and lead manufacturers, the best-known symptoms are colic and wrist drop. Kidney irritation with albuminuria, ending in granular degeneration with attendant heart hypertrophy, optic neuritis and blindness. There is an excess of uric acid in the blood of persons under the influence of lead and actual gouty deposits and gouty attacks have been observed. In one case of lead poisoning, there was an enlargement of the knees and contraction of the lower limbs, completely crippling the patient. Useful for general sclerotic conditions. It affects the muscles, nerves, spinal cord, abdomen, navel, kidneys, blood vessels and blood. Particularly affects the blood, alimentary and nervous systems. Lead paralysis is chiefly of extensors, forearm or upper limb from center to periphery with partial anesthesia or excessive hyperesthesia, preceded by pain. Localized neuralgic pains, neuritis. Progressive muscular atrophy. Infantile paralysis. Locomotor ataxia. Bulbar paralysis. Peripheral disorders. Paralysis of single parts, wrist drop, flaccid with hyperesthesia, worse touch. Tremors, followed by paralysis. Attacks of the neural axons and the anterior horns. Multiple sclerosis, posterior spinal sclerosis. Contractions and boring pain. Retraction, sense of a string pulling back or in. Constrictive sensation in internal organs. Violent contractions. Convulsive trembling and jerking of the limbs. Convulsions, chronic epilepsy with marked aura with hemorrhages. Boring, cramps. Lightning pains that extort cries. Small aneurysms all over the body. Dropsical swelling. Arthralgia. Symptoms appear slowly, insidiously, progressively, often with violent side effects of very changeable and incoherent character, coming in single parts, etc. Anesthesia is as marked as excessive hyperesthesia. Exaggerates her condition. Perception slow, comprehension is difficult. Delirium, coma and convulsions. Hematosis is interfered with, rapid reduction in number of red corpuscles, causing pallor jaundice, and anemia. Hypertension and arteriosclerosis. Gout. Acute nephritis with amaurosis and cerebral symptoms. Impulse to stretch with abdominal distress. Retraction of abdomen, anus, testes, navel etc. Excessive and rapid emaciation. Emaciation of limbs with plump body, of paralyzed parts, of single parts after neuralgias. Marasmus of infants in apparently hopeless cases, abdomen large and hard and constipation extreme. MIND - Mental exhaustion from physical labor. Confusion of mind while standing. Weakness or loss of memory (Anae., Bar-c.). Deficiency of ideas. Increasing slowness and apathy. Slow perception. Stupid, imbecile. Timid, restless and anxious. Unable to find proper word while talking. Amnesia aphasia. Mental depression. Quiet and melancholy. Gloom alternating with excitement. Censorious. Taciturn. Aversion to company. Timidity about appearing in public. Restlessness at night, wants to go from one bed to another. Anxiety with restlessness and yawning. Hysteria, only while being watched. Screams from time to time. Fright without cause. Frantic, bites, strikes. Fears of poisoning, of being assassinated. Thinks every one about her is a murderer. Delusion of dead persons. Paretic dementia. Feigns sickness or exaggerates her condition. Inclined to cheat and deceive. Plays antics. Foolish behavior. Cursing. Wild delirium with distorted face. Delirium, nocturnal, alternating with colic or pain in the limbs. Delirium from hearing music. Delirium after epilepsy. Disposition to suicide or do himself some bodily injury. Time passes too slowly.

Head - Headache, as if a ball was rising from the throat into the head. Delirium alternating with colic. Hair very dry, falls from beard.

Eyes - Pupils contracted. Yellow or deep bluish red sclerotics. Optic neuritis, central scotoma. Intra-ocular, suppurative inflammation. Glaucoma from spinal disorders. Sudden loss of sight after fainting. Paralysis of upper lid. Profuse hot lachrymation.

Ears - Tinnitus (Chin., Nat-sal., Carb-s.). Hears music with frightful delirium. Occasional sudden deafness.

Nose - Coldness of the nose. Erysipelatous inflammation of nose. Obstruction of nose. Accumulation of tenacious mucus in nostrils. Fluent coryza with discharge of serous mucus. Fetid smell in nose. Loss of smell with epilepsy.

Face - Yellow, corpse-like, cheeks sunken. Skin, greasy, shiny. Pale and emaciated. Swelling of face, one side. Twitching of side of face (right). Tremor of naso-labial muscles.

Mouth - Sweet taste. Sticky saliva, blue. Yellow inside the mouth. Aphthae, fetid ulcers. Gums swollen, pale. Hard tubercles on gums. Distinct blue lines along margins of gums. Tongue tremulous, red on margin. Cannot put it out, seems paralyzed. Loud motion of lower jaw and frightful grinding of teeth.

Throat - Solids cannot be swallowed. Dysphagia, fluids can be swallowed. Paralysis of gullet with inability to swallow. Globus hystericus. Stricture of esophagus from spasms. Vertigo - Fainting in a room full of people or on going from one room to another. COMMENTS - Tunzelmann reported a number of cases of acute poisoning from drinking water containing lead. In one such case, a cook was ill for three weeks. Unable to retain any food in the stomach, constant nausea and, even when no food was taken, frequent vomiting of greenish watery fluid, worse at night. Skin was yellowish, conjunctiva decidedly yellow. Tongue was furred, coated at back, very yellow, horrible taste, fetor of breath, bowels confined. Extreme debility. Hydr. 3c gave great relief, but three months later the hands became paralyzed, which led to the testing of the drinking water and the discovery of lead. A boy, age 12, had bronchial catarrh with a loose cough and consolidation of left apex. As soon as the poisoned water was stopped, he rapidly recovered. An elder brother had hemoptysis, and coughed up half a pint of blood. Nothing was found wrong with the lungs beyond a slight feebleness of respiration at the apices. Three months later, after a day's rowing, the hematemesis returned with a nosebleed. Now distinct dullness was found at right apex. Rapid recovery followed stopping the water. Women who work with lead frequently abort. Women who do not work with lead but whose husbands do, abort in even greater proportion. Children bom under these conditions are frequently idiotic or epileptic. Characteristic retraction and sense of retraction. Sensation of or actual drawing in of abdominal wall, were drawn back by a string to the spine. The cheeks are retracted, sunken. Excessive and rapid emaciation. Emaciation of certain parts (Caust.). Anemia. Memory loss. Progressive muscularatrophy. Parkinson's disease. Paralysis of single muscles. Paralyzed parts lose flesh. Progressive locomotor ataxia. Stroke, with spastic paralysis. Epilepsy preceded by vertigo, sometimes sighing, followed by a stupid feeling. Cramps, spasms, convulsions, paralyzes, tremors. Clonic or tonic convulsive movements of limbs from cerebral sclerosis or tumor. Cramps in the fingers. Wrist drop, weak wrist from ovemse. Lead palsy. Spasm of bladder of esophagus. Violent colic. Strangulated hernia. Colon spasms. Painful impacted bowels (Alum, and Op. are painless). Vaginismus, spasm of utems and expulsion of its contents. Useful for vaginismus resulting in paralytic symptoms. Sensation as if there was not room enough for fetus. Anesthesia and hyperesthesia. Restlessness, lassitude, faintness. Sensation in abdomen at night that causes patient to stretch violently for hours, must stretch in every direction. Assumes strange positions in bed at night. Pains are wandering or radiating, vague, paroxysmal. Ailments develop slowly and can intermit for a time. Alternations are common, delirium with colic, diarrhea and constipation jerks of flexors and extensors, paralysis and colic. Right side is most affected, symptoms go from left to right (throat). Symptoms worse 8 a.m. to 9 a.m. Frohling related the case of N., a farmer, 46, who was taken ill in November 1893 with attacks of colic with vomiting and extreme constipation, action only obtained by large enemata. Had been constipated in former years, but without illness. Op. had given only temporary relief. After December 1983, vomiting was rare, but colic increased in intensity up to February 1894, when Frohling saw him first and found him wasted to a skeleton, abdomen drawn in, appetite bad, feeling ill. His mind was somewhat affected, unable to give sensible answers to questions. Constant urgent call to stool, but only small, hard, black balls were passed. Liver dullness only heard from upper border of sixth to upper border of seventh rib. Lead poisoning was suspected, but as no evidence of it could be found, Plb. 6c three times a day was prescribed. In six days the colic attacks were less frequent and less severe, two stools passed without enema, his mind clearer. Improvement continued in all respects, and in fourteen days N. was able to leave his bed to which he had been confined since November. By the middle of March he made an hour's journey to see Frohling and was hardly recognizable, he had gained so much flesh and his liver was of normal size. Wingfield reported two characteristic cases. The first concerned Mrs. D., 50, no children, sparely built, very nervous, constipated fifteen years, took a teaspoonful of Cascara extract every other night. Tongue coated with yellowish white fur. Had constant headaches and after each motion was thoroughly exhausted and had to lie down the rest of the day. Plb. 6x was given, three grains twice a day. In two days, bowels began acting naturally.In three weeks the headaches were gone, tongue clean, much less nervous. Wingfield's second case was Miss M., 25, florid, had boils appear on face and arms and chronic constipation. The constipation had been a trouble since she was twelve years old. Slight spinal curvature. Tongue furred, occasional headaches. Suffered much during menstrual periods. Plb. 6x twice daily at once relieved the constipation and soon the boils disappeared. Patient soon felt quite well. Arriage, of Mexico City, reported the case of a woman, 73. seized with symptoms of intestinal occlusion, violent colic, nausea, constipation, meteorism, complete anorexia and no fever. Nux-v. relieved the colic, and then Plb. 12c and later 13c, gradually brought about recovery in four days. Nash cured a severe case of post-diphtheria paralysis in a middle-aged man. The leading symptom was excessive hyperesthesia, he could not bear to be touched anywhere due to the pain. A single dose of Plb. 40,000c cured. Nash told of a man, 70, attacked with severe pain in his abdomen and finally a large, hard swelling developed in the ileo-cecal region, very sensitive to contact or least motion. It began to assume a bluish tint and, on account of his age and weakness, the man's life was despaired. But his daughter, the wife of a medical man, found the symptoms in Raue under Plb. in the chapter on Typh., and Plb. 200c cured. Theuerkaufcured a case of hypopion with great pain in six weeks using Plb. 6c. Skinner cured a case of epilepsy in which the head turned to the right after a fit. W. H. Woodyatt reported a case of “vasomotor neurosis” affecting the left eye. Mrs. D., 29, had been ill for two weeks and supposed she had caught cold in the eye. She had a drooping upper lid, intense photophobia, very profuse lachrymation of hot teai s, peri-corneal injection, deep bluish redness of sclerotica, most marked at corneal margin. Cornea was very faintly hazy. Pupil contracted. Sight misty. Ars. 6x and Plant. 6x failed to relieve. Plb. 6x was then given with immediate Plumbum metallicum improvement, which went on to cure in seven days. Plb. cured acase of right-sided sciatica that had been greatly benefited by Gnaph. 1c, but which had returned. The symptoms included stiffness, soreness from great trochanter and point of exit of nerve to knee, weakness in thigh, worse by stooping, walking causes sensation as if pushing a knife in thigh. Plb. 6c was given four times day. Up to the twelfth day there was no change, on that day, the pain suddenly disappeared. The case had lasted nine months. RELATIONS - Antidotes: Plat., Alum., Petr. Compare: ( 1) Plb-acet. (2) Plb-i. Alum., Plat., Op., Podo., Merc., Thal. (3) Plect. - paralysis, spastic, spinal form, (4) Plb-chr. (5) Plb-p. - loss of sexual power, locomotor ataxia. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Contraction in esophagus and stomach, pressure and tightness. Gastralgia, better hard pressure, bending backwards. Foul or fecal belchings. Periodical or persistent vomiting of food. Vomiting of brown-black liquid or of green mucus. Vomiting of fecal matter with colic and constipation.

Abdomen - Colic, accompanies many symptoms. Colic alternates with delirium and pain in atrophied limbs. Obstructed flatus with intense colic. Abdominal wall feels drawn by a string to spine. Navel feels retracted. Abdomen is drawn into uneven lumps. Radiating abdominal pains to all parts of the body. Hernia, navel. Intus- susception, strangulated hernia. Boring or as if forced through a narrow place. Pain causes desire to stretch.

Rectum - Anus feels drawn up or painfully contracted. Neuralgiaofrectum. Prolapsed anus with paralysis. Constipation. Stools, hard, lumpy, black with urging and spasm of anus. Stools, granular, hard black balls like sheep dung, passed with an urging cramp in anus. Obstructed evacuation from impaction of feces (Plat.). Stubborn constipation or colics of infants. Sensations - As if everything were weighed down. As if something were working at top of head with a sense of screwing from throat into brain. As if a wheat hull in throat. As if abdomen and back were too close together, abdomen drawn to spine with a string. Bowels as if twisted, constricted, distended with gas. As if abscess forming near umbilicus. Anal sphincter as if drawn in. As if a bag not quite filled with fluid lay in bowels. As if fluid rolled from one side to other of abdomen. As if thighs pierced with needles. As if feet made of wood.

Male - Testicles drawn up, feel constricted. Frequent pollutions. Loss of sexual power.

Female - Vaginismus with emaciation and constipation. Vulva and the vagina hypersensitive. Ovarian pain, better stretching legs. Menorrhagia with sensation of string pulling from abdomen to back. Cannot pass urine in pregnancy from lack of sensation or paralysis. Tendency to abortion from undeveloped uterus. Feeling of lack of room for fetus in uterus.

Chest - Oppression of chest, appearing periodically. Pressure on chest, especially when breathing deeply or laughing. Shootings in chest and sides, sometimes with obstructed respiration. Apices of lungs affected. Small red papules on chest, desquamation. Constitutions - Particularly adapted to adults, males more than females, particularly to persons of a dry, bilious constitution with somewhat jaundiced, irascible, hypochondriac or disposed to religious monomania.

Heart - Cardiac weakness. Pulse soft and small, dicrotic. Pulse wiry, slow sinks even to 40. Painful constriction of peripheral arteries.

Back - Spinal cord sclerosis. Lightning-like pains, temporarily better by pressure. Breasts - Stitches and burning pains in breasts (Apis, Con., Carb-an., SiV). Induration of breasts.Breasts become momentarily harder or smaller with colic. Causations - Ill effects of repelled eruptions. Sexual excess. Lead, cadmium or aluminum poisoning.

Limbs - Paralysis oflowerlimbs. Paralysis of single muscles. Pain in atrophied limbs, alternating with colic. Sciatica and muscular atrophy. Lightning like pains better by pressure. Stinging and tearing in limbs, also twitching and tingling, numbness, pain or tremor. Weakness and painful lameness of arms and hands. Extension is difficult. Paralysis from overexertion of the extensor muscles in piano players (Cur.). Arms shaky when attempting to use them. Wrist drop. Paralysis of lower limbs after childbirth. Pains in muscles of thighs, come in paroxysms. Cramps in calves. Loss of patellar reflex. Hands and feet cold. Feet swollen. As if feet were made of wood. Pain in right big toe, very sensitive to touch.

Sleep - Falls asleep while speaking, talking during sleep. Nocturnal sleeplessness with abdominal spasms. Jerks during sleep. Odd position during sleep. Must stretch in every direction. Many dreams, sometimes lascivious with erections. Coma and lethargy, sometimes with dizziness.

Skin - Oversensitive to open air. Dry, wrinkled, shriveled and drawn over the bones. Jaundice. Yellow, dark- brown liver spots. Bluish, red spots. Dilated veins of forearms and legs. Small wounds easily inflamed and suppurate. Dry, burning ulcers. Bed sores. Blisters, corns, bunions. Gangrene.

Modalities - Bending back ameliorates pressure in stomach, pain in epigastrium, pain in back. Bending double ameliorates colic. Better by hard pressure, rubbing, physical exertion, stretching limbs. Better at rest, lying down. Worse from motion, grasping smooth objects, touch. Worse mental exertion, company. Worse at night, open air, clear weather, foggy weather. Damp weather causes profuse salivation. Swelling in abdomen and cough are worse lying on right side.

Kidneys - Chronic interstitial nephritis with great pain in abdomen. Contracted kidney. Paralysis of bladder, difficult urination or retention, suppression. Frequent ineffectual tenesmus. Scanty urine. Urine profuse, but flows slowly, drop by drop. Albuminous, low specific gravity. Diabetes mellitus. Uremia.

Temperature - Coldness from exertion. General cold sweat during stools. Feet cold, only when walking.

author: Murphy

CLINICAL - AIDS. Bone, cancer. Bone marrow, affections. Brain, tumors. Cancer. Diarrhea. Fatigue. Fibrosis. Hodgkin's diseases. Leukemia. Lung, cancer. Lung, complaints. Radiation, poisoning. Thyroid, enlarged. Virus infections. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Very serious pathologies. Cancers, leukemia. Periodicalfatigue. Paralyzing fatigue. Chilliness and shivering, yet great feeling of heat in head and face. Desire to lie down from feeling of extreme heaviness. Body seems to be heavy like lead. Head very heavy, like an enormous weight, difficult to keep head up. Feels the pull of gravity. Desire to lie down on one's back and on the floor. Sensation of dryness in throat, as if swallowing of food would be impossible. Paralyzing pain in sacral region. Pain as if broken or twisted. Great restlessness at night. Weakness of lower limbs. Cannot walk upright, must crawl on all fours. MIND - Serious, no smile on the face, as if carrying burden of world on their shoulders. Extremely conscientious. Delusion of having too many responsibilities. Fastidious, impulse to put things in order. Deep religious feelings or philosophical thoughts. Feels alone and empty. Aggressive, reckless impulses. Irritability and aggression. Resentment, controlled anger. Reproachful, reproaches his wife. Outbursts of violence. Aggressive fantasies. Dominant behavior. Anxiety about health. Fear of falling ill, of catastrophes. Fear of narrow places, claustrophobia. Fear of one's own impulses, of being too aggressive. Panic-stricken. Persistent feeling of existential threat. Delusion of being threatened. Delusion of decaying and disintegrating. Depressed, dark gloomy mood. Weeping on account of physical pain. Sadness better company. Restlessness, cannot find a place or position to relax. Delusion of changing one's identity. Clairvoyant. Severe mental illnesses.

Head - Shattering headache, in forehead. Pain as if vertex comes up, as if it would explode. Pressing pain in forehead. Sensation of enormous heaviness. Sensation of great heat in head and face.

Eyes - Burning sensation. Food - Desires bacon, raw meat, lamb, pork, ham, fat.

Abdomen - Cutting pain, better bending double.

Rectum - Anal warts. Sensation of insecurity in rectum when passing flatus.

Back - Paralyzing pain in sacral region. Back pain extending to posterior part of thigh and popliteal region. Breasts - Sensation of heaviness and fullness in breasts. Sensation of tension in breasts, desire to wear a bra.

Limbs - Sensation of leaden heaviness. Sensation as if left leg were shorter. Pain in soles of feet on account of vesicles on toes.

Sleep - Short sleep improves. Sleeplessness and restlessness from pain in sacral region, tossing about to relieve pain; sleeplessness from feeling of heat. Dream of falling. Dream of killing or murders, of dead people, of bodies. RELATIONS - Compare: Androc., Aur., Care., Hydrog., Med., Rad-br., Stram., Syph., Tarent., Uran-n., X-ray. REFERENCES - Sherr.

Modalities - Better warmth, sitting in the sun, hot applications, hot bathing. Better massage, strong pressure, after long sleep. Worse from walking. Worse 3 p.m., sunset, evening, night. Worse overcast weather, first ray of sun.

name: Pneumococcinum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from the open air, in the country. Better from movement, a hot foot-bath, a short nap after meals (Nux- v.). Worse on entering a warm room, from damp before menses. Worse from inactivity (Rhus-t.), sitting for a long time, especially when remaining motionless, rest at night. Pains aggravated by rest, at night, better by movement (Rhus-t.)..
constitution: Hemicrania. Hypochondria. Memory, loss. Neuralgia of the skull. Pneumonia.
keynote:

CLINICAL - Hemicrania. Hypochondria. Memory, loss. Neuralgia of the skull.…
full:
PHARMACY - pneu. Pneumococcinum venenosum. Pneumococcus nosode. Bacteria of the Diplococcus genus, Micrococcales. Non-pathologic bacteria of the mucus membranes. Nosodes. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Hemicrania. Hypochondria. Memory, loss. Neuralgia of the skull. Pneumonia.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pneumococcus is a gram positive bacteria of the Diplococcus genus and of the Micrococcaceae family. Pneumococcus is a saprophyte host of the mucus membranes. It is found in the saliva, nasal and pharyngeal mucus, orthe conjunctiva of 50% of healthy subjects. Sevaus conducted a clinical symptomatological study, but there is no homeopathic proving. Respiratory complaints localized in the bronchial region. Cardiac palpitations. Dysmenorrhea with late menses and premenstrual syndrome. Intoxication. Depressive condition associated with pains situated all over the cervical and dorsal regions. Acute pains, which come suddenly of the stinging (Nit-ac.) or cramping type (Cupr.), lasting only a short while. Constricting pains, as if in a vice (Cact.). MIND - Loss of memory. Depressive condition with anguish, anxiety. Desire to stay at home, horror of going out (Sep.). Lack of taste for life. Impression that the patient is going to collapse, that he cannot walk. Very afraid of being ill, of dying.

Head - Pains in left frontal sinus. Headaches lasting for 3 to 4 consecutive days. Headache on coughing or bending the head. Frequent headaches, localized at the nape of the neck, worse by noise. Right or left hemicrania, worse by walking, which causes throbbing in the head. Feeling of liquid in the head on stooping.

Eyes - Fatigue from neon light. Frontal pains above the eyes.

Ears - Otitis media.

Mouth - Aphthae in the mouth.

Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Frequent nausea after eating. Gastric pains, especially when hungry. Stomach cramps with burning sensations. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Med. - amnesia for recent facts. Hasty with restless legs and burning in the heels. Burning pains in the joints and vertebral column. Improvement at the seaside and in the knee-chest position. (2) Thuj, - hydrogenoid condition, melancholy, worse from changing weather or after a trauma. Flatulence, diarrhea, periodic skin complaints. REFERENCES-Julian.

Abdomen - Bad digestion. Hepatic deficiency. Air in the stomach and colon. Distention and pain in the left hypochondrium, eased by expulsion of wind. Gas with alternation of constipation and fetid stools.

Rectum - Gas with the alternation of constipation and very fetid stools. Constipation with empty urging (Nux- v.). Constipation when traveling (Ign.).

Female - Premenstrual aggravation. Menstrual cycle short, every 22 or 24 days. Menses stopping on the 2nd day. Menses late, scanty, legs heavy and swollen before menses. Menstrual migraines and vertigo. Bearing down pain and crosses legs (Sep.). Burning sensation during intercourse in cases of fatigue. Frigidity. Lack of orgasm. Food - Ameliorated by eating (Anae.).

Heart - Aching in the precordial region with pains. Cardiac neurosis. Basedow's heart. Rhythmic anomalies. Emotive palpitations. Frequent palpitations at any time of the day. Palpitations forcing him to stop when walking rapidly or climbing stairs. Frequent redness of the face when going into a hot room.

Back - Dorsal and lumbar arthrosis. Dorsal pains, preventing standing. Constitutions - Bilious and nervous, depressive, anxious. Allergic, psoric constitutions. sycotic, cancerous, and tubercular constitutions.

Neck - Neck pains with frontal aching. Cervical pains with back aching. Chronic degenerative rheumatism of the cervical column.

Limbs - Pains in the arms. Pains in the legs. Legs restless, especially before menses (Zinc., Lach.). Legs heavy in the morning on waking. Trembling in the legs. Cramps in the feet. Poly-arthrosis. Lungs - Sinusitis. Tracheitis. Chronic bronchitis. Emphysema. Incessant cough with no expectoration, especially at night with nausea. Feeling of having a feather in the throat (Kali-bi.). Dry cough in the cold or heat. Coughs in the heat, particularly when entering a hot room and clears the throat (Rhus-t.). Sickening cough in the morning after breakfast. Does not cough any more after 9 a.m. Coughs a great deal as a result of frequent bronchitis during childhood. Has to stoop to cough.

Sleep - Sleepiness around 3 p.m.

Skin - Itching with eruptions spread over the neck and forehead. Small eruptions on the face. Hands clammy.

Modalities - Better from the open air, in the country. Better from movement, a hot foot-bath, a short nap after meals (Nux- v.). Worse on entering a warm room, from damp before menses. Worse from inactivity (Rhus-t.), sitting for a long time, especially when remaining motionless, rest at night. Pains aggravated by rest, at night, better by movement (Rhus-t.).

Kidneys - Weakness of the bladder. Passes urine when coughing (Caust.).

name: Podophyllum Peltatum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: External heat ameliorates pain in bowels. Better by pressure, rubbing or stroking liver. Better lying down, lying on abdomen, stretching in bed. Hot weather, summer, aggravates diarrhea. Worse in early morning, 2 a.m. to 4 a.m., night. Worse open air, washing. Worse eating, swallowing, drinking, acid fruits, milk. Worse before, during and after stool, dentition, mercury. Worse from motion, walking, ascending stairs, exertion..
constitution: Acidity. Amenorrhea. Anus, prolapsed. Asthma, bronchial. Bedwetting. Bilious, attack. Bronchitis. Cataract. Cholera. Cornea, ulcer. Dentition. Deafness. Depression. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Duodenum,catarrh. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspepsia. Fevers. Flatus. Gagging. Gallstones. Gastric, disorders. Goiter. Headaches. Heart, pain. Hemorrhoids. Jaundice. Liver, disorders. Ovary, disorders. Ovarian, tumo
keynote: PHARMACY - podo. Podophyllum peltatum. May-apple. American mandrake. N. O. Berberidaceae by some placed in Ranuncu- laceae. Closely related to both. Tincture of root gathered after ftuit has ripened of whole fresh plant of ripe fruit. Solution of resinous extract, podophyllin.…
full:
PHARMACY - podo. Podophyllum peltatum. May-apple. American mandrake. N. O. Berberidaceae by some placed in Ranuncu- laceae. Closely related to both. Tincture of root gathered after ftuit has ripened of whole fresh plant of ripe fruit. Solution of resinous extract, podophyllin. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acidity. Amenorrhea. Anus, prolapsed. Asthma, bronchial. Bedwetting. Bilious, attack. Bronchitis. Cataract. Cholera. Cornea, ulcer. Dentition. Deafness. Depression. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Duodenum,catarrh. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspepsia. Fevers. Flatus. Gagging. Gallstones. Gastric, disorders. Goiter. Headaches. Heart, pain. Hemorrhoids. Jaundice. Liver, disorders. Ovary, disorders. Ovarian, tumor. Palpitations. Pneumonia. Proctitis. Prolapsed, uterus. Prolapsed, rectum. Prostatitis. Pustules. Sciatica. Stomatitis. Strabismus. Taste, disorders. Tenesmus. Tongue, burning. Urticaria. Uterus, prolapsed. Vomiting. Whooping cough. Worms. Yellow, diarrhea.

HERBAL - Podophyllum grows throughout the United States in damp, shady places, usually in woods. It has five to nine-lobed leaves, large white nodding flowers, and yellowish, egg-shaped fruits. The fruits are not unlike a small lemon, hence the plant is sometimes called “wild lemon.” It flowers in May and June, and the fruit ripens in October. Indian tribes used the root to expel worms, and dropped the juice of the root into the ear to cure deafness. “All the tribes are fond of the fruit,” said Raffinesque, quoted by Hale, who gave an account of the medicine. The herbal practitioners adopted the remedy and used it as the “vegetable mercury.” The first homeopathic proving was made by Williamson.

HOMEOPATHIC - Podo, is a remedy for bilious constitution. It affects chiefly the duodenum, small intestines, liver, rectum, ovary, scapula and throat. It generally affects the right side. Torpidity of the liver. Jaundice. Hypogastric pain. Gastro-enteritis with colicky pain and bilious vomiting. Painless cholera morbus. Profuse diarrhea. Stool is watery with jelly-like mucus, painless, gushing and offensive. Diarrhea, while being bathed or washed, of dirty water soaking through napkin, with gagging. Portal engorgement with a tendency to hemorrhoid. Fullness of superficial veins. Relaxed sphincters. Prolapsed uterus. Pendulous abdomen after confinement. Troubles during pregnancy. Alternating conditions, diarrhea alternating with constipation, headache alternating with diarrhea. Sudden shocks from jerking pains. Constantly shaking and rubbing region of liver with hands. Much drowsiness and desire to stretch. Great loquacity during chill and heat. Thirst for large quantities of cold water. Viscid mucus in mouth, coating teeth. Intense desire to press the gums together. MIND - Fidgety and restless, cannot sit still. Whining. Child wants to be carried. Depression of spirits. Disgust for life, during headaches. Imagines he is going to die or be very ill. Delirium from eating acid fruits. Fatigue of mind from business. Aphasia. Want of power of expression even of simplest ideas. Absurd words being chosen in place of right ones. Stupid during paroxysm of fever patient. Loquacity during chill and fever, afterwards forgets what has passed. Inclined to talk, but would drop a sentence before half finished. Great desire to talk during chill, but can't because he forgets words.

Head - Headache, dull pressure, worse Podophyllum peltatum morning, with heated face and bitter taste. Headache alternating with diarrhea, or better by diarrhea. Darting pain in forehead, must close the eyes. Rolling of head from side to side with moaning, during dentition, from business worry. Child perspires on head during sleep.

Eyes - Jaundiced. Eyes sunken. Eyes glazed and motionless. Cataract. Smarting, inflammation of lids. Lids half closed. Pain in eyeballs and temples.

Ears - Aching pain in right ear, with rough feeling extending along right Eustachian tube.

Face - Hot. Cheeks flushed during diarrhea. Jaundiced.

Mouth - Offensive odor. Bitter, foul, putrid taste. Everything tastes sour or putrid. Loss of taste, could not tell sweet from sour. Tongue, broad, large, moist. Tongue coated as of mustard spread on it. Burning, rough or flabby indented tongue. Grinding the teeth at night. Difficult dentition with intense desire to press the gums together (Phyt.).

Throat - Gagging in infantile diarrhea. As of a lump in esophagus. Sore throat, pain extends to ears. Dryness, swallowing painful. Sore throat right extends to left. Rattling of mucus in throat. Goiter. Vertigo - Vertigo, tendency to fall forward. Vertigo with sensation of fullness above eyes. Vertigo while standing in open air. Vertigo from gastric or bilious disorders. COMMENTS - An unintentional Podo, proving recorded by E. V. Rose brought out the chief characteristics and showed that its reputation as a “vegetable mercury” is well deserved. At 11 a.m., Mr. J., 26 took grains x of Podo, lx to “stir up his liver.” At 6 p.m. he was taken with an indescribable sick feeling all over and a persistent, dry, rough feeling in pharynx and esophagus, extending along right Eustachian tube with dull, aching pain in right ear, feeling as though a ball or lump in upper esophagus. At 8 p.m., he had a dull and stupefying headache, chiefly frontal, worse lying down. Fullness in stomach, belching of gas, sour belchings, marked salivation and an offensive odor from the mouth. Sleep was disturbed, full of confused dreams, rolled and tossed about, bed felt too hard and a feeling as though head and shoulders were lying too low. At 3 a.m., urge to stool, which was profuse, watery, and dark green. Frequent urging. Before stool there was a peculiar weak, dull, griping pain below umbilicus, fullness in rectum. During stool there was a weak feeling in the stomach. After stool, tenesmus and faint feeling. These symptoms passed off in two or three days, the diarrhea was followed by Podophyllum peltatum constipation, which was quickly removed by Nux-v. External irritant. Produces a rawness like intertrigo when applied on the skin. The dust of the powdered root sets up intense inflammation, ulceration and leucoma if it gets into the eyes. Useful in potency for eye disorders. Irritation of the brain, generally reflected to the abdominal viscera (cholera infantum), or the teeth (dentition). Moaning and whining during sleep, the head is thrown back and rolls from side to side, the child grates its teeth. Great desire to press gums or teeth together. Salivation, foul breath and moist, tooth-indented tongue (Merc.). Burning sensation on the tongue. Thirst. Bilious, remittent, and intermittent fevers. Loquacity during chill and heat. Prone to sweat. Delirium, apt to be loquacious. Much drowsiness and desire to stretch. Congested, sensitive liver with excess or absence of bile. Generally for diarrhea with any other symptoms, painful or painless. Children's diarrhea (Ars., Nit-ac.). Yellow, profuse, offensive and excoriated diarrhea in infants with a raw and burning anus. Profuse stools, yellow or white. Early morning diarrhea. Dysentery, colitis. Cholera. Hepatitis concomitant with severe diarrhea. Severe cases of jaundice, gallstone attacks, and worms. The stools may be painless or may be preceded, accompanied, and followed by colic, tenesmus and other symptoms. Pains in sacrum in lumbar region with rectal and uterine symptoms, cramps in calves with stools. Fullness and tenderness of the rectum. Proctitis, inflammation of the rectum and anus. Tendency to prolapse in the rectum and genital organs. “Symptoms of prolapse uterus with pain in sacrum with muco- gelatinous stools,” and “sensation at stool as if the genital organs would fall out.” Pains in the ovaries, especially the right, extending down the anterior and inner side of thighs. Vomiting during pregnancy. Swelling of labia during pregnancy. “Can lie comfortably only on stomach” during the early months of pregnancy. Severe after- Podophyllum peltatum pains with strong bearing-down sensation, hemorrhoids and prolapsed rectum after confinement. Alternating conditions. Diarrhea alternating with constipation, headache alternating with diarrhea, headache in winter, diarrhea in summer, inflammation of scrotum or of the eyes, not of both. Antidotal to mercury. Worse hot weather. Nash cured an obstinate case of intermittent fever with violent chills, followed by intense fever with great loquacity. When the fever was past, the patient fell asleep and, on waking, remembered nothing of his loquacious delirium. W. A. Burr related a case of a young man who had for some weeks a burning sensation along the left edge of his tongue, occasionally shooting to tip or through to opposite edge. He had been in poor health, “bilious,” for years. With catarrh of stomach, duodenum and bile ducts, extreme discomfort followed even the blandest foods. Podo. 3x improved in two days and the tongue was well in a week. Clarke often cured prolapsed anus in children with Podo. 6c. With Podo, lx, Mr. Knox Shaw relieved “continual urging and straining” in a case of rectal cancer too far gone for operation. L. M. Barnes noted the case of a stout woman, 60, who complained of burning, aching, cutting pain in rectum. She was obliged to be on her feet all day. Nervous, cross, irritable. Podo, cured. Barnes also reported the case of a woman who, for four months after a miscarriage, had ovarian pain, worse at night. She was sleepless, nervous, restless. Bearing down in abdomen and back. She was a large, stout woman with a pendulous abdomen. Podo, cured after Puls, and Cimic. had only partially relieved. Guernsey mentioned that it is often called for in complaints of pregnant and parturient women with the sensation as if intestines were falling down. He mentioned also whooping cough with costiveness and loss of appetite. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Mand. – Great desire for sleep, exaggeration of sounds and enlarged vision. Bowels inactive, stools large, white andhard. (2) Aloe, Chel.,Merc., Nux-v., Sulph. (3) Prune. - colitis. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Stomach so weak that rice wouldn't digest. Heartburn, gagging or empty retching. Hot, sour belching, nausea and vomiting. Belchings smelling like rotten eggs. Constant gagging. Vomiting of a hot, frothy mucus. Vomiting of milk in infants.

Abdomen - Distended abdomen, heat and emptiness. Sensation of weakness or sinking. Can lie comfortably only on stomach. Fullness in right hypochondrium, with flatulence, pain and soreness. Rumbling and shifting of flatus in ascending colon. Rubs for relief. Weight in hypogastric region. Pain in right inguinal region, shoots down inner thigh to knees. Colic, in abdomen, with cramp-like knots, better flexing limbs. Colic continues after stool. Abdominal viscera are sore, worse during vomiting, diarrhea, before and during menses. Abdominal pains and stool excited by eating and drinking. Sick, empty feeling after stools.

Rectum - Fetid flatus. Long standing diarrhea. Diarrhea alternating with other symptoms. Diarrhea early in morning, during teething, with hot, glowing cheeks. Diarrhea while being bathed or washed, in hot weather, after acid fruits. Morning, painless diarrhea when not due to venous stasis or intestinal ulceration. Gurgling through the bowels, then yellow profuse putrid stools gush outpainlessly. Cholera infantum and morbus. Constipation alternating with diarrhea (Ant-c.). Constipation, clay-colored, hard, dry, difficult. Prolapse of rectum before or with stool. Internal and external hemorrhoids. Sensation of weakness in rectum. Severe burning, deep in rectum, after stool. Anus feels very sore, sensitive and swollen.

Stool - Stools yellow with undigested food. Stools green, watery, at times mixed with Podophyllum peltatum mucus, gushing. Yellow, fetid profuse diarrhea. Stools, white like water. Pale, hard, chalky stools. Stools foaming with meal-like sediment. Stools run right through the diaper, followed by weakness. Muco-gelatinous stools after miscarriage. Stools involuntary during sleep, when passing flatus.

Male - Diseases of prostate gland associated with rectal troubles.

Female - Suppressed menses with pelvic tenesmus. Menorrhagia from straining. Sensation as if the genitals would come out during stool. Pain in the region of the ovaries (right), down the crural nerve worse stretching the legs. Ovarian tumor with pain extending to shoulder. Pain in uterus and right ovary with shifting noises along ascending colon. Can lie comfortably only on the abdomen during early months of pregnancy. Swelling of labia during pregnancy. Hemorrhoids with prolapsed anus during pregnancy. Prolapsed uterus on straining or overlifting after childbirth. Food - Thirst for large quantities of cold water (Phos., Bry.). Appetite variable, at times voracious. Indifference to food. Loss of appetite. Smell of food causes loathing. Satiety from small quantity of food, followed by nausea and vomiting. Craves acids, which disagree. Worse after eating and drinking, especially acid fruit and milk. Diarrhea after sour milk, canned fruits, acid fruit and milk.

Chest - Oppression in chest. Pains in chest worse by deep inspiration. Catarrh of chest during dentition. Constitutions - Suited to persons of bilious temperament, especially after mercury poisoning.

Heart - Palpitations with a clucking sensation, rising up to the throat, from emotions.

Back - Nape of neck stiff, muscles sore. Pain under right scapula. Pain between shoulders. Pain in small of back. Pain in lumbar and sacral regions, worse during stool, and still worse after stool. Pain in loins, worse walking on uneven ground or from misstep.

Limbs - Paralytic weakness on left side. Pain between shoulders, under right scapula, in loins and lumbar region. Pain along ulnar nerve of both arms. Pain in right inguinal region, shoots down inner thigh to knees. Cramps in calves with stools.

Sleep - Sleepy after paroxysms of malaria. Heavy sleep, fatigue on waking. Moaning and whining during sleep. Rising up in sleep without waking. Sleep disturbed, full of confused dreams.

Skin - Moist, warm, jaundiced. Cold, clammy skin. Sallow skin jaundice, also in children. Rawness and itching of genitals. Erysipelas. Intolerable itching of body and arms. Urticaria. Pustules, slow in healing. Scabs on arms and legs.

Modalities - External heat ameliorates pain in bowels. Better by pressure, rubbing or stroking liver. Better lying down, lying on abdomen, stretching in bed. Hot weather, summer, aggravates diarrhea. Worse in early morning, 2 a.m. to 4 a.m., night. Worse open air, washing. Worse eating, swallowing, drinking, acid fruits, milk. Worse before, during and after stool, dentition, mercury. Worse from motion, walking, ascending stairs, exertion.

Liver - Sore and painful liver, better rubbing. Stitches in liver region, worse while eating. Liver and whole abdominal viscera are sore. Jaundice with gallstones. Lungs - Inclination to breathe deep, sighing. Sensation of suffocation. Pneumonia. Chronic bronchitis. Bronchial asthma, worse after Catching cold. Loose, dry, hacking cough, with remittent fever. Whooping cough with constipation and loss of appetite.

Kidneys - Frequent urination, at night, during pregnancy. Urinates immediately after drinking. Bedwetting. Diabetes mellitus and insipidus.

Perspiration - Profuse, offensive sweat with sleep. Warm sweat on head and legs. Sweats on head with coldness of skin. Sensations - As if strabismus would occur. Pain in head as from ice on occipital protuberance. As if tongue, throat and palate had been burned. Ball in upper esophagus. As if heart ascending to throat. As if a thousand live things moving about in abdomen or of fish turning over. As if everything would drop through pelvis.

Temperature - Chills at 7 a.m. with pain in hypochondria and knees, ankles, wrists. Great loquacity during fever.

Hyperlipidemia. Injuries. Joint, pains. Joint, weakness. Leucorrhea. Malaria. Metrorrhagia. Muscle, weakness. Pyorrhea. Sores. Sprains. Tendon, disorders. Tinnitus. Tumors. Vertigo. Wounds.

HERBAL - Polyg-m., in material doses of tincture or low potencies, has been found useful in treating all kinds of musculoskeletal disorders. Astringent, demulcent and tonic. Combined with otherremedies, Solomon's Seal is given in pulmonary consumption and bleeding of the lungs. It is useful also in female complaints. It is used mainly in the form of a poultice and is believed to pre vent excessive bruising and to stimulate tissue repair. The infusion of 1 oz. to a pint of boiling water is taken in wineglassful doses and is also used as an injection. It is a mucilaginous tonic, very healing and restorative, and is good in inflammations of the stomach and bowels, piles, and chronic dysentery. A distilled water made from the whole plant has been used as a skin tonic and is an ingredient of expensive cosmetics. Young shoots can be cooked, boiled and used as an asparagus substitute, they make an excellent vegetable and are widely used in Turkey. Root - cooked. Rich in starch. The root should be macerated for some time in water in order to remove bitter substances. Normally only used in times of famine, the root was powdered and then made into a bread by the North American Indians. COMMENTS - According to the English- Chinese Rare Chinese Materia Medica, raw ho-shou-wu, that is, the dried root that has not been prepared with soybeans, is used to treat toxicosis (infections yielding abscess, swellings beneath the skin, sores, carbuncles, and eruptive diseases like rubella), inflammation, constipation, and hyperlipidemia. The soybean-prepared ho-shou-wu is used as a tonic for yin and blood, nourishing the hair, strengthening the bones and muscles, and used to treat pale complexion, dizziness, tinnitus, premature graying of hair, weakness of loins and knees, numbness of extremities, metrorrhagia, profuse leucorrhea, weakness due to lingering diseases (e.g., malaria), and hyperlipemia. According to evaluations done with raw and processed ho-shou-wu, the processed version does have different properties, and is the one with the most dramatic effects on preserving the immune system functions. Processed ho-shou-wu is currently the only one that is regularly exported from China. During the past thousand years in China, processed ho-shou-wu has been used to nourish the liver and kidney, promote the growth of hair, treat alopecia, and premature graying of hair. RELATIONS - Compare: Bell-p., Ruta, Calc., Symphytum. REFERENCES - Murphy.

PHARMACY - polyg. Polygonum punctatum. Smartweed. Polygonum hydropiper. Polygonum acre. Persicaria urens. Water pepper. Pursh. N. O. Polygonacae. Britain, North America. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Antrum, pain. Blepharitis. Colic, flatulent. Cough. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Dysuria. Eczema. Epilepsy. Gonorrhea. Gravel. Heart, disorders. Hemorrhoids. Hysteria. Laryngitis. Nephritis. Neuralgia. Orchitis. Prostatitis. Sciatica. Spermatic cord, pain. Spleen disorders. Strangury. Ulcers.

HERBAL - The Polygonum are named by Gerarde “Arse-smarts.” Burnett regarded it as a splenic and as useful in old cases of syphilis. As a splenic, he found it was often required in cases of gout and in gouty eczema with much irritation; he used it with much benefit in the 6c, 12c and 30c. Hale stated, “Smart Weed is a popular domestic remedy throughout U.S.A. Applied externally it has the effect of a mustard plaster and the leaves saturated with hot water are applied to relieve cramps and colic. Also as an emollient in inflammation and sprains.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Polyg. was proved by W. E. Payne and others. The provers were all men, but clinical experience has shown a definite action in the female generative sphere, as amenorrhea, aversion to sex and congestion of the ovaries have been cured by it. Acts upon the genito-urinary organs and the intestines, causing cutting pains, along the ureters, along ovarian ducts, up spine with bearingdown. Pulsating, flashing, wandering pains in prostate. Coldness alternating or coincides with heat in the same or other part, burning in chest with cold feeling in pit of stomach. Smarting discharges. Leading symptoms include aching pains in hips and loins with weight and tension in pelvis and tearing in groin, worse right. Metrorrhagia, also amenorrhea in young Polygonum punctatum girls. Varicose veins, hemorrhoids and rectal pockets. Burning in stomach followed by feeling of coldness in the pit of the stomach.

Head - Acute pulsative pains in temples.

Eyes - Puffiness under right eye. Lids twitch when closed and when lying down.

Ears - Acute pain, on bending head down, better bending backwards.

Face - Coldness in right face, when pain is most severe in left.

Mouth - Itching, burning palate, wants to scratch it. Tongue feels swollen.

Abdomen - Cold feeling in stomach with burning in chest. Cutting pains with great rumbling, as if whole intestinal contents were in a fluid state. Griping pain with great rumbling, nausea and liquid feces. Flatulent colic. Nausea. Breasts - Shooting pains through the breasts.

Rectum - Hemorrhoids with itching. Interior of anus studded with itching eminence. Liquid feces. Sensations - As of sudden rising of scalp. As if whole intestinal contents were fluid. As if hips drawn together. As of galvanic shock through lower limbs.

Male - Scrotum excoriated. Pulsating, burning pain in prostate on urinating. Pain in testes, spermatic cord on urinating.

Female - Metrorrhagia, amenorrhea in young girls. Cutting pain along the fallopian tubes with bearing down. Aching pains in hips and loins. Sensation as if hips were being drawn together. Sensation of weight and tension within pelvis.

Limbs - Aching in lower limbs. Feet alternately hot and cold. Sore pains in heels.

Skin - Superficial ulcers and sores on lower limbs, especially in females at menopause. Urticaria. COMMENTS - Lancinating, cutting, pulsating, shooting, wandering and flashing pains. One prover described them as like aurora borealis, and a case of sciatica with pains of this description was cured with Polyg. The left temple was markedly affected, left side generally more so than right. Epilepsy and hysteria. Marked diarrhea (Rheum, and Rumx.) and dysuria. Excessive weakness, trembling and sensitiveness to cold. Cold sensations, alternating or coinciding with heat in the same or other parts. Coldness of right side of face when pain in left side was most severe. Burning in chest with cold feeling at pit of stomach. Feet burning, then suddenly cold. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Card-m. - ulcers. (2) Ham., Senec. (3) Polyg-pe. - kidney colic, stones, gangrene. (4) Polyg-s. (5) Polyg-a. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Modalities - Better from warmth. Worse pressure of clothes. Worse by cold, damp, change of temperature. Lying down causes pressure in occiput, dizziness and wavering of sight. Rising causes sudden pain in occiput.

Kidneys - Nephritic colic with grinding, griping, cutting bellyache. Suppurative nephritis. Cystitis. Painful constriction at neck of bladder. Cutting pain along ureters. Urine scanty, dribbling, dark or calcareous, adherent sediment.

CLINICAL - Anus, prolapse. Constipation. Hemorrhoids. Intermittent,fever. Liver, disorders. Malar bone, pain. Neuralgias. Prolapse, anus. Rheumatism. Spleen, disorders. Tonsils, enlarged. Polyporus pinícola HOMEOPATHIC - The pine agaric, Polyp-p., like the larch agaric, Polyporus officinalis, or Bol., was proved by Dr. Burt. The symptoms of the two have a very close resemblance and many are common to both. Hale said it is a remedy for ague in the middle and southern states, taken during the intermission macerated in whisky. Quotidian fevers are most suited to it. Intermittent, remittent and bilious fevers with headache, yellow tongue, constant nausea, faintness at epigastrium and constipation. Despondency, aching distress in many parts. Stiffness of back of fingers, enlarged tonsils with dysphagia and constant inclination to swallow. Neuralgic pains in head, face and temples, pain in liver and spleen with diarrhea or constipation and hemorrhoids these are the chief features of the proving. Modalities - Better by rest. Worse in damp air. Worse after stool, motion, walking. COMMENTS - Great lassitude. Congestion of head with vertigo, face hot and flushed, prickling sensation all over. Headache about 10 a.m. with pain in back, ankles and legs increasing until 3 p.m., then gradually better. Restless at night from pain in wrists and knee, rheumatic pains. Profuse perspiration. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Similar to its botanical relative, Polyporus officinalis or Bol. Deep dull, severe pain in shin bones, preventing sleep. (2) Bol-lu., Agar. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - pop-c. Populus candicans. Balm of Gilead. Populus balsamifera. N. O. Salicaceae. The name Balm of Gilead tree is given to the Black Italian Poplar. Tincture of the resinous buds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aphonia. Asthma. Brain, congested. Bullae. Colds. Constipation. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspepsia. Dysphagia. Ecthyma. Heart disorders. Liver, disorders. Phosphaturia. Sinusitis. Sunstroke. Throat, sore. Vagina, burning.

HERBAL - The name Populus balsamifera applies especially to the variety Populus candicans, but also to all P. balsamiferae. In England, the name “Balm of Gilead tree” is given to the Black Italian Poplar, which abounds in Italy, but the origin of which is not known. C. F. Nichols gave an account of Pop-c., the effects of which he observed. “The resinous gum exuding from buds and stalks, deliciously aromatic in perfume is widely used to heal wounds, open sores and eruptions and often suppresses these latter to the harm of the patient.” As an application, Nichols said, it is like Arn., dangerous, though most people are not susceptible to its poisonous effect. He never saw blisters of the size of those of Pop-c. produced by any other drug. Blisters hung down like bags of water the size of walnuts. Burning was a common symptom in the eyes, nose, throat, bowels, vagina.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pop-c. seems to have a remarkable power over acute colds, especially when accompanied by a deep, hoarse voice or even aphonia. Instantaneous voiceproducer (Coca). General insensibility of surface, worse back and abdomen, rubbing and pounding borne without pain and is grateful on account of warmth produced. Fingertips thickened, horny insensible to pinching and prickling. MIND - Loquacity. Discusses her symptoms with everyone. Hopeless foreboding, worse after sleep. Fear and anguish. Expectation of death. Feels as if the will were paralyzed. Vanishing of thought. Forgets to finish a sentence. Voices sound distant and words just spoken seem as if uttered long ago, objects seem multiplied.

Head - Weight on vertex. Hot head with cold limbs. Cold-sores on lips (Nat-m.). Burning irritation of eyes, nose, mouth, throat and air passages.

Eyes - Sensation as if left eye were twisted during the headache. Burning irritation in eyes, nose, mouth, throat, and air passages.

Face - Face yellow. Burning, prickling on face.

Mouth - Speech thick. Taste bitter, sweet in morning.

Throat - Rawness and soreness of throat. Throat is red, dry. Throat and nostrils burn. Burning and paralysis in throat. Pharynx and larynx feel dry and the voice weak and toneless. Acute hoarseness.

Stomach - Belching of gas, feeling like hot steam. Nausea with a sinking in epigastrium. Vomits bile.

Abdomen - Flatulent colic, doubling the body forward. Pain in right hypochondrium with enlargement. Wears her clothes loose.

Rectum - Stools small, round, preceded by cramps in abdomen, lack of expulsive power. Constipation, bowels feel hot and dry. Stools watery, green, alternating with constipation. Sensations - Whole body feels swollen, bruised, lame, sore and painful, exhausted as in dry, sultry weather. Eye feels twisted with the headache.

Female - Menses scanty, usually delaying, afterwards absent, then abundant, early, with dysmenorrhea, better hot cloths. Vagina burns as if scalded. Food - Appetite lost, loathes meat. Nothing relished. Hungry but dares not eat for fear of choking.

Chest - Rawness, soreness of chest, throat.

Heart - Pain in heart, stitches. Palpitations when rising or lying on left side with vertigo. Heart’s sound irregular, usually muffled, worse before menses.

Back - Numbness in back radiating from spine. Burning weariness in lower back.

Limbs - Fingertips thickened, horny, insensible to pinching and pricking. Nails blue as in ague (not thickened). Lungs - Suffocation. Breathing dry, asthmatic with dyspnea. Sits bent forward with dry cough, worse lifting arms. Dry cough when tired. Cough caused by “cobwebs” in his throat. Cough of children caused by naso- pharyngeal catarrh, mucus drops from posterior sinuses.

Sleep - Sleepless after midnight with restlessness. Dreams frightful, vivid, fearful after fitful sleep.

Skin - Skin harsh, dry and cold with burning-stinging. Burning, prickling on face, chest, and hands. Blisters hanging down like bags of water.

Modalities - Better hot applications. Worse on moving, lifting arms, contact of clothes. Worse after sleep, before menses. Worse after food and drink.

Tongue - Tongue white, dry, feels thick and numb. Tongue and mouth feel burnt and dry, but are moist, worse after food and drink. Vertigo - Vertigo from lifting head. Vertigo and heat of head as if scorched by sun. COMMENTS - W. C. Stilson related a case of poisoning in a man who one evening drank rum in which Balm of Gilead buds had been placed for making a liniment. A few hours later his wife heard him breathing heavily and on waking him found he could not speak. Stilson found him only able to speak in hoarse whispers and he would forget in the middle of a sentence what he was going to say. Face ashy pale, wild look. Tongue and mouth dry. Throat dry, burning, constricted, felt as if spiders had spun webs on it. It was some days before he recovered. Since this occasion, Stilson cured several cases of catarrhal hoarseness and aphonia with Pop-c. and one case of nervous aphonia. Mrs. S. had nervous prostration and, during the attack, aphonia. The aphonia remained after the patient got well otherwise. Among the peculiar symptoms observed by Nichols is surface anesthesia with or without numbness. The fingertips are thickened, horny, insensible to pinching and pricking. Skin is harsh, generally dry and cold with a stinging burning behind the surface as if an eruption would appear or as if sweat would break out. Numbness in back radiating from spine. Constipation, bowels feel hot and dry. The menses were at first scanty, later abundant and early, with dysmenorrhea pain, better by application of hot cloths. RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Rhus-t. Compare: (1) Salx-a., Pop. (2) Salicylates. (3) worse contact of clothes, Lach. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Kidneys - Urine strong, high colored, hot, scanty, increased, variously colored, red, dark, light, phosphates abundant. Urine dark, straw color, smoky.

Temperature - Fever and unrest. Fever with congestion of brain, fullness, heaviness, dullness, soreness. Dry heat. Sweat on head and neck. Sudden coldness of limbs with numbness of them and heat of head.

name: Populus Tremuloides
author: Murphy

HERBAL - Prim-o. is an ornamented variety of primrose. Gardeners, amateur and professional, have discovered after much suffering that in some people it has a powerful action on the skin, taking place chiefly by contact but partly by effluvia.

HOMEOPATHIC - The poison of the Primrose is in its glandular hairs, which break easily and discharge an irritating fluid which is absorbed into the skin. But skin symptoms of poisoning appear in sensitive patients even without coming in direct contact with the plant, mere nearness begin sufficient, like poison ivy. Prim-o. has deep infiltration and tension of tissues. Paralyzed sensation. Weakness. Pain in liver and spleen. Pharyngeal soreness alternates with diminished facial irritation. Blisters. Intermittent symptoms, worse right side.

Eyes - Burning irritation of eyeballs and eyelids, nostrils, and mouth. Lids greatly swollen, covered with large bullae. Lids half closed, stiff and immovable.

Face - Moist eczema. Papular eruption on chin. Burns at night. Urticaria-like eruption. Eyelids swollen.

Abdomen - Pain in region of liver, and a less severe pain in spleen, worse by bending from side to side.

Limbs - Eczema on arms, wrists, forearms, hands, papular and excoriated. Purple blotches on back of hands, palmar surface stiff. Blisters on fingers. Palms dry and hot. Cracking over joints and fingers. Rheumatic pain around shoulder.

Skin - Eruption between fingers. Great itching, worse at night, red and swollen like erysipelas. Tumefied. Small papules on a raised base. Skin symptoms accompanied by febrile symptoms.

Temperature - At night feverish, hands and face would burn, then intolerable itching. COMMENTS - The Rev. F. H. Brett, who was one of the first to notice its poisonous properties, undertook to prove it. He had handled the plants freely up to that time without experiencing any ill effect. He cut up some young plants and added some vigorous fresh leaves of an old one and made a tincture. This he allowed to stand for a week and then took three or four drops, three times a day for four days. Two days after ceasing to take it symptoms began to develop in the right little finger and two days afterwards in the right thumb. These became very intense and ran a chronic course. He could not go near a plant of Prim-o. without worsening the symptoms. They were also worse at night, and by rubbing or scratching. At the same time, Brett noted that the pains in the liver and spleen to which he had been subject now troubled him no more. The right hand was much more affected than the left. Clarke cured a chronic psoric dry eruption on the leg of a woman with Prim-o. 3c. Cooper relieved a case of severe eczema on the leg with bleeding. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rhus-t., Fago, (antidotal). (2) Hume., similar skin symptoms. (3) Anag., Prim-v., Verat. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - Progesterone is a hormone secreted by the ovary in the second two weeks of the menstrual cycle in reproductive age ovulating women. Progesterone, or progesterone-like substances called progestogens or progestins, are ingested by women in birth control pills and menopausal hormone replacement therapy. Progesterone acts to stabilize the tissue lining of the uterus (endometrium) so if it is absent, such as with ovarian anovulation, irregular and heavy menstrual bleeding often occurs after a period without any menstrual bleeding. Thus progesterone is used to prevent this irregularity of bleeding if it is given continuously. If, on the other hand, a onetime bolus of progesterone is given such as with a shot or with only 5 days of oral pills, then the falling progesterone levels will actually cause an estrogen-primed endometrium to slough and therefore start a menses. It is sometimes used to induce a menstrual period or regulate abnormal bleeding problems if menses are skipping or bleeding is irregular or prolonged. Progesterone has been used as therapy for premenstrual syndrome and for women with infertility or frequent miscarriages. Too much progesterone often causes tiredness and even sedation. This side effect can be beneficial in a women who has epilepsy or even uterine irritability causing preterm labor because progesterone in high doses can decrease seizure activity and uterine contractions. Progesterone tends to promote vaginal dryness by counteracting the effect on lubrication of estrogens, and it can also decrease the amount of menstruation or block it entirely by reversing estrogen effect on the growth of the uterine lining. Progestegens can cause some medical conditions to worsen, examples are asthma, heart failure, epilepsy and migraine headache. Natural progesterone tends to have fewer side effects. Progesterone can cause blood clots, particularly in the legs. Irregular vaginal bleeding. Breast tenderness. Liver disease. Painful swelling of the abdomen. Bloating. Nausea. Constipation. Head - Digestive migraine. Frontal headache with feeling of heaviness, aggravated during the week preceding menses. Headache in the morning. Headache with diarrhea and furred tongue. Pressing pains. Beats head against the bed. Knocks head against things. Hair falls out. Alopecia.

Eyes - Burning pains. Acute pains, stitching. Pains ameliorated by pressure. Eyes red, tired by light. Intermittent failing of sight. Meibomian cyst.

Ears - Acute or burning pains like otitis, but without fever. Noises during vertigo. Ménière's disease.

Nose - Impression of greasy discharge at the back of the nose. Hypertrophic chronic rhinitis. Nasal blockage. Nasal obstruction in warm room.

Face - Dryness of lips. Corners of mouth cracked. Itching of upper lip. Herpes about lips. Acne on chin.

Mouth - Aphthae and mouth ulcers. Taste of salt in the mouth. Gums sensitive. Cracking at the corners of the lips, resistant to treatment.

Throat - Acute pharyngitis with difficulty speaking. Dryness during excitement. Vertigo - Vertigo when looking at moving objects, while riding in a carriage, during railroad travel. Vertigo with feeling that the ground is coming up to meet him. Vertigo, accompanied by colored lights. COMMENTS - Keynote suddenness and violence with nervous symptoms and spasm. Slow build up of stress with a sudden catastrophe. Emotional hysteria (Ign., Nat-m.). Violent temper in a child with kicking. Spasm in peripheral vessels, Raynaud's Syndrome (Sec.). Migraines headaches with blurred vision and Meniere's syndrome. Petit mal attacks of epilepsy. Herpetic eruptions with pain out of proportion to the lesion. Angioneurotic edema. Hemorrhage or perforation without any previous stomach symptoms but with a history of nervous strain. RELATIONS - Related: Ign., Nat-m., Apis, Cupr. Compare: (1) Psor. - Inhibition, chilliness, sadness, periodic migraine, nocturnal need to eat, morning diarrhea, weakness in the back and joints, evil-smelling eruptions, appearing in winter, disappearing in summer. (2) Sulph. - Allergic, psoric conditions, burning skin with eruptions and itching. Impatient, quarrelsome, asthenic. (3) Tub. - Unstable, emotional, aggravated by physical or mental effort, emaciation, sweating, morning diarrhea. Aggravated by damp and cold and weather changes. REFERENCES - Bach. Julian.

Stomach - Stomach pain while fasting. Empty sensation in stomach, not better eating. Acidity, heartburn, sourness. Acrid dyspepsia. Aerophagy. Gastric and duodenal ulcers.

Abdomen - Hematemesis and melaena. Aerophagy. Acrid dyspepsia. Gastric and duodenal ulcers. Spasmodic colon infections. Oxyuric diseases.

Rectum - Diarrhea from excitement. Diarrhea with headache and furred tongue. Alternation of diarrhea and constipation. Constipation with empty urging. Sensation of a lump. Hematemesis and melaena. Presence of oxyuris in stools. Stools yellow, soft, in the morning after breakfast.

Female - Blood-streaked, brownish discharge before menses. Menses regular, with blood clots for seven days. Menses clotted, protracted. Fibrous blood clots at the end of menses. Leucorrhea before menses, between menses. Leucorrhea, acrid, brown, copious. Leucorrhea offensive, thick. Copious white discharge, worse during ovulation. Vaginitis. Metritis of the cervix. Vulvar pruritus. Anal and vulvar boils. Food - Food allergies. Desires fats, butter, eggs, rich food. Desires sweets, sugar, salt. Aversion to butter, pork, beef. Aversion to eggs, especially hard-boiled eggs. Aversion to cranberries, raw food, salads, green beans, cucumber, onions, garlic. Aversion to chocolate, which he cannot digest. Worse fats, rich food, eggs, garlic, cranberries, cucumber and chocolate.

Chest - Eruptions, boils in axilla. Constitutions - Allergic and psoric constitutions. Carbonic, flouric, and phosphoric constitutions.

Heart - Coronary disease. Angina pectoris. Feeling of weight in the precordial region. Palpitations after excitement. Palpitations from the slightest emotion, when lying down.

Back - Backaches. Spinal neurasthenia. Hernia.

Limbs - Arthritic diathesis. Sciatic pain. Intermittent claudication. Legs look bruised. Pain in the calf, pain forcing him to walk with a stick, cramps in the legs. Pain in calves of legs after walking. Muscular cramps. Functional or professional contracture. Writer's cramp, pianist's cramp, dancer's cramp. Spasms of the hands. Flexor contraction of the little finger. Cannot close the hand. Awkwardness of hands, drops things. Moist eruptions, eczema, on backs of hands. Coldness and blueness of hands. Feet numb, as if frozen, aggravated by cold weather. Hammer-toes. Lungs - Cough with sputum.

Sleep - Dreams of dead people, of death or dying.

Skin - Eczema. Itching vesicles. Boils maturing slowly. Herpes. Herpetic eruptions at muco-cutaneous margins. Papular, pustular eruption, erythematous, dry, peeling. Severe pruritus. Nails split. Hair falls out. Alopecia.

Modalities - Better resting, lying down, one hour after rising. Better from stretching, eating, drinking whisky. Better from mild temperature, in the mountains. Aggravation in the morning on waking, from exertion, from climbing stairs. Worse from drinking wine. Worse in stormy weather, cold, winter, heat, exposure to sun. Worse from lying down, at night.

Kidneys - Pyelitis. Pyelonephritis. Pain in the loin. Cystitis, after eating pork. Violent, burning pains in the urethra. Urine cloudy and fetid. Whitish tissues in the urine.

Temperature - Copious perspiration from the axilla, falling in large drops, clammy hands.

HERBAL - Prunella vulgaris is useful in sore and relaxed throat. Astringent. Internal bleeding, leucorrhea, etc. The infusion of 1 oz to 1 pt of boiling water is taken internally in doses of a wineglassful. Externally it is used as a gargle and injection. Culpeper wrote, “Here is another herb of Venus, Self-heal whereby when you are hurt you may heal yourself; it is a special herb for inward and outward wounds. Take it inwardly in syrups for inward wounds, outwardly in unguents and plasters for outward. The juice thereof used with oil of roses to annoint the temples and forehead is very effectual to remove headache.” COMMENTS - There is an old German saying that “He needs neither physician nor surgeon that hath Self- heal and to help himself. “ REFERENCES - Murphy. Potter.

Glaucoma. Heart, af- fection. Headaches. Hernia. Herpes zoster. Leucorrhea. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Neuralgias. Sprains. Strangury. Stricture. Toothache. Vitreous, opacities.

HOMEOPATHIC - Prun.wasprovedbyWahle. The symptoms resemble those of Prun-p. in general, but some very strongly characterized ones were produced. Acts especially on the nerves, respiratory orbital and on urinary organs. Special action on the urinary organs and the head. Shooting from within out, from before backward. The pains were pressive, and out pressing and out-shooting. Lightning like pains, wandering, causing shortness of breath. Spraining pains and pains which take away the breath. Pains are felt in the skull, eye, root of the nose and ears. The teeth feel raised out of their sockets. Glaucoma, choroido-retinitis, irido-choroiditis, irido-cyclitis. Ciliary neuralgia (Spig.). Neuralgias. Nerve paralysis. Anasarca and edema. Dropsy caused by defective heart. Ankle and foot feel sprained. Pains after shingles. Cramps. Compensatory effects. MIND - Restlessness, walks about constantly, cannot remain in one place.

Head - Pressing, tearing pain beneath skull. Shooting from right frontal bone through brain to occiput. Headache from heat of sun. Piercing toothache, as if teeth were pulled out, worse taking anything warm.

Eyes - Ciliary neuralgia. Shooting like lightning through the brain to occiput. Sudden pain in eyeball as if it would burst, better by lachrymation. Irido-choroiditis. Opacity of vitreous humor.

Mouth - Teeth feel pulled out. Toothache better by biting teeth together.

Abdomen - Ascites. Cramp-like pain in bladder region, worse from walking.

Rectum - Hard, nodular stool with rectal pain, as if angular body were pressed inward. Burning in anus after slimy diarrhea. Sensations - As if a sharp corner pressing against top of head. As is skull would be pressed outward by a sharp plug. Headache as if from sun. As if inner portion of eye would be torn out. Eyeball as if crushed or pressed asunder. Sighing as if climbing a steep mountain. As if small of back had been injured. As if right thumb sprained, as if left ankle sprained, as if first joint of big toe pulled out.

Male - Pulsation in glans from jar of walking.

Female - Menses, thin, watery, too early, too copious, with sacral pain. Leucorrhea, acrid, watery purulent, staining yellow.

Chest - Angina pectoris.

Heart - Hypertrophied. Cardiac dropsy. Angina pectoris. Throbbing of carotid arteries. Knocking at heart with labored breathing, worse least motion. Furious beating of heart, worse slightest motion.

Back - As of a lump below the left scapula. Causations - Ill effects of sun, sprains, over-lifting.

Limbs - Edema of feet. Itching at the fingertips as if frozen. Thumb as if sprained, hindering writing. Lungs - Oppression of chest, anxious, short respiration. Wheezing when walking. Short breath with pains. Feeling as if air inhaled did not reach the pit of stomach, has to yawn and try to take a deep inspiration. Air hunger.

Skin - Herpes zoster. Dropsy. Itching on fingertips, as if frozen.

Modalities - Better from rest, doubling up. Biting the teeth together helps toothache. Worse stooping, ascending, motion, jarring, must walk carefully. Worse by touch, pressure, night. Toothache worse from warm food.

Kidneys - Neuralgic dysuria. Tenesmus of bladder. Ineffectual effort to urinate. Urgent desire to urinate, urine reaches glans penis and then returns with violent pain and spasms and tenesmus in rectum. Cramp in bladder from pressure of flatus, must double up to urinate. Glans pains on urinating. Must press a long time before urine appears. Pulsating pudendum. Stream of urine thin like a thread or forked.

Temperature - Night sweat. COMMENTS - “Breath al ways seems to remain sticking in pit of stomach.” This symptom, with “pain as if sprained in left ankle,” led Lippe to make a remarkable cure in the case of a young woman, 16, who jumped from a carriage while the horse was running away and sprained her ankle. Left ankle and foot much swollen. As swelling abated, breathing became rapid, great oppression with constantly recurring desire to take a long breath, felt as if air inhaled did not reach pit of stomach and until she could force air so far down had to yawn and try to take a deep inspiration. The tightness, stitches and sticking pains in chest have marked Prun. as a remedy in many cases of neuralgic pains with or following herpes zoster. “Flatulence presses on bladder and causes cramps in bladder so that he is obliged to double up.” Strangury. Hurriedly compelled to pass urine, which seems to pass forward into glans penis and then return and cause most violent pain in urethra. Menses are too early, too profuse, last too long, and are thin and watery. There is lectureship, which weakens and stains yellow. The right side is much more affected than the left. C. M. Boger gave the case of a man, 60 with enlarged prostate, had frequent urging to urinate, day and night. Shooting pains in neck of bladder unless desire to urinate is at c nee gratified. D. Urination delayed if any great amount has accumulated. Spasmodic tenesmus of bladder and rectum at close of urination with pains in glans. Pulsation in glans from jar of walking. Prun. 1,000c. (Fincke) removed the symptoms. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Laur. (2) Prun- p., bird-cherry - sore throat, pressure behind sternum and sticking pain in rectum. (3) Pyrus., mountain ash - irritation of eyes, constriction around waist, spasmodic pains in uterus, bladder, heart, cold-water sensation in stomach, coldness extends up esophagus, neuralgic and gouty pains. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
