HERBAL - Pasque flower is in bloom at Easter, its flowers have been used for coloring Easter eggs. It is a medicine of ancient times, and its affinity for the eyes seems to have been noted from the beginning. Perhaps its tearful propensities gave rise to the legend that it sprang from the tears of Venus. Dioscorides mentions it as a remedy for headache and ophthalmia.

HOMEOPATHIC - Stoerck was the forerunner of Hahnemann in the modem use of Puls.; he employed it especially in chronic disorders of the eyes (catarrh, amaurosis, spots on cornea). Pulsatilla affects the emo- tions, veins, mucus membranes, respiration and one side. It is pre-eminently a female remedy, especially for mild, gentle, yielding disposition. Useful in acute as well as chronic diseases. Most suitable when not only the physical symptoms correspond but also when the mental and emotional disorders peculiar to the remedy encounter similar states in the disease to be cured, or at least in the temperament of the patient. The disposition and mental state are the chief guiding symptoms. Sad, crying readily, weeps when talking. Moody, contradictory. Changing, shifting symptoms, known as a weather cock remedy. Alternations. Symptoms rise to a certain pitch, then suddenly cease. Changeable nature. Erratic temperatures in fevers. Alternate pallor and redness of face. Wandering pains shift rapidly from one part to another, also with swelling and redness of the joints. Hemorrhages apparently stop and in a few hours return. Stools constantly changing color, no two stools alike. When one set of symptoms comes on another vanishes. Symptoms appear on one side or go to side lain on. The patient seeks the open air, always feels better there, even though he is chilly. Thirstless, chilliness and shortness of breath with digestive or menstrual disorders. Chilliness with pains but burning with stitching pains with numbness. Mucus membranes are all affected. Mucus discharges are profuse, bland, thick, yellowish- green.Metastasis. Hemorrhages, passive, vicarious, blood dark, easily coagulating. Varicose veins. Anemia. Emaciation of suffering parts. Symptoms in distant parts of the body cause dyspnea. Epilepsy with absent or irregular menses. Never well since puberty. Chorea from amenorrhea or dysmenorrhea. Peevish. Great sensitiveness. Scraping, jerking, tearing, ulcerative pains, wandering pains. Numbness, partial, hands, feet etc. of the part lain on of suffering parts. Heaviness. Pulsation through whole body. Wants the head high. Feels uncomfortable with only one pillow. Lies with hands above head. The longer he lies in the morning, the longer he wishes to lie. Child wants to be carried slowly. Sensation of distention in size, as if one part or every part were growing too large during pain. Bandaged sensation. Wearing of flannels or woolen clothes cause itching and eruptions. Great inclination to stretch feet. Often indicated after abuse of iron tonics and after badly managed measles. MIND - Changeable moods. Timid, irresolute. Mild, emotional and tearful. Highly emotional, easily moved to tears and laughter. Craves affection and sympathy. Desires company. Capricious. Easily discouraged. Whining. Wandering thoughts. Forsaken feeling. Sadness from disagreeable news. Sadness from injuries of head. History ofabandonment or grief. Silentgrief with submissiveness. Remorse in evening. Weeps easily. Can hardly give her symptoms without weeping. Better being held and hugged. Weeps at everything, whether it is joyful or sorrowful. Weeping when disturbed at work. Weeps easily before menses. Over-sensitiveness to pain. Given to extremes of pleasure and pain. Consolation improves all symptoms. Children like to be carried slowly and held. Children like affection and caresses. Children are extremely affectionate, which they manifest by kissing and caressing. Very irritable, touchy, feels slighted or fears slight. Sensitive to reprimand. Easily offended. Answers yes or no by nodding head. Selfishness. Miserly. Jealousy. Envy. Delusion she is alone in the world, that she is always alone. Suspicious. Disgusted at everything. Fastidious. Fixed ideas about food, sex, religion. Imagines that certain articles of food are not good for the human race. Fixed ideas about marriage. Thinks that sex is a sinful act. Religious melancholy. Religious mania. Mania from suppressed menses. Despair of salvation, seeks aid in constant prayer. Weary of life, thinks of drowning. Full of cares about domestic affairs. Anxiety better open air, better motion. Anxiety and uneasiness in bed, must uncover. Fear, wants to hide or run. Fear of abandonment, of being unlovable. Fear of marriage. Morbid dread of opposite sex. Fear of being alone, of dark, of ghosts in the evening. Fear of high places. Fear of insanity.

Head - Confusion of head as after intoxication. Headaches from overwork, suppressed sexual desire, indigestion. Headache from overloaded stomach, from pastry, fats, ice cream. Headache from abuse of coffee, spirits or chamomile tea. One-sided headaches, pulsating, bursting, with scalding. One-sided headaches, lachrymation of the affected side. Headaches of schoolgirls at puberty. Headaches, better walking in open air. Occipital pain, worse coughing. Numbness of head during headache. Occipital headache worse coughing. Shooting pains in temples. Wandering stitches about head, pains extend to face and teeth. Frontal and supra-orbital pains. Neuralgic scalding pains, beginning in right temporal side. Pressure on vertex. Head seems heavy, cannot hold upright, cannot raise it. Sensations of emptiness in head. Humming in head. Tumors on scalp, suppurating. Profuse sweat on hairy scalp.

Eyes - Pupils dilated or contracted. Ophthalmia neonatorum. Ophthalmia after suppressed gonorrhea. Ophthalmia with amenorrhea. Spots on cornea. Superficial ulcers on cornea. Incipient cataract. Catarrhal conjunctivitis. Sub-acute conjunctivitis with dyspepsia, worse in warm room. Conjunctivitis from colds. Thick, profuse, yellow, bland discharges. Burning, itching in eyes, must rub. Child frequently rubs eyes. Profuse, acrid lachrymation and secretion of mucus. Pressure, as from sand in eyes, when reading. Weeping eyes. Fistula lachry- malis, discharging pus on pressure. Lids inflamed, agglutinated. Veins of fundus oculi greatly enlarged. Styes, recurrent, upper lids. Blepharitis with acne of face. Oversensitive to light. Allergies.

Ears - External ear swollen and red. Lobes of ear swollen. Catarrhal otitis media. Ear infections, worse at night. Otorrhea, discharge of pus, blood, thick yellow humor, offensive after exanthemata. Threatened ulceration and perforation of tympanum. Itching deep in ears. Severe earache, not better warm applications. Earaches, worse night. Sensation as if something were being forced outward. Hearing difficult, deafness, as if ears were stopped up. Can hear better in car and in a warm room. Deafness after suppressed measles. Impaired hearing, worse cold, damp weather, better in warm room. Sounds of wind or rushing water.

Nose - Foul discharge or odor before the nose. Bad smells, as of old catarrh. Imaginary smells. Stoppage of nose with loss of smell, taste and appetite. Coryza, stoppage of right nostril, pressing pain at root of nose, better going out in the open air. Chronic bland yellow discharge. Yellow mucus, abundant in morning. Sinusitis with thick yellow, green nasal discharge. Yellowish-green discharge, worse indoors, better open air. Nose stopped up in house, fluent in open air. Nose swollen and itching in evening. Frequent sneezing. Sneezing in sleep. Large green fetid scales in nose. Sore nasal bones. Nosebleed, before, during menses. Nosebleed from suppressed menses.

Face - Face puffed, blue, red. Flushes. One cheek red, the other pale, during fever. Paleness of face during vertigo. Painful sensitiveness of skin of face. Facial erysipelas with stinging, pricking pains, skin peels off. Acne of young, growing girls. Prosopalgia towards evening until midnight, chilly with pain. Facial neuralgia. Right- sided neuralgia, with profuse lachrymation. Mumps, especially metastatic to the breast or testes. Tension of face and fingers, as if parts would become swollen. Boring pain in left malar bone. Frequently licks dry lips. Swelling of lower lip. Licks lips, crack in center of lower lip. Sweat on one side of face.

Mouth - Crack in middle of lower lip. Frequently licks dry lips. Offensive breath. Offensive odor from mouth (Aur., Merc.). Copious salivation during pain in stomach. Much sweet saliva. Tenacious saliva, like frothy cotton. Watery saliva like water brash. Dry mouth without thirst, wants it rinsed frequently. Yellow or white tongue, covered with a tenacious mucous. Dimin- ished taste and smell to all foods. Loss of taste with nasal catarrh. Alterations of taste, bitter, bilious, greasy, salty. Foul taste. Greasy taste. Food, especially bread, tastes bitter. Food leaves an aftertaste. Taste as of bad meat.

Throat - Great dryness of throat, in morning. Dry, sore throat with sense of dysphagia. Food lodges in throat. Constricted feeling about throat. Rawness and scraping. Stinging, sharp pain worse swallowing saliva or after food. As if a lump in it, when swallowing. Tough mucus in throat, worse night and morning. Hoarseness, comes and goes. Hoarseness and roughness of throat, can't speak a loud word. Nervous aphonia. Sensation of a worm wriggling up. Dilated or varicose veins in throat. As of a sulphur vapor when coughing.

Stomach - Pain as from subcutaneous ulceration. Visible pulsations in the pit of stomach (Asaf.). All-gone sensation, especially in tea drinkers. Weight as from a stone, especially in morning on awakening. Gnawing, hungry feeling (Abies-c.). Bitter taste, diminished taste of all food. Stomach disordered, feels heavy. Pain in stomach an hour after eating (Nux-v.). /ndigestionfrom rich, greasy, fatty foods. Worse after ices, fruits, pastry. Dyspepsia with great tightness after a meal, must loosen clothing. Flatulence. Heartburn. Water brash with foul taste in the morning. Belchings, taste of food remains a long time. Hiccough when smoking tobacco. Persistent nausea. Nausea, with colic, better after vomiting. Vomiting after fruits, fats, pastry, ices. Vomiting with pale face and chilliness. Vomiting of food eaten long before. Morning sickness. Stools - Changeable stools. No two stools alike after fruit (Ars., Chin.). Green, bilious, stools. Stools resembling stirred eggs, perfectly white, yellowish white. Discharge of acrid, mucus stools, with sensation of weakness in loins, during urination. Mucus, blood, mixed with stool.

Abdomen - Great soreness of epigastrium. Cutting, pulsation in epigastrium. Abdominal walls sensitive and swollen, tender to touch. Feeling of numbness. Chilliness from abdomen. Tense distension in upper abdomen. Pressure as from a stone. Painful, distended abdomen loud rumbling. Abdominal colic from ices, fruits, pastries, fat or greasy things. Colic, with chilliness in evening. Colic and rumbling of wind in upper abdomen. Colic from getting feet wet. Incarcerated flatus. Flatulence. Cholera morbus from drinking ice-water. Pains extend into groins. Hard painful lumps in both groins.

Rectum - Changeablestools. Notwostools alike after fruit (Ars., Chin.). Rumbling, watery, worse at night. Obstinate constipation. Constipation with headache, irregular menses. Constipation alternating with diarrhea. Frequent urging, as if diarrhea would occur. Dysentery, mucus and blood with chilliness (Merc., Rheum.). Diarrhea in jaundice with sensation of heat. Diarrhea after fright. Diarrhea during or after menses. Discharge of blood from rectum even when not at stool. Pressure in rectum after stool. Burning and cutting pains in rectum during stool. Smarting of anus after stool. Blind hemorrhoids with itching and sticking pains, worse menses, lying down. Sensations - As if beside himself. As if death were near. As if looking through a sieve. As if one had turned in a circle a fong time, as if he would fall, as if he were dancing. As if in a hot atmosphere. Chill as if drenched with cold water. As if brain would burst and eyes fall out of head, on coughing. Limbs as if bruised, as if asleep. Tongue as if burnt. Pain as from subcutaneous ulceration. As of a hot coal above ulcer.

Male - Orchitis, pain from abdomen to testicles. Orchitis, gonorrheal or from sitting on cold stones. Testicles hang low down. Soreness of testes. Burning and aching of testes, with or without swelling. Burning down left spermatic cord. Epididymitis. Acute prostatitis with pressure and great heat in perineum. Enlarged prostate. Hydrocele, varicocele, sarcocele. Thick, yellow discharge from urethra, late stage of gonorrhea. Bloody emissions. Pain and tenesmus while urinating, worse lying on back. Venous congestion of penis. Sexual desire in morning on waking, long-lasting morning erections. Nocturnal emissions, without dreams. Sexual excesses resulting in headache, backache, limbs heavy.

Female - Amenorrhea (Ign., Cimic., Polyg., Senec.), from wet feet, nervous debility, anemia or chlorosis. Menses delayed at puberty. Suppressed menses. Dark, thick menses. Menses too late, scanty after bathing. Mensesclotted,changeable. Flow more during day while walking about. Menses intermittent, irregular, or vicarious. Tardy menses. Bearing down pain, worse lying. Dysmenorrhea beginning in puberty. Dysmenorrhea, with chilliness, paleness of face, stretching and yawning. Metrorrhagia after abuse of quinine and iron. Leucorrhea worse lying down. Acrid, milky leucorrhea, thick like cream, with swollen vulva. Leucorrhea with pain in the back and exhaustion. Leucorrhea after masturbation. Vaginismus. Serous cysts, indurations or polyps in vagina. Promotes expulsion of moles. Nymphomania. Threatened miscarriage after fright. Malposition of fetus, breach position. Labor pains causes palpitations. Labor pains too weak or ceasing, with somnolence. Weak labor pains. Bearing down pain, worse lying. After-pains too long and too violent. Post-partum hemorrhages from retained placenta. Food - Hunger, but doesn 'tknow for what. Changeable appetite. Sudden loathing, worse eating. Food tastes too salty. Thirstlessness with nearly all complaints. Aversion to butter, pork, meat, fats, milk, bread, buckwheat. Aversion to warm food and drink. Aversion to smoking. Craving for what disagrees, pungent food, cheese, sweets, ice cream, peanut butter, soft-boiled eggs, herring. Craves or dislikes butter. Desire for tonics, acids, sour, lemonade, refreshing things, beer or alcoholic drinks. Worse from rich foods, fats, pork. Worse pastries, desserts, ice cream. Bad effects from onions.

Chest - Smothering sensation on lying down. Pressure and soreness upon the chest. Chest oppressed, as by a load. Soreness beneath clavicles. Tension in chest, worse drawing a long breath. Pain as from ulcer Pulsatilla nigricans in middle of chest. Paroxysms of burning in chest. Hard, painful, throbbing glandular swelling in right axilla. Congestion to chest and heart at night with anxious dreams. Chest symptoms, worse lying on painful side. Constitutions - For females of mild, gentle, plethoric, yielding disposition, who cry readily and weep when talking. Pale, chilly blondes.

Heart - Burning in region of heart. Catching pain with short breath, better by pressure of a hand and walking. Murmur in jugular veins. Anxious palpitations with amenorrhea, from emotions, after dinner. Nervous palpitations in young girls during puberty, or from amenorrhea. Palpitations, worse lying on left side. Pulse with distended blood vessels. Beat of pulse is felt in pit of stomach. Pulse frequent in evening. Pulse slower in morning. Heart symptoms reflex from indigestion.

Back - Curvature of the upper part of the spine. Pain in back and small of back as from prolonged stooping. Back painfully stiff, like a board. Backache worse lying on back, better lying on sides or changes of position, especially during pregnancy. Back feels bandaged. As if cold water was poured down the back. Chilliness and pain in sacral region during menses. Chilliness in lumbar region after stool. Lumbago, must move, yet motion gives no better. Shooting pain in the nape and back, between shoulders, in sacrum, after sitting. Swelling of cervical glands. Stiffness of neck after stool.

Limbs - Swollen, red joints. Pains down lower limbs, alternating sides. Pains, worsefrom letting the affected limb hang down (Vip.). Tensive pain, letting up with a crack. Drawing, tensive pain in thighs and legs with restlessness, sleeplessness and chilliness. Pain in limbs, shifting rapidly. Rheumatism caused by getting wet. Rheumatism from protracted wet weather. Legs feel heavy and weary. Numbness in legs when after long standing. Painful hip joint. Knees swollen with tearing drawing pains. Sticking in tibia worse lying better cool air and walking. Milk leg. Periostitis. Inclination to stretch the feet. Feet red inflamed, swollen, edematous. Boring pain in heels toward evening. Cold sweat on legs. Foul foot sweat. Arms feel broken and dislocated. Elbows numb. Veins in forearms and hands swollen. Veins full, varicose, painful. Lungs - Craves open fresh air, must open the window. Shortness of breath, anxiety and palpitations worse lying on left side (Phos.). Smothering sensation on lying down, worse in warm, stuffy rooms. Asthma in evening after a meal. Asthma from suppressions. Dry, hacking cough, from tickling in epigastrium. Dry cough in evening and at night. Cough must sit up in bed to get relief. Loose cough in the morning with copious mucus expectoration. Urine emitted with cough (Caust.). Cough after measles. Expectoration, thick, purulent, slimy, sweet, salty, bitter as it loosens up. Bland, yellow, greenish expectoration. Large quantities of yellow, thick, lumpy mucus, worse mornings. Groaning or rattling breathing. Broncho-pneumonia in chlorotic or anemic women. Acute suppuration of lungs. Pneumonia from hepatic troubles or during measles.

Sleep - Sleeps late in morning. Wakes unrefreshed, confused. Great sleepiness during day. Irresistible sleepiness in afternoon. Frequent yawning. Yawning during cough. Sleeplessness on account of an anxious sensation of heat. Sleeplessness from ideas crowding on mind. "Wide awake in the evening, restless first sleep. Talks, whines or screams during sleep. Chattering in sleep. Lies upon back, with hands over head, or with arms crossed on abdomen and feet drawn up. Dreams, frightful, disgusting, voluptuous, confused. Anxious dreams when lying on left side. Dreams of cats, of black beasts, of men, of falling. Sad dreams with weeping.

Skin - Skin itches on being heated. Itching as from numerous fleas. Herpes zoster. Erysipelas. Moles or freckles in young girls. Urticaria after rich food, with diarrhea. Urticaria from delayed menses, worse undressing. Urticaria in summer. Acne at puberty. Ulcers with hard, red, glistening areola. Wounds suppurate. Pus thick, yellow, bland, too profuse. Swollen glands. Measles with catarrhal symptoms. Varicose veins.

Modalities - Better from cool, fresh, open air. Better uncovering, cold applications, cold food and drinks, though not thirsty. Better from erect posture, lying with head high. Better continued, gentle motion, pressure, rubbing, massage. Worse from warmth of air, stuffy rooms, clothes, bed, sun. Worse getting feet wet, before and during thunderstorms. Worse at twilight, sunset, evening and night. Worse rest, beginning motion. Worse lying on one side, hanging down limbs. Worse puberty, before menses, pregnancy. Worse from eating, long after. Worse from rich foods, pastry, fats, ice cream, pork, eggs, tea. Worse hot food, is vomited immediately, aggravates toothache. Worse from iron, quinine. Never been well since puberty (anemia, bronchitis, phthisis).

Teeth - Sensation as if teeth would be forced out. Sharp, shooting pains in teeth. Looseness of painful teeth. Toothache, better holding cold water in mouth (Coff.). Toothache from picking teeth. Toothache from abuse of quinine. Toothache better outdoors, returns on coming into room. Sore gums, with gnawing pain.

Tongue - Dryness of tongue in morning. Edges of tongue feel sore as if scalded, middle of tongue feels as if burnt. Tongue feels too broad, too large. Yellow or white tongue, covered with tenacious mucus. Tongue bright red and covered with a network of dilated and congested veins. Blisters on sides and tip of tongue. Biting pain on tip of tongue. As if tongue would be torn out. Vertigo - Vertigo caused by indigestion. Vertigo with nausea and gastric disturbances. Vertigo on stooping, with nausea. Vertigo as if intoxicated, with whirling. Vertigo with loss of sight. Vertigo, better in open air, worse sitting up, looking up. Vertigo before, during menses, after suppressed menses. Vision - Diplopia. Amblyopia, with diminished hearing. Obscured vision in morning on rising, and on going into a warm room. Dim vision, as from accumulation of mucus. Dim vision, after getting warm from exercise, before menses. As if veil before eyes, worse in bright light. Loss of vision at night, as if eyes were tightly bound by a cloth, with menstrual disturbances. Day blindness with amenorrhea. Fiery circles. Bright streaks and rainbow colors. COMMENTS - Hahnemann gave in the picture of Puls, “a timid, weeping disposition with a tendency to inward grief and silent peevishness or at all events a mild and yielding disposition. Especially when the patient in his normal health was good-tempered and mild or even frivolus and good-humored. “It is therefore especially adapted for slow, phlegmatic temperaments, on the other hand, it is but little suitable for persons who form their resolutions with rapidity and are quick in their movements, even though they may appear to be good-tempered. “Puls, acts best where there is a disposition to chilliness and thirstlessness. It is suitable for females when their menses come on some days after the proper time. Especially when the patient must lie long in bed at night before he can get to sleep and when the patient is worse in the evening. It is useful for the ill effects caused by eating pork.” Rapid, changeable moods and desires. Capricious. Changeable and soft. Generally healthy, affectionate, loving, humble, particularly as children. Very sociable, needs attention, desires company. Exaggerated mothering instincts (opposite of Sep.). Better from consolation. Babies better from picking up, gentle rocking. Strong fear of loneliness, often an etiology. Fear of abandonment, grief over abandonment, “forsaken feeling.” Helpless feeling. Depression, insomnia, stemming from loneliness. Fear of being alone, the dark, more often in children. Fear of being unlovable. Weeps easily, poor confidence, jealous. Self pity. Dependent, strong desire to please. Inability to make decisions. Fixed ideas, from parents, about diet, relationships, religion. Seeks stability. Can smother people in relationships, drive them away because of their neediness. Likes sex because of closeness, company. Generally soft and fleshy. Great desire for fatty, creamy, buttery foods. Worse from fatty foods, rich foods, pastries, pork, sweets. Can have digestive problems, even nightmares, from overly rich foods. Dependency on food, eats when depressed. Emotional addiction to food, bulimia. Obliged to exercise to lose weight and to rationalize food choices. Food cravings, but doesn't know what for. May eat too late in the evening, leading to nightmares, headaches and stomachaches. All-gone sensation in stomach, especially in tea-drinkers. Thirstless. Great dryness of mouth without thirst. Chilly or warm blooded, but susceptible to cold, wet weather, worse sinus and menstrual symptoms. Craves fresh, open air. Will cover themselves with many blankets, then open a window to feel a cool breeze. Loves to walk slowly outdoors, improves symptoms. Likes the seashore, walking by the ocean. Better slow, passive motion in the open air. Worse from warm, stuffy rooms. Dislike the confines of clothing. Fear of suf- focating, drowning. Feels closed in. Better lying with the head higher than the rest of the body. Worse at twilight, sad at twilight (Rhus-t., Phos.). Measles, mumps, typhoid fevers, bilious, catarrhal intermittent, or rheumatic. In fevers, “chilly, worse by warmth, thirstless.” Chilliness may be one-sided and associated with numbness. Chilliness flitting in spots, now here, now there. Heat with distended veins and burning hands that seek cool places, without thirst. Profuse sweat, may be one-sided, sour, sweetish sour or musty in odor. “Mousey” odor, similar to measles, as well as a cough, catarrhal symptoms and rash. Ear trouble as a sequelae or complication of measles or other fever. Effects of suppressed rashes and metastases, as of mumps to testes or breasts. Prophylactic against measles (Bell.). For scarlatina, give 3c three times a day. Pains appear suddenly and leave gradually, or tension increases until very acute, then “lets up with a snap.” Characteristic wandering pains. When lying down, pain is in side on which patient is not lying, but when changing position, pain goes to the side that had been lain on before change of position. Rheumatoid arthritis. Rheumatic pains shift from joint to joint. Suffering parts emaciate. Vascular engorgement. Congestion in respiratory system. “Pressure upon the chest and soreness.” Coughing with a copious expectoration. Sinusitis. Secretions are generally thick, bland and yellowish green. Earaches (Cham.), sore throats, particularly with clinging and changeable moods. Colic, in babies. Can have a history of many acute infections and drug treatment. Can almost be regarded as an organ remedy for the generative organs of both sexes. Gonorrhea with thick, purulent secretion. Effects of suppressed gonorrhea orchitis and cystitis, prostatitis, sarcocele, varicocele, and hydrocele. Metastasis of mumps to testes or breasts. Useful for the sexual period from puberty to menopause, including menstruation, pregnancy, the puerperium and breast-feeding. First serious impairment of health is referred to age of puberty, “never been well since,” anemia, bronchitis, tuberculosis. Premenstrual syndrome. Irritable before menses, weeps easily. Delay of menses in spite of evident symptoms of a flow of blood towards the uterus. Menstrual blood is black, coagulated, impoverished if menses either too early or too late. Menstrual cramps with chills and weeping. Epilepsy with absence or irregularity of menses. Vaginitis with thick yellow or yellow green discharge, or without specific symptoms (Thuj., Nat-p.), may or may not have itching. Menopause with heat and flushing, desire for fresh air. Weeping during pregnancy. Fears during pregnancy, that they are unloved, that no one will help with the baby. Feelings of helplessness, lead to weeping. Fear that they will not be a good mother, that something is wrong with the baby. Morning sickness with headaches, vomiting and nausea, and a large appetite. Labor pains. Ineffectual and weak labor (Caul.). Bojanus related two cases, the first in which agir!, 18, of good constitution with no hereditary predisposition, had amenorrhea for six months and a fit occurred at the time each period was due. In the epileptic aura, she looked sad, pale as death, had chewing movements. Puls. 6c one dose a day was given. The next month, menses returned and there were no more fits. The second case was of a robust girl, 14, with no hereditary predisposition. She had fits for twelve months. The exciting cause was the non-appearance of menses. She had one great fit per month, small fits daily. In the epileptic aura she was self willed, angry, stood on one spot, stared into vacancy, stamped her foot. In the fit she cried, had deathly paleness, bit her tongue, urine flowed. She continued the occupation she was engaged with at the beginning of the fit. Puls. 30c one dose a day was given. Some weeks after, she had a slight fit. A month later, menses came on for first time, she had no great fits, and small ones were rare. She was given Puls. 30c one dose a week. A month later, she had a great fit. Puls, was then given once a day. She had no more great fits, only a few small ones. The cure was permanent. Teste noted a case of Stoerck's, in which a young girl who had amaurosis of both eyes since infancy. Stoerck cured in two months, administering an extract internally and externally a dry powder. The latter caused at first an acute pain and profuse flow of tears after which the pains, which had existed previous to the lachrymation, diminished as soon as it commenced and finally disappeared with it. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Cham, and Puls, antidote each other and follow each other well. If either one has over-acted the other will probably neutralize the ill effect and carry on the good. Coff., Ign., Nux-v. When the improper use of Puls, has affected the air passages, Calc-p. has proved the best antidote. Antidote to: Chin., Chin-s., Ferr. (in chlorotic girls who have been damaged by iron, Puls, has excellent effect). Compare: (1) Puls., similar effects. Cycl., Kali-bi., Kali-s., Sulph. (2) Tearfulness, Sep., Nat-m., Ign. (3) Varicose veins, varicocele, orchitis, milk leg, Ham. (4) Ophthalmia, Arg-n. (5) All-c., both have worse in room, better open air, but All-c. discharge is thin and excoriating, Puls, thick and bland. (6) Stinging pains in throat worse swallowing saliva and after eating, Apis. (7) Feeling as if food lying in esophagus, Chin., Abies-n. (8) Effect of fat food, Ip. Thuj., Carb-v. (9) Effect of ice cream, Ars., Carb-v., Ip., Bell-p. (10) Mixed diet, Nux-v., Ip., Chin. (11) Desire for lemonade, Cycl., Sabin., Bell. (12) Gastric ailments from pork, (13) Retained placenta, Canth. after-pains, Cham., Xan., Cupr. (14) Non-appearance of milk, Urt-u., Ric., Agn. (15) Uterine affections, Caul., Melon., Alet., Cycl., Hydr., Lil-t. (16) Measles, Morbill., Kali-bi. (17) Earache, Bor. Compatible: Ars., Bry., Bell., Ign., Kali-bi., Lyc., Nux-v., Phos., Rhus-t., Sep., Sulph. Complementary: Coff., Cham., Nux-v., Pen. often indicated after Puls, in later colds. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Kidneys - Cystitis with weeping. Urging to urinate when lying on back. Sensation as of a stone rolling in the bladder. Stricture, urine passed only in drops and stream interrupted (Clem.). Urine dribbles when angry. Spasmodic pain in bladder after urinating. Burning in orifice of urethra during and after urination. Hematuria after urination. Heavy pressure or cramp in bladder after urination. Involuntary urination at night during sleep, while coughing, sneezing or passing flatus. Involuntary on lying down, laughing, hearing sudden noise after surprise, shock.

Bladder - Region of bladder painful to touch. Sensation as if a stone rolling in bladder. Sharp pain, pressure on neck of bladder. Burning in orifice of urethra during and after urination. Pain and tenesmus in urinating. Constrictive pain in region of bladder with urinary tenesmus and involuntary emissions of a little urine. Spasmodic pain in bladder, after urinating. Urination more frequent during attack of headache. Hematuria with burning at orifice of urethra. Retention of urine after childbirth. Involuntary urination at night, on coughing orpassing flatus. Involuntary urination on laughing, sneezing. Dribbling of urine from anger. Nocturnalbedwetting after measles, worse in autumn, especially little girls. Breasts - Lumps occurring in breasts of young girls, painful and affecting arm of corresponding side. Thin, milky fluid escapes from breasts before puberty. Aching, sore breasts. Secretion of milk during menses. Milk suppressed or very scanty. Weeps when the child is put to breast. Child refuses breast. Galactorrhea, in women who are not nursing their children. After weaning, breasts swell, feel stretched, tense, intensely sore, milk continues to be secreted. Causations - Ill effects of suppressions, otorrhea, menses, lochia, milk etc. Abandonment. Grief. Eating ice cream, pork, fats, pastry, desserts, mixed rich diet, tea. Chill. Wetting feet.

Cough - Dry cough in evening and at night, must sit up in bed to get relief. Loose cough in morning, with copious mucus sputum. Dry, hacking cough from tickling in epigastrium. Short, dry cough, worse becoming warm and after sleeping. Cough from dryness in larynx and trachea, worse eating and evening. Dry cough, often with palpitations, nausea, retching, headache, backache. Loose cough by day, dry after every sleep. Cough with retching and desire to vomit. Loose cough, with vomiting of mucus. Cough with diarrhea. Cough after measles.

Perspiration - One-sided pains during sweat. Sweats only on face and scalp. Sweats at night, with stupid slumber. Profuse sweat in morning. Sweats during cough. Sour, musty sweat. Sweetish acid odor sweat. Sweat like musk.

Temperature - Body hot, limbs cold. Childhood fevers, chickenpox, earaches, measles and mumps. Prophylactic for measles. Erratic temperature in fevers. Feverish, hot, body temperature normal. Moaning during fever. Attacks of flushes of heat. Feverjust at sunset. External heat is intolerable. Intolerable burning heat at night with distended veins. Heat in parts of body, coldness in other. Partial sweat. During apyrexia, headache, diarrhea, loss of appetite, nausea. Chilly, yet averse to heat in warm, stuffy rooms with pain, on lying down at night. Chilliness without thirst. Chilly with pains in spots, worse evening. Chill about 4 p.m. One-sided coldness with numbness. One hand cold.

name: Pulsatilla Nuttaliana
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better walking in open air. Better from rubbing with brush, scratching. Worse coming in from open air, warmth, at night. Worse from reading, walking, urinating, after eating, eating a pear..
constitution: Amenorrhea. Clavus. Cold, liability to. Deafness. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Feet, fidgety. Homesickness. Knees, rheumatism. Liver, pains. Measles, prophylaxis. Menses, retarded. Ptosis. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Shoulder, pain. Tinnitus. Uterus, pains.

full:
PHARMACY - puls-n. Pulsatilla nuttalliana. American pulsatilla. American Pasque Flower. Anemone Ludoviciana. Anemone nuttaliana. N. O. Ranunculaceae. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Clavus. Cold, liability to. Deafness. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Feet, fidgety. Homesickness. Knees, rheumatism. Liver, pains. Measles, prophylaxis. Menses, retarded. Ptosis. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Shoulder, pain. Tinnitus. Uterus, pains.

HERBAL - The American pulsatilla is more similar to Puls, vulgaris than to Puls. nig. in its botanical characters. It flourishes especially in the dry and sandy bluffs which form the bed of the Mississippi. Hale wrote “The flower is pale purplish. The odor of the dried plant is rather faint, being slightly camphor-like, the taste of the dried flowers simply sweetish and herbaceous, that of the leaves more astringent with very slight acrimony. The taste and to some extent the odor of the fresh plant are both acrid and irritating.” A. W. Miller, a pharmacist, analyzed Puls-n. The extracted substances had an acrid, almost caustic taste and well-marked camphor-like odor. When volatilized, they produced an irritating, pungent vapor, affecting the eyes and causing sneezing. His analysis revealed constituents including organic grape-sugar, gum, resin, an alkaloid and anemonic acid. Inorganic sulphate of potash, carbonate of potash, chlorate of potassium, carbonate of lime, magnesia and “a proto-salt of iron.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. W. H. Miller, an allopath, claimed to have used Puls-n. with success in many chronic eye affections, particularly catarrh, amaurosis and corneal opacities, skin eruptions and secondary syphilis. Homesick feeling. Trembling weakness, weariness, heaviness. Great debility, on rising in evening. Languid, feverish, depressed. Snapping noise in ears. Hands constantly hot and dry. Stiffness of fingers. Fidgety feet. Colic before and after stool. Colic after eating a pear. MIND - Sad, gloomy, with frequent belchings. Homesick, despondent. Anxiety, at night. Irritable, quick, nervous motions. Dull, disinclined for work.

Head - Dull heavy headache, in the mornings, better by active exercise before breakfast. Dull, oppressive, frontal headache, on waking. Hard pains in upper forehead pass in wave to occiput involving whole brain. Flying pains in head and feet. With headache cutting pains in the epigastrium. Hard pain over left eye, as if a nail being pressed into forehead. Pain over right eye afternoon, better walking in open air, worse in warm room with sense of heat, fullness in head and dryness of eyes. Sharp, shooting pains through both temples in right temple. Dull pain in right temple in vertex. Severe throbbing on vertex. Full, hot feeling at cerebellum. Headache arising from nape of neck and upwards.

Eyes - Neuralgic pains in eyeballs, while walking, worse right side. Dull pain deep in eyes with smarting. Dryness, smarting, profuse flow of tears. Profuse secretion of mucus from eyes. Profuse lachrymation with dull pains in eyeball extending to malar bone. Tarsal edges red, dry, irritable. Eyelids agglutinated, profuse secretion of soft, yellow or white matter. Paralysis of lids. Edema of left upper lid. Twitching of left brow and upper lid for half an hour after going to bed, right lids worse reading.

Ears - With the pains in head and eyes, frequent drawing pains in ears from within out. Hard, drawing pains along right Eustachian tube. Sharp pains in right ear and temples. Left ear feels closed, later both. Snapping noises in ears, fluttering in right. Deafness with edema of left upper eyelid.

Nose - Dryness and heat in nose.

Face - Face red, hot, flushed. After eating, flushed, pressure of blood in face. Complexion at first rough, later very clear after disappearance of rash. Painful drawing in left cheekbone and jaw. Lips dry.

Mouth - Tongue coated white, covered with tough slime, red, rather dry and swollen, yellowish coat along center, unusually red after eating. Teeth indented on tongue. Breath offensive to self and others after eating. Mouth filling with saliva. Mouth and lips dry. Smarting of velum palati. On waking, dry, flat, pappy taste in mouth, as if tongue thickly coated (which it was not). Flat, bitter, rough, sweetish, bad taste. Wakes with vinegar-like acidity in mouth and dull, pressing pain in stomach.

Throat - Scratchy, husky feeling in throat. Sensation of plug in lower throat. Frequent inclination to clear throat. Throat dry, smarts on waking, contains much tough mucus that is hard to dislodge. After eating, slight irritation in throat with easy expectoration of white, tough mucus. Vertigo - Dizziness on entering house from open air, sudden in afternoon, with fullness of head. COMMENTS - Hale instituted the first homeopathic research and Burt was the first prover. The symptoms have a strong resemblance to those of Puls, and cases cured with Puls-n. are mostly such as would be amenable to Puls. The Puls, flying pains were very noticeable in the proving. Feeling as if needles being pressed through stomach. Heat in stomach gradually increasing to pain, worse in spots under sternum, burning, pricking burning. The proving showed a powerful effect on the menstrual function and Hale reported many cures of amenorrhea, including the case of a young woman, formerly subject to retardation of menses. She had constant chilliness, cold hands and feet, loss of appetite, sour belchings, nausea after meals, hemicrania, toothache, melancholy, and general malaria. Menses were two weeks late, took a chill at the time they were due, when she had precursory symptoms, no symptoms of menses now. Hale gave Puls-n. lx in water every two hours. After the first dose, the menses came on and the constitutional symptoms cleared off. Hale also noted the case of a plethoric, usually healthy young woman, who had menses delay two weeks. Continual severe headache, a heaviness and fullness, worse moving or stooping. Sight dim, complete blindness on stooping or rising suddenly, weight in uterine region severe aching extending to back, worse evening. Hands and feet cold, weakness in lower limbs. Act. failed to relieve. Puls-n. lx, 5 drops every three hours, brought speedy improvement. The next day menses came on profusely but without pain, two days before the expiration of the eighth week. Hale reported the case of a strong, healthy looking man who had wandering rheumatic pains chiefly in dorsum of right foot, loins, thighs, chest, arms, head. The head pain was a dull, heavy pressure in vertex, nearly constant with occasional sharp pains. Some fever but no local inflammation of joints or muscles. Urine scanty, depositing gravel. Acidity of stomach. Appetite good. Bowels normal. Puls-n. lx cured in three days. A patient of Clarke’s was incidentally cured of a tendency to catch colds by taking Puls-n. for some weeks as a prophylactic against measles. Burnett cured with Puls-n. a case of deafness and edema of left upper eyelid. RELATIONS Antidoted by: Ant-c. Compare: (1) Puls. (2) In fidgety feet, Zinc, Caust. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Stomach - Gnawing, empty sensation. Painful emptiness, pressure, then rising towards esophagus like heartburn. Emptiness after action of bowels, after eating. Fullness in stomach preventing eating in spite of appetite. Weight and pressure in stomach after eating with faintness. Distress with severe cutting pains in epigastrium. Heartburn. Belchings, of food, hot, tasteless wind, sour air. Thick gulping. Nausea and dull headache, then faintness at stomach, on entering house.

Abdomen - Dull pains in the right hypochondrium. Aching in one spot worse by moving. Aching in left groin, above left iliac crest on moving or bending. Dull pains in the abdomen, by spells in hypogastrium. Severe pain in umbilicus, 6 a.m., with desire for stool, stool dark, covered with mucus, severe pains for half an hour after. Rumbling after dinner of wind in distended abdomen moving from epigastrium to hypogastrium. Colicky pains after eating a ripe pear.

Rectum - Feeling as if must go to stool immediately, with constant distress in lower epigastrium and umbilicus. Constipation. Sudden attack of diarrhea while riding on horseback. Stools dark, thin, pap-like, watery, light yellow, painless, mushy, dark, slightly covered with mucus, dry, hard, lumpy.

Male - Distressing erection, soon subsiding. Emission. Pain in penis on waking, worse on urinating. Hard, sticking pains in left spermatic cord and testes. Dull pains in testes, worse right.

Female - Feeling as if menses coming on. Menses, weak, too soon (discharge, which had been formerly too dark and with pain, was this time natural in color and painless). Menses, always copious, increased to flooding and lasted three days. In morning on awaking found menses had returned first time since weaning babe (two months). Painless leucorrhea. Leucorrhea, bland but so profuse and with so great depression that the prover refused to take more of the drug although it removed a pleuritic pain. Stinging, darting pains passing through uterus from side to side. Food - Great hunger, rapidly returned after eating. Loss of appetite. More thirst than usual, cold water extremely grateful.

Chest - Sharp, stabbing pain in pectoralis major muscle, followed by burning distress. During evening, severe pain under left arm nearer back. Aching pain in chest all forenoon. Itching blotches on right breast, right side chest.

Heart - Audible pulsation of heart. Pulse accelerated.

Back - Stiffness right side of neck, in the morning. Backache. Woke frequently with backache. Lameness in back, especially loins. Weakness of loins, feeling as if menses coming on.

Limbs - Muscles stiff. Cramp. Nervous sensation, irresistible fidgets, worse night, with desire to urinate afternoon and at night. Legs heavy while walk ing, trembling weakness, nervous pains. Aching in limbs and loins wakes him frequently. Sharp neuralgic pains along sciatic nerve from hip joint to middle of thigh. Pain in both knees, rheumatic. Dull pain in ankles, flying pains. Very cold feet, evening. Frequent flying pains in hands, feet, toes. Rheumatism of right shoulder. Lameness in muscles of right upper arm. Frequent momentary pains in wrists and fingers. Hands dry and hot all day. Fingers stiff. Lungs - Constant inclination to cough. Small sore spot in upper trachea.

Sleep - Sleepy, sleep not refreshing. Sleepless for an hour at 4 a.m., for several hours from over-eating. Restless with frontal headache. Many confused dreams.

Skin - Red rash on body, face, neck, back, chest, abdomen, limbs, worse chest and abdomen. Itching, scattered pimples, right side of chest, light red, rash-like blotches on right breast, itching severely at night, worse when heated. Slight rash on back and shoulders. Elevated, blotchy eruption on legs and back. Erythema, nodules, turn white after scratching. Intense itching all over, worse night before bedtime, better rubbing, worse riding in cold air, returned repeatedly throughout the winter.

Modalities - Better walking in open air. Better from rubbing with brush, scratching. Worse coming in from open air, warmth, at night. Worse from reading, walking, urinating, after eating, eating a pear.

Kidneys - Frequent urination. Tenesmus, extending up ureters, uneasiness in kidneys. Pain on urinating, at end of urethra. Urine pale, albuminous, excess of water, skunk-like odor.

Temperature - Chilly, with a full, uncomfortable feeling in stomach, with inclination to yawn, with papescent stool, shaking. Heat, feverish with debility, skin hot, flaccid, better cool, blustering wind. Hot face, cold feet, hands hot and feverish.

name: Pyrarara
author: Murphy
constitution: Chloasma. Dermatitis. Elephantiasis. Gangrene. Leprosy. Nodules. Scleroderma. Syphilis. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Varicose veins. Vitiligo. Wounds.
keynote:
PHARMACY - pyrar. Pyrarara. Amazon fish lard. The lard of the Pyrarara fish of the Amazon river. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Chloasma. Dermatitis. Elephantiasis. Gangrene. Leprosy. Nodules. Scleroderma. Syphilis. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Varicose veins. Vitiligo.…
full:
PHARMACY - pyrar. Pyrarara. Amazon fish lard. The lard of the Pyrarara fish of the Amazon river. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Chloasma. Dermatitis. Elephantiasis. Gangrene. Leprosy. Nodules. Scleroderma. Syphilis. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Varicose veins. Vitiligo. Wounds.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pyrar. has been used clinically for various skin affections, leprosy, tuberculosis, syphilis, varicosities, etc. COMMENTS - Dr. Frederick M. Dearborn, New York, 1915, who brought some of the “lard” from South America and turned it over to Boericke and Tafel wrote, “I had curiosity enough to inquire of my homeopathic friends, while visiting Rio recently, if they knew of any 'new' remedies. “While a number were suggested that I had never heard of, Pyrarara appealed to me because of its manifest dermal indications and because I was able to procure, through the endeavors of Dr. Theodore Gomes, a small supply of the extract, and by the courtesy of Dr. Marques de Oliveira, a genuine clinical record.” “Before proceeding to the recital of the clinical case, it might be well to mention that the use of Pyrarara is not limited to the treatment of leprosy, but has been used to relieve a number of dermatoses.” “The exact diagnoses of these conditions were hard to determine, but their descriptions would lead me to think of the tuberculosis, the syphilis, scleroderma, vitiligo, chloasma, elephantiasis, varicosed vessels and the attendant dermatitis, gangosa, jaws and the varieties of gangrene. I received some positive assurances as regards its use in varicosities.” “Pyrarara is not listed in any group of Brazilian or South American remedies that I can discover and has not been scientifically proven, but I hope the following translation of Dr. Oliveira's notes may be of interest: “The lard of the Pyrarara, a fish of the Amazon river, was brought from Acre by Major Carpenter of the Engineers, who offered it as a curiosity to Mr. Liberato dos Santos. The Major said that he had heard from the inhabitants of the Amazon valley that the lard has the property of changing the color of the plumage of parrots fed upon it, and that a person abusing the use of the fish, as a food, would develop leprosy or symptoms similar to that disease. After a talk with Mr. dos Santos, he gave me some of the lard for homeopathic experimentation on people affected with leprosy.” “The following is the result: Maria Theresa, 36 years old, has suffered from leprosy since she was 19 years old. The first appearance of the disease was on the extremities of her fingers and on her face after suppression of menstruation. She was treated by Dr. Gabizo for three years without any result and by many other doctors, using various medicines and electricity, but still no result was attained.” ‘The disease had reached the highest state of development; her anatomic structure had become deformed and her facial changes took away from her the appearance of a human being. Her body was covered with nodules and ulcers in constant suppuration; her ears were inflamed and deformed; her nose was ulcerated and corroded; her lips were tumefacted and ulcerated; her throat was so affected that her voice was completely lost; her arms looked like a piece of raw flesh; and the phalanges of all her fingers were destroyed. Certain areas of the skin were anesthetic and there was a general coppery discoloration.” “It was at this period that she came to me. I proposed experimenting upon her with the new medicine, which she reluctantly accepted, after many days of insisting. In June, 1905, we began our treatment, at first using the 3x trituration with a dose of three tablets every three hours applying, externally, vaseline with calendula. The first month there was no apparent dermal improvement, but her appetite increased. I then began to use the 5x potency and during the first two weeks there was a great transformation.” “Through the open lesions came an abundant discharge of a whitish color tinted with blood and very thick, and the body was covered with bullae, where there were no ulcers before, but always the same kind of discharge. Her appetite became very good and digestion regular, but she became prostrated and suffered from neuralgic pains in the head, face, and feet. During the month of August the inflammation of the lips was disappearing and the wounds of the lips healing. She was very cheerful with the result. As her sight was getting feeble, Asafoetida was given to her and the eye symptoms improved to a great extent.” “At the beginning of September the ulcers had ceased suppurating, the bullae did not appear any more and her general state was very good. As the menstrual periods came, she felt great pain in the lumbar and ovarian regions and Pulsatilla 30th was given to her and the menses appeared, although very feeble. I then gave Pyrarara in the 30x potency for a few days and she continued to improve. The nodules diminished in size and the ulcers became almost dry, with scant discharge, while the tumefaction disappeared.” “About this time Aurum met. 5th potency and afterward Apis 5x potency and Cuprum met. 5x potency were used as the symptom called for. On the following month the menses came freely. In November I returned to the use of Pyrarara 30x potency. The healing of the wounds continued and only three ulcers were to be found on the whole body, one on the forearm, on the foot, and one on the middle finger. The tumefaction gradually disappeared, except on the ears. General condition was very good. By the 25th of December one could hardly detect her sickness.” “The intense redness of her face was gone; the forehead was white, the natural color having returned; the lips, mouth and throat were normal; while the ears were still tumefacted, the nodules had disappeared; the body was free from ulcers and nodules; the forearm completely well. Only one ulcer on the middle finger was to be found. Her organic functions were re-established, sensibility had almost returned and she could move the deformed fingers, but the sense of touch was not complete. By January, 1906, after seven months of treatment, she disappeared.” “This medication has been tried since on different people with splendid results, but lack of persistency has prevented complete cures. On the other patients the Pyrarara has been used, employing the centesimal scale of potencies.” REFERENCES - Anshutz.

name: Pyrethrum Parthenium
author: Murphy
constitution: Convulsions. Delirium. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Fevers. Loquacity. Rheumatism.
keynote:
PHARMACY - pyre-p. Pyrethrum parthenium. Feverfew. Chrysanthemum parthenium. Anacyclus officinarum. Leucanthemum parthenium. N. O. Compositae. Tincture of fresh plant. Tincture of dried roots. Historical dose: Tincture, all potencies.

CLINICAL - Convulsions. Delirium. Diarrhea.…
full:
PHARMACY - pyre-p. Pyrethrum parthenium. Feverfew. Chrysanthemum parthenium. Anacyclus officinarum. Leucanthemum parthenium. N. O. Compositae. Tincture of fresh plant. Tincture of dried roots. Historical dose: Tincture, all potencies.

CLINICAL - Convulsions. Delirium. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Fevers. Loquacity. Rheumatism.

HERBAL - Pyrethrum has bitter tonic properties like those of chamomile (Anthémis nobilis) and is a popular remedy in slight fevers, hence the name “feverfew.” The Treasury of Botany noted that the smell of the whole herb is said to be particularly offensive to bees. Some popular insect powders were made of the dried flowers of Pyrethrum roseum. Radix pyrethri, or Pellitory of Spain, which is used as an irritant and as a toothache cure is the root of Anachycles pyrethrum. The roots of the genus have a hot taste, the source of the name pyrethrum (fire).

HOMEOPATHIC - One observation was recorded with pyrethrum; a boy, 3 1/2 took 50 minims of the tincture. It nearly proved fatal, causing diarrhea, convulsions of a tetanic nature, twitchings, loquacious delirium, restless, rapid and weak pulse and profuse sweat at night. Twitching of muscles, of limbs, subsided by morning of third day. Violent convulsions lasting an hour and leaving the child apparently moribund, but he gradually recovered. Feet, legs and body, which were swollen, were decidedly reduced and the next menstrual period was dark and deficient in a gouty woman, age 50. She also had convulsive movements like tetanus. Restlessness. Stupor. Cooper cured cases of sub-acute rheumatism with Pyrethrum roseum. MIND - Very excited, talks incessantly for hours. Lying in state of stupor, easily roused but quickly relapsing.

Mouth - Soreness of tongue.

Rectum - Tenesmus followed by involuntary evacuations of mucus, slightly tinged with blood, better next morning. Diarrhea, 5 a.m. w ith pain, at first profuse and exhausting.

Limbs - Old sub-acute rheumatism of hands and small bones.

Pulse - Pulse very rapid (120 to 130) and feeble.

Temperature - Profuse perspiration and restlessness at night. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cham., Cina, Absin., Art-v. (2) other Compositae. REFERENCES Clarke.

name: Pyrogenium
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from heat, hot bathing, hot drinks. Better from pressure, stretching, motion, changing position, hard rocking and walking. Worse cold, damp. Worse sitting, motion, moving eyes, passing flatus..
constitution: Abscesses. Appendicitis. Bedsores. Bites. Blood,poisoning. Boils. Bright's disease. Boils. Bones, pain. Constipation. Debility. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Eczema. Enteric, fever. Fevers, high. Fistula. Food poisoning. Headache. Heart, disorders. Hectic, fever. Hepatitis. Influenza. Injuries. Intestines, ulceration. Lymphangitis. Malaria. Miscarriage. Offensive, discharges. Ovary, abscess. Palpitations.

PHARMACY - pyrog. Pyrogenium. Rotten meat pus. Pyrogen. Pyrexin. Sepsin. A product of the decomposition of chopped lean beef in water, allowed to stand in the sun for two or three weeks. Nosodes. Dilutions. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Appendicitis.…
full:
PHARMACY - pyrog. Pyrogenium. Rotten meat pus. Pyrogen. Pyrexin. Sepsin. A product of the decomposition of chopped lean beef in water, allowed to stand in the sun for two or three weeks. Nosodes. Dilutions. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Appendicitis. Bedsores. Bites. Blood,poisoning. Boils. Bright's disease. Boils. Bones, pain. Constipation. Debility. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Eczema. Enteric, fever. Fevers, high. Fistula. Food poisoning. Headache. Heart, disorders. Hectic, fever. Hepatitis. Influenza. Injuries. Intestines, ulceration. Lymphangitis. Malaria. Miscarriage. Offensive, discharges. Ovary, abscess. Palpitations. Peritonitis. Plague. Ptomaine, poisoning. Puerperal, fever. Pyemia. Tabes mesenterica. Tuberculosis, lungs. Typhoid. Restlessness. Septic,fever. Septicemia. Sores. Syphilitic. Ulcers. Varicose veins. Wounds.

HOMEOPATHIC - John Drysdale, in 1880, was the first to suggest the use of this substance as a medicine. This nosode is prepared from decomposed lean beef allowed to stand in the sun for two weeks, or from septic pus. Pyrog. is the great remedy for septic states with intense restlessness. H. C. Allen indicated that it is an anti- septic, useful in septic fevers, especially puerperal. Chronic complaints that date back to septic conditions. For all types of septic states when blood is disorganized. The heart becomes weak and muscles prostrated. Hectic, typhoid, typhus, ptomaine poisoning, and diphtheria states. Dissecting wounds. Sewer-gas poisoning. Characteristic carrion-like odor of bodily emaciation, secretions and excretions. Horribly offensive discharges, foul, menstrual, lochia, diarrhea, vomit, sweat, breath, taste, body odor. Constipation from impacted feces in fevers, stool large, black, carrionlike. Great pain and violent burning in abscesses. Septic fevers. Temperature rises rapidly. Quickly oscillating temperature. Fever commencing with pains in the limbs. High fevers with sore limbs and delirium. Threatening heart failure in zymotic and septic fevers. Influenza, typhoid symptoms. Cerebrospinal meningitis. Chronic malaria. Rosy red streaks, lymphangitis. After-effects of miscarriage. Food poisoning. Great heat with profuse sweat, but sweating does not cause a fall in temperature. Sweats without relief. Shivers and begins to move about restlessly. Cold and chilly all day. No fire will warm, sits by fire and chilly whenever he leaves it. Chill begins in back, between scapulae. Severe general chill of bones and limbs. Aching, bruised, sore pains and prostration, yet restless. Bones pain. Restless, must move to ameliorate the soreness of parts. Cannot lie more than few minutes in one position, better change. Bed feels too hard (Bapt., Arn.), aching all over. Great muscular debility, rapid recovery in few hours. Debility in morning, staggered on trying to walk. MIND - Sensitive, anxious, confused. Confusion of mind. Active mind, making speeches and writing articles at night. Loquacious, thinks and talks faster than ever before. Prostration of mind, mental exhaustion, brain fag. Weeping, tearful mood. Morose, sulky, cross, fretful, ill-humor, peevish. Anxiety in morning. Full of anxiety and insane notions. Desires to be rocked. Talks or whispers to herself in sleep. Cannot tell whetherdreaming while awake or asleep. Semi-conscious and muttering. Stupor. Bed feels too hard (Bapt., Arn.). Restlessness, tossing about in bed. Restlessness and delirium with fever. Delirium on closing the eyes. Delirium, anxious and confused. Delirium from sepsis. Delusions, sees images, phantoms. Delusion that he is very wealthy. Delusions, he is enlarged, body parts were scattered about bed. Sensation as if she covered the whole bed. Feels if crowded with arms and legs. Confusion as to his identity. Sensation of duality. Feels when lying on one side, one person, and another person, when turning, on the other side. Disgust at his own body odor.

Head - Excruciating, violent, throbbing headache, better bandaging. Bursting pain with restlessness. Great throbbing of arteries of temples and head. Painless throbbing all though front of head, sounds like escaping steam. Dull throbbing in mastoid region. Rolls head from side to side. Skull-cap sensation. Forehead bathed in cold sweat. Erysipelas.

Eyes - Cornea, keratitis. Sore, bruised pain. Eyeballs sore, worse looking up and moving eyes, particularly left eyeball. Swelling of eyes. Projecting eyes. Photophobia. Roughness of margins, edges of lids. Styes.

Ears - Burning pains. Discharges, offensive. Ears red, as if blood would burst out of them. Ears feel cold. Pulsation, synchronous with pulse. Noises like steam escaping. Loud ringing like a bell.

Nose - Cold feeling in nose. Obstruction, alternating sides. Fan-like motion of the alae nasi. Sneezing from uncovering. One-sided coryza. Nosebleed with sepsis. Nosebleed during fever. Nosebleeds, awakened by dreaming it and found it was so. Disgust at his own body odor.

Face - Face, burning, yellow, very red, pale, greenish, chlorotic, sunken and bathed in cold sweat. Hippocratic. Bluish around eyes. Circumscribed redness of cheeks. Hectic flush 3 p.m. to 4 p.m., lasting until midnight, then covered with large drops of cold perspiration.

Mouth - Dryness of mouth. Horribly offensive, cadaverous, putrid breath. Taste sweetish, terribly fetid. Excoriation of mucus membrane. Sordes. Abscess of teeth, roots.

Throat - Septic sore throats. Abscessed tonsils. Diphtheria with extreme fetor. Membrane, exudation, malignant diphtheria. Dry throat, difficult articulation. Hoarseness. Voice husky, weak.

Stomach - Coldness, chilliness in stomach. Stomach feels too full. Eructations sour. Belching of sour water after breakfast. Nausea, vomiting and purging. Urging to vomit with cold feet. Nausea, better very hot drinks and vomiting. Vomits water when it becomes warm in stomach. Persistent, brownish vomiting, offensive smelling. Bile or bloody vomit, or like coffee-grounds. Vomiting, fecal with impacted or obstructed bowels. Vomiting with constipation.

Abdomen - Distension. Full feeling of abdomen. Bloated, sore, cutting pain. Soreness of abdomen can hardly breathe or bear any pressure over right side. Sore, bruised pain and tenderness. Cutting pain. Cramping, griping pain in hypochondria. Severe cutting pains right side going through back, worse by every motion. Bubbling or gurgling sensation in hypochondria, extending back to left of spine. Rumbling, gurgling noises. Colitis. Peritonitis, enteritis. Tabes mesenterica. Pain in umbilical region with passage of sticky, yellow stool. Ileus, obstruction of bowels, impaction. Appendicitis. Hepatitis. Cholecystitis. Buboes.

Rectum - Inactivity of rectum. Constipation with complete inertia (Op.). Obstinate constipation from impaction. Constipation, stool remains long in rectum with no urging. Intolerable tenesmus of both bladder and rectum. Involuntary stool during urination. Diarrhea with fever. Diarrhea from excitement, emotions. Diarrheafrom septic conditions. Painless diarrhea. Hemorrhage from anus. Sore, bruised pain. Fistula. Perspiration about the anus and perineum.

Stool - Hard, dry stools, like small black balls, sheep dung. Knotty, nodular, lumpy stools. Offensive, putrid, carrion-like stools. Bloody streaks in stools. Mucus, slimy bloody stools. Long, narrow stools. Horribly offensive, brown-black diarrhea. Painless, involuntary stools. Insufficient, incomplete, unsatisfactory stools.

Male - Testes hang down, relaxed. Relaxed scrotum. Scrotum looks and feels thin. Prostatitis.

Female - Fever at each menstrual period. Menses, bright red, clotted. Menses horribly offensive, carrion- like. Menses too short, last but one day, then a horribly offensive, bloody leucorrhea. Genitals severely swollen (Bright's disease). Pelvic peritonitis or cellulitis. Abscess in ovaries. Abscess of left ovary, acute throbbing pain, great distress with fever and rigors. Ovaritis. Pulsating pain in ovaries. Salpingitis. Prolapse uterus, better holding the head and straining. Uterine hemorrhage of bright red blood with dark clots. Metrorrhagia, bright red, clotted, coagulated. Puerperal peritonitis with extreme fetor. Septicemia following a miscarriage with the fetus or placenta retained and decomposed. Retained placenta. Septic infections after childbirth. Lochia thin, watery. Lochia, acrid, offensive, bloody, intermittent. Lochia suppressed, followed by fever, chills and profuse fetid sweat. Post-operative cases with overwhelming sepsis. Food - No appetite or thirst. Great thirst for small quantities of cold drinks, but the least liquid is instantly rejected. Better by drinking very hot water. Nausea, better very hot drinks.

Chest - Pain in right lung and shoulder, worse talking or coughing. Aching pain behind sternum. Chest sore, with purple spots. Oppression of chest. Severe contracting pain within lower sternum, sometimes extending to rib joints and up to throat, as if esophagus was cramped.

Heart - Anxiety in region of heart. Consciousness of the heart. Sensation as if heart enlarged, too full of blood. As if the heart were pumping cold water. Purring at region of heart. Cardiac weakness from septic conditions. Threatened heart failure in zymotic and septic states. Fluttering sensation. Heart tired, as after a long run, increased action worse least motion. Palpitations, worse by motion. Palpitations are increased without corresponding increase of temperature. Pulse quick, out of all proportion to temperature or the reverse. Loud heartbeats, audible to herself and others. Throbbing felt in head and in ears, preventing sleep.

Back - Weakness, tired feeling in back. Weak feeling in back, stitching pain on coughing. Coldness, chill. Sharp, shooting pain. Caries, necrosis of spine. Lumbago. Pulsation, cervical region. Throbbing of vessels of neck running up in waves from clavicles. Breasts - Sore, bruised pain. Pains in the region of left nipple. Causations - Chronic complaints since septic conditions. After-effects of miscarriage. Remote effects of hepatitis, diphtheria, chronic malaria. Typhoid fever, puerperal fever. Bites, cuts, dissecting wounds, blood poisoning. Ptomaine poisoning, sewer-gas poisoning.

Limbs - Soreness, better from motion (Rhus- t.). Aching in bones, all over body as from a severe cold with soreness. Bed feels too hard (Bapt., Am.). Rapid bedsores of septic origin. Great debility in the morning. Chilliness. Cold limbs. Numbness of hands, arms and feet, extending over whole body. Cramps. Pain in right shoulder, worse coughing, talking. Automatic movement of right arm and right leg, in cerebrospinal meningitis. Tingling in right little toe as if frostbitten. Feet and legs swollen (Bright's disease). Milk leg, phlegmasia alba dolens, phlebitis. Perspiration on limbs. Ulcers. Varicose ulcers on lower limbs. Panaritium. Exfoliation of nails. Nails threaten to fall off or feel loose. Lungs - Pain in right lung, worse coughing, talking. Neglected pneumonia. Pleuritis. Empyema. Tuberculosis, last stage. Difficult breathing during sleep. Dyspnea, better open air. Wheezing when expiring. Horribly offensive expectoration, rusty mucus. Bloody expectoration, spitting of blood. Rusty sputum. Rattling ex- pectoration. Thick, offensive, purulent, viscid expectoration. Abscess opens, discharging pus.

Sleep - Restlessness. Unable to sleep for brain activity and crowding of ideas. Sleepless from fevers. Sleeplessness, bed feels too hard. Sleeplessness from thoughts. Kept awake by purring of heart. Seems to be in semi-sleep. Position changedfrequently. Slept awhile, wakes to roll and tumble. Whispering in sleep. Cries out in sleep that a weight is lying Pyrogenium on her. Restless sleep from dreams. Vivid dreams all night, of various things, of business. Frightful, anxious dreams.

Skin - Pale, cold, dry. Dryness and burning. Unhealthy skin, every scratch festers or heals with difficulty. Small cut or injury becomes very swollen and inflamed, discolored. Septic cuts, bites, wounds. Abscess. Ulcers offensive, putrid, purulent, fetid, sloughing. Ulcers with bloody discharges. Varicose ulcers. Offensive ulcers of old persons. Bedsores during fever. Lymphangitis, red streaks on skin. Boils. Blood boils. Carbuncles. Scarlatina. Smallpox. Purpura hemorrhagica. Obstinate varicose veins. Erysipelas. Ecchymosis. Actinomycosis.

Modalities - Better from heat, hot bathing, hot drinks. Better from pressure, stretching, motion, changing position, hard rocking and walking. Worse cold, damp. Worse sitting, motion, moving eyes, passing flatus.

Tongue - Tongue red and dry, clean, cracked, smooth, as if varnished. Brown streak down center. Red stripe down center. Cracked, fissured tongue. Excoriation of tongue. Fiery-red, glistening, tongue. Yellow tongue. Smooth, shining, glazed, glistening, glossy tongue. Large, flabby tongue, with imprints of teeth. Clean, clear tongue. Protruding the tongue is difficult. Vertigo - Staggers as if drunk on rising in morning. Dizziness on rising up in bed. COMMENTS - Drysdale prepared a tincture of Pyrog., which he preferred to call Pyrexin since it is not a mere fever-producer. Others have called it Sepsin, but this is too close to Septicemia, a name given to a related and perhaps identical nosode. The provings and most of the clinical experience have been obtained from this preparation. Subsequently, Dr. Swan po- tentized some septic pus, which has also been proved and clinically applied. There does not seem to be any marked difference in their effects. As Drysdale put it, “The most summary indication for Pyrog. would be to term it the Aconite of the typhus or typhoid quality of pyrexia,” and it is likely useful wherever there is poisoning by bacterial products (e.g. in the hectic of tuberculosis). Sepsis is the essence of its action. H. C. Allen, who published the proving and most of the cases in Med. Adv., rightly describes Pyrog. as a “Product of Sepsis.” He gave the indication for its use in septic state, “When the best selected remedies fail to relieve or permanently improve,” analogous to the action of Psor. and Sulph. in other conditions. Drysdale's original cases include a number in which threatened typhoid was averted, a case of tabes mesenterica cured, and one of ulceration of the colon greatly benefited. Drysdale's success was encouraging, but as he continued to use the tincture and the lowest potencies it was difficult to keep the preparation. The remedy did not come into extensive use until Burnett published his pamphlet on Pyrogenium in Fevers and Blood-poisoning in 1888. Burnett used chiefly the 6c dilution, which is perfectly harmless and which will keep indefinitely. Heath, who made one of the preparations used by Burnett, gave some of it to Swan of New York, who ran it up into the high infinitesimal. Much of the American experience is with Swan's potencies, including a proving by Sherbino. Yingling collected symptoms from many reported cases and arranged them with the symptoms of the proving. In Sherbino's proving, he was cured incidentally of a consciousness of the heart, and its working and palpitation from least excitement or anxiety, worse beginning to move, congestion to head as if a stroke would ensue. Cact. had done no good. Sherbino cured a case of puerperal fever with Pyrog., being led to its selection by the very high pulse rate. He also had a case of relapsed typhoid, with pulse 140, temperature 102 F., both were normal in twenty-four hours. He had a third case of a young woman, 17, with a fever and aching bones where the bed felt very hard. She had a numb, paralytic feeling. As the fever left, the pulse kept mounting up. Sherbino used Swan's potency, Pyrog. 100,000c, repeated as often as effect ceased. Clarke had ample opportunity to observe the power of Pyrog. over typhoid fever, typhoid, and hectic states, including one of discharging abscess connected with Pott's disease of the spine. Burnett had cases of fully developed typhoid cut short at the height by Pyrog. 6c given every two hours. In his pamphlet he included Dr. Shouldham's successful experience with Pyrog. 6c in two cases of diphtheria sore throat. Burnett also recorded that Pyrog. 5c, five drops in water night and morning, assisted in the cure of a case of anal fistula. Under its action a sweating at the seat, which the man had for many years, disappeared. The skin of his hands, which were subject to dry eczema, assumed a much cleaner aspect. J. S. Hunt reported five cases of varicose ulcers, all of which healed quickly under Pyrog. Bellairs gave Pyrog. 200c to an elderly woman who suffered for years with an ulcerated leg, which was riddled with deep, burrowing wounds, extremely painful and discharging freely. Hep., Sil., Ars., and Ham. did no good. Under Pyrog. once or twice a day, “a large boil” formed on the calf of the leg and discharged its contents after which the various ulcers healed up directly. Septicemia (Bapt., Merc., Rhus-t., Lach., Ars., Echi.), after surgery. Septic bites, cuts, wounds, and snakebites (Led., Hyper.). Blood poisoning, from dissecting wounds. Gangrene (Sec.). Abscesses with violent, burning pain. Abscesses in the muscles and major organs. Abscesses of the ovaries. Ruptured abscess of the lung, pus in the lungs. Ruptured organs, blood filled with pus. Septic organs, rotting away. Septic kidney with offensive urine. Ulceration of the colon with blood and pus in the stool. Severe, acute, abdominal infections; acute appendicitis, peritonitis. Septic varicose veins. Large boils with accompanying fever. Septic fever with pus, decomposed tissue, abscesses (Aeon, and Bell., are clean, inflammatory). Sudden, septic onset (Bapt.). Infected bite, cute or wound that lead to an infected fever. High fevers, 105-106 F. Fever and pulse don't match, high fever, slow pulse. Throbbing pains, sudden chills, rigors. Chill felt in the bones. Cold, clammy hands. Never well since septic fever (Bapt.). Typhoid, diphtheria. Toxic flu (Ars., Nux-v.). Delirium. Loquacity. Confusion about the body, delusion of too many limbs. Feel as if their body fills the whole bed. Cannot find their body. Delusion of a man at the foot of the bed. Staggers as if drunk, vertigo. Confused, muttering, talking in a whisper. Toxic state. All discharges and odors are offensive and fetid, diarrhea, sweat, breath, menses. Putrid, fetid, offensiveness. Stench-like odors; cadaver-like (Kreos., Bapt.). Offensive perspiration (Merc.). Bitter, offensive taste. Tongue is brown, yellow at the back. The tip of the tongue can be red (Rhus-t.). Constipation with black, putrid balls. Infected anal fissures with abscesses and offensive pus. Vomit of bile, blood and water, coffee grounds (Ars., Cadm-s.). Rapid, irregular heartbeats, high pulse. Feels as if the heart is pumping cold water. Hemorrhage of dark, offensive blood with high fever, especially with pelvic infections and abscesses. Nosebleeds with offensive blood. Uterine hemorrhage. Horribly offensive menses (Kreos.). Bloody, vaginal discharges that are offensive, no matter the cause. Septicemia after a miscarriage. For expelling a dead fetus (Sec.), beginning to decompose in the womb, with a fever. Decomposing placenta after labor. Severe muscle aches and soreness. Restless in bed. The bed feels hard (Arn., Bapt.). Difficulty getting comfortable. Flesh feels tender and sore. Bone aches, bruised feeling (Arn.). Pains better motion. Cannot lie in the same place very long, must move (Ars.). RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Echi., Carban., Ars., Lach., Rhus-t., Bapt. (2) Sepin. - a toxin of Proteus vulgaris, prepared by Dr. Shedd, same symptoms as Pyrogen of which it is the main constituent. (3) Malar., Lach. (4) In typhoid with soreness, bed feels hard, Bapt., (5) Arn., Rhus-t., better motion and stretching limbs, Rhus-t. (6) Cough worse by motion and in warm room, Bry. (7) Uterine hemorrhage, Ip. (8) Offensive diarrhea, Psor. (9) Black stools, Lept. (10) Constipation, Op., Sanie., Plb. (11) Lochia thin, fetid, Nit-ac. (12) Vomits water as soon as warm in stomach, Phos. Complementary: Ars., Bapt., Bry. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Kidneys - Bright's disease. Intolerable tenesmus of both bladder and rectum. Urging to urinate before fever. Frequent calls to urinate as fever comes on. Urination twice a day, scanty. Urine clear like water, Pyrogenium adhesive, red, slimy, sediment, deposits like red pepper. Putrid smelling urine, horribly offensive, carrion-like odor. Urine scanty, yellow after standing, cloudy with substance looking like orange peel. Urine, containing casts. Red sediment in urine hard to wash off. Albuminous urine during and after delivery, parturition. Suppression of urine, anuria.

Cough - Cough with large masses of phlegm from larynx, worse by motion, in warm room. Coughs up yellow sputa at night. Cough, with night-sweats, frequent pulse. Cough causes burning in larynx and bronchi. Cough better sitting up, worse lying down.

Perspiration - Clammy sweats. Shivering with sweats. Great heat with profuse hot sweat. Sweating does not cause a fall in temperature. Sweats without relief. Profuse sweats at night. Perspiration horribly offensive, carrion-like. Sour smelling sweats. Disgust, up to nausea, about any effluvia arising from her own body.

Temperature - Chilliness with perspiration. Cold sweatoverbody. Violentchill, begins in back between scapula, felt in bones with sweat, at night. Shivers and begins to move about restlessly. Cold and chilly all day, no fi Temperature rises rapidly. Quickly oscillating temperature. Great heat with profuse sweat. Sweating does not cause a fall in temperature, re would warm, sits by fire and chilly whenever he leaves it. Cold, then hot. Quotidian fever. Septic fevers. Latent pyrogenic condition. Cerebrospinal meningitis. Fever commencing with pains in the limbs. High fevers with sore limbs and delirium. Slowly advancing hectic fever. Fever and pulse don't match, high fever, slow pulse. Frequent calls to urinate as soon as fever came on, urine clear as water.
