full:
PHARMACY - pyrus. Pyrus americanus. Mountain ash. N. O. Rosaceae. The British is Pyrus aucuparia. Swamps and mountain woods from Maine to Pennsylvania. Tincture of fresh bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, irritation, prolapse. Chills. Clairvoyance. Dyspepsia. Gout. Heart, disorders. Hysteria. Rectum, constriction. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Tongue, paralysis. Uterus, prolapse.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pyrus Americanus, the Mountain Ash, was proved by Gatchell on himself, a married woman and two boys. Gatchell's only symptom was “irritation of the eyes.” Another prover had a similar symptom. By far the greatest number were induced in the woman, though hers were largely confirmed by those of the boys, and included severe neuralgic pains, and rheumatic and gouty symptoms. Labor-like or spasmodic pains were frequent in uterus, in bladder, like prolapse. Constrictive at base of lungs and around waist, like spasm of heart. Aches in every joint, acute intense pains like inflammatory rheumatism. Pains seem to move in lines. Worse motion, dreads to move on account of joints. Feels as if full of cold water. Worse cold, sensitive to cold and air. MIND - Brain active, intellect clear, thoughts vivid, whole being intensified. Indolent, indifferent, no inclination to read. Full of gloomy determination. Feels gloomy and discouraged but cannot cry. Sad, weeping mood, tears will come. Hypochondriac, not nervous, lazy, would like to lie in bed and be waited on. Feels weak as if about to die, moans, groans, calls for help. Cries and feels apprehension, fears something terrible going to happen. Seems to her that fundus of stomach is depressed in abdomen and pyloric end of fire, a red spot like raw beef there as if stomach burnt up with raw whiskey. Thinks she is clairvoyant, can read character and understand motions, see into herself. Seems to be able to go out of herself for a short distance to walk around and return into her body.

Head - Headache begins over eyes, pains knife-like, left side of headaches terribly like a toothache. Headache extends to right side. Head feels as if it would burst. Great weight at vertex. Shooting pains in forehead. Headache penetrating in temples.

Eyes - Irritation of eyes. Eyes feel as if they had been crying a long time, smart.

Mouth - Tongue partially paralyzed, cannot direct it.

Throat - Throat feels obstinate. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. Compare: (1) Neuralgic and gouty pains, Prun. (2) Heart, Crat. (3) Chilliness, Camph. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Stomach - Stomach feels weak as if nothing would digest, it feels dry and wrinkled. Feels as if stomach full of cold water. Thinks mucus accumulated in cold stomach. Feeling of coldness extends up sternum and esophagus.

Abdomen - Feels constricted around waist, obliged to loosen clothes at once.

Rectum - Sensation as if rectum were shrunken and dried up. Sensations - As if she were outside of herself and could see into herself. As if stomach full of cold water, coldness extends up esophagus under sternum. As if rectum were shrunken and dried up. As if left leg drawn up and would never straighten again.

Female - Bearing down and pressing out as if swollen and burning all over. Sense of prolapse of womb. Food - Craves hot tea. Wants soft food, feels as if meat would not digest.

Chest - Feels as if lungs congested, especially at base and constricted.

Heart - Oppression about heart as if it had stopped beating, as if going into convulsions. Sense of spasm at heart, as if blood too thick to circulate (better by Camph.). Heart aches as if from some great sorrow.

Back - Sick feeling under right scapula.

Limbs - Twinging pains in arms, legs and toes. Drawing, cutting pain. Joints feel constricted and sore. Some pain in finger joints. Pains drawn, rending along backs of thighs to toes, worse left. Feels as if left leg drawn up and would never straighten again. Tight feeling of patella. Pain in knees is followed by pain in tendons and along calves. Knees and toes feel as if immensely swollen and ache. Left great toe feels as if torn from its socket. Toes burn. Unendurable aching of bones of toes. Lungs - Can hardly breathe, as if cold water in stomach. Spasmodic breathing as of nervous women. Dry cough, as if pharynx stuffed with cotton. Hoarseness. Can't talk loudly, voice gone.

Skin - Clammy feeling of skin.

Kidneys - Irritation of bladder and urethra. Sensation as if bladder prolapsed.

Temperature - Chilly when air strikes him. Chilly down back and both legs. Very cold, shivering internally, thinks she must look blue. Cold creeping all over. Chilly and with a very tranquil feeling, especially of consciousness. Glow all over, hands sweat.

full:
PHARMACY - quas. Quassia amara. Quassia wood. Picrena excelsa, (Jamaica) and Quassia amara (Surinam). N. O. Simarubacee. Tincture or cold infusion of the wood. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Ascites. Cataract. Cirrhosis. Dyspepsia. Dysentery. Headaches. Heartburn. Indigestion. Intermittent fever. Threadworms. Worms.

HERBAL - The Quassia now found in the shops in the form of “Quassia chips” is the wood of Picrena, the Jamaica Quassia. The name “Quassia” was given by Linneus to Quassia excelsa of Surinam from the name of a healer, Quassi or Coissi, who employed its bark as a remedy for fever. The wood of this tree was formerly employed under the name of Surinam Quassia. The wood is very bitter and yields its properties best to cold, distilled water. In the old school the infusion is used as a bitter tonic in dyspepsia, and in enemas for clearing the rectum of threadworms.

HOMEOPATHIC - Quas. acts on digestive organs as a tonic (Gent., Hydr.). Pressure and stitches in liver and sympathetically in spleen. Pain in right intercostal muscles above the liver. Seems to possess a marked action on eyes, producing amblyopia and cataract.

Head - Constant dullness of head.

Stomach - Dyspepsia after infectious diseases, especially influenza, dysentery. Atonic dyspepsia with flatus and acidity. Heartburn and gastralgia. Regurgitation of food.

Abdomen - Sticking pains between umbilicus and stomach. Abdomen feels empty and retracted. Abdomen hard and distended.

Rectum - Stools at first hard with great effort, afterwards pasty, once very thin.

Back - Sensation of coldness running over back with constant inclination to yawn and stretch out the feet.

Neck - Severe drawing pains in cervical muscles.

Limbs - Prostration, with hunger. Inclination to yawn and stretch (Rhus-t.). Sensation of coldness over back. Cold limbs with sensation of internal coldness (Helo.). Drawing pain in calves.

Tongue - Tongue dry or with brown sticky coating. COMMENTS - There is a short homeopathic proving. J. O. Muller took a single dose of the tincture, Eidherr four doses of Quas. 30x. Lembke took the extract. The most peculiar characteristic symptoms were drawing in hypochondria and sensation as if abdomen were empty and retracted, with sensation as if he would have a stool. Stool at first hard with effort, later pasty. Sticking in liver and abdomen. Peculiar beating through abdomen, extending into limbs. Eidherr had “coldness running over back with constant inclination to yawn and desire to stretch out the feet,” which gives a clue to its action in fevers. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Fevers - Cedr. (2) Worms - Cina. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Liver - Very acute sticking in hepatic region, followed by dull pain. Cirrhosis of liver with ascites.

Kidneys - Excessive desire, impossible to retain urine. Secretion of urine increased, solid constituents diminished. Copious urination day and night. As soon as the child wakes up the bed is drenched.

PHARMACY - queb. Quebracho aspidosperma. White quebracho. Aspidosperma quebracho. N. O. Apocynaceae. Tincture and trituration of the bark. Trituration and solutions of the alkaloid aspidospermine and its salts. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

full:
PHARMACY - queb. Quebracho aspidosperma. White quebracho. Aspidosperma quebracho. N. O. Apocynaceae. Tincture and trituration of the bark. Trituration and solutions of the alkaloid aspidospermine and its salts. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Cardiac, asthma. Cyanosis. Dyspnea. Emphysema. Fever. Heart, disorders. Paralysis. Pulmonary stenosis.

HERBAL - Quebracho is a Brazilian herbal remedy from which the alkaloid aspidosper- mine has been isolated. The alkaloid takes the form of small, very brilliant, white crystals, sparingly soluble in water, readily soluble in alcohol and ether. Queb. removes obstruction to the oxidation of the blood by stimulating respiratory centers. Increases oxidation and excretion of carbonic acid.

HOMEOPATHIC - Shortness of breath during exertion. Dyspnea, respiratory paralysis, slowed heart and paralysis of limbs. Dyspnea with cyanosis. Dyspnea in tuberculosis and pleurisy. Uremic dyspnea. Asthma, cardiac asthma. Emphysema. Pulmonary stenosis. Thrombosis of pulmonary artery. COMMENTS - Dr. Hale reported that Aspin, or Queb. is derived from the Chilean “White Quebracho” (Aspidospermine Quebracho). At Santiago de Chile, the bark is used as a substitute for chinchona as a febrifuge. The alkaloid forms salts with citric, hydrochloric and sulphuric acids. Hale said Queb. produces in animals dyspnea, respiratory paralysis, slowed heart and paralysis of limbs. It relieves dyspnea in tuberculosis and pleurisy, but without influencing the fever. The lx relieved asthma with livid face, and dyspnea with cyanosis is frequently relieved by it. Following this were signs of emphysema and severe attacks of asthma. Rales were heard and “pearls” of rounded gelatinous masses were expectorated. Aspin. 3x gave more relief than any other remedy. Hale noted two cases relieved by it, one of mitral incompetence and stenosis with severe nocturnal dyspnea, the other of fatty heart (Queb. had no influence on the edema, which was removed by Dig.). Jos. P. Cobb recorded a case of heart affection of some duration in a man, age 24. There was some heart enlargement, especially of right side. Much dyspnea and a slight mitral murmur. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Hale.

name: Quercus Glandium Spiritus
author: Murphy
constitution: Alcoholism. Breath, offensive. Constipation. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Fistula. Giddiness. Gout. Intermitting, fever. Leucocythemia, splenica. Liver, disorders. Spleen, disorders. Spleen, dropsy.
keynote: PHARMACY - querc. Quercus glandium spiri- tus. Acom kernels. Aqua glandium quercus. Quercus robur var. English oak. Quercus pedunculata. Quercus sessilifera. N. O. Corylacee or Cupulifere. Fagaceae. Tincture of acoms are peeled and crushed or shredded. Water extract of acoms…
full:
PHARMACY - querc. Quercus glandium spiri- tus. Acom kernels. Aqua glandium quercus. Quercus robur var. English oak. Quercus pedunculata. Quercus sessilifera. N. O. Corylacee or Cupulifere. Fagaceae. Tincture of acoms are peeled and crushed or shredded. Water extract of acoms with addition of alcohol for Aqua glandium quercus. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Breath, offensive. Constipation. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Fistula. Giddiness. Gout. Intermitting, fever. Leucocythemia, splenica. Liver, disorders. Spleen, disorders. Spleen, dropsy.

HERBAL - Rademacher gave the tincture of acorns to an old brandy drunkard who had long suffered from the spleen, which was at times very painful and who was at that time “sick unto death” with ascites and dropsy of the legs. The urine at once increased, but the patient complained that each dose of the medicine caused constriction of the chest. This led Rademacher to prepare the Distilled Spirit and finally the Aqua, as milder preparations, which they proved to be, for the remedy completely cured the patient without causing further constriction of the chest. In the course of cures of spleen cases Rademacher noticed that not only was the flow of urine increased, there was also, especially in old spleen engorgements, an eliminative diarrhea with amelioration of the symptoms generally. A passing diarrhea often appears for a time when using it.

HOMEOPATHIC - Querc. is one of Rademacher's splenic remedies. It was introduced to homeopathic practice by Burnett, who published a translation of Rademacher's account of the remedy. Chronic spleen disorders and spleen dropsy. Dropsy and liver disorders. Useful in gout, old malarial cases with flatulence. Flushed state. Vertigo, deafness with noises in head. Exceedingly nervous. Antidotes effects of alcohol. Desire for alcoholic drinks. Burnett does not find Querc. a remedy for the liquor habit, it stops short at that, but it diminishes the craving and antidotes the alcoholic state. Clarke noted that Querc. acts well in trituration of the Acorn 3x in splenic cases, flatulence, old malaria and alcoholic history. Missionaries who used Querc. on Burnett's indications in spleen disorders found it no less effective in the intermittent fevers which gave rise to the enlarged spleens. Powdered oak bark is an excellent dry dressing for ulcers and discharging wounds. MIND - Nervous, depressed, glum, taciturn. Easily moved to tears, not quite capable of stating his own case.

Head - Peculiar sensation in head, feel as when drunk, sensation lasts a minute or two. Gouty eczema of scalp, poll and backs of hands.

Mouth - Foul breath, stercoraceous. Tongue foul.

Stomach - Gnawing at pit of stomach. Flatulent dyspepsia. Removes craving for alcohol. Vertigo - Wheeling vertigo. Vertigo with disorders of spleen and left side. Afraid to move for fear having a stroke or giddiness would come on. COMMENTS - Burnett noted the symptom “Certain few people feel, as soon as they have taken it, a peculiar sensation in the head, lasting barely a minute or two, which they say is like being drunk.” This led him to use it in the treatment of alcoholism and its effects, which he elaborated in his Gout and its Cure. The first case Burnett noted was that of a military man, 64, broken down with gout and alcoholism and pretty severe chronic bronchitis. Heart irregular. Liver and spleen enlarged. Complained bitterly of gnawing at pit of stomach. Gait tottering, hands quivered. He had lost his wife and had to keep himself up with nips of spirits, for which he had a constant craving. Querc., ten drops in water, three times a day, completely revolutionized his state and took away his abnormal craving for spirits. In a merchant of 57, given to nips of sherry, Querc. threw out a gouty eczema on scalp, poll and backs of hands, which took three months to cure after which Querc. was again given and completed the cure. An officer who drank too much had foul breath, eyes yellow, puffy underneath. Querc. cured. A hunting man, 40, free liver, gouty, had varicose veins of legs originating apparently in enlarged spleen, left by typhoid fever. Querc. cured. The patient said it kept his “bowels very regular.” A country squire, 60, bachelor, appeared in a hopeless condition. Was unable to state his own case. Flushed, much pain over the eyes and in both rib regions. Stooping caused great pain, worse left hypochondrium. Liver and spleen much enlarged. Nervous, depressed, glum, taciturn, easily moved to tears. Could not walk without support on account of his great giddiness. Breath in highest degree disgustingly stercoraceous, nearly caused Burnett to vomit when examining him. That smell of breath, said Burnett is an unmistakable sign of the chronic tippler indicating undigested alcohol. Burnett subsequently ascertained that he was quite a sober man, but took frequent nips, particularly when confined to the house by wet weather. The pain in left side, giddiness, and flushed state indicated Querc., which was given. In a week the breath was normal, giddiness a little better, tenderness of rib region much diminished. In six weeks he was quite well. Clarke, noting that giddiness with spleen trouble is met by it, gave Querc. to a young woman for extreme whirling vertigo, an affect of influenza. The patient was greatly relieved when she took it in a severe attack, but if she took it when the giddiness was only slight it caused severe aggravation. Patients to whom Cooper gave Querc. complained that they “felt as if in a vice, dared not move for fear of having a stroke or an attack of giddiness.” “Deafness with noises in the head” is another effect observed by Cooper. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ange., Nux-v. (2) Lach., Nat-m. (3) Helia., Cean. - spleen enlarged and painful. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Abdomen - Pain in spleen region. Pain in hypochondria, worse left, much worse by stooping. Ascites.

Rectum - Diarrhea. “It keeps his bowels open. ” Fistula in alcoholics.

Chest - Constriction of chest in précordia. Ears - Deafness and noises in the head. Eyes - Eyes yellow, puffy underneath. Face - Flushed.

Heart - Fluttering, irregular heart. Kidneys - Increased flow of urine. Limbs - Gouty eczema of backs of hands. Hands tremble. Dropsy tottering gait. Varicose veins.

Liver - Enlarged liver and spleen.

full:
PHARMACY - quill. Quillaya saponaria. Chile soap bark tree. N. O. Rosaceae. Soap bark contains saponine. Tincture of the dried bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bronchitis. Catarrh. Colds. Coryza. Coughs. Lung, disorders. Sneezing. Sore, throats.

HOMEOPATHIC - Quill, is most effective in the beginning of colds, coryza, often checking its further development. Colds with sore throat, heat and dryness of throat. Acute catarrh, sneezing and sore throat. Coughs with difficult expectoration. Squamous skin. COMMENTS - Quill, is used herbally to loosen cough in chronic bronchitis and pulmonary complaints. The infusion of 1/2 oz of bark in 1 pint of boiling water is taken in tablespoonful doses or more as required. It is also used externally as a cleansing application to cutaneous ulcers and eruptions. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kali-hp., Gels., All-c., Squil. (2) Sapo. - sore throat involuntary urination. Seneg. REFERENCES - Boericke. Murphy.

name: Radium Bromatum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better lying down, after sleep. Better continued motion, pressure, hot bath, open air. Better eating, cold drinks. Worse from smoking, shaving, washing. Worse getting up, warmth of the bed. Worse at night, noon, 3 a.m., 4 a.m., 7 a.m., and 11 a.m..

Tic douloureux. Trachoma. Ulcers. Warts. X- ray dermatitis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pure radium is a white metal which “oxidizes in water, bums paper, turns black on exposure to air and has the property of adhering firmly to iron.” This last quality is not without significance and shows a close affinity with fenrum. It is found in ore pitchblende. The discovery of radium and its properties in 1898 by Pierre and Marie Curie set many persons thinking and among them, naturally, those who are engaged in the healing of the sick. Curie himself made the first “proving.” He put a tiny bit of radium salt in an India rubber capsule and fastened it to his arm, leaving it there for ten hours. When he took it off the skin was red, the place turned into a wound, which took four months to heal, leaving a white scar the size of a shilling surrounded by discolored, puckered skin. On another occasion he left it for half an hour. A wound appeared at the end of a fortnight and took another fortnight to heal. On a third occasion, it was left for eight minutes only, two months later the skin became red and a bit sore, but it soon passed off. Skin and nerves are affected. Acne rosacea, nevi, moles. Cancer. Lymphoid tissue. Ulcers due to radium burns, that take a long time to heal. Effects of x-ray burns. Effective for rheumatism and gout. Chronic rheumatic arthritis. Severe aching pains all over with restlessness, better moving about. Nerves are affected causing suddenly shifting or electric pains, must lie down. Electric shocks through the body during sleep. Dull, hard aching pains all over, deep in joints, very restless. Numbness, worse stretching the part. Dry burning heat, as if on fire, through the entire body, craves cool air. Constriction of the chest, heart etc., with air hunger. Lowered blood pressure. Necrotic changes. Marked increase in the white bloodcells. Lateness in appearance of symptoms. Weakness, lassitude, tiredness. Great weakness. MIND - Apprehensive, depressed. Tired and irritable. Cross. Easily vexed. Torpid, apathetic. Great desire to be with people, wants to have someone near. Fear of being alone, of the dark.

Head - Both eyes ache. Severe pain over right eye, spreading back to occiput and to vertex, better in open air. Occipital and vertex pain, accompanying severe lumbar aching. Frontal headache. Head feels heavy. Aching pain of right lower jaw. Violent trifacial neuralgia.

Eyes - Red, smarting, worse reading. Sensation as if pieces of cotton in eyes, better rubbing.

Ears - Sound of rushing water, better lying on face.

Nose - Burning in nose. Itching and dryness of nasal cavities, better in open air.

Face - Flushed. Acne rosacea. Aching pain in angle of right lower jaw. Violent trifacial neuralgia.

Mouth - Dry mouth. Breath seems hot. Metallic taste. Prickling sensation on end of tongue.

Throat - Dry, sore, raw with earache. Feeling in throat as from eating pepper. Vertigo - Vertigo with pain in back of head, left when in bed. COMMENTS - After investigating radium for ten years, Dieffenbach reported that when the provings commenced, one prover’s hands had eczematous eruptions, cracks, scaly excrescences and wart-like growths as a result of X-ray and radium-ray experiments. These gradually disappeared after his proving with 6x. This is confirmed by a case reported by Mr. E. S. Pierrepont. A girl employed in the X-ray department of the hospital with which he was connected developed dermatitis of the right hand and fingers. An ointment was prescribed without benefit, and cracks appeared on the skin. Two doses of Rad- br. 30c were given, on Mr. Pierrepont’s suggestion, one in the morning and one in the evening. The following day the patient came out in a rash, which the matron mistook for measles. Her eyes watered, fingers very sore and she felt very ill. By the following day, the rash had disappeared and she felt well. The fingers were now better and they got quite well, except that a sore feeling was left after washing. A feature of Dieffenbach’s proving was the disappearance of small nevi, which is significant as the rays are used for the destruction of nevi. Useful for indolent and phagedenic ulcers. Sores that refuse to heal. Skin cancers, especially cancerous ulcers. Severe psoriasis. There is some history of moles and birthmarks disappearing. Dermatitis and eczema after radiation exposure. Radium burns. Ulcers due to radiation treatment (Fl-ac.). After affects of radiation exposure, weakness, tendency to infections, where nothing else seems to work (Stront.). Rad-br has been used in cases of lupus, epithelioma, carcinoma of the cervix uterus and urethral caruncle. There are numerous cases of skin cancers cured with Rad-br. in potencies. T. Simpson recorded one such case. A retired officer had an intractable eruption on his genitals and the inner surface of thighs and legs that had prevented him from getting any refreshing sleep for three years. One tablet of Rad-br. 30c each morning was prescribed for a month. All conditions were vastly improved and the patient got well without further medication. Clarke reported the case of a young, unmarried woman who, after the application of a belladonna plaster to the back for lumbago, developed an edematous rash involving the whole face and neck. It was extremely irritating, worse at night, preventing sleep. At the back of the neck was a sore, oozing patch. After temporary relief from some remedies, there still remained an irritating, oozing rash, sore eyes, first right, then left, lids swollen, oozing from corners, lips hard, swollen. One dose of Rad-br. 30c was given. The result was dramatic. The first night she was able to sleep, waking only once. Two days later, the rash had nearly gone and the eyes had ceased to water. In a few days all had vanished and the patient could enjoy open air. Dr. S. L. Guild-Leggett recorded the case of a girl, 2.5 years, who had shifting rheumatism from her left foot to right knee, then to left knee, hands and toes. She had also a peculiarity about her stools, they were slate- colored, very offensive, urgent and came at noon during a meal. Guild-Leggett used symptoms from Dieffenbach’s proving: “defecation at noon, stool soft, dark or offensive, slate-color, clay-color, pains in limbs, wakes 4 a.m., pains in all joints knees, ankles, feet, could not walk, had to lie down.” Rad-br. was given and cured entirely. RELATIONS-Antidotes: Rhus-v., Tell. Compare: ( 1 ) Anae. - the ulceration produced by it is like radium. It may appear elsewhere than on place of contact and appear late. (2) X-ray, Rhus-t., Sep., Uran-n., Ars., Puls., Caust. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Empty feeling in stomach. Warm sensation in stomach. Nausea and sinking sensation, belching of gas.

Abdomen - Alternating with chest or ear symptoms. Pain over McBurney’s point and at location of sigmoid flexure. Colic better bending double and passing stools. Pain, violentcramps, rumbling, full of gas. Much flatulence.

Rectum - Alternating constipation and loose movements. Stools, soft, dark or offensive, slate colored. Rectum sore, prolapsed. Itching of anus and hemorrhoids. Sensations - As if skull too small, as if foreign body in eye, as if something dropped into trachea. Knees feel as if the bones would protrude. Intolerance of tobacco can be produced.

Male - Eczema of penis and inner surface of thighs. Itching. Dysuria, then erection.

Female - Itching genitals, pruritus vul- vae. Aching over pubes during menses. Delayed and irregular menstruation and backache. Menses last one day, then bloody leucorrhea. Leucorrhea, white and scanty, curdy and cheesy. Uterine hemorrhage (Ip.). Lochia putrid, scanty or suppressed. Food - Nausea, better eating. Usual food not relished, sour things taste good. Craves pork. Aversion to sweets, ice creams, of which she is usually very fond.

Chest - Tightness of chest. Chest pain alternating with indigestion and stuffed up feeling.

Heart - Constriction. Wakes with palpitations. Pulse, rapid, irregular, fluttering. Low blood pressure.

Back - Aching in back of neck. Pain and lameness in cervical vertebrae, worse dropping head forward, better standing or sitting erect. Weakness between scapulae. Backache between shoulders and lumbar- sacral region, better after walking. Lumbar and sacral aches, pain appears to be in bone, continued motion relieves, better hot bath, worse going upstairs. Breasts - Right breast sore, better hard rubbing. Causations - Ill effects of x-ray, radiation burns.

Limbs - Arthritis, aching pains, worse at night. Deep pain in joints, knees and ankles. Muscles of legs and hips sore. Pain in toes, calves, hip joint, popliteal spaces. Legs, arms and neck feel hard and brittle, as though they would break on moving. Cracking in shoulder. Sharp pains in shoulders, arms, hands and fingers. Arms feel heavy. Rheumatism of the hands. Dermatitis of the fingers. Trophic changes in the fingernails. Lungs - Tightness of chest, feels as if she could not get enough air. Spasmodic cough. Persistent cough from tickling in throat pit. Cough, worse lying, smoking, better eating and open air, sitting up, exercise.

Sleep - Restless. Sleepiness with lethargy. Wakes panting with palpitations. Dreams vivid, busy, of fire, which seems true.

Skin - Itching all over body, burning of skin, as if on fire. Irritable, thick, moist if scratched, worse face and genitals. Erythema and dermatitis with itching, burning, swelling and redness. Eczema. Psoriasis. Small pimples. Branny scabs. Scabby on ears. Scleroderma. Callosities. Cancer. Necrosis and ulceration. Epi- thelioma.

Modalities - Better lying down, after sleep. Better continued motion, pressure, hot bath, open air. Better eating, cold drinks. Worse from smoking, shaving, washing. Worse getting up, warmth of the bed. Worse at night, noon, 3 a.m., 4 a.m., 7 a.m., and 11 a.m.

Kidneys - Nephritis with rheumatism. Kidney irritation, albuminuria, granular and hyaline casts. Increased elimination of sediment. Bedwetting.

Temperature - Cold sensation internally, with chattering of teeth. Internal chilliness followed by heat of the skin, associated with bowel movements and flatulence.

name: Radon
author: Murphy
constitution: Adenocarcinoma. Emphysema. Lung cancer. Lung, disorders. Pneumonia, interstitial. Pulmonary fibrosis. Respiratory lesions. Silicosis.
keynote:
PHARMACY - rado. Radon. Radioactive gas. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Adenocarcinoma. Emphysema. Lung cancer. Lung, disorders. Pneumonia, interstitial. Pulmonary fibrosis. Respiratory lesions. Silicosis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Radon is a toxic radioactive gas, formed by…
full:
PHARMACY - rado. Radon. Radioactive gas. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Adenocarcinoma. Emphysema. Lung cancer. Lung, disorders. Pneumonia, interstitial. Pulmonary fibrosis. Respiratory lesions. Silicosis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Radon is a toxic radioactive gas, formed by the natural radioactive decay of uranium in rock, soil, and water. It is colorless, odorless, tasteless, and chemically inert. Radon gas decays into radioactive particles that can get trapped in the lungs when breathed in. The primary adverse health effect associated with chronic exposure to radon is lung cancer. Squamous cell carcinoma. Small cell carcinoma. Large cell carcinoma. Adenocarcinoma. Other harmful respiratory effects associated with chronic exposure to radon include emphysema, pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory lesions. Chronic interstitial pneumonia. Silicosis. COMMENTS - Uranium changes to different elements as it decays down to its final element of lead. All of the elements it changes into are solids except one, radon, which floats freely in the soil and is easily drawn into the lower level of homes by the natural flow of air. Radon’s primary hazard is caused from inhalation of the gas and its highly radioactive heavy metallic decay products (polonium, lead, and bismuth) which tend to collect on dust in the air. REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Rajania Subsamarata
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from coolness, discharges. Worse from moving, speaking..
constitution: Abscesses. Anthrax. Bacillary, dysentery. Blepharitis. Boils. Colitis. Diphtheria. Encephalitis. Fevers. Mastoiditis. Measles. Meningitis. Myelitis. Typhoid. Vaccination, reactions.
keynote:
PHARMACY - raja-s. Rajania subsamarata. Amphypterygium adstringes. N. O. Anacar- diaceae or Dioscoreaceae family. Tincture from the triturated and macerated bark in 80% alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Anthrax. Bacillary, dysentery.…
full:
PHARMACY - raja-s. Rajania subsamarata. Amphypterygium adstringes. N. O. Anacar- diaceae or Dioscoreaceae family. Tincture from the triturated and macerated bark in 80% alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Anthrax. Bacillary, dysentery. Blepharitis. Boils. Colitis. Diphtheria. Encephalitis. Fevers. Mastoiditis. Measles. Meningitis. Myelitis. Typhoid. Vaccination, reactions.

HERBAL - Rajania subsamarata is a shrub 1.50m high, which grows in the Michoacan in the warm territories of Morelos and Guerrero. It has dioecious leaves, a trilocular herbaceous stem and the limb is cut near the top. It has six fibrous stamens, an ovary linked to the perigon tube with two to three seeds in the receptacle.

HOMEOPATHIC - De Legarreta proved the remedy, reporting symptoms of high fevers, general exhaustion. Stares, stunned, closes eyes as if to think more easily. Jaw hangs, muscles relaxed, slips into bed. No longer has the strength to speak. Swelling of the neck and parotid region. Measles, diphtheria or whooping-cough. Epidemic spinal and cerebral meningitis. Acute post infectious encephalitis in the child. Post-vaccination encephalitis. Circumscribed inflammation of the skin with swelling or ulceration. Congestion of the nerves and blood vessels. The diarrhea is muco-purulent and blood-streaked. Metrorrhagia of black, putrid blood. MIND - Indifferent towards everything around him, bewildered. Loss of sense of identity. Mumbles in his delirium, weeps and sighs and speaks incoherently. Sings bawdy or religious songs. Fits of exaltation, fury and lasciviousness.

Head - Acute headache, like a nail being driven into the head. Pain in the head persisting for a long time, accompanied by anguished lamentation.

Eyes - Eyes bloodshot. Eyes bright at first, then lusterless, as if covered with a film of gum or tears, which are burning and corrosive. The pupil is contracted and insensitive to light. Conjunctivitis. Eyelids are heavy, eyelashes stuck together. Blepharitis.

Ears - Mastoiditis. Catarrhal discharge. Suppurating inflammation of the eardrum. Sensitive to sharp sounds. Buzzing. Sensation of blocked ear, as if full of earth. Sounds seem far off like distantrain. Later total deafness.

Nose - Rhinitis. Sinusitis. Ozaena. Nose dry. Hairs inside the nose bristling, as if dusty. Attacks of nosebleed, which ameliorate. If abundant, they are exhausting.

Face - Face dull, serious at first, then aspect becomes hippocratic, cadaverous. Earthy, dirty, moist.

Mouth - Breath fetid, putrid, repulsive. Sticky saliva, nicotine-colored like that of a tobacco chewer. Aphthae and ulcerations which bleed at times, on the tip of the tongue. Tongue fissured with black stripe injhe middle and red, excoriated edges. Teeth tarnished with yellow, then brown, deposit, despite frequent brushing. Lips swollen. Mouth open, lowerjaw dropping. Slight trismus at times.

Throat - Throat dry with need for liquid in order to swallow. Cold foods go down better than warm foods. External swelling of the throat and parotid region. COMMENTS - Rajania has been used in compress form for ulcerations, diluted in water with 1% or 2% of the mother tincture. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Mur-ac. - Adynamic conditions, prostration, hyperthermia, deep, bleeding ulcerations. The patient is so exhausted that he falls into bed. (2) Lach. - Acute infections, adynamic condition with tendency to hemorrhage and decomposition of the blood. Loquacity, burning pains, cannot bear anything tight, cardiac failure, ameliorated by drainage, spontaneous ecchymosis. (3) Anthr. - Septic infections, burning pains, extreme prostration. (4) Bapt., Hyos., Bell., Stram. and Crot-h. REFERENCES-Julian.

Stomach - Paresis of the esophagus with difficulty in swallowing. Hiccoughs, nausea, vomiting.

Abdomen - Hypogastric region painful, especially when speaking. Abdomen retracted into a boat shape. Rumbling and abdominal wind. Gurgling in the right iliac cavity and pain at McBurney’s point. Cholera-like enteritis. Enteritis. Ileitis. Bacillary dysentery. Hemorrhaging recto-colitis.

Rectum - Constipation for the first few days, then diarrhea. Diarrhea, mucopurulent, blood-streaked, loosely bound, very fetid.

Male - Soft canker. Ulcers. Epithelioma of the glans. Penis limp, scrotum slack. Fetid sweating, smelling of rancid cheese.

Female - Menses ameliorate the general condition. Menses with evil-smelling blood, black and irritating. Menses with a bitter odor. Metritis. Profuse, sticky leucorrhea, causing vaginal insensitivity. Labia majora excoriated. Puerperal fever. Venereal granuloma. Ulcerous vulvar elephantiasis.

Heart - Fall in arterial tension. Sub-acute myocarditis. Pericarditis. Palpitations and diffuse pains in the precordial region. Pulse thready, weak. Heartbeat irregular, moderate tachycardia. Hears the heart heat when lying down, as if the heart were on the pillow.

Limbs - Limbs trembling and slack with convulsions. Limbs are cold, purple. Continual involuntary movements of the hands, as if seizing particles in the air. Lungs - Chest swollen, panting and anguish. Respiration weak, becoming imperceptible. Pulmonary gangrene. Pulmonary abscess. Breath fetid.

Skin - Skin rough, sticky sweat. Earthy appearance with petechiae on the chest, abdomen and on the inside of the arms. Erysipelas. Pimples, boils, suppurating abscesses. Bedsores. Varicose ulcers. Painful, purulent anthrax. Soft canker with fetid, blood-streaked discharge. Gangrenous patches. Septic gangrene. Cancerous tumors and ulcerations with blue-black edges, painful and bleeding.

Modalities - Better from coolness, discharges. Worse from moving, speaking.

Temperature - Fever high, general exhaustion. Temperature between 39.5°C and 41 °C.

name: Ranunculus Acris
author: Murphy
constitution: Erysipelas. Fever. Gangrene. Lumbago. Neuralgia. Rheumatism. Ulcers.
keynote:
PHARMACY - ran-a. Ranunculus acris. Goldcup. Crowfoot. Ranunculus acer. N. O. Ranunculacee. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Erysipelas. Fever. Gangrene. Lumbago. Neuralgia. Rheumatism. Ulcers.

HERBAL - Ran-a. is distinguished from Ran- b. by…
full:
PHARMACY - ran-a. Ranunculus acris. Goldcup. Crowfoot. Ranunculus acer. N. O. Ranunculacee. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Erysipelas. Fever. Gangrene. Lumbago. Neuralgia. Rheumatism. Ulcers.

HERBAL - Ran-a. is distinguished from Ran- b. by its slender cylindrical flower-stalk, that of Ran-b. being furrowed. Both are common buttercups, and have acrid and poisonous properties.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ran-a. was proved by Franz and Lembke. The chief skin symptoms were observed in a woman of seventy who applied a handful of the herb to her limbs with the result of setting up violent constitutional symptoms, fever and intense inflammation, going on to gangrene of the skin of the legs. Rheumatic pain in the muscles and joints, especially ankles and wrists. Pains when walking and at rest. Lumbar pains, worse on bending or turning the body. Heat, faintness and fever. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ran-b. REFERENCES Clarke.

name: Ranunculus Bulbosus
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from standing, sitting bent forward. Worse from open air, drafts, change of temperature, atmospheric changes. Worse damp, cold, rainy and stormy weather. Worse from change of position, motion of arms, standing, breathing, touch. Worse evening and morning. Worse after eating, alcohol. Worse from fright, vexation, anger..
constitution: Adhesions. Alcoholism. Breast, pain. Cachexia. Chest, pains. Chilblains. Corns. Delirium tremens. Depression. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dyspnea. Eczema. Epilepsy. Feet, pains. Gastralgia. Hangovers. Hay fever. Herpes zoster. Hiccoughs. Hydrocele. Hydrothorax. Intercostal, pain. Jaundice. Liver, pain.Neuralgias. Nyctalopia. Ovaries, neuralgia. Pemphigus. Pleurodynia. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Spinal, irritatio
keynote:
PHARMACY - ran-b. Ranunculus bulbosus. Buttercup. Bulbous crowfoot. North America. N. O. Ranunculacee. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Adhesions. Alcoholism. Breast, pain. Cachexia. Chest, pains. Chilblains. Corns. Delirium tremens.…
full:
PHARMACY - ran-b. Ranunculus bulbosus. Buttercup. Bulbous crowfoot. North America. N. O. Ranunculacee. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Adhesions. Alcoholism. Breast, pain. Cachexia. Chest, pains. Chilblains. Corns. Delirium tremens. Depression. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dyspnea. Eczema. Epilepsy. Feet, pains. Gastralgia. Hangovers. Hay fever. Herpes zoster. Hiccoughs. Hydrocele. Hydrothorax. Intercostal, pain. Jaundice. Liver, pain.Neuralgias. Nyctalopia. Ovaries, neuralgia. Pemphigus. Pleurodynia. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Spinal, irritation. Warts. Writer’s cramp.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ran-b. was proved by Franz and some effects of its external application have been observed and results of inhaling the fumes while preparing the plant or when it has been burned. The last caused headache and in one instance epilepsy, followed by cachexia, gout, headache and death. One prover, who expressed the juice with the fingers, reported a long-lasting and recurrent eruption of vesicles on the fingers, with blue vesicles and horny scabs. “Small, deep, transparent, dark blue little elevated blisters of the size of an ordinary pin ’ s head. Crowded together in oval-shaped groups of the size of a coin with intolerable burning itching, emitting when opened a dark yellow lymph afterwards becoming covered with a herpetic, horny scurf.” Symptoms rising from the acrid vapor while the juice of the plant was being prepared included “Smarting from eyes as from smoke in evening. Smarting in eyes, nose and fauces, the eyes run and are very painful. He has to stop using them for half an hour because he cannot see anything, whites slightly inflamed, mucus runs in torrents from nose.” Ran-b. is a painful remedy, affecting nerves, muscles, eyes, serous membranes, chest, skin, fingers toes and left side. Its most characteristic effects are upon the chest walls like pleurodynia. Hydrothorax. Fauces painful as if sore during an inspiration, less during deglutition. Hay fever. Pains are stitching, stabbing, shooting, extort tears with shuddering, cannot rest in any position. Burning, biting, bruised soreness or as of deep ulceration. Sore, spots. Burning in small spots from sedentary living. Neuralgia. Herpes. Bad effects of alcohol, including hiccough, epileptiform attacks, and delirium tremens. Spasmodic hiccough. Epilepsy of alcoholics. Weak and tottering patients, from the prolonged use of whisky, brandy or other alcoholic stimulants. Sudden weakness and fainting. Trembling from anger. Distended feeling. Shocks throughout the whole body. Sensitive to air and touch. As of a cold wet cloth, especially on chest, worse on going into cold air. Caustic and pain producing properties. Ran-b. forms a constituent of some arsenical plasters used to disperse cancers. M. Jousset noted it for chronic sciatica, he applied the tincture to the heel of affected leg. MIND-Quarrelsome, angry mood. Irritability, with pains. Anxious. Worse thinking of complaints. Restlessness at night. Obtuse intellect. Vanishing of thoughts on reflection. Stares at one point. Cowardice. Weeping in evening. Depression of spirit and desire to die. Great fear of ghosts in evening, dares not be alone. Ailments from fright, vexation or anger. Delirium tremens, with hiccough. Delirium tremens, with talkative mania, unusual exertions and powerful efforts to escape from bed. Bad mental effects of alcohol.

Head - Irritable with pains in forehead and eyeballs. Aching in forehead and vertex as if pressed asunder with nausea and sleepiness. Pressing pain in forehead from within outward. As if too large and distended. Creeping sensation in scalp.

Eyes - Herpes vesicles on cornea with intense pain, photophobia and lachrymation. Eyeballs sore on moving them. Hemiopia during pregnancy. Day-blindness, mist before eyes, pressure and smarting in eyes, as from smoke. Night-blindness. Lids burn. Pain over right eye, better standing and walking.

Ears - Shootings in ears, especially in evening. Cramp-like sensation in and on ears.

Nose - Crawling and tingling in nostrils^ in posterior sinuses. Tries to relieve it by hawking and blowing the nose. Sensations - Confusion of head as if intoxicated. As if head would be enlarged. As if head pressed asunder. Hypochondria in lowest ribs painful as if bruised. Burning in left side of chest in region of short ribs. As if a full breath could not be drawn. As of a knife thrust through side and into back. As if something tearing in chest. As if cold wet cloths applied.

Mouth - Increased saliva. Butter tastes too sweet. Crawling on palate, wants to scratch it. Cramp, spasms of lips.

Throat - Inflammatory burning pains. Scraping, burning down the throat. Accumulation of much tough mucus in throat. Spasmodic sensation of something which ascends esophagus and passes into throat. COMMENTS - Pains in nerves, serous membranes, muscles, tendons, joints, eyes and internal organs. The pains are lancinating, pressing and outpressing, jerking and sticking, as if bruised with external sensitiveness. Pains are sharp, stitching, shooting, come in paroxysms. Pains are induced by atmospheric changes, sudden exposure to cold or heat, worse in wet, stormy weather, from touch, motion or turning the body. General sensitiveness to cold air and change. “Worse during inspiration.” Sensitiveness to touch with a sore, bruised sensation, soreness of parts affected. Pains particularly in the chest. Muscular pains about the margins of shoulder blades in women of sedentary employment. H. C. Allen noted burning pains in small spots from close work. “Jerks and shocks and sudden tearings in right forearm and between thumb and index finger while writing.” Writer’s cramp and professional neuroses. “Pressure and smarting in eyeballs.” Day-or night-blindness. Herpes. Spinal neuralgia. White-coated tongue. Bitter, sour or sweetish taste with accumulation of saliva. Scraping, burning in throat. Spasmodic hiccough, spasmodic feeling in esophagus and pharynx, ascending. Painful indigestion. Belchings, nausea. Pressure on sternum with labored breathing. Violent burning in cardiac end of stomach, hunger early in morning, thirst in evening. Pains in liver and spleen region, worse by touch. In pleurisy, pleurodynia intercostal neuralgia. Hering mentioned “hemeralopia” as having been cured with Ran-b. in a woman during pregnancy and in her three-year old son. The word “hemeralopia” has been used to denote both day-blindness and nightblindness. Hering used it in the latter (rarer) sense, for he says of the woman, she “can see well during the day.” The concomitant symptoms were “heat, biting and pressure in eyes, redness of conjunctiva and lids, especially inner surface of lower lids, lachrymation, pus in canthi, pustules on eyes. Eyes look weak, pupils dilated, candlelight appears as a bright circle, can see well during day.” In a child who was cured of ague with subsequent dropsy and hydrocele by applying Ran-b. to the wrist, ulcers of the fingers penetrating down to the flexor tendons were produced. The “cold-water feeling” occurred in a patient of Burnett’s. A woman, 30, had a fall two years before Burnett saw her and ever since had the peculiar sensation that whenever she goes out of doors she feels as if wet cloths were applied to three different parts of the anterior walls of thorax-both infra-clavicular fossae and under left breast. Never felt indoors, but constant as long as she is out. Guided by this symptom, “Unusual chilliness of outer parts of chest when walking in open air, with the worse in open air and worse walking in open air,” Burnett gave Ran-b. In two days, the patient was better; in three weeks, the sensation had completely gone and the general health very much improved. Dudgeon reported the case of a woman, 27, who went for a drive three weeks after confinement. The day was cold and an accident occurred to the carriage which frightened her. In the evening she had a slight rigor and complained of pain in her left side about sixth and seventh ribs. Worse slightest movement, better sitting rather bent forward and leaning a little to the left. Pulse 120, no heat of skin. No signs of lung or pleural involvement. Bry., and later Arn., gave no relief and for two days the symptoms grew worse. The patient had to be propped up with pillows, leaning forward and to the left. Her head rested on her breast, not daring to breathe at all deeply. Ran-b. 1c relieved her in ten minutes, when she “felt a wrench in her side and the pain was gone.” She was able to lie down, slept all night and made a rapid recovery. There were some slight returns of pain, now on one side, now on the other. But Ran-b. soon removed them. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Bry., Camph., Puls., Rhus-v. Compare: (1) Rad-a. - pain in lumbar muscles and joints by bending and turning body. (2) Rad-g. (3) Rad-r. - crawling sensation in forehead and scalp in evening in bed. (4) Rad-fl. (5) Bry., Crot-t., Mez., Euph. Incompatible: Sulph., Staph., Nit-s-d., alcohol, wine, vinegar. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Pains in stomach. Pressure on scrobiculus. Frequent risings. Nausea in afternoon or evening, sometimes with headache. Spasmodic hiccoughs of alcoholics.

Abdomen - Hypochondria bruised. Tenderness of abdomen to pressure. Pinching colic, alternating with chest pains.

Female - Acrid and gnawing leucorrhea. Ovarian neuralgia always excited by atmospheric changes. Food - Thirst augmented in afternoon. Feeling of hunger and rumbling in stomach early in morning. Butter tastes too sweet. Bitter, empyreumatic taste while eating or after having eaten dry food.

Chest - Various kinds of pains and soreness, as if bruised in sternum, ribs intercostal spaces and both hypochondria. Intercostal rheumatism. Rheumatic pain in chest. Sharp, cutting, stitching in chest, bilateral. Stitches in chest, worse when inspiring, moving. Small sore spot as from subcutaneous ulceration in chest. Herpes zoster. Pleurodynia. Pleurisy, adhesions after intercostal neuralgia. Chilliness in chest when walking in open air.

Back - Muscular pain along lower margin of the shoulder blade. Pain extending through lowerhalfof left chest. Burning in small spots from needlework, type writing, piano playing. Scapula adherent. Muscles of neck rigidly contracted, can speak only by moving shoulders up and down. Causations - Bad effects of alcohol injury, fright, vexation. Cold air brings on all sorts of ailments.

Limbs - Crawling and tingling in fingers. Itching palms. Sudden jerking, stitching pain in forearm (right) while writing. Pain in heels as if pinched by boots.

Skin - Herpetic eruptions with great itching. Vesicular and pustular eruptions. Shingles, bluish vesicles. Burning and intense itching, worse contact. Flat, burning, stinging ulcers. Pemphigus. Blister-like eruption in palms, itching. Fingertips and palms chapped. Horny scabs. Hard excrescences. Corns, smart or burn worse touch.

Modalities - Better from standing, sitting bent forward. Worse from open air, drafts, change of temperature, atmospheric changes. Worse damp, cold, rainy and stormy weather. Worse from change of position, motion of arms, standing, breathing, touch. Worse evening and morning. Worse after eating, alcohol. Worse from fright, vexation, anger.

Liver - laundice with itching of body, especially palms. Lungs - Anxious, oppressed breathing with desire to draw deep breath. Dyspnea from anger.

Temperature - Chilliness, worse open air. Shivering in evening with heat in face. Heat in head with coldness in hands.

It promotes digestion when eaten in moderation. In a woman who applied the plant to herwrist, itproducedgangreneofthearmdown to the tendons and bone. Ulceration. REFERENCES Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - ran-fi. Ranunculus ficaria. Lesser celandine. Pilewort. Ficaria ranunculoi- des. Ficaria venia. Scrophularia minor. N. O. Ranunculacee. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Hemorrhoids.

HERBAL - The “lessercelandine” is not botanically related to the true celandine, Chelidonium majus, or to the Figwort tribe (Scrophularia) although it is named Scrophularia minor in old books. Ran-fi. is in all respects a true crowfoot except that it has three deciduous instead of five persistent sepals and nine petals instead of five. Gerarde noted that “It growth in meadows, by ditches and trenches and it is common everywhere in moist and dark places. It comes forth about the Calends of March and flower a little after: it beginneth to fade away in April, it is quite gone in May afterwards it is hard to be found, yea scarcely the root.” Gerarde wrote that the idea of its use in hemorrhoids was derived from the cluster of small tubers growing around the crown of the root, which bear a striking resemblance to a bunch of hemorrhoids. REFERENCES Clarke.

Right-sided early morning headache, better by rising. General copious night-sweat, especially abundant on thighs. Coldness of thighs. REFERENCES - Clarke.

CLINICAL - Back, pulsation. Coma. Eyes, disorders. Feet, weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ran-r. has furrowed flower-stalks like Ran-b., but it has a spreading calyx and creeping scions. Franz reported a number of symptoms experienced from preparing the juice of this plant, including phantasmagoria. Jahr quoted an account of the effects of eating Ran-r. observed in a flock of sheep. Several fell down as if struck by lightning, eyes rolled, breathing hurried. Some reeled and died with heads bent towards left groin. Great weakness in feet remained behind. Sleep, short butrefreshing. Mucus membranes of eyes injected, mouth dry. Abdomen slightly distended, ruminations ceased. Bleeding worse. Some raised themselves, reeled, fell down again, bleated piteously, most were in profound coma. Ether in milk gave much relief. REFERENCES - Clarke.

CLINICAL - Aneurysm. Anus, itching. Blisters. Chest, sternum, pain behind. Coms. Coryza. Diphtheria. Earache. Glossitis. Gout. Hemorrhoids. Herpes, zoster. Liver, pain. Neuralgia. Nose, ulceration. Pemphigus. Quinsy. Sternum, pains. Stomatitis. Toes disorders. Tongue, peeling, mapped. Varicose veins.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ran-s. has the most acridity of all the Ranunculi, causing burning in mouth, throat, stomach, chest, urethra and other parts. It causes blisters on the skin which leave a raw surface with acrid discharge. The effects of Ran-s., which German shepherds call “cold fire,” on horned cattle is loss of appetite, trembling and shivering, and distention of abdominal veins. A dog poisoned with it became anxious, howled, tossed about, bent double, and was very restless at night. Affinities for the chest, skin, vertex and right side. Rawness, burning, smarting, gnawing or boring pains. Overall sore feeling. Convulsive twitchings. Periodical complaints. Shortness of breath. Fainting with pain in stomach. Burning in the mouth, throat, stomach, chest, urethra. Sensation as of a plug. Characteristic “mapped or peeled tongue,” with smarting, burning and rawness. Pemphigus. Ran-s. cured pemphigus in a three-months old infant with continual thirst, weak intermitting pulse, trembling with anxious features. After Ars. 4c had caused improvement, Ran-s. 3c healed up the resulting ulcers. MIND - Indolence and aversion to mental work. Sadness and melancholy in the evening.

Head - Fluent coryza with sneezing and burning urination. Gnawing pain in small spot on vertex or either temples. Biting, itching on the scalp. Frightful dreams about corpses, serpents, battles, etc.

Nose - Fluent coryza, with sneezing, with burning urination.

Mouth - Burning and rawness of tongue. Tongue cracks and peels off, denuded patches. Tongue mapped. Mouth sore and raw. Teeth and gums sensitive. Blunt teeth with toothache.

Throat - Burning scraping in throat. COMMENTS - External sensitiveness, especially of chest and sternum. Chest disorders, including aneurysm. Arrest of breathing. Pains in liver, spleen, chest or heart, worse on deep inspiration and associated with external soreness. Most of the symptoms are right-sided, but there is one left-side symptom that is peculiar: continual gnawing in left palm. The right toes, especially the right big toe, are the seat of many acute pains, giving the remedy a high place in acute attacks of gout and painful corns. Mahoney cured with Ran-s. 3c an aged woman subject to gout aching in dorsum of feet, especially the right, with wakefulness at night. Kali-c. 30c had previously removed pain passing downward over the glutei. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Puls. Wine and coffee antidote only partially. The ulcers were somewhat relieved by Peruvian Balsam. Compare: (1) Ran-b. - Ran-s. more irritative. (2) Headache, gnawing in small spot at vertex, Puls. (3) Mapped tongue, Nat-m., Ars., Rhus-t., Tarax. (4) Ran-s. has more burning and rawness than any. (5) Cobweb sensation, Am-c., Bor., Brom., Bry., Calc., Con, Graph., Mag-c. Follows well: Ars. in pemphigus. Followed well by: Lach, in diphtheria with denuded tongue. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Nausea worse after midnight. Pain with fainting.

Abdomen - Sensation of a plug behind umbilicus. Pressure as of a plug behind right false ribs, worse deep inspiration.

Chest - Integument sensitive. Bruised pain and weakness in the chest every evening. Sore burning behind xiphoid cartilage. Face - As if covered with cobwebs.

Heart - Sensation as if a plug in heart.

Limbs - Boring pain. Gnawing in knee, left palm. Gout of fingers and toes. Sudden burning, sticking pain in right toe. Sudden stitches in big toes, passing into burning. Corns with burning and soreness, especially when feet hang down.

Sleep - Dreadful dreams of dead bodies, snakes and fights.

Skin - Yellow vesicles. Bullae with acrid contents. Pemphigus.

Modalities - Pains better after midnight. Worse from motion, walking, letting limb hang down. Worse by touch, pressure, blows. Worse deep breathing, open air. Worse evening, after midnight, morning. Worse after a meal.

Liver - Pain over region of liver with sensation as if diarrhea would set in. Lungs - Stitches in chest muscles, chest and sternum are sensitive to touch. Sore burning behind sternum. As of a plug forced between ribs, worse deep breathing.

full:
PHARMACY - raph. Raphanus sativus. Black garden radish. Wildradish. Raphanus raphan- istrum. N. O. Cruciferae. Tincture of fresh root immediately before flowering in spring. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscess. Alcoholism. Amblyopia. Axilla, inflamed. Breast pains. Catalepsy. Coughs. Diarrhea. Emaciation. Esophagus. Faintness. Fevers. Flatulence. Flushings. Gas, pains. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Heel, pain. Hernia. Hysteria. Insomnia. Intoxication. Lienteria. Liver, affections. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Myopia. Nosebleeds. Nymphomania. Palpitation. Pemphigus. Seborrhea. Tonsillitis. Toothache. Tympanitis. Vomiting. Yawning.

HOMEOPATHIC - Nusser proved both the garden radish and the wild radish (the former probably only a cultivated variety of the latter). He took tinctures of the long, round and black (the favorite in Germany) varieties of garden radish, and ate the different radishes themselves. Raph. affords a marked example of a common article of diet being at the same time a poison and a medicine. The symptoms are from effects of eating radishes and provings by Curie made on a woman with 15c and 30c dilutions. The symptoms will not appear if salt is used with the Radish. Cooper wrote “A man, has these symptoms whenever he eats even a single radish: “Burning sensation in epigastrium, followed by hot belchings, lasting a whole day and ending in a headache.” Turnips (Brassica rapa) produce in him a similar effect, but in less degree. Raph. produces in provers hysterical, mental and uterine symptoms. Numbness, changing places. Coldness of one foot. Can only lie on back. Seborrhea with greasy skin. Pemphigus. Stopped sensation in ears. Teeth feel as if made of paper. Produces pain and stitches in liver and spleen. Increases of bile and salivary secretion. Globus, as of hot ball from uterus goes up to the throat. Appetite without hunger 4 a.m. in bed. Drinks more than one urinates. Urine thick like milk. Great accumulation and incarceration of flatulence. Retained flatulence, cannot be passed up and down. Post- operative gas pains. Loss of vision and hearing just before vomiting. Vomiting of fecal matter. Hysteria, chilliness in back and arms. Epilepsy, reflex from removal of an adherent prepuce, the healing being delayed by furious priapism. Sexual insomnia. (Kali-br.) Nymphomania. The leaves of Raph. are said to antidote its roots, and the arum root is said to antidote the effects of radish leaves. MIND - Forgetful during menses. Hysteria during first day of menses. Brain excitement. Extreme anxiety with feeling of impending death. Fear of becoming a burden. Anguish with fear of death, which is supposed to be near. Capricious, stupefaction, sadness, tears. Hopefulness alternating with sadness. Weeping on waking. Sadness with aversion to children. Aversion to her own sex and children especially girls. Dread of men. Nymphomania. Sexual insomnia. Delusion she has an unrecognized disease. Fancies herself talking. Delusion of being in different places. Sense of intoxication. Alcoholism.

Head - Headache, brain feels tender and sore. Headache after dinner. Severe headache in temple, eyes and root of nose. Aching above root of nose. Dull pain in occiput, better by throwing head back. Gnawing in occiput followed by numbness. Sharp pains in vertex. Tightness in skin of vertex. Sweat on head after rising.

Eyes - Eyes filled with blood, sight lost. Edema of lower eyelids. When she turns her eyes in the direction of the ear she feels a pain in the ear, temple and parietal bone.

Ears - Tearings and shootings in left ear. Lancinations in right ear. Itching in concha of left ear, which is painful to the touch. Loss of sight and hearing just before vomiting.

Nose - Nose pointed. Dull pain in root of nose extending to occiput. Pressure, as from a weight, on back of nose. Breath feels burning hot in nose. Stoppage of nose. Mucus in posterior sinuses. Frequent sneezing or at least frequent want to sneeze. Nosebleed of deep red blood. Smell of horseradish.

Face - Face, red, somber. Cheeks burn, are red, whole head and face red. Face disfigured.

Throat - Hot-ball feeling from uterus to throat, stopping there. Heat and burning in throat. Vertigo - Vertigo with loss of vision. Vertigo with dim sight in evening, head feels tightly bandaged. COMMENTS - The hysterical, mental and uterine symptoms of Curie’s prover were very well marked, including a state approaching catalepsy: “On returning a little to herself she was unable to speak or stir.” “Globus” symptoms. Sensation of a number of balls ascending from abdomen to throat. Sensation of a morsel, too large to be swallowed, sensation of something hard to digest, leaving an empty sensation with hunger. Constant, violent thirst. “Drinks more than he urinates.” “Pains more severe when he drinks liquid.” Pressure in hypogastrium as if a hernia would protrude. Flatulence. Accumulation of gas almost stops the breathing, cannot be passed either up or down. Hot, foreign body goes up like a ball from uterus and stops at the beginning of the throat. Nymphomania. Aversion to her own sex and to children, especially girls. Cough, causing jarring of head and chest, seems to come from epigastrium. Low cough to loosen phlegm. Expectoration of a large amount of tenacious white mucus from pharynx and esophagus, with sensation of stricture in throat. Pain in vertebral column as if a foreign body passed through it from top to bottom and was stopped at certain points by obstacles causing pain. Pains in the back on swallowing. On breathing, pain under breasts and in back. Heavy lump and coldness in center of chest between breasts, preventing sleep. Acute pains in coccyx, sensation as if an abscess forming. Sensation as of an abscess in liver. Throbbings in the body that became lancinations. Chilliness along the back and posterior surfaces of arms. Icy cold knees. Sensation as if she had put her cold feet into very hot water. Fever sensation, as if a cold coming on. E. T. Blake reported two cases of sexual insomnia cured with Raph., one of which shows that Raph. has an influence on the male sexual sphere analogous to that it has on the female. A young man suffering from reflex epilepsy had a generally adherent prepuce removed. Healing was delayed by furious priapism, which caused dragging at the sutures. Raph. lx given each night cured. Blake’s second case was in a woman of 40 with old pelvic troubles. Orig. had failed and Plat, had helped only slightly. Raph. cured. RELATIONS -Antidoted by: Copious draft of cold water (Milk and water worsen the pains in abdomen).

Stomach - Pains in stomach, which urge continual eating. Burning in epigastrium, followed by hot eructation. Putrid belchings. Black vomit. Vomiting of fecal matter.

Abdomen - Distended. Tympanitis, no flatus emitted upward ordownward. Griping about navel. Retching and vomiting, loss of appetite.

Rectum - Stool liquid, frothy, profuse, brown, with colic and pad-like swelling of intestines. Vomiting of fecal matter. Sensations - Sensation of stiffness. Sensation of an iron band around waist. Swelling of abdomen. Hot breath, hot belchings. Sensation of a number of balls rising from abdomen to throat. Sensation of a hot foreign body like a ball going up from uterus to throat. Numbness in hands in soles of feet and buttocks of the parts near the painful bones. Sensation of swelling of bones of hands, arms, eyes, yet feet feel small.

Female - Menses very profuse and long-lasting. Nervous irritation of genitals. Nymphomania, with aversion to her own sex and to children, and sexual insomnia.

Chest - Pain in chest extends to back and throat. Heavy lump and coldness in center of chest.

Back - Weak back. Burning, itching on the back. Acute pains in coccyx, as if an abscess forming. Cracking in nape of neck. Numbness of muscles of neck near left ear, coldness in left eye.

Limbs - Weakness and bruised feeling in limbs. Trembling of limbs. Sticking pains in left shoulder. Gland in right armpit, swollen and tender to touch. Numbness of soles and buttocks. Cramp in calf, at night in bed.

Sleep - Nervous yawning. Inclination to sleep. Sleep with dreamy reveries, lascivious dreams.

Skin - Skin greasy. Painless pemphigus. Itching and heat of skin, fever, pimples under skin. Itching of whole body, scratching causes burning.

Modalities - Better walking in open air. Throwing back head ameliorates pain in occiput. Worse at night, morning on wak- ing, 3 a.m. to 4 a.m. Worse eating or drinking. Worse from touch, jarring. Motion aggravates pain in belly. Laughing causes a cough. Cough causes painful shock in brain, efforts to vomit, pain in chest. Riding in carriage causes pain in heart. Pain in heart worse after breakfast.

Compare - (1) Mom-b. - Worse near splenic flexure. (2) Carb-v, Anae., Arg- n.. Brass. Follows well: Lyc., Coch., Brass., Cheir., Thlaspi., Matth., Sin a. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Kidneys - Urine scanty or else more in quantity than the drink swallowed. Urine more copious, thick like milk. Turbid urine with yeast-like sediment. Pale urine of a dirty yellow.

author: Murphy

Worse from anxiety, uneasiness of mind, at night. Worse exertion, touch, sitting bent over, stooping, straining at stool. Eating aggravates, better emission of flatus..

Hemoptysis. Hiccoughs. Hydrothorax. Itching. Metrorrhagia. Miscarriage. Metrorrhagia. Nipples, fissures. Nosebleed. Pimples. Pinworms. Pleurisy. Pterygium. Scurvy. Snoring. Speech, arrested.
