full:
PHARMACY - rat. Ratanhia peruviana. Rhatany root. Mapato. Krameria triandra. Pu- macuchu. N. O. Polygalacee or Leguminosae according to some. Tincture of the dried root Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies. Locally, the Cerate has proved invaluable in many rectal complaints.

CLINICAL - Anus, fissures. Breast, fissures. Breast pain. Breath offensive. Constipation. Diabetes. Dysentery. Dyspepsia, atonic. Fissures. Gonorrhea. Hemoptysis. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Hemoptysis. Hiccoughs. Hydrothorax. Itching. Metrorrhagia. Miscarriage. Metrorrhagia. Nipples, fissures. Nosebleed. Pimples. Pinworms. Pleurisy. Pterygium. Scurvy. Snoring. Speech, arrested. Stomach, disorders. Throat, contraction. Tinnitus. Worms.

HERBAL - Ratanhia is remarkable for its entire, ovate, acuminate leaves, covered on both sides with silky hair; it is one of the species most known as yielding the Rhatany root of commerce. All the species Ratanhia peruviana of Krameria, as far as known, are intensely astringent. The root of several species of Krameria, especially Krameria triandra, is used to make the remedy. The Treasury of Botany noted that the infusion of the root is blood-red, and has a history of being used to adulterate port wine. The infusion has been used as a gargle and wash, and the powder, mixed with charcoal, forms an excellent tooth-powder. In Peru, an extract is made that is a mild, easily assimilated astringent medicine, useful for passive, bloody or mucus discharges. As a tonic, it is used for the weakness of digestive organs and muscular debility, and restores tone to relaxed parts. Ratanhia is useful for delicate and nervous women, and to prevent miscarriage in those with a history of it. Can arrest passive hemorrhages. Styptic action, astringent. Used in intermittent and putrid fevers.

HOMEOPATHIC - Teste put Rat. in his Sulph. group. He wrote, of its pre-homeo- pathic use, “There is perhaps no plant the properties of which have been so well indicated by chance as this.” Anal and rectal symptoms have received a great deal of clinical confirmation. Pinworms. Various forms of incontinence of urine. Mucus discharges, such as chronic catarrh of the bronchia, vagina, large intestines, etc. Violent hiccoughs. Hemorrhages, passive. Nosebleed, hemoptysis and metrorrhagia. Cracks, fissures. Cracked nipples (Graph., Sil.). Chronic edema of the skin. Scurvy. Pterygium. Weakness and prostration with anxiety and sweat over whole body. Pains are here and there. Shooting pains, as from excoriation. Jerking in different parts. Sense of constriction. Dark thin scrawny persons. MIND - Irritable, peevish and quarrelsome humor. Changeable mind. Depression when alone, better in company. Desire for company. Fear something will happen when alone, better conversation. Anxiety at night on waking. Starting from sleep. Desire to die during pains.

Head - Bursting headache when straining at stool or after stools. Bursting in head when sitting with head bent forward. Pain in middle of forehead, as if brain would fall out, while straining at stool. Long-lasting headache, as if screwed in a vice. Dullness of head, as if intoxicated. Sensation as if scalp from nose to vertex were stretched. Itching of scalp, not better by scratching.

Eyes - Pains in eyes as if compressed in a vice and could not be moved. Inflammation of sclera. Contractions and burning sensations in eyes, especially in evening. Agglutination of eyes at night and lachrymation in morning. Jerks and quivering of eyes and eyelids. Very rapid twitching of eyelids. Stiffness of upper lids with soreness of upper tarsal edges. Pterygium. White spot before eye, which obstructs the sight with constant urging to wipe the eyes. Vision dim for distant objects. Myopia.

Ears - Tearing, itching and shooting in ears. Violent stitch in right ear. Crawling as if insect in right ear. Chirping in right ear. Nocturnal tinkling and ringing in ears.

Nose - Itching in nose. Violent itching on tip of nose, better by rubbing. Nostrils inflamed and scabby with burning sensations. Dryness of nose with frequent sneezing. Dry coryza with complete stoppage of nose. Violent nosebleed, three times a day, for five days in succession.

Face - Heat in face. Burning vesicles on the red part of upper lip. Tearing pain in face and jawbones. Violent tearing in left malar bone, evenings. Tearing in left side of lower jaw and corresponding teeth. Tearing in inner surface of lips in a small spot. Sensation of cobwebs above right side of mouth.

Mouth - Offensive breath. Dryness of mouth at night. Tasteless water collects in mouth. Acid blood from gums on sucking them. Tension and burning sensation at tip of tongue. As if cool air came from teeth. As of a cobweb about the right side of the mouth.

Throat - Sore throat, generally felt during empty swallowing. Painful spasmodic contraction in throat, which stops the voice. Unable to speak a loud word. COMMENTS - Teste quoted from Trousseau and Pidoux a case in which Bretonneau cured a fissure of the rectum. In the case, a woman suffered from constipation and fissure of the rectum that caused her horrible pains and had damaged her health. Bretonneau ordered a daily injection mixed with one-fourth of Rat. and in a short time the constipation and fissure were cured. Other similar cases were also cured and the treatment was shown to be successful in cases of fissure without constipation. One patient of fissure, cured by Rat., was better by an application of hot water, he sat in a sitz- bath as hot as he could endure, the relief only lasted while in the bath. The provings of Hartlaub and Trinks bring out the keynotes of Rat. in rectal cases: “straining, stool so hard she cried out with great protrusion of hemorrhoids, followed for a long time by burning in anus.” Burning in the anus, persists for a long time after the stool and it occurs when the stool is diarrhea as well as hard. Burning also precedes and accompanies the stool. Dry heat with sudden stitching, like knife-stabs. Oozing at anus. Dropping of blood from anus. Anal fissures (Graph., Nit-ac„ Sil.). The anus and rectum feel as if they’re sitting on glass. Hemorrhoids with severe bleeding and burning pains. Worms with severe itching. Bursting headache that accompanies and follows a straining at stool. “Pains in middle of forehead, as if brain would fall out,” and a similar pain after stool. Head pains are worse on bending forward. Violent nosebleed. Burning, smarting of the eyes. Obscured vision. Inflammation of the whole eye, a membrane seemed to extend to central point of eye, which burned. Pterygium. Twitching of lids. Bleeding gums, toothache, worse lying down. Aching molars with a sensation as if coldness rushed out of them. Toothache during pregnancy, compelling the patient to get up at night and walk about. Tasteless water collects in mouth. Contractive sensations in stomach, groin, anus, eyes, neck, muscles, throat, “painful spasmodic contraction of throat during which she could not speak a loud word.” Causes and prevents miscarriage, metrorrhagia and leucorrhea. Fissure of the breasts or nipples in nursing women. Dr. Toumel, who, no doubt, did not suspect that Ratan. produced abortion, had the idea of prescribing it as a tonic in cases of incipient miscarriage and thus preventing that accident in delicate and nervous females who had never yet been able to go their full time. Rummel related the case of a servant girl who had rapid twitching of the lids of right eye to such an extent as to hinder her seeing. There seemed to be also a rotary motion of the ball. Bell, and Calc, failed to relieve. Rat. 12c relieved quickly. Cushing, who made a proving of Rat., said it caused great itching in the rectum and he has cured with it since nearly every case of pin-worms in his practice. Cushing considered that, next to Sang-n., Rat. meets more rectal cases than any other remedy. In an old and feeble woman, he cured with Rat. 3x internally and a Rhatany rectal suppository each night. There were frequent discharges of mucus, blood and pus from the bowels night and day with great pain and burning in rectum almost wholly preventing sleep. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Pleurisy, Seneg. (2) Fissureof anus, Nit-ac. (3) Anal symptoms, Sulph., Iris-v., Canth., Peon. (4) Graph, is similar, but has not the constriction of Rat. (5) Splinters of glass in rectum, Thuj. (Sticks, Aesc.). (6) Pain in head from straining at stool Ind., Puls., Sil. (7) Hiccough, Cycl. (8) Burning on tongue, Raph., Ran-s., Sang. (9) Toothache ofpregnancy,Raph.,Mag-c.,Cham. (10) Alive sensation, Croc., Thuj. (11)Cobweb sensation, Ran-s., Bar-c. Follows well: Sulph., Bov., Sep. in uterine affections (Teste). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Stomach feels too full. Sudden painful bursting in pit of stomach. Pains as from ulceration in stomach. Heat and burning sensation in stomach. Cutting like knives or griping pain better belching. Empty belching with taste of food. Violent hiccough, which causes pain in stomach. Long-continued hiccough after dinner. Nausea and disgust with retching and vomiting of food, worse in open air. Vomiting of water, of mucus streaked with blood.

Abdomen - Griping in lower abdomen, externally violent itching. Heat and burning sensation in epigastrium. Repeated violent sticking in hypochondrium. Pinch- ings in abdomen and sides of abdomen, sometimes with a burning sensation. Pullings and a sensation of coldness in umbilical region. As if abdomen had been cut to pieces, worse deep breathing. Movements in sides of abdomen as of something alive.

Rectum - Constriction or as of sharp splinters of broken glass in rectum. Dry heat at anus with sudden knife- like stitches. Fissure of anus with great constriction, burning like a fire. Hemorrhoids burn like fire, temporarily relieved by cold water, protrude with straining. Stool is forced with great straining and followed by prolonged aching and burning, better hot water. Fetid, thin diarrhea, stools burn, burning pains before and after stools. Discharge of blood from rectum with or without stools. Oozing at anus. Dry, itching anus. Pinworms (Sant., Teucr., Cina.). Ascarides. Sensations - As if intoxicated. As if head in a vice. As of a white speck before eyes, skin before eyes. Eyelids feel stiff. As if coldness rushed out of molars. As of Ratanhia peruviana cobwebs about right side of mouth. As if abdomen or chest cut to pieces. Movement as if something alive in abdomen. As if rectum and anus were all twisted up. As if splinters of glass in rectum and anus. As if rectum protruded and then suddenly went back with a jerk. Jerkings and quivering. Right side is most affected.

Male - Chronic gonorrhea. Burning in root of penis while urinating. Itching in scrotum, not better by scratching.

Female - Menses suppressed with swelling of abdomen and breasts, simulating a pregnancy of several months with profuse leucorrhea and kidney pain. Menses delayed. Menses too early and of too long duration and too copious, with pains in abdomen and loins. Metrorrhagia. Pressure in groin, as of a general bearing- down pain towards genital organs, followed by leucorrhea. Leucorrhea with itching in rectum and discharge of bloody mucus. Miscarriage. Compelled to get up at night and walk about during pregnancy, with toothache. Food - Thirst in evening. Constant desire to eat. Anorexia with dislike of food and drink.

Chest - Painful constriction in both sides of chest. Sticking, burning, cutting pains. Burning stitch in last ribs near back, on stepping. Rush of blood and heat to chest with difficult breathing. Violent pressure in chest as from a stone, with short breath on slight exertion. Ulcerative pain in chest during and after coughing.

Heart - Sharp sticking in precordial region, rather external. Full pulse.

Back - Tearing in nape of neck with heaviness of head. Stiffness in nape on turning head, better on violent motion. Drawing tension from nape of neck to the bottom of spine. Bruised pain in whole spine. Bruised pain in loins and hips, morning rising, better on motion. Breasts - Fissure of the breasts. Cracks in nipples in nursing women.

Limbs - Tearing in limbs. Tearing in shoulder, arms, forearms and wrists. Contraction of flexor muscles. Spasmodic and painful contractions in elbows and fingers. Pain in bend of elbow when flexed, better extended. Jerking, tearing and stitches in thumbs. Drawing and tearing in thighs, knees, legs, feet and toes. Tension and burning sensation in thighs. Tearing from left Achilles tendon, up the leg. Sticking and burning tearing in left big toe. Tickling on heels on soles. Voluptuous itching in left sole. Lungs - Malaise with frequent yawning, repeated and labored attempts to draw a long breath and distressing constriction across chest. Dry cough with tickling in larynx and pain of ulceration in chest. Some tight mucus evacuated with great difficulty.

Sleep - Disposition to sleep, especially after dinner. Violent yawning. Retarded sleep. Snoring. Frequent waking and prolonged wakefulness. Waking with a start, with trembling inquietude and fear. Dreams of battles, sick people, quarrels, anger, vexation, funerals, death of friends, and earthquakes.

Skin - Sickly looking skin. Small red and white pimples that do not suppurate, especially between shoulders and on loins. Pimples, itching and burning after scratching. Formication and itching eruption on back. Itching in nape and between scapula, on scrotum, front of thigh, bends of knees.

Modalities - Better from hot water applications, hot bath, cool bathing. Better walking in open air, exercise. Pressure ameliorates pain in chest. Worse from anxiety, uneasiness of mind, at night. Worse exertion, touch, sitting bent over, stooping, straining at stool. Eating aggravates, better emission of flatus.

Teeth - Toothache in evening, especially after lying down, compelling one to rise and walk about. Toothache with tearing or jerking. Digging pains. Pulsative pain in teeth. Bleeding of teeth. Painful sensation of coldness and elongation in the molars and as if coldness rushed out of them. Violent pain in incisors, painful to the touch.

Kidneys - Frequent and urgent want to urinate with scanty emission. More frequent and more abundant emission of urine, even at night. Pale urine. Urine more scanty, deposits a cloud and becomes turbid. Burning in urethra and root of penis when urinating.

Temperature - Predominance of coldness and shivering, especially in evening. General chill 8 or 9 p.m. Chilly even in warm room. Heat of whole head with heaviness. Heat and puffiness of face. Dry heat in anus with cuttings. Nocturnal perspiration. Wakes 1 a.m. with sweat, thirst and dry mouth.

full:
PHARMACY - rauw. Rauwolfia serpentina. N. O. Apocynaceae family. Java and India. Containing, among others, the alkaloid reserpine. The tincture is prepared from the root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Addison’s disease. Angina pectoris. Basedow’s disease. Colitis. Dystonia. Hypotension. Pancreatitis. Parkinson’s disease. Thyroid, disorders. Vasomotor complaints.

HERBAL - Rauwolfia serpentina, found in Java and India, belongs to the Apocynaceae family. A very old drug in Ayurvedic medicine, the roots and rhizomes contain hypotensive and neuro-depressive alkaloids. In 1952, the Russian chemist Muller isolated the specialized reserpine under the name of “serpasil.” Most of the alkaloids are built on the base of reserpine, a harmonic group linked with a second isoquinoleic group.

HOMEOPATHIC - The homeopathic proving was conducted in 1954 by Leeser and Schrenk at the Robert Bosch Hospital in Stuttgart. The proving was carried out on twenty-four doctors, using the lx and 3x potencies, for a period of fourteen to twenty-eight days. W. Lee Templeton also conducted a proving at the Faculty of Homeopathy in London in 1954-55 on six provers, using the 3x, 6x, 12c, and 30c potencies, depending on the subject, for a period of six months. Beja of Orléans began a self-proving in July-August 1956 using the 3x potency, for one month, at the rate of 10 drops four times a day. Finally, Julian undertook detailed clinical studies to determine the range of action of Rauw. in a homeopathic potency. Rauw. has a general and cerebral hypotonia. Lack of tone in the nerves and circulatory system. Congestive vascular condition. Pallor, alternating with redness and hot flushes. Insomnia after midnight. Chronic allergic condition progressing to cancer. Chronic neurotic conditions with development of arthrosis or depression. Rapid, widespread trembling. General stiffness. Heaviness in the legs. Libido disorders. Dripping after urination. MIND - Uneasiness with irritability and apprehension. Aversion to company, better when alone. Abrupt. Face expressionless and he avoids any effort. Dullness from alcohol. Diminution of the memory and powers of concentration. Phases of increased ability to work and well being, alternating with phases of fatigue and exhaustion. Alternating excitability and depression. Maniacal depressive psychosis. Psychosis in elderly people. Restlessness at night in bed. Neurosis from anguish. Psychological complaints during the menopause. Melancholic conditions. Hyper-emotiveness. Unstable personality. Delusions, everything seems unreal. Sudden impulse to kill.

Head - Congestive headache with arterial palpitations in the temples and forehead. Frontal headache, spreading towards the occiput, ameliorated in fresh air, accompanied by hot flushes, dizziness.

Nose - Dryness of the nasal mucus membranes. Nosebleed with ulcerations on the nasal wall. Sinusitis. Spasmodic rhinitis.

Face - Congestion of the face and possible nosebleed. Neuralgia of the upper maxilla, ameliorated by heat. Numbness sensation in the right half of the face, followed by shooting pains.

Mouth - Excessive salivation. Impression of a rotten taste in the mouth.

Throat - Dryness of mucus membranes of the nose and throat. Tickling in the throat with need to cough, aggravated by lying down. Laryngitis. Vertigo - Vertigo and precordial heaviness, cramping pains spreading towards the neck, discomforts, tendency to faintness with sticky sweating from the hands and feet. Amelioration from movement in the open air. RELATIONS-Compare: (l)Lach. -Circulatory dystonia with localized congestion, amelioration by discharges, occurring predominantly on the left side. (2) Phos. - Agitation with uneasiness, worse at dusk, vertigo on waking, burning sensation at the hands and between the shoulders. (3) Ars. - Anxious, especially between 1 a.m.and3a.m.,edema of the lower eyelids, thirst for small quantities of iced water, diarrhea with vomiting, physical and mental agitation. (4) Nux-v. - Nervous irritability. Sleepy after meals, ameliorated by a short nap. Heaviness in the stomach, constipation and hemorrhoids. (5) Aur. - Congestions, disgust for life, obsession with suicide, palpitations. Pains in the bones and right testicle, worse at night and from contact. REFERENCES - Julian.

Stomach - Excessive hydrochloric gastritis. Alcoholic gastritis.

Abdomen - Abdominal plethora and dropsy. Chronic pancreatitis. Feeling of gastric and abdominal repletion. Heartburn, nausea, malodorous flatulence. Aerophagy, air in the colon. Colitis from fermentation, enterocolitis.

Rectum - Morning attacks of colic with evil-smelling black diarrhea-type stools. Sudden urging, followed by pallor of the face with sweating, thirst and faintness. Anal fissure. Congestive hemorrhoids, bleeding at times.

Male - Clear diminution in libido, sometimes with a temporary phase of excitement. Impotence. Sterility. Prostatitis.

Female - Heaviness in the small pelvis with frequent need to urinate. Amenorrhea. Menses too early, accompanied by cramping pains. Too frequent menses. Endometriosis. Fibroma. Menopausal complaints. Frigidity.

Chest - Angina pectoris. Constitutions - Carbo-phosphoric types with nervous or sanguine temperament.

Heart - Hypotonia with diarrhea. Constriction, angina pectoris and rhythmic anomalies. Bradycardia, aortitis. Aortic aneurysm. Palpitations, prickling and irregular heartbeat. Palpitations and irregularity of the heart when lying down, ameliorated by standing and walking. Cardio-renal edema.

Limbs - Chronic rheumatism. General stiffness and pain in all the limbs. Legs heavy, black and blue, as if shattered. Joint pains in the left hip and big toes, which are hot and swollen. Arthrosis of the knee. Painful flat feet in adolescents. Gout. Soft edema, puckered, located in the malleolar region, at times connected to a generalized edematous infiltration including the upper limbs and the face.

Sleep - Insomnia. Slow in going to sleep and stays awake for hours after midnight. Erotic dreams. Dreams of wasps, drowning, death, dying.

Skin - Clammy, odorous sweating from the axilla, hands and feet. Dyshidrosis. Lymphaedema. Elephantiasis- type edematous dystrophy. Sweating. Fissures. Cracks. Ulceration of the heel.

Modalities - Better in the open air, fresh air. Better from violent exercise, prolonged movement, strong pressure. Better from the emission of gas or stools. Worse from heat, confined air. Worse on waking, after meals, from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m.

Liver - Cirrhosis of the liver. Pigmentary cirrhosis or glandular pigmentation or hypertrophic pigmentary cirrhosis in sugar diabetes. Biliary sycosis. Lungs - Dyspnea from exertion with lack of air. Tracheal bronchitis. Fitful cough with expectoration of sticky, sometimes blood streaked, mucus.

Kidneys - Difficulty in urinating with need to squeeze to push. Dysuria. Cystitis. Urine reddish-brown. At the end of urination, a little urine is passed, drop by drop. Bedwetting from compression (fibromas, prostate).

Blood - Circulatory dystonia. Hypotension, faintness. Temporary rise and then fall in arterial tension. Vasomotor complaints. Vascular or febrile congestion.

Temperature - Sensation of heat on the whole body with or without sweating and accompanied by congestive headache and general uneasiness.

name: Red Chestnut
author: Murphy
constitution: Rd-ch-b. belongs to Bach’s group For Those who Have Fear, with Rck-r-b., Mimul-b., Cher-p-b. and Asp-b. Fear for the welfare of others. Extreme physical nervousness and anxious weakness, with tightening in the stomach and abdominal region from fear. MIND - Fearful worries about loved ones’ welfare. Nervous energy. Grief and worry. Sense of danger. Fears for life and limb. Helplessness, self-blame.

full:
PHARMACY - rd-ch-b. Red chestnut. Aes- culus carnea. The flowering clusters are boiled for half an hour. The boiled water is strained and used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.

HOMEOPATHIC - Rd-ch-b. belongs to Bach’s group For Those who Have Fear, with Rck-r-b., Mimul-b., Cher-p-b. and Asp-b. Fear for the welfare of others. Extreme physical nervousness and anxious weakness, with tightening in the stomach and abdominal region from fear. MIND - Fearful worries about loved ones’ welfare. Nervous energy. Grief and worry. Sense of danger. Fears for life and limb. Helplessness, self-blame. REFERENCES-Bach.

full:
PHARMACY - resc-b. Rescue Remedy. Rescue Remedy is made up of a combination of five Bach flower remedies. Add two drops from stock bottles of each of the five remedies listed below to a one ounce (30cc) bottle filled with brandy or alcohol. Historical dose: Add three drops of the Rescue Remedy to a glass of water. The patient should sip this frequently and as he or she grows calmer, at intervals of fifteen minutes, and then every half hour according to the progress made.

HOMEOPATHIC - Bach discovered this unique combination of five remedies which aim at restoring balance and calm to aperson in acute emergency situations. Cher-p-b. - for desperation, to balance intense tension and the fear that events and one’s own life, including one’s mental power, is out of control. Clem-b. - for that faraway, out-of-the-body state that precedes fainting or loss of consciousness. Can reduce faintness or coma. Imp-b. - to counteract inner turmoil, tension and impatience. Rck-r-b. - to counteract terror and panic. Star-b- b. - to reduce shock, trauma, sadness and prevent the trauma’s possible long-lasting effects on mind, emotions and body from imprinting. Rescue remedy is of great value immediately after accidents or similar moments of shock and panic when there is faintness, trembling, or other failing of normal physical functioning. Useful as the first medicine administered on arrival at the accident. After accidents, shocks, traumas or during severe illness, mental or physical. Can be given before stressful events to help calm the anticipation or fear. Anxiety, panic attacks and sudden fear. Speechless and trembling. Can also be used as a daily remedy in chronic situations of intense nervousness and tension when the vital force needs to recharge and recuperate. Can prevent or give a peaceful death if given at the right moment. MIND - Rescue Remedy helps to bring balance, calm and synchronicity of functioning within the levels of the human being, these being the mind, emotions and body. REFERENCES - Bach. Muiphy.

full:
PHARMACY - reser. Reserpinum. Reserpine. Alkaloid of Rauwolfia serpentina. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Cancer. Catalepsy. Diarrhea. Duodenal, ulcer. Dyspepsia. Headache. Hemorrhoids. Hypotension. Hypothermia. Jaundice. Migraines. Melancholy. Nasal polyps. Parkinson’s disease. Pharyngitis. Rhinitis.

HOMEOPATHIC - It is one of the alkaloids of Rauwolfia serpentina and was found commercially under the name of serpasil ciba. The proving was carried out by Julian on a group of thirteen provers during the winter of 1964-65, using the 3x, 5c, 7c, 9c, 15c and 30c potencies. Sleepiness. Sleeping after meals. Slowing down of the mind and body. Asthenia, particularly accentuated between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m. General condition of weakness. Habitual trembling. General excitability. Anxiety. Suicidal tendencies. Muscular hypertonia and a total lack of movement. Hard trophic edema. Intermittent stomach pains. Hypotension. Bradycardia. Vertigo. Allergies. Cancer. MIND - Slowing down of the mind and body. Lassitude and aversion to work in the evening. Catalepsy. Nervous depression. Melancholy. Anxiety and suicidal tendencies. Difficulty working. Very hyperactive and aggressive. Feeling that the nerves are at skin level in the evening. Premature senility.

Head - Headache on waking, better by breakfast and worse again at the end of the morning.

Eyes - Myosis.

Nose - Nasal obstruction. Congestive rhinitis. Nasal polyps.

Mouth - Tongue covered with a yellowish coating. Excessive salivation.

Throat - Pharyngitis. Throat sensitive. Vertigo - Violent attackof vertigo with feeling of a black hole in front of the eyes and leaving an empty feeling for a few minutes, then return to former condition. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rauw. (2) Aur. - Depressive suicidal condition. (3) Lach. - Emotional instability. (4) Ars. - Anguish and fear of dying. (5) Nux- v. - Complaints of the nervous and digestive systems. REFERENCES - Julian.

Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Slight nausea. Gastric pain coming late after meals in painful bursts. Gastric and duodenal ulcer. Cancer of the stomach.

Abdomen - Spasmodic attacks of pain in the colon. Breasts - Excessive milk in the mother. Constitutions - Allergic and psoric constitutions. Syphilitic, asthenic types with tendency to inhibition of nervous reactions.

Rectum - Jaundice. Constipation followed by diarrhea. Diarrhea. Hemorrhoids.

Heart - Hypotension. Tension instability. Bradycardia, with vertigo. Permanently slow pulse.

Limbs - Fidgets in the legs. Lungs - Laryngitis and tracheitis.

Sleep - Sleepiness. Sleeping after meals.

Skin - Dry, ligneous scabs. Hard, trophic edema. Lymphaedema. Dull and damp hair.

Temperature - Hypothermia, at 31°c, adynamic condition, hypertonia total indifference.

PHARMACY - rham-cal. Rhamnus californica. California coffee tree. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, tenesmus. Constipation. Dizzy. Dysmenorrhea. Gastralgia. Heart, disorders. Lumbago. Muscular pains. Pleurodynia. Rheumatism.

HOMEOPATHIC - Provings were done using the 2x potency. Rumbling, griping and cutting pains in ileocecal region. Bladder tenesmus. Pleurodynia. Gastralgia. Dysmenorrhea of muscle origin, pain in head, neck and face. Rheumatism and muscular pains. Inflammatory rheumatism, joints swollen, painful. Lumbago. Rheumatic heart. Tendency to metastasis. Profuse sweat. MIND - Nervous, restless, irritable. Lassitude, mentally dull and dazed, unable to concentrate mind on studies.

Head - Dizzy full feeling. Heavy bruised sensation, better from pressure. Bursting feeling with every step. Soreness, especially in occiput and vertex, worse bending over. Dull pain in left temple. Dull aching in frontal region (left), extending backwards and over forehead. Deep, right-sided frontal headache. Twitching eyelids.

Ears - Dullness of hearing. Soreness, deep under right tragus, on swallowing.

Face - Flushed, hot and glowing. Outward pressure from malar processes.

Mouth - Canker sore between gums and lips. Tongue coated, with clean, pink, central patch.

Throat - Dry, rough. Soreness on right side and tonsil. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rham-cath. or Rham-f., European Buckthorn - a rheumatic remedy, abdominal symptoms, colic, diarrhea, hemorrhoids, especially chronic. (2) Rham- p. (3) Cas-s. - palliative in constipation, as an intestinal tonic and dyspepsia dependent thereon. 10-15 drops of tincture. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Rectum - Constipation with some flatus. Tenesmus and dry stool. Flatulent diarrhea.

Chest - Sub-sternal oppression. Tenderness on pressure of right intercostal muscles.

Heart - Variation of pulse. Slow pulse.

Limbs - Legs sore. Unable to control muscular action. Walked like a drunken man.

Modalities - Worse in evening.

Kidneys - Increased urination. Tickling in anterior urethra, small morning drop (no previous gonorrhea). Sexual desire increased.

name: Rhamnus Cathartica
author: Murphy
constitution: Appendicitis. Canker, sores. Colic. Constipation. Diarrhea. Tympanites. Typhlitis.
keynote:
PHARMACY - rham-cath. Rhamnus cathartica. Purging buckthorn. Buckthorn. N. O. Rham- nacae. Tincture of fluid extract of ripe berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Appendicitis. Canker, sores. Colic. Constipation. Diarrhea. Tympanites.…
full:
PHARMACY - rham-cath. Rhamnus cathartica. Purging buckthorn. Buckthorn. N. O. Rham- nacae. Tincture of fluid extract of ripe berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Appendicitis. Canker, sores. Colic. Constipation. Diarrhea. Tympanites. Typhlitis.

HOMEOPATHIC - The common buckthorn produces black, shiny, four-sided berries with an acrid taste. A syrup is made from these berries, and forms the Rhamni succus of the old school. Symptoms were observed in a boy poisoned by eating the berries. Copious watery stools. Nausea and severe vomiting. Rham-cath., in doses of a few drops, is a useful palliative in cases of constipation. The ileo-cecal symptoms seem to indicate it as a possible remedy in cases of appendicitis. Milne noted that it was formerly given in dropsy.

Head - Unable to rise, seemed to desire to press his head against the wall.

Eyes - Eyes glistening and injected.

Face - Trembling of lips. Commencing trismus. Food - Complete loss of appetite.

Mouth - Coated tongue. Extremely bitter taste.

Throat - Scraping in throat. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cas-s. (2) Cean. in appendicitis, Iris-t. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Abdomen - Abdomen hard, tympanitis. Colic. Violent rumbling and griping. Cutting pains in ileo-cecal region and in transverse colon.

Rectum - Diarrhea. Liquid stools.

Limbs - Weakness and prostration in all limbs. Lungs - Respiration short, anxious.

Kidneys - Urine highly colored.

Pulse - Pulse variable.

Temperature - Violent chilliness. Skin at one time warm, at another cold.

HOMEOPATHIC - All parts of Rham-f. appear to produce irritant and cathartic properties. The majority of the symptoms were the result of the root bark, but the leaves were no less active. There was more vomiting with Rham-f. than with Rham-cath., and the former was abandoned as a cathartic because it so frequently produced vomiting instead. Burning in urethra while urinating and frequent urination may prove an indication in gonorrhea. Stools of a dark-green color, copious, thin or pasty. HERBAL - Cas-s. is apalliative forconstipation, fifteen drops of fluid extract restores normal function by its tonic effects. Only material doses have been used.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pathogenic effects on patients taking it for constipation have been recorded, including vomiting, severe griping, and hemorrhage. In one case, temporary insanity was produced from a homemade decoction of the bark. In two cases, cholera symptoms were produced. This is a well-known purgative as it has been found curative in cases of acute and chronic rheumatism with constipation. Chronic indigestion, cirrhosis and jaundice. Hemorrhoids and constipation. Gastric headache. Broad, flabby tongue. Foul breath. Kidneys - Must wait before flow starts, then comes in drops at first.

Stomach - Chronic indigestion. Gastric headache. Vomiting. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Hydr., Nux-v. (2) Rham-cal - tincture for constipation, tympanites and appendicitis and especially rheumatism. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Rectum - Hemorrhoids. Severe constipation.

Limbs - Rheumatism of muscles andjoints with obstinate constipation.

Liver - Cirrhosis and jaundice.

author: Murphy

PHARMACY - rheum. Rheum palmatum. Turkey rhubarb. Rheum officinale. Rhabar- barum. N. O. Polygonacae. China. Tincture and trituration of the dried root. A tincture of the fresh leaves and young stalks should be investigated. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Ardor urine. Breath offensive. Constipation. Deafness. Dentition, difficult. Diarrhea. Duodenum, catarrh. Dysentery. Ears, thickening. Esophagus, constriction. Headaches. Jaundice. Kidneys, disorders. Meniere’s disease. Milk, abnormal. Mouth, mucus. Nipples, pain. Nose, pain. Nursing disorders. Rheumatism. Salivation. Screaming, children. Snoring. Stomach, disordered. Sour smelL Taste, bad. Tongue, numbness. Urination, difficult. Urine, red.

HERBAL - Rhubarb, called ‘Turkey rhubarb,” comes from China, but the exact species is unknown. Milne summarized its action from the traditional point of view as being “tonic, cathartic and a feeble astringent, the latter property being overborne by the cathartic and only coming into play afterwards,” i.e., the constipation which follows rhubarb purgation. “In small doses, it improves digestion and appetite and renders the kidney secretions more healthy. In larger doses it is an excellent cathartic, acting on the whole bowel and especially the duodenum and increasing the peristaltic action.” It affects the liver, duodenum, bile ducts and intestines.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hahnemann’s proving of Rheum confirmed many of its traditional uses. Rheum is a remedy for nursing infants andchildren especially during dentition, and suited to pregnant and nursing women. The whole child smells sour, washing does not remove it. Colicky children who are always screaming and crying. Sour diarrhea, taste, vomits, stools, sweat etc. Difficult dentition. Requires very little sleep and not much food. Sensation of crepitation. MIND - Impatient and vehement, desires many things and cries (Cina.). Impetuous desire for particular objects. Temper of child is as acrid as are the stools. Child dislikes even its favorite things. Child cries and tosses all night. Full of fear. Fear of death, and restlessness, in first days after confinement, with diarrhea. Anxiety from motion, when stooping. Indolent. Taciturn. Asks for nothing. Morose. Delirious talking. Quarrelsome in sleep. Restless with weeping.

Head - Sweat on hairy scalp. Wet, sopping hair.

Eyes - Weak when looking steadily at any object. Convulsive twitching of eyelids.

Ears - Otalgia with itching in ear. Pressure and throbbing in ears. Dullness of hearing.

Nose - Stupefying drawing from root of nose to tip, where it tingles. Heat in nose.

Face - Cool sweat on face, especially about mouth and nose, on upper lip. Tendency to frown. Forehead wrinkled. Twitching.

Mouth - Salivation with colic or diarrhea. Offensive mucus in the mouth after sleep. Breath smells sour (Cham.). Food tastes bitter, even sweet things. Teeth feel cold. Difficult teething, restless and irritable.

Throat - Contraction of gullet. COMMENTS - Characteristic sourness and acidity. The stools are sour, the taste is sour, the whole body has a sour smell. No amount of washing will wash the sourness out. The breath, stools, and sweat smell sour (Mag-c., Nat-p., Calc.). Sopping-wet hair. Often indicated in nursing babies when they get sores in their mouth and soursmelling diarrhea. Dentition with sour stools. Colic with night screaming. “Screaming of children with urging and sour stools." Sour disposition (Cham.). Peevish, impatient, screams for things, dislikes even his favorite playthings. Stomach disorders with a sour, flat, slimy, insipid or nauseous taste. Food tastes bitter, even sweet things. The mouth is covered with offensive mucus after sleeping, with a bad taste and offensive breath. Hunger for various kinds of food, but the first few mouthfuls nauseate. Bad effects of eating plums orunripe fruit. Nausea. Severe colic, compelling one to bend double, worse standing, worse just before stool, not better after, worse at once by uncovering an arm or leg. Evacuations accompanied by shivering and renewed urging. “Shivering with stool.” Symptoms are mostly left-sided or go from above down or from right to left. Generally affects the left loin, brain, upper part of body (sweat). With a few drops of Rheum, Clarke relieved severe constipation in an acid child who was intolerant of almost all remedies in the potencies. On the indication “diarrhea only during active exercise,” Hundall cured a horse of a diarrhea that only came on when he was at work. Cooper noted that “Rheum has the property of setting up pains in old disease, in the old cellulitis and old psoriasis patches. Hot burning pains therein as well as in the unaffected veins of the thighs and other parts. Its good effect in old middle and internal ear thickenings seems due to the creation of tissue-activity in dormant structures.” Cooper offered two cases, the first was that of a woman who suffered from characteristic symptoms of Meniere’s disease, feeling of things spinning around with extreme giddiness and noises in the head. She was cured by a chemist giving her 10 grains of powdered rhubarb based on the idea that it was due to the liver. Before this, great suffering had been endured without any relief. The second case concerned vertiginous symptoms due to brain exhaustion with flushings followed by perspiration and awful muffled and discordant tinnitus. Great relief followed the sniffing of 3x trituration of Rheum. RELATIONS - Antidotes: Camph., Cham. Compare: (1) Mag-c., Mag-p., Hep., Podo., Cham., Cina, Ip. Complementary: Mag-c. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Throbbing and shootings pain in pit of stomach. Contractions in stomach. Fullness in stomach with pressure, as if overloaded. Nausea during colic.

Abdomen - Wind seems to rise up to chest. Colicky pain about navel. Colic with screaming, better doubling up, worse uncovering any part, Then diarrhea.

Rectum - Frequent, ineffectual urging to stool, worse motion and walking. Tenesmus. Before stool, unsuccessful urging to urinate. Renewed urging after stool, when moving. Colicky, even ineffectual urging to evacuate altered fecal stools. Severe constipation. Diarrhea only when walking. White diarrhea from eating unripe fruits with jaundice. Sour diarrhea during dentition. Diarrhea in first days after confinement, withcolic. Loose, soursmelling stool with colic, immediately after nursing child. Sensations - Sensation as if brain moved when standing. Heaviness as on waking from a heavy sleep. Coldness in teeth. Blunt feeling in teeth. Tongue numb, numbness of part of limb lain on. Constriction of stomach of gullet. Crackling, crepitation or bubbling in muscles and any part of body.

Stool - Stools smell sour, with shivering and tenesmus, and burning in anus. Sour diarrhea during dentition. Diarrhea of varying color and consistency, usually frothy and of a sour odor. Diarrhea only when walking. Stools pasty, pappy, brown, green, fermented, slimy or acrid. Yellow stool, turning green on standing. Stools with shivering, tenesmus and burning in anus. Thin, pasty, sour-smelling stools, with straining before, and colicky, constrictive cutting in abdomen after. Stools worse from eating unripe fruit, or in the evening.

Female - Urinary complaints after abortion. Diarrhea after childbirth. Yellow and bitter milk in nursing women, infant refuses breast. Food - Loss of appetite. Requires little food. Loathing after first bite. Food tastes bitter, even sweet things. Desire for various things, but cannot eat them. Plums and prunes disagree.

Chest - Lancinations in chest. Rush of blood to chest. Crackling bubbling (even audible) in right then left pectoral muscles. Constitutions - For nursing children, especially during dentition, and for pregnant and nursing women.

Back - Stiffness in sacrum and hips, cannot walk straight. Cutting pain in lumbar region, worse after stools. Causations - Eating prunes, unripe fruit. Dentition. Spasms, dislocations.

Limbs - Limb on which he lies falls asleep. Twitching in arms, hands and fingers. Bubbling sensation in elbow joint from bend of knee to heels. Lameness of wrist and knee after sprains and dislocations.

Sleep - Restless with whining and crying. Twitching of face and fingers. Requires very little sleep and not much food.

Skin - Sweat stains yellow. Pemphigus on face, scalp and hands, face, lips and tongue swollen, face livid. Itching rash on forehead and arms.

Modalities - Better from warmth, wrapping up. Better lying bent, lying doubled up, takes the queerest positions in order to rest awhile. Worse uncovering, summer, night, after sleep, and morning. Worse motion, dentition. Worse after eating, plums. Worse before, after and during stools. Worse in nursing women.

Liver - Jaundice from eating unripe fruits, with white diarrhea. Lungs - Snoring inspiration during sleep. The cough is dry in evening, with expectoration of mucus.

Kidneys - Burning in bladder and kidney, before and during urination. Unsuccessful urging to urinate before stool.

Perspiration - Child smells sour, even if washed or bathed. Sweat on scalp, about mouth, nose, and on upper lip. Easy perspiration, on forehead and scalp. Stains yellow.

Temperature - Chilliness alternating with heat. Internal, with external heat. Heat all over, mostly on hands and feet, with cold face, no thirst.

Dull headache. Loose cold in head. Feels weak, dizzy and a tired feeling. Stiff neck and rheumatic pain down left shoulder and arm. Cough scratchy, wheezy. Thick, yellow mucus from chest. Lips dry. Itching in arms, palms and face. Hyperactive peristalsis, tenesmus after stool. Loose stools with gripings in abdomen. More urine passed. Nausea, especially from sweets. REFERENCES - Boericke.

full:
PHARMACY - rhodi-o-n. Rhodium oxydatum nitricum. Nitrate oxide of rhodium. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anus, itching, burning. Constipation. Ears, pains. Hemorrhoids. Headache. Hearing, illusions. Impotence.

HOMEOPATHIC - Rhodium is often found in association with platinum. Hering’s preparation was obtained from exposing a small quantity of rhodium sponge, hydrate of potash and nitre to the action of a blowpipe until oxidized. After having the oxide well washed and boiled in nitric acid for a few minutes and exposed to a gentle heat for an hour, the nitrate was obtained from the oxide, producing a fluid of a golden color of the consistency of syrup. Dilutions of this were made and the 4th was proved for Hering by Dr. Person, the 2nd and 3rd by Dr. Negendank. The bowels were affected in both, constipation with hemorrhoids being relieved in one and constipation with itching of the anus being caused in the other. Headache on being woken in the night. Headache alternating with faintness. Faintness better by passage of stool. Heat preceding chill and alternating with it. Sensation as if teeth blunt, as if sand between them. A scraping or harsh noise causes disagreeable sensation in teeth. The hearing is more acute, illusion that he hears whispering. REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Rhododendron Chrysanthum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better after the storm breaks, when the sun shines. Better heat, warmth, wrapping up, wrapping head. Better motion and eating. Worse before a storm, rough weather. Worse during windy, cold, damp, cloudy weather. Worse when the seasons change, midsummer. Worse getting wet, catching cold. Worse at night, towards morning, from rest. Worse wine, eating fruit..

Flatulence, incarcerated. Fibrositis. Gout. Gums, itching. Headaches. Hydrocele. Lienteria. Lumbago. Memory, weak. Meniere’s, disease. Neuralgias. Nightmares. Nosebleeds. Orchitis. Ovary, cyst. Periostitis. Rheumatism. Sple

PHARMACY - rhod. Rhododendron chry- santhum. Yellow snow rose. Rhododendron aureum. Siberian rhododendron. Gout rose. N. O. Ericacee. Tincture of fresh leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea.Arthritis. Asthenopia. Bone, pains. Bunions.…
full:
PHARMACY - rhod. Rhododendron chry- santhum. Yellow snow rose. Rhododendron aureum. Siberian rhododendron. Gout rose. N. O. Ericacee. Tincture of fresh leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea.Arthritis. Asthenopia. Bone, pains. Bunions. Chorea. Ciliary, neuralgia. Colic. Coryza. Delirium. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dysmenorrhea. Earache. Eye, disorders. Fever. Flatulence, incarcerated. Fibrositis. Gout. Gums, itching. Headaches. Hydrocele. Lienteria. Lumbago. Memory, weak. Meniere’s, disease. Neuralgias. Nightmares. Nosebleeds. Orchitis. Ovary, cyst. Periostitis. Rheumatism. Spleen, pain. Sprains. Stiff-neck. Testes, disorders. Tinnitus. Toothaches. Vagina, cysts. Wrists, pains.

HERBAL - The golden flowered rhododendron grows among the fog and storms of the Siberian mountains. It is not well known in general medicine, but the Treasury of Botany said that “it is narcotic in its properties and is used medicinally.” Gmelin, during his travels in Siberia, noted that the Cossacks and Mongolians used it for rheumatism and gout. The hunters and mountain rangers would drink an infusion of it to remove the weariness and pains from their limbs after fatiguing expeditions. Gmelin was the first to recommend rhododendron in Europe as a remedy for gout and rheumatism. The first publication on the subject was by Professor Kolpin, of Stettin, in 1779. It was used with greater or less success, and recommended accordingly by many German physicians.

HOMEOPATHIC - Rhod. is a gouty, rheumatic remedy, affecting the fibrous tissues, forearm, lower legs, small joints, bones, genitals, nerves, and single parts. Fibrositis. Arthritis. Great weakness after slight exer- tion. Formication with sweat. Undulating sensation. Tearing, zigzag, boring, rapidly changing, descending, paralytic pains. Rhod. produces delirium, fever, headache, neuralgias, rheumatism and inflammations. Symptoms come on or are worse on the approach of a storm, worse during a storm or in wet weather. Sensitiveness to electric changes, lightning (Phos.). Weather vane, can predict an upcoming change (Calc., Rhus-t., Dulc.). Arthritis cases are especially sensitive to barometric changes. Aggravated symptoms before a storm, usually arthritis, headaches, neuralgias, toothaches and earaches. Increased warmth of hands even in cold weather. Sensitive to windy or stormy wet weather, even if he is in the house. Fornervous persons who are afraid of thunder, dread of storms. Chorea before storm. Disorders which come on in the spring and autumn. Rheumatism in the hot season. Symptoms alternate. MIND - Dread of a storms. Fear of thunderstorms in nervous persons (Phos.). Nervous before storms. Fits of anxiety. Confused and stupid. Impatience. Irritability. Peevish, without any apparent cause. Phlegmatic mood, he is affected by neither pleasant or unpleasant impressions. Gloomy mood. Sadness, being alone aggravates. Indifferent. Aversion to everything, especially to occupations. Aversion to his business. Stupefaction. Obscuration or loss of senses. Forgets what he is talking about, leaves out whole words while writing. Does not recollect what he had been talking about until he has thought a while. Vanishing of thoughts. Easily affected by wine. Mental derangement. Frightful visions. Delirium, he staggers, tosses his head about and reels. After a short time, falls asleep upon his knees. In vain he attempts to rise, but is overcome with sleep for an hour and a quarter, during which he starts continually and appears terrified, but awakes cheerful.

Head - Headaches, worse wine, wind, cold and wet weather, early in the morning, better eating. Aching in temples. Throbbing in right side. Bursting pains, better pressure and rubbing forehead. Tearing pain in bones. Drawing, tearing under scalp. Hair stands up as if electrified. Heat in afternoon, evening. Pressure in temples, as if compressed. Contracting, as if scalp stretched tight.

Eyes - Muscular asthenopia. Ciliary neuralgia involving orbit, eyeball and head, worse before storm. Heat in eyes when using them. Darting pains, red-hot needles darting from within out. Contractive pain behind the eyes, with pain in forehead. Pain in eyes before a storm.

Ears - Earache. Sensation as of a worm in the ear. As if hot air was flowing from throat to ears. Tinnitus with vertigo. Difficult hearing with whizzing and ringing in ears. Hearing better in the morning, noises come on after patient has been up a few hours. Deafness, long after rising.

Nose - Dryness, soreness inside nose. One sided nasal obstruction. Nostrils obstructed, alternately with fluent coryza, better in open air. Nasal discharge, viscid like gravel on dry mucus membranes. Paroxysmal sneezing. Nosebleed. Diminished smell.

Face - Prosopalgia, violent jerking pain involving dental nerves from temple to lower jaw and chin. Pains better warmth and eating. Painful pimples, better pressure.

Mouth - Salivation with nausea and intermittent pain in stomach. Insipid, bitter taste. Dryness in the mouth, palate, and tongue. Speech impossible due to numbness of cheeks, and lips, in morning after waking.

Throat - Dryness. Burning pain. Swelling of throat. Chocking, constriction and burnin" sensation in throat. Scratching, scrapin^ in throat, sensationasif lined with m -c"^ Mucus tough, gluey, green, diffi. .. to detach with cough and retching. Sensation of foreign object. Heat, as if hot air were to gush out from throat to ears. Vertigo - Vertigo, when lying in bed, better when moving about. Tinnitus with vertigo. COMMENTS - Characteristic loss of memory. Words are omitted while writing, thoughts suddenly disappear, forgets what they are talking about, has to think a while before they can recall it. Narcotic symptoms. Intoxication, and sensitivity to wine. One pupil dilated, the other contracted. Vertigo and confusion, “brain feels as if surrounded by fog.” Vertigo while lying in bed, better by moving about. Tinnitus aurium, associated with the vertigo. Meniere’s disease. “Loud sounds re-echo long in ears.” Symptoms frequently alternate, left and right nostril, burning in uterus and pains in limbs, chilliness and heat. Pains go from within outward. Both sides are affected. Arthritis, worse rest and better motion (Rhus-t.). Better from warmth and wrapping the area up. Chorea of left leg, arm and face, worse on approach of a storm. Splenic stitch on walking fast. Offensive smell in the axillary sweat, but the general sweat may be aromatic in odor and not unpleasant. Formication with sweat. Like the other Ericacee, Rhod. has a strong effect on the kidneys, producing increased urine with offensive smell, clear, brown red or of greenish tinge and, whatever color it may be, of offensive smell. Diarrhea. Paralytic condition of the rectum, effort is required to expel a soft stool. “Flatus felt in the back,” in cases of flatulent indigestion. Pains in rectum extend to genitals. The scrotum shrinks, testes are retracted or else they swell (especially at night) and are the seat of a bruised pain, as if they had been crushed violently. Pains are worse by touch, worse sitting, better moving about. Pains may be so violent as to arrest breathing. The menses are too early and too profuse. Menses are accompanied by fever and headache. Menses reappear soon after they have ceased. In one prover, Rhod. restored the menses after six months’ absence. Vaginal cysts, has caused the rupture of ovarian cysts. The paralyzing effect of Rhod. was exemplified by the poisoning of a flock of sheep from eating the leaves. A number of them died and the autopsy showed that cause of death was paralysis of the swallowing muscles. Cooper cited a parallel case of death from post-diphtheria paralysis affecting the throat muscles, occurring afew minutes after drinking tea. In both instances, the fluid entered the trachea instead of the gullet and caused suffocation. H. S. Budd related the case of Mrs. X., 44, who was married ten years and had three children. She had neuralgia for three years. Attacks usually occurred on Friday or Saturday and would last until Monday or Tuesday, but were induced any time by high winds, damp weather or an approaching storm. Passi. only partly relieved, sometimes enabling the patient to get sleep. The pain was worse after hard work, during any movement, in very cold weather or from hot applications. She had intense soreness all over the right half of her head, she could not rest on a pillo w or endure even the lightest hairpins when pain was worst. Worse at night. She was intensely nervous and hysterical at being touched, even by accident. During the pain, she had increased activity of the kidneys, that ceased when pain ceased. Pain was greatest in her right lower jaw. Sometimes better for an hour by chewing gum or eating. Afraid of thunder. Omitted words when writing. Rhod. 16x every hour was given on May 12. Each dose caused an immediate worsening of symptoms. The next morning, pains stopped suddenly and did not return. On June 7th there was a premonitory twinge and a powder of Rhod. 1,000c was given, after which there was complete immunity. E. V. Moffat treated a girl, 10, for neuralgia, which had existed for several years. The patient was of a marked gouty heredity and had been treated by leading old-school doctors in New York. She was well during Rhododendron chrysanthum the summer, but suffered intensely during winter. Pains were general and shifting, sometimes intercostal, sometimes sciatic in bad weather, never absent. The last form was a prostrating headache incapacitating her for schoolwork. Her eyes were normal. While the sun shone, she was comfortable. If it stormed or threatened, she was miserable. If she had a headache on a stormy day and the sun came out in ten minutes she was relieved, and it returned at once if snow or rain came on. A cold day, especially if damp, was almost as bad as a storm. Rhod. in repeated and increasing doses, cured in three weeks. Color, spirits, strength returned and she no longer minded the weather or missed her school. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ampe-qu. - hydrocele and kidney dropsy. (2) Med., Dulc., Rhus-t., Nat-s. (3) It is analogous to and follows as regards the testes, Puls., Aur., Spong., as regards hydrocele, Clem., Graph. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Empty feeling in morning. Weak feeling, better eating. Feels full after a little food. Paroxysmal pain. Heartburn. Belching, after eating eggs. Heavy pressure from cold drinks. Nausea, better fresh air. Green, bitter vomiting after drinking cold water.

Abdomen - Colic at navel. Flatus felt in back. Undulating sensation arising from abdomen. Sickening pain in spleen on walking fast. Pain from rectum to genitals. Paroxysmal pain, lying on abdomen impossible. Pain in left hypogastrium. Umbilical pain.

Rectum - Diarrhea worse fruits, does not weaken. Difficult evacuation, even of soft feces. Feces of pap consistency. Mucus evacuations. Sensations - Brain as if in a fog. Scalp as if bruised. As if a worm in ear. As if water rushing into ear. As if throat lined with mucus. As from tension under short ribs. As if a fist pressed forcibly against stomach. Undulating sensation arising from abdomen. Warm undulations in heart. Testicle as if violently contused or crushed. As if blood ceased to circulate in arms. As if arms asleep. As if feet and legs asleep. As if heavy weights hanging to feet. As of subcutaneous ulceration. Bruised pains. Pains flying about. Crawling sensations.

Male - Hydrocele of boys from birth (Sil.). Drawing from spermatic cord into abdomen and thighs. Orchitis. Itching, wrinkled, sweaty, scrotum. Testes, especially the epididymis, are intensely painful to the touch swollen, drawn up, worse left. Contusive pain in the testes. Induration and swelling of testes after gonorrhea. Glans feels crushed. Burning, sore pain between the genital organs and thighs, especially when walking.

Female - Suppressed menses. Painful menses. Dysmenorrhea. Fever with headache, with each menstrual period. Serous cysts in vagina. Burning in uterine region after childbirth, alternating with pain in limbs, fingers spasmodically flexed. Sexual desire increased. Food - Desires sweets. Dullness of taste, food has no flavor. Gnawing, hungry sensation before a meal. Speedy satiety with good appetite, followed by uneasiness. Augmented thirst. Generals - Burning, stitching pain. Pressure on certain points ameliorates. Trembling. Weakness. Weariness, worse afternoon. Lack of vital heat. Sensation of heat. Desires open air.

Chest - Violent pleuritic pains running down the left anterior chest. Crampy pain under short ribs. Stitches in spleen from fast walking. Breathless and speechless from pain. Constitutions - Suited to nervous persons who dread a storm and are particularly afraid of thunder.

Heart - Warm undulation at heart. Strong heartbeat.

Back - Stiff neck. Sacrum pains, worse sitting. Pain between scapulae. Backache, lumbar region. Stitching pain, extending to pit of stomach.

Limbs - Swollen joints. Rheumatic and tearing pains in all the limbs, especially right side. Rheumatic pains worse at rest and in stormy weather. Rheumatism in hot weather. Numbness. Numbness as if limbs have gone to sleep, must move about. Stitching pain. Pain, better motion. Drawing, tearing in periosteum of long bones. Pain in bones, in spots, and reappear by change of weather. Coldness of limbs. Sensation like a cool draft of air over limbs. Gout. Gouty inflammation of great toe joint. Cannot sleep unless legs are crossed. Lower legs, cold, skin wrinkled, Rhododendron chrysanthum feel as if asleep. As of a weight hanging to feet. Feet cold even in warm room, even in bed. Pain in Achilles tendon on stepping. Shoulder pain, better firm pressure and warmth on certain points. Pain in shoulders, arms, wrists, worse when at rest. Bruised, sprained feeling in wrist. Hands feel warm in cold weather. Lungs - Bruised, sprained feeling in chest. Breathless and speechless from violent pleuritic pains, running down anterior chest. Expectoration in mornings, 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. Crumbly expectoration, left-over food, like leaves in the mouth.

Sleep - Cannot sleep unless legs are crossed. Wakes, as if called.

Skin - Eruptions. Burning and tearing with erysipelas. Itching, burning and creeping.

Modalities - Better after the storm breaks, when the sun shines. Better heat, warmth, wrapping up, wrapping head. Better motion and eating. Worse before a storm, rough weather. Worse during windy, cold, damp, cloudy weather. Worse when the seasons change, midsummer. Worse getting wet, catching cold. Worse at night, towards morning, from rest. Worse wine, eating fruit.

Larynx - Dryness. Hoarse voice. Trachea irritation, mucus. Sensation of mucus that he is not able to eject. Burning pains, like splinters.

Teeth - Swollen gums. Stumps of teeth are loosened. Toothache in damp weather and before a storm. Toothache, better eating and warmth. Toothache ceases suddenly, worse again in two or three hours.

Kidneys - Frequent urging to urinate with drawing in the bladder region. Pain in the urethra as from subcutaneous ulceration. Profuse, foul, greenish urine.

Bladder - Frequent desire to urinate. Burning in the urethra before and during urination. Copious urine. Causations - Catching cold. Stormy weather, thunder, getting wet. Sprains. Eating fruit.

Cough - Choking. Suffocative coughs, worse motion. Cough from tickling in trachea. Paroxysmal coughs with retching, choking. Morning coughs, from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. Dreams - Erotic dreams. Exhausting, frightful dreams. Nightmares.

Perspiration - Offensive smell in the axillary sweat, but the general sweat may be aromatic in odor and not unpleasant. Formication with sweat.

Temperature - Formication and itching of skin with sweat. Chilliness, 11 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. Shaking, shivering rigors. Cold feet, even in warm room or bed. Hands warm in cold weather.

full:
PHARMACY - rhus-a. Rhus aromática. Fragrant sumac. Rhus canadensis. Rhus suaveo- lens. Betula triphyIla. Lobadiumaromaticum. Turpinia glabra. N. O. Anacardiacae. Tincture of fresh root bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Atony. Bedwetting. Bladder, hemorrhage. Cystitis. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Hematuria. Hemorrhages. Kidneys, hemorrhage. Uterus, hemorrhage, atony.

HERBAL - J. T. McClanahan’s account of Rhus-a. : “It is a shrub, growing from two to six feet high, on high, rocky soil, stems straight, branching near the top. The flowers are yellow, fruit clustered, red, seedy and acid. When the bush is fractured it emits a strong odor. The bark of the root is the proper medicinal part.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Rhus-a. has kidney and urinary disorders. Diabetes, large quantities of urine of low specific gravity (Ph-ac., Acet- ac.). Bedwetting due to bladder atony, senile incontinence. Hematuria and cystitis. The urine is pale, albuminous. Incontinence of urine. Severe pain at beginning or before urination, causing great agony in children. Constant dribbling. COMMENTS - McClanahan mentioned hemorrhage from kidneys, bladder and uterus, menorrhagia and other discharges accompanied by a relaxed condition of the uterus as indicating the remedy, also atonic conditions generally. These experiences have been confirmed by others. McClanahan's grandfather, Dr. John Gray, used Rhus-a. as a remedy in diabetes, and his father, Dr. F. McClanahan, in other genito-urinary diseases. J. T. McClanahan recorded several cases, including the case of Mr. A., 27, cadaverous, emaciated, haggard, had diabetes insipidus. Rhus-a., teaspoonful doses of the powdered root bark in sweet milk, three times a day, completely cured in four months. Mrs. B., 37, had diabetes mellitus. First noticed increase of urine ten months before, became so weak she had to abandon house-work. Pain in back, thirst, appetite, now ravenous, now deficient. Skin sallow, doughy. Cough and night-sweats occasionally. Diarrhea at times. Rhus-a., half-teaspoonful doses every four hours, was given. Quantity of urine diminished next day and as this diminution progressed the doses of Rhus-a. were given at increasing intervals, and in three months it was discontinued. Proper diet had been observed in the meantime. Mr. C. had incontinence of urine more than a year, constant dribbling. Rhus-a. tincture 10 drops, three times a day, improved at once and cured completely in eight weeks. A girl had bedwetting during the day and night for two years. Rhus-a. tincture, one part to glycerine three parts, a teaspoonful three times a day, cured. A boy, early in summer had diarrhea, stools pale and thin, running from him like water, no particular pain or fever. Pale, emaciated, limbs trembling, scarcely able to stand. Abdomen flabby. Rhus-a. tincture 3 drops in water after each stool, cured rapidly. A laborer had “chronic dysentery” for two months. On the average, had five stools a day, sometimes copious and painless, sometimes scanty and with pain. Stools consisted largely of blood and mucus or clear blood. Patient was thin, anxious, bowels (abdomen) flabby. Skin sallow. Rhus-a. tincture in ten- drop doses with boiled milk diet, cured. J. A. McKay related the case of Mrs. S., 45, who had severe, profuse uterine hemorrhage for eight days, which three old-school doctors failed to arrest. The condition was becoming desperate, large clots passing away and the patient fainting from the loss. Rhus-a. tincture 10 drops, every six hours, was given. The first dose checked the flow, which ceased entirely after the second. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

CLINICAL - Chickenpox .Eczema. Erysipelas. Fatigue. Skin, sensitive. Sprains.

HOMEOPATHIC - Rhus-d. is an antidote to Rhus-t. Affects the skin with violent skin symptoms with frightful itching. Much swelling of the face, hands and genitals. The skin is very sensitive with eczema and erysipelas. Tired from least effort, goes to sleep from sheer exhaustion. Great nervous weakness. Causations - Ailments from overexertion, lifting, physical labor. Strains. Sprains. COMMENTS - Murray Moore observed the effect of Rhus-d. on three persons. The first was Miss M., 25 of brown hair and fair complexion. She walked up a hill one warm morning and, while perspiring, gathered fems which grew among the Rhus-d. trees. the leaves of which she must have touched, though she did not pull any. The result was a very severe poisoning. J. W., a light-haired, robust Englishman, 23, lay down while sweating among the bushes and was smartly poisoned. Ver-v. tincture internally and a lotion of magnesia sulph. externally checked the spread of the disease. A boy, 10, pure blond type with thin, freckled skin, plucked some of the leaves and in eighteen hours the poisoning symptoms came on, facial erysipelas with extreme edema, closing both eyes, itching and burning. The symptoms became general. M. Moore also related the case of a man who was poisoned in California in September, returned to the eastern states, and suffered from an annual eruption for six successive years. During the seventh attack he was carried off with pneumonia, which Moore thought would not have been the case but for the Rhus-d. complication. RELATIONS - Rhus-d. is an antidote to Rhus-t. Compare: Rhus-t. REFERENCES-Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - rhus-g. Rhus glabra. Smooth sumac. Rhus Carolinas. Rhus elegans. Rhus virginica. Pennsylvania sumac. Upland sumac. N. O. Anacardiacae. Rocky or barren soils in North America. Tincture of fresh bark of root. Tincture of berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aphthae. Debility. Diarrhea. Dreams, annoying. Dysentery. Hemorrhages. Headache. Mouth ulcers. Nosebleed. Pharyngitis.

HERBAL - Rhus trypanosomiasis, Rhus glabra and Rhus coriaria have acid fruit and astringent bark, which is used in tanning. Rhus-g. is a deciduous shrub with a stem 2 to 12 feet high and has terminal flowers and fruit clothed with acid crimson hairs like the other non- poisonous Rhus. A tincture made of the whole pannicle, “Sumac-bobs" cured a patient who had every spring an attack of laryngeal cough with dyspnea and almost complete loss of voice. Farmers place “bobs ” in the mangers of hoses who have “heaves. ”

HOMEOPATHIC - The tincture of the bark was proved by Dr. A. V. Marshall on himself with very substantial doses. The symptoms are his and they bear out the traditional uses of the remedy. One of these is “profuse perspiration arising from debility.” Marshall had “profuse sweat during sleep” and such a degree of debility that he was obliged to leave off the proving. Hale mentioned that an infusion of the root had a popular repute in diarrhea and dysentery, especially when the discharges are fetid, and that the berries were used for chronic cough, wheezing cough and laryngeal asthma. It was claimed that this remedy will so disinfect the bowels that the flatus and stools will be free from odor. It acts well in putrescence conditions with tendency to ulceration. Fetid flatus. Used locally on soft, spongy gums, aphthae, pharyngitis, etc. Ulceration of mouth. Nosebleeds and occipital headaches. Dreams of flying through the air (Stict.). Exhaustion and painful fatigue. Loss of weight. MIND - Stupid, forgetful, indifferent to surrounding objects. Distaste for society.

Head - Dull, heavy headache on waking, better by exercise. Dull heavy pain in front and top of head.

Nose - Bleeding from left nostril and mouth. Bloody scabs in left nostril. Left nostril hot and dry.

Mouth - Taste flat, alkaline. Taste of drug remains long. Tongue furred white. Bleeding from mouth. Aphthous stomatitis. Several small, very sensitive ulcers on mucus membrane opposite the bicuspids. Scurvy, nursing sore mouth (Vero-o.).

Throat - Expelled two clots of blood from throat soon after waking. COMMENTS - Cooper observed an aggravation in a case of psoriasis in which the patient felt irritable and despondent and the skin became irritable. Aggravation of stomach symptoms by either food or drink. In the proving there were dull, heavy headaches, better by exercise. Hale said Rhus-g. has cured occipital headaches. RELATIONS - Said to be antidotal to the action of Merc, and has been employed in the treatment of secondaty syphilis after mercury. Compare: (1) Rhus-t. Anae, and other Ana- cardiace, and the Xanthoxylaces, which are an allied order. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Distress in stomach, disturbed, very restless. Pain in stomach, much worse by all food or drink.

Abdomen - Sharp cutting in umbilical region and abdomen. Umbilical region tender to pressure.

Rectum - Diarrhea in afternoon, worse towards evening. Dry, hard stool, latermoist, then natural, and again diarrhea.

Back - Pain in small of back. Food - Loss of appetite. Hunger at breakfast, could eat but little though feeling as if he had fasted many days.

Limbs - Aching and fatigue of lower limbs, can hardly stand.

Sleep - Sleep disturbed by annoying dreams, very restless. Dreams of flying through the air.

Modalities - Better by movement. Worse after sleep. Abdomen, ulcers in mouth, worse from touch.

Kidneys - Scanty, high-colored urine.

Perspiration - Profuse perspiration arising from debility (Chin.). Sweat, profuse during sleep.

Temperature - Sense of coldness while there is actual increase of heat in the skin. Skin hot, dry with thirst.

HERBAL - This variety grows abundantly in the Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys, as well as in the…
full:
PHARMACY - rhus-1. Rhus laurina. Laurel sumac. N. O. Anacardiaceae. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Edema. Itching. Skin, eruptions. Swelling. Urticaria. Vesicles.

HERBAL - This variety grows abundantly in the Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys, as well as in the mountains and is found in all parts of California. It differs from Rhus-t. principally in the shape of the leaves, and in the entire absence of the slightest pubescence, both on their superior and inferior surfaces. The sap of the plant is a thin milky fluid, but when allowed to touch the skin, it produces a dark purple stain, and for three or four days afterwards, whenever the part is washed, it looks as if it had been recently touched with silver nitrate.

HOMEOPATHIC - M. J. Rhees, M.D. wrote, “Some persons are much more readily and severely affected by this plant than others, while a very few are entirely exempt from its influence. The great majority are more or less susceptible to its action. I have seen very many cases of poisoning by it. “Some have presented the same symptoms and the same kind of eruption as were present in my own case, but in more severe form. I have seen eyes completely closed for 24 hours by the swelling, and the scrotum and prepuce have been so badly swollen in a few cases as to render it necessary to support them with a suspensory bandage. “In other instances, the vesicles are much longer than in my case, and become confluent, forming a dark scab of an inch or more in diameter. I have not seen any case in which the tongue or pulse were materially disordered. I have been informed by a gentleman in this city, that two persons with whom he was acquainted, died from the effects of the poison, but I have been unable to learn anything concerning their symptoms. “Dr. Lewis Post, of San Jose, California, informs me that if he rides within ten feet to leeward of the plant, he is speedily affected by it, particularly and almost exclusively on the scrotum and prepuce. It seems to have a great affinity for this part of the body, as almost all the cases I have seen have complained of the intense voluptuous itching of the external genital organs and the inside of the thighs.” COMMENTS - Recorded in proceedings of the American Institute of Homeopathy on rhus-1., M. J. Rhees, M.D. wrote, “On the 4th of the present month, at 10 o’clock a.m., I procured several branches of both sexual varieties of Rhus laur., and cut the leaves tenshoots, and clusters of flowers into small fragments, and put them into a vial, with the intention of making a tincture. “While doing so, I was troubled with a smarting and burning in the eyes. My hands were protected at the time by kid gloves, and I washed them carefully with strong soap before I touched any part of my body. In the evening I began to experience slight itching and burning in the face, particularly about the eyes and forehead; and voluptuous itching on the scrotum and prepuce. At night, felt a sense of oppression as if the air was too heavy. “April 5th. Last night the sleep was disturbed and full of dreams, which were lascivious, and of venereal pleasure; felt heavy and unrefreshed in the morning; during the day the itching in the face has increased and spread over the nose, the edges of the nostrils, the upper and lower lips, the external ears, and the inferior portion of the neck immediately above the sternum and clavicles; the skin on these parts feels rough, and is covered with a minute eruption of lenticular vesicles, filled with transparent serum. “Itching on the back of the hands, particularly between the fingers. The itching on the scrotum and prepuce has become more troublesome, and is much increased by scratching; scratching, or rubbing of the parts is followed by intense burning; the prepuce is slightly swollen. In the evening the nose is quite red and shining; the redness is not removed by pressure. “April 6th. This morning I felt weak and languid. Dull, aching pain, and weakness across the loins. Redness, and swelling of the skin of the forehead, eyelids, nose, cheeks, lips, and ears, behind the ears, and on the front of the neck. “The skin on these parts is covered with the minute lenticular vesicles spoken of yesterday, which are more filled with serum. These vesicles seem to be situated in the rete mucosum; at least they involve a deeper tissue than the cuticle. During the day some of them find their way to the surface, and are ruptured while being scratched. “The itching is so intolerable that it is impossible to resist the inclination to scratch. After scratching, the parts burn and sting, become more swollen, and feel stiff and dry; the prepuce is much swollen and very red, and the itching is unbearable about once in five or six hours on this part and the scrotum; the scrotum is red, swollen, and much corrugated. “After scratching for a few minutes, the itching is entirely relieved for several hours; eruption of pimples and minute vesicles with excessive itching on the backs of the hands and between the fingers; itching on the inside of the thighs. “April 7th. The same symptoms continue as were noted yesterday, but with increased violence. The eyes were nearly closed in the morning, by the swelling of the lids. Chilly sensation during the day, through the whole body, while sitting in a warm room. “April 8th. The itching and swelling on the face, between the fingers, and on the scrotum and prepuce, became so intolerable, that, fearing it would incapacitate me for business, I took Rhus tox. 6th, every four hours, and bathed the parts with cream. This treatment alleviated the symptoms somewhat. At night itching and redness on the inside of the thighs, from the perineum to the knees. “April 9th. The itching and swelling in the face is very much abated, as well as that on the scrotum and prepuce. The itching on the hands and between the fingers is very harassing, and is much increased by rubbing and scratching. “The itching comes on at intervals of 5 or 6 hours, but it may be produced at any time by rubbing or scratching. Scratching is followed by excessive burning, and between the fingers by a dull, aching pain, the skin becoming more swollen, hard, and white, as in urticaria. “This evening took a hot bath, as hot as it could be borne, using Castile soap and the flesh-brush freely. This was followed by immediate and complete relief for several hours. Continued the Rhus tox. as yesterday, and the cream externally. “April 10th. The itching in the neck returned at bed time, last night, and was somewhat troublesome through the night. This morning the itching returned with great severity in the hands, and was again relieved by bathing them in hot water, which was repeated this evening. “The face is very dry and rough, and has a scurfy appearance, and the skin seems to be thickened and indurated; all other parts have been comfortable through the day, with the exception of the thighs and the skin covering the lowerportion of the abdomen, which has at long intervals itched considerably. “April 11 th. Bathed the hands in hot water this morning, and they have not been at all troublesome through the day. There has been some itching on the thighs and scrotum, but not nearly so much as formerly. “April 12th. The hands have been very troublesome at intervals of 12 hours during the day. This morning vesicles made their appearance in the palm of the left hand wherever the sap of the plant had touched the skin, in gathering it. “April 19th. Up to the present time, the itching and burning in the palm of the left hand, and between the fingers of both hands, have been very annoying, almost painful, at intervals of 10 or 12 hours. Wishing, however, to know how long the effect of the plant would continue, I have made use of no remedies since the 11th. It is now evidently abating.” RELATIONS - Compare: Rhus-t. Anae, and other Anacardiace, and the Xanthoxylaces, which are an allied order. REFERENCES Rhees.
