PHARMACY - rosm. Rosmarinus officinalis. Rosemary. N. O. Labiatx. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Baldness. Dandruff. Dizziness. Headache. Lice. Menses, too early. Memory, weak. Miscarriage. Sleeplessness.

HERBAL - Rosemary oil has an ancient reputation as a remedy for baldness, headache and flagging mental powers. It has been called the “Herb of Memory,” which Shakespeare alludes to when he has Ophelia say, “There’s Rosemary, that’s for remembrance.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Memory deficient. Head heavy, drowsy. Menses too early, violent pains followed by uterine hemorrhage. Chilly with icy coldness of lower limbs without thirst, followed by heat. MIND - Anxiety. Memory weak. Dullness.

Head - Headache. Heaviness and dullness of head. Weight and tension around head. Baldness. Lungs - Oppression of breathing. Spasms in chest.

Female - Violent pains followed by uterine hemorrhage and miscarriage, succeeded by faintness, spasms of chest, cold hands and feet, small, rapid, irregular pulse. Menses four days too early.

Sleep - Overpowering sleepiness with yawning. Sleeplessness.

Skin - Hair loss. Dandruff. Lice.

Temperature - Coldness so that she could not leave the bed. Chill over whole, legs icy cold, no thirst and no subsequent heat. Vertigo - Dizziness. COMMENTS - The most violent of the symptoms of Rosm. were observed on a woman who took a strong infusion for eight days resulting in a miscarriage. In another woman, it brought on the menses four days too soon. Chilliness predominated, the chill not being followed by heat. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Hedeo., Menth., Puls. REFERENCES - Clarke.

HERBAL - Blackberry is also known by the common names brambleberry, dewberry, and cloudberry. The berry grows on small, bushy vines, each berry being a cluster of tiny black knobs. In England, they are often referred to as brambleberries because of the prickly thorns, or brambles. It is astringent, tonic, mild diuretic, and hemostatic. The fruit and juice is considered a refrigerant and tonic. The root-bark and the leaves are strongly astringent, depurative, diuretic, tonic and vulnerary. Blackberry leaf is more specific to the stomach and intestines. The fruit is more specific to liver and kidneys. The root is the most astringent part. It has been used as a preventative for dropsy. It makes an excellent remedy for diarrhea, hemorrhoids, and cystitis. The root-bark as well as the dried and powdered fruit have been used for dysentery. Extract of the root has been used for stomach problems as well as an antidote to poison. In American folk medicine the root was also used for tonsillitis. It has been used as an anti-inflammatory for conditions such as laryngitis and pharyngitis. The root decoction was once used during the spasmodic phase of whooping cough. A decoction of the root has been used for lung problems in general, as well as amenorrhea. Medicinally, the leaf of the Blackberry is most often used. The white underside of the leaves was said to “draw” while the smooth green upper side was said to “soothe.” The leaves, root, and root bark have been used for inflammation of the throat, mouth and gums (also bleeding gums), as well as hemorrhoids and leucorrhea. The leaves were used in England for burns and scalds. Blackberry leaves were also used as a poultice for wounds and insect bites, and as a wash for oily skin. Blackberry leaves have been made into a tea to ease the discomfort of sore throat. It has also been used internally to loosen phlegm. The leaves were chewed to treat bleeding gums and mouth sores. Blackberry leaf tea was used as a gargle to treat sore throats, mouth ulcers and gum inflammations. A strong tea of the leaves has been used externally for eczema. Another method was to soak leaves in hot wine to make an infusion, then placing a cloth dipped in the liquid on the ulcerations morning and evening. A decoction of the leaves was once used as a fomentation for ulcerations. Blackberry leaves have also been used to inhibit excessive menstrual bleeding. Blackberry tea made from the roots was a remedy for pregnant woman who were in danger of miscarrying due to overwork. The leaves have been used as a uterine tonic. Blackberry tea, made of the scrapings of the bark of the branches, was used for bronchial infections. As a poultice, it was used to treat pneumonia. Boiled vines, roots, and berries for a drink for those vomiting and spitting blood. Boiled the cane to use as a diuretic and used a root tea for diarrhea. The fruit and juice have been used for anemia and to regulate menses. The flowers and fruit were once used for venomous bites and the young shoots eaten to tighten loose teeth. The ancient Greeks used blackberries to treat gout, mouth infl animation, and bowel inflammation. Blackberry was believed useful for appendicitis. Steeped berries in water was drunk as a vermifuge. European settlers to North America used blackberry jam to remedy diarrhea. Blackberry jelly was an English folk remedy for swelling of the limbs (especially those associated with heart problems). The jelly was added to apple cider vinegar and used as a compress. Blackberry glycerite was also used as a compress on swollen joints. COMMENTS - The common name blackberry also includes the species Rubus villosus. Rubis lacinniatus, Rubus procerus, and other Rubus species, which are used interchangeably with Rubus fructicosus. The primary constituents of this herb include tannins, gallic acid, villosin, and iron. The fruit portion contains vitamin C, niacin, pectin, sugars, anthocyanins, and flavonoids (kaempferol, quercitin). The tannin content of blackberry leaves makes it an effective astringent. It also has diuretic properties. The tannins in blackberries also contribute to the plant’s ability to treat diarrhea and dysentery, as well as to constrict blood vessels, which inhibits bleeding. REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Ruby
author: Murphy
constitution: Allergies. Anemia. Anger. Angina. Belching. Blood, disorders. Circulation, weak. Constipation. Cough. Debility. Diarrhea. Earache. Flatulence. Heart, disorders. Heartburn. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Hepatitis. High blood pressure. Immune, disorders. Infections. Leucorrhea. Migraine. Nausea. Nosebleed. Palpitations. Vomiting. Wounds.
keynote:

CLINICAL - Allergies. Anemia. Anger. Angina. Belching. Blood, disorders. Circulation, weak. Constipation. Cough. Debility. Diarrhea. Earache. Flatulence. Heart, disorders. Heartburn. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids.…
full:
PHARMACY - ruby. Ruby. Gemstone. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Anemia. Anger. Angina. Belching. Blood, disorders. Circulation, weak. Constipation. Cough. Debility. Diarrhea. Earache. Flatulence. Heart, disorders. Heartburn. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Hepatitis. High blood pressure. Immune, disorders. Infections. Leucorrhea. Migraine. Nausea. Nosebleed. Palpitations. Vomiting. Wounds.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ruby has an affinity for the blood, immune system, heart and circulation. It is a blood cleanser, blood tonic. Wounds, stab or lacerations. Hemorrhages. Encourages speedy coagulation. Anti-septic properties. For the after-effects of bacterial and viral infections. Chronic fatigue and all states of debility. Poor vitality due to liver dysfunction. Chilliness, affecting one side of the body, generally the right. Patches of cold, especially if they are felt to move around the body. Affinity for children and adolescents and for those from the Indian sub-continent and Southeast Asia. MIND - Clear mind, sensation of energy breaking free all over body. Mental and physical clutter. Mental blankness with an inability to focus one’s ideas or thoughts. Forgetful. Cannot remember details. Fastidious. Feels isolated. Helps to restore a sense of self-worth (Aur.). Feeling of unworthiness due to the recognition of how much worse off are others, while feeling that there is nothing that can be done to redress the balance. Sense of being consumed by worldly events or by family emotions. Inability to let go of emotions. Guilt and shame. Resentment. Confused and distressing thoughts. Escapist daydreaming. Anger comes up in outbursts. Anger that is expressed inappropriately. Suppressed anger (Staph.). Anger associated with sexual frustration. Vehemence and intolerance. Impatience with slowness and poor articulation of expression. Teenage anger. Anticipation. Shaking or trembling with fear. Fear of new situations. Fear of the dark. Fear of one’s own dark side, of being in someone else’s power. Fear of death, of being sacrificed.

Head - Head pain started at left front and moved to the back of my head. Migraines with nausea and vomiting, especially when the liver is involved. Pain from the cervical area and up and over the head to the forehead. Compression down the back from the head and neck. Sensation of pushing down on the vertex or of pushing inwards. Head feels split. Hair fuller, thicker, healthier and stronger. Hair feels dry. Cannot detangle hair at nape of neck.

Eyes - Pupils dilated, eyes were very wild and maniacal looking. Bloodshot and glassy, red and dry. Eyes tired and burning, itching. Pain in the corner of the right eye as if stabbed by a finger. Heavy eyelids, burning sensation.

Ears - Aching pain in left ear, with fullness like earache. Ears feel full. Hearing not registering. Heightened sense of hearing, all sounds are so clear.

Nose - Middle separation of nostrils is sore to touch. Rawness in nose and throat came and went, itchy and dry. Nose very wet and damp in the morning. Pain at the root of the nose as if it is blocked. Nose plugged, crusted, hard. Nose mucousy, tight without discharge. Intermittent sneezing, relieves. Sneezing, nose is running, like allergies or hay fever. Profuse nosebleeds. Sensitivity to smells, especially vinegar and beer. Everything smells different.

Face - Face puffy. Tingly cheeks. Face grayish with blemishes, irritated.

Mouth - Taste somewhat enhanced. Food tastes funny. Burning, dryness on sides of tongue. Pain under left side of tongue,, at the root, could be felt even exteriorly. Sore under tongue, behind teeth, very painful. Sores on inside of lip, on lower gums. Swollen gums.

Throat - Heat around esophagus, in morning, with heat in chest and pressure. Burning esophagus. Closing up. Rawness in throat and nose, came and went, itchy, dry. Instantly dry throat. Throbbing sore throat. Sore throat, tight and dry, mild headache, sneezy, running nose. Wakes with slight dryness in back of throat, full ears.

Stomach - Digestion sluggish. Sensation of a stone in the stomach. Heaviness in the upper abdomen. Empty pit feeling. Bloating, both flatulence and flatus. Constant heartburn. Belching to the point of interrupting conversation. Burping loudly, involuntary, repeatedly. Foamy belching. Constant nausea. Empty, nauseous feeling. Nausea, not from stomach but umbilicus. Morning sickness. Cancer.

Abdomen - Ache in epigastrium. Epigastrial discomfort, as though the lateral edges of the muscles contract in towards each other, better with massage. Ache in left hypochondrium. Pain in right hypochondrium. Fullness and heaviness in lower abdomen. Sharp tweaks in lower abdomen, right side (psoas muscle), constant heaviness like pressing down. Mild cramping in lower abdomen, comes straight up midline. Bloating more than usual. Foul gas, nimbly (not painful), very bloated lower abdomen. Loud, painless gurgling in stomach. Reduction in abdominal gas.

Rectum - No bowel activity. Constipation. Diarrhea, explosive, loose, watery, painless. Gassy diarrhea, gassy expulsion. Bouts of loose stool with sudden urge (9 a.m. to noon). Small stool with urination. Foul gas, nimbly, painless. Blood from the hemorrhoids with each stool. Prolapsed old hemorrhoids.

Stool - Diarrhea, explosive, loose, watery, painless. Defecate with expulsion, gassy diarrhea, gassy expulsion. Five bouts of loose stool with sudden urge. Small, dry stools with blood.

Urine - Smells acidic, like acidosis. Vertigo - Some vertigo and weakness in the sun. Dizzy feeling when stands up, like wavering in a clockwise motion. COMMENTS - Ruby is one variant of the simple mineral corundum, the other is sapphire. Corundum is a compound of aluminum and oxygen, AL2 03 (aluminum oxide). Chromium is responsible for the color of ruby, while iron, titanium and other elements cause the coloration of sapphires. The name “corundum” is derived from the Sanskrit word “kuruvinda” via the Tamil name for ruby, “kuruntam.” The name “ruby” comes from the Latin word for red, “ruber.” Sluggish system with low energy. Circulation feels dull and weak. Heavy feeling, body heavy like lead, heaviness, hard to exercise. All over tiredness. Felt need to lie down, fighting gravity. Very tired in the evening, barely made it to bed. Hungover or fluish feeling. No desire to exercise. Better as day goes on. Weight gain. Body warm all over. Cooler temperature. Goosebumps on upper arms and thighs. Tingling all over body. Sensation as if air were passing through certain areas of the body. All senses acute. Left ear painful with dull ache, ear fullness. RELATIONS - Compare: Amber, Staph., Ferr. REFERENCES - Murphy.

Male - Anger associated with sexual frustration. High sexual energy. Not interested in sex.

Female - Labia feels swollen and itchy. Vaginal discharge yellow and curdsy. Leucorrhea, yellow, lumpy, and not itchy. Early sexual awareness. Increased desire. High sexual energy. Uses sex as a way of avoiding hidden emotions. Decreased or absent sexual desire. Food - Appetite diminished, not hungry. Appetite increased, very hungry, wakes hungry. Thirsty. More thirstless than usual. Craving meat, salty food, fatty foods, bread.

Chest - Heat in chest and pressure in the morning, around esophagus, centrally located. Heavy constricted chest, all day belching and heartburn, need to burp feeling, know it will taste bad. Dull pain in heart region, lasted several minutes. Circulation feels dull.

Heart - Heart disorders. High blood pressure. Compression of the cardiac area. Pain in heart, seized up, sharp constriction for five minutes. Pain behind the sternum as if a heart attack would come on. Angina. Palpitations.

Back - Pain in lower sacral, right side. Bladder - Frequent urination.

Limbs - Right side feels alive while the left side feels dead. Tingling in the legs. Fidgety and restless. Pins and needles in the right leg. Itching and aching in the right leg. Tweak in right hip. Feet and legs are cold. Goosebumps on upper arms and thighs. Poison oak like rash between wrist and elbow, itching and oozing. Mark on right arm (the underside in the middle of forearm which itches on occasion). Backs of the hands feel itchy. Nails healthier and stronger.

Sleep - Deep sleep. Sleep interrupted, woke often beginning at 2 a.m. then 3 a.m., 4 a.m. Awoke unrefreshed, feeling almost drugged, hard to open eyes. Groggy in morning. Sleepy in the morning. Difficult getting up. Nap in the afternoon, did not feel good from nap. Can’t get enough sleep.

Skin - Flushed, mottled skin. Itching rash, especially on buttocks. Itchy all over, better with scratching.

Teeth - Grinding teeth. Hard to floss, teeth are tight.

Liver - Useful after hepatitis when the body is weakened and cannot restore itself to full strength. Lungs - Cough in the middle of the night. Dry, gagging cough, with thick phlegm. Wakes with choking cough.

Blood - Anemia. Blood disorders. Immune disorders.

Perspiration - Body sweaty, unusual. Sweating at peak of anxiety attack. Sweats all night long. Hot and sweaty had to take covers off. Apple-like smell coming off body.

HERBAL - Sorrel was at one time cultivated as…
full:
PHARMACY - rumx-a. Rumex acetosa. Sorrel. N. O. Polygonacae. Tincture of the leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Convulsions. Esophagus inflammation. Gastritis. Paralysis. Throat, sore. Uvula, elongated.

HERBAL - Sorrel was at one time cultivated as a salad. The Buckler-shaped or French Sorrel is cultivated in France, where it is considered a powerful anti-scorbutic. The leaves contain a large quantity of Bin oxalate of Potash (Kali-ox.).

HOMEOPATHIC - The Rumx-a. symptoms were observed on three men who ate largely of the leaves. In one, very violent convulsions were induced of a peculiar kind, the limbs being thrown reciprocally backwards and forwards and the head from side to side. The hands being alternately clenched and unclenched, the eyes prominent. Other remarkable symptoms included swelling of the lower eyelid. Elongated uvula. Pain all down esophagus worse by swallowing. Persistent short, dry cough. Complete paralysis of bodily powers, copious green vomit, constipation. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kali-ox., Lapa. (2) In persistent cough, Rumx. REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Rumex Crispus
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from covering mouth. Better wrapping up, lying on right side. Better from discharge of offensive flatus. Worse weather change, warm to cold, cold to warm. Worse from cool air, inhaling, open air. Worse deep or irregular breathing. Worse uncovering. Worse motion, riding, lying on left side. Worse from pressure on trachea, talking. Worse eating, after meals. Worse evening and night, morning, on waking. Worse 3:30 p.m., 11 p.m., 2 a.m. to 5 a.m..

full:
PHARMACY - rumx. Rumex crispus. Yellow dock. Curly dock. Sour dock. Narrow dock. N. O. Polygonaceae. Tincture of ftesh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abortion. Acne. Anemia. Aphonia. Asthma. Botborygm.Bronchitis. Catarrh. Coms. Coryza. Coughs. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Dyspnea. Feet, tender. Flatulence. Gastralgia. Headache. Heart, disorders. Heartbum. Hiccough. Indigestion. Irritation. Jaundice. Lichen. Miscarriage. Mouth, ulceration. Nausea. Nosebleeds. Phimosis. Prurigo. Rheumatism. Throat, sore. Trachea, disorders. Tuberculosis. Urticaria.

HERBAL - Rumex is an old Latin word for “lance,” referring to the shape of the leaves. Crispus means “curly,” also in reference to the leaf shape. The yellow dock or curly dock is a common British weed, a member of the buckwheat family. It grows abundantly throughout North America. The common yellow dock includes the species Rumex occidentalis, Rumex venosus, Rumex obtusifolius and Rumex sangineus, which are used interchangeably with Rumex crispus. The common dock of fields and roadsides, Rumex obtusifolia has a well deserved reputation among children as the best antidote to the nettle’s sting. Rumex crispus, according to Joslin, was used by herbalists internally and externally for the cure of scabies. Yellow dock has been used for hundreds of years for its astringent properties, treating a variety of skin problems, including boils, rashes, blemishes and burns. Topically, the crushed leaf of yellow dock can soothe the stings from nettle plants. It can also be added to a tooth powder for spongy gums, and to a gargle for laryngitis. Salves, poultices or compresses of this herb have been used for eczema, hives, itchy skin, scabies and ringworm. The properties of this herb are alterative, laxative, purgative, cholagogue, and astringent. It has been used for nutritional support of the blood, lungs, and urinary system. Yellow dock is valued today as one of the best available sources of iron. Its high iron content makes it beneficial for treating anemia and pregnant women. Yellow dock has also been known to help improve bladder and liver functions, and reduce bowel inflammation and glandular swelling. This herb can be used to treat some cases of jaundice, and skin eruptions associated with the toxicity of the intestines.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hale noted that among the constituents and salts of Rumx. are Sulph. and Calc-p., and Sulph., Calc, and Phos. are strongly represented in its action. Rumx. is a close ally of Rheum and has analogous purgative and other properties. The provings were made by Houghton, Joslin, Paine, Bayard, Rhees and Co., both with the tincture and potencies, and its characteristics were well defined. Dry, hacking, tickling cough (Bry.). Constant tickling in the pit of the throat, runs into bronchi. Trachea sore to external pressure, feels excoriated, as do the fauces. Lump sensation in the throat that descends and comes back up after they swallow. Cough is excited by pressure on throat. Touching the throat brings on the cough. Violent cough with a scanty difficult expectoration. Rattling cough. Coughing as if a piece of phlegm is stuck in chest. Cough caused by an incessant tickling in the throat, tickling runs down to the bifurcation of the bronchial tubes. Cough, worsefrom the least cold air or uncovering. Cough ceases by covering the body and head with bedclothes. Marked action on the skin, producing an intense itching. Numerous and varied pains, neither fixed nor constant. Sharp pains, neuralgias. Acts on joints, especially ankles, the skin, left side, chest. Cold affects the joints. Obesity. Rumx. diminishes the secretions of mucus membranes and at the same time exalts sensibility of the mucus membranes of the larynx and trachea. Dry and sensitive mucus membranes. Mucus secretions decrease causing stickiness with burning. Lymphatics are enlarged and secretions perverted. MIND - Disinclination to mental exertion. Indifferent about his surroundings. Restlessness in evening. Patient refuses to speak or even listen to conversation, lest his attentio.i should be withdrawn from the supervision of his respiratory acts. Low spirited with serious expression of the face. Suicidal mood. Feels like killing herself in despair.

Head - Headache after waking in morning. Headache and nausea after eating. Catarrhal headache with great irritation of larynx and trachea. Darting or sharp piercing pains, in left side. Bruised feeling in forehead. Dull feeling in head Rumex crispus during cough.

Eyes - Burning indoors, puffed up in morning. Pain in eyes as from dryness, lids inflamed, worse evening. Sore feeling in eyes without inflammation. Deep-seated pain in right eye. Sharp, shooting pain in left eye. Lachrymation when yawning.

Ears - Ringing in ears. Itching deep in ears. Pain, throbbing, stopped sensation in ears.

Nose - Nose obstructed, dry sensation in posterior sinuses. Copious mucus discharge from nose and trachea. Yellow mucus from posterior nares. Sneezing attacks, fluent coryza. Violent sneezing and painful irritation of nostrils. Itching that extends from the end of the nose to pharynx. Desire to pick nose. Nosebleed.

Face - Sodden complexion. Pale, while standing. Pain in right jaw, morning.

Mouth - Bitter taste in morning. Dry tongue and mouth. Tongue sore at edges, coated. Tongue feels as if burned. Tongue coated yellowish-brown or reddish-brown. Toothache, entirely better after dinner, rinsing mouth with cold water. Toothache with acute colds. Ulceration of mouth and throat.

Throat - Throat feels hollow. Rawness of larynx and trachea. Hawks much tenacious mucus. Lump, not better by hawking, descends and rises again after swallowing. Irritation in larynx when eating, causes cough. COMMENTS -Guernsey described the cough of Rumex as a “cough caused by an incessant tickling in throat- pit, which tickling runs down to the bifurcation of the bronchial tubes touching the throat brings on the cough, by covering up all the body and head with the bed-clothes there is no cough.” Shakes head as if it would fly to pieces and chest so that he feels he might raise blood any minute. Exhausting paroxysms, rapid coughing spells (Coc-c., Cor-r.). Coughing if the hands get cold. Headache during cough. Cough causes expulsion of urine and it may even cause expulsion of the fetus in pregnant women. Palliates late stage tuberculosis (Phos., Ph-ac., Stann.). Cold air and drafts bring on coughing spells, as well as itching and skin aggravations. Characteristic sensitivity to cold air. The cough and skin symptoms are worse by uncovering or exposure to air. Wants to be covered (Hep.). Worse from change of weather, temperature, talking with cough, eating. Worse motion, lying on the left (Phos.). Worse touching the throat. Irritated by irregular or deep breathing. Coughing worse at night around 11 p.m., and from 2-4 a.m. Flu with a dry, hacking cough. Dryness of the nose and throat. Tendency to colds easily, with cough. Asthmatic cough, allergic asthma with constriction and a hacking, tickling cough. Allergies with more coughing than sneezing, with a runny nose. Irritation of the nose. Burning, smarting, rawness in nasal passages (Caust.). Rapid sneezing. Severe sinus headaches, especially when the discharge dries up. Thick, white discharges deep in the lungs or in the sinuses. Mucus or dryness alternating with total obstruction of thick mucus. Catarrh of the nose, eyes and chest that is gluey, thick, white, gelatinous, ropy and lumpy (Ant- t.). Nosebleeds from hawking. Lachrymation of the eyes. Aphonia, aphasia. Hoarseness and change of voice (Spong.). Toothache, worse from inhaling cold air, may be better from cold drinks. Raw, burning sensation on inhaling. Disturbed circulation. Violent palpitations of the heart and throbbing throughout the whole body. Itching with burning, worse scratching, after bathing (Sulph.). Skin is worse being uncovered (Hep.). Scabies with severe itching. Eczema with small, red pimples. Itching without eruptions (Spong., Alum., Sulph.). Sensation of weight in stomach. Borbo- rygmi, particularly on the left. Flatulence and rumbling. Diarrhea in the early morning, driving the patient out of bed. Morning diarrhea, brown, watery, offensive. Diarrhea after catarrh, often associated with a cough. Sadness and aversion to work, with irritability. Restless, sleep with vivid dreams, especially when the cough wakes them. Dreams of danger and robbers. Can wake up coughing or with diarrhea. Paine noted a particular symptoms that led to many cures of skin cases where exposure to air is the exciting cause, “while undressing and for some time after, considerable inching of surface of lower limbs.” P. P. Wells related the case of Mrs. X., who had eight miscarriages all in the early months of pregnancy. Each miscarriage was attended with a severe dry, shaking, spasmodic cough in violent attacks. This was regarded as the cause of the miscarriages. At the beginning of the ninth pregnancy she came under homeopathic treatment. The cough came on very dry, harsh, loud, shaking, worse at night, preventing sleep, excited instantly by pressure on the trachea. Rumx. 30c promptly relieved. Wells also cured with Rumx. 200c a cough in a man that began with tickling behind top of sternum, sometimes in paroxysms lasting for five to ten minutes. Joslin pointed out the left chest had more verified symptoms than any other region. Conditions are worse lying on left side, better lying on right side. Worse at 11 p.m. and 4 a.m. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Bell., Hyos.,Con., Lach., Phos. Compare: ( 1 ) Caust., Sulph., Bell., (2) Rumx. contains chrysophanic acid to which the skin stitches correspond. (3) Rumx-a. - Sheep sorrel - Gathered in June and dried, used locally for Epithelioma of face. Dry, unremitting short cough and violent pains in bowels, uvula elongated inflammation of esophagus, also cancer. (4) Rumex obtusifolius - Broadleaf dock - nosebleed and headache following, pain in kidneys, leucorrhea. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Tight, suffocative, heavy ache in epigastrium to back, clothes feel tight. Chronic gastritis, aching pain in pit of stomach and shooting in the chest, extends towards the throat, worse any motion or talking. Hiccough, heartburn. Nausea, better by belchings. Eating meat causes belching and itching.

Abdomen - Annoying rumbling flatulence in women. Flatulence. Flatulent abdominal colic soon after a meal. Creeping near navel better by discharge of offensive flatus.

Rectum - Brown, watery diarrhea, early in morning with cough, driving him out of bed. Sudden, profuse, foul, painless, brown, black or thin, watery stools. Itching of anus with sensation as of a stick in rectum. Hemorrhoids. Valuable in late stage tuberculosis (Seneg., Puls., Lyc., Ars.). Sensations - Eyes pain as if from dryness. Tongue as if burned. As if cough did not reach low enough to raise phlegm. Lump in throat, it descends on deglutition, but immediately returns. Hands cold when coughing. As if head would fly to pieces with cough. As if he might raise blood any minute. Hard substance in pit of stomach. As if heart suddenly stopped. Pressure of a stick in rectum.

Male - Tendency to phimosis. In evening, feeling of soreness and excoriation with redness of end of prepuce. Itching of prepuce. Sexual desire diminished, lost.

Female - Pain from right ovary to back. Tendency to miscarriages, in early stage of pregnancy (Sep.). Miscarriage with dry, shaking, spasmodic cough, in paroxysms of great violence. Food - Ravenous appetite. Worse when eating and after meals. Worse after excessive use of alcohol. Gastric disturbances, from tea drinking. Can’t eat meat, it causes eructations, pruritus. Worse from apples.

Chest - Pain under sternum, under right nipple. Pain in left side of chest after meals with flatulence. Burning, sticking pain in left chest near the heart, worse deep breathing. Rawness or burning under clavicle as if the air penetrated there, worse hawking. Clavicular pain, worse hawking. Soreness behind sternum, especially left side in region of left shoulder. Constitutions - Tubercular or nervous constitutions.

Heart - Feels as if suddenly stopped, followed by heavy throbbing through the chest.

Back - Pain under scapulae, right. Breasts - Pain in the left breast after meals.

Limbs - Pain in left shoulder on coughing, on raising arms. Hands cold when coughing. Spasmodic cramps in ankles and feet.

Sleep - Sudden sleepiness. Sleep disturbed, wakeful, restless, short naps and unpleasant fancies, even when awake. Unpleasant dreams of danger and trouble.

Skin - Acne vulgaris on back. Intense itching of skin, especially of lower limbs, worse exposure to cold air or when undressing. Urticaria, contagious prurigo. Jaundice after excessive use of alcohol.

Modalities - Better from covering mouth. Better wrapping up, lying on right side. Better from discharge of offensive flatus. Worse weather change, warm to cold, cold to warm. Worse from cool air, inhaling, open air. Worse deep or irregular breathing. Worse uncovering. Worse motion, riding, lying on left side. Worse from pressure on trachea, talking. Worse eating, after meals. Worse evening and night, morning, on waking. Worse 3:30 p.m., 11 p.m., 2 a.m. to 5 a.m.

Teeth - Pain in teeth of both sides, morning. Toothache better after eating dinner, better by rinsing with cold water.

Liver - Jaundice after excessive use of alcohol. Lungs - Dyspnea on retiring. Better closing the mouth or covering the head. Breathing worse in wind. Asthma. Copious mucus discharge from nose and trachea. Profuse, frothy, thin expectoration, stringy and tough, by the mouthful.

Kidneys - Sudden urging, involuntary with cough. Copious, colorless urine in afternoon. Urine less copious, flocculent deposit, oily surface, marked brick-dust sediment.

Cough - Suffocative choking coughs. Tickling in throat causes cough. Dry, tickling cough, preventing sleep. Barking cough. Cough worse by pressure, talking, lying on left side, inspiring cool air and at night. Cough provoked by changing rooms. Cough by change from cold to warm and warm to cold. Cough from uncovering, drafts. Cough comes regularly at 11 p.m., 2 a.m. and 5 a.m., in children. Continuous coughing. Cough in the daytime only. Cough worse during early pregnancy, may cause miscarriage.

Temperature - Sweat on waking from a sound sleep.

full:
PHARMACY - russ. Russula foetens. N. O. Fungi. Tincture of the fresh mushrooms. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bedwetting. Blindness. Chorea. Coma. Convulsions. Cyanosis. Dyspnea. Spasms. Tremors.

HERBAL - Some species of Russula are edible and are much esteemed as a food.

HOMEOPATHIC - Alphonse Barrelet observed the effects of eating cooked Russula foetens, which produced a very severe poisoning. Russ, has produced hallucinations, muscular tremors and clonic spasms recall the effects of Agar. The eye symptoms were even more pronounced, complete blindness lasting many days occurred with this peculiarity of the pupil, that it was sometimes normal, sometimes dilated and sometimes contracted. Constant trembling of muscles, at times interrupted by tonic contractions increasing to general clonic spasms with complete loss of consciousness. Muscular spasms, deathly anxiety, dyspnea. Patient recovered after two or three weeks. MIND - Hallucinations constant for three days after spasms ceased. Unconsciousness. Deathly anxiety.

Eyes - Pupils at one time normal, at another time dilated, at another contracted. Consciousness returned on third day, patient could hear but was completely blind.

Face - Cyanosis.

Abdomen - Nausea, colic, vomiting, diarrhea, with cold limbs.

Skin - The attack was followed by pseudoerysipelas on elbows and painless furuncles over whole body, especially on scapulae and small of back. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Kidneys - Involuntary urination. Lungs - Dyspnea.

Pulse - Pulse small and contracted.

name: Ruta Graveolens
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from lying on back. Better warmth, motion, rubbing, scratching. Worse from overexertion, lifting, injury, sprains. Worse exertion, ascending or descending stairs. Worse lying down, sitting, stooping. Worse eyestrain, reading. Worse pressure on an edge. Worse from cold air, damp, wind, wet. Worse during menses. Worse from uncooked Ruta graveolens or indigestible food. Warm stove causes chilliness..

full:
PHARMACY - ruta. Ruta graveolens. Garden rue. Bitterwort. N. O. Rutaceae. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Anus, prolapse. Arthritis. Asthenopia. Backache. Bedwetting. Bone, bruised. Bruises. Bursitis. Cancer. Carpal tunnel Cartilages, bruises, pains. Chest, pains. Constipation. Dislocated, joints. Dyspepsia. Exostosis. Eye-strain. Facial paralysis. Fevers. Fractures. Ganglions. Hemorrhages. Hands, pains. Injuries. Joint, injuries. Lameness. Nosebleeds. Paralysis. Perichondritis. Periostitis. Rectum, cancer. Rectum, prolapsed. Restlessness. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Spleen, disorders. Sprains. Stammering. Strains. Tendonitis. Tongue, swelling. Urination, difficulty. Varicocele. Veins, swollen, varicose. Vision, weak. Warts.

HERBAL - The common rue is a native of southern Europe. Teste noted that it was formerly in great repute in medicine for epilepsy, hysteria, hydrophobia and weakness of sight from excessive reading. Ozaena, nosebleed, foul gumboils, flatulent colic, and inertia of the bowels have been cured with it empirically. Teste added that Ruta graveolens was supposed to be a kind of universal antidote, “Even in our own time the Roman ladies imagine that the most odoriferous flowers may be left in their rooms without the least danger provided a bush of garden rue be amongst them.” Practitioners have perhaps been deterred from employing it by the symptoms of acrid- narcotic poisoning induced by an overdose. It is noted, in The Treasury of Botany, that locally applied rue is a powerful irritant and one species, Ruta montana, is dangerous to handle even with gloves Green’s Herbal mentioned that Ruta is “useful in feverish complaints, promotes perspiration and removes noxious material in headache, nervous and hysteric complaints, weakness of the stomach and pains in the bowels, suppressed menses and if taken for a long time it benefits epilepsy. The expressed juice benefits nightmare.” M. Helie indicated that, in large doses, it causes violent gastric pains, excessive and sometimes bloody vomiting, profuse salivation and swelling of the tongue. Great prostration and confusion of the mind. Convulsive twitchings and, in pregnant women, miscarriage.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hahnemann’s proving showed how largely the old uses were founded on a homeopathic relationship. The vulnerary remedies indicate in symptoms of their provings the peculiar form of injuries for which they are adapted. Like the sprained pains of Rhus-t. and the bruised pains (in skin and muscles) of Arn., Ruta also has bruised pains, but these are more particularly manifested in bones. Historically, it was used to ward off plague. Affinity for fibrous tissue, flexor tendons, joints, ankles, wrists, cartilages, periosteum, uterus and skin. Acts upon the eyes and uterus. Eyestrain. Overstrain of ocular muscles. Jaundice. For injured joints, tendons, bones and especially bruised bones. Rheumatism. Tendonitis. Formation of deposits or nodes in the periosteum, tendons and about the joints especially wrists. Brittle bones. Lain on parts become sore, even in bed. The pains are bruised, sore, aching with restlessness, a feeling of intense, painful weariness. Lameness after sprains. Sprains with weakness in joint (Arn.). Complaints from straining flexor tendons especially. All parts of the body are painful, as if bruised. Heaviness, as of a weight in forehead or hanging to feet or lower limbs. As of a rough blunt plug in part, head, nose etc. Paralytic rigidity. Distortions. Grating, burning pains, neuralgia. MIND - Stupefaction. Thought and comprehension slow. Feeling of intense lassitude, weakness and despair. Indifference. Disinclined to work. Quarrels and contradicts. Inclined to anger and vexation. Morose, peevish, fretful. Disposed to weep. Frequent anxiety, with despondent thoughts and fear. Fear of death during fever. Anxious restlessness. Anxious all day, as though he had done something wrong. Fear that someone will come to arrest him. Melancholy, dissatisfied with life, and sad. Dissatisfied with himself and others. Mistrustful. Suspicious, imagines that he is always being deceived. Delusion someone is behind him. Starting from sleep from slightest touch. Desire for light.

Head - Heat in head, with anxious restlessness. Headachefrom eye-strain. Stitches, worse reading. Aches as if a nail is driven into it. Pain as from a nail after excessive intoxicating drinks. Pressure over eyebrow. Pulsative, pressive, in forehead. Head externally painful, as if bruised or beaten. Periosteum sore. Erysipelas and swelling of forehead. Erysipelas of scalp, arising from wounds. Corrosive itching on scalp. Humid scabs on head.

Eyes - Amblyopia. Asthenopia. Weakness of ciliary muscles. Spots on cornea. Eyes burn like fire. Lachrymation in open air, not indoors. Pressure deep in orbits. Eyestrain with headaches. Weary pain while reading. Red, hot and painful from reading fine print, sewing (Nat-m., Arg- n.). Itching inner canthi. Tarsal cartilage feels bruised. Spasm in lower eyelids, when it ceases, lachrymation starts. Pressure over eyebrow.

Ears - Earache with scraping pressure. Itching lancinations in ear. Cartilages of ears as if bruised. Pain in ear and under mastoid process as from a bruise. Pain as from a blunt piece of wood.

Nose - Pressive, hard aching at the root of nose, with nosebleed. Perspiration on back of nose.

Face - Acne. Acne rosacea. Eruption of pimples on lips. Lips dry and sticky. Pain as if bruised in periosteum of facial bones. Spasmodic tearing in cheekbone. Itching and gnawing at face and on cheeks. Coldness beneath left eye. Erysipelas in forehead with swelling. Facial paralysis after catching cold.

Mouth - Woody taste. Dryness in mouth and throat. Mouth dry and glutinous. Profuse salivation and swelling of tongue. Cramp in tongue, causing embarrassment of speech. Boring pains in lower teeth. Gums bleed easily.

Throat - Sensation as if a lump in throat on empty swallowing. Larynx as if bruised. Vertigo - Whirling vertigo, which causes falling when rising in morning. Vertigo when seated, when walking in open air. Vision - Amblyopia dependent upon anomalies of refraction. Amblyopia from writing by artificial light. Disturbances of accommodation. Obscuration of vision as if one had looked too long and intently at an object. Blurred vision with burning, aching in eyes and strained feeling. Blurred vision from fine sewing, reading too much, worse using eyes in evening. Letters seem to run together. Dim vision, as if a shadow were flitting before objects. Green circle around light in evening. COMMENTS - The vulnerary power of Ruta does not appear to have been known before the provings were made, but an old use of the remedy for impaired sight due to eyestrain, corresponded to symptoms from the provings. “His eyes feel as if he had strained the sight too much by reading,” “weak, pressive-like pain in right eye with dimness of surrounding objects, as if from having looked too long at an objects that was fatiguing to the eyes,” “a feeling of heat and burning in the eyes and pain in them when he reads (in the evening and by candle-light).” Eyestrain, with burning and itching in the eyes. Eyestrain headaches (Onos.). Blurry vision. Contracted pupil. Eyeballs ache. Paralysis of the eye muscles and neuralgias. Facial paralysis from catching cold in robust, sanguine persons. Rheumatic paralysis of wrists and ankles. Affinity forthe joints, especially the tendons and ligaments. Joints feel weak and bruised. Chronic weakness and inflammation. Structural abnormalities. Torn or overstretched ligaments. Often ahistory of injury, remaining weakness in injured spot. Often follows or is complementary to Rhus-t. Twisting injuries to the spine (Arn., Hyper., Rhus-t.). Wrenching injuries. Injuries to the shin and face. Injuries that are close to the bone. Bone injuries with tom ligaments, muscles or nerves (Am., Calc-p., Symph.). Hard lump after injury (Am.). Ovemse of joints, particularly the wrists. Dislocated joints, or the tendency to dislocate. Weak ligaments or joints. Carpal tunnel syndrome (Caust.). Shooting pain in wrist (Rhus-t., Hyper.). Chronic shortening of tendon due to ovemse. Fibrositis. Bursitis, tendonitis, from overuse. Chronic knee complaints. Frozen shoulder. Thickening of the periosteum or nodules after injury (Bellis). Stiff and aching (Am., Rhus-t.). Sharp pains (Hyper.). Deep, grinding pain. Sharp, tearing nerve pain. Drawing pain, as if area is being pulled shorter. Feeling of lameness ever since injury. Worse sitting or lying down. Chronic weakness after an injury. Gnawing, grinding pains, especially in the shoulder. Pain worse in cold, damp weather. Stiffness, worse in the morning, better from motion and heat (Rhus-t.). Coldness down the spine, leg or sciatic nerve. Tearing pain down the sciatic nerve. Great weakness, pain in limbs after a short walk. Limbs feel bmised, pain in small of back and loins. Tottering as if thighs were weak. Uneasiness and heaviness in legs, difficultly finding a comfortable position. All parts of the body on which he lies, even in bed, are painful as if bruised. Restlessness. Sore spot on sternum. Pain below right scapula and stitches in small of back. Backache. Lying on back ameliorates many conditions, has led to relief in cases of malignant disease of kidneys and bladder. Cramp in the tongue with embarrassed speech. Swollen tongue. Toothache with digging pain. Dry sockets, with achy pain. Slow pulse. Hangovers. Rhus poisoning, itching, inflammation, and rashes. Skin is red, swollen with watery vesicles. Rectal polyps. Constipation, since trauma to the area (Bell-p.), since childbirth (Sep.). Constipation from inactivity of rectum or impaction of feces following mechanical injuries. Hemorrhoids and impacted feces after an injury. Prolapse of the rectum after confinement. Prolapse is worse by stooping and crouching, comes on immediately on attempting a passage. Tearing stitches in rectum when sitting. Tearing in rectum and urethra while urinating. Sensation of nausea located in the rectum. Rushmore cured with one dose of Ruta 900c (Fincke) a case of prolapse preceding a very difficult stool. A prolonged use of Ruta 3x has cured ganglion in front of left wrist. Cooper said, “It certainly acts strongly on deposits of scirrhus material in both the breasts and in the vagina and sometimes lessens the size of these.” He used Ruta ointment, prepared by extracting the plant in warm Vaseline, as an application in broken cancer of the breast. RELATIONS-Antidbte'di’y.-Camph.Anrii/ote to; Merc. Compare: ( 1) Arn., Bell-p., Rhus-t., Hyper., Calc., Calc- f. (2) Restlessness, effects of cold and damp, Rhus-t. (3) Eye-strain, Nat-m., Onos., Seneg. (4) Prolapsed rectum, Aesc. Bell., Chin-s., Nit-ac., Podo. (5) Pain in back, worse in morning before rising, Pet. (6) Sore as if bruised in parts lain on, Am., Bapt., Pyrog. (6) Constipation after injuries, Am. (7) Warts on palms, Nat-c., Nat- m. - on backs of Ruta graveolens hands, Dulc. chafing. (8) Arg-n., Con., Euphr., Lyc., Cham., Sep. (9) In diseases of bone, Ang., Conch. Compatible: after Am. in joint injuries, after Symph. in bone injuries, Calc., Caust., Lyc., Ph-ac., Puls., Sulph., Sul-ac. - diseases of bone. Complementary: Calc-p. in joint disorders. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Epigastric region sensitive. Aching, gnawing pains in stomach. Tension in stomach, better drinking milk. Pains in stomach after eating bread or crude and indigestible food. Burning, gnawing pain. Dyspepsia caused by straining stomach when carrying heavy weight. Frequent odorless eructations. Hiccough, with depression. Sudden nausea when eating, with vomiting of food. Nausea felt in rectum.

Abdomen - Painful swelling of the spleen. Gnawing ache in region of liver. Gnawing and eating pain about navel. Sick feeling in abdomen followed by soft stools. Pinching pain in abdomen after bread and butter. Cancer of lower bowel. Colic in children, from worms.

Rectum - Constipation from impaction of feces following mechanical injuries. Constipation, alternating with mucous, frothy stools, discharge of blood with stool. Difficult stool, evacuated only with straining. Feces often escape when stooping. Protrusion of rectum when stooping. When sitting, tearing stitches in rectum. Urging to stool, causing rectum prolapses. Rectal prolapse. Sudden prolapsus recti, with tenesmus, after eating grapes. Anal prolapse on stooping. Anal prolapse after delivery, during hard or soft stools. Stricture of rectum. Cancer affecting lower bowel. Nausea felt in rectum. Sensations - As if a nail were driven into head. Head as if bruised or beaten. Eyes, as if strained, as if a shadow flitting before them, as after looking too long and intently at an object, as if eyes were balls of fire. As if one were digging about in the ear with a blunt piece of wood. As of a lump in throat. Bladder as if constantly full. Spine as if beaten and lame. Pain as if from a fall in periosteum. As if pain were in marrow of bone or as if bone were broken. Wrists as if sprained. Thighs as if beaten, as if weak. As if there were an ulcer on ankle. All parts of body bruised at night, feeling as if it were time to rise.

Male - Varicocele following a strain. Injury to genitals, testes. Hematocele in which the effusion is small and firmly coagulated.

Female - Menses very irregular. Menses scanty, lasting but two days, preceded and followed by leucorrhea. Corrosive leucorrhea after irregular or suppressed menses. Symptoms worse at menstrual period. Vaginal pruritus. Bearing-down pains. Prolapsed uterus. Metrorrhagia as a forerunner of miscarriage. Miscarriage, at seven months. Lameness and soreness all over with feeble contractions during labor. Sterility. Food - Appetite normal, but aversion to everything as soon as he begins to eat. Disgust at first mouthful with a sensation of fullness and satiety in abdomen. Great thirst during chill. Violent thirst for ice cold water. Headache from abuse of alcohol. Worse after eating bread, butter, eating meat, grapes, raw or indigestible food.

Chest - Short breath with tightness of chest. Painful spot on sternum. Sensation of coldness or heat in chest. Gnawing, biting and burning pains in chest. Tuberculosis after mechanical injuries to chest. Ill effects of mechanical injury to chest. Constitutions - Suited to robust, bloody persons and corresponds to hemorrhages from nose (with pressure at root), gums, and rectum.

Heart - Anxious palpitations. Pulse somewhat accelerated only during fever.

Back - Backache from injury or strain, better pressure and lying on back. Bruised pain in coccyx, sacrum. Spine and limbs feel bruised. Vertebrae slip out of place easily. Coldness of spine, downwards. Drawing in nape of neck and in the shoulder blades. Tension and pressure in nape and shoulders. Pain in small of back, groin and nape. Weak, bruised feeling in lower back. Lumbago worse morning before rising. Stitches in lumbar region.

Limbs - Bursitis. Cracking in joints, worse walking in open air. Paralytic weakness of legs after spraining of the back. Sciatica, worse lying down at night, pain from back down hips and thighs. Hamstrings feel shortened (Graph.). Great restlessness. Thighsfeel broken, worse when stretching the legs. Legs give out on rising from a chair (Phos., Con.). Knees give way, while ascending and descending stairs. Pains as if deep in long bones, must walk about. Tendons sore. Aching pain in Achilles tendon. Pain in bones of feet and ankles. Ankles swollen from strain or injury. Contraction of fingers. Pain and stiffness in wrists and hands. Ganglion of wrist (Benz-ac., Calc-f.). Nodes in palms. Lungs - Cough with copious, thick, yellow expectoration, chest feels weak after. Waking from cough, about midnight. Violent cough, with expectoration of tough mucus and nausea. Shortness of breath from tightness of chest.

Sleep - Sleepiness during day, with stretching. Yawns, stretches and extends hands. Yawning and stretching, after eating. Frequent waking at night, as if it were time to rise. Vivid, confused dreams.

Skin - Easily chaffed from walking, riding, also in children. Flat, smooth, painful warts, on palms. Warts with sore pains. Corrosive itching over whole body, better scratching. Itching of skin from every attempt to eat meat. Erysipelas after mechanical injuries of hands. Skin becomes easily chafed, from walking and riding.

Modalities - Better from lying on back. Better warmth, motion, rubbing, scratching. Worse from overexertion, lifting, injury, sprains. Worse exertion, ascending or descending stairs. Worse lying down, sitting, stooping. Worse eyestrain, reading. Worse pressure on an edge. Worse from cold air, damp, wind, wet. Worse during menses. Worse from uncooked Ruta graveolens or indigestible food. Warm stove causes chilliness.

Bladder - Constant urging to urinate, can hardly retain urine. If urine forcibly retained, could not pass afterwards, with severe pain. Urging with scanty urination. Sensations as if bladder were still full, after urinating. Pressure in neck of bladder after urinating, painful closure (Apis). Sensations as if bladder is moving up and down at every step. Scanty, green urine. Frequent urination at night. Incontinence at night, or even during day when walking. Causations - Ill effects of bruises, fractures, carrying heavy weights. Bone or joint injuries. Overuse of tendons. Sprains. Going up and down stairs causes hamstrings _________________ Ruta graveolens to feel shortened and weak. Dyspepsia from straining stomach by carrying heavy weights. Over-exertion of eyes.

Perspiration - Cold sweat on face. Perspires in morning in bed. Sweats after walking in open air.

Temperature - Coldness and shivering, with great thirst. Cold shivers run over back. Coldness running over one side of head. Chills mostly left-sided, worse up and down back, shakes even near a warm stove. Heat of face and dull head. Frequent attacks of quick flushes of heat. Glowing heat on face, skin etc.

name: Sabadilla Officinalis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from heat, warm food and drink, swallowing. Better being wrapped up, open air. Better quick motion of affected part. Warm stove ameliorates chilliness. Worse from cold air. Worse forenoon, new and full moon. Worse periodically, every week, two weeks, four weeks, same hour. Worse odors, wine. Worse undeveloped rash. Worse mental exertion. Worse forenoon..
constitution: Allergies. Ascarides. Chilliness. Colds. Coryza. Coughs. Debility. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dyspepsia, pregnancy. Earache. Esophagus, stricture. Hay fever. Headaches. Imaginary diseases. Influenza. Intermittents. Lice. Mania. Melancholia. Neuralgia. Nosebleeds. Pinworms. Rheumatism. Tapeworm. Throat, sore. Toothache. Uvula, elongated. Vertigo. Worms.
keynote:
PHARMACY - sabad. Sabadilla officinalis. Cevadilla seed. Cebadilla. Asagraea officinalis. Scoenocaulon officinale. Veratrum officinale. N. O. Melanthaceae of the Lili- aceae. Tincture of seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Ascarides.…
full:
PHARMACY - sabad. Sabadilla officinalis. Cevadilla seed. Cebadilla. Asagraea officinalis. Scoenocaulon officinale. Veratrum officinale. N. O. Melanthaceae of the Lili- aceae. Tincture of seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Ascarides. Chilliness. Colds. Coryza. Coughs. Debility. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dyspepsia, pregnancy. Earache. Esophagus, stricture. Hay fever. Headaches. Imaginary diseases. Influenza. Intermittents. Lice. Mania. Melancholia. Neuralgia. Nosebleeds. Pinworms. Rheumatism. Tapeworm. Throat, sore. Toothache. Uvula, elongated. Vertigo. Worms.

HERBAL - Asagraea is a Mexican genus belonging to the Colchicum family, Melanthaceae. It has only one species, Asagraea officinalis, furnishing the cebadilla seeds from which Veratrine is prepared. According to the Treasury of Botany, the seeds were formerly used to destroy vermin.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sabadilla first appears in homeopathic literature as one of Stapf s additions; Hahnemann was one of the provers. Stapf s additions form a kind of appendix to the Materia Medica Pura. Stapf said that the plant was first described by Monades around the year 1572. At first, it was almost exclusively used for destroying lice and worms in putrid ulcers and the intestines. Sabadilla has affinities for the mucus membranes of the nose, lachrymal glands, anus, digestive tract, and the nerves. Coryza and symptoms like hay fever. Allergies. Chilliness, sensitive to cold. Nerves are affected, producing weakness. Alternate nervous and bodily symptoms. Cutting pains in bones. Formication. Worms. Reflex nervous symptoms with twitching, convulsive trembling or catalepsy. Children’s diarrhea with constant cutting pains. MIND - Nervous, timid and easily startled. Mental exertion aggravates. Thinking produces headaches and sleeplessness. Feels miserable. Fright causes hysterical paroxysms. Unresponsive to questions. Loss of consciousness, then he jumps up and runs recklessly through the room. Rage. Mania better washing head in cold water. Delirium during intermittents. Erroneous, fixed ideas about himself. Imagines he is very sick. Imagines that she is pregnant or that she has cancer. Imaginary diseases. Imagines that parts are sunken, limbs are crooked, chin is elongated. That one side is longer than the other.

Head - Dullness and oppression. Unilateral head pains or alternating sides, worse thinking, better eating. Burning, itching, crawling on hair and scalp, better scratching. Headache in schoolgirls.

Eyes - Red, burning eyelids. Redness of margins of eyelids. Lachrymation, worse during pain, sneezing, coughing, yawning. Pressure on eyeballs, especially when looking up. Weakness of sight.

Ears - Otalgia with troublesome pressure, with snapping as of electric sparks before ears. Tickling in ears. Itching in ear, alternately with itching at anus. Burning, itching and shootings in tips of ears. Humming, gurgling, and detonation in ears. Deafness as if there were a band over ears. Boring in parotids.

Nose - Influenza. Hay fever. Spasmodic sneezing with running nose. Copious, watery, nasal discharge. Coryza with severe frontal pains and redness of eyes and lachrymation. Fluent coryza, worse from the odor offlowers, even thinking of flowers increases the discharge. Oversensitive to odors, cannot tolerate the smell of garlic. Dry, itching, tickling in nose, rubs or picks at it. Tickling in nose spreads over the whole body, then dyspnea. One or the other nostril stuffed up. Hawks bright red blood from naso-ph^rynx.

Face - Lips hot, burn as if scalded. Heat of face with fiery redness, especially after drinking wine. Blue circles around the eyes. Boring in lower jaw and submaxillary glands. Cracking of the articulation of the jaw on opening mouth wide.

Mouth - Itching of the soft palate. Dryness of the mouth without thirst. Sweetish taste. Copious saliva, jelly- like saliva. Cannot bear anything hot or cold in mouth. Lips as if scalded. Tongue as if burnt, as if full of blisters. Pricking, soreness in tip of tongue. Cannot protrude tongue with sore throat.

Throat - Chronic sore throat, worse from cold air. Sore throat, left to right, worse empty swallowing, better hot drinks. Tonsillitis after coryza. Much tough phlegm. Sensation of a skin hanging loosely, must swallow it. Warm food and drink relieve. Painful empty swallowing. Dry fauces and throat. Sensation of a lump in throat with constant need to swallow. Vertigo - Vertigo with sensation as though all things were turning around each other. Vertigo accompanied by blackness before eyes and sensation of fainting. Vertigo, sudden on waking at night or rising from stooping, better resting head on table. COMMENTS - Stapf pointed out that the provings reveal strong febrile symptoms. Sabad. may be as clock- like as Cedr., and is a leading remedy in intermittent fevers and neuralgias. Sabad. is a chilly remedy, the symptoms, especially the coryza, are generally worse in the open air. Intolerant of mental exertion, thinking causes a headache. Tendency to be startled. Erroneous impressions as to the state of his body. Imaginary diseases, imagines parts shrunken. Imagines she is pregnant if there is distention from flatus. Giddiness, may cause staggering and even fainting. Objects seem to whirl around or to whirl around each other. Sitting aggravates vertigo. Rising from seat causes vertigo. Lying perfectly still ameliorates vertigo. Severe catarrhal symptoms. Hay asthma. Allergies. Hay fever with itching and tingling in the nose (All-c., Ars.). Tingling and numbness in the nose (Petros, in the urethra.). Itching in the roof of the mouth, rubbed raw by the tongue (Wye. ). Spasmodic sneezing. Coryza, sneezing and runny nose (All-c.). Thick, yellow discharge, worse stuff rooms, better fresh air (Puls.), alternates with watery discharge. Sore throats characterized by a sensation of a lump or foreign body in the throat and a constant need to swallow. Pressure on larynx causes sore throat. Lying down causes cough immediately, worse expectoration. Kent said it is suited to “old, chronic sore throats that are worse from cold air. The patient is sensitive to cold air. Every time he takes cold it settles in his nose and throat. Tonsillitis going from left to right.” Desires hot drink (opposite of Lach.). Overly sensitive to the smell of garlic (Thuj.). Opening mouth wide causes cracking of jaw joints.Disordered digestion and loaded tongue. Sinking at stomach and gnawing hunger. Indigestion, during pregnancy. “Violent itching of hairy scalp, compelling her to scratch until blood comes.” “Itching of the vertex as if a quantity of vermin had collected there, obliging him to scratch incessantly.” “Itching of anus and rectum as from ascarides.” “Itching of anus alternating with itching of alae nasi and meatus auditorius.” Scratching ameliorates itching of scalp, causes burning of anus. Kent gave Sabad. to a pet dog which had great irritation of anus and soon afterwards the dog passed a very large number of worms. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Lach., Lyc., Puls., Con. Compare:(l)Colch.,Nux-v., Bry., Arund. and Poll. (2) Veratrina is alkaloid of Sabad., not of Verat., locally in neuralgias and for removal of dropsy. Five grains to two drams. Lanolin, rubbed on inside of thighs, causes diuresis. (3) Phle. - Timothy-Hay - Potentized to 12c a specific to many cases and evidently acts in a desensitizing manner. Cumin. - hay fever. Follows well: Bry. (Pleurisy). FoUowedwellby: Ars. Bell., Merc., Nux-v. Complementary: Sep. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Spasmodic pain in stomach with dry cough and difficult breathing. Heartburn, copious salivation. Cold, empty feeling in stomach.

Abdomen - Bowels feel knotted. As of a lump or thread moving rapidly in abdomen.

Rectum - Constipation. Stools burning, frothy, loose, brown, floating. Broken, hard, scanty stools. Itching, crawling in rectum and anus, as from ascarides, alternating with itching in nose or ears. Pinworms, lumbrici, tapeworm. Sensations - As if things were turning around each other. As if she would fall if she did not hold on to something. As if eyes went around with the whirling sensation. As if uvula were down. As if esophagus would be closed. As of a lump in abdomen. As if a ball of thread were moving and turning rapidly through abdomen. As if knives were cutting abdomen. As if abdomen were shrunken, were empty. Croaking as of frogs in abdomen. As of something alive in abdomen. As if stomach were gnawed.

Male - Digging and pressive pain in testes. Tensive and painful erections, without desire for sex. Pollutions with flaccidity of penis. Diminished sexual desire.

Female - Menses too late, come by fits and starts, intermit, sometimes stronger, sometimes weaker (Kreos., Puls.). Nymphomania from worms. food Thirstless. Canine hunger for sweets and farinaceous food. Desires hot things, milk. Loathing for strong food. Aversion to all food, meat, sour things, coffee, garlic. During pregnancy, no relish for food until she takes first mouthful, then she makes a good meal.

Chest - Burning sensation on chest. Pressure on the chest. Breathing obstructed, as if there were a stone in the chest. Shootings in sides of chest. Inflammation of pleura. Red spots and points on chest. Constitutions - Suited to sensitive persons of light hair, fair complexion with a weakened, relaxed, muscular system. Children and old people.

Heart - Palpitations with pulsations through whole body.

Back - Contusive pain in back and loins, especially when seated. Burning, tingling, stinging sensation between scapulae. Stitches in rapid succession in right side of back. Causations - Ill effects of fright, mental exertion, thinking. Worms, causing convulsions, nymphomania.

Limbs - Upward jerking of arms. Cutting pains in bones. Red spots on arms and hands. Yellow spots on fingers. Swelling of feet with painful soles. Cracking of skin under and beneath toes. Inflammation under toenails. Thickened, deformed horny nails (Ant-c.). Lungs - Wheezing respiration. Short, difficult breathing. Breathing obstructed, as if there were a stone in the chest. Asthmatic breathing with itching of skin, nose and anus. Violent coughing attacks, muffled, worse anger with lachrymation. Hawking up of bright red blood, which comes from the nose. Cough dry with perspiration and water in the eyes. Cough immediately on lying down. Pleurisy with great paralytic debility.

Sleep - Great inclination to sleep during day. Sleep comes on when thinking, meditating or reading. Agitated and unrefreshing sleep at night, with anxious dreams. Sleep retarded by a multitude of thoughts. Starts up as from a fright in the morning.

Skin - Parchment-like dryness of skin. Hot burning, creeping and crawling sensation. Itching with asthmatic breathing. Tingling and burnings shooting under skin. Red bands, spots, and points in different parts of skin.

Modalities - Better from heat, warm food and drink, swallowing. Better being wrapped up, open air. Better quick motion of affected part. Warm stove ameliorates chilliness. Worse from cold air. Worse forenoon, new and full moon. Worse periodically, every week, two weeks, four weeks, same hour. Worse odors, wine. Worse undeveloped rash. Worse mental exertion. Worse forenoon.

Teeth - Toothache with drawing and pulsa- tive pain. Shooting pains in molars. Tooth decay. Pricking in gums. Bluish gums.

Kidneys - Urgent want to urinate, especially in evening, with tenesmus and scanty emission. Increased secretion of urine. Turbid, thick urine, like clay-water. Burning in urethra when urinating.

Temperature - Chill predominates from below upwards. Heat in head and face, hands and feet icy cold with chill. Thirstless, thirst after chill only. Lachrymation with chill. Shivering as a concomitant.

name: Sabal Serrulata
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better after sleep, from milk. Worse from cold, damp, cloudy weather. Worse in early morning, from rising, at bedtime. Worse from sympathy. Worse before menses. Worse from motion. Backache worse after sex. Catarrhal symptoms are worse in cold, damp weather. Cough worse on lying down at night. Depression worse before menses..
