full:
PHARMACY - salol. Salol. Phenol salicylate. Salolum. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Fever. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Influenza. Neuralgia. Rheumatism. Smallpox.

HOMEOPATHIC - Salol, was primarily used as an anti-rheumatic, especially in the treatment of acute cases. It was given as an antipyretic in 30 to 45 grain doses in powders or tablets. It is soluble in ether and petroleum spirit, very sparingly, if at all in water. It does not disturb digestion because it passes through the stomach unaltered, being decomposed in the duodenum, by the ferments of the pancreas into salicylic acid and phenol (it contains 38 percent phenol). These are excreted by the kidneys and the condition of intestinal digestion has been estimated by the iength of time required after the ingestion of Salol., for them to appear in the urine. Helbing reported that it has been used in acute diarrhea, dysentery, cholera and other diseases where intestinal asepsis in indicated and also in disorders of the bladder and urethra as a substitute for ordinary mechanical irrigations and injections. Its internal use in gonorrhea (in 5-grain doses three times a day) has met with much success. Dull aching in head and all over body. Can hardly go up stairs, and it is dreadfully painful to sit on a hard stool. The hands shrink when cold, cannot straighten the little fingers without much pain.

Head - Dreadful headache, especially over eyes. Dull aching in head and all over body.

Limbs - Rheumatic pains. Feeling of stiffness in joints. Limbs sensitive to touch. Pain in shoulder. Pain in right arm in evening. Pain in wrists. Cramp in hand on writing. Hurts even to carry a book in hand. Buttocks sore. Pain in left buttock, especially on walking.

Skin - Burning and itching eruption. Smallpox. COMMENTS - The only proving of Salol, was made incidentally onachemistfrommakingup powders of the remedy. He experienced very severe symptoms from inhaling the odor, and possible also some of the powder. Rheumatic pains in joints with soreness and stiffness were marked, especially pain and soreness in the buttocks, knees, and wrists. The prover was subject to headaches, but he never had so violent a headache as that produced by Salol, and conversely after the proving, Salol. 12c immediately relieved him when threatened with one of his usual headaches. The first symptom he noted was that his urine smelled of violets and it was only when this passed off that the other symptoms came on. The joints felt stiff, “as if they wanted oiling.” C. Beg referred to the use of Salol, in smallpox and other skin disorders attended with burning and itching. The relief of itching in smallpox was a constant and most satisfactory result. When administered early it prevented maturation of pustules. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Bry. Compare: (1) Sal-ac., Salin.., Nat-sal., Carb-ac. (2) Wrist rheumatism, Act- sp., Led., Viol-o. (3) Urine smells of violets. Terebe. (4) Gonorrhea, Napht., Petros. (5) Smallpox, Carb-ac., Sarr., Vario. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Modalities - Worse walking, raising eyes, ascending stairs. Pain in buttocks worse sitting on hard stool. Worse by touch, in evening.

Kidneys - Urine smelled strongly of violets.

name: Salvia Divinorum
author: Murphy
constitution: Amnesia. Ascites. Debility. Delusions. Depression. Diarrhea. Drug, addictions. Edema. Headache. Intoxication. Memory, loss. Nightmares. Panic attacks. Personality, disorders. Rheumatism. Vi- sions.
keynote:
PHARMACY - salv-d. Salviadivinorum. Shepherdess’s herb. Ska pastora. Shka pastora. Maria pastora. Mexican mint. Yerba de Maria. N. O. Lamiaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves and blossom-tips. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amnesia. Ascites. Debility.…
full:
PHARMACY - salv-d. Salviadivinorum. Shepherdess’s herb. Ska pastora. Shka pastora. Maria pastora. Mexican mint. Yerba de Maria. N. O. Lamiaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves and blossom-tips. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amnesia. Ascites. Debility. Delusions. Depression. Diarrhea. Drug, addictions. Edema. Headache. Intoxication. Memory, loss. Nightmares. Panic attacks. Personality, disorders. Rheumatism. Vi- sions.

HERBAL - The Latin name Salvia di vinorum literally translates to “sage of the seers.” The genus name Salvia is derived from the Latin salvare, meaning “to heal” or “to save.” The words salvation and savior also come from this root. Salvia di vinorum is a sprawling perennial herb which grows wild only in the Sierra Mazatec region of Mexico. Its leaves contain the extremely potent salvinorin-A. It has a history of use as a divinatory psychedelic for oral use and has been widely available since the 1990’s primarily as a smoked herb. Salvia divinorum is traditionally used by chewing pairs of leaves. Modern use includes both smoking and chewing the leaves. When the leaves are chewed, the quid and bitter juice are held in the mouth to increase absorption. Strong effects can be difficult to attain from smoking dried leaf, but extracts and potency-bred leaves can cause dramatic, sometimes frightening deep mind-states. Many people who try S. divinorum do not find the effects at all pleasant and choose not to repeat the experience. Historical uses include headache, diarrhea, rheumatism, debilitation and ascites. Intense shaking of body. Inability to control muscles and maintain balance. Tendency to stagger, fall. Depression. May prove to be useful for those troubled with addictions. MIND - Altered perceptions. Clarity of thought. Introspection. Insights into life and existence. Trances and visionary states of intoxication. Dreamlike experiences. Powerful visions with open orclosed eyes. Visions of past lives and times. Feels the presence of entities. Delusions and visions. States of tranquility and ecstasy. Great relaxation and bliss. Uncontrollable hysterical laughter. Restlessness. Panic attacks./n- tense experiences of fear, terror and panic. Speechless. Complete loss of memory. Overlapping realities. The perception that one is in several locations at once. Feel detached from reality with a heightened senses of space, sight smell and sound. Loss of the body and personal identity. Sensation of dying. Near death experiences. Out of body experiences. Sensation of entering or perceiving other dimensions, alternate realities. Revisiting places from the past, especially childhood.

Back - Prickling and tingling up and down the spine.

Perspiration - Increased perspiration. Sensations - Sensation of pins and needles all over my body. Prickling and tingling. Sensation that the body becomes suddenly very heavy. Sensations of physical push, pressure, or wind. Various sensations of motion, or being pulled or twisted by forces of some kind.

Temperature - Change in body temperature, flushing. COMMENTS - One person wrote, “For the next two hours I felt light headed and restless. I couldn’t sit still. Whenever I sat down I felt compelled to get up. I tried to eat something and drink a little wine in order to get grounded and relaxed, but I couldn’t seem to swallow anything. I had been shaken to the soul.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Anh., Bani-c., Cann-i., Op. REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Salvia Officinalis
author: Murphy
constitution: Cough, tickling. Fever. Gums, bleeds. Mouth, sores. Night-sweats. Perspiration, excessive. Tuberculosis.
keynote:
PHARMACY - salv. Salvia officinalis. Common Sage. N. O. Lamiaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves and blossom- tips. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cough, tickling. Fever. Gums, bleeds. Mouth, sores. Night-sweats. Perspiration, excessive.…
full:
PHARMACY - salv. Salvia officinalis. Common Sage. N. O. Lamiaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves and blossom- tips. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cough, tickling. Fever. Gums, bleeds. Mouth, sores. Night-sweats. Perspiration, excessive. Tuberculosis.

HERBAL - Gerard wrote, “Sage is singularly good for the head and brain, it quickened the senses and memory. Sage strengthen the sinews, restore health to those that have palsy and take away shaky trembling of the members.” French doctors called attention to sage for gargling in cases of inflammation of the throat and for washing the mouth in disorders of the gums.

HOMEOPATHIC - Salv. exerts a tonic influence on the skin. Controls excessive sweating when circulation is enfeebled. Night-sweats in persons suffering from disorders of the respiratory organs, especially tuberculosis. Colliquative perspiration. Soft skin, relaxed with enfeebled circulation and cold limbs. Suffocating, tickling cough. Galactorrhea. COMMENTS - Salv. should be given in doses of 20, 30 or 40 drops in a tablespoonful of water. The effects manifest themselves very quickly, two hours after taking a dose, and these effects persist for two to six days. The tickling cough of tuberculosis and the nightsweats are entirely relieved by doses of 20 to 40 drops in a tablespoonful of water. In the numerous experiments made with it, there were never any disagreeable concomitant effects. Salv. acts even more favorably on the tickling coughs in tuberculosis patients than Bell., Rumx., so that preparations of morphine and codeine could be dispensed with. In one case. Ms. Smith had for three weeks an irritating cough following an attack of pneumonia. The irritation being particularly great, she was given, fresh from the garden, some sage to chew, and the irritation was instantly relieved. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Phel., Merc., Tub. (2) Chrysan. (3) Salv-sc - tonic influence on nervous system, dose, teaspoonful to one pint hot water, as inhalant for sponging. (4) Rub-t. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Sambucus Canadensis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better by sweat, getting out of bed. Worse from lying down..
constitution: Albuminuria. Angina pectoris. Asthma. Blotches. Cuts. Larynx, dry. Lumbago. Wounds.
keynote:
PHARMACY - samb-c. Sambucuscanadensis. Elder-bush. Marsh elder-bush. Sambucus humilis. Sambucus glauca. N. O. Capriflia- ceae. Tincture of buds, flowers, tender shoots and leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Angina pectoris. Asthma.…
full:
PHARMACY - samb-c. Sambucuscanadensis. Elder-bush. Marsh elder-bush. Sambucus humilis. Sambucus glauca. N. O. Capriflia- ceae. Tincture of buds, flowers, tender shoots and leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Angina pectoris. Asthma. Blotches. Cuts. Larynx, dry. Lumbago. Wounds.

HERBAL - The indigenous North American elder grows in rich alluvial soils, flowers in July and fruits in September. The species, said Millspaugh is not sufficiently distinct from the European elder (Samb. nigra), differing only in being less woody and having more loose cymes, larger flowers and more compound leaves. Millspaugh said of Samb-c. that a decoction or ointment of the flowers and leaves was used as an application to large wounds.

HOMEOPATHIC - The severe chest symptoms and blotched face recall symptoms of Samb. with which it is probably identical in action. Uneasiness, and unrest. Exhaustion. Recurrence of symptoms. MIND - Depression and dread of undefined danger.

Head - Severe drawing in head with fullness, motion causes sensation as if water were undulating in it. Head heavy, confused with drawing and darting pains.

Face - Face flushed and broken out in blotches, looks ill.

Mouth - Mouth parched, dry, desire for drink.

Throat - Pharynx and larynx felt dry and swollen, impeding free respiration. REFERENCES-Clarke.

Chest - Palpitations. Heaviness and constriction in chest, as from a heavy load. Aroused from sleep by a terrible constriction of chest and heart, cannot lie down for fear of choking.

Heart - Constriction of chest and heart, lying down causes choking. Sharp pain in heart (region of valves), with palpitations, at times visible through the clothes. Heart labors heavily. Pulse rose to 100, but became normal at end of perspiration.

Back - Back felt sprained. Pressing pain in lumbar region.

Limbs - Sharp, darting rheumatic pains hands and feet. Lungs - Breathing labored, asthmatic, wheezing. Has to sit up in bed to get breath.

Modalities - Better by sweat, getting out of bed. Worse from lying down.

Kidneys - Pressure in kidney region, followed by profuse flow of clear urine. Frequent urination. Urine albuminous.

Temperature - Sweat, soon becoming profuse, which gradually ameliorates all other symptoms (except exhaustion). Head perspired less than rest of body.

name: Sambucus Nigra
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better sitting up in bed, motion, from pressure over a sharp edge, and wrapping up. Worse from dry, cold air, uncovering. Worse cold drink while over heated, eating fruits. Worse motion. Worse sleep, rest, lying down in bed, on left side. Worse about midnight, after midnight, 2 to 3 a.m., wakes with sense of stoppage of air tubes. Head low aggravates, must sit up to regain breath..
constitution: Angina pectoris. Asthma. Chest, oppression. Choking. Colic. Contusions. Coryza, dry. Coughs. Croup. Cyanosis. Edema. Emaciation. Headaches, catarrhal. Hoarseness. Hydrocele. Ileus. Laryngismus. Spasms. Snuffles. Suffocation. Tuberculosis. Whooping cough.
keynote:
PHARMACY - samb. Sambucus nigra. Elder. N. O. Caprifliaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves and flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Asthma. Chest, oppression. Choking. Colic. Contusions. Coryza, dry. Coughs. Croup. Cyanosis. Edema.…
full:
PHARMACY - samb. Sambucus nigra. Elder. N. O. Caprifliaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves and flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Asthma. Chest, oppression. Choking. Colic. Contusions. Coryza, dry. Coughs. Croup. Cyanosis. Edema. Emaciation. Headaches, catarrhal. Hoarseness. Hydrocele. Ileus. Laryngismus. Spasms. Snuffles. Suffocation. Tuberculosis. Whooping cough.

HOMEOPATHIC - Samb. was proved by Hahnemann and appears in his Materia Medica Pura. It acts especially on the respiratory organs, kidneys and the skin. Spasm, mainly affecting the respiratory system, larynx, chest and nasal passages. Shortness of breath. Snuffles in infants preventing breathing and nursing. Dry coryza. When it occurs lower down in the tract, it causes dyspnea. The child awakens suddenly nearly suffocated, face livid, blue. Sits up in bed, turns blue, gasps for breath, which it finally gets. The attack passes off but is again repeated. Child inspires but cannot expire. Sleeps into the attack. The breathing is rattling. Croup, whooping cough, asthma. Profuse sweat during waking hours, dry heat when asleep, particularly in tubercular or febrile conditions. A deep, dry cough precedes the fever paroxysm. Fever without thirst. Dreads uncovering. Edema, dropsical swellings in various parts of the body, especially legs, instep and feet. When edema affects the nose it may give rise to obstruction. Contusions cause dark red swelling. MIND - General trembling with anxiety. Constant state of fretfulness. Very easily frightened. Fright followed by suffocative attacks. Worse from fright or strong emotions. Sees images when shutting eyes. Abdomen - Pressive pain in abdomen with nausea. Spasmodic tearings, shootings and pinchings in abdominal muscles, with expulsion of flatus. Colic with nausea and flatulence. Frequent, watery, slimy stools.

Eyes - Pupils at first contracted, then greatly dilated. Photophobia. Half open in sleep.

Ears - Sharp stitches in right inner ear, with cramp pain in it. Itching, creeping in ears and in throat.

Nose - Dry coryza with snuffles in infants. Sensation of numbness in nose with itching on bridge. Obstruction of nose with accumulation of thick and viscid mucus in nostrils. Dry coryza of children. Pelvis - Pains in loins with drawing pressure. Incisive blows in loins.

Face - Pale, bluish, puffy. Turns blue with cough. Blotches on face. Red, burning spots on cheeks. Heat and perspiration of face. Hot face with icy cold feet.

Mouth - Dryness of the mouth and throat without thirst. Half open in sleep. Toothache with tearing and lancinations in all the teeth and with a sensation as if cheeks were swollen.

Throat - Hoarseness with tenacious mucus in larynx. Screeching voice. Spasms of glottis. Itching, tingling in throat. Vertigo - Dizziness and confusion in the head, during movement, on rising. COMMENTS - The leaves of Sambucus nigra have an unpleasant odor when bruised, which is supposed to be offensive to most insects. A decoction of the leaves is sometimes used by gardeners to keep caterpillars off delicate plants. Green noted that sheep that have the rot can be cured by letting them eat the bark and young leaves of Samb. Herbalists use the inner bark, as well as the leaves, to make an ointment. The flowers serve for fomentations or are made into a medicinal tea. According to the Treasury of Botany, the berries are the principal ingredient in elderberry wine. Millspaugh said that the bark contains viburnic acid, which is identical with valerianic acid. This no doubt accounts for the odor and suggests a relationship in action between sambucus, valerian and the viburnum. Nash once relieved with Samb. 200c a very bad case of asthma in an old woman, who had suffocative attacks. The relief was accompanied by a profuse flow of urine, which carried off a large amount of dropsical effusion in her legs and abdomen. Severe croup, whooping cough, bronchitis, and asthma. Infants with chronic snuffles (Thuj., after vaccinations). Suffocating attacks (Ip.). Tendency for attacks to recur. Croupy attack “passes off but is again repeated.” Spasms in the throat. Severe coughing with mucus. Thick, white, upper respiratory mucus that suffocates and gags the person (Ant-t.) Patient can wake up in the middle of the night, grab at their throat, face turns blue. Waking with a spasm where the oxygen gets cut off (Cup.). Worse about midnight or after midnight, worse 2:00 to 3:00 in the morning. Worse dry, cold air. RELATIONS - Samb-c. may be regarded as practically identical with Satnb-n. Antidoted by: Ars., Camph. Antidote to: Ars. - relieves ailments from abuse of Ars. Compare: (1) Ip., Meph., Op. (2) Samb-c. - great value in dropsies. (3) In Miller’s asthma, Arum-d. (4) Dyspnea, inspires, cannot expire. Chlor., Meph. (5) Sleeps into the attack, Lach. (6) Peculiarities of sweating. Chin., Con., Thuj., Puls. (7) Dreads uncovering, Nux-v. (8) Fat people emaciate suddenly, lod., Tub. (9) Tenacious mucus in larynx, Kali-bi. (10) Effects of cold drink when over-heated, Bell-p. (11) Effects of dry cold. Aeon. Snuffles, Am-c., Nux-v. Compatible: Bell., Con., Nux-v., Phos., Rhus-t., Sep. Follows well: Op. (effects of fright). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Pressure in stomach. Acute lancinations under the stomach, worse by pressing upon it. Vomiting in morning, first of mucus and milk (or food) that had been taken, followed by bile.

Rectum - Irritable anus with hemorrhoids. Frequent, watery, slimy stools. Sensations - As if head were filled with water. Skull as if stretched. As if suffocating.

Male - Hydrocele from injury. Swelling of scrotum.

Female - Menses too profuse, like metrorrhagia. Debilitating sweats after childbirth. Food - Thirst without relishing the drinks. Head - Headache as from intoxication. Motion of head causes tension and dizziness. Pressure and expansion in head. Sudden shocks in the brain. Digging pain in vertex. Scurf on head with intolerable itching.

Chest - Oppression of chest with pressure in stomach, nausea and weakness. Pressure on sternum. Sudden sensation of contraction in sides of chest. Constitutions - Suited to diseases of scrofulous children that affect the air passages especially. Suited to persons previously robust and fleshy who suddenly become emaciated.

Heart - Orgasm in whole body. Occasional omission of heartbeat. Pulse generally very frequent and small, sometimes slow, full. Intermitting. Angina pectoris where pressure proceeds from spine.

Back - Aching in middle of spine during repose and movement. Lancinations in scapulae. Causations - Ill effects of fright, grief, anxiety, excessive sexual indulgence. Fright causes suffocative attack.

Neck - Pressive heaviness in nape. Deep incisive lancinations in muscles of neck. Sweat on throat and neck with children.

Limbs - Tension in hamstrings as if they were too short. Tearing in legs and ankles. Edematous swelling in legs, insteps and feet. Icy-cold feet with a warm body. Hands and feet bloated and blue. Drawing in forearms and bones of hands. Paralytic heaviness in elbow joint. Lancinations in wrists. Trembling of hands (when writing). Lungs - Spasmodic croup. Asthma. Cyanosis. Sudden suffocation or strangling on falling to sleep, or waking him at midnight with violent sweat. Child awakes suddenly, nearly suffocating, sits up. turns blue. Paroxysmal, suffocative cough, coming on about midnight with crying and dyspnea. Loose choking cough. Spells of coughing, before fever. Dry coryza. Sniffles of infants, nose dry and obstructed. Cannot expire (Meph.). When nursing child must let go of nipple, nose blocked up, cannot breathe. Whistling breathing.

Sleep - Frequent waking with a start, with obstructed respiration. Child starts up suddenly as if suffocating. Incomplete sleep with mouth and eyes half open. Sleeps with arms above head. Dry heat during sleep, profuse perspiration after waking. Lascivious dreams.

Skin - Dry heat during sleep. Tingling, itching of skin. Sudden painful drawing in all points over surface while sitting. Edema, anasarca. Bloated and swollen, general dropsy, profuse sweat on waking.

Modalities - Better sitting up in bed, motion, from pressure over a sharp edge, and wrapping up. Worse from dry, cold air, uncovering. Worse cold drink while over heated, eating fruits. Worse motion. Worse sleep, rest, lying down in bed, on left side. Worse about midnight, after midnight, 2 to 3 a.m., wakes with sense of stoppage of air tubes. Head low aggravates, must sit up to regain breath.

Kidneys - Dropsical symptoms with vomiting of bile and distress in stomach after eating. Acute nephritis. Profuse urination with a sensation of heat in the body, dry heat of skin. Urine frequent and scanty.

Perspiration - Very debilitating sweats. Profuse sweat over entire body during waking hours. Continued perspiration while awake, changing into dry heat as soon as one goes to sleep. Night sweats, except on head, worse towards morning.

Temperature - Shuddering with shivering. Icy coldness of hands and feet. Pricking, tingling in skin. Intermittent fever. Dry, burning fever while asleep, copious sweating on waking. Fever with excessive perspiration, especially at night. Debilitating night sweats (Salv., Acet-ac.').Dreads uncovering. Dry, deep cough precedes the fever paroxysm. Sweats with cough.

name: Sanguinaria Canadensis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better acids, sour things. Better vomiting, passing flatus. Better cool air. Better darkness, sleep, lying on back or on left side. Worse from motion, raising arms, looking up. Worse touch, right side. Worse light, sun, odors, and sweets. Worse 3 a.m., weekly, nightly, periodically. Worse menopause..
constitution: Alcoholism. Anemia. Aphonia. Arthritis. Asthma. Bilious, disorders. Blood, disorders. Breast, tumor. Bronchitis. Cancer. Catarrh. Chest, pains. Cold. Croup. Deafness. Diphtheria. Dysmenorrhea. Dys- pepsia. Ear, polyps. Gleet. Granular, lids. Headaches. Heartburn. Hemoptysis. Hot, flashes. Influenza. Keratitis. Liver, disorders. Menopause. Menstruation, painful. Migraines. Nails, ulceration. Neural
keynote:
PHARMACY - sang. Sanguinariacanadensis. Blood-root. Puccoon. N. O. Papaveraceae. Tincture of fresh root. The resin, leaves, seeds, seed-vessels, powdered root and expressed juice have also been used. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Anemia.…
full:
PHARMACY - sang. Sanguinariacanadensis. Blood-root. Puccoon. N. O. Papaveraceae. Tincture of fresh root. The resin, leaves, seeds, seed-vessels, powdered root and expressed juice have also been used. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Anemia. Aphonia. Arthritis. Asthma. Bilious, disorders. Blood, disorders. Breast, tumor. Bronchitis. Cancer. Catarrh. Chest, pains. Cold. Croup. Deafness. Diphtheria. Dysmenorrhea. Dys- pepsia. Ear, polyps. Gleet. Granular, lids. Headaches. Heartburn. Hemoptysis. Hot, flashes. Influenza. Keratitis. Liver, disorders. Menopause. Menstruation, painful. Migraines. Nails, ulceration. Neuralgias. Edema, glottidis. Ophthalmia. Pharyngitis. Tuberculosis. Physometra. Pneumonia, acute. Polyps. Pregnancy, disorders. Quinsy. Rheumatism. Rhus poisoning. Shoulder, rheumatism. Sinusitis. Smell, loss. Stomach, neurosis. Syphilis. Tinnitus. Tumors. Vomiting. Whitlow. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - The bloodroot is commonly found throughout the United States and Canada, and is the sole representative of the genus Sanguinaria of the Papaveraceae. It is herbaceous, has a thick, branching root stock, which creeps along underground. In early spring, it sends up from the ends of the little side branches a single long- stalked leaf and another stalk bearing a solitary flower. The leaf is wrapped around the flower bud when it rises from the ground and is bluntly five to nine-lobed, roundish at first, but later kidney-shaped. The Treasury of Botany noted that Native Americans used the orange-colored juice of the root for smearing their bodies and for staining various domestic articles. The plant had also been successfully used by American and French dyers.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sang, is a right-sided remedy, affecting the head, liver, chest and deltoid. Affects chiefly the mucus membranes, especially of the respiratory tract. Suited to pulmonary disorders with liver involvement. Marked vaso-motor disturbances, as seen in the circumscribed redness of the cheeks, flashes of heat, determination of blood to head and chest, general pulsations and distention of temporal veins. Burning heat and ebullitions. Burning in various parts. Burning sensations like from hot water. Burning in palms and soles. Burning in throat, under sternum, spots or stitches in chest, palms and soles. Burnt feeling in tongue. Applicable to menopausal disorders. Influenza coughs. Sudden stopping of catarrh of respiratory tract followed by diarrhea. Tuberculosis. Mucus membranes become dry. Acrid, blood-streaked or foul discharge. Sick and faint from odor of flowers. Polyps, nasal, uterine. Fungus excrescences. Pains in places where bones are least covered. Internal rawness. Lies on back with head elevated. Bilious. Pains increase and decrease with the sun. Symptoms ascend or end in bilious vomiting. MIND - Hopefulness, confident of recovery. Mind confused, better by belchings. Anxiety and dread preceded vomiting and delirium. Borrows trouble. Grumbling. Angry, irritability, moroseness. Rage after insults. Disgusting thoughts and ideas. Sensitive to noise. Mental torpor, stupor, heaviness, sleepiness. Lassitude, indisposed to move or make any mental effort. Indolence. Dreamy state with eyes open. Sensation as if paralyzed and unable to move while lying on her back. Recognizes everything but can’t move. Abdomen - Throbbing in abdomen. Tension in epigastrium. Awoke with severe pain in region of spleen. Violent stitches in spleen. Sensation as if hot water poured itself from breast into abdomen, followed by diarrhea. Flatulent distention with escape of flatus from vagina. Colic with torpor of liver.

Head - Periodical sick headache, pain begins in occiput, spreads upwards or ascending from occiput to over right eye. Pain in the occiput like a flash of lightning. Pain in small spot over upper left parietal bone. Veins and temples are distended. Headaches if he goes without food. Headaches, better sleep, vomiting and passing copious flow of urine. Headaches return at menopausal, every seventh day (Sulph., Sabad.). Sun headache. Hemicrania increases and decreases with the sun.

Eyes - Acute conjunctivitis. Yellow sclera, jaundice. Retinal congestion. Catarrhal ophthalmia, granular lids. Redness of eyes in morning. Burning dryness in eyes, followed by copious lachrymation. Lachrymation with coryza, tears hot. Vapor or cloud before eyes. Eyeballs painful on moving them. Swelling over eyebrows. Blepharitis.

Ears - Burning of ears with redness of cheeks. Cracking in right ear while stroking cheek. Earache with headache. Polyps. Humming and roaring in the ear, painfully sensitive to sounds, at menopause. Throat disorders causing deafness and earache.

Nose - Nasal polyps. Chronic rhinitis, membrane dry and congested. Hay fever. Ozaena with profuse, offensive, yellowish discharges. Coryza, followed by diarrhea. Pain at the root of nose. Rose-cold with subsequent asthma. Sensitive to odors. Loss or perverted sense of smell, smell in nose like roasted onion.

Face - Hectic flush, redness and burning of cheeks. Neuralgia, pain extends in all directions from upper jaw. Fullness and tenderness behind angle of jaws.

Mouth - Ulceration of mouth and fauces with dry, burning sensation. Palate feels scalded. Tongue white, feels burnt. Anterior tongue looks red, like raw beef. Offensive breath. Sweet things taste bitter.

Throat - Dry cough, tickling in throat. Tonsillitis. Ulcerated sore throat, as if raw and denuded. Sore, swollen (right), pains to ear and chest. Burning, worse eating sweet things. Dry and constricted. Sensation in pharynx as if scalded by hot drink. Edema of larynx. Larynx, full and dry in singers. Aphonia.

Stomach - Sinking, faint, all-gone feeling (Phos., Sep.). Stomach pains to right shoulder. Burning in stomach with headache, and vomiting. Hiccough while smoking. Nausea with salivation, not better by vomiting. Vomiting of bitter water, sour, acrid fluids, of ingesta, of worms. Spitting of bile, gastro-duodenal catarrh.

Rectum - Alternate diarrhea and constipation. Colic followed by diarrhea. Diarrhea as coryza improves. Dysentery. Urging to stool, but only discharges of flatus. Ineffectual urging to stool, then vomiting. Bilious, liquid, gushing diarrhea (Nat-s., Lyc.). Copious apple-green stools with flatus. Hemorrhoids. Cancer of rectum. Sensations - As if forehead would burst. As of a band across forehead. As if head were drawn forward. As if electric current shooting through head. As if temples and scalp were alive with irrepressible pulsation. As if eyes would be pressed out. As if hairs were in eyes. As if paralyzed. As if she was in a railway car that was moving and jarring her and as if all about her moved rapidly and confusedly.

Male - Burning in glans. Cheesy secretions from glans (syphilis). Gleet, old cases. Emissions two nights in succession, after which he felt very well.

Female - Amenorrhea. Before menses, itching of axilla. Menstruation too early with a discharge of black blood. Menses offensive, profuse. Leucorrhea fetid, corrosive. Uterine polyps. Menopausal disorders, especially flushes of heat. Burning of palms and soles at menopause. Food - Loss of appetite with great weakness of digestion. Unquenchable thirst. Craves, knows not for what. Craving for spicy things. Aversion to butter, leaves a sweetish taste. Sweet things aggravate, taste bitter, cause burning. Bilious headaches if he goes without food.

Chest - Pain, burning soreness, in right chest to shoulder. Burning in chest, as of a hot steam extending to abdomen with cough. Tickling behind sternum, causes a constant hacking cough, worse at night on lying down. Hemoptysis. Hydrothorax. Pneumonia.

Heart - Weak feeling, irregular action. Palpitations. Valvular disease with lung development, phosphates in urine and loss of flesh. Metastasis of rheumatism (or gout) to heart from outward applications.

Back - Soreness down muscles of back. Pain in inner border of right shoulder blade. Pain in sacrum from lifting. Breasts - Sore and enlarged breasts, at menopause. Pain in right breast to shoulder. Severe soreness under right nipple. Hot streaming from breast towards liver. Pain in breast with periodic cough.

Neck - Soreness of nape on being touched. Rheumatic pain in nape, shoulders and arms. Pain in right side of neck as if strained in left side.

Limbs - Rheumatism of right shoulder. Pain in shoulder, worse night. Cutting pain or stiffness in right deltoid, worse raising or turning arm. Pain in arm better swinging arm to and fro. Itching in axilla, worse before menses. Aching and swelling of ball of thumb (right). Palms wrinkled. Burning of palms and soles, worse covers, at menopause. Rheumatism of left hip joint and nape of neck. Pain in bones near surface. Neuritis better by touching the part.

Sleep - Drowsiness causing mental and bodily indolence. Sleeplessness at night, awakens in a fright as if he would fall. Can’t sleep without brandy. Slightest noise disturbs, yet is sleepy and dreamy. Dreams of sea voyages with sensation of being rocked. Dreams of frightful business matters.

Skin - Heat and dryness of skin. Prickling heat spreading over body. Burning and itching, worse by heat. Circumscribed red spots. Red, blotchy eruptions, worse in spring. Acne with scanty menses. Scaly eruptions, carbuncles. Itching and nettlerash before the nausea. Old indolent ulcers with callous borders and ichorous discharge. Fungus excrescences. Antidotes rhuspoisoning. Jaundice.

Modalities - Better acids, sour things. Better vomiting, passing flatus. Better cool air. Better darkness, sleep, lying on back or on left side. Worse from motion, raising arms, looking up. Worse touch, right side. Worse light, sun, odors, and sweets. Worse 3 a.m., weekly, nightly, periodically. Worse menopause.

Teeth - Looseness of teeth, with salivation. Toothache from picking teeth. Pain in hollow teeth, especially when touched by food. Pain in decayed teeth after cold drinks. Bleeding, spongy, fungoid gums.

Tongue - Burnt, sore feeling. Tip of tongue burns as if scalded. Crawling, pricking on tip of tongue. Stitches in left side of tongue. White coated tongue with slimy, fatty taste. Red streak through middle of tongue. Vertigo - Vertigo, worse looking up and moving head rapidly, with nausea, fainting and headache. COMMENTS - Acts powerfully on the outer chest, sternum and breasts. Reputed to cure cancer, polyps and new growths (Chel.). Clarke saw breast tumors diminish under its action. Grimmer stated that this remedy has cured breast cancer with severe burning pains and inflammatory symptoms of the mucus membranes, the respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts, and the skin. Pronounced heat, flushing and redness of the skin. Characteristic burning pains (wherever pain exists). S. L. Mitchell recorded the fatal poisoning of workmen who drank the tincture in mistake for brandy. They were all soon seized with severe racking and burning pains in the stomach and bowels with intense thirst. “Burning” is one of the leading notes of the remedy and is found in many different parts. Winterburn published a case illustrating this indication in the region of the stomach. Mr. F., 48, ofsanguino- bilious temperament, energetic and refined, had been ill with pains in the stomach for several months. A clairvoyant had recommended “a decoction of blood-root and bone-set in tablespoonful doses.” Each dose produced “intense burning pains in the stomach lasting for hours,” and it had to be discontinued. Weeks later, Winterburn was consulted and found Mr. F with burning in his epigastrium with pressure, worse at night, but coming on soon after lying down and compelling the patient to rise. Belching gave no relief. Great appetite, torpid bowels, an unsatisfactory relief each morning, leaving a sense of discomfort. There was a peculiar drawing pain in the shoulders and arms during sleep, so that when he woke his fists were tightly clenched and flexed on the sternal end of his clavicle, lameness and weariness of the muscles followed. Sang. 200c, was chosen aftercareful comparison with Nux-v., Graph, and others. It was given every night at bedtime. After the first dose, the symptoms disappeared “like magic,” and the patient was soon well. Leonard said “a circumscribed burning in the chest, commonly followed by heat through abdomen and diarrhea,” is a strong indication for Sang, in pneumonic conditions. Sang, also has the circumscribed hectic flush on the cheeks, as in tuberculosis in which it is frequently indicated. Flushed face, at times dark red or livid (Op.). It has the “hopefulness” of tubercular patients. Severe headaches. Migraine, starting at the back of the head and moving to above the right eye (Sil.). Headaches begin at occiput, spreading upwards and forwards, settling over the right eye. Pains like a flash of lightning in occiput. Bursting headaches, as if the eyes would be pressed out. Better by sleep. Symptoms begin in the morning, increase to noon, then diminish. Headaches return at menopause. Right-sided headaches with the flu. Bilious or gastric headaches. Hering described the headache as the “American sick-headache.” There is a rush of blood causing faintness and nausea, pains are sharp or throbbing. Patients cannot bear light, odors, or the least jar, as that of anyone stepping across the floor. There can be vomiting of food and bile. Pain so violent the patient goes out of her mind or seeks relief by pressing head against pillow or pressing with the hands. Cooper gave as a keynote, “If he goes without food, gets bilious headaches.” Violent, throbbing headache with extreme nausea and vomiting, frequent, fetid belch- ings and great salivation. Severe burning in stomach, vomits bitter water and sour, acrid fluids. Nausea may not be relieved by vomiting. Sweets taste bitter, aggravate the burning. Vomiting of worms. Tormenting thirst. Offensive breath and flatus. Irritation of the nasal mucus membrane. Polyps. Coryza with pain at root of the nose. Influenza, hay fever and ozaena. Sinusitis, more on the right side. Lost or perverted sense of smell, sensitive to the odor of flowers. Laryngitis and membranous croup. Tracheal and bronchial coughs in epidemic influenza. Cough after influenza or whooping cough, particularly in children. Cough returns with every fresh cold. Violent, dry cough, wheezing, whistling, metallic. Offensive and acrid discharges. Sputa is almost impossible to raise. Clarke recorded several cases in which Sang, relieved patients who had thick plugs of suffocating mucus which the patients were too weak to dislodge. Offensive menses, bright red flow, later blood darker and less offensive. Itching of axillae before menses. Eruptions on the face of young women, during scanty menses. Menopausal disorders, flashes of heat, leucorrhea, and painful enlargement of breasts. Neuralgia of the face, ameliorated by kneeling down and pressing head firmly against the floor. Pain extends in all directions from the upper jaw. Rheumatism. Rheumatic pain in right arm and shoulder, worse at night. Cannot raise the arm, but can swing it to and fro. Frozen shoulder. Great affinity for the right shoulder. Right side generally more affected. Symptoms go from right to left. Marked periodicity. Pains in places where the bones are least covered. Cooper gave the case of a woman, 19, who had a condition of her throat from scarlatina three years previously, and lately increasing deafness. There were noises all over her head and vertigo. Sudden flushings in daytime, menses too frequent, and profuse leucorrhea. Backache, paining her to walk, forcing her to give up teaching from the pain. Poor appetite from the headaches and tinnitus, she often had pain behind the angles of lower jaw and swollen glands. All symptoms disappeared after a single dose of Sang, tincture, although at first the leucorrhea was increased. F. Nichol, in giving Hale his experience with Sang, in croup, said he used a solution of Sanguinarine in vinegar, and he found that the most effective preparation. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Just. - bronchial catarrh, coryza, hoarseness, oversensitive. (2) Dig. (migraine). (3) Bell., Iris, Meli., Lach., Ferr., Op. (4) Chel., Op. In rheumatism of right deltoid, Mag-c. (5) Headache extending forward from occiput and settling over right eye, Spig. (6) Headache better by hard pressure, Chin., Indg., Mag-m. (7) Paroxysms of headache ending in profuse urination, Ign., Gels., Verat. (8) Menstrual headache, Sep. scanty flow, Sang, profuse. (9) Right side, throbbing, congestive headache, worse light and noise, Bell. (10) Periodic sick headaches, Iris-v. (11) Pneumonia, Phos., Ant-t. Compatible: Bell. - in scarlatina rashes. It antidotes: Op. Complementary: Ant-t. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Liver - Pain over region of liver. Jaundice. Liver-cough. Lungs - Severe dyspnea and constriction of chest. Asthma with stomach disorders (Nux-v.). Pneumonia, catarrhal, right side, better lying on back. Sudden stoppage of catarrh of air passages brings on diarrhea. Tuberculosis. Hemoptysis from suppressed menses. Cough of gastric origin, relieved by eructation. Cough with burning pain in chest, worse right side. Tough, rust-colored, purulent, offensive sputum, almost impossible to raise. Spasmodic cough after influenza andafter whooping cough. Cough returns with every fresh cold.

Kidneys - Dull, heavy pain across kidneys. Urine dark yellow with jaundice. Copious and frequent, clear, worse at night. Urine high-colored, red sediment. Ardor urine.

Temperature - Fever, heat and delirium. Intermittent fevers, marsh fevers, nervous fever. Fever from pulmonary, hepatic or gastric inflammation. Flushes of heat, rising into face and head with headache. Burning, scanty sweat. Copious sweat, cold sweat. Heat flying from head to stomach. Chill with nausea, headache. Chill and shivering in back. Shaking chill.

full:
PHARMACY - sanguin-n. Sanguinarinum nitricum. Sanguinarine nitrate. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Adenoids. Allergies. Asthma. Borborygmus. Bronchitis. Catarrh. Colic. Colds. Coryza. Coughs. Deafness. Eustachian catarrh. Hayfever. Headaches./n/7uenza. Laryngitis. Pharyngitis. Polyps. Post-nasal catarrh. Quinsy. Stiff-neck. Throat, sore. Tinnitus.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sanguin-n. is a very fine brownish-red powder, pungent, acid, bitter and inodorous. It is soluble in alcohol, ether, water and oils, but not in the same proportion in all. Pure sanguinarine is a pearly- white substance, but when combined with any of the acids the result is a salt of some shade of red, crimson or scarlet. The color of the blood-root may be due to the presence of some native salt of Sanguinarine. Sang-n. was proved in 3x trituration by Professor Owens of Pulte Medical College. Nasal polyps. Acute and chronic catarrh. Acute pharyngitis (Wye.). Smarting and burning in throat and chest especially under sternum. Influenza. Chronic follicular pharyngitis. Lachrymation, pains in eyes and head, sore scalp, sense of obstruction.

Head - Pain in supra-orbital region. Burning pain in forehead and root of nose. Sensation of obstruction and fullness in head, ameliorated by discharge of a large quantity of thick, yellow, sweet-tasting mucus.

Eyes - Sore, aching pain in eyeballs. Burning, pressing aching, and sore pains in eyes. Profuse lachrymation, tears gush out. Redness and soreness of inner canthi. Redness of lids and conjunctiva. Sight dim, as if looking through gauze. Food - Little appetite. Everything tastes dry like chips. Coffee did not taste natural, wanted something succulent, not pungent, but soothing to mouth and throat.

Ears - Obstruction of Eustachian tube. Roaring in right ear. Difficulty in distinguishing sounds.

Mouth - Acrid, burning sensation on tongue. Ulceration on the side of the tongue. Roughness and dryness in mouth and throat. Heat in mouth as if pepper had been taken. Increased flow of mucus and saliva with sneezing and burning in forehead. Bitter taste extending back to root of tongue. Nose' - Dry and burning nostrils. Feels obstructed. Enlarged turbinates at beginning of hypertrophic process. Profuse, watery mucus with burning pain, with pressure over root of nose. Sneezing. Secretion scant, tendency to dryness. Nostrils plugged with thick, yellow, bloody mucus. Small crusts which bleed when removed. Post-nasal secretions stuck to naso-phar- ynx, dislodged with difficulty. Rawness and soreness in posterior sinuses.

Throat - Voice altered, deep, hoarse. Rough, dry, constricted, burning. Right tonsil sore, swallowing difficult. COMMENTS - The catarrhal symptoms of Sanguin-n. appear in great intensity, the nose, eyes, throat and bronchi being affected. Sensation of obstruction and fullness in the head, accumulation of mucus obstructing nose, awakes frequently with dry mouth, the nose being obstructed. Accumulation of mucus behind center of sternum, sense of suffocation, feeling as if air-passages lined with thick, stiff mucus or pus. Heat and tension behind sternum is characteristic and so is expectoration of quantities of sweet-tasting mucus. Expectoration of thin, frothy, very tenacious mucus. Lachrymation, pains in eyes and head, sore scalp, obstructed nose and burning pains throughout all regions were experienced. Symptoms of influenza, even to the loss or perversion of taste. “Sensation arising to nostrils as if he had eaten strong horseradish.” Hale reported the case of Mr. B., 40, dark, had for eight years in spite of continuous old-school treatment, chronic post-nasal catarrh, bronchitis and laryngitis. Voice altered, deep, hoarse, speech with effort, as if from chest. Severe pressure from behind sternum. Mucus membrane dry, raised only a few balls of gray mucus. He spent two winters on St. John’s River, Florida, and was better there, but worse again on his return north. Sanguin-n. 6c trituration, was given every two hours. In one week he was better, there was more moisture in his throat than three had been for two years. Voice markedly better. Sanguin-n. was given every four hours. In ten weeks he regained six pounds of his lost weight and strength in proportion. The voice not having improved in the same degree, Caust. 6c and afterwards Dros. 3c, were given and in sixteen weeks he was perfectly well. Mrs. S., city missionary, 49, had constant hacking cough, raw, sore feeling in throat, sore aching and pressing behind sternum. She was much exposed to cold winds of winter, which set up coryza and irritation. Sanguin- n. 6c. every two hours, enabled her to follow her occupation without suffering and in ten weeks she was completely cured. O. W., 55, subject to frequent attacks of cold in head, throat and chest. After a long drive in open trap contracted a severe cold in head, throat, lungs. Sore and lame all over, frequent sneezing, lachrymation. Next day sore throat very marked, constant tickling in throat-pit, exciting cough, at first short and hacking, but in two days it became violent and convulsive. Bell, and Dros. did little good. Pressure behind sternum became very severe. Sanguin-n. 6c was given every two hours. In four hours copious perspiration came on with frequent sneezing. Next day, sore throat appeared after waking from a troubled and restless sleep, constriction of throat with difficult swallowing, tension across chest radiating from behind sternum. Sanguin-n. was given every hour. In one hour, free discharge from nose set in; three hours, moisture and relaxation of constriction across chest. The discharge was yellow and sweetish-tasting, continued all day. Slept well and woke next morning feeling quite free. But little cough or coryza during the day. The following morning he was quite well. C. Wesselhoeft regarded Sanguin-n. as the simillimum for “New England colds.” Adenoids and polyps have been cured with it. There is great craving for air. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sanguin-t. - exophthalmos. (2) Mydriasis, dim vision. Arum- t., Psor., Kali-bi., Sang. (3) Burning in nostrils, Arum-t. (4)Tenacious mucus, Kali-bi. (5) Hay fever, Psor. (6) Sweet expectoration, Stann. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Sensation of burning in stomach and esophagus. Belching up of putridsmelling gas though she had eaten nothing since morning.

Abdomen - Borborygmus and pains in abdomen, as if diarrhea would set in, with sharp, cutting pains.

Chest - Pressure behind center of sternum. Tightness in the chest. Tension in chest, burning and accumulation of mucus behind center of sternum. Short, hacking cough arising from sensation of tightness in chest.

Back - Stiffness in muscles of left neck and shoulder. Causations - Driving in cold wind, winter weather, exposure.

Limbs - Stiffness in muscles of left shoulder and neck. Lungs - Strong desire for fresh air. Sense of suffocation. Dryness and burning in throat and bronchials. Feeling as if air passages lined with thick, stiff mucus or pus. Chronic nasal, laryngeal and bron chial catarrh. Raises thin, frothy mucus, which is very tenacious. Tickling cough. Short, hacking cough with expectoration of thick, yellow, sweetish mucus. Cough is deep and rattling.

Sleep - Sleep poor, restless from feverish and irritable condition.

Modalities - Worse touch, at night. Pressure aggravates soreness of eyes. Bathing with warm water ameliorates heat in forehead. Headache is ameliorates by discharge of much mucus from nose.

Kidneys - Passed urine every hour during the night. Urine had bright yellow or white sediment.

PHARMACY - sanguin. Sanguinarinum pura. N. O. Papaveraceae. Trituration. Solution in vinegar. Historical dose: All potencies.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sanguin, is a pearly white substance. Thomas noted that in smallest physiological doses it acts as “expectorant,” in large, it causes nausea and still larger vomiting. In repeated doses, it lowers the pulse rate. Useful for croup. Pseudo-membranous croup. Great dyspnea. Hoarse, muffled cough, with complete aphonia. Grasped his throat in agony. Nausea and vomiting. COMMENTS - T. Nichol gave his experience with a solution of one grain of Sanguin, in two ounces of vinegar in cases of pseudomembranous croup. He related the case of W. G., age 5, who had been ill some days. Nichol found him with a hoarse, muffled cough, complete aphonia, pulse 132. Soft palate and fauces covered with pearly, fibrinous exudation, a hissing sound was heard on auscultating larynx. Great dyspnea. The child stretched back his head and grasped his throat in agony. Features swollen and dark. Sangn. acet, was given and in fifteen hours there was notable improvement. In forty-eight hours the boy was out of danger. REFERENCES-Clarke.

PHARMACY - sang-t. Sanguinarinum tartari- cum. Sanguinarine tartrate. Papaveraceae. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Exophthalmos. Mydriasis. Stool, bilious. Vision, dim.

HOMEOPATHIC - Tully and Terry experimented with Sang-t. in considerable doses. Tully said he repeatedly witnessed all the effects of sanguinaria root, save the neuralgic pains and the convulsive disorders, from the use of Sang-t. The most peculiar of the symptoms are starting and protrusion of the eyes, extreme mydriasis, haggard expression and cold surface and cold sweats. REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Sanicula Aqua
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from open air, warmth. Better vomiting. Worse from strain, jarring. Worse motion, raising arm, putting hands behind, descending. Worse cold wind on occiput or neck..
constitution: Amenorrhea. Anterior crural, neuralgia. Asthma. Bedwetting. Bee stings. Boils, blind. Borborygmus. Coccyx, soreness. Condylomata. Conjunctivitis. Constipation, children. Cornea, ulceration. Coryza. Cough. Dandruff. Debility. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Digestion slow. Dropsy, during pregnancy. Eczema. Emaciation. Excoriations. Foot sweat. Gastritis. Gumboil. Sanicula aqua Headaches. Indigestion. Influenza

full:
PHARMACY - sanie. Sanícula aqua. Mineral Springs of Ottawa, Ill., USA. Containing, approximately in grains per gallon, Nat-m. 93, Calc-m. 23.5, Mag-m. 23.25, Calc, bicarb. 14.25, Calc-s. 9.5, Kali-s. 5, Nat-bic. 1, Nat- br. 3, Fe. bi-carb. 1, Nat-i. 12, Sil. 5, Alum. 01 and traces of Lith. bi-carb., Nat-p., Bor. Dilutions of the spring water. Triturations of the evaporated salt. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Anterior crural, neuralgia. Asthma. Bedwetting. Bee stings. Boils, blind. Borborygmus. Coccyx, soreness. Condylomata. Conjunctivitis. Constipation, children. Cornea, ulceration. Coryza. Cough. Dandruff. Debility. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Digestion slow. Dropsy, during pregnancy. Eczema. Emaciation. Excoriations. Foot sweat. Gastritis. Gumboil. Sanicula aqua Headaches. Indigestion. Influenza. Intermittents. Itch, suppressed. Itching. Leucorrhea. Liver, soreness. Lumbago. Marasmus. Melancholy. Milk, thin. Morning, sickness. Motion sickness. Mouth, sore. Neuralgia. Neurasthenia. Night-terrors. Nose, crusts. Ophthalmia, tarsi. Os uterus, dilated. Ossification, early. Ozaena. Perspiration, excessive. Pot-bellied children. Rectum, cramp. Rheumatism. Rickets. Ringworm. Scurvy. Seasickness. Shoulder, rheumatism. Throat, sore. Tongue, burning. Toothaches. Uterus, prolapsed. Uterus, tumor. Vomiting, milk, water. Wrist, boils.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sanie, has sometimes been confused with the plant Sanicula mary- landica. or black snake- root. The water is odorless and colorless, and has an agreeable and slightly alkaline taste. Sherbino proved Sanie, in the potencies and a large number of the symptoms of the provings have been confirmed. It’s a polycrest and anti-psoric of wide range. Guernsey considered Sanie, the chronic of Cham. Sanie, affects the nutrition, female organs, rectum, neck and skin. Useful for bedwetting, seasickness, motion sickness, constipation, etc. Rickets. Marasmus. Thick, acrid, yellow pus. Body smells like old cheese. Bursting in perineum, bowels, bladder, vertex, chest. Shifting pains. Cannot bear to have one part touch another or cannot lie near another person. Enlarged feeling in throat, vagina etc. Child kicks off covers at night, wants to lie on something hard though thin. Clothes feel cold, damp. MIND - Irritable, least word or action would upset her. Misconstrues everything. Crossness quickly alternating with playfulness in children. Headstrong, obstinate, touchy children. Restless desire to go from place to place. Instability of purpose. Does not want to be touched. Constant desire to look behind. Dread of downward motion. Fear of the dark.

Head - Bursting in vertex. As if a cold cloth around brain. Cannot bear cold air on occiput and neck. Profuse sweat on occiput and neck, worse during sleep. Electric crackling in hair when combed. Profuse scab dandruff, falling of hair. Small boils on head that do not mature.

Eyes - Lids agglutinated in morning. Lachrymation in cold, open air or cold application. Eyes burn, exuding a sticky fluid. Ulcerated cornea. Dim sight. Photophobia. Dandruff of the eyebrows.

Ears - Eustachian catarrh. Soreness behind ears with discharge of white, gluey, sticky substance. Stuffed feeling in left ear.

Nose - Sneezing and itching of nose. Nose sore and stuffed with yellow scabs. Fluent coryza, worse eating. Water smells like old, musty rainwater.

Face - Acne about eye and cheek. Itching eruptions in beard, especially under chin, worse when warm. Excoriation of upper lip.

Mouth - Offensive breath. Mouth and palate covered with ulcers, white aphthae. Profuse flow of white, clear, transparent, stringy saliva when teething. Teeth sensitive to cold air, as if they were very thin. Teeth feel too long. Gums sore and painful, worse from eating. Gumboils.

Throat - Dry throat. Hoarseness following sore throat, must clear throat before speaking. Cold, icy sensation, like peppermint. Throat feels too large. Can swallow solids better than fluids. Ulcers with yellowish base on tonsils.

Stomach - Bloating of stomach on beginning to eat. Sensation of a lump in stomach. Thirst little and often, water is vomited as soon as it reaches the stomach. Sour, rancid, burning belchings. Nausea after eating with sick feeling, better from smoking. Vomiting of milk soon after nursing.

Abdomen - Bowels bloated as if they would burst. Sore pains in groin. Loud gurgling, pot-bellied children.

Rectum - Constipation with ineffectual urging. Pain, bursting in the perineum during stool. Even soft stool requires great effort to expel. Stool of one large heavy mass, foul like rotten cheese, or dry, small balls. Stools, misshapen, changeable, involuntary. Stools must be removed or crumbles at the verge of anus.

Male - Increased sexual desire at first, then much decreased. Discharge of semen too early, with little sensation. Scrotum relaxed, clammy sweat about parts. Briny odor of the genitals, a few hours after sex. Child’s parts smell of fish brine even after bathing.

Female - Leucorrhea with strong odor of fish-brine, worse stools. Bearing down as if contents of pelvis would escape, worse jar, walking. Supports the relaxed parts by placing the hand against vulva, better rest. Vagina feels large, cannot stop menstruation. Os cervix open and dilated. Food - Child wants to nurse all the time, yet loses flesh. Craves, salt, bacon or ice cold milk. Eating causes urging for stool, must leave the table. Feels better after eating. Great longing for the spring water. Thirst little and often.

Chest - Tickling under sternum. Great soreness of upper chest, must hold it with hands when coughing. Constitutions - Patients are thin and look old, especially children.

Back - Neck weak and emaciated, child cannot hold its head. Stiff backache, worse least turning, raising arms or putting hands behind him. Must turn whole body to look around. Sits, head forward, to ease the pain. Cold lumbar spine. Lumbago, better lying on right side. Lumbar vertebras as if dislocated or were gliding past each other. As if back is broken in two pieces. As if a damp cloth on sacrum. Causations - Poor diet, strains.

Limbs - Pain in shoulders, worse raising arms or putting them behind back. Hands become sweaty when putting them together. Cold, clammy hands and feet. Burning of palms and soles. Feet as if in cold water. Cramps in feet. Foul foot sweat, chafes toes, destroys shoes or stiffens the hose.

Sleep - Falls asleep after vomiting. Frequent waking at night. Dreams of robbers and cannot sleep until the whole house is searched. Dreams of murder and remorse, lascivious dreams. On waking, child rubs eyes and nose with its fist.

Skin - Eczema exuding sticky fluid, behind ears, on wrists, fingers and toes. Itching, worse by scratching. Skin is dry, brownish, flabby. Skin about neck wrinkled and hangs in folds. Copper-colored syphilitic sores. Fissured hands and fingers. Cracks on fingers. Tendency to small boils that do not mature.

Modalities - Better from open air, warmth. Better vomiting. Worse from strain, jarring. Worse motion, raising arm, putting hands behind, descending. Worse cold wind on occiput or neck.

Tongue - Sides of tongue turn up. Tongue adheres to roof of mouth. Tongue, large, flabby, burning, must protrude to keep it cool, ringworm on tongue. Thick yellow coating on back of tongue. Vertigo - Vertigo on rising from stooping. Vertigo while sitting at table or desk. Vertigo after eating with nausea. Faint, smothering sensation with great desire for open air. Seasick sensation. COMMENTS - Itching skin, eczema, worse bathing (Sil.). Sweaty, smelly feet, particularly in children (Sil.). Fear of the dark, sensitivity to storms (Phos.). Children are very obstinate, stubborn, hard to please. Offensive vaginal discharges that smell like fish brine or dead fish (Hep.). Strong fishy odor in hemophilis, gardnerella and Sanícula aqua trichomonas. Discharge can also smell like rotten cheese. RELATIONS - W. J. Guernsey considers Sanie, the chronic of Cham. Compare: (1) Sil., Phos., (2) The constituents of the Sanie, water, especially Nat-m. and Calc. (3) Dread of downward motion, Bor. (4) Head sweat, Calc., Sil. (5) Soreness behind ears, viscid discharge, Graph., Psor. (6) Ringworm on tongue, Nat-m., Ran-s., Tarax. (7) Drinks little and often, vomits as soon as it reaches stomach, Ars. (8) Symptoms change constantly, Care., Lac-c., Puls. (9) Sphincter not under control, Aloe soc. (10) Stool recedes, Sil., Thuj., must be removed mechanically, Sei. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Liver - Soreness through hepatic region. Enlargement of liver, sensitive to pressure and jar. Lungs - Asthmatic breathing, worse after supper. Wheezing, rattling under sternum, worse during or after eating. Deep, hollow cough with loud rattling, caused by tickling under sternum. Tickling on lying down at night and on waking. Rattling cough, child gags and vomits a mouthful of tough, stringy matter. Expectoration of large, yellow, cheesy masses.

Kidneys - Bursting in bladder with urgent call to pass urine. Frequent, profuse, sudden urination, urging ceases if desire is resisted. Briny urine, stains diaper red. Child cries before urinating, strains to urinate while at stools.

Temperature - The cold air chills him. Chill every day at same time. Whole body feels too hot at night. Begins to sweat as soon as covered. Sticky sweat, particularly on side lain on. High fever every night with sleeplessness.

full:
PHARMACY - santa. Santalum album. Sandalwood. Santalum freycinetianum. Santalum paniculatum. N. O. Santalaceae. India, Sandwich Islands. The oil distilled from the wood. Dilutions with alcohol. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cystitis. Gonorrhea. Kidney pain.

HERBAL - The word “Santalum” is of Persian origin. Sandalwood oil is obtained from several species of Santalum, S. album being the chief. Its chief use in old-school practice is in gonorrhea.

HOMEOPATHIC - Shirtliff observed in a man taking the oil for gonorrhea, soon after each dose, an acute aching pain felt in the kidney region, so severe that if he was standing he was obliged to sit, which slightly relieved. Shirtliff gave the same indication in his case of an elderly man, who looked worn and haggard, complained of pain in region of left kidney from ribs to iliac crest, brought on by walking, better leaning forward, completely better by lying down. Better pressing clenched fist into back. The pain lasted six months and was very acute; Sulph., Berb. and Bry. gave no relief. Santal, (oil), one drop every four hours, soon gave great relief and entirely removed the pain in two months. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

author: Murphy
constitution: Amblyopia. Bedwetting. Blindness. Cataract. Color blindness. Convulsions. Cough. Cystitis. Delirium. Diarrhea. Dysuria. Eyes, paralysis. Enteralgia. Enteritis. Epilepsy. Gastroenteritis. Hallucinations. Hemoglobinuria. Hemiplegia. Hysterical. Incontinence. Nephritis. Infantile remittents. Melancholy. Night, cough. Nosebleed. Photophobia. Strangury. Tetanus. Urination, frequent. Urticaria. Vision,
keynote:

CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Bedwetting. Blindness. Cataract. Color blindness. Convulsions. Cough. Cystitis. Delirium. Diarrhea.…
full:
PHARMACY - sant. Santoninum. Santonin. A neutral active principle obtained from Ciña. N. O. Compositae. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Bedwetting. Blindness. Cataract. Color blindness. Convulsions. Cough. Cystitis. Delirium. Diarrhea. Dysuria. Eyes, paralysis. Enteralgia. Enteritis. Epilepsy. Gastroenteritis. Hallucinations. Hemoglobinuria. Hemiplegia. Hysterical. Incontinence. Nephritis. Infantile remittents. Melancholy. Night, cough. Nosebleed. Photophobia. Strangury. Tetanus. Urination, frequent. Urticaria. Vision, yellow. Vomiting. Worms.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sant, is the active principle of Santonica, the unexpanded flower heads of Cina Artemisia Marítima. Sant, is the favorite anthelmintic of the old school and it has been chiefly given against lumbrici. Fatal poisonings have caused convulsions, left side paralysis, delirium, vomiting and purging. Worm affections, corresponding to the “pain in shocks” (Cina.). Gastro-intestinal irritation, itching of nose, restless sleep, twitching of muscles. Asearía lumbricoides and thread worms, but not tapeworms. Colorblindness and yellow vision. Visual illusions,yellow sight, violent light not recognized, colors not distinguishable. Chronic cystitis. Urine deep saffron color. Chronic gastric and intestinal troubles. Night cough of children. Laryngeal crises and lightning pains of tabes. Spasms and twitchings. Violent convulsions, unconscious, head hot, face flushed, purplish. Spasm begins in face and spreads to limbs. Partial paralysis of one (left) side. Restlessness and prostration. MIND - Delirium. Excited, laughs and sings. Hysterical. Restless and irritable. Wants ev erything, but satisfied with nothing. Profound and unusual depression with irresolution and want of confidence, unfitting him for work of any kind. Melancholy like that produced by jaundice. Coma.

Head - Occipital headache with chronic hallucinations. Head turning and twisting, restless. Dullness of head. Pain in forehead.

Eyes - Dark, blue rings around eyes. Eyes rolled convulsively, distorted, staring. Pupils dilated and insensible. Pressure in eyes. Photophobia with lachrymation. Sudden dimness of sight. Flickering before eyes. Objects seem to totter and dance, visions of figures, cherries, animals. Color blindness, xanthopsia. Yellow soup looks red, blue evening sky looks green, objects look green, white looks yellow, violet. Yellow vision, objects as if in yellow haze or yellow light. Strabismus due to worms.

Nose - Nosebleeds. Hallucinations of smell. Things smell peculiar.

Face - Red, hot face, staring eyes. Face pale. Pale around mouth, worse afternoon. One cheek white, the other one is red. Lips swollen, glistening with the distention. Swelling under chin, left side of face. Face pinched, drawing in of lips over teeth with pinched expression of mouth and nose. Convulsive movements of muscles of face, especially lips and lids. Food - Deficient appetite. Thirst intense, continual for ice cold water.

Mouth - Frothing from mouth. Tongue deep red, dry. Burning pains apparently torment her, as she forces everything into her mouth. Hallucinations of taste.

Throat - The glands of neck, parotid and submaxillary are swollen. Vertigo - Giddiness and intense headaches, every object looks bright green. COMMENTS - A case recorded by Demme was quoted in Brit. Med. Jour., 1892. A boy, 3, was given fifteen tablets over three days by his mother. Each tablet contained 1/3 grain of Sant. The symptoms produced were vomiting, dilatation of the pupils, collapse, cyanosis, dyspnea and finally convulsions. Dilatation of the pupils, collapse, cyanosis, dyspnea, and finally convulsions. After a warm bath with cold applications to the head and spine, consciousness returned. The temperature was 103.5, nosebleed and hemoglobinuria occurred and a scarlatinalike eruption was noticed. The child ultimately recovered. After a dose of 7 centigrams, a child, 2, was seized with prostration, convulsions, cramps and jaundice, followed on the third day by salivation and ulceration of the gum. Less serious but very characteristic are the effects on the senses, especially the sense of sight. Visions of figures have been produced and colored vision is a frequent phenomenon, even when the lower triturations have been used. Yellow is the predominant color, but green and violet vision are also marked. The urine also is yellow colored and stains yellow and is passed with much urging and painful burning. A kind of giant urticaria occurred in one case. Hale recorded that Sant, cured cases of “nervous blindness.” It was given to an old man, quite blind, for worms and his sight partially returned. This led to further trials in which it wrs given in nine cases of cataract and, according to Hale, four were cured, the rest not benefited. Hale also mentioned bedwetting, strangury, chronic cystitis, as having been cured by it. Chronic catarrh of the bladder. Infantile remittents with or without worms,. In one prover there was “sensitiveness of the abdomen.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cina, Teucr., Napht., Nat-m. Phos., Spig. (2) Amaurosis, Benz-d., Carbn-s. (3) Colored vision, Cycl. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Dull pain in pit of stomach. Frequent belchings. Nausea and vomiting. Nausea, better after eating. Vomiting and purging of yellowish, slimy mucus with severe abdominal pains.

Abdomen - Rumbling, very sensitive abdomen. Bruised but soft, hot, full. Severe abdominal pains with vomiting and purging. Every night pain in intestines before stool.

Rectum - Well-marked tenesmus. Purging of watery, flaky, foul-smelling stools, followed by vomiting. Stools copious, grayish, putrid-smelling.

Chest - Paralysis of lungs, needs artificial respiration.

Heart - Pulse is quick and full, rapid, lowered, left absent, right soft and steady.

Limbs - Spasms of limbs. Convulsive jerking of upper limbs. Twitching of hands and feet. Gait unsteady and tottering, staggered. Lungs - Coughed incessantly all night from tickling in larynx and trachea. Breath is rapid, sighing, quick and catchy, rattling.

Sleep - Sleepy, tired. Sleep restless, disturbed, woke unrefreshed with sickness, frontal headache, and deficient appetite.

Skin - Urticaria, with edema of nose, lips, and eyelids, over almost entire lids, with vomiting.

Teeth - Grating teeth during sleep. Teeth clenched.

Kidneys - Nephritis. Feeling of fullness of bladder. Incontinence and dysuria. Bedwetting. Frequent efforts to urinate, only passes a few drops at a time, that color linen yellow. Urine greenish if acid and reddish purple if alkaline. Urine deep saffron yellow, thick, sulphur yellow, greenish. Hemoglobinuria.

Temperature - Whole body icy cold, lips and ears blue, face white as snow. Limbs cold, very clammy coldness. Cold sweats. Hot sweat in occiput, more clammy in front. Violent fever, rapid pulse, burning heat of skin, face puffy, eyes brilliant, fixed.

HOMEOPATHIC - Acute colds, coryza, sore throat, etc. Will often “break up” acold. Worse at night, mental exertion, left side. MIND - Depressed with sleepiness. Apathetic. Utter indifference to pain or possible death.

Head - Stitching pain, supra-orbital, worse left side, evening, motion. Throbbing over orbits. Congestions to head, tired feeling in nape.

Eyes - Violent eye pains. Hot stitches deep in eyeball. Ciliary neuralgia, worse left side. Exophthalmos, worse reading and writing. Increased intra-ocular pressure. Glaucoma. Photophobia.

Nose - Coryza. Stopped up feeling in nose, also itching and sneezing.

Face - Left-sided trigeminal neuralgia, especially supra-orbital.

Stomach - Difficult swallowing. Nausea, heartburn, full feeling not relieved by eructation. Vertigo - Sensation of drunkenness with constant endeavor to go left-wards. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sapin. (2) Verb., Cocc. - both containing Sapin. (3) Quill., Anag., Helon., Sars., Par., Agrostema, Cycl. and others contain Saponin. REFERENCES - Boericke.

Heart - Impulse weak, pulse less frequent. Palpitations with anxiety.

name: Saponinum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better by stool, onset of menses. Better by cold, cold bathing. Better while sitting. Worse by moving, even motion of the eyes. Worse mental labor. Worse by warmth. Worse swallowing. Desire to vomit and defecate, worse when quiet. COMMENTS - Two female provers had marked disturbance of the menstrual functions, especially pain and sufferings before the flow. Miliary eruption, colic and leucorrhea before the menses, pain better but not removed when the flow was established. Severe sore throat, worse right side, was experienced by several provers, and Hills had so much swelling of the tonsils that he was obliged to abandon the proving. Bodily and mental depression. Exophthalmos and strabismus. Roughness of mouth mucus membrane, raised papillae on palate and tongue. Strawberry tongue. Involuntary emission of urine when walking. Nausea and vomiting, colic and diarrhea, “nausea more in esophagus and throat, worse in a warm room.” This worse by warmth was met with in relation to many symptoms and is probably a keynote. At the same time there was much chilliness and lowered temperature is a characteristic feature. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Tough mucus, Kali-bi. (2) Onset of menses ameliorates, Lach. (3) Spleen pain, Cean. (4) Kidney pain, Santa. (5) Worse by movement, moving eyes, Bry. (6) Sleepy but cannot sleep, Bell. (7) Early waking, Bell., Nux-v. (8) Worse in warm room, Puls. (9) As if damp stockings on, Calc., Sanie. ( 10) Strawberry tongue, Frag., Bac. ( 11 ) Involuntary emission of urine when walking, Ferr., Caust. (12) Seneg. REFERENCES-Clarke..
