name: Sarcolacticum Acidum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Worse at night. Worse from movement, from standing upright..
constitution: Addison’s disease. Chronic fatigue. Diabetes. Dyspnea. Headache. Influenza. Lichen planus. Myasthenia. Myasthenia. Myotonia. Neurasthenia. Polyuria. Prostration. Psoriasis. Rheumatism. Raynaud’s syndrome. Rhinitis. Tumors.
keynote:
PHARMACY - sarcol-ac. Sarcolacticum acidum. Sarcolactic acid. Dextrum lacticum acidum. Isomer of lactic acid. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Addison’s disease. Chronic fatigue. Diabetes. Dyspnea. Headache. Influenza. Lichen planus. Myasthenia. Myasthenia. Myotonia.…
full:
PHARMACY - sarcol-ac. Sarcolacticum acidum. Sarcolactic acid. Dextrum lacticum acidum. Isomer of lactic acid. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Addison’s disease. Chronic fatigue. Diabetes. Dyspnea. Headache. Influenza. Lichen planus. Myasthenia. Myasthenia. Myotonia. Neurasthenia. Polyuria. Prostration. Psoriasis. Rheumatism. Raynaud’s syndrome. Rhinitis. Tumors.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sarcol-ac. is formed in muscle tissue during muscle exhaustion. It differs from ordinary lactic acid in its relation to polarized light. It represents a much broader and more profoundly acting drug and its pathogenesis is quite dissimilar from the normal acid. The proving was the work of W. Griggs of the Hering Laboratory, Philadelphia. The experimentation was carried out in 1940 on eleven people (nine men and two women), using the 4x, 6x, 15x, and 30x potencies. Wm. B. Griggs found Sarcol-ac. of great value in the most violent form of epidemic influenza, especially with violent and retching and greatest prostration, when Ars. had failed. Influenza with rhinitis. Locally in the tuberculous ulceration of vocal cords. Intra-muscular lactic acid, following prolonged exercise, which generates fatigue. This chronic fatigue, when pushed to an advanced stage, results in an almost paralyzing weakness with prostration. Spinal neurasthenia, muscular weakness, dyspnea with myocardial weakness. Extreme fatigue, anxiety, prostration. Muscular cramping pains, aggravated by movement. Digestive intolerance. Dryness and itching of the skin. Morning sickness, diabetes and rheumatism offer a field for this remedy. Troubles in the breasts. MIND - Feeling of laziness, weakness. Dejection. Irritability, becomes easily annoyed by the smallest thing.

Head - Headache and vomiting, pain situated on the forehead and above the eyes, ameliorated by going to stool.

Nose - Coryza, throat dry and painful, swallowing impeded, alleviated by day, aggravated at night.

Throat - Constriction in pharynx. Sore throat with tightness in naso-pharynx. Tickling in throat. COMMENTS - According to Dr. Kuhl, lactic acid has an anti-cancerous preventive action and he recommended a special diet with additional lacto-fermented products. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Eup-per. - cracking sensation with acute pains in the bones. (2) Bry. - aggravation by movement. (3) Am. - muscular bruises. REFERENCES - Boericke. Julian.

Stomach - Heavy, painful feeling in the pit of the stomach. Digestive intolerance, especially of cold water. Acrid dyspepsia. Nausea. Uncontrollable vomiting even of water followed by extreme weakness.

Abdomen - Sedative, palliative for gastrointestinal tumors.

Rectum - Burning hemorrhoids. Stools acrid and expulsion of gases in profuse, easing the condition.

Chest - Aortic pain and rapid pulse after exertion.

Heart - Cardiac rheumatism. Raynaud’s syndrome.

Back - Tired feeling in back and neck and shoulders. Paralytic weakness. Cramping pains in the back and lumbar region, aggravated when standing.

Limbs - Psoric rheumatism. Rheumatoid arthritis. Fibrous rheumatism. Paresthesia, joint numbness and pains. Extreme weakness from climbing stairs. Stiffness of thigh and calves. Cramp in the calves. Arms feel as if no strength in them. Wrist tires easily from writing. Writer’s cramp. Difficulty in brushing hair. Lungs - Dyspnea, feeling of cardiac weakness, croupy cough, especially at night. Bronchitis. Dry, painful pleurisy.

Sleep - Difficulty in going to sleep, sleep light when it comes. Wakes aching and exhausted.

Skin - Intense general itching, improved by the cold. Keratotic eczema. Lichen planus. Psoriasis. Scleroderma (Graph.).

Modalities - Worse at night. Worse from movement, from standing upright.

Kidneys - Polyuria. Profuse nocturnal urination. Urine clear with traces of proteinuria.

Temperature - General chilliness with coldness of the limbs. Extreme chilliness in bed. The right hand does not become warm by external heat.

name: Sarothamnus Scoparius
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from cool air, rapid motion, passing flatus. Worse turning on left side..
constitution: Acne rosacea. Albuminuria. Alopecia. Angina pectoris. Bacillary, dysentery. Cheyne-Stokes. Choroiditis. Collagen diseases. Diabetes insipidus. Emaciation. Glaucoma. Hay fever. Heart, disorders. Hodgkin’s disease. Hypertension. Hypotension. Impetigo. Insomnia. Iritis. Kidneys, disorders. Leukemia. Nephritis. Ozaena. Palpitations. Parasites. Pityriasis. Sinusitis. Tobacco, heart. Worms.
keynote:
PHARMACY - saroth. Sarothamnus scoparius. Scotch broom. Spartium scoparium. Cystisus scoparius. Genista scoparia. N. O. Legumi- nosae. Papilionoideae. Europe. The tincture is prepared from the flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne rosacea.…
full:
PHARMACY - saroth. Sarothamnus scoparius. Scotch broom. Spartium scoparium. Cystisus scoparius. Genista scoparia. N. O. Legumi- nosae. Papilionoideae. Europe. The tincture is prepared from the flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne rosacea. Albuminuria. Alopecia. Angina pectoris. Bacillary, dysentery. Cheyne-Stokes. Choroiditis. Collagen diseases. Diabetes insipidus. Emaciation. Glaucoma. Hay fever. Heart, disorders. Hodgkin’s disease. Hypertension. Hypotension. Impetigo. Insomnia. Iritis. Kidneys, disorders. Leukemia. Nephritis. Ozaena. Palpitations. Parasites. Pityriasis. Sinusitis. Tobacco, heart. Worms.

HERBAL - Sarothamnus scopariumis ashrubby tree, widespread throughout Europe. The twigs are used for the extraction of the official spar- tein, the flowers are rich in flavonoids, and the plant contains aromatic amines. Sparteine sulphate, an alkaloid found in scotch broom, causes a lowering of the systolic and diastolic pressures of the provers. It also lowers blood-pressure. Depresses the heart by its poisonous action on the myocardium, and this, with the stimulating action of the drug upon the vagus, accounts for the lowered blood pressure and reduced pulse rate. It weakens the cardiac contraction. The total amount of urine is increased, diuretic properties, useful in dropsy.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hinsdale attempted the first homeopathic proving in 1918, on three students. In 1897, Schier conducted a proving on six people, using the tincture and the infusion of the winter root, as well as the tincture and infusion of the fresh flowers. Mezger undertook a true proving on twenty-seven provers of whom seven were women, at the Robert Bosch Hospital in 1951-52. He used the 4x, and 2x potencies as well as the mother tincture. Saroth. is a heart tonic, affects the kidneys, cord, muscles and left side. Sparteine sulphate increases the strength of the heart, slows it and reduces the blood pressure. Hinsdale reported that it continues the good effects of Verat. and Dig. without any of the undesirable effects of either. Irregular heart action from influenza or other infectious diseases. Arterial hypertension, arteriosclerosis. Relieves the congestion of kidneys enabling them to eliminate and relieve the distress upon the heart. Heavy aching. Cheyne-Stokes respiration. Irregular heart following grip and various infections. Hypotension. Very useful in sustaining heart after stopping habit of morphine. Indicated when primarily the muscles of the heart and especially the nervous apparatus is affected. Acts rapidly and lasts three to four days. Does not disturb digestion. Specific action on the kidneys, enabling them to eliminate and relieve the stress on the heart. Nephritis. Albuminuria. Congestion of the thyroid gland, hands clammy, sleep disturbed, hot flushes, emaciation. Increase in the size of the thyroid. Extreme tiredness. Leukemia with eosinophil. MIND - Irritable, loses his temper at the slightest thing. Irritability from trifles. Inner agitation, ideas escape him. Easily irritated and likely to explode. Excitement at night. Melancholic disposition is upset easily. Apathetic without spirit, distracted. Absentminded. Everything is too much for him, difficulty in concentrating. Weakness of the senses and body. General inhibition, but especially erotic. Obsession with erotic thoughts. Sexual thoughts intrude and crowd around each other.

Head - Pulsating headaches, as if the skull would burst. Headache, as if wearing a helmet, going from the eyes towards the occiput (glaucoma). Congestion in the head. Flashes of heat in head.

Eyes - Chronic glaucoma. Choroiditis. Iritis. Burning and stinging pains, especially behind the left eyeball. Pain on moving the eyes. When looking at an area of light, the brightness of the light and the rainbow colors of the halo seem more intense.

Ears - Monotonous rumbling and crackling in both ears, particularly intense between 7 p.m. and 8 p.m. Buzzing and other noises.

Nose - Hay fever. Ozaena. Maxillary sinusitis. One-sided obstruction. Nostrils blocked alternately. Nasal secretions, streaked with blood and abrasion of the nasal orifices. Tickling in the nose with frequent sneezing. Small new growths on the nasal wall.

Face - Barber's itch.

Mouth - Vesicles on the lips and mouth.

Throat - Irritation of the larynx with dry cough, coming from the throat. Tickling in the throat. Acute and chronic laryngitis. COMMENTS - Weakness of the senses and body. Sensation of uneasiness and cold, which is worrying, only the head needs fresh air. Sensation of coldness, except for the head, which is better in fresh air. Pain in the cardiac region and rhythmic anomalies. Pains and cardiac palpitations with tingling and feeling of soreness, especially when lying on the left side. Palpitations, especially at night and when resting, but also from slight exertion. Violent cardiac pulsations, which shake the whole body. Pulse accelerated. Extra systole, notices the irregularity of the contractions. Left ventricular cardiac deficiency. Angina pectoris. Rhythmic anomaly. Basedow’s heart. Aortitis. Bubbling sensation in the head. Precordial constriction with anguish. Rheumatic pain, moving from right to left. Sudden pain in the left sciatic nerve around 10 p.m. Hollow sensation in the stomach and abdominal repletion. Sleep long in coming. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kalm. - Pains along the nerves from the center to the periphery and from top to bottom. Sudden pain, which moves around. Palpitations, worse when lying on the left side. Pulse slow. (2) Spig. - Violent palpitations with oppression and anxiety. Must lie on the right side with the head high. (3) Iber. - Violent palpitations at the least exertion. Pulse full, irregular. Aggravated in a warm room and when lying on the left side. REFERENCES - Boericke. Julian.

Stomach - Ptosis of the stomach and intestines. Dyspepsia. Aggravation of stomachache by food.

Abdomen - Stomach and bowels seem to be filled with stones or as a firm mass. Spasmodic entero-colitis. Flatulency with much mental depression. Sensation of abdominal repletion and stomach feels hollow. Passage through intestines accelerated with three to six evacuations a day. Bacillary dysentery. Intestinal tuberculosis. Intestinal parasites.

Rectum - Tenesmus, ameliorated by emission of wind. Colic, then bright acrid foaming stools followed by burning in anus. Stools yellow, glairy with tenesmus. Stools hard like balls, covered with mucus and mixed with a frothy diarrhea. Alternating diarrhea and constipation. Hemorrhoids with splinter-like pain.

Male - Loss of libido, genital deficiency and evil-smelling sweating from the genital region.

Female - Excessive menses and long intervals between menses. Menses late and prolonged. Sex drive increased. Loss of libido, genital deficiency and evil-smelling sweating from the genital region. Food - Appetite increases, constant need to eat. Persistent feeling of hunger, despite constant feeling of nausea. Loss of appetite with aversion to food and strangling feeling. Aversion to eggs and meat.

Chest - Angina pectoris. Constriction in the precordial region with sensation of tightness and anguish. Constitutions - Tubercular, thyroidism or nervous. Allergic, psoric constitutions.

Heart - Anxious oppression, radiating to left shoulder and neck. Hypotension. Tobacco heart. Angina pectoris. Irregular action, disturbed rhythm due to gas, feeble in Sarothamnus scoparius nervous hysterical patients. Myocardial degeneration, failing compensation. Pal- pitations with congestion to head.

Back - Pain in the lumbar region.

Limbs - All the muscles are painful, as if stiff. Shooting pains. Sudden pains, regularly in the sciatic nerve. Sciatica. Neuralgic pains, beginning on the right side, moving towards the left and diminishing on the right. Drawing joint pains. Chronic inflammation of the hip. Nocturnal pain in the hips and sacrum, left shoulder, left elbow and fingers of the right hand. Fidgets in the legs, which prevent him from falling asleep. Strumous edema of the legs. Deadness of right arm and fingers. Chilblains. Acrocyanosis. Lungs - Asthma.

Sleep - Insomnia. Sleep long in coming with abundant ideas. Sleep light, easily woken by noise. Waking between 3 a.m. and 5 a.m. Dreams are pleasant and colorful. Dreams at times, about disappearances, murders, deaths. Unrefreshing sleep. On waking, feels tired and has the impression of not having slept enough. Great need for sleep, spends a large part of the day in bed.

Skin - Allergic eruptions. Urticaria. Folliculitis. Boils. Pityriasis. Dysidrosis. Adenitis of the sweat glands. Impetigo. Acne rosacea. Small vesicles, extremely irritating. Eczematous eruption, both damp and dry. Infiltration and bluish coloring in the joints of the toes. Copious nocturnal sweating with a strong odor. Hair stiff, dandruff. Loss of hair in patches. Alopecia.

Modalities - Better from cool air, rapid motion, passing flatus. Worse turning on left side.

Kidneys - Drawing pains in the kidneys with colic pains. Increased urination. Very profuse, bright foaming urine, then burning in the pudendum. Hydronephrosis. Albuminuria. Diabetes insipidus. Frequent need to urinate at night, especially around 5 a.m. Bedwetting.

Blood - Leukemia. Eosinophilia. Attacks of vasodilation at the limbs in the big toe and foot. Breasts - Nodular congestion of the right breast (especially in men).

Temperature - Sensitive to the cold, worse in the evening, feeling of head, sweating, numbness.

name: Sarracenia Purpurea
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better in fresh air, out of bed. Worse about midnight, in the morning, at 3 p.m. Worse rising from lying, trying to walk. Worse in stormy weather. Open air causes chilliness, hands and feet cold, causes head to be hot. sore and feel full. Cold air causes to chilliness and aggravates bone pains..

PHARMACY - sarr. Sarracenia purpurea. Pitcher plant. N. O. Sarraceniaceae. Grows in boggy places from Canada southward. Contains a very active proteolytic enzyme. Tincture of fresh plant. Tincture of root. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

full:
PHARMACY - sarr. Sarracenia purpurea. Pitcher plant. N. O. Sarraceniaceae. Grows in boggy places from Canada southward. Contains a very active proteolytic enzyme. Tincture of fresh plant. Tincture of root. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Back, pains. Bones, pains. Bor- borygmus. Constipation. Coxalgia. Diarrhea. Eruptions, scrofulous. Femur, pains. Herpes. Influenza. Lumbago. Psoriasis. Smallpox. Vision, disordered.

HERBAL - The use of the pitcherplant in smallpox is a discovery of the Native Americans of North America, the spotted appearance of the plant probably suggesting a resemblance to the disease.

HOMEOPATHIC - A proving by T. C. Duncan, Thomas and others brought out symptoms of fever, backache, headache and gastric disturbance. Hale collected much confirmatory evidence of its power to antidote the smallpox poison. Sarr. is a remedy for variola. Congestion to head with irregular heart action. Sick headache, throbbing in various parts, especially in neck, shoulders and head, which feels full to bursting. Visual disorders. Chlorosis. Feels dull and heavy, sweats freely. Insensibility of right side, paralysis of hearing and smell. Debility, heavy, languid. Dull, heavy, sore feeling in all bones. Phlegmonous swelling with a rosy tint on various parts. Unrefreshed though slept soundly. MIND - Melancholy. Great depression of spirits with frontal headache. Dullness of mind. Forgetful. Loss of memory with the headache. Difficult to concentration. Alternate apathy and intellectual activity. Anxious about everything.

Head - Light feeling in head. Sensation as if he had received a knock on the head, drowsiness and staggering gait. Sensation as if head were split.

Eyes - Eyes feel swollen and sore. Pain in orbits. Photophobia. Black objects move with the eye.

Ears - Ringing in ears. Sticking pains deep in right ear, transient but recurring often, same in left ear. Intense earache, fears he will lose his senses. Swelling of parotids.

Nose - Nosebleed nearly producing fainting. Nose swollen, red, with pressure and pulsation at root. Fluent coryza with cold chills and loss of smell. Foul-smelling, green, yellowish, or bloody discharges. Fetid smell.

Face - Face flushed. Heat and redness of face. Face pale with heat and chill alternating. Erysipelatous swelling of face. Miliary eruption. Scaly herpes on face. Intense neuralgic pains from temples to jaws.

Mouth - Tongue is dry, coated brownish white. Mouth dry, lips and mouth parched. Toothache at night in bed, from least contact, and cold air.

Throat - Throat dry, not better by tea or water. Vertigo - Vertigo with cramps in neck, worse at night. COMMENTS - Hering quoted several instances of Sarr. action. The first was a woman far advanced in pregnancy who was cured of smallpox with Sarr. 3c, 6c and 9c, delivery as accomplished during her convalescence, the infant bearing on its body numerous red blotches indicating that it had been affected with the disease. A second case concerned an infant a few months old who was attacked with a grave form of smallpox with variolous angina so severe that it was with difficulty it could take the breast, the mother took Sarr. 3c, 6c and 9c and continued to nurse the infant, which promptly recovered, the mother not taking the disease. In an epidemic occurring in the environs of Wavre, Sarr. was given to two thousand people living in the very middle of the disease and coming in constant intercourse with it, but all who took Sarr. escaped. During the same epidemic, two hundred cases were treated with Sarr. without a death. Bilden, who used the 1 x tincture in an epidemic with success, concluded that San. is to smallpox what Gels, is to bilious fever. HalequotedSurgeon-MajorC. G. Logie’s (an allopath) account of his experience with San. (decoction probably) in smallpox: “Four of the cases in my hospital have been severe confluent cases. They have throughout the disease all been perfectly sensible, have had excellent appetites, been free from pain and have never felt weak. “The effects of this medicine, which I have carefully watched, seemed to anest the development of the pustules, killing, as it were, the virus from within, thereby changing the character of the disease and doing away with pitting.” A number of eye symptoms appeared in the provings and Sarr. has cured disordered vision. A case of “phlyctenoid herpes” has also been reported cured by it. Extreme lassitude and pains in the bones were prominent in the provings. Week feeling in the arms. Very sensitive to cold air. Sarr. has the empty, hungry, sinking sensation of the anti-psorics. Dryness of mouth and throat. Faint after stool. Bladder and rectal tenesmus. Stool smells of musk. The right side was more affected than the left. RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Podo. Compare: (1) In smallpox, Ant-t., Merc., Vac., Vario., Maland. (2) In bone pains, Eup-per. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Sleepy during meals. Empty, hungry feeling, can keep nothing in his stomach. Burning pains in stomach with palpitations and contraction. Pinching pain in stomach, it feels distended and torn. Copious, painful vomiting.

Abdomen - Transient pains in bowels. Bloated about navel. Borborygmi and some pain in bowels with constipation, dry throat.

Rectum - Rectum and anus swollen and inflamed. Much flatus. Much tenesmus, dysenteric diarrhea. Stool copious, dark, fetid, evacuated with great straining, morning. Stools very hard, covered with mucus, and dark. First part of stool natural, last diarrhea. Morning diarrhea, faint after stool. Sensations - Heat in face as if on fire. Left eye as if congested. Swelling in uterus as if from a tumor or dropsy, as if full of cysts. As if bones of leg were too thick.

Female - Bloody discharge at other times menstrual period, as during menopause. Watery or milky leucorrhea. foul-smelling, with spasmodic pains in uterus. Pulsative pains in womb with swelling as if from a tumor or dropsy. Uterus swollen as if full of cysts. Cervix swollen, hot. Miliary eruption and heat in vulva. Food - Hungry all the time, even after a meal. Appetite unusually active. Little appetite, but what is eaten agrees. Great desire to sleep during eating.

Chest - Pains in third and fourth ribs, with great apprehension of heart disease. Pain in angle of ribs. Soreness of pectoralis major.

Heart - Congestion to chest, heavy feeling about heart. Feeling of congestion about head, with irregularity of heart’s action.

Back - Deep-seated pain in back. Pains shooting in zigzag course from lumbar region to middle of scapula. Weakness between the shoulders. Warm sensation passed up back into head. Back weak, wants to lean on something. Pain and soreness in sacrum.

Limbs - Limbs cold when still, as from poor circulation. Weakness of limbs with paralytic debility. Limbs weak, bruised pain in knees and hip joints. Pains and soreness in diaphyses of all long bones. Bones in arm pain. Lungs - Paroxysms of suffocation and nosebleed. Tuberculosis and bronchial disorders. Cough with desire to vomit, and vomiting. Hemoptysis, thick cough, continual tickling in larynx and bronchi. Hard cough, shaking chest and bowels. Expectoration of mucus, tenacious, filamentary, with a bitter, putrid, oily taste.

Sleep - Sleepy in daytime, sleep disturbed by strange and frightful dreams. Awakes early in a fright with urging to urinate.

Skin - Eruptions similar to crusta lactea. Herpes. Psoriasis. Scrofulous eruptions. Smallpox, aborts the disease, arrests pustules.

Modalities - Better in fresh air, out of bed. Worse about midnight, in the morning, at 3 p.m. Worse rising from lying, trying to walk. Worse in stormy weather. Open air causes chilliness, hands and feet cold, causes head to be hot. sore and feel full. Cold air causes to chilliness and aggravates bone pains.

Kidneys - Urine phosphatic, scanty, limpid.

Temperature - Feverish and shaking chills, worse morning. General chills between shoulder blades. Chills, heat, and sweat, 5 p.m. Skin hot and dry. Hands hot, warm all over. Head and body warm. Perspires freely.

Worse from touch, pressure, tight clothes. Worse motion, sitting, going up and down stairs. Worse scratching, yawning. Worse after urinating, before menses, from suppressed gonorrhea..

Emaciation. Eruptions. Eyes, disorders. Faintness. Glands, enlarged. Gonorrhea. Gout. Gravel. Hands, chapped. Headaches. Hernia. Herpes. Hiccoughs. Intermittent fever. Kidney, colic. Kidney, disorders. Marasmus. Mas
keynote: PHARMACY - sars. Sarsaparilla officinalis. Wild licorice. Smilax officinalis. The root of several species of Smilax. N. O. Smila- ceae, by some classed as a sub-order of the Liliaceae. Triturations and tincture of the dried rhizome. Historical dose: Tincture and all…
full:
PHARMACY - sars. Sarsaparilla officinalis. Wild licorice. Smilax officinalis. The root of several species of Smilax. N. O. Smila- ceae, by some classed as a sub-order of the Liliaceae. Triturations and tincture of the dried rhizome. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Bedwetting. Bladder, disorders. Blood, disorders. Bones, disorders. Breast, scirrhous. Bright’s disease. Constipation. Cystitis. Cracks, skin. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspepsia. Dysuria. Emaciation. Eruptions. Eyes, disorders. Faintness. Glands, enlarged. Gonorrhea. Gout. Gravel. Hands, chapped. Headaches. Hernia. Herpes. Hiccoughs. Intermittent fever. Kidney, colic. Kidney, disorders. Marasmus. Masturbation, effects. Melancholy. Menopause. Mercury, abuse. Mycosis. Nephritis. Nipples, retracted. Plica polonica. Rheumatism. Seborrhea. Spermatic cords, swelling. Spermatorrhea. Stones. Strangury. Syphilis. Ulcers. Warts.

HERBAL - The dried root or rhizome of sarsaparilla, as imported, is of the thickness of a goose quill, many feet in length, reddish brown, odorless, mucilaginous in taste, feebly bitter, and faintly acrid. It was historically reputed, according to Mile, to be a diaphoretic tonic, alterative. It was given in scrofula and secondary syphilis and the concomitants of these diseases such as ulcers, cutaneous eruptions, nodes indurated glands, decay, and necroses. Joint swellings and rheumatism often improve under a protracted course of it. Some think it a kind of restorative after an exhausting course of mercury.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hahnemann proved Sars., confirming many of the historical uses. Sars. is “restorative ” after over-dosing with Merc., because it is a homeopathic antidote to Merc. It covers the syphilitic, sycotic and psoric constitutions. Affinity for the genito-urinary organs, skin, bones, and lower right extremity. Marasmus, emaciation. Kidney colic. Marked urinary symptoms. Moist eruptions about the genitals or between the scrotum and thighs. Periosteal pains due to venereal disease. Retraction of nipples in those of cancerous inheritance or constitution. Clears the complexion. Eruptions following hot weather and vaccinations, boils and eczema. Fig warts. Scratching causes itching to begin in another place, causes eruption on forehead to become humid. Parts feel screwed together. Nightly bone pains. Pains shoot in different directions and are accompanied by depression and anxiety. As if salt were put upon the wound. Very sore, gouty nodes. Rheumatism. MIND - Depression and anxiety from pain. Despondent, gloomy without any cause. Ill humored and taciturn. Sensitive, easily offended.

Head - Itching and humid eruption of forehead. Moist eruption on scalp. Scalp sensitive. Crusta lactea beginning in face. Shooting pain from above right temporal region. Pains from occiput to eyes or to root of nose. As of a painful tight band around the head. Periosteal pains due to venereal disease. Pains cause depression.

Eyes - Foggy vision, worse seminal emission. Itch like eruptions on eyelids.

Ears - Words reverberate in ear to the root of nose.

Nose - Stoppage for years. Swelling at the root of nose.

Face - Yellow, wrinkled, old looking. Eruptions on face and upper lip, worse during menses.

Mouth - Aphthae, salivation. Offensive breath. Metallic taste, no thirst. White tongue. Pain in jaw, worse bending head back.

Stomach - Sensation of emptiness after a meal as while fasting, or else nausea or disgust when thinking of what has been eaten. Drinking water causes vomiting.

Abdomen - Rumbling with sensation of emptiness. Much flatus, rumbling and fermentation. Colic and backache at the same time, with diarrhea. Cholera infantum.

Rectum - Cholera infantum. Obstinate constipation with frequent want to urinate. Sand in stools. Sensations - As if in a dream. Buzzing as if a large bell had been struck in head. As if he had been hit with a hammer on top of head. As of a great weight in head. As if breath were stopped by a spasm. Breastbone as if bruised. As if chest were too short. Limbs as if paralyzed. As if fingertips ulcerated or as if salt were put on a wound.

Male - Genitals moist and offensive. Itching on scrotum and perineum. Herpetic eruption on genitals. Syphilis, squamous eruption and bone pains. Intolerable stench on genitals. Bloody semen. Spermatic cord painful after emission, swollen after unrequited sexual excitement. Jerking along urethra.

Female - Moist eruption and soreness in right groin before menses. Menses late and scanty. Dysmenorrhea, with retracted nipples or sore breast.

Back - Emaciation of neck. Backache with colic. Pain from small of back down the spermatic cord after emission.

Limbs - Rheumatism, bone pains, worse at night. Rheumatic pains after gonorrhea (Thuj.). Paralytic, tearing pains. Affections of any kind in general in right lowerlimb. Trembling of hands and feet. Burning on sides of fingers and toes, under nails. Deep cracks on fingers and toes, worse sides. Cutting sensation under nails (Petr.). Tetter on hands, ulceration around ends of fingers (Psor.).

Sleep - Yawning. Complaints concomitant to yawning. Worse when yawning. Sleep early in evening. Nocturnal sleeplessness and frequent waking. Frightful dreams.

Skin - Emaciated, shriveled, skin lies in folds (Abrot., Sanie.). Dry, flabby skin. Skin hard, indurated. Cracks on hands and feet. New skin cracks and burns. Itching, scaly spots. Dry, itching rash from exposure to open air, comes on in spring, becomes crusty. Summer cutaneous disorders. Herpetic eruptions, ulcers. Irritating pus. Copper-colored eruptions. Ecchymoses in old age. Edema.

Modalities - Better from uncovering neck and chest, warmth. Standing improves difficult urination. Worse at the close of urination. Worse from cold, wet, dampness, spring, at night. Worse from touch, pressure, tight clothes. Worse motion, sitting, going up and down stairs. Worse scratching, yawning. Worse after urinating, before menses, from suppressed gonorrhea.

Kidneys - Pain from right kidney downward. Kidney colic and painful urination, in infants. Child screams before and while passing urine. Gravel.

Bladder - Bladder distended and tender. Tenesmus of bladder. Urging to urinate before menses. Pain at meatus, in urethra going back to abdomen. Jerking along the urethra. Can pass urine only when standing, urine dribbles while sitting. Urine passes in thin, feeble stream. Urine scanty, slimy, flaky, sandy, pus, bloody. Air passes from bladder during urination. Crusty urinary sediment. Sand on diaper. Severe pain at conclusion of urination. Breasts - Sore, shriveled breasts. Nipples retracted or cracked, small and shriveled. Nipples retracted before menses. Constitutions - Anti-syphilitic and anti- sycotic. Suited to children with faces like old people and enlarged abdomens, to thin, frail, shriveled, old looking persons. To dark-haired persons, and to lithic or sycotic diathesis.

Temperature - Chill starts from region of bladder to back. Influenza. COMMENTS - Sars. chiefly affects the urinary organs, genitals, rectum, skin and bones, right lower extremity, right lower side inner, and one-sided head. General “sinking” sensation of the great anti-psorics. General sensitiveness. Acute and chronic bladder infections. Kidney stones, and the tendency to form kidney stones. Acute kidney stone colic (Berb.). Cystitis. Bladder infections in children, the child screams when they feel the urge because they anticipate the pain (Petros.). Cannot pass urine freely except when standing, dribbles when sitting. Excessive pain in urethra that runs back into abdomen. Great pain and burning at end of urination (Equis.). Tenesmus. Urine is turbid, full of flakes and mucus or gravel, red or gray sand, or particulate matter. Urine with mucus or blood. Gonorrhea, and the effect of suppressed gonorrhea. Herpes. Moist eruptions on scrotum and thighs. Spermatorrhea with swollen cords. The semen may be bloody. Offensive odor about genitals in both sexes. “Moist eruption in right groin before menses.” Painful and disordered menstruation. Nipples are soft, unexcitable, retracted, inverted. Cracked nipples (Cast-eq.), associated with cancer (Aster., Phyt.). Breast abscesses (Phyt.), with inverted nipples. Scirrhus of the breast. Helpful in patients of cancerous history with retracted nipples. Herpetic eruptions in all parts. Moist and dry tettery eruptions. Cracks. Itch-like eruptions, prone to appear in spring. Itching eruption on forehead during menses. Emaciation, causing the skin to be shriveled and lie in folds. Pains shoot in different directions. Anxiety accompanies the pains, and can cause depression. Warmth generally relieves. Warm diet aggravates, cold diet relieves. Warm room aggravates vertigo. Washing, bread and yawning aggravates. Grimmer wrote, “Ulcers, cutaneous eruptions, nodes indurated glands, decay, necroses, joint swellings and rheumatism often improve under a persistent course of this remedy.” One of Sars. popular uses was for “clearing the complexion.” When it succeeds it is by virtue of its similarity, for Clarke saw a very extensive crop of blotches it produced in a young woman. Farrington offered several indications for Sars., including sycotic eruptions with little spots scarcely raised above the skin, often scaling a little, but looking like the roseola of syphilis and itching intolerably, worse in spring. Moist eruption on scalp, the pus from which causes the inflammation of any part it touches. Sycotic headache, beginning at back of head, coming forward and settling at root of nose with swelling of nose. Moist eruption about genitals or between the scrotum and thighs. With Sars., Skinner cured many cases of retraction or flattening of the nipple in nursing women. On two occasions with high potencies of Sars. he enabled a woman to nurse her child when it was utterly hopeless. ELATIONS - Antidoted by: Bell., Merc. It antidotes: Merc. Compare: (1) Berb., Lyc., Nat-m., Petr., Sass. (2) Saur. - Lizard’s tail - irritation of kidneys, bladder, prostate and urinary passages. Painful and difficult urination, cystitis with strangury. (3) Cuc- c. - Watermelon, infusion of the seed acts promptly in painful urination with constriction and backache, relieves pain and stimulates flow. Compatible: Hep., All-c., Phos., Rhus-t., Sulph., Sep. Complementary: Merc., Sep. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer. Murphy. Phatak.

author: Murphy

full:
PHARMACY - sass. Sassafras officinalis. N.O. Lauraceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HERBAL - Sassafras is a warm, aromatic stimulant, alterative, diaphoretic, and diuretic. Also used in diseases of the kidneys and bladder. The oil is said to relieve the pain caused by menstrual obstructions, and pain following parturition, in doses of 5 to 10 drops on sugar, the same dose having been found useful in gleet and gonorrhea. Dr. Shelby of Huntsville stated that it would both prevent and remove the injurious effects of tobacco. The mucilage of the pith (2 drachms to 1 pint of water) is used as a local application in acute ophthalmia, and is a demulcent drink in disorders of the chest, bowels, kidneys, and bladder. Externally, as a rubefacient, in painful swellings, sprains, bruises, rheumatism, etc., and is said to check the progress of gangrene. A lotion of rose-water or distilled water, with sassafras pith, filtered after standing for four hours, is recommended for the eyes. An infusion of the bark administered internally and applied externally is reputed an excellent treatment for rhus poisoning. Dr. King has also derived some benefit from its internal use in gonorrhea and obstinate gleet, 5 to 10 drops on sugar, 3 times a day. REFERENCES - King. Murphy.

HOMEOPATHIC - The Saur, plant is…
full:
PHARMACY - saur. Saururus cernuus. Lizard’s tail. N. O. Piperaceae. The entire plant including the root is macerated in twice its weight of alcohol. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Cystitis, Kidneys, disorders. Prostate, disorders.

HOMEOPATHIC - The Saur, plant is an indigenous perennial found in swampy localities in some parts of the United States. It has been and is still used in domestic practice for those conditions for which Dr. Phares commended it, including irritation and inflammation of the kidneys, bladder, prostate and urinary passages. Phares considered it peculiarly adapted to all such cases if they were attended by strangury or painful difficult urination. He used the remedy both externally and internally and he found that the stomach was very tolerant of the rather heroic doses he prescribed. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Canth., Berb. REFERENCES - Anshutz.

CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Gastro-enteritis. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Scam, is a drastic cathartic, producing copious watery evacuations and griping. Scam, must be compared with Jalap., another purging convolvulus. Spren- gel recorded a case of fatal poisoning in an infant whose mother took a large quantity of Scam, and herself suffered no effects. Symptoms includedswdden vomiting and copious green stools, distention and sensitiveness of the abdomen, and finally death.

Stomach - Sudden vomiting. Pain in stomach with the bowel movements. Inflammation of mucus membrane attended with - loss of appetite and headache. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Abdomen - Distention and sensitiveness of abdomen. Violent pain and rapid succession of stools, leaving inactivity of lower intestines for several days.

Rectum - Copious green stools. Loose evacuation of feces with slight pain in stomach. Rapid succession of stools.

author: Murphy
constitution: Albuminuria. Nephritis. Scarlet, fever. Skin disorders. Throat, sore.
relationships: Compare: (1) Apis, Ars., Rhus-t., Morbill., Diph. REFERENCES - Clarke..

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Nephritis. Scarlet, fever. Skin disorders. Throat, sore.

full:
PHARMACY - scarl. Scarlatininum. Scarlet fever nosode. Nosodes. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Nephritis. Scarlet, fever. Skin disorders. Throat, sore.

HOMEOPATHIC - Scarl. has been used, like other nosodes, for the prevention and cure of the disease from which it takes origin. Its well-known affinity for the skin, throat and kidneys suggests its applicability for disorders of those organs. COMMENTS - Zinke reported a case in which a patient suffered from angina with hyperthemia. Profound asthenia and infectious look. Grave hyperthemia of tonsils swollen, pillars, the uvula dark red, the submaxillary glands swollen, painful. The patient had suffered from scarlatina treated by penicillin. Since that time the general condition was bad. Zinke prescribed Scarl. 12x, twice 2 globules the first day. Immediate amelioration which the patient had not had till then. Repeated once 12 and 14 days after one dose of Scarl. 30x. The patient was cured. RELATIONS - Bell, is the nearest analog and should be its antidote and the various Mercuries come next.

Compare - (1) Apis, Ars., Rhus-t., Morbill., Diph. REFERENCES - Clarke.

W. Poulson on a young woman who ate a few berries after dinner, as well as on himself. He ate the leaves as well as the berries and experienced heartburn, griping in liver and “a kind of drawing sensation a in the spinal cord and cerebellum.” Abdomen - Rolling and flatulence in the bowels. Griping sensation in the liver.

Stomach - Long continued vomiting, “as if all the bowels would be emptied out.” Vomiting very painful, as the vomiting subsided diarrhea came on, the diarrhea being painless. Heartburn, dryness of esophagus. RELATIONS - Compare: Anae., Rhus, Com. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Rectum - Painless diarrhea following painful vomiting. Profuse diarrhea continuing all night.

Back - Drawing sensation as in the spinal cord and cerebellum.

full:
PHARMACY - scler-b. Scleranthus. Scler- anthus annuus. The flowering sprigs are placed in a bowl of water and left in the sun for several hours. The water is strained subsequently and used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.

HOMEOPATHIC - Scler-b belongs to Bach’s group For Those who Suffer Uncertainty, with Cer-b., Gent-b., Gors-b., Hom-b. and Wld-o-b. States of indecisiveness and vacillation between options. The body is marked by a changeability of symptoms as well. Symptoms may alternate between mental, emotional and physical states. Vacillating between feeling loved and rejected. Bipolar disorders, manic-depressive states, dissociative personality disorders, such as multiple personality disorder and in conversion disorder (Chic-b., Heath-b.). Hysterical neurosis when symptoms vacillate between extremes. Quick changes in weight. Travel sickness due to disturbance in equilibrium. After head injuries (Horn-b., Must- b., Wld-o-b.), when the mind is imbalanced or over-stimulated, with a sense of chaos. Susceptibility to lung tuberculosis, other lung conditions. Gives mental calm and restores the mind’s ability to be in charge, to regain an overview (Elm-b.). State of prolonged indecisiveness, usually in regard to a vital decision, has been found to precede the onset of illness. MIND - Inner uncertainty. Unable to come to a satisfying decision. Changes mind frequently. Preoccupied, over stimulated with internal arguments, disoriented and exasperated. Dread about possibly making the wrong choice paralyzes the mind. Over stimulated by details and cares. Confusion. Inability to calm the mind. Feels overwhelmed, inadequate. Emotional instability, Capriciousness, mood swings. Too easily impressed, overreacts. Sudden interest and disinterest. REFERENCES - Bach.

full:
PHARMACY - scol. Scolopendra morsitans. Centipede. Centipeda. The insect is triturated with sugar of milk in the usual way. Tincture of whole animals. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Backache. Constipation. Convulsions. Deafness. Dysmenorrhea. Gangrene. Headache. Hyperacidity. Leucorrhea. Malignant pustule. Nausea. Vertigo. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - When the centipede bites, it secretes a very active venom which contains cyanhydric acid and sulphuric acid. Swelling, pain inflammation and gangrene of the bitten part, often with appearance like malignant pustule. Vomiting and precordial anxiety. In one fatal case the paroxysms of vomiting increased in intensity until the child, in a convulsive struggle, ceased to breathe. In the case of a man bitten in the arm by a centipede, reported in the Nashville Jour- Scolopendra morsitans nal of Medicine, 1870, among the striking symptoms was no perspiration in the arm for three months. Dr. Sherman of California reported the following symptoms as prominent in a woman bitten by a centipede: vertigo with blindness, worse in the morning, nausea and vomiting, unable to retain either food or liquid. Terrible pain in back and loins, spasmodic and irregular, at times extending down the limbs. Pains returned every few days for three weeks, commencing in the head and going out at the toes. “Resembled labor pains as nearly as anything I ever saw.” MIND - Severe headache that makes him think that he has some brain tumor. Fear he is going to lose his mind. Delusion that he has been bewitched. Awakes with fear and a start. Loss of memory.

Head - Headaches in forehead. Sensation as if the head would split open. Burning pain. Piercing sensation. Vertigo.

Eyes - Burning in the eyes. Pupil is red. Inflammation of the cornea. Sensation of gravel. Sensation as if the eye would burst. Sensation of pressure over the eyes. Weakness of vision.

Nose - Sinusitis with severe pain in the forehead. Acute rhinitis. Itching and sneezing. Greenish discharge.

Mouth - Burning of the tongue with diminution of the taste. Tongue is coated. Bad breath. Severe toothache, especially on the left side.

Stomach - Hyperacidity. Burning in the stomach. Sensation of fullness. Nausea. Vomiting of a pale yellow, glairy matter, continued at short intervals with increasing violence. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Clarke.

Abdomen - Tympanitis. Weakness in the epigastrium.

Rectum - Severe constipation. Stool is hard. Stool of a strong odor.

Female - Irregular menstruation. Menses, the blood is black and coagulated. Dysmenorrhea. Leucorrhea, purulent discharge. Inflammation of the uterus and the vagina. Itching in the nipples. Food - Anorexia.

Chest - Pain in the chest on the right side. Ears - Severe pain in the ears. Itching in the ear. Abundant wax. Buzzing noise. Deafness.

Heart - Precordial anxiety.

Limbs - Feet cold and aching. Cramps from the feet up to the calf. Arm greatly swollen. Erysipelatous blush extending half over arm. No perspiration on right arm. Lungs - Respiration short. Dry cough. Mucus rales. Expectoration purulent.

Skin - A large red spot, becoming black in the middle. Malignant pustules, associated with swelling of lymphatic glands. Violent itching, followed by violent pain in bitten part.

keynote: PHARMACY - scroph-n. Scrophularia nodosa. Knotted figwort. Scrophularia mary- landica. American variety introduced from Europe and Asia. N. O. Scrophulariaceae. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Apply locally to cancerous glands (Semp.). Historical dose: Tincture and all…
full:
PHARMACY - scroph-n. Scrophularia nodosa. Knotted figwort. Scrophularia mary- landica. American variety introduced from Europe and Asia. N. O. Scrophulariaceae. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Apply locally to cancerous glands (Semp.). Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Adenoma. Appendicitis. Bedwetting. Breast, disorders. Breast, tumors. Cancer. Colic. Crusta lactea. Deafness. Dyspepsia. Eczema. Eyes, disorders. Glands, enlarged. Hemorrhoids. Hodgkin's disease. Liver, pains. Lymphoma. Nodosities. Palms, cramp. Pemphigus. Peritonitis. Rheumatism. Sigmoid flexure. Sleepiness. Stiff-neck. Ureter, pain.

HERBAL - The plants of the genus Scrophularia generally have an unpleasant smell. The generic name is derived from the supposed property of the roots to cure scrofula. The Treasury of Botany noted that a decoction of one of the common British species, S. nodosa, is sometimes used by farmers to cure the scab in swine.

HOMEOPATHIC - Scroph-n., according to Dr. Cooperof London, has an especial affinity for breast tissue. Adenoma and cancer come within its curative range. Enlarged glands. Hodgkin’s disease. Epithelioma. Nodosities in the breasts (Scirr.). Breast tumors. Scrofulous swellings (Cist.). Threatened abscesses that show no sign of disappearing. Lupoid ulceration. Tubercular testis. Eczema of the ear. Vaginal itching. Painful hemorrhoids. Pain in all flexor muscles. Cutting pains in the joints (Rhus-t.), but more intense and longer-lasting, worse by rest and i n open air, better in warm room. Darting pain from knee to ankle joints, which feel stiff. Weakness, languor, wants to lie down. MIND - Despondency, much troubled about the past and very apprehensive about the future. Miserable and sluggish feeling in mind when moving about.

Head - On rising, indescribable pain and fullness in head, especially occiput and vertex, causing congestion of conjunctive with puffiness, followed by nosebleed. Heaviness and distress in head, as after eating too much. Pain at exit of right facial nerve from hypo-mastoid foramen, darting to right eye. Headaches above the eyebrows while walking. Severe headache through temples, appearing every morning, extending to vertex and occiput. Severe, sharp pain in vertex, forehead and temples, dull and throbbing, returning periodically, worse resting, worse in open air, worse leaning forward, worse by study. Eczema behind ear.

Eyes - Scrofulous keratitis. Sore eyeballs. Severe cutting pains in eyes, unable to move them, passed off with profuse sweat. Distressing photophobia (Con.). Black spots before eyes. On closing the eyes visions of objects. Pulsating stitches in right eyebrow. Blepharospasm.

Ears - Inflammation about auricle. Deep ulcerated auricle. Eczema around ear, behind right ear. Ringing in ears and sudden loss of hearing. Deafness in bull-necked boys. Deafness before and after menses, improving during the flow.

Nose - Dry coryza.

Face - Pleasant warmth in cheeks. Recurrent periostitis of lower jaw in a syphilitic.

Mouth - Bitter taste. Accumulation of sweetish water in several parts of tongue. Sick, sticking taste just above pit of throat, frequently lasting an hour with sensation as if a soft substance (a plug of mucus) were lodged there. Increased saliva, then dry mouth. Teeth feel loose. Pain in carious teeth, worse upper jaw. Gums bleed freely.

Throat - Thick, tenacious, offensive mucus in throat in forenoon. Rancid taste in throat with great weakness and stiffness in hollows of knees. Irritation of esophagus. Vertigo - Dizziness, fullness and pressure in vertex. Vertigo in top of head when standing, even with severe aching in supra-orbital region. COMMENTS - Scroph-n. was proved by Franz, and later in America by W. H. Blakeley, who took from 10 to 60 drops of the tincture several times a day. Blakeley’s proving showed pain in sigmoid flexure. Both Franz and Blakely noted pains in the liver. The most remarkable of Franz’s Scroph-n. symptoms included excessive drowsiness in forenoon, in afternoon, and before and after eating. Sensation of a soft body in the gullet. Constriction of the chest. Oppression of chest with trembling as after much weeping. A sickly, giddy feeling with a sense of weakness and sinking at pit of chest, too weak to speak, along with pain from forehead to back of head. Most of these symptoms were confirmed by Blakeley. Gerard mentioned “hard kernels” and painful, swollen hemorrhoids as its indications. Cooper saw Scroph-n., in the form of a poultice, relieve peritonitis affecting the lower abdomen. Colic from slight vexation occurred in Franz’s proving. Cooper gave Scroph-n. to a patient who had been poisoned by an Indian arrowpoison which produced inflammation and suppuration of the glands. Scorph-n. relieved a most painful condition of the rectum and purulent discharge that had kept up for years afterwards. Cooper reduced strumous glands with it, cured deafness in a “bull-necked” patient, and cured a case of sycosis using Scroph- n. externally as well as giving it internally. ’ “Nodosities in the breast” is another indication of Cooper’s. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Bry. - chest symptoms. Compare: ( 1 ) Dig., Euphr., Grat. (2) Pains in joints worse by rest, better in warm room, Rhus-t. (3) Sleepiness, Nux- m., Op., Lup. Lob-e., Ruta, Care., Con., Aster. Followed well by: Dig. in enlarged glands. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Cooper. Murphy.

Stomach - Appetite greatly increased at first, later nausea with weakness and oppression at epigastrium. Feeling as if he had missed his regular meal. Dyspepsia.

Abdomen - Eczema around the navel. Peritonitis. Pain in sigmoid flexure. Pain in right hypochondrium, worse deep inspiration or lying right side. Twistingpinching pain in umbilicus (left side). Dull, heavy, periodic pain worse when abdomen compressed, legs extended. Colic just below navel. Griping below naval, in the side in afternoon, 7 a.m., after a slight vexation. As a local remedy for appendicitis.

Rectum - Rectal pain. Several stools daily with tenesmus. Painful, bleeding, protruding hemorrhoids.

Female - Recurring metritis with painful hemorrhoids. Irritation, soreness and burning in vagina and anus.

Chest - Oppression with tremulous movement as from much weeping. Constricted feeling, which causes uneasiness. Cramplike pain transversely across lower chest. Stitches in right chest, about 6th rib with shivering. Violent pinching stitches near right last true ribs, while walking during rest, seeming to be in liver.

Heart - Anguish in précordia, worse after food. Indescribable sensation in heart, with severe audible palpitations. Pulse full, regular.

Back - Pain in spinal column with slight opisthotonos. Stiff neck with pain and contraction of right sternomastoid muscle.

Limbs - Drawing rheumatic pain in all flexors of arms and legs. Tingling in limbs as from a blow on a nerve. Deep-seated cutting pain in all muscles of arms. Tingling or buzzing in arms and hands. Sticking and drawing in right palm from joints of fingers to middle of hand as far as carpal bones, muscular cramp of palms.

Sleep - Great drowsiness in morning, with weariness and fullness in whole body. Sleep irresistible before and after a meal. Prolonged afternoon sleep.

Skin - Irritating vesicles on inside of lip, loaded with spindle-celled epithelium.

Modalities - Better in warm room. Worse lying on right side, in morning. Worse pressure, rest, after food. Worse deep breathing, breathing cold air and studying in cold air.

Liver - Cutting, pains in liver on pressure. Lungs - Violent dyspnea, oppression of chest with trembling. On turning on either side, violent dyspnea, worse on right, with cutting in liver on pressure. Asthma in scrofulous patients. Pain about bifurcation of trachea. Pain in right lung, on taking a deep inspiration, which causes cough without expectoration. Cutting in upper left lung, worse breathing cold air.

Kidneys - Pinching and tearing as if in ureter, extending from anterior superior spine of ilium down to pubis. Increased secretion of urine with burning in urethra. Frequent, scanty emission of urine in afternoon. Bedwetting.

Temperature - Chilliness for several hours on moving about in cool air, after rising in morning, passing off with profuse sweat, followed by stupor and absence of all symptoms. Body feels dry and hot with burning sensation, followed by profuse sweat.

name: Scutellaria Laterifolia
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better by sleep. The hemicrania is better moving about in open air. Headache worse from motion. Worse by overwork or over-exertion. Worse by work or excitement..
constitution: Ardor, urine. Brain, irritation. Chorea. Delirium tremens. Dentition. Diarrhea. Exophthalmos. Flatulence. Headache. Hiccoughs. Hydrophobia. Hysteria, insomnia. Nervousness. Night-terrors. Sleeplessness. Tobacco-heart.
keynote:

CLINICAL - Ardor, urine. Brain, irritation. Chorea. Delirium tremens. Dentition. Diarrhea. Exophthalmos. Flatulence. Headache.…
full:
PHARMACY - scut. Scutellaria laterifolia. Skullcap. Mad-dog. N. O. Labiatae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Ardor, urine. Brain, irritation. Chorea. Delirium tremens. Dentition. Diarrhea. Exophthalmos. Flatulence. Headache. Hiccoughs. Hydrophobia. Hysteria, insomnia. Nervousness. Night-terrors. Sleeplessness. Tobacco-heart.

HERBAL - Hale, who introduced Scutellaria into homeopathy, noted that it is in the domestic practice of North America with the equivalent usage ofvalerianin Europe. “Its calming effects on the nervous system have been known ever since the settlement of New England.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Scut, is a nervous sedative. Nervous fear or excitement predominates. Chorea, twitching of muscles. Restlessness. Chronic fatigue. Tired weak feeling. Uneasiness. Languor. Nervous weakness after influenza. Nervous irritation and spasms of children during dentition. Cardiac irritability. Tobacco-heart. Like its relation, Lycopus, it caused weak and irregular action of the heart and protrusion of the eyes. Hale used Scut, with success in sleeplessness, night-terrors, hysteria, nervous agitation from pain or exciting emotions, cerebral irritation of children from dentition or intestinal irritation. MIND - Confusion of mind. Fear of some calamity. Apathy. Irritability. Inability to study orfix the attention on one’s work (Aeth.).

Head - Dull, frontal headache. Migraine, worse over right eye. Nervous sick headaches, worse noise, odor light, better night, rest. Explosive headaches of school teach-ers with frequent urination, headaches in front and base of brain.

Eyes - Aching in eyeballs. Eyeballs painful to touch. Eyeballs feel too large, pressed outwards.

Face - Flushed face.

Mouth - Bad taste, sour, bitter.

Throat - Sensation of lump in throat which could not be swallowed. COMMENTS - Provings by G. W. Gordon and G. H. Royal gave the homeopathic data. Royal’s provers took 3x and 30x. Gordon took repeated doses of 10 to 50 drops. Royal had this indication for Scut, given to him by a friend: “Nervo-bilious headache with the nervous symptoms uppermost and nothing the matter with her.” He related the case of Miss M., 32, who was the head of a large school, complained of being used up, unable to sleep or think. Pain in head almost constant, sometimes frontal, mostly at base of brain. Whenever called upon to overdo herself, she could not sleep that night and then there is either a nervous explosion the following day or a nervous sick headache, either being followed by complete collapse. This was in May. Pic-ac. and later Phos- ac., gave relief and in September the patient resumed work. Late in December there was another breakdown, and Stych-p. was given. A week later after a very long and fatiguing day’s work, Royal was summoned at 2 a.m. He found the patient screaming. Every few minutes she had to urinate and passed only a few drops. Stools frequent, loose, watery. Pulse irregular. Scut, was given, ten drops every half-hour. Patient was better after the second dose, slept after the fourth. Since then she kept the medicine by her, but only took it when overworked. She never had another nerve explosion or headache. In this case there was “nothing the matter with her” i.e., no organic defect to which the sufferings could be attributed. Hale quoted many eclectic writers who give various indications King mentioned depression of nervous and vital powers after long sickness, over-exercise, over-study, long-continued and exhausting labors. It controls nervous agitation. It was Burnett’s chief remedy in the nervous debility after influenza. Scudder mentioned chorea, delirium tremens and hydrophobia, as its popular name “Mad dog” suggests. Rafinesque cited cases of prevention of hydrophobia and Hale observed it produce in a patient taking it “Spasmodic or constrictive closing of jaws and a tightness of the muscles of the face.” A writer, quoted in the N. Y. Med. Times, said Scut, has the remarkable effect of calming fear in delirium tremens. Paine added the indications subsultus tendinum following fevers in delirium tremens, epilepsy, catalepsy, and hysteria. Coe, who used Scutellarin, the concentrated preparation, mentioned sunstroke, tenesmus, tetanus, cramps. Churton gave 60 drops of the tincture every two hours in a case of “severe and rapid hiccough” which chloroform, morphine and pilocarpine had failed to relieve permanently. After the eighth dose, the patient slept and the spasms gradually diminished and stopped for good by the fourth day. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Heart, Grave’s disease. Lycps. (2) Nervous exhaustion, Cypr. according to Hale, acts more on brain, Scut, on spinal cord. (3) Trismus, Nux-v. Hydrophobia, Agar., Fagus, Lach., Bell. (4) Overworked women, Mag-c. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Poor appetite. Sour belchings. Nausea. Vomiting of sour ingesta, hiccough. pain and distress in stomach.

Abdomen - Gas, fullness and distention, colicky pain and uneasiness. Constitutions - Suited to persons of a nervo- bilious temperaments.

Rectum - Diarrhea. Light colored. Stools preceded by colicky pain in abdomen.

Male - Seminal emissions and impotency, with fear of never being better.

Limbs - Chorea. Twitchings of muscles, must be moving. Tremors. Sharp, stinging pains in upper limbs. Nightly restlessness. Weakness and aching.

Sleep - Restless, must move about. Disturbed sleep and frightful dreams. Night terrors. Sleep is unrefreshing.

Modalities - Better by sleep. The hemicrania is better moving about in open air. Headache worse from motion. Worse by overwork or over-exertion. Worse by work or excitement.

Kidneys - Frequent urination but quantity small. Quantity of urine diminished. Biliary salts increased.

Lymphoid, tumors. Mania. Menstrual, colic. Metritis. Miscarriage. Myelitis. Nosebleed. Numbness. Nymphomania. Paraplegia. Petechia. Prostration. Puerperal, fever. Puerperal, mania. Raynaud’s disease. Tetanus. Thrombosis. Varicose, veins. Varicose, ulcers.

HOMEOPATHIC - Rye and grasses are apt to be affected with the ergot disease in damp seasons and when grown on damp, ill-drained lands. If breeding cows are turned on pastures where infected grasses grow, they are very liable to drop their calves. Ergot has been known to hasten childbirth from remote times. Secale’s other actions have been, for the most part, learned from the terrible epidemics of “ergotism” which have occasionally devastated districts in which rye infected with ergot has been ground into flour and eaten by the population. Death takes places in convulsions, from gangrene and consequent exhaustion, or from exhausting hemorrhages or discharges, as diarrhea. Many who escape immediate death are reduced to a cachectic state from which they never recover, are paralyzed, have limbs distorted and senses impaired. In general, the sufferer retains a clear intellect and a good, even abnormally good appetite to the last. Sec. contracts the muscles of blood vessels and the uterus. It also decomposes the blood, producing hemorrhage which is thin, fetid, watery, black, oozing continuously. Small wounds bleed much. Mortification, gangrene. Traumatic gangrene, from application of leeches or mustard, better from cold. Lymphoid tumors. Useful for old people with shriveled skin or for thin, scrawny, old women. Produces contraction of the unstriped muscular fibers, hence a tight feeling throughout the body. Produces an anemic condition, with coldness, numbness, petechiae. Restlessness, anxiety, extreme debility and prostration. Collapse. Emaciation, though appetite and thirst may be excessive. Discharges are dark, thin, foul and exhausting. Varicose veins. Thrombosis. Hinsdale noted that Sec. decreases the flow of pancreatic juice by raising the blood pressure. Chronic, sharp, stinging neuralgic pains, which burn like fire, better application of heat. Tetanic spasms with full conscious- . ness. Facial and abdominal muscles twitch. Twitchings, spasms with fingers spread apart. Gnawing and cramps with stiffness. Numbness. Insufferable tingling, crawling, better rubbing. Sensation of burning in the whole body or as of sparks falling on them or here and there like fire. Loss of power of voluntary motion. Coldness, but does not want to be covered up. Symptoms are better from cold, the whole body is pervaded by a sense of great heat. Sensation of deadness in any part. Everything feels loose and open. Walking causes giddiness. The right side is predominantly affected. MIND - Mania fear or depressed by fear. Anxiety with fear of death, restlessness and difficult breathing. Fear of death before menses. Suspicious. Unconsciousness during pregnancy or childbirth. Unconsciousness, with heavy sleep. Excessive sadness, gradually changes to cheerfulness. Seems besides herself after miscarriage. Forgetful after sex. Weakness of mind after spasms or exhausting sex. Indifference to exposure of person. Impotence. Nymphomania during menses. Grasping at genitals during spasms. Puerperal mania, exposes the body, tears at the genitals, inserts her finger into the vagina and scratches until it bleeds, all ideas of modesty lost. Sardonic laughing. Madness, inclination to bite or drown himself. Laughs, claps her hand over head, seems besides herself. Delirium, abandons her relatives. Mocking at his relatives. Treats his relations contemptuously and sarcastically. Wants to fight. Rage, followed by continuous deep sleep. Wandering talk and hallucinations. Raving delirium. Delusion that two sick people were in bed, one of whom got well and the other did not. Foolish behavior during spasms. Impulse to jump into river.

Head - Passive, congestive headache, rises from back of head. Twisting of head to and fro. Head drawn back. Feels light or heavy, with tingling in legs. Falling of hair. Hair is dry and gray.

Eyes - Dilated pupils, distortion and strabismus. Incipient cataract, senile, especially in women. Pustulous conjunctivitis. Suppuration of cornea. Diabetic retinitis. Ptosis. Catarrh. Suppressed tears. Sparks before the eyes. Double or triple vision. Blindness. Eyes sunken and surrounded by blue rings. Paralysis of upper lid from coal gas.

Ears - Great difficulty in hearing, with roaring, humming in ears. Confused hearing or lost, after chorea. Sensitiveness of hearing, so that even the slightest sound re-echoed in her head.

Nose - Nosebleed, oozing, dark blood, with great prostration in old people, alcoholics or young women.

Face - Spasmodic distortion, or sunken. Pale, pinched. Wild look. Livid spots on face. Tingling, twitching, or cramps in face, which spread over the body. Lockjaw.

Mouth - Salivation, with fetid breath. Much acid fluid in mouth. Spitting of blood. Bloody or yellowish green foam at mouth. Dryness of mouth. Stuttering, indistinct speech. Speech difficult, slow and weak.

Throat - Painful tingling, burning. Post diphtheria paralysis. Feeble voice inaudible, stammering. Voice hoarse and hollow. Painless aphonia in morning, as the day goes on he gets hoarse.

Stomach - Burning in stomach and abdomen. Tympanites. Hiccough. Belchingsof bad odor. Empty retchings. Nausea, easy vomiting of blood and coffee-grounds fluid. Hematemesis.

Abdomen - Excessively inflated and tight, wants uncovered. Empty feeling in hy- pogastrium or bearing down, must lie doubled up in bed. Twitching of abdominal muscles. Formation of large lumps and swelling in abdomen.

Rectum - Cholera-like stools with coldness and cramps. Gushing offensive, painless, watery stools with collapse and great exhaustion. Olive-green, thin, putrid, bloody stools with icy coldness and intolerance of being covered. Involuntary stools, no sensation of passing feces. Anus feels loose and wide open. Sensations - As if intoxicated while undressing. As of a solid plug in nose. Uterus as if burnt. As if contents of uterus would fall forward. As if soft air were creeping through back. As if sacrum would be forced out. As if something alive creeping under skin. As if limbs had been a long time in hot water. As if sparks of fire falling on different parts. As if mice creeping under skin. Fuzzy feeling in limbs.

Female - Menstrual colic with coldness and intolerance of heat. Menses irregular, copious, dark, continuous oozing of watery blood until next period. Passive hemorrhages in feeble, cachetic women. Brownish offensive leucorrhea. Burning pains in uterus. Threatened miscarriage about the third month (Sabin.). Never well since miscarriage or abortion. During labor no expulsive action, though everything is relaxed. Bearing down pain with coldness. Puerperal fever and putrid discharges. Contracted uterus, hourglass labor contractions. Septic placenta. Severe after-pains. Dark offensive, green lochia. Prolapsed uterus after forceps delivery. Tympanitis, coldness, suppressed urine. Vagina hot or cool. Weak uterus. Metritis. Gangrene of female organs. Food - Unquenchable thirst. Thirst with dry mouth or burning. Unnatural, ravenous appetite. Craves acids and sour things. Averse to fat and meat.

Chest - Dyspnea and oppression with cramp in diaphragm. Boring pain in chest. Angina pectoris. Pains through chest, on pressing spine. Burning in lungs. Constitutions - Hemorrhagic diathesis. Suited to irritable, plethoric subjects or to thin, scrawny, feeble emaciated women. To very old, decrepit persons. Women of very lax muscular tissue, everything seems loose and open, no action, flabby vessels.

Heart - Precordial tenderness. Palpitations with contracted and intermittent pulse. Palpitations after sexual excess in males.

Back - Spinal irritation, tingling of lower limbs, can bear only slightest covering. Tingling in back, extending to fingers and toes. Formication and numbness. Locomotor ataxia. Myelitis. Pressure on affected portion causes pain there as well as through the chest. Breasts - Suppression of milk with stinging in breasts. Breasts do not fill with milk properly. Causations - Abortion, miscarriage, childbirth. Hemorrhages, wounds. Suppressions of tears, lochia, milk, or sweat.

Limbs - Paralysis with distorted limbs, of lower limbs, of one side of one arm or one leg, with tingling, numbness and prickling. Paralysis after spasms. Paraplegia. Locomotor ataxia. Formication, pain and spasmodic movements. Violent cramps, in hands, legs, feet and cramps. Icy coldness of limbs. Numbness. Fingers and feet bluish, shriveled, spread apart or bent backwards. Cold, dry hands and feet in heavy smokers, with feeling of fuzziness in the fingers. Varicose ulcers, foul indolent. Trembling, staggering or shuffling gait, as if feet were dragged along. Violent pain in fingertips, tingling in toes. Toes drawn up. Lungs - Heavy, anxious, obstructed breathing with moaning, sighs, sobs. Spitting of blood, with or without cough. Expectoration of blood during violent efforts to breathe.

Sleep - Deep, lethargic, profound and long sleep. Insomnia with restlessness, fever, anxious dreams. Insomnia of drug and liquor habits.

Skin - Shriveledskin, numb, mottled, dusky- blue tinge. Skin cold,dry, wrinkled or bluish, worse over affected part. Raynaud’s disease. Edema neonatorum. Twitchings or quivering in the skin. Formication under skin. Burning sensation, better by cold, wants parts uncovered, though cold to touch. Aversion to heat. Petechiae. Dry gangrene, developing slowly. Slight wounds continue to bleed. Bloody blisters. Livid spots. Boils with green pus, matures slowly.

Modalities - Better lying doubled up in bed. rocking, forcible stretching. Better cold applications, cold bathing. Better open air, uncovering, fanning. Better after vomiting. Worse from heat, warmth, warm cover. Worse touch, motion, exertion. Worse eating, smoking. Worse loss of fluids, sexual excess. Worsejust before or during menses. Worse pregnancy and after miscarriage.

Tongue - Tongue dry, cracked, blood like ink exudes. Tongue coated thick, viscid, yellowish. Cold, livid. Tingling of tip of tongue, which is stiff. Tongue swollen, feels paralyzed. Stuttering as if tongue were paralyzed. Tongue clean, with dry, red tip. Vertigo - Vertigo with stupefaction and heaviness of head. Reeling, inability to stand erect. Vertigo as from intoxication. Vertigo on slightest motion. Vertigo while sitting. COMMENTS - Convulsive nervous symptoms. The body is at times rigid, at times alternating with relaxation. This is especially seen in the hands, which are either clenched or have the fingers spread widely apart (a keynote symptom). The muscles of the face and abdomen twitch. Spasmodic twitchings of muscles in various parts (especially spreading of fingers), eyes sunk, features pinched, shriveled, dry, as though no moisture were left in the body. Anesthesia. Cold to the touch, but cannot bear to be covered. Characteristic burning sensations, burning in all parts of the body as if sparks were falling on the patient. Worse from warmth and external heat. Characteristic numbness, tingling as if ants were crawling all over, better from rubbing. Contraction and then dilatation of blood vessels. Vascular headaches, constriction. Migraines. The fingers turn bluish black. Hemorrhagic diathesis, persistent offensive bleeding. Hemorrhages with tingling. Small wounds bleed persistently. Purpura. Hollow viscera and violent palpitations. Dry gangrene. Threatened amputation. Gangrene aggravated by heat, affected part feels cold. Shriveled, dry skin. Harsh and sallow complexion. Small and painful boils with green contents, mature very slowly, heal slowly and are very weakening. Exophthalmic goiter. Spasmodic retching, the stomach is violently contracted. Incontinence or retention of urine. Involuntary diarrhea with wide-open anus. In cholera where the patient is cold, almost pulseless. Exhausting and offensive discharges. Loss of fluids, debility. Threatened miscarriage, especially at the third month. Tendency to miscarriage. Prolonged, forcing pains, bearing-down, bearing down forwards (Sep. is bearing down downward). Irregular, too weak, feeble or ceasing labor pains (Puls., Caul.). Everything seems loose and open, but no expulsive action. Used to hasten and promote delivery. Fainting. Hourglass contraction of the uterus. Too long, excessive after-pains. Postpartum hemorrhage of dark, oozing blood. Retained placenta. Suppression or non-appearance of the milk. Menses are irregular, copious, dark, fluid, accompanied by labor-like pains in abdomen. There may be a continuous watery discharge of blood during the whole time between the periods. Teste recorded the case of a woman, 50, fat, very soft flesh, who had flooding which nothing could stop. After several useless attempts, Teste gave large doses of Sec. with scarcely any effect. The patient asked for infinitesimal doses. At that time. Teste had no faith at all in infintesimals, but he yielded to the patient ’ s request and gave one drop of the 6c. Then the bleeding ceased immediately and permanently. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Op. Compare: (1) Ergot. (2) Pedi-can. - symptoms of locomotor ataxia, spinal irritation. (3) Brass. - dropsical swellings, scorbutic mouth, voracious appetite, tympanitis, dropping of nails, gangrene. (4) Cinnam., Colch., Ars., Aur-m. 2x - locomotor ataxia. (5) Agro. (6) vertigo, headache, difficult locomotion, burning sensation, Ust., Carb- v. (7) Pituin. - dilated os, little pain, no progress. Compatible: Chin., Ars., Aeon., Bell., Merc., Puls. Teste classes Sec. with Chin, in his Ferr. group. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Kidneys - Paralysis of bladder. Retention with unsuccessful urging. Suppressed urine, pale, watery. Bloody urine, white, cheesy deposit. Discharge of black blood from bladder. Bedwetting in the elderly.

Temperature - Coldness. Cold, dry skin, clammy sweat, excessive thirst. Internal burning with icy coldness externally, yet averse to being covered, worse abdomen. Heat as of sparks. Puerperal fever. Erysipelas. Cold or foul sweat destroys shoes.

PHARMACY - sed-ac. Sedum acre. Small houseleek. Wall pepper. Crassulaceae. Tincture of the whole plant Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

(2) Sed-t. - uterine hemorrhages, also for bowels and rectum, menorrhagia, at menopausal. (3) Sed-r. - Cancer, specific action on abdominal organs, pain, loss of strength. REFERENCES - Boericke.

name: Selenium
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better after sunset. Better inhaling cool air, taking cold air or cold water into mouth. Worse loss of sleep, night watching, after sleep, rest. Worse in open air, draft, even if warm. Worse hot weather, sun and with the sun’s increase. Headaches worse every afternoon. Worse singing, mental exertion. Worse by touch, pressure, motion. Worse after seminal losses, after stools. Worse wine, cinchona..

Masturbation. Myasthenia. Prostatitis. Prostatorrhea. Psoriasis. Scabies. Skin, disorders. Spermatorrhea. Stammering. Sun, effects. Syphilis. Tea, effects.
