full:
PHARMACY - sei. Selenium. The Element (Se, At. Wt. 79.5). Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Bedwetting. Comedones. Constipation. Debility. Diabetes insipidus. Eczema, scalp.Hair, loss. Headache. Hoarseness. Impotency. Laryngitis, tubercular. Liver, disorders. Masturbation. Myasthenia. Prostatitis. Prostatorrhea. Psoriasis. Scabies. Skin, disorders. Spermatorrhea. Stammering. Sun, effects. Syphilis. Tea, effects.

HOMEOPATHIC - Selenium was discovered in 1818 by Berzelius and was named by him after the moon, because it is found associated with tellurium (Tellus, the earth). It is also found associated with sulphur. All three belong to the same group of elements. Selenium is found either in its natural state or, more often, as a metallic selenide. Colloidal selenium has been used as an injection for inoperable cancer. Pain, sleeplessness, ulceration and discharge are markedly diminished. Marked effects on the genito-urinary organs. The larynx and liver are also affected. Often indicated in elderly men. especially for prostration and sexual atony. Bedwetting. Chronic urethritis. Diabetes insipidus. Irritability after sex. Sexual weakness. Lascivious, but impotent. Loss of sexual power with sexual thoughts. Prostate weakness with dribbling of urine. Escape of semen especially when straining at stool. Chronic gleet. Great debility, worse heat. Debility after exhausting diseases, fevers. Patient becomes easily debilitated by heat or hot weather, a little mental or physical exertion makes him sleepy. Easy exhaustion, mental and physical in old age. Early senility. Hemicrania. Neuritis and neuralgia of the head. Marked effects on the supra orbital nerves (left). Myasthenia. Chronic diseases of the bone-marrow. Emaciation of single parts, face, hands, thighs etc. Pulsation in the whole body especially in abdomen, worse eating. Cramps, then stiffness. Biting, here and there. Aversion to draft of air, warm cold or damp. MIND - Dullness of mind. Difficult comprehension, concentration. Mental labor fatigues. Total unfitness for any kind of work. Forgetful in work, but dreams of what he has forgotten. Great forgetfulness when awake with distinct recollection during half sleep. Fails to understand what he hears or reads. Lack of enthusiasm and of interest, indifference. Apathy. Talkative, when excited, stammers, pronounces some words incorrectly. Stutters. Extreme sadness. Depression in the morning, aggravated in the evening. Despair, melancholy. Aversion to company of intimate friends. Dread of society. Reveries of a religious and melancholy character. Easily irritated by noise, people and conversation. Easily antagonized. Irritability after sex. Confusion after emissions. Dipsomania before menses. Erotic thoughts with impotence. Lascivious thoughts. Becomes drunk easily.

Head - Pain over left eye, worse walking in sun, strong odors and tea. Nervous headaches. Headache from intellectual labor. Headache every afternoon. Headache after drinking lemonade, wine or tea. Headache of alcoholics, headache after debauchery. Pain in the scalp as if hair were pulled out. Scalp feels tense. Does not want hair touched. Hair falls out from eyebrows, whiskers and genitals.

Eyes - Blurred vision, with difficult accommodation. Myopia. Pains deep in orbits. Discharge of a thick, yellow secretion, especially in the morning. Heavy, painful, burning, blood-shot with red marks on the eyelids. Spasmodic twitching of left eyeball. Itching vesicles on eyebrows and margins of lids. Styes. Blepharitis. Dacy- rocystitis. Falling off of eyebrows.

Ears - Deafness from hardened wax. Ear stopped.

Nose - Sinusitis. Atrophic rhinitis. Coryza, ending in diarrhea. Fluent coryza in evening. Yellow, thick, gelatinous mucus in nose. Full of thick glairy mucous. Complete chronic obstruction of nose. Nasal itching with the need to scratch the inside of the nose. Inclination to bore fingers in the nose. Sense of smell diminished at times. Smells a repulsive odor like garlic.

Face - Great emaciation of face and hands. Twitching in muscles of face. Greasy, shining skin of face. Upper lip cracked. Comedones.

Mouth - Sweetish taste. Bitter taste in the mouth. Extreme dryness of the mouth. Tongue loaded with a thick white coating in morning. Burning at the tip of the tongue. Pain under root of tongue. Pain in the left molars, which spreads to all the teeth. Bleeding gums and ulcerations in the mouth. Stammering speech, articulates with great difficulty.

Throat - Chronic laryngitis. Voice hoarse and husky, as soon as he begins to sing, talk or read, affected by even cold. Voice rattles. Nodes on vocal cords. Incipient tubercular laryngitis. Throat dry, painful on waking, especially on the left side with extreme thirst. Cough in the morning, expectoration of a bloody mucus. Much clear, starchy mucus (Stann.). Laryngeal cough. Hawking and raising transparent lumps of mucus every morning. Vertigo - Vertigo on lifting head, rising from a seat, raising himself in bed, moving about with nausea, vomiting. Faintness, worse for an hour after breakfast and dinner. COMMENTS - The Sei. proving was conducted by Hering. In London, Raeside repeated a complete proving on sixteen provers and six controls in 1959-60, using the 6c, 12c, and 30c potencies. A leading feature of Sei. is the weakness it causes, a weakness involving all parts of the body, easy fatigue from any labor, night watching, mental exertion and especially from hot weather. The hotter his body the weaker he is; strength rises as the sun sinks. Irresistible desire to lie down and sleep, strength leaves him suddenly, especially in hot weather. Sluggishness, wants to sleep from sheer exhaustion and is worse after. Cannot bear any nervous drain, hence worse after sex or seminal emissions. Impotence. Debility after fevers, infectious diseases. Great emaciation of face, hands, legs, feet, affected parts and single parts. Pulsation in whole body, especially in abdomen after eating. Very great aversion to a draft of air, either warm, cold or damp. Irritability, headaches and other troubles following or worse by seminal emissions. Headaches are accompanied by profound melancholy and may be caused by indulgence in alcoholics or in tea, by hot weather, by over-study, and they are worse by strong odors. Headaches may be periodical and are frequently located above the left eye. Chronic liver disorders. Sensitiveness of liver. Enlargement of liver with loss of appetite. In the morning, sharp stitching pain worse on any movement or pressure. “Fine rash over liver region.” Coryza ending in diarrhea. Hungry at night, longing for spirituous liquors, an almost irresistible maniacal desire. Aversion to salted food. Sensation as if a biting drop were forcing its way out of the urethra. Constipation from weakness with impacted feces. Dribbling of semen after stool and after urination. Sufferings after seminal emissions mental confusion, headache, almost paralytic weakness of spine, involuntary escape of prostatic fluid. Itching in folds of skin, as between fingers and about joints, especially the ankle-joint (Sulph.). The itching may occur in small spots and be accompanied by tingling (showing involvement of the nervous system). Clarke frequently relieved “psoriasis palmaris” with Sei., which shows that it has a relation to syphilis. The scalp is affected with an eczematous eruption which oozes thin fluid after scratching. Hair falls off scalp and all parts of body. Clarke cured with Sei. many cases of hoarseness, the special indications being hoarseness of singers, appearing as soon as they begin to sing or after long use of the voice with frequent necessity to clear the throat from accumulation of clear, starchy mucus. Scrofulous and incipient tubercular laryngitis have been cured with Sei. RELATIONS -Antidoted by: Ign., Puls., Mur- ac. Compare: (1) Agn., Calad., Sulph., Tell., Ph-ac. (2) Arg-n. - Nervous imbalance with weakness, trembling, vertigo, ataxia. (3) Alum. - Paretic weakness, especially of the rectum and bladder. (4) Stann. - Nervous exhaustion and extreme weakness of the respiratory organs. (5) Calad. - Depressive state as a result of excess of tobacco and sexual over-indulgence. (6) Rauw. Compatible after: Calad., Nat-c., Staph., Ph-ac. (in sexual weakness). Itch checked by Merc, or Sulph. often requires Sei. Incompatible: Chin., wine. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - After eating, pulsation all over, especially abdomen. Pressure in stomach as if cramp would occur. Cramp in stomach. Belching. Hiccough and belchings after smflking. Inclination to vomit. Feels very sick after sleep. Nausea, vertigo, thirsty for cold water, general weakness one hour after eating.

Abdomen - Sensation of abdominal distention on the left side, ameliorated by pressure, aggravated by going to stool or by coughing. Left abdominal hyperesthesia, spreading towards the left kidney area. Violent shoot- ings in spleen when walking. Pulsation all over the body especially in abdomen after eating which hinders sleep.

Rectum - Anal andrectal itching, especially towards evening. Constipation from rectal weakness with flatulence. Hard evacuations, followed by a discharge of mucus or of blood when passing the last portion of it. Stools large, hard, requiring a great effort, even a mechanical aid to expel them. Stools exceedingly difficult and threaten to tear anus from their immense size. Somewhat liquid feces with tenesmus. Filament like hair in feces.

Male - Irritability after sex. Loss of sexual power-with lascivious fancies. Lascivious but impotent. Increases desire, decreases ability. Sexual weakness. On attempting sex, penis relaxes. Easy loss of semen during sex with feeble erection, but long continued voluptuous thrill during stools. Semen watery, odorless. Dribbling of semen during sleep. Prostatitis, prostatic adenoma. Oozing of prostatic fluid during sleep, while sitting, walking and at stool. Hydrocele. Chronic gleet. Bedwetting, chronic urethritis. Papillomas on the penis.

Female - Rare menses. Menses early, scanty, painful. Menses painful on the first day. Awakened by pain of menses. Menses copious and dark. Menses delayed about eight days. Throbbing in abdomen during pregnancy, worse eating. Food - Thirstless. Anorexia in morning with white-coated tongue. Hunger at night. Craves stimulants, brandy, tea etc. Desire for alcoholic drinks. Aversion to salty food. Worse from tea, sugar, salt, lemonade, wine. Sweetish, disagreeable taste after smoking.

Chest - Constrictive or stinging pain behind the sternum and in the upper left thoracic region. Pains in right side, around under last ribs, especially on inspiration, extending to region of kidneys. Constitutions - Suited to blondes and persons of light complexion.

Heart - Pulse very accelerated. Arterial pulsation, especially in the abdominal aorta, preventing him from sleeping. Pain in the heart region. Rhythmic anomalies. Syphilitic aortitis.

Back - The back becomes almost paralytic after a temporary illness. Paralytic pain in small of back, better lying on abdomen. Sensation of paralysis in loins. Pain as from lameness in small of back in morning. Hard swelling on back. Severe pain in the coccyx, aggravated when sitting, ameliorated by walking. Pain through left side of neck and down back of left leg. Bones - Osteoporosis during menopause. Inflammation of the bones and cartilages in the young adult, attacking the knee, then the elbow and the hip. Bones fragile. Breasts - More or less acute pain, prickling or dull aching in the left or right breast. Causations - Bad effects from excess of tobacco or tea. Ill effects of debauchery, alcohol, sugar, salt, lemonade, loss of vital fluids, masturbation, sexual excess, over-study. Walking, exertion.

Neck - Glands of neck large and hard. Cramp in neck. Rigidity of muscles of neck and nape, which hinders head being turned.

Limbs - Pains in all the limbs, as if caused by a chill. Legs feel weak, with fear of paralysis after typhus. Sudden left sciatic pain leaves soreness behind. Itching pimples on buttocks and thighs, near the scrotum. The knees crack when they are bent. Cramps in calves and soles. Flat ulcers on lower legs. Itching in feet, especially around ankles in evening. Blisters on toes. Emaciation of hands, of legs. Dry, scaly eruption on palms with itching, having syphilitic base. Psoriasis of palms. Painful hang-nails. Scabies-like pimples on hand. Tearing in hands at night with cracking in wrists. Itching at wrist in palms, itching vesicles on and between fingers. Miliaria in forearm.

Sleep - Sleep prevented by pulsation in all vessels, worse abdomen. Sleepless until midnight, awakens early and always same hour. Insomnia, following alcoholism, infectious diseases, heart diseases. Disposition to sleep early in evening with imperfect sleep and frequent waking during night. Jerks in body when going to sleep. Erotic dreams. Dreams of fire, murders, robbers, quarrels and unnatural cruelty. Waking early in morning and always at same hour.

Skin - Seborrhea, comedones with an oily surface of the skin. Oily. Frequent tingling in circumscribed parts of skin with great provocation to scratch. Red rash on region of liver. Miliary eruption. Vesicular eruption between fingers (Rhus- t., Anae.). Dry, scaly eruption in palms with itching. Itching about the ankles and folds of skin, between fingers. Acne. Prolonged oozing from parts which have been scratched. Flat ulcers. Loss of hair from the head, armpits, pubic region and eyebrows. Hair falls off head, whiskers and other parts. Alopecia.

Modalities - Better after sunset. Better inhaling cool air, taking cold air or cold water into mouth. Worse loss of sleep, night watching, after sleep, rest. Worse in open air, draft, even if warm. Worse hot weather, sun and with the sun’s increase. Headaches worse every afternoon. Worse singing, mental exertion. Worse by touch, pressure, motion. Worse after seminal losses, after stools. Worse wine, cinchona.

Teeth - Teeth covered with mucus. Toothache from tea. Toothache with feeling of coldness, better taking cold water and cold air into mouth. Toothache which compels use of toothpick until the blood comes. Boring in molars. The teeth become free of mucus, hard and smooth and crack when rubbed.

Liver - Chronic liver affections. Pain in the liver, especially on taking an inspiration, extending to the kidney region with sensibility to external pressure. Enlarged with fine rash over liver region. Lungs - Weak feeling in the chest. Frequent efforts to breathe deeply like sighing. Difficulty breathing when walking in open air. Respiration obstructed at night, when lying down, by pains. Dry hacking cough, worse in the morning. Hawking up of mucus and of small clots of blood. Hawks up clear mucus in the morning. Frequent necessity to clear the throat in singers. Tubercular laryngitis.

Kidneys - Frequent urination with urgent need to urinate. Sensation in the tip of urethra, as if a biting drop were forcing its way out. Red, itching irritation at the tip of the penis. Urine dark red, thick, scanty, gritty with deposits. Dribbling of urine after urination and after stool. Involuntary dribbling, when walking. Urination predominantly at night. Nocturnal bedwetting.

Temperature - Chilliness, followed by hot flushes. Constant alternation of heat and cold. Sweating from the armpits and genital region. Burning heat, extending over the skin. Perspiration from least exertion. Perspiration as soon as he sleeps, day or night. Tendency to profuse perspiration when walking or during an afternoon sleep. Perspiration on chest, genitals and under axilla, which leaves yellow or white spots on linen and stiffens it. External heat with burning in skin and only in single spots.

name: Sempervivum Tectorum
author: Murphy
constitution: Bites, insects. Breast, cancer. Cancer. Hemorrhoids. Herpes zoster, Menopause. Menses, suppressed. Ringworm. Scir- rhus. Tongue, indurations. Tumors. Warts. Wounds, poisoned.
keynote:
PHARMACY - semp. Sempervivumtectorum. Houseleek. N. O. Crassulaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bites, insects. Breast, cancer. Cancer. Hemorrhoids. Herpes zoster, Menopause. Menses, suppressed. Ringworm. Scir- rhus.…
full:
PHARMACY - semp. Sempervivumtectorum. Houseleek. N. O. Crassulaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bites, insects. Breast, cancer. Cancer. Hemorrhoids. Herpes zoster, Menopause. Menses, suppressed. Ringworm. Scir- rhus. Tongue, indurations. Tumors. Warts. Wounds, poisoned.

HERBAL - In Hufeland’s Journal, said Kallen- bach, the fresh juice of Sempervivum tectorum is recommended in chronic aphthae in grown persons in causal relation to hemorrhoids, as well as in scirrhus indurations of the tongue. In many countries, it has a popular reputation for indurations and sores on the tongue. Reichel of Staben, considered it curative in spasms of the uterus and in menstrual disturbances of all kinds. Cases of too exalted vascular activity in the sexual sphere. Also in ear troubles consequent on hardened earwax and in inflammatory exudations of the ear. It is externally used for bites of insects, stings of bees and poisoned wounds, warts. Herpes zoster and cancerous tumors. Breast cancer. Ringworm. Hemorrhoids.

HOMEOPATHIC - Grimmer stated, “Sempervivum tectorum has cured many cases of induration and sores on the tongue, it also has definite action on the uterus and menstrual function in cancer constitutions, it could be thought of in cases of tongue cancer.” COMMENTS - Kallenbach was consulted by Mrs. S„ 44, childless of sickly looks, for an affection of the tongue. For the previous six months menses had appeared only every eight to ten weeks and were accompanied with Sempervivum tectorum pains darting from small of back to uterus and vulva. During the six months, she had stitching pain on the right rim of her tongue about 3/4 inch from the point, at which place after a few weeks, a swelling formed, the size of a small bean. The swelling bled at times, and at night caused a burning sensation as of a small coal, disturbing sleep. Sour food caused pain. The swelling was not hard on the surface, but contained two hard nodules the size of lentils, one of which was denuded and bled on touch. Three enlarged veins crossed the swelling and entered the tongue muscle behind it. She had been treated for over a month with Aur., Ars., Carb-v. in vain. Kallenbach moistened the swelling with the fresh juice of Semp. thrice a day. Within three days it was smaller and folds appeared, the enlarged veins were contracted, formed thin, tense vessels crossing the swelling and seemingly tying it. During the next three days, the patient applied the juice too energetically and Kallenbach found the surroundings in inflammatory irritation and very sensitive. The applications was stopped and Semp. 2x was given internally. After a week’s use the swelling had shriveled to one-third the size, and ten days later the menses, which had ceased altogether, reappeared and continued very profusely for five days. The swelling shriveled to the size of a small pea, was firmer, harder, devoid of sensation and gave no further trouble. The menses continued regularly. In another instance, Mrs. X., 27, a mother of a six month old healthy boy, formerly frequently afflicted with swelling of the glands, very sensitive to homeopathic remedies, complained of a pain under her tongue of ten days’ duration, interfering with eating and speaking. There was a bluish red elevation on under side of tongue the size of a split bean. It was hard, and along both sides there were enlarged veins. On the side a denuded spot exuded a whitish albuminous matter which could easily be wiped off. Semp. 6c was given, one powder every forty-eight hours. On the second day, the swelling was less sensitive, and in a week, much smaller. Then the menses reappeared (first time since confinement) and in three weeks the whole swelling was gone, leaving only in its place a somewhat engorged vein. Kallenbach treated with applications of lx General V. B. who had nodules on the left rim of his tongue with swollen veins, the nodules disappeared and the sensitiveness was removed and the patient was so well that he refused to stay for the completion of the cure and failed to report. Clarke’s experience with Semp. was in domestic practice. For some child affections of the eyes he used rags moistened with “house leek and cream” (about equal parts of the juice and fresh cream) were applied and his recollection of it is that the application was exceedingly pleasant. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer.

name: Senecio Aureus
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Colic is better bending forward and better by stool. Better at onset of menses, from menstruation. Worse puberty, sexual excitement. Worse dampness, cold open air. Worse at night, in afternoon. Worse sitting, must keep moving about..

PHARMACY - senec. Senecio aureus. Golden ragwort. Senecio gracilis. Squaw-weed. N. O. Compositae. North America, found in swamps. Tincture of fresh plant in flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Ascites. Cirrhosis. Coryza. Cough. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Dysuria. Fainting. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Hemorrhages. Homesickness. Hysteria. Kidney, cohc. Kidney, inflammation. Leucorrhea. Lumbago. Mania. Menorrhagia. Menstruation, disorders. Nails,brittle. Nervousness. Neurasthenia. Nosebleeds. Prostate, enlarged. Prostatitis. Puerperal, mania. Sciatica. Spermatic cord, pain. Tuberculosis. Wounds.

HERBAL - The golden ragwort had a reputation in domestic and eclectic practice as a regulator of menstrual functions when Hale introduced it into homeopathic practice. Its action on the female organism was clinically verified. Lyman Watkins said, “Females taking Senec. generally improve in health and strength, accumulate flesh, become lightheaded and cheerful. This may be due to some tonic influence.”

HOMEOPATHIC - A. E. Small and others proved it and clinical additions have filled out the picture. Like many other Compositae, the Ragworts or Groundsels, have power over hemorrhagic conditions, whether arising from disease or from wounds. Marked action on female and urinary organs, especially bladder. Lack of reaction in genito-urinary tract. Hemorrhagic tendency from other organs especially with suppressed or delayed menses. Dropsy after hemorrhage. Debilitating or vicarious discharges. Backaches of congested kidneys. Early cirrhosis of liver. Tightness in nose, throat etc. Muscles draw into a knot. Nervous, pale, weak and sleepless hysterical women. Globus. Very sensitive to open air, tendency to catarrhs. MIND - Despondent. Nervous and irritable, whining. Self centered. Elated and sad alternately. Inability to fix mind upon any one subject.

Head - Wave-like dizziness from occiput to sinciput. Sharp pains over left eye and through the left temple. Dull, stupefying headache. Headache precedes leucorrhea and irritation in bladder.

Eyes - Tears are irritating, causing itching.

Ears - Itching in Eustachian tube.

Nose - Burning in nostrils. Fullness of nasal passages, burning, sneezing, profuse flow. Tightness in nasal passage. Nosebleed or nasal catarrh take the place of menses when suppressed from any cause. Coryza with nosebleed.

Face - Sharp, cutting pain in left side. Dryness of fauces, throat and mouth.

Mouth - Twitching about mouth. Teeth very sensitive.

Throat - Dry mouth, throat and fauces. Burning in pharynx, raw feeling in nasopharynx, must swallow, though painful. Vertigo - Wave-like sensation of dizziness from occiput to sinciput. COMMENTS - Hale noted that the country people call Senec. “Wild Valerian,” and use it for nervousness, hysteria and low spirits, sleeplessness, especially in women. He referred to this “globus” symptom of the pathogenesis: about the middle of the afternoon, sensation as if a ball was in the stomach. Rising up into the throat, lasting for about an hour. Sensation of tightness in the throat with a disposition to attempt to relieve it by swallowing. Respiration as if greatly fatigued. Coughs and tuberculosis. “It is especially serviceable in mucus coughs.” “In chronic coughs, catarrhal affections, hemoptysis incipient tuberculosis attended with troublesome cough, the result of obstructed menstruation.” Pains are radiating, shifting, lancinating. Symptoms alternate.  “Dull, heavy pain in left spermatic cord, moving along cord to testicle. Prostatic gland enlarged, feels hard and swollen to touch. Lascivious dreams with pollutions.” Hemorrhagic function of menstruation. Menses, profuse and early, retarded or absent. Ailments from non- appearing menses. Nosebleed or nasal catarrh when menses are suppressed. C. M. Foss reported the case of Miss L., 18, who had seen no period for fifteen months. She was chlorotic, had a dry. hacking cough with frequent pulse, made still more frequent by any excitement, headache, poor sleep, constipation. The abdomen had been gradually enlarging for six months and tapping had been decided upon when Senec. lx was given. All symptoms rapidly cleared up and the menses returned within a short time. Senec. lx also cured a girl, 21, who had suppression of urine in addition to chlorosis, ascites and suppressed menses. S. H. Talcott reported an important case bearing on the same point. Mrs. X., 26, a mother of two children. Before confinement, the patient was haunted with the idea that her child would be stillborn. Nine days after its birth, strong andhealthy, she was admitted to hospital in a state of violent acute mania, which continued with high temperature, for three months, with great physical activity. The mental state was that of a wild, violent and almost uncontrollable person. There was severe pain in the head, great nervous irritability and sleeplessness and hysterical weakness. These symptoms, coupled with the fact (now first ascertained) that the lochia had ceased suddenly after confinement and the menses had not come on, led to the choice of Senec., which was given in drop doses of the 3x every two hours. Steady improvement resulted and after a few weeks the patient was allowed out on parole. A relapse followed and Bell, did no good. Senec. was again given with good effect and complete recovery took place. Talcott remarked that recovery from puerperal mania seldom occurs unless menstruation is re-established. Talcott’s case becomes more significant in the light of Cooper’s observation of the brain action of Senec-j. Hale reported the following case of dysmenorrhea: Mrs. X., mother of one child, had an miscarriage three years before and another (at the second month of pregnancy) four months before Hale saw her. Since the last miscarriage she had suffered from painful menstruation, which had not been the case previously. Menses every three weeks, profuse, lasting eight or nine days, accompanied by much cutting pain in sacrum, hypogastrium and groins. Pale, weak, nervous, slight cough, generally at night. Senec., 5 drops, was given three times a day until the next period, which came on at the twenty-ninth day and was perfectly normal in quantity and without pain. Hale said he also found Senec. useful in advanced stages of gonorrhea and in prostatic disorders. Small, who proved Senec., recorded the case of a woman, 30, who had been ill six weeks, the symptoms steadily increasing until the following picture was presented: face bloated, abdomen enlarged, feet edematous, urine alternately profuse and watery or dark and scanty, frequent desire to urinate day and night. Senec., 10 drops, three times a day, cured quickly. Small remarked that he has found Senec. useful in the dysuria of women and children when evidently of catarrhal origin and in dysuria with uterine displacement. Mucus sediment in the urine is an indication. But the benefits of Senec. are not confined to the female sex. Small related the case of a man, 50, nervo- sanguine, subject of kidney inflammation affecting right kidney generally, causing intense pain, fever, prostration. On one occasion the pain was particularly intense and the bladder seemed implicated. Every time he passed water he cried out in agony. Urine reddish, very hot and acrid. Bowels constipated. Dull headache, mouth and throat dry, chilly, fever and perspiration. Senec., 20 drops in half a tumbler of water, a dessert spoonful every hour. There was relief from the first dose and the pain soon subsided entirely, leaving the patient freed from recurrence of the attacks. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Senec-j. - cerebrospinal irritation, rigid muscles, chiefly of neck and shoulders, also in cancer. (2) Alet., Caul., Sep. (3) Arn., Calen., Bell-p. (4) Uterine, chest and bladder symptoms, Puls., Helon. (5) Vicarious menstruation, Bry. Senec. has bloody expectoration. (6) Homesickness, Caps., Ph- ac. (7) Worse 4 p.m., Lyc. (8) Prostatitis and gonorrhea, Sabal., Solid., Puls., Pip-n., Cop., Thuj. (9) Nervousness, Coff., Cham., Valer., Ambr. (10) Fidgety feet, Caust., Zinc. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Sensation of a ball rising from stomach to throat. Sourbelchings. Nausea and vomiting of kidney origin.

Abdomen - Pain about umbilical region, spreading in all directions better stools, bending double. Ascites from suppressed menses.

Rectum - Thin, watery stool intermingled with hard lumps of feces (Ant-c.). Straining at stool, thin, dark, bloody with tenesmus. Stools, thin, watery, mingled with hard lumps of feces or thin, dark, bloody. Sensations - As of a wave from occiput to sinciput. As if he would pitch forward. As of a ball rising from stomach to throat.

Male - Lascivious dreams with involuntary emissions. Prostate enlarged, feels hard and swollen to touch. Dull, heavy pain in spermatic cord, extending to testicles.

Female - Before menses, inflammatory conditions of throat, chest and bladder after menstruation commences, these improve. Feels like the menses would come. Menses, retarded, suppressed with concomitant symptoms, dropsy, cough, backache. Amenorrhea of young girls with backache. Premature and too profuse menses (Calc., Erig.). Menorrhagia, a copious flow which continues until they become anemic. Anemic dysmenorrhea with urinary disturbances. Dysmenorrhea after abortion. Leucorrhea, thick, yellow, profuse, flows down thighs. Profuse flow of mucus from vagina from sexual excitation. Sexual irritation causing, itching, burning and swelling of labia. Pains from ovaries to breasts. Food - Aversion to all food, especially sweets and coffee which she was very fond.

Chest - Chest sore and raw. Constitutions - Suited to women and little girls of nervous temperament.

Back - Lumbar backache, as if to break with amenorrhea. Kidney disease. Breasts - Burning in left nipple. Pains from ovaries to breasts. Causations - Ill effects of suppressed or delayed menses, wounds, venesection.

Limbs - Wandering rheumatic pains, periodical. Feet cold in bed. Brittle nails (Sil., Thuj.). Lungs - Dyspnea on ascending (Calc.) Acute inflammatory conditions of upper respiratory tract. Loose cough with copious mucus expectoration and labored breathing. Cough tickling with blood- streaked sputum with suppressed menses. Dry teasing cough, stitching chest pains. Hoarseness.

Sleep - Nervousness and sleeplessness. Sleepless women with uterine troubles and amenorrhea. Drowsy during day. Great drowsiness with unpleasant dreams. Many dreams, erotic.

Skin - Dry.

Modalities - Colic is better bending forward and better by stool. Better at onset of menses, from menstruation. Worse puberty, sexual excitement. Worse dampness, cold open air. Worse at night, in afternoon. Worse sitting, must keep moving about.

Kidneys - Kidney colic (Pareir., Oci., Berb.). Nephritis. Great heat and constant urging, with kidney pain. Irritable bladder of children with headache. Dysuria in women with dysmenorrhea or uterine displacements and in children with headache. Scanty, high-colored, bloody with much mucus sediment and tenesmus.

Temperature - Hectic fever with anorexia.

name: Senecio Jacoboea
author: Murphy
constitution: Arthritis. Brain, disorders. Cerebrospinal, irritation. Depression. Bedwetting. Headaches. Twitchings. Ulcers. '
keynote:
PHARMACY - senec-j. Senecio jacoboea. St. James’ wort. Staggerwort. Ragwort. N. O. Compositae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis. Brain, disorders. Cerebrospinal, irritation. Depression. Bedwetting. Headaches. Twitchings.…
full:
PHARMACY - senec-j. Senecio jacoboea. St. James’ wort. Staggerwort. Ragwort. N. O. Compositae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis. Brain, disorders. Cerebrospinal, irritation. Depression. Bedwetting. Headaches. Twitchings. Ulcers. '

HERBAL - This is the common ragwort, which, with its yellow flowers, is such a conspicuous feature of English roadsides and commons throughout the summer months. Gerarde mentioned “green wounds and old filthy ulcers” as benefited by it, also “old aches and pains in the arms, hips and legs.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Cooperpublished several observations with Senec-j. MIND - Depressed in body and mind, it seemed as if brain would not work. Talks incoherently.

Head - Exhaustion felt in back of head, after Senecio jacoboea this felt lighter and better.

Rectum - Bowels (before fairly regular) began acting in gushes, large stools occasionally, but in no way regular. COMMENTS - Cooper gave a woman, 57 who had slight otorrhea of left ear with deafness on that side, a single dose of Senec-j. Immediately after, she began to feel depressed in mind and body, it seemed as if her brain would not work, for she talked incoherently. The bowels began acting in gushes and a bladder weakness was aggravated, so that there was bedwetting night and day for three days. Another woman from a single dose of the same had “exhaustion in the back of the head.” Yet another woman, 51, had depression all her life, coming in fits. “Memory and everything goes,” could not talk coherently to herself and dislikes conversation in others. On July 1, 1900, she wrote, “Have suffered agony from awful feeling of torpor of brain, which has made it an effort to put words together, memory seemed to go, felt altogether insensible, bowels have been confined.” One dose of Senec-j. was given and removed the depression and relieved all the other symptoms. It also produced constant rigidity of muscles, chiefly of neck and shoulders, worse at night, it seems like a habit. “And I try to relax them but find it most difficult, it to run back involuntarily, so that the weight of the head is somehow held in this way and though touching the pillow does not rest on it. Sometimes in the day the upper part of the legs gets a sort of ague fit of shaking.” On this Cooper remarked, “The exhaustion felt after a dose of Senec-j. in the back of the head in case 2 and the cropping up as a new symptom of this strange-looking rigidity of the muscles of the neck, at night chiefly together with the shaking of the legs in the daytime, points to incoordinated muscular action due to deranged cerebral control.” Cooper added the case of a man, 68, many years apoplectically inclined, who had constant twitchings at night with cascular deafness of right ear, loss of memory, pressure and heat of head. After a dose of Senec-j., he remained comfortable for three months and hearing improved. Senec-j. has been used like Senec. in cases of menstrual irregularity. REFERENCES - Clarke. Cooper.

Back - Constant rigidity of muscles, chiefly of neck and shoulders, especially at night, seems like a habit, but finds it most difficult to relax them, it seems to return involuntarily, so that the weight of the head is somehow held in this way and though touching the pillow does not rest on it.

Limbs - Sometimes in the day the upper part of the legs gets a sort of ague fit of shaking.

Kidneys - The bladder, which had been rather weak, became more so, the bedwetting continuing day and night for several days.

name: Senega Officinalis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better walking in open air, sweat, bending head backwards, walking in open air. Rest helps dry cough. Worse from inhaling air, open air, cold, wind, walking in open air. Worse in warm air, warm room. Worse going up stairs, stooping, bending forward. Worse by touch and pressure, rubbing. Worse rest, morning and night. Worse looking intently at an object..

Facial paralysis. Hay fever. Headaches. Hydrothorax. Hypopion. Influenza. Iritis. Lungs disorders. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Snakebites. Sneezing. Sprains. Styes. Throat, sore. Tuberculosis. Whooping cough.
keynote:
PHARMACY - seneg. Senega officinalis. Snake-wort. Snake-root. Polygala senega. N. O. Polygalaceae. Tincture of powdered dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Amblyopia. Ascites. Asthma. Bedwetting. Bladder, irritable. Blepharitis.…
full:
PHARMACY - seneg. Senega officinalis. Snake-wort. Snake-root. Polygala senega. N. O. Polygalaceae. Tincture of powdered dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Amblyopia. Ascites. Asthma. Bedwetting. Bladder, irritable. Blepharitis. Bronchitis. Chest disorders. Constipation. Cornea, opacity. Coughs. Esophagus, stricture. Facial paralysis. Hay fever. Headaches. Hydrothorax. Hypopion. Influenza. Iritis. Lungs disorders. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Snakebites. Sneezing. Sprains. Styes. Throat, sore. Tuberculosis. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - Senega is one of the sources of Saponin. It has a nauseous taste and leaves a scraping sensation in the throat. It is in disorders of the chest, eyes and bladder that homeopaths have found it of most service and the extensive provings have supplied excellent data for prescribing. Teste reported that Seneg. was introduced to medical practice by Dr. Tennant of Virginia, who was led to test its properties through hearing that the Native Americans used it as an antidote to snakebites as it relieved the symptoms of snakes’ venom. Tennant concluded that it might also relieve dyspnea, cough and hemoptysis arising from other causes and gave it with success in cases of pneumonia, pleurisy and hydrothorax. Other old-school practitioners used it as an expectorant in chronic respiratory catarrh, acute tuberculosis, rheumatic fever, dropsies incipient cataract, croup. It is regarded as “a stimulant, diaphoretic and expectorant in chronic bronchitis.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Seneg. affects the mucus membranes causing catarrhal symptoms especially of the respiratory tract and bladder. Eyes, serous membranes of chest, muscles and left side are also affected. Distinct eye symptoms of a paralytic type. Great soreness of walls of chest. Pressure on chest as though lungs were forced back to spine. Pleurodynia. Lying on right side causes pain in chest. Motion causes pain under sternum. Motion of arms causes soreness of walls of chest. Circumscribed spots in chest left after inflammations. Hoarseness. The throat is so dry and sensitive it hurts the patient to talk. Cough often ends in sneezing. Lying down causes tickling in larynx. Great accumulation of clear albuminous mucus, which is difficult to expel. Whooping cough in fat, chubby children, clear mucus like white of egg, difficult to raise, cough worse towards evening. MIND - Anxiety with hasty respiration. Fear of suffocation. Inclined to quarrel. Readily takes offense. Suddenly remembers unimportant regions which he saw long ago.

Head - Dullness with pressure and weakness of eyes. Pain in temples. Bursting pain in forehead into eyes, better cool open air.

Eyes - Oculomotor paralysis. Muscular asthenopia (Caust.). Opacities of the vitreous humor. Promotes the absorption of fragments. Staring. Lachrymation. Dryness with sensation as if too large for orbits. Eyeballs feel distended or like balls of ice. Sensation of trembling without visible trembling. Flickering, must wipe eyes frequently. Objects look shaded. Double vision, better only by bending head backward. Ptosis. Blepharitis, lids dry and crusty (Graph.).

Ears - Aching in the ear when chewing.

Nose - Dry. Coryza, much watery mucus and sneezing. Sneezes, so often and so violently that the head grows dizzy and heavy. Nostrils feel peppery. Sensations - Eyes, as if they were pressed out, as if eyeballs were being expanded, as if soap in eyes. As if red pepper throughout nostrils and air passages. Dyspnea as from stagnation in lungs. As if lungs pushed back to spine. As if chest would burst. As if chest too narrow. Wrist as if sprained. Joints as if lame.

Mouth - Dry scraping in mouth, worse talking. Taste, metallic like urine.

Throat - Catarrhal inflammation of throat and fauces with scraping hoarseness. Catarrh of larynx. Hawks viscid mucus in detached small clots. Burning and rawness. Sensation as if membrane had been abraded. Dry scraping, worse talking. Loss of voice. Voice unsteady, vocal cords partially paralyzed. Hurts to talk. COMMENTS - The prover took from 40 to 6 drops of the tincture. Extreme tenderness. Worse bending head forward and worse from stooping. Generally left-sided. Disordered digestive organs. Gnawing hunger and empty feeling. Irritability and catarrh of the urinary organs. Frequent urging, scalding in urethra before or after urination. Urine is loaded with mucus threads. Seneg. has been used as an emetic. Pressure, dullness, heaviness in the head. Painful sensitiveness of hearing. Eye symptoms as an accompaniment of head symptoms. “Violent rush of blood to head when stooping, especially to eyeballs, where a painful pressure is experienced.” Pains, inflammation both of the exterior and interior of the eye and lids, and much disorder of vision. The eye troubles are worse when looking intently at an object and better bending head backwards. The symptom in which it was first noticed was “When walking towards the setting sun he seemed to see another smaller sun hover below the other, assuming a somewhat oval shape when looking down, disappearing on bending head backwards and on closing the eyes.” Guernsey outlined its action, “Where there is a great burning in the chest, either before or after coughing, profuse secretion of mucus. Dryness of inner parts which are usually moist, dry skin. General disorders of the windpipe, left side of chest particularly, right eye, lower eyelids.” Nash, who had only obtained success with low potencies of Seneg., cured many cases of “cough with great accumulation of mucus, which seems to fill the chest with much rattling, wheezing and difficult breathing.” A very stout elderly woman of tubercular family history had pneumonia of both bases, especially right. She had a very violent paroxysmal cough with ropy, difficult expectoration tinged with blood. Seneg. 30c quickly relieved a very dangerous condition when other remedies had failed. Clinton Enos related a case of a very fat girl, age 10, with cold, damp feet and hands and sweating about the head, had spells of sneezing for two years, even since whooping cough. Several sneezing spells a day lasting about half an hour. Sharp pains in chest and temples during the attacks. In nose a large quantity of mucus with stuffed-up feeling. One dose of Seneg. 200c removed the whole trouble in a week. RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Bry., Am., Bell., Camph. Compare: (1) Sapin. - a derivative of Senega root. (2) In bronchial affections, Am-c. (3) Fat, plethoric people disposed to catarrhs, Calc. (4) Muscular asthenopia, loss of voice, paralysis (facial, etc.), Caust. (5) Laryngeal and pulmonary catarrh, Phos. (6) Bronchial catarrh, Spong. (7) Whooping cough, Coc-c., Kali-bi. (Seneg. clear phlegm, cough worse towards evening, Coc-c. clear phlegm worse morning, Kali-bi. yellow phlegm in morning). Follows well: Calc., Phos., Lyc., Sulph. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Loathing and nausea with inclination to vomit.

Abdomen - Boring and digging pains in abdomen. Flatulent disorders with a sensation of a general bearing down towards hypogastrium.

Chest - Chest feels oppressed on ascending. Pressure on chest as though lungs were forced back to spine. Pain in spots, as if bruised shifting pains on stooping. As of a crushing weight or weakness starts in chest. Sore from coughing, pressure, sneezing or moving arms. Burning in chest before or after coughing. Dry scraping in chest worse talking. Thorax feels too narrow. Exudation in pleura. Hydrothorax. Circumscribed spots in chest left after inflammations. Constitutions - Suited to plethoric, phlegmatic persons, persons tending to obesity, fat persons of lax tissue, fat, chubby children and old persons. Suited to females of slender and tall, but having retained a good deal of sprightliness and moral power.

Back - Bursting, distending pain in kidney region. Causations - Ill effects of poisonous bites, sprains.

Modalities - Better walking in open air, sweat, bending head backwards, walking in open air. Rest helps dry cough. Worse from inhaling air, open air, cold, wind, walking in open air. Worse in warm air, warm room. Worse going up stairs, stooping, bending forward. Worse by touch and pressure, rubbing. Worse rest, morning and night. Worse looking intently at an object.

Kidneys - Bursting, distending pain in kidney region. Scalding before and after urinating. Increased or decreased in amount. Greatly diminished urine, loaded with shreds and mucus. Urine, foamy, acrid with mucus shreds. Lungs - Bronchial catarrh with sore chest walls, much mucus, sensation of oppression and weight of chest. Bursting pain in back on coughing. Hacking cough. Cough often ends in a sneeze. Rattling in chest (Ant- t.). Albuminous or blood-streaked sputum. Exudations in pleura. Pleuropneumonia. Hydrothorax (Merc-s.) Difficult raising of tough, profuse mucus in the aged. Asthenic bronchitis of old people with chronic interstitial nephritis or chronic emphysema. Old asthmatics with congestive attacks.

name: Senna
author: Murphy
constitution: Acetonemia. Colic. Constipation. Exhaustion. Fainting. Flatulence. Liver, disorders. Nitrogenous, waste. Oxaluria. Sleeplessness. Sneezing with heat.

PHARMACY - senn. Senna. Cassia acutifolia. Alexandrian senna. Cassia angustifolia. Cassia obovata. N. O. Leguminosae. Caes- alpinioideae. The leaflets of several species of Cassia. Trituration or tincture of the dried leaves. Historical dose: Tincmre and all potencies.

full:
PHARMACY - senn. Senna. Cassia acutifolia. Alexandrian senna. Cassia angustifolia. Cassia obovata. N. O. Leguminosae. Caes- alpinioideae. The leaflets of several species of Cassia. Trituration or tincture of the dried leaves. Historical dose: Tincmre and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acetonemia. Colic. Constipation. Exhaustion. Fainting. Flatulence. Liver, disorders. Nitrogenous, waste. Oxaluria. Sleeplessness. Sneezing with heat.

HOMEOPATHIC - The symptoms are mostly derived from overdosings. Senn, is used as a laxative in ordinary practice. Senn, has proved an excellent remedy in the colicofinfantswith incarcerated flatulence and sleeplessness. Infantile colic, when the child seems to be full of wind. Constipation with colic and flatulence. Oxaluria with excess of urea increased specific gravity. Liver enlarged and tender. Exhaustion. General swelling. Ebullitions of blood at night. “Repeated sneezing, which caused heat (especially of hands), exhaustion and panting breathing.” Acetonemia, prostration, fainting. Unclean body swell.

Head - Heaviness of the head when stooping, as if it were pressed down.

Nose - Repeated sneezing, which caused heat, especially of hands, exhaustion and panting breathing.

Face - Livid lips. Commissure of lips covered with small burning blisters. Food - Anorexia. Thirst.

Stomach - Empty or watery and fetid, risings. Loathing and nausea with inclination to vomit. Sinking immediately after meals. COMMENTS - Farrington said it is one of the best remedies in the Materia Medica for “simple exhaustion with excess of nitrogenous waste.” The exhaustion is exemplified in the sinking immediately after meals. The pods caused an unclean smell from the body of a woman taking them for constipation. Acts as a tonic where the system is broken down, bowels constipated, muscular weakness and waste of nitrogenous materials. RELATIONS - Antidotes: Nux-v., Cham. Compare: (1) Cassi-s., Kali-c., Jal. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Abdomen - Sensation of coldness in the abdomen with emptiness and uneasiness in the stomach. Accumulation of flatus with grumbling and fermentation in the abdomen and discharge of fetid flatus. Painful colic from incarcerated flatulence. Colic, especially in children, infants.

Rectum - Burning in rectum with strangury of bladder. Constipation with colic and flatulence. Stools hard and dark with loss of appetite, coated tongue, bad taste and weakness. Diarrhea with straining and prolapsed rectum and sore anus in children. Liquid stools with griping pains. Loose evacuation with tenesmus and followed by a burning sensation in the anus .Yellowish fluid,with pinching pains before. Greenish mucus, never- get-done sensation (Merc.).

Limbs - Heat in limbs, especially of hands.

Sleep - Ebullition of blood, especially at night, disturbing the sleep. Sleeplessness with cries and tossing, especially in the case of infants.

Liver - Liver enlarged and tender.

Kidneys - Specific gravity and density increased. Hyperazoturia, oxaluria, phos- phaturia and acetonuria.

author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better sitting with legs crossed, crossing or drawing limbs up. Better from exercise,running, dancing, vigorous motion. Better pressure, warmth of bed, hot applications. Better after sleep. Better cold drinks, cold bathing, open air. Worse from cold, air, dampness, north wind, snowy air, snowfall. Worse before thunderstorms. Worse washing clothes, laundry-work. Worse morning and evening. Worse after first sleep, falling to sleep. Worse left side. Worse after sweat. Worse sitting, standing, kneeling, jarring, stooping. Worse ascending, lifting. Worse from touch, rubbing, scratching. Worse after sex, sexual excess. Worse before menses, after pregnancy, miscarriage..
