full:
PHARMACY - sin-a. Sinapis alba. White mustard. Brassica alba. Senescent. N. O. Cru- ciferae. Trituration and tincture of the seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anus, disorders. Backaches. Breast-feeding, disorders. Chills. Colic. Dyspepsia. Esophagus. Flatus. Gastric ulcers. Gastritis. Headaches. Heartbum. Mouth, inflammation. Pregnancy, problems. Salivation. Threadworms. Vomiting. Worms.

HERBAL - Sin-a., like Sin-n., is indigenous to Great Britain. The Treasury of Botany reported that “Its seeds are larger than those of Black Mustard and of a yellow color externally. Chemically they differ in containing a crystalline substance known as sulpho-sinapisin. Moreover, its myrosine yields with water a pungent oil of a different character from the Volatile Oil of Mustard. The seed-leaves or cotyledons of Sin-a. furnish the “mustard” of “mustard and cress,” the “cress” being Lepidium sativum.

HOMEOPATHIC - Bojanus proved Sin-a., taking substantial doses of the triturated seeds and of a tincture made therefrom. Under Sin-a. the prover, who had no sign of threadworms since his thirteenth year, passed many both living and dead and had all the usual rectal symptoms which accompany their presence. The urine too, was turbid, as is often the case in helminthiasis. Marked throat symptoms, especially pressure and burning with obstruction in esophagus, sensation of a lump in esophagus behind the sternum and with eructations, similar symptoms in rectum. The well-known emetic effects of mustard were produced by it and also its “burning” sensations in many parts, notably anus, stomach and esophagus. Flatulence. Headache, (better walking in open air. worse in warm room). Salivation. MIND - Distracted in mind, while reading must make great efforts to keep thoughts from wandering.

Head - Sensation as if head hollow. Rush of blood to head. Headache better in open air worse in warm room. Heaviness in the forehead, as from intoxication or too great warmth of room. Pain in left frontal eminence, paroxysmal, pressive in the evening. Pressive pain in right frontal eminence worse moving head back and forth. Dullness with obscured vision, especially of forehead over eyes, worse walking.

Eyes - Sudden sensation of warmth with stitching in left eye compelling winking, eye fills with tears, after which the sensation disappears. Food - Thirst.

Mouth - Root of tongue thickly coated yellow, on rising in morning, later extends along sides, especially left. Profuse salivation with nausea, nausea better at rest, worse walking about. Saliva frothy, salt.

Throat - Scraping in fauces, provoking frequent hawking. Burning in pharynx in esophagus rising up from stomach like heartburn and pressure in esophagus. Sensation of hard body high up in esophagus, worse swallowing hard food and on empty swallowing in afternoon seems as if a plug sticking in pharynx (this sensation alternated with biting and crawling in anus). Sensation of constriction on swallowing hard food. Sensation as if a large morsel of food had been swallowed. COMMENTS - A. L. Fisher said that for twenty years Sin-a. has had a prominent place in his armamentarium. He used it on the indications of the proving and he found that the states of pregnancy and breast-feeding seem to favor development of the conditions calling for it. He verified “Excessive accumulation of watery saliva or mucus.” “Acute bruised pain, even on slight pressure, just beneath ensiform cartilage.” “Vomiting, ejecta consisting of flakes of mucus with black veins like clots of blood.” “Crawling and burning in anus with griping in abdomen.” “Spasmodic griping in anus, appearing at intervals and especially noticed after swallowing anything.” He cured with Sin-a. “Sore mouth with intensely red mucus membrane, dotted with minute white ulcers, the least food, even of blandest character increasing the burning that is present all the time and also in the throat.” Bojanus noticed an alternation between the symptoms of the anus and those of the pharynx. Clarke cured with Sin-a. “Sharp, shooting pain in right frontal eminence, worse in warm room, better moving about and in open air.” RELATIONS - An overdose of table mustard, which contains both Sin-a. and Sin-n. with starch is immediately antidoted by smelling bread. Compare: (1) Sin-n. - plug sensation. (2) Anae. - ball in anus, Sep. lump in stomach. (3) Bry., Abies-n., Nux-v., Puls. (4) Cina, Sant., Teucr., Napht., Scirr., - worms, helminthiasis. REFERENCES-Clarke.

Stomach - Burning, pressure, fullness and distention in pit of stomach. Thirst without heartburn, drinking water causes sensation of heaviness and fullness in abdomen as after eating. Belchings are tasteless and odorless. Belchings of acid liquid with griping scalding in pharynx, tasting of food. Nausea, qualmishness inclination to vomit, salivation. Nausea better at rest, worse by movement. Retching and vomiting of water. Vomits flakes of mucus with black streaks, yellow, odorless, tasteless matter with much tenacious, jelly-like mucus. After vomiting, scraping in throat and burning rising from stomach.

Abdomen - Movements in abdomen. Heaviness as of a weight, fullness and distention in abdomen. Rumbling and gurgling with emission of odorless flatus. Emission of offensive flatus. Griping colic.

Rectum - Burning, itching in anus, obliging to scratch. Crawling biting in anus. Violent, sudden pain in anus. Spasmodic griping in anus, worse after swallowing anything. Sensation as though a hard substance were lying in anus and could not be evacuated, not better by stool. Stools, black, hard, covered with mucus. Stools, small, thin, soft, greenish, copious, pasty, partly hard partly soft, sour, fermented, yellowish gray. Stools with dead threadworms. Sensations - As if head hollow. As of a plug in throat of hard substance high up in esophagus under sternum, something hard lying in stomach after a moderate meal, hard substance in rectum not better by stool.

Male - Emissions without lascivious dreams.

Chest - Oppression of chest, compelling frequent deep breathing. Burning beneath sternum.

Back - Pains in small of back and coccyx, as if sprained and bruised with urging to stool.

Limbs - Heaviness in lower limbs.

Sleep - Sleeps in afternoon with vivid dreams, aftereating. Vivid dreams of dead people and of death. Dreams confused and unremembered of foreign countries and dangerous expeditions.

Modalities - Better rest, open air. Worse by touch, pressure, motion, warm room. Crawling in anus worse swallowing. Sensation of hard substance in stomach worse after eating.

Kidneys - Urine dark yellow, soon forming transparent cloud, bright golden yellow, dark brown like beer. Many grains of red sand deposited and iridescent film on surface. Thick, fatty pellicle. Cloud remains suspended in urine. Sediment white, like chalk and containing grains of white sand.

Pulse - Pulse full and hard.

Temperature - Creeping chills on moving about, over whole body after vomiting with coldness of hands and feet and frequent belchings of gas. Inclined to perspire.

name: Sinapis Nigra
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better by study or mental diversion. Better sitting erect, shutting eyes. Better hearty meal. Better lying down at night, except dreams. Worse by touch and pressure. Worse motion, leaning forward, stooping. Worse thinking of symptoms. Worse warm room, July, August, damp weather. Worse evening, 4 p.m. to 6 p.m., 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. Laughing causes cough..
constitution: Allergies. Amenorrhea. Asthma. Catarrh. Chlorosis. Chordee. Chorea. Colds. Constipation. Coryza. Coughs. Diarrhea. Hay fever. Headache. Heartbum. Hemorrhoids. Hiccoughs. Intermittents. Menses, premature. Mucous, fever. Pharyngitis. Post-nasal catarrh. Priapism. Scurvy. Strokes. Variola.
keynote:
PHARMACY - sin-n. Sinapis nigra. Black mustard. Brassica nigra. N. O. Cruciferae. Trituration and tincture of seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Amenorrhea. Asthma. Catarrh. Chlorosis. Chordee. Chorea. Colds. Constipation. Coryza. Coughs.…
full:
PHARMACY - sin-n. Sinapis nigra. Black mustard. Brassica nigra. N. O. Cruciferae. Trituration and tincture of seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Amenorrhea. Asthma. Catarrh. Chlorosis. Chordee. Chorea. Colds. Constipation. Coryza. Coughs. Diarrhea. Hay fever. Headache. Heartbum. Hemorrhoids. Hiccoughs. Intermittents. Menses, premature. Mucous, fever. Pharyngitis. Post-nasal catarrh. Priapism. Scurvy. Strokes. Variola.

HERBAL - Sin-n. yields the greater part of the condiment so generally used in England. The plant is indigenous, but is nevertheless largely cultivated in Yorkshire and Durham. Like many other Cracifers, Sin-n. has antiscorbutic properties and it has cured cases of ague, mucus fever, catarrh of bladder of stomach and of air passages. It hasbeen most used in the treatment of hay fever. Cooper suggested the use of Sin-n. as an aperient. He considered that the chief agent in effecting dislodgement of feces in constipated states is flatus. His method of producing this is as follows: A tumblerful of hot water is to be taken in sips in the early morning, the same at breakfast time with some plain brown bread or with no solid food at all. At 11 a.m. one or two capsules of pure mustard, each containing about five grains of the powder to be taken, followed by half a tumbler of hot water. “This last is most important, as the water drives on the capsule and prevents its staying about the cardiac orifice of the stomach and consequent distress to the patient. It also causes contraction of the walls of the stomach and consequent expulsion of flatus into the duodenum.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Sin-n. is of use in hay fever, coryza and pharyngitis. Mucus membrane dry and hot, no discharge, worse afternoon and evening, either nostril may be affected alone or they may be affected alternately. Dry sinuses and pharynx with thick, lumpy secretion. Mucus hawked orcoughed from posterior sinuses felt cold. “Sweat on upper lip and forehead.” Smallpox. During the proving, symptoms were noted including “It seemed to double him up, could hardly stand, tears ran from eyes intense pain across epigastric region. Rose late, feeling sore and stiff all over. Weakness in all muscles.” MIND - Mind worked rapidly. Better by study or mental diversion. Irritable, difficult to think and study. Unreasonably cross.

Head - Headache over right eye worse stooping. Head dull, heavy, better when mind occupied by study, shutting eyes, in open air, worse in warm room, when thinking of it. Frontal headache, most over bridge of nose and around edge of orbits. Forehead hot and dry. Sensation as if scalp were adherent to bones. Scalp hot and itches.

Eyes - Eyes feel weak, pressure causes pricking in them. Pressing feeling in eyes.

Nose - Severe colds. Allergies. Hayfever. Mucus from posterior sinuses. Scanty, acrid discharges, making skin smart. Stoppage of left nostril all day or in afternoon and evening. Nostrils alternately stopped. Dry, hot with lachrymation, sneezing, hacking cough, better lying down. Dryness in both nostrils. Scurvy with copious and frequent nosebleed.

Face - Shrunken features. Burning prickling in face. Sweat on upper lip andforehead. Lips dry and feel as if tissues were stiff. Red around mouth with smarting of lips. Sensation as if cheek were bulged outward by bubble of air, just below malar bone in afternoon.

Mouth - Offensive breath, smelling like onions (Asaf., Coch.). Taste of garlic, causing nausea of horseradish. Profuse saliva. Dry, burning, extending to stomach. Tongue feels blistered. Black tongue. Tongue fissured in middle, dirty white coat, sore, raw. Teeth sensitive to warm drinks and cold air, especially stopped teeth. Swollen bleeding gums.

Throat - Hoarseness, evening from 4 p.m. Feels scalded, hot inflamed. Dry sensation back of nose and throat. Throat sore, left side, on swallowing saliva. Whole throat behind uvula injected light red. Sore throat right side extending to left. Vertigo - Vertigo of old people, violent attacks with hard hearing after eating heavy food, fat. COMMENTS - Hansen added “Acute coryza with thin, watery, excoriating discharge, lachrymation, sneezing. Hacking coughs, better from lying down. Acute pharyngitis, throat feels scalded, hot inflamed. Loud coughing spells with barking expiration, heard at a great distance.” RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Smelling bread (immediate effects of taking excess of condiment): Nux-v„ Rhus- t., or when blistering has been produced by a mustard poultice, soap is the remedy. Compare: (1) Sin-a., Thiosin., Coch. (2) Scalded sensation on tongue, Sang. (3) Cough worse laughing, Arg-n., Phos. (4) Cough, better lying down, Ferr., Mang. (5) Worse from4 p.m. to 6 p.m., Lyc. (6) Amenorrhea, Sulph., Puls. (7) As if hot water in blood vessels (Rhus-t. as if blood running cold). (8) Sulph., Caps., Coloc. (9) Sin-a.. (10) Mustard oil by inhalation - acts on the sensory nerve endings of the trigeminal. Relieves pain in middle ear disease and in painful conditions of nose, nasal cavities and tonsils. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Burning in stomach, extending up esophagus, throat and mouth, which is full of canker sores. Ulceration of stomach and intestines. Pressure in epigastric region. Pain in region of stomach with sensation of faintness compelling to bend forward, which relieves. Hiccough. Heartburn and belching. Hot sour belchings. Colic, pains come on while bentforward, better sitting up straight. Sweat relieves when nausea comes on.

Abdomen - Dull pain in left hypochondriac region. Heavy, dull pain as from weight below umbilical region. Severe twisting in umbilical region. Pain from left of umbilical region to left iliac region, later to right side, ascending colon. Accumulation of flatus with twinges of pain about umbilicus. Rumbling. Left inguinal gland swollen and painful. Sharp pain in right inguinal gland. Dull pain in right inguinal region better by pressure.

Rectum - Before stool uneasy feeling in rectum after stool, smarting cutting low down in rectum and anus. Desire for a stool without passage. Constipated, stools hard like balls. Diarrhea. First stool normal, second loose. Stools offensive. Smarting, cutting pain low down in anus after a stool. Sensations - Vertex as if empty. As if she had taken cold. As if scalp was adherent to bones. As of pins sticking in eyeballs. Eyeballs as if pressed on from above. As if nostrils stopped up. As if movements impeded all around the chest. As if something heavy oppressed her on all sides from neck to diaphragm. As if cheeks were bulged out by a bubble of air below malar bone. Skin of lips as if stiff. As if blisters on tip of tongue. As if a load on stomach. Pain as if heart were on right side. As of hot water in blood vessels.

Male - Violent erections during day and night, obstinate, painful and continued. Awakening him at night with lascivious thoughts, dreams and emissions at night.

Female - Menses appear long before the proper time. Amenorrhea and chlorosis. Food - Appetite good. All food tastes of Sinapis nigra horseradish, later tasteless. Aversion to sweets.

Chest - Wandering pains in chest. Pain in left side of chest in region of heart. Sensation in right chest as if heart were on right side. Respiration at base of left lung roughened.

Heart - Dull, continual pain in heart toward apex in evening, seemingly in heart substance. Heart pains return daily. Sensation as if heart were on right side. Pulse accelerated, full.

Back - Rheumatic pain in intercostal and lumbar muscles, sleeplessness from pain in back and hips. Severe, dull, pulsating pain under inferior angle of left scapula. Slight backache, becoming intolerable towards bedtime, better motion.

Limbs - Dull, heavy ache in legs. Weariness in limbs, with cramps incalves. Weakness in calf-muscles. Constant pain in ankles and calves. Occasional dull pain in left shoulder joint. Lungs - Allergies. Asphyxia. Pituitous asthma. Asthmatic breathing. Loud coughing-spells with barking expiration. Cough is relieved by lying down. Cough mostly dry or with expectoration of lumps of mucus worse in cold air, better lying down. Expectoration from posterior sinuses much mucus, which felt cold, white in tenacious masses.

Sleep - Sleepiness during day, sleepless at night. Sleeps little at night, but does not feel loss of sleep. Restless sleep from pains in back and hips. Vivid or lascivious dreams.

Skin - Burning heat and stitches in skin. Skin turns red. Ecchymosis. Chronic eczema. Smallpox. Ulcers on legs. Frightful suppuration and gangrenous inflammation reaching down to sternum (fatal effects of mustard applied to swollen glands of neck).

Modalities - Better by study or mental diversion. Better sitting erect, shutting eyes. Better hearty meal. Better lying down at night, except dreams. Worse by touch and pressure. Worse motion, leaning forward, stooping. Worse thinking of symptoms. Worse warm room, July, August, damp weather. Worse evening, 4 p.m. to 6 p.m., 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. Laughing causes cough.

Bladder - Pain in bladder. Frequent copious urine flow day and night. Desire frequent, flow increased. Urine, pale, straw colored without sediment. Causations - Damp weather, summer.

Temperature - Severe chills, chattering of teeth, sensation of general coldness with shrunken feeling (from mustard bath). Heat through whole body, especially down spine. Quartan ague and inflammatory fever. Sweat and feeling of hot water in all blood vessels, better when menses came on. Sweat general, especially on forehead and upper lip. Sweat free from mental or physical exertion, from external heat.

HOMEOPATHIC - Knowledge of water parsnip is derived from cases of poisoning…
full:
PHARMACY - sium. Sium latifolium. Water parsnip. N. O. Umbelliferae. Tincture of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Convulsions. Dizziness. Opisthotonos. Spasms. Tetanus.

HOMEOPATHIC - Knowledge of water parsnip is derived from cases of poisoning through eating the root. The Sium, symptoms bear a strong resemblance to those of the other poisonous Umbelliferae. The most pronounced features of the convulsions were the drawing of the arms to the middle of the body, flexure of the fingers and the preponderance of the contractions on the left side. Opisthotonos. Spasms, at first violently clonic, diminishing with each succeeding convulsion until they became little more than tremors. Loss of voluntary motion. Lack of mental energy (Aeth.). MIND - Mentally excited. Lack of mental activity. Fear of death.

Head - Dizziness, headache. Lungs - Breathing slow and stertorous.

Eyes - Pupils dilated, responded steadily to bright light.

Throat - Burning along digestive tract, especially esophagus. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Stomach - Nausea and vomiting, followed by a convulsion.

Abdomen - Sense of swelling and flatulence about bowels.

Temperature - Skin cold and clammy. Head hot, rest of body cold. Wet with perspiration.

name: Sisyrinchium Glaxoides
author: Murphy
constitution: Coma. Delirium. Snakebites. Wounds.
keynote:
PHARMACY - sisy. Sisyrinchium glaxoides. Blue-eyed grass. N. O. Iridaceae. The fresh root is macerated in twice its weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Coma. Delirium. Snakebites. Wounds.

HERBAL - Sisyrinchium was one of the old…
full:
PHARMACY - sisy. Sisyrinchium glaxoides. Blue-eyed grass. N. O. Iridaceae. The fresh root is macerated in twice its weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Coma. Delirium. Snakebites. Wounds.

HERBAL - Sisyrinchium was one of the old “Thompsonian remedies.” Dr. W. U. Reed of Indiana contributed the following in 1892 to the Hom. Recorder, concerning this little known remedy. “The roots of Sisyrinchium are used in the treatment of snake bites. A tincture is made from the roots, it is said to have been used by the Indians in treating snake bites, by bruising and moistening the roots and applying to the wound.” The symptoms of the snake bites cured with Sisy. are bluish black colored skin, as if dreadfully bruised. The whole body becomes very red, hot and dry, face dark red. The leg and foot are enormously swollen and of the same general appearance. The foot, calf of the leg and thigh turn black. Patient delirious but would cry out if touched. Wild delirium all night. Unconscious. Pulse quick and hard. COMMENTS - Dr. W. U. Reed stated* We have growing in our woods and fields a small plant, which I believe to be a specific for the treatment of persons or animals bitten by the rattlesnake. From my own experience and observation in the use of this remedy, I believe it to be a positive cure in all cases if exhibited in any reasonable time. “I have never known it to fail in a single instance, even where the alcoholic treatment and many other kinds had failed. I am not aware of its ever having been used as a medicine by the profession and, so far as I know, I am the first to prepare and use it in the form of a tincture.” Dr. Reed gave these cases: “( 1 ) Bessie A., aged six years, while playing in the yard on a farm, some twelve miles in the country, was bitten in the hand by a rattlesnake which was killed a moment after by the mother of the little girl who was attracted by the screams of the child. “Sixteen hours after I arrived, everything having been done in the meantime that had ever been heard of by the parents, even to applying a poultice the wound with entrails of a black chicken. “The little sufferer was indeed, an object of pity. The hand and arm were swollen almost to bursting, the swelling extending to the shoulder and spine, being of a blush black color as if dreadfully bruised. This discoloration extended over the back to the hips. Skin hot and dry, face flushed, pulse quick and hard. Child unconscious. “1 felt that the case was hopeless. But, through the earnest entreaties of the mother, I proceeded to do what I could. Saturating a piece of cotton with the tincture I had prepared, I bound it on the wound, then dropping twelve drops in a glass of water I directed that a teaspoonful be given every hour, the compress to be renewed every hour also, until my return. “I confess I had little hope of seeing my little patient alive again but on my return the following day I was much rejoiced to find a decided change for the better in the condition of the little sufferer. The swelling was not nearly so tense, the fever had subsided, the delirium gone and the danger seemed past. The treatment was continued and a speedy and permanent recovery followed. “(2) Burt Whitten, aged ten, while out in a marsh with a number of older boys gathering huckleberries, was bitten in the right ankle by a rattler. He was so frightened when he saw the snake, as it bit him, that he ran all the way home, a distance of nearly a mile, although the day was very hot. “This patient came to my hands after the usual alcoholic treatment for twenty four hours by an allopathic physician with the patient growing worse all the time. I found this patient in about the same condition as the first. “The leg and foot were enormously swollen and of the same general appearance, the foot, calf of the leg and thigh were black, the whole body was very red, hot and dry, face dark red, pulse quick and hard, patient delirious but would cry out if touched. “Fifteen drops in a glass of water. Teaspoonful every hour with cotton saturated with the tincture applied to the wound. In this case the change, I was informed by the father, was quite noticeable in two hours. “The boy had been in a wild delirium all night and up to the time he received the first dose of Sisy. After the second dose he became quiet and in two hours the delirium had passed away. Under this treatment the patient was able to be out on the streets again in four days, though the discoloration did not disappear for some time after. “Many more cases might be given where this remedy has been given to both man and beast with the same results.” REFERENCES - Anshutz.

name: Skatolum
author: Murphy
constitution: Allergies. Breast, tumor. Catarrh. Coryza. Eczema. Hayfever. Lithemia. Otitis media. Ozaena. Rheumatism. Skin, disorders. Urticaria. Vaccination, effects.
keynote:
PHARMACY - skat. Skatolum. Skatol. Methyl-indol. Minerals, carbon compounds. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Breast, tumor. Catarrh. Coryza. Eczema. Hayfever. Lithemia. Otitis media. Ozaena. Rheumatism. Skin, disorders. Urticaria. Vaccination,…
full:
PHARMACY - skat. Skatolum. Skatol. Methyl-indol. Minerals, carbon compounds. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Breast, tumor. Catarrh. Coryza. Eczema. Hayfever. Lithemia. Otitis media. Ozaena. Rheumatism. Skin, disorders. Urticaria. Vaccination, effects.

HOMEOPATHIC - The medical and curative properties of this remarkable lake were known to the Native Americans of the northwest; they have many legends and tribal history concerning the lake, and it was held in much reverence by them. The country around this lake was called “Sahala Lyee Illihe,” or “Sacred Grounds,” and no matter how hostile the tribes were to each other no members j ourneying to or from the “Skookum Limechen Chuck,” or “strong medicine water,” were ever molested. “In the Skookum Chuck we have a remedy for all our ai Iments. We only have to bathe i n and drink its water and we are made well. If we sign the treaty we will forever offend the Great Spirit, we will sign away our mother and she will cry. Her tears will dry up these lakes and we will be hungry and sick. We will go the Skookum Chuck only to find that its water have disappeared.” It is an anti-psoric remedy. Affinity for the skin and mucus membranes. Skin disorders. Eczema. Urticaria. Lithemia. Vaccinal eczema. Dry skin. Hay fever. Profuse coryza and constant sneezing. Catarrh. Profuse, ichorous, cadaverously smelling discharge. Otitis media.

Head - Frontal headache, worse over left eye in the evening, better by short step.

Nose - Profuse coryza with constant sneezing as in hay fever.

Mouth - Tongue coated. Foul taste. Salty taste to all cereals.

Stomach - Belching.

Stool - Light, yellow, narrow, very offensive stool. Intestinal dyspepsia. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Indol., Bapt., Sulph. REFERENCES Boericke. ***SKOOKUM CHUCK AQUA (Mineral Springs) PHARMACY - skook. Skookum chuck aqua. Mineral springs. Skookum limechen chuck. Medical lake. Strong Medicine Water. Salts of water from Medical Lake near Spokane, Wash. A lake in Western USA containing in grains per gallon: sodic carbonate 63.54, sodic chloride 16.37, sodic silicate 10.63, potassic chloride 9.24, ferrous carbonate. 526, Mag-c. 237, Calc. 186, aluminic oxide. 175 with traces of lithic carbonate, Bor. and potassic sulphate. Trituration of the dried salt. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, third trituration.

Back - Heaviness in sacrum. Food - Appetite increased.

Limbs - Severe rheumatic pains in limbs.

Sleep - Increased desire to sleep, wakes unrefreshed, half doped feeling.

Skin - Eczema. Urticaria. Dry skin. COMMENTS - In the U. S. Med. Investigator, 1889, Dr. W. D. Gentry told the story of a Frenchman passing by the lake, before the properties of the water became known to the white men, with a drove of sheep afflicted with a skin disease called “the scab.” As soon as the sheep saw the water they ran to it. but would not drink. They stood in the water for some time, and in a few days they were well of the “scab.” The Frenchman was suffering with rheumatism and decided to try the water for his disease. He was steadily cured. Stories of marvelous cures were reported by the Native Americans and by seeing those who had been taken there on litter, appearing at the point of death, return in health and vigor. The cure of many cases of inveterate skin disease is on record, the external use of Skook. soap or ointment has been employed as well as the internal administration. W. D. Ingalls reported the case of Mrs. D„ 48, who had eczema of her feet. Fissured skin, exuding an acrid secretion. So excessively sore that the patient had not been able to wear shoes or walk any distance for two years. Skook. 2x was given internally, an ointment of a drachm to the ounce of vaseline applied and Skookum soap used for washing. In two months the patient was able to wear shoes and in three months the feet were well. Mrs. H., 23, had a benign growth in left breast, noticed eight months. No history of tuberculosis or cancer in family. Skook. was gi ven for the first week, one grain of 1 x every four hours, for the second week, two grains of Skook. 2x every four hours, for the next seven weeks, five-grain powders of Skook. 3x, when the patient was cured. Mr. J., had chronic nasal catarrh, discharge greenish yellow having odor of ozaena, was greatly relieved and apparently on the way to cure. B. F. Bailey reported the cure of Mrs. X., 40 of lithemic diathesis, never free from eczematic trouble for years. At times much rheumatism. Not infrequently the rheumatism disappears and is immediately followed by styes on the eyelids. Formerly treated allopathically and also homeopathically. Skook. 3x every four hours. Improvement soon showed itself and the patient was well in three months and remained so. Mrs. Y., 26, lithemic with flushed face and yellowish background. Urine, 1030 and with marked uric acid deposits. Much difficulty of digestion. Great dryness of skin, especially of scalp. Hair falling out to such an extent that baldness was feared. Skook. 3x was given every four hours. Hair ceased to fall out. The heated, congested feeling of head and face disappeared and the patient became well. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Tab. Compare: (1) Nat-c., Nat-m. (2) Skin disorders, Graph., Med., Maland., Vac. (3) Saxon. - appears has remarkable cleansing, deodorizing and soothing properties for the skin. Eczema, scalds, burns, sores and hemorrhoids. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Kidneys - Frequent, scanty, burning, difficult.

name: Slag
author: Murphy
constitution: Constipation. Debility. Diarrhea. Flatulence. Headache. Hemorrhoids. Housemaid’s knee. Lumbago. Spleen, disorders. Tuberculosis.
keynote: PHARMACY - slag. Slag. Pulverized slag. Blast-iron-furnace cinder. Slag silica. Silico-sulphocalcite of alumina. Slag was analyzed and found to contain the following: Silica, Alumina, Calcium, Sulphur, part of these occur as Calc-s., Ferrum, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Manganum.…
full:
PHARMACY - slag. Slag. Pulverized slag. Blast-iron-furnace cinder. Slag silica. Silico-sulphocalcite of alumina. Slag was analyzed and found to contain the following: Silica, Alumina, Calcium, Sulphur, part of these occur as Calc-s., Ferrum, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Manganum. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Constipation. Debility. Diarrhea. Flatulence. Headache. Hemorrhoids. Housemaid’s knee. Lumbago. Spleen, disorders. Tuberculosis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Slag was introduced into medicine by J. Meredith who gave the 6x trituration to a patient suffering from housemaid’s knee and in addition to relieving this it took away “a dreadful anal itching, hemorrhoids and constipation as if by magic.” Meredith confirmed the rectal power of Slag by experiments on his own person. Acting on Meredith’s suggestion, George Herring instituted a proving with the 3x on himself and others. Herring’s only symptom was a creeping irritation of the skin or under the skin in the umbilical region, sufficiently severe to keep him awake. Drowsiness in evening. Digestive weakness and flatulence. Soreness of the anus. Constipation and diarrhea. Hemorrhoids with anal itching and soreness. Tuberculosis. Housemaid’s knee. Lumbago. Spleen disorders. Spleen pain and stitches in heart. A pain (dull, heavy sensation) alternated between inter-scapular region and spleen. Stiffness at back of head, neck and pain between shoulders. Dull, stupefying frontal headache. COMMENTS - One prover, in which Slag produced no symptoms, was cured of flatulent distention in the evening and an oppressive feeling over the heart. Another prover had constipation relieved, but Slag produced “soreness of anus.” In a delicate woman of tubercular history, took Slag 3x twice a day, and experienced diarrhea, debility, quick pulse, lumbago with pain in back, distention of stomach, so that she had to loosen her dress, profuse night- sweat, cough and expectoration. Phos., Ph-ac., Carb. v. were given to this patient in succession and all helped. Another proving of Slag was made by F. C. B. The prover was age 33, rather dark, nervo-bilious, had chronically enlarged tonsils and tendency to colds in the head. He took Slag by way of experiment, hoping to cure his tonsils. RELATIONS - Effects were relieved by: Phos., Ph-ac., Carb-v. Compare: (1) Constipation, flatulence, Lyc., Carb-v., Sulph. (2) Anal symptoms, Graph., Nit-ac. (3) Intolerance of tight clothing, Lach. (4) Housemaid’s knee, Stict., Apis., Sep. REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Sol
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Ameliorated by cloudy weather. Better hot bath, when chilled to bone. Better short naps, sleep. Better bending double, sitting down. Eyes better hot flannel. Throat better cold sweet drinks. Headaches better pressure, cold application, orange juice. Worse sunlight (Nat-m.), from sunrise to sunset. Spasms coming with sunrise and ceasing with sunset. Worse from standing. Eyes are worse from wind..
constitution: Allergies. Backache. Burns. Cancer. Cataracts. Chills. Constipation. Dermatitis. Faintness. Freckles. Headaches. Heat, stroke. Lupus. Menses, premature. Paralysis. Photophobia. Radiation, sickness. Skin, cancers. Skin, disorders. Snowblindness. Sunburns. Sunstroke.
keynote:
PHARMACY - sol. Sol. Sunlight. Lactose is exposed to concentrated sun’s rays and stirred with a glass rod until saturated. Potencies made by Fincke. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Backache. Burns. Cancer. Cataracts. Chills. Constipation. Dermatitis.…
full:
PHARMACY - sol. Sol. Sunlight. Lactose is exposed to concentrated sun’s rays and stirred with a glass rod until saturated. Potencies made by Fincke. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Backache. Burns. Cancer. Cataracts. Chills. Constipation. Dermatitis. Faintness. Freckles. Headaches. Heat, stroke. Lupus. Menses, premature. Paralysis. Photophobia. Radiation, sickness. Skin, cancers. Skin, disorders. Snowblindness. Sunburns. Sunstroke.

HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Finsen, of Copenhagen, revived and confirmed much of the ancient light-therapy. O. V. Thayer published, in 1893, a series of cases in which he had used concentrated rays of sunlight (solar cautery) including cases of skin cancer, rodent ulcer, parasitic diseases, moles, small wens, and birthmarks. H. T. Webster gave details ofacase of epithelioma in which the growth was removed by solar cautery and a scarcely perceptible scar left. Sunlight has cured skin cancers ' and lupus in the hands of Finsen. Potentized sunlight has been used for sun dermatitis, heat stroke, cancer and radiation. Chronic sun headaches ( Verat., Glon., Nat- c, Nat-m.). Violent headache from vertex down to forehead with hot sensation in face. Keynote photophobia. Very sensitive to sunshine. Sunburns easily. Never well since severe sunburn. Sunlight damage of the eyes, from over-exposure, snow- blindness, sunblindness. Cataracts. Radiation exposure with nausea, vomiting, hair loss, emaciation (Cadm- s., X-ray.). Mental excitement and anxiousness, at first with trembling of the heart, finally remaining in the stomach pit. Faintness, prostration and general stiffening up of the whole system, the body strength seems more equalized. Spasm coming with sunrise and ceasing with sunset. Some spasms appearing at sunset. MIND-Decisiveness and assertive. Impatient to make decisions. Cheerful. Urge to be healthy, to eat fruit. Mental restlessness. In control, then out of control. Irresolution. Light headed and mentally disorientated. Loses his way in well-known streets. Depression, tearful. Sensitive. Suspicious. Irritable, impatient and frustrated. Irritability over trifles. Fastidious. Argumentative and angry. Nasty. Desire to bang head and scream. Escapism. Excitement. Anxiety with trembling in heart. Anxiety in solar plexus. Anxiety if somebody comes towards her. Nervous, as if ail the nerves were trembling. Very sensitive and easily frightened. Frightened on the approach of anyone coming toward them. Delusion of being pursued.

Head - Light headed and mentally disorientated. Violent headache from vertex down to forehead. Headache with the excitement and anxiousness at stomach pit. Left sided headache. Pain in forehead, as if forehead would crush itself down upon the eyes. Headache from sunshine on bare head, better by laying a glass of water on solar plexus. Very sensitive to sunshine on the vertex. Extreme painfulness if the sunshine strikes the bare head. Violent stitches in brain. Stitching pain if she does not gain the shade, stomachache and nausea follow. Sensation of undulating or floating in head after mental excitement. Instantaneous shock to brain, followed by prostration and a scalding sensation on top of head. Excessive perspiration of head and neck.

Eyes - Painful eyes from glare of sunlight. Photophobia. Light offends eyes. Snow-blindness. Diminished sensitivity of eyes, odd-blindness. Blurry vision with headaches. Suffusion of veins, of sclerotica. Cataracts. Stinging pains. Sensation of swelling, as if eyes would force themselves out of sockets. Puffiness around the eyes.

Ears - Sharp shooting pain from left ear to nose, continued at intervals for some time. Partial deafness.

Nose - Sneezing with a little sore throat, as if she had taken cold. Stopped up, right nostril blocked completely.

Face - Jaws rigidly set as in trismus. Painful large spot on cheek. Pressing pain with sensation of heat in face. Perspiration on face, warm and tingly. Hot sweat on face, cold to touch. Dripping perspiration.

Mouth - Offensive breath. Brown tongue, unpleasant taste on tongue. Food tastes like something she cannot tell. Food is more palatable if put in the sunshine. Dry mouth in morning. Sore gum, right side, top of mouth. Nail biting. Stupid, cannot articulate a word. Articulates with difficulty.

Throat - Swollen glands. Yellow ulcer on right side of throat, no pain. Swollen throat, white pus on left side. Sore, achy throat, on waking, desire for cold drinks. Sore throat better eating, worse after dinner. Catch in throat after sudden dry mouth in morning. Sensation of loose skin flopping on back of throat on swallowing. Catarrh. Vertigo - Vertigo on waking at 6 am, better lying, worse closing eyes. Dizziness with nausea, worse standing, sitting. Dizziness with nausea, much better lying, sleeping. COMMENTS - In 1880, Swan published a pathogenesis which contained information obtained from four provers and from Reichenbach’s experiences from hypersensitives. The common effects of strong sunlight, such as sneezing, freckling and sunstroke, may be added to the list. Dr. Thayer, in 1893 in southern California, wrote a paper on sunlight for a homeopathic journal. He described how to “Concentrate the sun rays to a diseased part until slightly burned or charred and then wait until it heals and then repeat the procedure.” He claimed to have cured all kinds of cancers, removed birthmarks, tattoos, warts, sebaceous cysts, ulcers, varicose veins and all other types of benign growths. “Unlike other caustics, it can be applied upon the most delicate of tissues and it causes only slight irritation and most heal with only the slightest scar.” Dr. Thayer coined the term “solar cauterization.” A magnifying glass was used and the sunbeam was focused right on the skin cancer, until a burning sensation was felt, then stopped. This would be repeated once or twice a day. After a week or ten days the melanoma would fall off and it would heal without a scar. Thayer had a whole practice based on the magnifying glass and focusing the sunlight in 1893 and very few homeopaths used his methods. Dr. Foubister revived interest in Sol in its potentized form as an antidote for radiation poisoning from radiation therapy with cancer patients. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Aeon., Bell., Glon., Gels, and other sunstroke remedies. Compare: (1) Luna, Elect., M-aust., X-ray. (2) Cadm-s., radiation poisoning. (2) Dislike of sun, Lach., Nat-c., Nat-m., Glon. REFERENCES - Clarke. Daws. Foubister. Murphy. Scriven.

Stomach - Anxiety in solar plexus. Heat in pit of stomach. Empty feeling in stomach, as if she had not eaten anything substantial yesterday and today. Sensation of faintness and vacuity in stomach pit. Nausea, no hunger, desires cold drinks. Nausea on waking, worse as morning progressed. Nausea after lunch. Slight inclination to vomit, or actual vomiting. Desire to vomit but unable to.

Abdomen - Anxiety in solar plexus. Swollen sensation on right side. Distention and hardness. Abdominal cramps with menses. Cramping pain on right side, better bending double. Griping pain, like diarrhea. Foul flatulence. Sensation as after childbirth or at conception (with great excitement).

Rectum - Constipation. Pale colored stool. Diarrhea at night in bed, yellow/brown, painless with green leucorrhea. Diarrhea on going to bed just before menses. Loose stools. Pains better stool. Hemorrhoids.

Male - Loss of libido. Increased libido.

Female - Achy and bloated before menses. Diarrhea before menses, on going to bed. Menses six to seven days too soon. Menses, bright red blood. Menses slow, spotting. Very heavy menses, bright red blood, occasional clots, abdominal cramps. Sharp pain in uterus which turned to cramp, worse bending forward. Spots on back during menses. Green leucorrhea at night, with yellow-brown diarrhea. Itching genitalia, some discharge. Food - Diminished appetite and thirst. Loss of appetite first thing in the morning. Desire for hot chocolate. Desire for juicy, refreshing things, oranges and grapefruit. Desire for cheese and salty foods. Desire for meat, prawns. Thirst, desires cold sweet drinks, lime juice. Thirstless, sips lemon squash, which relieves the throat.

Chest - Sensation as if a weight on chest. Chest very tight with wheezing. Armpits perspired without exertion. Sharp pain, top of rib cage.

Heart - Anxiety with trembling in heart. Weakness about heart.

Back - Backaches. Pain in left side of back, hip joint area. Heat rash, red blobs, on back. Spots on back during menses. Itchiness, worse evening and in bed, better scratching. Breasts - Tender, swollen breasts, before menses. Sharp pain in left breast.

Limbs - Drawing through all his limbs after rising. Right side, arm and foot, weak as from partial paralysis. Pain in left elbow. Hands and feet cold. The back of hand exposed to sunshine feels warm, while at same time a coolness appears in palm and runs up whole arm into temple. Cool, refreshed sensations. Pains as if bruised. Pain like toothache deep inside left hip, better as day progressed, better walking. Fingers numb with cold, chilled to bone. Lungs - Wheezing, difficulty in breathing, before bedtime. Wheezing on exhalation and inhalation. Coughs on talking. Coughed up green catarrh and blood, worse evening.

Sleep - Sleeplessness until 3 a.m. to 4 a.m. Head very much excited, could not sleep for hours. Great sleepiness all through the head and not merely in the eyes, heavy, sound sleep all through night. Sound sleep, oversleeping. Dreams of being lost, of travel. Tired on waking. Tired all day with irritability, worse early evening, better sleeping. Sleepiness, better short naps.

Skin - Freckles. Itching, red skin. Red blotches from sunlight. Skin sensitive to sunlight. Sunburns easily. Never well since severe sunburn. Skin cancer. Dermatitis, often with cold limbs, degenerates into megrim. Nevi. Painful spot on cheek. Spots on back during menses. Peeling of skin on left hand.

Modalities - Ameliorated by cloudy weather. Better hot bath, when chilled to bone. Better short naps, sleep. Better bending double, sitting down. Eyes better hot flannel. Throat better cold sweet drinks. Headaches better pressure, cold application, orange juice. Worse sunlight (Nat-m.), from sunrise to sunset. Spasms coming with sunrise and ceasing with sunset. Worse from standing. Eyes are worse from wind.

Teeth - Grinding of teeth as in helminthic spasms.

Kidneys - Increased urine though drinking less, night as well as day. Polyuria, urinates five times in night. Nocturia. Urine and stool invariably suspended.

Perspiration - Perspiration streaming out of stomach pit over whole body. Perspiration under armpits with no exertion.

Temperature - Cold shivers with aching neck glands. Chilled to bone, very cold. An agreeable coolness extends over whole body. Chills. Running chills of increasing sensation of cold in all limbs from holding wires partially exposed to the sun. Shivering. Felt cold in night, drew up more cover and perspired. Congestive chill from exposure to sun right after drinking cold water freely.

name: Solaninum Aceticum
author: Murphy
constitution: Lungs, paralysis. Tetanus. Ticklishness.
keynote:
PHARMACY - solin. Solaninum aceticum. Solanium aceticum aut purum. An alkaloid obtained from various Solanums, especially dulcamara and nigrum, also from the potato plant. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

full:
PHARMACY - solin. Solaninum aceticum. Solanium aceticum aut purum. An alkaloid obtained from various Solanums, especially dulcamara and nigrum, also from the potato plant. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Lungs, paralysis. Tetanus. Ticklishness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Solin. is obtained from many of the Solanaceae. and especially from Dulc. It exists in potatoes, and under certain conditions of germination, potatoes may contain a poisonous amount. An accident of that kind occurred in soldiers at Pfuhl who were supplied with potatoes containing about 24 percent Solin. Sixty-six soldiers had marked poisoning symptom including shivering, fever, vomiting, syncope and in one case convulsions. Skin and conjunctiva were tinged yellow. Clarke’s first acquaintance with Solin. was through seeing the effect of Solin. 2c in solution given by Dr. Hughes to a diabetic and semi-paralytic man of 60 who had frequent threat of respiratory paralysis with accumulations of mucus which he was unable to expel. Solin., more than any other remedy, rescued him from danger and prolonged his life. Solin. was proved by Clarus and Schroff, among others. Slowed and oppressed respiration was a marked feature. Respiration was slowed in inverse proportion to the increase in the pulse rate. Cerebrospinal irritation, hyperesthesia and convulsions, worse by touch. Fainting. Weakness. Sensitiveness to light, noise and touch. Skin more easily tickled than usual. In animals, the hind limbs were rigid and paralyzed and in the pro vers the lower limbs were weakened. MIND - Stupefaction without previous excitement. Fainting.

Head - Vertigo. Cerebrospinal meningitis. Head hot. heavy, dull, painful. Pain in occiput.

Eyes - Pupils slightly contracted.

Mouth - Salivation. Bitter taste. The pure alkaloid has a cooling, acid and salt taste and when chewed causes a glutinous sensation in pharynx and throat with scraping which extends to stomach, where it becomes a peculiar sticking pain.

Throat - Scraping in throat. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Dulc., Bell., Sol-c., Sol-nig., Sol-tub. or Sol-t-ae. (2) In respiratory paralysis, Dulc., Bell. (3) Sleepy but cannot sleep, Bell. (4) Hyperesthesia, Nux-v, Tetox. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Stomach - Constant belchings. Nausea and diarrhea and vomiting. Nausea, violent ineffectual efforts to vomit. About 5 p.m., vomiting three times without previous nausea or pain or any intestinal symptoms.

Abdomen - Rumbling in abdomen.

Chest - Convulsions of thorax, which were associated tonic spasms of limbs.

Heart - Pulse increased in rapidity, weak, thready. Pulse and respiration slowed. Increased pulse rate with slowed respiration.

Limbs - Weakness of lower limbs. Slight tonic spasms of lower limbs. Lungs - Hoarseness. Breathing is slow, superficial, difficult and oppressed, distressed, especially on inspiration. Moist rattle during inspiration. Frequent violent outcry. Masses of mucus in larger air passages. Paralysis of respiration.

Sleep - Frequent yawning. Great sleepiness with inability to sleep. Sleep restless, frequently disturbed by frightful dreams. Sleep frequently interrupted, without dreams.

Skin - Yellow discoloration of skin. Skin dry. Hyperesthesia, creeping along spine when touching the skin, more easily tickled than natural. Itching.

Kidneys - Albumen in urine.

Temperature - Limbs cold. Shivering, fever, vomiting and syncope. Profuse perspiration without weakness.

full:
PHARMACY - sol-c. Solanum carolinense. Horse-nettle. N. 0. Solanaceae. The fresh, ripe berries are macerated in twice their weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HERBAL - In 1889 Dr. Napier called attention to Solanum carolinense as a remedy for the treatment of epilepsy, stating that it was used as a domestic remedy in for convulsions and “that he had successfully prescribed it in his practice.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Sol-c. has convulsions and epilepsy, twenty to forty-drop doses is of great value in grand mal of idiopathic epilepsy, where the disease has begun beyond age of childhood, hystero-epilepsy, also in whooping cough. COMMENTS - Dr. Charles S. Potts of the University of Pennsylvania, contributed a paper to The Gazette, Dec., 1895, on the remedy, giving several cases. H. T., male, aged thirteen years. Idiopathic epilepsy, had his first spell five years ago, averaged one paroxysm daily. Sol-c. was first given in 10 drops doses without effect. When increased to 25 drops, the spells were lighter in severity, but occurred about as often. The dose was finally increased to a teaspoonful four times daily. After being put upon this dose he was under observation six weeks during which time he had six seizures much lighter in severity. T. H., male, aged twenty-eight years. He had epileptic seizures for three years, following an injury to the head which rendered him unconscious, but produced no other visible injury. Since this, however, had almost constant headache. The first spell was six months after the injury and have been frequent after, averaging three to four weekly, of an ordinary type. Sol-c. in 40-drops doses three times daily was given, the spells at once decreased in frequency and severity. During the last six weeks he was under observation he only had three spells, very mild in type. A. N., male, aged thirty years. First spell one year ago, have since occurred every two weeks, good deal of headache. Sol-c. 30c drops three times a day. No spells for one month and headache ceased. He then stopped attendance. J. D., female, aged eighteen years. First spell when thirteen years old, had one spell a month at the time of her menstrual period. About a week before her next period, she was given Sol-c. 40 drops three times a day and escaped the usual spell. The following month however, she had one. I. K., female, aged twenty-five years. Nocturnal epilepsy forpast three years, about one spell a month. While using Sol-c. 40 drops three times a day, went three weeks longer than usual without a spell. The dose was then increased to 1 fluid drachm, she then ceased her visit. F. S., female, aged twelve years. First spell five weeks before her visit, had been having them daily since. Sol- c. 30 drops ordered, this dose was gradually increased to 1 fluid drachm. During the three months that she was under observation her spells averaged in number about one a week. H. B., male, aged eighteen years. First convulsion at age of ten years, then had none until three months before visit, had general convulsions about once daily since. Sol-c. 40 drops ordered. He was only under observation nine days, having during that time four spells, much milder in character. A. C., female, aged fifteen years. First convulsion one year before, they had been increasing in frequency, up to one about every three days. During the three weeks she was taking Sol-c. 30 drops three times a day she had one spell, occurring during the third week. H. K., male, aged eighteen years. First spell when fourteen years old. Every three or four days had several attacks in succession, an average of about one daily. While taking Sol-c. 40 drops, afterwards increased to teaspoonful-doses, he had twelve in thirty-eight days, an average of a little less than one in three days, going six without having any. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke.

CLINICAL - Coxalgia. Coughing. Hemoptysis. Imtabi lity. Sleep, abnormal. Thought, difficult. Tobacco, effects.…
full:
PHARMACY - sol-m. Solanum mammosum. Apple of sodom. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of fresh ripe fruit. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Coxalgia. Coughing. Hemoptysis. Imtabi lity. Sleep, abnormal. Thought, difficult. Tobacco, effects. Twitching.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hering is the authority for Sol-m. The chief symptoms are irritability and inability to think. Uneasiness and inability to keep quiet. Sleepiness without being able to sleep, a kind a stupor worse at time of flood tide, at the full moon, better with ebb tide. Hawking, of blood-streaked mucus. Sensitiveness to tobacco (Ign.). MIND - Irritability. Becomes exasperated at what he thinks may happen. Mental confusion. Inability for continuous thought. Difficulty expressing ideas.

Rectum - No stool, stool occurred later than usual and after much pressure.

Back - Twitching of large muscle below right scapula, as if the flesh were pinched up by the hand and shaken back and forth.

Limbs - Sticking pain in left hip joint that made him quite lame, frequently during and after walking, disappearing after standing and sitting down. Lungs - Mucus hawked from the larynx contains streaks of bright blood.

Sleep - Great weariness and desire to sleep without ability to sleep, followed by slumbering without real sleep. Deep sleep, from which he awoke and could not collect his senses for a long time and remained long in an irresolute condition. Sleepy in evening and sleeps well all night, even after afternoon sleeping. Dreams of death with violent weeping. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Skin - Causes blotches over whole body from poisoning.

name: Solanum Nigrum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better closing eyes. Worse by touch, motion. Worse moving head, beginning to move after sitting. Worse walking (inclines to left), misstep. Worse swallowing. Worse morning on waking, light. Worse bright sunshine (eyes)..
constitution: Amaurosis. Blindness. Chorea. Convulsion. Coryza. Delirium. Headaches. Heartburn. Hydrocephalus. Mania. Meningitis. Night-terrors. Parotiditis. Peritonitis. Psoriasis. Puerperal convulsions. Scarlatina. Skin, disorders. Smallpox. Stammering speech. Tetanus. Trismus. Tympanitis. Typhoidfever. Ulcers. Varicose veins. Vertigo.
keynote:

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Blindness. Chorea. Convulsion. Coryza. Delirium. Headaches. Heartburn. Hydrocephalus. Mania. Meningitis.…
full:
PHARMACY - sol-n. Solanum nigrum. Black nightshade. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Blindness. Chorea. Convulsion. Coryza. Delirium. Headaches. Heartburn. Hydrocephalus. Mania. Meningitis. Night-terrors. Parotiditis. Peritonitis. Psoriasis. Puerperal convulsions. Scarlatina. Skin, disorders. Smallpox. Stammering speech. Tetanus. Trismus. Tympanitis. Typhoidfever. Ulcers. Varicose veins. Vertigo.

HERBAL - Sol-n. is a common weed found in waste places. It has white flowers and black berries. Green’s Herbal recorded that “The leaves applied externally ease the pain and abate inflammation. Too large aquantity occasions violent sickness and headaches, giddiness, drowsiness and other dangerous symptoms. The Arabs apply the leaves to burns and ulcers, skin diseases and scrofulous and cancerous affections, they are diaphoretic, diuretic and purgative.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Hale said some country practitioners used Sol-n. with much success under the impression that it was “an indigenous Belladonna,” having been misled by the name “nightshade.” Hale verified its use in meningitis and headache. Also in scarlatina when the eruption is blotchy. He justly pointed out the close affinity of Sol-n. with Bell.: Delirium, headache, flushed face, sparkling eyes, pains coming and going suddenly, fiery rashes, burning skin and sweat. “Frightful” headaches. Splitting, throbbing, bursting, piercing headaches, worse by least movement of head, least movement after sitting, light, noise, stooping. Headache is worse in a warm room and better in open air. Great sensitiveness to cold air. Marked action on head and eyes. Brain irritation during dentition. Restlessness of a violent and convulsive nature. Formication with contraction of limbs. Ergotism with tetanic spasms and stiffness of whole body with mania. Black appearance, bruised feeling all over the body. Chronic intestinal toxemia. MIND - Mania. Furious delirium, characterized by the cephalic cry, efforts to escape and stammering speech. Night-terrors. Complete cessation of the mental faculties due to headaches.

Head - Terrible headaches and complete cessation of the mental faculties. Congestive headaches (Bell.). Splitting, throbbing, bursting, piercing pains. Headaches at 10 a.m. Headache causes him to close eyes. Headaches, worse by least movement of head, light, noise, stooping. Lungs - Constrictive feeling in chest with difficult breathing, cough with tickling in throat. Expectoration thick, yellow.

Eyes - Pain over both eyes. Alternate dilatation and contraction of pupils, weak sight, floating spots.

Nose - Acute coryza, profuse, watery discharge from right nostril, left stopped up with chilly sensation, alternating with heat. Sensations - Brain as if swimming. As if things moving in a circle, when stooping. As if brain shaking about in skull, on moving head. As if head would split. As from a blow on forehead. As if sand in eyes. As if splinter in right tonsil. Tongue as if scalded. Pains come and go suddenly. Symptoms extend upward. Right upper, left lower. Alternate coldness and heat.

Chest - Pain in left side, sore to touch.

Sleep - Night terrors.

Modalities - Better closing eyes. Worse by touch, motion. Worse moving head, beginning to move after sitting. Worse walking (inclines to left), misstep. Worse swallowing. Worse morning on waking, light. Worse bright sunshine (eyes).

Temperature - Alternation of coldness and heat. Scarlet fever, eruption in spots, large and vivid. Vertigo - Vertigo with a terrible headache and complete cessation of the mental faculties. The vertigo is worse on moving the head. Sensation as if the bed was being rapidly turned in a circle. Inclines to left on walking. COMMENTS - The provings and symptoms of poisoning cases are unusually distinctive. Tendency to blackness of the skin. Painful swelling, it enlarges, becomes shiny, hard and deep red and in several places, quite black. Marked dilatation of the pupils (Bell.). Dryness of mouth and throat. Spasms, convulsions and tetanic rigidity of the whole body. “In the midst of these convulsions the children frequently stretch out their little hands, then carry them eagerly to their mouths and go through the motions of chewing and swallowing.” A patient of Cooper’s, after one dose of the tincture, patches of psoriasis on the knees, elbows and forehead, scaly with red irritating spots at roots of hair disappeared. The day after taking a single dose of tincture, another patient of Cooper’s had, “Head feels full across forehead, eyes heavy and forehead burns, could not apply himself to work.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bell. (2) Sol- m. - pain in left hip joint. (3) Sol-t. - cramps in calves and contraction of fingers, spitting through closed teeth. (4) Sol-v. recommended in facial paralysis. (5) Sol-a. - threatening paralysis of the lungs in the course of bronchitis in the aged and children must cough a long time before able to raise expectoration. (6) Sol-ps. - acute pains in lower abdomen, Sol-t. (7) Aegrotans - diseased potato. (8) Sol-t. Potato berries - cramps in the calves of the legs and fingers. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

PHARMACY - sol-o. Solanum oleraceum. Juquerioba. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Breast-milk, profuse. Breasts, swelling. Catarrh. Glands, swelling. Herpes Leucorrhea. Pustules. Sleep excessive. Styes. Urticaria.

HOMEOPATHIC - Mure reported that this plant is herbaceous, stem somewhat woody, the upper branches being covered with short and crooked thorns. It grows on the shores around Rio Janeiro in damp and shady places. The most remarkable symptom of the proving was “swelling of the breasts with profuse effusion of milk” occurring in a woman of 60. “Pain and swelling of face and throat with inflammation.” “Cold feeling in left chest after drinking.” Drowsiness with headache. The generally deranged sleep of the other Solanaceae. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Solanum Tuberosum
author: Murphy
constitution: Amaurosis. Colic. Cramps. Diarrhea. Faintness. Headache. Iritis, rheumatic. Stammering. Trismus. Tumors. Vomiting.
keynote:
PHARMACY - sol-t. Solanum tuberosum. Potato. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of the berries. Tincture of green potatoes. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Colic. Cramps. Diarrhea. Faintness. Headache. Iritis, rheumatic.…
full:
PHARMACY - sol-t. Solanum tuberosum. Potato. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of the berries. Tincture of green potatoes. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Colic. Cramps. Diarrhea. Faintness. Headache. Iritis, rheumatic. Stammering. Trismus. Tumors. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - The poisonous properties of the berries and leaves of the potato plant are well known, and the tubers are popularly believed to have anti-scorbutic properties when eaten as food. Under some conditions the tubers have been known to contain poisonous quantities of Solanin. The symptoms are the result of eating new potatoes, green potatoes, an extract and the berries. The last proved fatal in a number of instances. Sickness and diarrhea with tenesmus, giddiness, dilated pupils and indistinct vision. Tossing to and fro in bed. A paralytic condition of the tongue, cramps and tetanic spasms. General rigidity. Patient is exceedingly weak. Faintness. MIND - Almost lost consciousness.

Eyes - Eyes deep in sockets. Pupils dilated. Staring look. Vision indistinct.

Face - Hippocratic face. Anxious expression.

Mouth - Constantly spitting through the closed teeth, viscid, frothy phlegm. Tongue covered with brown, moist fur. Tongue is heavy and difficult to move, hardly able to articulate. Speech thick. Speechless.

Stomach - Epigastric region sensitive to pressure. Felt sick, a darkness over her eyes, skin cold, cramped all over. Violent retching followed by vomiting and diarrhea.

Abdomen - Violent colic and vomiting. Pain in bowels. Tumors.

Rectum - Diarrhea with tenesmus. Tends to relax bowels.

Female - Tumors around cervix, uterus.

Limbs - Cramps, especially in calves with spasmodic contractions of fingers and thumbs. Lungs - Difficult breathing. Respiration is hurried, irregular, at times suppressed, usually short and incomplete, only seldom slow and sighing.

Skin - Skin livid.

Pulse - Pulse small, rapid, scarcely perceptible.

Temperature - Skin cold. Face, chest and limbs cold. Skin beaded with cold, clammy sweat. Vertigo - Vertigo, headache, stupor. COMMENTS - Cooper relieved with a single dose of Sol-t. tincture a case of rheumatic iritis. Burnett cured a case of tumors feeling like masses of potatoes in the abdomen with Sol-t. It also assisted him in the cure of a case of tumors all around the cervix uterus. Urt-u. finished this cure. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Solin. (2) In paralysis of tongue, Caust., Dulc. (3) Iritis, Bell. (4) Stammering speech, Merc., Stram. REFERENCES Clarke.

name: Solanum Tuberosum Aegrotans
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Worse by touch, pressure, walking. Worse from smell of alcohol. Worse at 5 p.m., sleeping. Headache is worse on waking, from working..
constitution: Anal, prolapse. Breasts, painful. Constipation. Nosebleed. Headache. Ileus. Menses interrupted. Noma. Pruritus vulva. Rectal, prolapse. Scalp, painful. Sciatica. Scurvy. Tenesmus. Tongue cracked. Vertebra, pain, pulsation.
keynote:
PHARMACY - sol-t-ae. Solanum tuberosum aegrotans. Rotten potato. Diseased potato due to several fungi. Tincture of the affected tubers. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anal, prolapse. Breasts, painful. Constipation. Nosebleed. Headache. Ileus. Menses interrupted.…
full:
PHARMACY - sol-t-ae. Solanum tuberosum aegrotans. Rotten potato. Diseased potato due to several fungi. Tincture of the affected tubers. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anal, prolapse. Breasts, painful. Constipation. Nosebleed. Headache. Ileus. Menses interrupted. Noma. Pruritus vulva. Rectal, prolapse. Scalp, painful. Sciatica. Scurvy. Tenesmus. Tongue cracked. Vertebra, pain, pulsation.

HOMEOPATHIC - According to the Treasury of Botany, the “potato murrain” is characterized by “the rapid putrescence of the leaves and haulm, which is first indicated by the presence of a little mold, Peronospora infestans, which preys upon the tissues, spreading rapidly in every direction. The tubers also exhibit brown spots on their surface and within their tissues and according to circumstances decay with greater or less rapidity.” In 1846, the sudden inroad of this disease led to the famine in Ireland, resulting in the death of thousands. Mure made the first proving of Sol-t-ae., using a potato “in an entire state of decomposition without, however, being completely rotten.” Effects of eating diseased potatoes, some of them fatal, have been observed and these have been added to Mure’s. Dark skin. Breath and odor of body are offensive. Excruciating muscular pains. Cold water causes shock. The urine has an oily pellicle. Prolapse of the rectum and anus. Tumors of rectum look like decayed potato. Dreams of pools of blood. Irritability. MIND - Quarrelsome, irritable mood. Bad temper. Dread of work. Hypochondriac mood. Fancies she is miserable, and dwells much on the future. Wants to enjoy achange of scenery. Crowd of ideas. Attention is easily disturbed by other things. Confusion of mind.

Head - Heat in head, evening. Heaviness of head. Catarrhal dullness. Lancinations, as if brain would burst open. Headache at noon, worse by the smell of spirits. Sensation of water splashing in head. Painful sensitiveness of scalp and roots of hair, cannot bear combing.

Eyes - Congestion of the conjunctiva. Prickling and burning in eyes. Profuse lachrymation, on waking. Burning in lids. Prickling about the lids, the surface of which is red. Spasmodic contraction and twitching of left upper lid.

Ears - Ringing in the left ear.

Nose - Repeated sneezing, followed by feeble cough. Pressure at root of nose. Nosebleeds. Smell of blood.

Face - Face pale, bloodless. Swollen, especially about eyelids, nearly closing them. Face hot and red. Red pimples on cheeks. Desquamation of face. Bluish-black, fetid ulcer of left cheek. Upper lip is bleeding, cracked.

Mouth - Dry mouth. Breath horribly fetid. Tongue pale, coated white or yellowish white. Tongue yellowish along the median line. Tongue swollen, cracked, early in the morning. Prickling in right half of tongue.

Throat - Feeling as of a fleshy growth in throat. Feeling as if something sticking in throat. Mucus accumulates in throat. Fauces and mouth inflamed, ulcerated in patches. Inflamed fauces, unable to swallow saliva. COMMENTS - The symptoms of the Sol-tae. proving were severe, and one of the most important, prolapse of the rectum, has been confirmed by the poisoning cases. A man and three children ate boiled diseased potatoes and among their symptoms were “Pain of an acute character was referred to the region of the anus, which on examination was found perfectly patulous and exquisitely tender to the touch. Two of the four patients had prolapsed anus, which was probably caused by the violent and ineffectual efforts to discharge the contents of the rectum. There had not been an evacuation of the bowels, nor had they passed water, except in drops and with extreme suffering, for six days. On introducing the finger into the rectum, which caused acute pain, it was found that the intestine was completely filled to within an inch of the orifice with a solid substance.” The foul odor of the diseased potato is reproduced in the breath and body odor of the patients. Lips cracked and raw, gums bleeding tongue coated, thick, cracked, throat inflamed and ulcerated with sensation of something sticking in it or a fleshy growth. In one poisoning case a condition of noma of left cheek was induced. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bry., Ars., Plb., Nux-v., Sep., Stron., Viol-t., Squil., Puls., Graph., Alum., Merc., Nat-m., Ign., Calc. (2) Sensation of machinery inside, Nit-ac. (3) Constipation, black balls, Op. (4) Prolapsus anus, Podo., Ruta. (5) Patulous anus, Apis., Phos. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Stomach - Pain in stomach, with red face, after breakfast. Spasmodic pains, griping- tearing at night. Acidity, bitterness, and gulping-up, after eating. Belchings followed by rumbling in stomach. Sour belchings causing a cough.

Abdomen - Painfulness of abdomen to contact along the median line. Belly hard, swollen, dropsical. Pain after eating, spasmodic pains, as though the bowels became twisted together, rumbling. Pain, as if sprained, in right groin. Stitch in right groin near inguinal ring. Flatulence.

Rectum - Alternate protrusion and retraction of rectum during stool. Contraction of anal sphincter. Prolapsed rectum and anus. Acute pain in anus. Great heat in anus. Frequent urging to stool. Has to strain until tears come. Hard, large, lumpy stool, with violent burning in anus and rectum. Constipation. Copious greenish-yellow diarrhea. Violent colic previous to stool. Sensations - Of water splashing on head, as if brain were leaping in skull (on stooping). As of something sticking in throat. As if there were a fleshy growth in throat. As if a spring unrolled in left hypochondrium. As if a hollow body were turning rapidly in chest. Of stoppage in trachea. Of something becoming detached from sacrum.

Male - Weight in right testicle all day.

Female - Suppression of the menses. Menstrual blood rose-colored. Menses smelling of foul fish. Small pimples and intolerable itching of labia. Burning and itching in vagina. Flatulence presses on uterus. Spasmodic pains in uterus. Twisting pains through uterus. Feeling of dislocation in hip joint with pain in womb after a slight exertion. Food - Canine hunger. Salt taste. Taste of raw potatoes. Food tastes as bitter as gall. Great desire for spirits and oranges. Burning thirst.

Chest - Oppression in chest. Congestions to chest. Tearing in chest. Prickling as from a thousand pins on the inner surface of sternum. Violent stitching pain above right breast. Acute pain in the sides like a stitch.

Heart - Weight and pain in heart region. Lancinations in heart. Palpitations of heart. Pulse is irregular, sometimes weak, hard and tense.

Back - Violent beating in spine, early, when lying. Prickling sensation in spine. Stinging pain. Sensation of weariness in whole back. Stiffness in muscles of back. Tingling in sacrum. Prickling in psoas muscles. Pain in lumbar vertebra, impeding walking. Swelling of muscles of neck. Breasts - Breasts are painful, especially when raising arm.

Limbs - Sense of weariness in all the limbs. Inclination to stretch. Joints swollen and very painful. Acute pains in hip joint caused by least motion. Feeling of dislocation of hip joint. Legs edematous. Shuddering in right leg. Heat in hands. Lungs - Constriction and difficulty breathing. Constant involuntary sighing. In trachea, tearing, prickling with cough. Cough with expectoration of yellow mucus, at night. Dry cough, day and night. Expectoration of lumps of black blood, early in the morning. After eating choking and difficult breathing caused by dryness of mouth. Hoarseness on walking.

Sleep - Irresistible drowsiness. Sleepless. Restless sleep. Starting from sleep, as in a fright. Amorous dreams. Dreams about men who become transformed to talking animals. Confused dreams, about fires, revolution, corpses, thieves.

Skin - Skin is tender. Rose-colored patches appear and as suddenly vanish. Small red pimples cause violent itching.

Modalities - Worse by touch, pressure, walking. Worse from smell of alcohol. Worse at 5 p.m., sleeping. Headache is worse on waking, from working.

Teeth - Teeth covered with white mucus. Swelling of mucus membrane of the inner margin of the two incisors. Teeth loose and very painful. Gums, especially lower, spongy, oozing blood.

Kidneys - Region of bladder distended. Difficult urination. Urine reddish, mingled with mucus. Urine is very thick, soapy, turbid, of a dingy yellow with copious white sediment. Constant urination while at stool. Heat and pain in urethra after urinating.

Temperature - Chilliness and sensation of internal coldness. Alternate burning heat and chilliness, at night. Sweat all over, early is morning, in bed, cold nightsweat. The sweat makes the bed smell of potatoes. Heat all over with sweat. Fever, afterwards dropsical appearance. Violent paroxysms of heat.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Asthma. Boils. Bronchitis. Buboes. Cough. Cystitis. Dropsy. Dysuria. Hemorrhoids. Hoarseness. Kidney, disorders. Kidney, stones. Lung, disorders. Ophthalmia. Pneumonia. Smallpox. Teeth, decay. Urinary, stricture. Vomiting.

HERBAL - Ayurvedic physicians prized Sol-x. as an excellent remedy for cough, respiratory troubles, cough associated with hoarseness, ophthalmia, stone or calculus, stricture, and retention or suppression of urine. Sol-x. is an aperient, carminative, expectorant, and diuretic. It is given in asthma, cough, catarrhal affections of the lungs, fever, flatulent and pain in the chest. As a diuretic, the decoction is given in dysuria, cystitis, calculi and dropsy, also given in costiveness. A paste of the seeds is locally applied to promote suppuration of boils, buboes, and other indolent chronic abscesses. Fumigation of the fruit is largely used by natives as sialogogue and applied for the relief of pain in carious teeth. Charaka recommended Sol-x. in hemorrhoids, cough, delirium tremens, urinary difficulties, stone and calculus. Shushruta found it efficacious in ophthalmia, respiratory troubles, cough, urinary difficulties and troubles and stricture. Chakradatta said that Sol-x. is useful in cough, stricture, and urinary troubles. Bangasena has recommended it in the cough of children. Sol-x. is used by them separately or as a principal ingredient in their compound medicines for the above mentioned complaints.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hoarseness (Caust., Phos., Sei.), associated with cough. Bronchitis, pneumonia, or bronco- pneumonia associated with voice loss. Asthma. Fevers associated with thirst, vomiting, aversion to food, burning sensation felt over the body and pains felt over the collective body of the ribs. Stricture, suppression or retention of urine and kidney stone. Preventive against smallpox. The Ayurvedic physicians also used it against smallpox, dose being 1/8 tola of its root (white variety) to be given in the morning in empty stomach. RELATIONS - Compare: In the cure of kidney maladies it can be compared with Berb., Canth., Sars. and Lyc. REFERENCES - Ghose.
