full:
PHARMACY - sulo-ac. Sulphurosum acidum. Sulphur dioxide. Sulphurous acid. Sulphurous anhydride. The remedy is obtained by dissolving sulphur dioxide in water. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne rosacea. Allergies. Colds. Constipation. Croup. Diphtheria. Eczema. Epidemics. Favus. Hands, chapped. Heartburn. Infections. Influenza. Nipples, sore. Pityriasis versicolor. Stomatitis, ulcerative. Tuberculosis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sulo-ac. is soluble in water, it produces an acid solution containing sulphurous acid. In this way, relatively weak solutions are obtained. Gutman carried out a clinical study, and taking as a base the results obtained, he drew up aclinical symptomatology in 1968. Julian completed Gutman’s description with reference to the symptom data which resulted from acute and chronic poisoning cases. Sulo-ac. irritates any mucus membrane with which it comes into contact and by becoming oxidized, it is transformed into sulphurous acid and then into sulfuric acid. Acting on the upper respiratory tract, it is known even to create retro-sternal constriction and phenomena such as anoxia ischemia and myocarditis. Predisposition to pulmonary tuberculosis. Chronic, purulent hyper secretion of bronchial mucus in the young without dilatation of the bronchi. Need for fresh air, vertigo. Irritation of the nose, pharynx and larynx. Dyspnea, wheezing, coughing and retrosternal constriction. Pulmonary tumors. Cold in the head, influenza. Asthma, bronchitis, croup. Chronic tuberculosis. Clergyman’s sore throat. Dyspepsia with ptyalism and gastric acidity. Keratitis and conjunctivitis. Chilblains, chapped hands. Diphtheria. Scarlatina malign. Typhoid fever. Sensitivity to infections.

Eyes - Irritation of both conjunctivae and cornea. Tension of the artery of the retina. Change in the reaction of the pupil. Conjunctivitis. Superficial epidemic spotted keratitis. Herpes of the cornea. Chronic glaucoma. Choroiditis. Dacryocystitis. Blepharitis. Edema of the eyelids.

Nose - Burning sensation in the nose and discharge of a viscous liquid. Mucopurulent rhinitis. Nasal polyps.

Mouth - Brownish stains on the teeth, especially on the incisors. Dental caries. Ptyalism, gingivitis. Ptyalism in pregnant women.

Throat - Burning sensation in the throat. Feeling of tightness around the throat. Lingering huskiness of voice. Scratching in the throat and chest. COMMENTS - Some forty years ago, when the germ theory of disease in its present form was in its infancy, Dewar of Fite, conceived the idea that sulphurous acid was an innocent and at the same time universal germ destroyer and consequently universal remedy. His views met with cordial acceptance and inhalationsofsulphurous acid given off from burning sulphur became the fashion. Dewar’s method was simple. A few red cinders were put in a kitchen shovel, this was placed in the center of a room and flowers of sulphur sprinkled thereon. In a very short time every person in the room was sneezing violently, coughing and wheezing and running at the eyes and nose. Dewar also used the ordinary solution and a spray. Wounds, sore nipples, bruises were also amenable to its local use. For erysipelas, a local application of equal parts of the acid and glycerine. Sulo-ac. doubtless shares the anti-septic properties of Sulph. The symptoms' are from observations of the effects on workmen in mines from air contaminated with Sulo-ac. Milne summed up its virtues, “Anti-septic, disinfectant, a powerful deoxidizer and destroyer of vegetable life.” As a gargle it is used in the strength of one to six. In parasitic skin disorders the B. P. solution is used and is effective. Ringer said that ten to fifteen minims taken ten minutes before each meal will remedy heartburn in most instances. It prevents flatulence and fermentations and that “the solution, either strong or diluted in varying proportions, speedily removes thrush.” In potencies, it has cured ulcerative inflammation of the mouth. Headache, better by vomiting. C. Wootton tasted the acid with this result it at once stopped the mucus secretion of the bowels. The constipation was so severe that he was in misery for nine months, until he took Hydr., which cured. The use of Sulo- ac. as a hair-wash at a later time produced the same result. RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Hydr. (constipation). Compare: (1) Sulph. in ulcerated sore mouth, Nat-m., Caps., Sul-ac. (2) The effects on the back recorded by Hahnemann as from the fumes of burning Sulph. were antidoted by electricity. (3) Brom. - Persistent, excoriating cold in the head, huskiness worse in the evening. dry cough and attacks of suffocation. (4) Kali-i. - Streaming, burning, excoriating, cold in the head, with violent cough and soapy, salty, greenish expectoration. (5) Tub. - Emaciation, varying pains, chronic swelling of the tonsils, palpitations, perspiration, very sensitive to the cold, coughing hoarseness. REFERENCES - Clarke. Julian.

Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Dyspepsia and hyperchlorhydria.

Chest - Angina pectoris. Constriction behind the sternum.

Heart - Rapid pulse, cold sweating. Accentuation of the second pulmonary sound. Systolic pulsation in the pit of the stomach. Inflammation of the coronary arteries.

Limbs - Chilliness at the limbs. Lungs - Feeling of suffocation and cyanosed face. Wheezing and rhonchi widespread in the chest. Bronchiectasis. Emphysema, asthma. Chronic pulmonary tuberculosis. Chronic bronchitis. Oppression, sneezing and spasmodic coughing. Expectoration of dirty-gray or bloodstained mucous.

Skin - Eruption of vesicles and edema. Brownish coloring of the skin. Eczematic eruption, very sensitive. Leucoderma. Urticaria.

Temperature - Septic fevers of all kinds. Epidemic influenza. Typhoid fever. Tuberculosis. Smallpox. Plague.

PHARMACY - sumb. Sumbulus moschatus. Musk root. Sumbul. Ferula sumbul. N. O. Umbelliferae. Tincture of the powdered root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Ascarides. Asthma. Breasts, pains. Chorea. Diarrhea. Epilepsy. Fainting. Heart, disorders. Pneumonia. Hysteria. Insomnia. Neuralgias. Numbness. Palpitations. Spermatorrhea. Throat, catarrh. Throat, spasms. Typhoid fever. Worms.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sumbul, as its name, “Musk-root,” implies, has an odor resembling that of musk. The resemblance is so close that Sumbul is used to adulterate musk. Sumb. was proved by Lembke, Cattell and others. The symptoms are as like to those of Mosch, as the physical resemblance would imply. Hysterical and nervous disorders. Easy fainting, nervous palpitations. Nervous, irritable and sleepless. Anomalous, functional, cardiac disorders. Sclerosed arteries. Menopausal flushings. Asthma. Yellow tenacious discharges. The left side was more affected than the right. Neuralgia. Chorea, constant jerking of the head and limbs with protrusion of the tongue. Numbness on becoming cold, on left side. Insomnia of delirium tremens (fifteen drops of tincture). Sensation as if water dropped down spine. As of a hot water flowing through part. Early senility. MIND - Emotional and fidgety. Mistakes in writing and adding. Weeps and laughs by turns. Fear of becoming insane. Faintness from hearing music.

Head - Dull in morning, clear in evening.

Nose - Comedones. Tenacious yellow mucus from nose. Sensations - Tongue as if scraped. Clogged sensation in left chest. As if heart beating in water. Like a string pulling in right breast. Corkscrew pains in (left) uterus and appendages.

Face - Neuralgia. As of a hair or cobweb on face. Idiotic expression.

Mouth - Tongue feels rough as if scraped.

Throat - Choking constriction, with con- stant swallowing. Hysterical. Spasm of pharyngeal muscles. Tenacious mucus in throat. COMMENTS - Hale gave indications for Sumb. including nasal and pharyngeal catarrh with nervousness, sleeplessness and tendency to spasms (especially in children), discharge of tenacious, yellow mucus. Catarrhal, spasmodic or cardiac asthma. Ascarides with bloated, drum-like abdomen and constipation, picking nose cured with Sumb. 15c. Oily pellicle in urine. Pain in left uterine region. Menopausal flushings. Neuralgia, facial or ovarian in women of quick and lively nervous constitutions. Neuralgia of the left hypochondrium, simulating angina pectoris with palpitation in nervous women. Insomnia of chronic alcoholism. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Asaf., Mosch. (2) Mosch., Asaf., Melit., Med., Mez. (3) Oily pellicle on urine, Sulph., Puls., Petr. (4) Tenacious, yellow mucus, Hydr. (5) Infra-breast pain, Cimic., Puls., Lil-t. (6) Worse thinking of symptoms, Ox-ac., Pip-m. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Burning water brash. Belching of gas from stomach.

Abdomen - Abdomen full, distended and painful.

Female - Ovarian neuralgia. Screwing pain in left side of uterus. Sexual excitability. Menopausal flushes.

Heart - Nervous palpitations in hysterical subjects or at menopause, worse least exertion and thinking of it. As if heart beating in water. Neuralgia around left breast simulating angina pectoris. High blood pressure due to arteriosclerosis. Cardiac asthma. Aching in left arm, heavy, numb and weary. Pulse irregular.

Back - Trickling along spine. Breasts - Pulling like a string in right breast. Neuralgia around left breast and left hypochondriac region.

Limbs - Left arm aching, heavy, numb, weary. Lungs - Asthma, cardiac, hysterical. Oppressed tightness in left chest, as if clogged. Loses breath on any exertion.

Sleep - Dreams of falling, of sex, followed by profuse, sudden emission.

Skin - Pale, cold. Internal itching.

Modalities - Better from gentle motion, warmth. Worse from cold, inspiration. Worse menopausal. Worse motion, active exercise. Worse left side, after sitting. Worse thinking of symptoms. Worse in morning. Music causes faintness.

Kidneys - Oily pellicle on surface of urine.

The “dark night of the soul.” Depressive disorders (Must-b.), especially when suicide is threatened with deep-seated despair Morbid preoccupation with death. Void of emotional life. Despair and despondent. Sense of meaninglessness of life may lead to carelessness of attitude. Lack of aspirations and meaningful purpose. REFERENCES - Bach.

full:
PHARMACY - swer-ch. Swertia chirata. N. O. Gentianaceae. Tincture from the flowers and leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acidity. Bilious. Boils. Cough. Dropsy. Dyspepsia. Fevers. Flatulence. Indigestion. Intermittent fever. Leprosy. Malaria. Typhoid fever. Worms.

HERBAL - Charaka recommended Swertia in hematemesis and dropsy. Habita found it efficacious in vomiting of pregnancy. Ayurvedic physicians extolled its therapeutic virtues in typhoid and intermittent fevers, malarial fever, respiratory troubles, bilious troubles, impurities of blood, burning, cough, dropsy, thirst, leprosy, boils and worms. Swertia is a well-known and well-tried febrifuge among these practitioners and they very often use it in all sorts of fevers. It has been in constant demand among the Kavirajas of India. Like cinchona and other bitter tonics, it is bitter, stomachiec, laxative, anthelmintic and febrifuge. It excites the appetite, strengthens digestion, but does not constipate. It diminishes flatulence and hyperacidity. Removes biliousness in atonic dyspepsia, liver troubles. Removes acidity of the stomach and flatulence, gout, intermittent and other fevers.

HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Kali Kumar Bhat- tacharjea, of Gouripore, Assam, made a short proving of Swer-ch. An account of the proving and the symptoms developed therein were published in the Hahnemann of Falgoon. Dr. Bhattacharjea prepared a tincture from the flowers and leaves of the plant. MIND - Dullness of mind, laziness, desire to lie down always.

Head - Dull pain over both the temples, gradually extending to the whole of the head. Coldness is felt over the head.

Eyes - Severe burning sensation in the eyes. Food - Desire for bitter substances and meat.

Ears - Hissing sound in the ears.

Nose - Flushes of heat come out of the nostrils.

Mouth - Bad taste in the morning, offensive odor.

Throat - In the morning and evening, pain is felt in the throat, not relieved by hot drinks.

Abdomen - Accumulation of wind in the abdomen.

Male - Weakness of the male sexual organ, slight discharge of semen.

Limbs - Aching pains in the hands and feet. Weakness of the legs, difficulty in walking.

Tongue - The middle of the tongue is enveloped with a thick yellowish coating. Heaviness of the tongue. Difficult speech. COMMENTS - A noted febrifuge. Acute and chronic malarial fevers. Chronic fevers. Liver troubles after fever has stopped. Debility after fevers. Long-lasting malarial fever, turns into Kala-azar associated with enlarged spleen and liver. The fever may come on at any time of the day and night; in chronic cases the fever appears usually in the afternoon. In the morning attacks, cold stage lasts for a long time, there is no appreciable thirst in this stage and if there be any, it is generally relieved by hot drinks. Before the appearance of hot stage, nausea and bilious vomiting trouble the patient. The hot stage lasts for 3 to 4 hours and there is slight thirst. Severe burning sensation in the eyes, continues as long as the fever is present. Indigestion, atonic dyspepsia. Flatulence. Loss of appetite. Troubles arising out of worms. Catarrhs, leprosy and some skin diseases. RELATIONS - Compare: Chin., Ars. REFERENCES - Ghose.

Liver - Enlargement of both liver and spleen associated with pain. Lungs - Hurried respiration during fever. Dry mucus, dry hacking cough. Dry cough in the bronchial region.

Kidneys - Dull pain in the kidney, especially on the right side. Urine is of high redcolor. Burning while urinating.

Temperature - Stage of coldness lasts long, but there is no desire for drinking. Cold with nausea, bilious vomiting. Desire for hot water. Hot stage generally lasts for three hours, and afterwards sweating stage appears. Sweat only on chest, axilla and thighs. Slight thirst with heat. No fixity of the appearance of fever. Burning sensation in the eyes during fever.

PHARMACY - syc-co. Sycotic co. bacillus. Sycotic bacillus. Bowel nosode. Bacillus streptococcus faecalis. Sycotic co. from non-lactose fermenting cocci ofintestinal tract. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Allergies, food. Alopecia. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Arthritis. Asthma. Backaches. Bedwetting. Conjunctivitis. Cough. Cystitis. Deafness. Dysmenorrhea. Enteroptosis. Fibrositis. Food, poisoning. Gastroenteritis. Headaches. Indigestion. Leucorrhea. Lumbosacral pain. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Neuritis. Otorrhea. Photophobia. Polyps. Rheumatism. Sebaceous, cysts. Vaginitis. Warts.

HOMEOPATHIC - Characteristic irritation, particularly in relation to the mucus membranes. Catarrhal states of the respiratory tract, the bladder and the vagina. Asthma, sinusitis. Cough about 2 a.m., worse from change of atmosphere. Irritation of synovial linings in rheumatism. Enlarged lymphoid tissue of tonsils and adenoids, glands. Meningeal irritation. Convulsions. Cold and sensitive to dampness. Warty growths. Ailments from vaccinations. Vulvo-vaginitis, leucorrhea. Gastroenteritis. Bedwetting, cystitis. Albuminuria. Stools are excoriating, loose and offensive with urgent call to stool on rising. MIND - Nervous and tense. Ailments from anticipation. Bites the fingernails. Nervous irritability. Cross, irritable and restless. Quick tempered, outbursts of temper from resentment. Oversensitive. Shy, sensitive and fussy. Exhausted. Timidity. Weepy and depressed. Fears of dark, of being left alone, of animals and dogs.

Head - Irritation of meninges, sub-acute or chronic. Headache from infection of sinuses. Aching pain deep in brain. Headache on left side. Frontal congestive headache which lasts for many days. Sick headache, worse at menstrual period. Throbbing, better heat and rest, worse noise. Sweating of head at night. Painful dry scaly spots. Premature gray hair. Alopecia. Baldness.

Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Vitreous opacities. Pain in eyeballs. Photophobia, hemiopia. Blinking. Tarsal cysts. Cystic tumors on eyelids. Swelling of upper eyelids.

Ears - Otorrhea. Excessive formation of wax. Deafness. Itching of meatus. Cracks under ears.

Nose - Nasal, post nasal catarrh. Catarrh extending to frontal sinuses. Turbinates congested, sinus infection. Vasomotor rhinorrhea. Hay fever. Coryza after eating eggs. Polyps. Nose dry, crusting and burning. Cracks at corners of nostrils. Nosebleed. Sense of smell lost.

Face - Puffy in morning, especially under eyes. Acne rosacea. Eruptions, herpes about mouth. Erythema. Vesicular eruption on cheeks. Malignant growth on right cheek. Hair on face and upper lip. Facial neuralgia. Twitching facial muscles.

Mouth - Salivation increased. Bad taste, sense of taste lost. Pins and needle sensation on tongue. Pain like a splinter in tongue. Tongue sore, scalded, dry, fissured, furred. Tongue dry, sticks to roof of mouth. Warts on tongue. Deep ulcers on tongue. Ulcers in mouth. Lips dry and cracked. Cracks in angles of mouth. Herpes of mouth.

Throat - Fibrositis of neck and throat. Goiter. Glands enlarged. Enlargement of tonsils and adenoids. Tonsillitis, cheesy masses from tonsil. Quinsy. Throat feels raw, scorched, dry. Profuse mucus from throat in morning. Swallowing difficult, chokes easily. COMMENTS - This organism of the intestinal tract is related morphologically and clinically to the gonococcus bacteria. Hahnemann related what he called “the Sycotic Miasm” to the disease, gonorrhea, but this disease is only one form of catarrhal infection of the mucus membrane of the urinary tract. There are many non gonorrheal organisms associated with the symptom picture of “Catarrh” and according to Dr. John Paterson the miasm “Sycosis” may be considered synonymous with “Catarrh.” Gonorrhea is an infection of mucus membrane, but catarrhal manifestations (sycotic) are not at all due to gonorrheal infection. Characteristic warty growths. Exanthema of chickenpox. Chronic and recurring cystitis, often treated several times with antibiotics. Usually additional remedies are required, particularly a constitutional prescription, but intercurrent doses of Syc- co. can be of great help. Griggs noted it for human “flu,” cat “flu,” foul pest, foot and mouth disease and canine distemper are all the signs of Syc-co. Convulsions, meningitis or epileptic forms of seizures are to be found in the clinical picture and also chorea, though less frequently than in Dysentery Co. Syc-co. 200c in nosebleeds of long standing in a girl without any apparent reasons, cured completely with a few doses at long intervals. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) The related sycotic remedies are Thuj, Nit-ac., Nat-s. and Bac. (2) Vesicular type of rash related to Ant-t., Rhus-t., Bac., and Thuj. Complementary: Lyc., is often complementary to this nosode. REFERENCES - Bach. Paterson.

Stomach - Anorexia. Burning pain in stomach. Pain and distention in the epigastrium. Flatulence. Acidosis attacks. Eructation acid, bilious attacks. Nausea from the smell of cooking. Nausea or sickness after eating eggs (Ferr.). Nocturnal vomiting, must empty stomach.

Abdomen - Distended abdomen, colon. Enteroptosis. Chronic irritation of whole digestive tract. Acute or chronic gastroenteritis in the child.

Rectum - Condylomata around anus. Anal warts. Splinter pain. Distended feeling in rectum. Prolapse. Constipation or looseness. Stool pale, crumbly, bad odor. Loose, offensive stool, excoriating (Med.). Diarrhea from excitement of emotions. Diarrhea after eating, fatty food. Liquid motion after every meal. Urgent call to stool as soon as rising out of bed.

Male - Impotency. Genital warts and herpes.

Female - Amenorrhea. Pain left ovary at menstrual period. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Dysmenorrhea. Leucorrhea acrid, excoriating. Leucorrhea copious, yellow. Leucorrhea profuse, bland. Vaginal discharge, offensive, fishy. Pruritus vulvae, vulvo-vaginitis, balanitis. Tumors, ovarian cysts. Uterine polyps. Genital warts, herpes. Food - Desires butter, fat, cheese. Desires sweets, milk and salt. Averse to breakfast. Aversion to egg, fat, cheese, milk, milk pudding, cream. Aversion to salt, vinegar, sugar, tea. Aversion to bread, potato, tomato, vegetables, meat. Aggravated by egg, causing nausea, vomiting, bilious attack and hay fever. Worse from fat, eggs, onion and oranges.

Chest - Pleurisy. Pleurodynia. Fibrositis of chest wall. Sudden pain at the base of right lung. Intercostal neuralgia. Pain in left shoulder blade. Constitutions - Pale, sallow, flabby and soft with long eyelashes (Tub.), and sweat of the head.

Back - Severe backache. Pain in morning on rising. Backache from damp weather. Stiff Mover. Fibrositis, myositis. Neuritis of head and neck. Sebaceous cyst back. Lumbosacral pain. Pain in sacral-iliac joints. Hips stiff.

Neck - Fibrositis in neck, shoulders and back.

Limbs - Fibrositis, shoulders. Muscular rheumatismof arms. Arthritis fingers, pain generally better dry day and hot water. Fingers deformed, nodules on fingers. Fingertips cracked. Fingers go dead, numb, with spasm of the fingers. Prickly feeling in hands. Nails brittle. Feet and legs painful when walking as if walking on loose cobble stones. Feet and legs painful at night. Pesplanus. Rheumatism of knees. Ankles swollen and stiff. Feet swollen at night. Fidgety feet at night in bed. Soles of feet painful. Big toe joint painful. Lungs - Dyspnea in morning on waking. Asthma and bronchitis, worse with damp and frost and better at the sea side. Frequent bronchial colds. Bronchitis in winter. Tracheitis. Wheeze and coughing at 2 to 3 a.m. Irritable cough of croupy nature at night, wakes from sleep. Coughs until sick. Chronic spasmodic persisting cough. Cough with tough sputum.

Sleep - Insomnia. Restless sleep. Perspiration of head and body during sleep. Wheeze or cough. Can’t sleep until 3 a.m. Wakes 2 to 3 a.m. Night terrors. Nightmares, of dead bodies.

Skin - Sallow and oily skin. Impetigo. Warts large, flat and rugged. Herpes on face, neck and chest. Herpes groin. Váricellar eruption of limbs since immunization. Intertrigo breasts. Eczema of face in infants. Eczema on back of hands. Palmar dermatitis. Cracks on fingertips. Paronychia. Nails and toenails brittle and painful. Cracks on heals. Varicóse eczema of ankles. Chilblains on feet.

Modalities - Wofse from change of atmosphere, damp.

Kidneys - Irritation of mucus membranes from kidney to urethra. Kidney pain. Nephritis, pyelitis, nephrosis, cystitis. Frequency and urgency. Urine corrosive. Albuminuria. Urinary tantrums.

Blood - Anemia and hydremia.

Perspiration - Profuse perspiration at night during sleep.

full:
PHARMACY - sym-r. Symphoricarpus racemosus. Snowberry. N. O. Caprifliaceae. Tincture of fresh ripe berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Constipation. Hematemesis. Indigestion. Morning sickness. Nausea. Vomiting. Water brash.

HOMEOPATHIC - Prof. S. Burdick investigated the medicinal properties of many plants hitherto unused by the profession, including Symphoricarpus racemosa. Useful for persistent vomiting of pregnancy. Nausea during menstruation. Nausea, worse from any motion. Averse to all food, better when lying on the back. Gastric disturbances, fickle appetite, nausea, water brash, bitter taste. Smell and thought of food repugnant. Constipation. COMMENTS - When Burdick gave some of the Sym-r. to the first prover, a woman, she felt the marked nausea, and exclaimed, as soon as it was produced, “Doctor, this is precisely like the morning sickness I always experienced during pregnancy.” Dr. Burdick became more interested, repeated the experiment with other provers, and obtained almost uniform results, viz., a feeling varying from qualmishness to intense vomiting. It was given to female provers only and merely tested far enough to verify that symptom. Upon this clue, Dr. Burdick gave Sym-r. in the higher potencies to patients suffering from the vomiting of pregnancy with the most satisfactory results. After a trial of many years, he found it so far superior to other remedies that he relied on it altogether with rarely any but entirely satisfactory results. Burdick mentioned the drug in his course of lectures, so Moaffat bore it in mind waiting for a test case. Soon that came in the person of a young woman three months advanced in her first pregnancy. She was suffering from a deathly nausea with vomiting and retching so prolonged and violent as to produce hematemesis. The smell or thought of food was repugnant in the extreme. An examination disclosed no malposition or apparent cause for the trouble, so he procured some Sym-r. 200c from Dr. Burdick and gave her one dose in the midst of a violent paroxysm. In a few minutes she stopped vomiting and said she felt soothed and quieted all over. In half an hour the nausea began again, but a few pellets checked it promptly and she fell asleep. Once during the night she awoke distressed and took a dose, but slept again quite soon. For a month or so she felt very well until after over-exerting herself she became nauseated once more, but it was promptly checked, nor did it return during her pregnancy. The indications have been observed in cases of pregnancy with a feeling of qualmishness, with indifference to food. In more severe cases, there is a deathly nausea, the vomiting is continuous, violent retching. Sym-r. does not seem to be confined to any particular morning aggravation, a prominent symptom is the disgust at the sight, smell or thought of food. In one case, the patient was comparatively comfortable while lying on the back, but would be nauseated by the slightest motion of the arms, particularly raising them. The case was completely relieved by a few doses of Sym-r. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Phatak

full:
PHARMACY - symph. Symphytum officinale. Comfrey. Knit-bone. Healing herb. N. O. Boraginaceae. Tincture of fresh root-stock collected before flowering and in autumn. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies. Tincture, externally as a dressing for sores and ulcers and itching of anus.

CLINICAL - Abscess. Amputation. Backache. Bone, cancer. Bone, fractures. Bone, injuries. Breasts, sore. Eyes, injuries. Fractures. Gingivitis. Glands, enlarged. Gunshot wounds. Hernia. Menses, suppressed. Osteoporosis. Periosteum, painful. Periostitis. Psoas, abscess. Sexual excess. Sprains. Stump, pain. Tennis elbow. Wounds.

HERBAL - Symphytum is also called consolida, and the word comfrey is derived from confirnare. The common name, knit-bone or bone-set, gives the indication for this remedy. The root contains a crystalline solid that stimulates the growth of bone cells and epithelium on ulcerated surfaces. The glutinous juice of the root seems, according to Gerarde, to have given the key to its action as a vulnerary. Symphytum may be considered the orthopedic specific of herbal medicine.

HOMEOPATHIC - Symph. is abone remedy. It may be administered internally in the treatment of gastric and duodenal ulcers, and in stomach pain, and externally for anal itching. External application disposes the swelling, due to injury or other growths. Wounds penetrating to perineum and bones. Injuries to bones, cartilages, ligaments, joints, tendons and the periosteum, with excessive pain. Pricking pain and soreness of periosteum. Pricking, sticking, jagging pains. Fractures, broken bones. Painful bone at point of fracture. Pricking, stitching pains, remaining after wound is healed, worse touch. Non-union of fractures. Painful, irritable stump after amputation. Painful old injuries. Bruises, sprains and inflammation of bones, diseased spinous processes. Deficient callus. Acts on joints generally. Neuralgia or arthralgia of the knee. Sore breasts. Psoas abscess. Sarcoma.

Head - Headache in occiput, in top of head, in forehead, changing places. Pain comes down bone of nose. Inflammation of inferior maxillary bone, hard, red, swelling. Skull fracture or head injury (Hyper., Nat-s.).

Eyes - Injuries to the eyes from blunt instruments, blows, knocks, to the eyeball, eye socket, or sclera. Black eyes (Arn., Led.). Bleeding inside the eye after injury. Retinal bleeding. Traumatic conjunctivitis. Long-lasting pain or soreness in the eye after injury. Eyelids spasmodically closed.

Ears - Cannot hear well, feels as if ears were stopped up. Inflamed ears.

Nose - Pain comes down bone of nose and sometimes down both sides of nose.

Face - Facial injuries. Inflammation of inferior maxillary bone, hard, red swelling. Cancer, tumor of antrum. Cancer of jaw bone.

Stomach - Ulcers of the stomach.

Abdomen - Pain about navel, worse sitting. Pains across epigastrium from one side to the other, when sitting. Griping pain.

Rectum - Dysentery. Inflamed and bleeding hemorrhoids. Sensations - As if upper lid passed over an elevation on closing eye. As if ears were stopped up.

Male - Testicles become painful and tender, prevent walking. Backache from excessive sexual indulgence, with spermatorrhea.

Female - Menses stopped. Leucorrhea.

Back - Backaches from excessive sexual indulgence, or from violent motion. Low back pain from injury, overexertion, or excess sexual activity. Spinal injury. Pain in back from a fall. Pott’s disease from a fall. Decay of vertebrae. Caries of spinal and other bones. Breasts - Sore breasts. Causations - Broken bones. Injures to eye, bone, periosteum. Falls. Blows from blunt instruments. Sexual excess.

Limbs - Bone fractures. Comminuted fracture. Non-union of bones. Accelerates the formation of callus. Reduces healing. Prickling, stitching pains. Bruises. Injuries from blunt instruments. Pain in area of bony protuberances, elbow, epicondyles, ankles. Injury to periosteum. Injury to hard tissue, shins. Bone inflammation, periostitis with pain and soreness. Osteoporosis. Brittle bones. Knee arthralgia. Tennis elbow. Psoas abscess. Bone cancers. Pain at the site of old wounds or fractures, past injury to cartilage or bone. Post-surgical pain at the site of amputation or bone puncture.

Skin - Cold.

Modalities - Better gentle motion, warmth. Worse frominjuries. Worse sexual excess. Worse touch, motion, pressure. Stooping causes weight in forehead. Sitting causes pain about navel. Walking causes pain opposite spleen.

Teeth - Periodontal disease. Toothache after injury. Jaw swollen and painful after dental work. Pain worse after tooth extraction. COMMENTS - Grimmer noted that, though the proving was meager, there was a rich clinical history. According to Gerarde, “The roots of Comfrey stamped and the juice drunk with wine, help those that spit blood and heal all inward wounds and bursting. The same bruised and laid to in manner of a plaster, do heal all fresh and green wounds and are so glutinous, that it will solder and glue together meat that is chopped in pieces, seething in a pot and make it in one lump.” Gerarde added that it eases pains in the back from violent motion such as wrestling or from excessive sexual indulgence (Arn.), even when spermatorrhea has been induced thereby. Peter Squire gave, as the medicinal properties of Symph., “Astringent, mucilaginous, glutinous, useful to form cases for injured limbs. The black rind of the root is scraped off and the mucilaginous root is then scraped carefully into a nice even pulp. This spread upon cambric or old muslin in wrapped round the limb and bandaged over, it shortly stiffens and forms a casing superior to starch, giving support and strength to the part.” Squire knew a bonesetter who rendered himself famous for setting compound fractures with this root, which he kept secret. He never removed the bandage after the first dressing until the limb was well. Sir Wm. Thomson of Dublin related a case of malignant tumor of the face that had extended to the nose. Microscopic examination proved it to be round-celled sarcoma. The patient, a man, refused advice at the time, and was examined by Felix Semon, who saw the man later. After still further delay, Thomson performed the operation in the month of May, 1896. A month later the growth began to show again, increased rapidly, closed the right eye, was blue, tense, firm, lobulated, but did not break. Thomson declined to operate again. Early in October, the man walked into Thom- son’s study well. “The tumor had completely disappeared from the face and I could not identify any trace of it in the mouth.” The man had applied poultices of comfrey root and the swelling disappeared. Comfrey ' s therapeutic history is rich with clinical cures of round-cell sarcoma of the antrum and many cases of bone cancer. It seems to have special curative action on the periosteum and bony structures, facilitating the formation of callus in fractures, bringing about union, even in compound fractures, and in cases of slow or delayed union. Curative in injuries to the eyeball by blows etc. It follows Arn. in such cases, as well as in injuries to and bruising of the testicles. Backaches after strains and from sexual excesses. Pott’s disease, psoriasis and abscesses from a fall. One case of inguinal hernia has been cured with the topical application of the tincture of the root. H. C. Allen referred to the following indications for Symph. given by Lippe: when the bone or periosteum has been injured and the soft parts have recovered from the bruised soreness under Arn., the remaining pain and soreness of periosteum may be promptly relieved by Symph. Symph. was the only remedy Lippe had seen which was efficient in traumatic injuries of bone or periosteum. He cured many cases after others had used Arn. and failed. H. C. Allen gave the following cure, reported by Fowler. Mrs. J. stepped on the edge of a scantling, which rolled and she turned her ankle. In a few minutes the ankle began to swell and become painful, pain increased rapidly, so that in hour or two the patient was in great agony. She declared that her leg was broken, she “could feel the rough ends of the broken bones jagging into the flesh.” She could not bear any one to approach her for fear of be- wgbMNedsi;^ promptly relieved, so that she went about her usual duties in forty-eight hours. Allen regarded pricking pain as a guiding symptom. He noted its usefulness, next to bone injuries, for injuries to the eyeball. “I have long since ceased to use Arn. in injuries of the globe of the eye, Symph. having given such prompt and permanent relief.” Croserio was one of the first to use Symph. in the potencies for fractures. “Injuries of the bones are healed most promptly with Symph. 30c internally, once a day.” Wells gave cases of his own, including the case of a boy, 14, who broke the bone of his forearm at the junction of middle and lower thirds, two years before. He had twice repeated the fracture by slight falls. The ends were now slightly movable on each other, and the arm was of little use. Three doses of Symph. 30c made a perfect cure and the boy became robust and much better in health than he had ever been before. Wells also recorded the case of a boy, 8, with a fractured humerus near the junction of condyles and shaft. Arn. 30c immediately arrested the spasmodic jerks of muscles of the injured arm. Arn. was continued three days, by which time all traumatic fever had subsided. Symph. 3c was given, one drop in half a tumbler of water, a teaspoonful morning and evening. The splints were removed the ninth day and the bone was found to be consolidated. The cure was entirely without pain. F. H. Brett cured himself of inguinal rupture by rubbing the part with tincture of the root. On another occasion, a blow on the lower part of the back from a fall resulted in a secondary affection of the spine in the mid-dorsal region, a protuberance as if from a light dislocation appearing at the spot. Again Symph. was applied. The tenderness at the point subsided after three applications, and in a few days the protuberance disappeared. Brett mentioned a case he had heard of a diseased arm that had begun to mortify. It was dressed with a poultice of comfrey root and this “drew off the mortified substance. The arm became sound again.” Cooper noted that one patient, just before her marriage, had a dangerous attack of scarlatina, leaving abscesses on both sides of the neck and great internal swelling, so that she could swallow only liquids and those with great difficulty. The external swelling extended from ear to chin and was hard and very painful. Poultices of comfrey root were applied. The pain was immediately relieved and her abscesses decreased rapidly until they were entirely absorbed without external opening so far as the patient could remark. For bone tumors, osteomyelitis, bone ulcers. Sarcomas. Bone cancers of the jaw or bones (Hecla.). Bone cancer, even if there is no bone injury (Calc-p., Hecla.). Non-union of fractures. Broken bones that don’theal well. Acutely for osteoporosis, or osteogenesis imperfecta (Calc., or Calc-p. chronically). Stump pain after amputation of a limb (Hyper., All-c., Coff., Calen.), strong aching pains. Spinal diseases after trauma and injury. Injuries that result in a lump or tumor. For swellings, nodules and tumors in bones and limbs after an injury (Bell-p. and Con. after injury to soft tissue). Tailbone injuries (Arn., Hyper.), with an aching pains. Blows to the eyes (Led., Arn.). Corneal abrasions. Hernias (Nux-v., Calc., Lyc.). As a compress for mastitis. In tincture for stomach ulcers. RELATIONS - Antidote to: Canth. Compare: (1) Arn., Bry., Calc-p. - fractures. (2) injuries, Arn., soft parts, Symph., hard, Arn., sore, bruised lame, Symph., pricking, stitching jagging pains. (3) Calen., Fl-ac., Hep., Sil., Staph., Led., Rhus-t., Hyper. (4) Effects of sexual excess, Am. (5) Calc., Calc-f. Follows well: Am. - for pricking pains and after the bmising of the soft parts is healed. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Kidneys - Stricture of urethra.

name: Syphilinum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better inland, mountains, high altitude. Better during day, from applied heat. Better continued or slow motion. Better changing positions. Worse at night, from sundown to sunrise. Worse full moon. Worse damp, thunderstorms. Worse extreme heat or cold, winter, summer. Worse at the seashore. Worse in any position, squatting. Worse motion, raising arms laterally. Worse protruding tongue..

full:
PHARMACY - syph. Syphilinum. Syphilis nosode. Luesinum. Lueticum. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Alcoholism. Anus, fissures. Aphasia. Asthma. Baldness. Bone, disorders. Breasts, sensitive. Bubo. Cachexia. Cancer, Chancres. Constipation. Deafness. Debility. Deltoid rheumatism. Dentition. Diplopia. Dysmenorrhea. Epilepsy. Hair, loss. Headache, syphilitic. Hoarseness. Hodgkin’s disease. Insomnia. Iritis. Leucorrhea. Mouth, ulcers. Myopia. Nerve, disorders. Neuralgia. Night-sweats. Ophthalmia. Otorrhea. Ovaries, disorders. Ozaena. Pains, severe. Paralysis. Pemphigus. Prostration. Psoas, abscess. Ptosis. Rectum, stricture. Rheumatism. Sciatic pain. Sleeplessness. Spine, decay. Strabismus. Strictures. Sunstroke. Syphilis. Teeth, decay. Throat, ulcerated. Tibia, pains. Tongue, cracked. Tongue, ulcerated. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Whitlow.

HOMEOPATHIC - The syphilis nosode is mainly used on the general symptomatology with the family and personal history of the patient. Its nightly aggravation of complaints, with extreme mental and physical restlessness, together with its intense irritability, are striking indications for its use. It’s frequently used to great advantage as an intercurrent remedy in the course of treatment in chronic disease, prior to or following the apparently indicated remedy when the patient’s response to that remedy is feebly or nil. Syph. has been used in cancer, tuberculosis, severe types of neuro-arthritis, mental disturbances or various forms of paralysis. Syphilitic disorders. Especially useful when there is hereditary tendency to alcoholism or a syphilitic miasm. Affects the nerves, mucus membranes and bones. Utter prostration and debility in the morning. Great weakness with very few symptoms. Shifting rheumatic pains. Chronic eruptions and rheumatism. Persistent pains in Syphilinum any part of the body. Cold pains. Pains from darkness to daylight, decrease and increase gradually. Violent or linear pains. Knots in muscles. Pains in bones. Bones, sore, decay, curvature. Exostoses. Ulceration of mouth, nose, genitals, skin. Stubborn ulcerations. Succession of abscesses. Fetid discharges, foul or green pus. Foul odor of the body. Ichthyosis Slowly advancing hemiplegia. Glands enlarged. Hodgkin's disease. Epilepsy, worse after menses. As of hot water in blood vessels. Crying infants, who begin crying immediately after birth. Dwarfed, shriveled up, old looking babies and children, bald head, pouting lips and big belly. MIND - Loss of memory, but remembers everything previous to his disease. Difficulty in making arithmetical calculations. Apathetic. Severe insomnia and suicidal depression (Aur.), especially during extreme attacks of pain. Sad and lamenting. Antisocial, aversion to company. Cross, irritable, peevish. Does not want to be soothed. Anxiety about health. Great restlessness and paces the floor at night. Hopelessness. Despair of recovery. Fear of suffering and pains. Desperate, can’t take the pain or suffering anymore. Fear of dying. Fears the night. Fears from exhaustion. Very nervous. Fastidious. Fear of germs, of catching an infection. Always washing or wringing the hands. Causeless weeping. Laughs or weeps without cause. Nightly delirium. Senile dementia. Feels as if going insane or being paralyzed. Insanity, syphilitic insanity.

Head - Stupefying headaches. Pain in bones of head. Deep, crushing headpains across the base of temples. Linear pains from temples across, or from eyes backward, cause sleeplessness and delirium at night. Beats head against the wall. Feels pulled back. Top of head feels as if coming off. Cerebral softening. Falling of the hair. Tubercles all over the scalp.

Eyes - Ophthalmia, neonatorum. Tubercular iritis. Amaurosis, atrophy of optic nerve. Spots on cornea. Chronic, recurrent, inflammation of cornea. Successive crops ofphyctenules and abrasions of epithelial layer of cornea. Intense pain at night. Feeling of cold air blowing on eye (Fl-ac.). Photophobia and profuse lachrymation. Glimmering vision. Diplopia. Vertical diplopia. Squints. Ptosis. Lids swollen, especially upper eyelids. Eyelids glued together.

Ears - Deafness without any obvious cause, nervous with cachexia. Abscess of the middle ear. Calcareous deposit on tympanum. Decay of ossicles in ear, of syphilitic origin.

Nose - Decay of nasal bones, hard palate and septum with perforation. Ozaena offensive, thick yellow-green discharge. Attacks of fluent coryza. Snuffles. Green lumps from posterior sinuses. Sinuses, painful, from inhaled air. Saddle across the bridge of the nose (Sep.). Itching nostrils.

Face - Pale, wrinkled, old looking. Pain over eyes (right) worse protruding tongue. Paralysis of one side with difficult speech, mastication and twitching of eyes, lids. Twitching of muscles.

Mouth - Excessive flow of saliva, it runs out of mouth when sleeping. Putrid taste, before epileptic fit. Ulcers, smart and burn. Tongue, coated, indented, deep longitudinal cracks along center. Paralysis of tongue. Aphasia.

Throat - Aphonia before the menses. Continuous pain in the larynx, worse touch. Sore, right to left, worse cold drinks. Chronic hypertrophy of tonsils with syphilitic taint.

Stomach - Nausea. Vomiting for weeks or months due to erosion from superficial ulceration of lining of viscous. Heartburn with pain and rawness from stomach to throat pit, often with cough.

Abdomen - Pain or distress deep in abdomen as if in omentum. Feeling of heat internally in hypogastric region. Pain in right groin followed by swelling of glands. Large, painless bubo in right groin, opened and discharged freely.

Rectum - Fissures in anus and rectum, prolapsed. Feels tied up with strictures. Obstinate constipation. Diarrhea, bilious, painless worse seashore, drives her out of bed about 5 a.m. Water from enema escapes, with pain. Sensations - A seething feeling as if hot water or hot oil running through all veins of the body, all night long. A far-away feeling with apathy. As if going insane or about to be paralyzed. As if top of head were coming off. As if teeth were loose. Tongue feels as if paralyzed. Fluttering as of something alive in teeth. As if throat tearing to pieces. As of a nervous chill commencing in anus and running down legs. Palms and soles as if pricked by needles. As if bitten by bugs.

Male - Nodular formation in testes, spermatic cord and scrotum. Chancres. Aching of genitals, cannot sit still.

Female - Menses, with putrid meat-like odor. Leucorrhea profuse, thin, watery, acrid with sharp, knife-like pain in ovaries. Yellow, offensive, acrid leucorrhea, so profuse it soaks through napkins and runs to the heels, with itching of the genitals. Ulcers on labia. Ulcers on the vulva with ovarian pain, sensitive to touch. Cutting pain in ovary during sex, at the moment of orgasm. Habitual abortion. Food - Capricious appetite. No food agrees or satisfies him. Total loss of appetite for months. Craves alcoholic drinks. Aversion to meat.

Chest - Soreness of chest. Rattling in chest and throat. Oppression of chest to such an extent as almost to arrest breathing. Sensation of pressure under upper part of sternum. Constitutions - Syphilitic.

Heart - Large, soft pulse. Valvular disease of heart. Sharp pains in heart from base to apex (Med. has reverse), at night. As if hot water flowing in the veins.

Back - Neck feels short. Pain at coccyx with sensation as if it is swollen, worse sitting. Pain in the back in the region of kidney, worse after urinating. Breasts - Sensitive to touch, feel sore during menses and other times. Causations - Sun. Syphilis. Damp weather, thunderstorms.

Limbs - Muscles contracted in hard knots. Indolent ulcers. Sciatica, worse at night, better about daybreak. Bones pain as if sawed. Bilateral exostoses sore and painful. Osteo-sarcoma in center of tibia. Cold pain in legs. Shin bones painful, better pouring cold water on them. Soles painful with feeling of contraction, worse standing on them. Cannot sit on low chair or squat. Redness and rawness between toes (Sil.). Rheumatism of shoulder j oint, at insertion of deltoid, worse from raising arm laterally or in front. Itching eruptions about elbows. Affections of middle fingers. Always washing the hands. Lungs - Asthma with wheezing and rattling (Ant-t.). Chronic asthma, worse in summer, during thunderstorms, at night, humid weather. Dry cough, worse lying on right side, worse at night, windpipe sensitive to touch (Lach.). Sharp pains from base of heart to apex at night.

Sleep - Sleeplessness. Great restlessness at night, impossible to keep leg in one position. Wakes soon after midnight and cannot sleep again until 6 a.m.

Skin - Extreme emaciation. Reddish-brown eruption with a disagreeable odor. Swollen and blotched. Biting as from bugs. Wandering erysipelas. Conical crusts. Bullae. White or pockmark scars. Coppery spots. Distorted nails.

Modalities - Better inland, mountains, high altitude. Better during day, from applied heat. Better continued or slow motion. Better changing positions. Worse at night, from sundown to sunrise. Worse full moon. Worse damp, thunderstorms. Worse extreme heat or cold, winter, summer. Worse at the seashore. Worse in any position, squatting. Worse motion, raising arms laterally. Worse protruding tongue.

Teeth - Teeth feel sticky, as of a worm in. Feeling as if teeth had all got out of place. Teeth decay at the edge of gums. Toothache better pressing them together, worse hot or cold things. Teeth cupped in children. Vertigo - Vertigo on looking up, seems to be caused by heat. COMMENTS - Syph. is useful for ailments since syphilis, or a history of syphilis in the family. Pains get worse or better gradually, are shifting and require frequent change of position. Unbearable pains (Aur.). Linear pain. Ulcers and bone pains (Merc.). Characteristic aggravated by night, pains from darkness to daylight, begin with twilight and end with daylight. All symptoms are worse at night. Terrible dread of night, because of mental and physical exhaustion on waking. Neuralgia and headache, asthma, coughs worse from sunset to sunrise, whether syphilitic or not. Sleeplessness (Sulph.). Epilepsy. Parkinson’s disease. Facial paralysis. Hemiplegia, “persistent pains in any part of the body.” Neurotic behavior, especially wringing and washing of the hands. AIDS, dementia, sleeplessness, anxiety, fear of infection, and neurotic behavior. Ulceration, affecting the mouth, nose, genitals or skin. Ulcers have grayish bases. Abscesses with foul secretions. Fetid pus formations. Succession of abscesses. Eruptions with copper-colored spots. Pemphigus. Ozaena with discharge of fetid clinkers. Catarrhal and nerve deafness. Itching of nostrils. Fetid discharges from the ear. Alopecia universalis. Dark purple lines between alae nasi and cheeks. Itching, scabby eruptions on face or breast, singly or in clusters, looking like herpes. Pain and pressure behind sternum. Ophthalmia neonatorum, the lids adhere during sleep, pains worse 2 to 5 a.m., profuse pus, better cold bathing. Iritis, syphilitic or rheumatic. Diplopia, one image seen below the other. Ptosis, sleepy look from drooping lids. Teeth decay at the edge of the gums and break off. Cupped teeth, serrated edges, dwarfed in size and converge at their tips. Deformities of the teeth. The teeth come in rotten and deformed (Calc-f., Kreos.). Paralysis of tongue. Aphasia. Craving for alcohol in any form. Hereditary tendency to alcoholism. Impaired nutrition, emaciation. Burnett recorded many instances of Syph. helping stunted children. Progeria. Babies that never stop crying and screaming ever since they were born (Jal., Aeon.). Leucorrhea, profuse, soaking through napkins and running to heels. Rectal pain. “Obstinate constipation for years, rectum seems tied up with strictures, when enema was used the agony of passage was like labor.” H. C. Allen said “Syphilitics or patients who have had chancre treated by local means and as a result have suffered from throat and skin troubles for years, are nearly benefited by this remedy at commencement of treatment unless some other remedy is clearly indicated.” ; Thomas Wildes noted that, in his experience with Syph., the chancre increases for the first two weeks and then gradually fades away, not being followed by secondaries. Wildes cured a bookkeeper who, for many months, had a piercing, pressing, excruciating headache over his right eye extending deep into his brain. It was so severe, he was losing continuity of thought and memory. Under Syph. 1,000c every night, the headache disappeared entirely in ten days and his mental faculties were fully restored. But in six weeks the whole eyebrow on that side broke out into a sickly, yellow, syphilitic eczema with a red, angry and oozing base extending under the arch to the lid, from canthus to canthus, up into forehead and down the side of the nose. The cure of this was tedious; Wildes attributed it to his change of remedy instead of continuing with Syph. This man had syphilis a few years before. In 1879 a woman, 26, extremely bright and intelligent, came to Wildes with a dreadful Syphilinum ozaena. She also had a spinal curvature and congestion of right ovary. She had always been delicate. Syph. cured the ozaena and improved her health, but it “drove out a saddle to which the Sepia saddle is but a shadow.” A furious inflammatory mass of syphilitic sores, scabs and eczema, red and angry with a fiery base extending from one malar prominence to the other, across nose up to eyes and forehead. This took eighteen months to cure. The ozaena never returned. A boy, age 4, had an obstinate rash, a combination of prurigo and herpes, on his chin, lips, cheekbone, forehead and hairy scalp, on arms, chest, back, bends of joints and on the joints and on fingers and hands, nowhere profuse. In spite of authorities to the contrary, Wildes maintained that syphilitic rashes may itch and that prurigo is infectious and is one of the initial stages of leprosy. This boy had a spot of eruption on the left thigh the size of the top joint of a man’s thumb. This was distinctly a leper spot. Syph. 1,000c caused the rash to come out strongly all over the body in patches, the face was one-third covered with a thick, yellow, scabby eruption. The remedy was continued and the boy got well, wonderfully improved in health, was no longer nervous, grew well, slept well, with good appetite. A girl, 16, had measles a year before which did not come out properly. A year and a half prior she was subject to neuralgic headaches. She had been ailing about two years, very despondent, wanted to die, headaches growing more violent. During the headaches, the temple veins stood out, had pains all over the body, was very irritable, restless, walked about much of the time, did not wish to be soothed, violent on being opposed, had tremors and seemed on the verge of convulsions, dazed, absentminded and almost insane. Always washed her hands. She was formerly constipated, but now subject to “a kind of diarrhea.” Menses never came on properly and for the past year had been very irregular, much delayed, scanty and always extremely painful. Often feverish. Anxious sleep, distressed and often wakeful and violently restless. The symptoms indicated Syph. and under this she steadily recovered. A young woman contracted “leprosysyphilis” from vaccination. She had ablood- boil on her arm that would not heal. Face broken out with a fiery rash. With Syph. 1,000c at bedtime she recovered rapidly. The arm healed quickly and her face became free from eruption. A boy, 3, had a cluster of yellow blotches on his fingers and roots of nails, distorting the nails. The boy ’ s father was epileptic. The boy was helped with Fl-ac. and cured with Syph., the nails became straight. G. H. Carr related the case of an old man who had been troubled for two or three winters with an intense cold pain in both legs. It came on every night on lying down and lasted all night, the only relief was from getting up and walking. Magnetic leggings had given the most relief. Syph. 1,000c, one dose daily, was given. He lost the pain for six weeks, when it returned in milder form. Syph. 100,000C was given and he had no more pains all the winter. The medicine, he said “made his genitals ache so that he couldn’t sit still.” This lasted over a month. Syph. 100,000c cured a woman of “asthma” that she had for twenty-five years, the attack coming on only at night after lying down or during a thunderstorm. Swan said he gave crying infants one dose of Syph. 100,000c, when they developed the propensity immediately after birth and did not cease, and it was difficult to make them cry after that. Yingling reported the case of Rev. D., 30, who was dark and free from venereal disease. Haggard look. He had a constant dull, heavy ache above inner angle of right eye, very distressing with an occasional thrust as of an iron rod from the same spot through to lower part of occiput. This thrust was excruciating. He was due to preach the next day, but the pain quite incapacitated him, which led him to appeal for help. Syph. 100,000c, one dose, was given. He was free from pain before he reached home, and was perfectly well the next morning. RELATIONS-Compare: (l)Merc„ Kali-hp., Nit-ac., Aur., Alum. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Kidneys - Urine frothy, scanty, yellow. Urinates only once a day, but profuse. Passes urine better while standing. Nocturnal bedwetting.

Perspiration - Perspires at night, with exhaustion. Sweats at night, most marked between scapulae and down to waist. Peculiar disagreeable odor from body.

Temperature - Chilly. Nervous chills preceded by pains in head. Fever dry, hot, shortly after going to bed, parted lips, great thirst. Sweats at night with exhaustion.

full:
PHARMACY - eug-c. Syzygium aromaticum. Clove oil. Eugeniacaryophallata. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis. Asthma. Bronchitis. Rheumatism. Sprains. Strains. Toothache.

HERBAL - The clove plant originated in the lowlands, valleys, and hillsides of the southern Philippine islands. The essential clove oil, the most popular clove product, is extracted from the flower of the clove. Clove oil constituents include eugenol, eugenyl acetate, caryophyllene and iocaryophyllene. Clove oil is used in connection with respiratory ailments such as asthma and bronchitis, muscle aches, sprains and strains, arthritis and rheumatism. Many individuals use clove oil for its analgesic effects for body pain. Clove oil is considered by many to be an effective antibiotic, antiseptic, antiviral, analgesic, antioxidant, carminative, expectorant, antifungal, anti-parasitic, spasmodic, and stimulant. REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Syzygium Jambolanum
author: Murphy

PHARMACY - syzyg. Syzygiumjambolanum. Jambol seeds. Syzygium cumini. Eugenia jambolana. Jumbul. N. O. Myrtacae. India. Trituration of the seeds. Tincture of the powdered fruit-stones. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Diabetes. Glycosuria. Pimples. Prickly heat. Ulcers.

HERBAL - Syzygiumjambolanum is a native of India. It has an edible fruit, the powdered stones of which have a popular use in India as a remedy for diabetes. Syzyg. has an immediate effect of increasing the blood sugar, glycosuriaresults. The dose is five to ten grains of the powdered stones three times a day, also, the tincture.

HOMEOPATHIC - Syzyg. is a most useful remedy in diabetes mellitus. Dudgeon used Syzyg. in the lower homeopathic potencies with marked success, which has been repeated by many others. Diminution and disappearance of sugar in the urine. Great thirst, weakness, emaciation. Very large amounts of urine, specific gravity high. Prickly heat in upper part of the body, small red pimples itch violently. Hansen mentioned “old ulcers of skin, probably of a diabetic foundation” as having been cured with Syzyg. COMMENTS - Dudgeon related the case of a scientific man, 56, who complained of “prickly heat” all over upper part of body and arms. The skin was covered with small, red papules, which itched so intensely he could get no rest. There was much thirst and great flow of urine, which he was obliged to pass every two hours, night and day, mouth very dry. Urine 1036, very saccharine. Syzyg. tincture, mixed with three times the quantity of alcohol, was given of this two drops every three hours. The specific gravity of the urine steadily declined, sugar disappeared and all the symptoms passed off. This in spite of the fact that the dietetic rules were relaxed. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Insulin. - an aqueous solution of an active principle from pancreas which affects sugar metabolism. If administered at suitable intervals in diabetes mellitus, the blood sugar is maintained at a normal level and the urine remains free of sugar. Overdosage is followed by weakness and fatigue and tremulousness and profuse sweating. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

PHARMACY - tab-fum. Tabacum fumus. Tobacco smoke. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Asthma. Bronchitis. Coughs. Lung, disorders. Tobacco, addiction.

HOMEOPATHIC - Tab-fiim. is made by blowing cigarette smoke into a bottle of water, which is then mixed and potentized. A homeopathic proving of Tab-fum. was done by Chachanidze. It has been used to reduce the cravings for smoking of cigarettes. Allergies to cigarette smoke, headaches and irritability from smell of tobacco. Asthma in cigarette smokers. MIND - Concentration difficult during study. Anxiety, which comes from the heart. Anticipation as if something bad will happen. Irritability in the crowd, desire to escape. Dullness. Indifference to habitual deeds. Sensation as if one has a disease of throat (fixed idea).

Head - Sensation of emptiness in the right half of the head with the nausea. Dull pain in the head. Headache, aggravation from the sun. Heaviness in the occiput, more in the left side, began in the morning awaking after. Heaviness of the whole head. Sensation as if head is bursting. As if all bones of the scull are aching, especially along the sutures. Nausea and emptiness in the head. Amelioration from the stool. Lungs - Shortness of breath even after slight physical exertion, worse ascending stairs. Hoarseness, burning of throat and weakness of voice. Dry cough, as if would choke.

Eyes - Burning, itching and lachrymation, worse in the right eye.

Nose - Sensation of smell of smoke. Stuffed-up nose, amelioration in open air. Discharge of mucus to the postnasal region. Sensations - Sensation as if faint, as if body is like cotton wool.

Face - Aching of the left upper jaw-bone in the morning after awaking, as if it is toothache. It is extending to the left eye- socket and left side of the nose bone, lasts whole day. Pain goes to the forehead and nose in the evening.

Mouth - Tickling. Heat in the mouth, as if hot air go out from mouth. Sensation that mouth is dirty. Desire to clean teeth. Sensation of loosening of teeth with bitter saliva. Salivation. Pressure of parotid glands as if after sour lemon. Desire to make massage with tongue of gums. As if toothache in upper incisors. Ache in the root of the tooth of upper jaw-bone. Sensation as if teeth are unnecessary. Desire to rub gums and teeth. Pain like from little nail. Stretching pain in the right submaxillary region. Sensation of swelling of the inner cheek. Little white ulcer on inner cheek.

Throat - Sensation of coating at the throat and at the postnasal region. Numbness of posterior part of gullet and of throat and hoarseness. Sensation feel like tissues are hanging from the gullet. Sensation as if ulcers on gullet. Vertigo - Sensation of vertigo, as if falling to the right. Vertigo with palpitations during walking. REFERENCES - Chachanidze. Murphy.

Stomach - Hunger, burning in stomach as if hot water is pouring, in the morning. Increased appetite with impatience. Hunger after eating. Desire chocolate.

Sleep - Drowsy from 7 to 8 p.m. Dreams of heavy shower, rain, flood, dirty water. Dreams of being dirty, desire to take a shower.

Tongue - Sensation of coating at the root of the tongue. Tickling and itching of tongue. Pricking in tip of tongue. As if beating of electricity to the tip op of tongue. Dryness, burning of tongue. Shooting pain in the root of tongue extending to the right Eustachian tube and to the right ear.
