full:
PHARMACY - tab. Tabacum nicotiana. Tobacco. Nicotiana tabacum. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of the fresh leaves collected before the flowers are developed. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Anemia. Angina, pectoris. Anus, prolapse. Asthma. Backaches. Brain, anemia. Brain- fag. Catalepsy. Cholera. Cholera, infantum. Color-blindness. Constipation. Diarrhea. Epilepsy. Esophagus, stricture. Fainting. Freckles. Giddiness. Glands, enlarged. Heartbeats, disorders. Heartburn. Hernia. Hiccough. Idiocy. Itching. Legjerking. Lip, cancer. Lung, disorders. Masturbation, effects. Ménière’s disease. Morning sickness. Motion, sickness. Nausea. Optic, neuritis. Pregnancy, disorders. Prostatorrhea. Rectum, paralysis. Seasickness. Speech, disorders. Strabismus. Strokes. Tetanus. Toothache. Varicocele. Vertigo. Vomiting.

HERBAL - When Columbus and his followers landed in Cuba in 1492, the practice of smoking tobacco was in common use among the natives throughout the island and also throughout the continent of America. On their return to Spain, the practice rapidly spread throughout the Peninsula. Nicotiana tabacum received its specific name from Jean Nicot, the French ambassador to Portugal, who was the means of introducing the tobacco plant into France about 1560. Sir Walter Raleigh and his companions introduced the practice into England in 1586. From that time, the cultivation, manufacture and use of tobacco, either by smoking, snuffing or chewing, rapidly became popular.

HOMEOPATHIC - Tab. has nausea, giddiness, deathly sinking, vomiting, icy coldness and sweat, with intermittent pulse. Complete prostration of the entire muscular system. Collapse. Seasickness. Marked anti-septic qualities, antidotal to cholera germs. Cholera infantum, cold, but wants abdomen uncovered. Vigorous peristaltic activity. Diarrhea. Produces high tension and arteriosclerosis of the coronary arteries. Angina pectoris with coronary sclerosis and high tension. Constriction of throat, chest, bladder and rectum. Pallor, breathlessness, hard cord-like pulse. Vagus, sympathetic, cerebro-spinal nerves and heart are prominently affected. Complete prostration and relaxation of the entire muscular system with free secretions, vomiting, profuse sweat, lachrymation, salivation etc. Constriction of the muscles of hollow organs, throat, bladder, rectum, chest etc. Cramps, then paralysis of bowels, heart etc. Convulsions, head firmly drawn back. Jerking throughout the body. Trembling. Pains are worse from heat. Excessive emaciation, especially of the muscles of back and cheeks. Gait slow and shuffling, unsteady, difficulty in ascending stairs. Faintness. Tetanus. Paralysis of sphincters. Slides in bed. Coughing causes hiccough, stitches in pit of stomach. Symptoms come in paroxysms, are periodical. Gastralgia, enteralgia. MIND - Mental confusion and fatigue. Confusion from motion. Brain fag. Idiotic, epileptic idiocy. Slow perception. Forgetful. Indifferent. Desire for company in evening and at night. Morose, sensation of extreme wretchedness. Feels wretched during menopause period and menses. Feels very despondent. Discontented. Apathetic, indifferent. Sadness is better after complaining. Sadness with impeded respiration. Weeping ameliorates symptoms. Suicidal disposition but lacks courage. Nervous and restlessness. Anguish when walking in open air. Sudden anxiety, with angina pectoris or oppression of chest, driving him from place to place. Anxiety from thinking about it. Anxiety better after crying. Anxiety at night. Fear after eating food. Fear from noises. Cheerful, merry and talkative. Sings all day. Silly talk. Talks nonsense. Talks to himself. Delusions, preventing sleep. Feels as if someone were coming to arrest him or murder him. Doesn’ t recognize his relatives. Unconsciousness, as in a trance, better when cold water poured over head.

Head - Head drawn back in convulsions. Sick headache with deathly nausea. Periodical headache from fatigue or excitement. Headache better in the open air. Headache with nausea and vertigo. Tight feeling as from a band. Heaviness sensation with heat of head, better open air. Sensation as if head would burst, or as if brain were being bored out. Sudden pain as if struck by a hammer, worse while passing urine. Hair falls out. Secretion from eyes, nose and mouth increased.

Eyes - Sunken eyes, blue around them. Heat and burning in eyes. Pupils dilated. Retina retains the image too long. Eyeballs injected, cornea covered with mucus, must wipe it off. Contraction of eyelids. Strabismus.

Ears - Burning heat and redness of the ears. Hyperesthesia to music and loud talking. Hearing music causes pain in the ears. Ménière’s disease with feeling of seasickness. Sensation as if ears were closed. Nerve deafness.

Nose - Burning sensation and tingling in the nose. Paroxysms of sneezing. Secretion increased. Dryness and obstruction of nose. Nasal catarrh with crawling sensation in nostrils. Naso-pharyngitis and tracheitis.

Face - Emaciation of face. Deathly pale, blue, pinched, sunken, collapsed, covered with cold sweat (Ars., Verat.). One cheek hot and glowing, other pale. Freckles. Miliary rash on cheeks. Violent tearing in facial bones and teeth, worse evening. Pain in maxillary joint, worse laughing. Spasms of the lower jaw.

Mouth - Profuse salivation. Salivation with burning in mouth and throat, tickling, dryness, rawness. Spits much with other complaints. Frothing from the mouth. Mouth full of white tenacious mucus. Dryness of the mouth and tongue with violent thirst. Tongue feels swollen. Swelling of glands under tongue. Drawling, monotonous style of reading. Lips retracted. Lips cracked, swollen, covered with a brown crust. Speech difficult. Weak, interrupted speech.

Throat - Throat dry, can hardly swallow. Much viscid mucus in throat. Nasopharyngitis and tracheitis. Hemming cough. Morning cough, sometimes with vomiting. Hoarseness of public speakers. Violent constriction of throat in angina pectoris. Swallowing difficult on account of spasms of pharynx. Scraping in larynx causes frequent hawking and coughing. Laryngismus stridulus. Vertigo - Vertigo with seasickness. Excessive vertigo, with copious cold sweat, worse opening eyes. Vertigo on open ing eyes, in sick headache with deathly nausea, periodical. Vertigo on rising or looking upward. Vertigo with nausea, worse indoors, better open air. Vertigo and fainting, loss of consciousness. Vertigo followed by vomiting of food and tremulous weakness. Ménière’s disease with feeling of seasickness. Vision - Amaurosis. Muscae volitantes. Central scotoma. Retina retains image too long. Diplopia. Dim and confused, as if black dots filled visual field. Sudden loss of vision without lesion, followed by atrophy of optic nerve. Loss of sight on looking steadily at any white object. Strabismus. COMMENTS - M. E. Douglass, in the Homeopathic News of 1897, wrote about the “medicinal uses” of tobacco and it seems that it was regarded as a perfect panacea by the Virginians for diseases of men and cattle. Douglass mentioned its palliative use for bee stings and mosquito bites. A portion of a leaf was moistened with vinegar and applied to the part. Ip., one of the antidotes of Tab., has a similar reputation. Strong tobaccojuice is the most effectual destroyer of the burrowing-flea, Chigoe. Leaves of tobacco are moistened with vinegar or camphor solution and applied to the forehead and nape for headaches. The pain is allayed and sleep induced. The local application over the pit of the stomach relieves nausea. Douglass used small doses of vinegar for the acute symptoms of nicotine poisoning, either chewing or smoking, with excellent results. Nothing, he said, relieves the sensation of constriction of the esophagus as quickly as vinegar. There is violent rectal tenesmus, paralysis, and prolapsed anus. The bladder sphincter is paralyzed, debility of urine, and bedwetting. Cholera. The power of Tab. to paralyze sphincters and morbid constrictions accounts for its traditional use in cases of strangulated herriia and obstruction of the bowels. Kidney colic comes under the same heading. Impotency in males, prostate discharges (Calad.), and constant dribbling of the urine. The same pair of opposites, relaxation and constriction are seen in the weakness, paralysis, and convulsions. All shades of nervous tremors, faintings, cramps, jerk- ings and restlessness. Tab. holds its place in society by its power of antidoting such conditions. Intermittent heartbeats and arrhythmias, especially in elderly people. Central nervous action that can lead to degeneration of nerve tissue, as seen in tobacco blindness. Amaurosis, optic nerve degeneration following blindness (Phos.). Tab. also produces a condition like brainfag, an inability to concentrate thoughts that may even go on to a state of idiocy. Silly talking in boys. Profoundly influences nutrition, retards growth in children. Characteristic deathly, sinking nausea. It is no doubt by virtue of this, acting homeopathically, that Tab. enables persons who cannot have proper meals endure starvation better than they otherwise would. Terrible faint, sinking feeling at pit of stomach. Pallor, coldness, icy cold surface, covered with cold sweat. Motion sickness (Cocc.). Morning sickness with cold sweats, sinking nausea and dizziness. Violent vomiting, as soon as he began to move, better on deck and in fresh air. Keynote better by uncovering abdomen. Child wants abdomen uncovered, it helps the nausea and vomiting. There may be a coldness of the abdomen at the same time. Skin affections with itching. Teste cured with it several cases of freckles, he repeated the remedy and gave it for weeks at a time : “A country girl had her face and hands covered with freckles, two-thirds of which disappeared completely [under Tab.] in summer, the season in which they are most frequent and obstinate.” Terry cured a case of seasickness, with heat along the spine from the nape down, cold sweat, then vomit. He also cured a case of Meniere’s disease with a feeling as if seasick. Boger cured, with Tab. 100,000c, a persistent backache, worse lying down, better walking, with a history of anginalike attacks. Burnett noted that an infusion of tobacco is a popular German remedy for scrofulous glands. Cooper gives as an indication, “intermittent heart in old people.” C. W. was troubled with spasm of lower jaw, worse outdoors. No remedy worked until he remained one evening with two friends who were smoking and saturated himself with the smoke. That cured him. Slight subsequent returns were always removed by Tab. J. W. Scott observed a case of epileptiform convulsions brought on by tobacco. For five months the patient had two attacks weekly and they grew worse in spite of treatment until the tobacco habit was discontinued. RELATIONS - Antidote: Vinegar, sour apples. Camphor in the physiological antagonist. Compare: (1) Calad., Daph., Lob. and Plan. - cause aversion to tobacco. (2) Nicot. (3) Ars. - chewing tobacco. (4) Ign. - aversion to tobacco smoke. (5) Sep. - neuralgia and dyspepsia), Lyc. impotency. (6) Nux-v. - bad taste due to tobacco. (7) Phos. - tobacco heart, sexual weakness. (8) Hydrobr-ac., Camph., Verat., Ars. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Coldness in stomach, with nausea. Shocks in stomach, at night while sleeping. Gastralgia, pain from cardiac end extending to left arm. Frequent fluttering sensation in pit, with heartburn. Acidity. Burning in stomach. Eructations, sour, hot, of small amounts of food, loud, noisy. Sense of relaxation of stomach with nausea (Ip.). Terrible faint, sinking feeling in pit of stomach. Incessant nausea, worse smell of tobacco smoke (Phos.). Deathly nausea and violent vomiting, worse least motion, better uncovering abdomen. Seasickness, motion sickness. Morning sickness. Nausea during pregnancy, with much spitting. Retching. Vomiting of fecal matter.

Abdomen - Coldness in abdomen. Wants abdomen uncovered, it lessens the nausea and vomiting. Sinking feeling in epigastrium with dreadful faint sense. Retraction of navel, abdominal muscles contracted. Violent burning in abdomen, extorting cries. Painful distentions. Intestinal obstruction. Incarcerated hernia. Strangulated hernia. Gurgling in bowels. Horrible colic, must shriek, with weakness. Colic during stool.

Rectum - Habitual constipation. Constipation with rectum paralyzed, prolapsed. Rectal tenesmus. Involuntary stool, watery or thick curdled stools like sour milk. Sudden diarrhea, watery with nausea and vomiting, prostration and cold sweat. Cholera infantum, warmth of body with icy-cold hands. Watery diarrhea, urgent, painless in morning. Evacuations like cholera, with deathly faintness, cold skin, irregular pulse. Sudden, papescent, yellow-green or greenish, slimy stools. Sensations - As if struck by a hammer on right side of head. As if a band around head. As if brains were being bored out. As if black dots filled visual field. As if ears were closed. As of a plug in esophagus. As if throat influenced by a hand. As if chest too tight. As if a crowbar were twisted around the heart. As if seasick. As if stomach were relaxed.

Male - Frequent erections. Nocturnal emissions. Impotency. Genital organs flabby, no erections or little sexual desire. Masturbation and its consequences. Discharge of prostatic fluid. Hyperesthesia and neuralgia of penis. Varicocele.

Female - Retarded and profuse menses. Leucorrhea of serous fluid, worse after menses. During menopause and menses, subjective coldness, epigastric sinking, palpitation, slight diarrhea, muscular relaxation. Excessive sense of wretchedness during menopausal period and menses. Morning sickness of pregnancy, nausea and vomiting, patient dreads least movement. Severe itching of the whole body during pregnancy. Food -. Thirstlessness. Great thirst, worse at night, in cholera infantum. Complete loss of appetite. Constant hunger, nausea if stomach is not satisfied. Incessant nausea, worse smell of tobacco smoke. Desires sweets, ice cream, salt. Immoderate smoking of cigars causes vertigo.

Chest - Angina pectoris. Tightness of chest, better inspiration. Violent constriction of chest. Oppression of the chest with anguish. Pain radiates from the center of sternum. Sticking under sternum with inability to take a deep breath. Nocturnal attacks of tightness across chest. Tuberculosis is said to make less rapid progress among tobacco workers.

Heart - Angina pectoris, pain in precordial region. Angina pectoris with nausea, cold sweat and collapse. Shooting pain from heart down left arm or up into neck. Pain radiates from center of sternum. Bradycardia. Tachycardia. Acute dilatation of heart caused by shock or violent physical exertion. Twisting about the heart. Unsteady heartbeat. Precordial oppression with palpitations and pain between shoulders. Violent beating of heart and carotids. Violent palpitations, worse lying on left side (Phos.). Palpitations due to tobacco. Pulse rapid and small. Pulse thready, intermittent, hard, cord like, imperceptible.

Back - Emaciation of the muscles of back. Pain in the small of back worse lying, better while walking. Heat down spine. Throbbing in sacral region. Red eruption on back. Pustules on nape and upper limbs. Violent pain, in lumbar region. Neck stiff. Neuralgia of neck, with tightness of throat. Head drawn back in convulsions. Causations - Effects of sunstroke. Bee-sings and mosquito bites.

Limbs - Formication. Feebleness of arms. Fingertips fuzzy. Cramps in single fingers, worse washing. Legs and hands icy cold, limbs tremble. Paralysis following a stroke (Plb.). Cramps in legs. Gait shuffling, unsteady. Can’t walk with angina pectoris. Tremor and disabling weakness of feet.

Sleep - Drowsiness, better in open air. Urgent inclination to sleep, especially after a meal and towards evening with frequent yawn- ings. Insomnia with dilated heart with cold, clammy skin and anxiety. Disturbed sleep at night with fright. Nightmares. Stupefying sleep at night. Smell - Diminished power of smell. Sensitive to smell of wine. Smell of tobacco, aggravates (Ign.). Patient tormented by smell of tobacco.

Skin - Skin swollen, yellow, hot and dry. Itching over the whole body, as from flea or insect bites. Eruption of itching pimples or vesicles with yellow serum and red areola. Red spots on face and on right shoulder, burning when touched. Violent itching of whole surface. Dark, color of skin. Vesicles containing yellow serum and surrounded by red areola. Cold skin in cholera, livid, with angina pectoris. Jaundice.

Modalities - Better when uncovering abdomen. Better cold, open fresh air, cold applications. Better walking. Better weeping, vomiting. Worse from motion of boat, riding in cars. Worse extremes of heat and cold, being indoors. Worse stimulants. Worse motion, pressure. Worse in evening, rising up, opening eyes. Worse lying on left side, causes palpitations. Music causes pains in ears.

Liver - Stitches in liver. Pressure in liver region as from a heavy body. Hepatic region sensitive to pressure. Lungs - Difficult, violent constriction of chest. Dyspnea with tingling down left arm when lying on left side. Difficult breathing, worse ascending, with distress in heart and palpitations. Paroxysms of suffocation. Hurried, anxious, irregular breathing. Inability to take a deep breath, from sticking under sternum. Periodical attacks of asthma, sits up in bed, suffering with extreme dyspnea. Asthma with blueness of face and swelling of jugular veins.

Kidneys - Kidney pain with cold sweat, deathly nausea. Kidney colic, violent pain along ureter, left side. Renal region sensitive to pressure. Paralysis of sphincters, urine dribbles. Enuresis. Urine increased, or scanty high- colored urine. Urine yellowish-red with increased secretion. Inflammation of the orifice of the urethra. Bedwetting.

Cough - Cough dry, teasing, must take a swallow of cold water (Caust., Phos.). Cough followed by hiccough. Cough and hiccough at the same time. Suffocative cough from irritation in throat and larynx, worse at night. Dry cough, cardiac in origin. Coughing causes stitches in pit of stomach.

Perspiration - Cold sweats. Sudden cold sweats with chill, angina pectoris, kidney colic etc. Perspiration at night. Cold, clammy sweats at night on hands, forehead and face.

Temperature - Icy cold skin. Chills with cold sweat. Coldness and shivering, sometimes with chattering of teeth. Chilliness after eating and drinking. Heat down spine, of one cheek, internal. Body warm, with icy coldness of hands and legs.

CLINICAL - Addictions. Alcoholism. Delirium tremens. Drug, abuse. Fatigue. Heroin, habit. Tobacco, habit.

HERBAL -…
full:
PHARMACY - tab-ib. Tabernanthe iboga. Iboga bark. Black bugbane. Bitter grass. N. O. Apocynacae. Bark and root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Addictions. Alcoholism. Delirium tremens. Drug, abuse. Fatigue. Heroin, habit. Tobacco, habit.

HERBAL - Tabernanthe iboga, also known as black bugbane, is a perennial rainforest shrub and hallucinogen, native to western Africa. Iboga stimulates the central nervous system when taken in small doses and induces visions in larger doses. Ibogaine is the active chemical in the African root. It is a strong, long-lasting psychedelic used traditionally in a coming of age ritual, but also known for its modern use in treating heroin addiction. Tabernanthe iboga The drug’s story as an anti-addictive began in 1962, when college dropout and heroin addict Howard Lotsof obtained a dose from a chemist friend. Iboga relieved him of all cravings for heroin. In 1986, Lotsof began to supply ibogaine to a clinic for addicts in Holland. The clinic found that ibogaine works in three stages. First the addict has about four hours of waking dreams in which he seems to confront inner demons. This is followed by an eight- to 10-hour “cognitive evaluation period," during which the user analyzes the waking dream. Then comes a sleepless day or two, which Lotsof calls the “residual stimulation phase.” Lotsof said ibogaine allows addicts, especially heroin users, to put aside their fears of withdrawal and begin the process of detoxification. One methadone patient said that in just four days he reached a state that normally would have taken him three months, but without the agony. The heroin addiction therapy may last several days and upon completion the subject is generally no longer physically dependent. Research suggests that ibogaine may also help to treat addictions to alcohol and nicotine. Ibogaine breaks down in the liver into a metabolite called nor-ibogaine. This metabolite has been shown in clinical research to prevent cravings for several weeks after a single dose in some individuals. Others have observed Iboga having some undesirable side effects regarding blood pressure and heartbeat. COMMENTS - The Iboga was brought back from Gabon in 1864 by Dr. Griffon du Bel- lay, a navy surgeon. He wrote, “The root of this plant is the part that the Gabonese eat. They say that it is inebriating, aphrodisiac, and, with it, they claim that they feel no need for sleep.” However, as early as 1885, Father Henri Neu had written in a manuscript entitled “Le Gabon” (Neu 1885), “The natives use an infusion of iboga root scrapings as a potent philter that enables one to discover hidden Tabernanthe iboga things and to tell the future. The one who drinks it falls into a deep sleep during which he is obsessed by uninterrupted dreams which, until the time that he awakens, he takes to be actual events.” REFERENCES - Lotsof. Murphy.

PHARMACY - tama. Tamarindus indica. Tamarind. N.O. Leguminosae. Tamari- caceae. Africa. India. Tincture of the fruit. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acidity. Asthma. Boils. Constipation. Rheumatism. Spleen, disorders. Tobacco, habit.

HERBAL - People in India use tamarind as a souring agent like vinegar. It is used in common preparations like chutneys. It is also eaten as a fruit by those who have a craving for sour things. Tamarind flavored beverages are popular in Italy and Latin America. Patients suffering from rheumatic problems are said to be aggravated from tamarind. MIND - Indifference, apathy. Indolence. Lethargy, no desire to work, even if it is important and requires immediate attention. Mental dullness, sluggishness. Difficulty thinking and comprehending. Forgetfulness. Restlessness, nervousness. Starting easily. Fear of his own shadow. Fear of passing stool, on account of pain. Irritability from trifles. Tolerance in persons normally easily annoyed and irritated. Quiet disposition. Involuntary sighing. Weeping, tearful mood. Dreams of talking to deceased grandfather.

Head - Heaviness of head.

Eyes - Lachrymation, especially in left eye. Food - Increase thirst. Desires ice-cold water, cold drinks, ice cream, tamarind, sour foods, spicy foods. Craves tobacco. Worse from spicy foods and tobacco.

Nose - Obstruction of nose.

Rectum - Ineffectual urging with unsatisfactory stools. Constipation. Rectal pain worse passing stools, walking, sitting, squatting. COMMENTS - Vakil stated, “People consuming tobacco in any form, chewing or smoking, are especially affected. Tamarindus may be useful to give up the habit of tobacco chewing or smoking. Provers addicted to tobacco developed some unbearable symptoms of tobacco, e.g. vertigo. One prover who had stopped smoking one year back, developed increased desire for smoking again and now he is not able to give it up.” Joseph Miller, in Potter’s Cyclopedia, wrote about Tamarindus, “They are accounted specific for all disorders of the Spleen, as being believed to lessen it much; nay they used to drink out of cups made of this wood to cure those illnesses.” RELATIONS - Compare: Phos., Ph-ac., Mangi, Sulph. REFERENCES - Murphy. Vakil.

Back - Pain in one spot under right scapula, worse lying on back.

Modalities - Better drinking cold water, worse from spicy foods and tobacco. Worse morning. Worse from the sun. Mouth - Dryness of mouth, lips and throat. Stringy salvia.

name: Tamus Communis
author: Murphy
constitution: Broken, bones. Bruises. Chilblains. Splinters.
keynote:
PHARMACY - tarn. Tamus communis. Ladies seal. Black bryony. Black bryonia. Blackeye root. Tamus crética. N. O. Dioscoreaceae. Tincture of fresh root. Tincture of the berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Broken, bones. Bruises. Chilblains.…
full:
PHARMACY - tarn. Tamus communis. Ladies seal. Black bryony. Black bryonia. Blackeye root. Tamus crética. N. O. Dioscoreaceae. Tincture of fresh root. Tincture of the berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Broken, bones. Bruises. Chilblains. Splinters.

HERBAL - The Greeks used the young suckers like asparagus, which they resemble. Tamus is a popular remedy for removing discoloration caused by bruises. The fresh root is scraped and the pulp rubbed into parts affected by gout, rheumatism, or paralysis. It is also reputed as a diuretic. The fruits steeped in gin are a popular remedy for chilblains. The tincture also has a reputation for curing chilblains when applied externally. The root-plaster of Tamus has been used to removed scars and deformities and it softens harden tissues (Thiosin.). It draws forth splinters and heals broken bones, dissolves congealed blood. If laid on hip or knuckles or any other part where there is great pain, it takes away the pain speedily. COMMENTS - Gerarde reported, “The root is very great and thick oftentimes as big as a man’s leg, black without and very clammy or slimy within, which having been scraped with a knife, it seems to be a matter fit to be spread upon cloth or leather in manner of a plaster of sear-cloth.” Dioscorides, according to Gerarde, said the fruit or berries take away sun-burns and other blemishes of the skin, and Gerarde added that these, “very quickly waste and consume away black and blue marks that come of bruises and dry beatings: which thing also the roots perform being laid upon them.” Joseph Miller stated, “A cataplasm of the root with vinegar and cow-dung, helps the gout” and he added significantly, “It is but rarely used.” REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Tanacetum Vulgare
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Worse at night, at 4 a.m. Suddenness is a characteristic of a number of the symptoms..
constitution: Abortion. Abscess. Amenorrhea. Chorea. Convulsions. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Epilepsy. Eyes, inflamed. Eyes, sclerotica. Hallucinations. Hydrophobia. Labia, abscess. Menorrhagia. Paralysis. Poison ivy. Strabismus. Worms.
keynote:
PHARMACY - tanac. Tanacetum vulgare. Tansy. Chrysanthemum vulgare. N. O. Com- positae. Tincture of the fresh plant in flower. Potencies of the oil. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abortion. Abscess. Amenorrhea. Chorea. Convulsions. Dysentery.…
full:
PHARMACY - tanac. Tanacetum vulgare. Tansy. Chrysanthemum vulgare. N. O. Com- positae. Tincture of the fresh plant in flower. Potencies of the oil. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abortion. Abscess. Amenorrhea. Chorea. Convulsions. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Epilepsy. Eyes, inflamed. Eyes, sclerotica. Hallucinations. Hydrophobia. Labia, abscess. Menorrhagia. Paralysis. Poison ivy. Strabismus. Worms.

HERBAL - The word “tansy” is derived from immortality with its deep-yellow button-like flowers, a close companion of the Ragwort (Senecio facobea). In olden times puddings were made containing tansy leaves and these puddings were called “tansies” also. Gerarde also said that the seeds kill and expel worms of every sort, the root is good in gout, and being drunk with wine relieves pain in the bladder and dysuria when a man is only able to urinate by drops.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hale noted it for amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia, uterine cramps and metritis. In one instance it caused a large abscess of the labia majora. Hale said acrystalline acid identical with Santonin has been isolated from it. Abnormal lassitude, a nervous and tired feeling. “Half dead, half alive feeling” all over. It is of use in chorea and reflex spasms due to worms. Tanac. is said to be a specific against effects of poison ivy. Tanac. induces all the cardinal features of rabies, including abundant salivation, excitability, tendency to bite. Hoarse cry. Hallucinations. Diminished sensibility and mobility, momentary paralysis. Frothy, bloody mucus in the air passages. Convulsions, without loss of consciousness. Opisthotonos. Spasms of pharynx, larynx and the thorax. MIND - Mental fatigue, nausea and vertigo, worse in a closed room. Inability to think coherently. Confusion of thought. Dullness of all the senses. Fatigue of the mind after the least exertion. Ambitious. Wants to stand on his head, stretches and draws up his feet, and says, “it does me good.” Sadness, with desire to be let entirely alone. Irritable, sensitive to noise. Irritable and lazy. Very nervous and low spirited, annoyed by trifles; noise of the children almost unbearable. Extremely sensitive to noise. Coma and violent convulsions.

Head - Weariness in head. Heavy, dull, confused. Dull, frontal headache with cutting in temples. Headache with least exertion.

Eyes - Eyes open, very brilliant, pupils equal, widely dilated, immovable. Pupils contracted. Sclerotic congested, dark purple, glassy-looking. Dull aching in eyeballs. Slight inward squint, right eye. Lids agglutinated in morning.

Ears - Stitches in internal ear. Ears seem to close up suddenly. Roaring, ringing in ears. Her own voice sounds strange in her ears.

Nose - Profuse secretion of mucus in nose with fluent coryza. Dryness of nostrils.

Face - Features seemed fixed, giving an expression of deep solemnity. Face dusky, flushed, cheeks bright red. Fullness of head and face.

Mouth - Flat insipid taste. Tongue white coated, feels rough. Mouth, blood-stained, frothy.

Throat - Roughness of throat. Feeling in throat as if one could cough all the time. Unable to swallow. COMMENTS - Like Senec., Tanac. has an action on the female generative organs and a large proportion of the observations with it have been on women who have taken it to procure abortion. Other effects are from its use as a vermifuge, and in addition to these are provings by Burt and others. In Russia, Tanac. has a reputation as a remedy for hydrophobia. M. Peyraud even used Tanac. as a substitute for Pasteurian “vaccinations,” and reported success. W. H. Pierson observed a woman who took two drachms of the oil to procure abortion. The attempt failed, but throughout her pregnancy she suffered from mixed tonic and clonic convulsions. Frothing at the mouth, clenched hands, thumbs turned in, followed by exhaustion and a short coma. Since then, Pierson treated every case of epilepsy which came to him with drop doses of the fluid extract of Tanac. four times a day, with marked success. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In uterine symptoms, Sabin., Tereb., Hedeo., Ruta. (2) In convulsions, Stram., Cic., Cupr. (3) Worm symptoms, convulsions, paralysis, Sant., Cina, Chen-a. (4) Abscess on labium majus, Stry., abscess of scrotum. Follows well: Cimic., Cina, Absin., Nux-v. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Hale.

Stomach - Thirst. Drawing, cutting pains in epigastrium. Faint and sick at stomach. Constant belchings, tasting of the oil. Belchings of sour air at night. Nausea and vomiting.

Abdomen - Dull pains in the right hypochondrium, sharp in left. Sharp, sticking pains in whole umbilical region.

Rectum - Pain in bowels, relieved by stool. Dysentery. Desire for stool immediately after eating. Sensations - As if something closed the ears very suddenly. His own voice sounds strange in his ears. Sensation like a thrill all through body. As though arms and legs suddenly swollen.

Female - Menses suppressed, later, profuse. Dysmenorrhea with bearing-down pains, tenderness, drawing in groins. Miscarriage in the early months of pregnancy.

Heart - Feeble heart-action and all signs of impending dissolution. Pulse increased in force and frequency, feeble.

Back - Severe attack of lumbago. Constant dull ache in loins.

Limbs - Numbness and sensation as though arms and legs were suddenly swelling. Prickling, coming and going, over limbs and along spine with flashes of heat. Cold numbness over limbs, going on to paralysis. Lungs - Breathing laborious. Hurried, stertorous respiration. Frothy mucus obstructs the air-passages.

Modalities - Worse at night, at 4 a.m. Suddenness is a characteristic of a number of the symptoms.

Kidneys - Constant desire. First suppression, then profuse flow. Marked diuresis, must rise in night to urinate. Urine is very fetid, high-colored increased. Urine caused slight scalding.

Temperature - Surface cool and moist. Cold, clammy sweat. Feeling of warmth diffused over whole abdomen.

name: Tanghinia Venenifera
author: Murphy
constitution: Anxiety. Debility. Delirium. Numbness. Paralysis. Stupor. Vomiting. Weakness.
keynote:
PHARMACY - tang. Tanghinia venenífera. N. O. Apocynaceae. Trituration of the seed. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anxiety. Debility. Delirium. Numbness. Paralysis. Stupor. Vomiting. Weakness.

HERBAL - Tanghinia, the Tanghin or Tanquen of Madagascar is the only…
full:
PHARMACY - tang. Tanghinia venenífera. N. O. Apocynaceae. Trituration of the seed. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anxiety. Debility. Delirium. Numbness. Paralysis. Stupor. Vomiting. Weakness.

HERBAL - Tanghinia, the Tanghin or Tanquen of Madagascar is the only representative of its genus of Apocynaceae. The fruit of the tree is ellipsoid, between two and three inches long, having a smooth, purplish skin tinged with green, containing a hard stone surrounded by Tanghinia venenífera a thick fibrous flesh.

HOMEOPATHIC - Intense and distressing vomiting, accompanied by anxiety and weakness. Great debility and anxiety with the vomiting. General weakness. Numbness, over whole body, especially of the hands. Staggers if attempts to walk, is unable to support his own weight and falls down helpless and paralyzed. Complete paralysis. Death, preceded by spasmodic movements of fingers and toes. MIND - Anxiety, with the vomiting. Stupor. Lies as if asleep and when roused answers like a drowsy man and then relapses into former condition. Delirium.

Mouth - Numbness, tingling in mouth and fauces.

Stomach - Vomiting intense, distressing and repeated, first of contents of stomach, then of bile and mucus. Vertigo - Giddy, staggers. COMMENTS - The seed has been used as an “ordeal” test for those thought to have committed a crime. The seed is pounded and a small piece is swallowed by the person to be tried. Those in whom it causes vomiting escape punishment. Those whose stomachs retain it are thought to have been proven guilty, and are quickly killed. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Rectum - Purging and urination.

Limbs - Hands numb. Spasmodic movements of the fingers and toes.

name: Tannicum Acidum
author: Murphy
constitution: Colic. Conjunctivitis. Constipation. Hematuria. Ileus. Nosebleed. Ophthalmia. Palpitations. Vomiting. Weakness.
keynote: PHARMACY - tann-ac. Tannicum acidum. Tannic acid. Tanninum. There are two forms of tannic acid, Gallo- tannic acid, derived from nut-galls. Also querc-tannic acid, derived from healthy leaves and bark of the oak. The former is the most used. Trituration. Solution in rectified…
full:
PHARMACY - tann-ac. Tannicum acidum. Tannic acid. Tanninum. There are two forms of tannic acid, Gallo- tannic acid, derived from nut-galls. Also querc-tannic acid, derived from healthy leaves and bark of the oak. The former is the most used. Trituration. Solution in rectified spirit. One-half percent solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Colic. Conjunctivitis. Constipation. Hematuria. Ileus. Nosebleed. Ophthalmia. Palpitations. Vomiting. Weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Tannin, or tannic acid, of which gallic acid is a derivative, has produced effects on healthy persons and on those taking it for diarrhea. Mostly used locally against excessive secretion of mucus membranes to contract tissue and check hemorrhage. Leathery dryness of mouth and intestinal canal, a condition like ileus and a very aggravated state of constipation. Obstinate constipation. Typhoid fever and dysentery. Intestines can be felt like cylindrical en- largements. Pain in abdomen, sensitive to pressure. Diabetes. Hematuria. Ulcerated tissues. Fetor of the perspiration. Weakness. Chronic nervous coughs.

Eyes - Acute and chronic conjunctivitis. Granular lids and vascular cornea. Chemosis and pannus. Ophthalmia. Purulent ophthalmia of infants.

Nose - Nosebleeds. Chronic catarrh and coryza.

Mouth - Leathery dryness of mucus membrane of mouth and intestinal canal. Hemorrhage and sponginess of the gums. Mercurial salivation. Toothache.

Stomach - Painful sensation in epigastric region and abdomen. Violent pains in stomach. Dyspepsia. Obstinate vomiting of bilious substances.

Abdomen - Abdomen is sensitive to pressure but not distended. Irritable bowel. Intestines could be felt like cylindrical enlargements through walls of abdomen. Ileus. Colic. Ulceration of bowels. Hemorrhage.

Rectum - Obstinate constipation. Chronic diarrhea. Painless and bloody discharge from bowels. Foul stools. Prolapsed rectum. Hemorrhoids.

Female - Sore breasts and nipples. Uterine bleeding. Syphilitic ulceration of the cervix. Food - Loss of appetite. Thirst.

Heart - Palpitations.

Skin - Ulcers with copious discharges.

Tongue - Tongue white, dry. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Querc., Gall-ac., Op., Plb. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Kidneys - Dysuria. Urine scanty, darkcolored. Albuminuria. Hematuria. Lungs - Tuberculosis. Bronchial catarrh. Nervous coughs. Whooping cough.

name: Taraxacum Officinale
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from touch. Better moving, walking, open air. Burning in throat is better by drinking. Worse while lying down, resting, at night. Worse from fat food..
constitution: Ague. Bilious. Cancerous, conditions. Debility. Diabetes. Flatulence. Gallstones. Headaches. Hepatitis. Jaundice. Liver, disorders. Liver, weakness. Neuralgias. Night, sweats. Rheumatism. Tongue, mapped. Typhoid fever.
keynote:
PHARMACY - tarax. Taraxacum officinale. Dandelion. Leontodum taraxacum. Taraxacum dens-leonis. N. O. Compositae. The tincture from the whole plant when in flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Ague. Bilious. Cancerous, conditions. Debility. Diabetes.…
full:
PHARMACY - tarax. Taraxacum officinale. Dandelion. Leontodum taraxacum. Taraxacum dens-leonis. N. O. Compositae. The tincture from the whole plant when in flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Ague. Bilious. Cancerous, conditions. Debility. Diabetes. Flatulence. Gallstones. Headaches. Hepatitis. Jaundice. Liver, disorders. Liver, weakness. Neuralgias. Night, sweats. Rheumatism. Tongue, mapped. Typhoid fever.

HERBAL - Taraxacum’s chief traditional uses are as a remedy for jaundice, liver obstruction in dysentery, involuntary emissions and in difficulties in passing water. The young leaves of the dandelion are sometimes eaten in salads. They have a bitter chicory like taste, as does the root. Children may eat the flowers, although they are supposed to cause bedwetting.

HOMEOPATHIC - The first provings were done by Hahnemann and his pupils. Hahnemann’s provings brought out the leading symptoms “painless urging to urinate,” and “frequent urging to urinate with copious discharge of urine.” Hahnemann pointed out that the urging to urinate with thirst may indicate Tarax. in some cases of diabetes. Hahnemann’s dosage was a single drop of the tincture. Langhammer noted the “mapped tongue.” The tongue is coated white and clears off in patches, leaving dark red, very sensitive spots. Affinity for the liver and bladder. A bilious remedy. Pains in both splenic and liver regions. Heaviness in the liver region. Gastric headaches, bilious attacks with mapped tongue and jaundiced skin. Jaundice with enlarged, indurated liver. Disorders of the liver, sour taste, darting pains in outer parts. Hysterical tympanites. Flatulence. Cancer of bladder. Hands and nose cold at 8 p.m. Cold fingertips. Feeling of sickness and exhaustion, inclined to sit or lie down. Muscular pains with shuddering and muscular prickling. Stitching pains. Affections in left upper side, right lower side, back of foot, sole of foot. Almost all symptoms appear while the patient is seated and are dissipated by walking. MIND - Depressive, morose, sad condition. Memory weak. Apathy, lack of reactions. Dislike for labor, but after beginning works well. Impatient and irritable. Anxiety while sitting. Restlessness on waking. Irresolution. Constant muttering to himself. Inclined to talk, laugh and be merry. Loquacity during perspiration. Unconsciousness.

Head - Heavy and numbing headache. Stinging pains in the head and face. Neuralgic headaches. Headaches due to liver disturbances. Headaches, as from contraction orexpansion of brain. Violent headache, felt only when standing or walking. Sensation of great heat in vertex. Drawing pain in left temple while sitting, ceasing when walking or standing. Tearing pain in occiput. Lancinations in forehead and temples. Tension of scalp.

Eyes - Pain in eyes, as if a grain of sand were in internal canthus. Burning and stinging pains in the eyes. Inflammation of eyes. Lachrymation and photophobia. Nocturnal agglutination of lids. Aversion to light.

Ears - Shootings in ears. Drawing pain in external ear. Stinging, rending pains in the ears.

Nose - Cold nose. Nosebleeds.

Face - Hot and red face. Sensation of heat and redness in face. Shootings and pressure in cheeks. Upper ftp cracked. Pusa/e in right corner of lips. Purulent pimples on face, cheeks, alae nasi and lips.

Mouth - Sour, bitter taste. Acid saliva in mouth. Salivation with sensation as if larynx was pressed shut Biller laste, rising from pharynx into mouth. Smarting, burning and rawness in mouth and fauces. Accumulation of sour water in mouth. Tough, ropy, sour-tasting saliva.

Throat - Hawking up of acid mucus. Sore throat with pressive pain, as from internal swelling. Dryness, shootings and bitter mucus in the throat. Burning in throat from smoking, better drinking.

Stomach - Gastric bilious attacks. Bitter taste, risings, belchings and hiccough. Empty belching after drinking. Nausea, as after an excess of greasy food. Nausea with inclination to vomit or vomiting from very fat food, with anxiety and pressive headache, better in open air. Nausea, with headache, anxiety, after fat food.

Abdomen - Stinging abdominal pains. Sharp stitches in left side. Grumbling and movements in abdomen. Sensation of bubbles bursting in bowels. Hysterical tympanites. Pinching in abdomen. Pressive shootings in abdomen and sides of abdomen, in left side of the hypogastrium.

Rectum - Stools white. Inefficient urging to go to stool. Evacuations often, but accomplished with difficulty, even if stool is soft. Feces of the consistence of pap, followed by tenesmus. Bilious diarrhea. Constipation following an abundant expulsion of feces. Voluptuous itching in perineum. Sensations - As if brain was constricted. As if teeth were set on edge. As if larynx were compressed. As if bubbles were forming and bursting in abdomen. As of rolling and gurgling in right scapula. As if limbs were bound or powerless.

Male - Pain in testes. Permanent erections. Frequent pollutions, on alternate nights.

Female - Suppressed menses. Food - Loss of appetite. Food tastes sour. Salt or acid taste of food. Butter and meat taste salty. Bitter taste after eating. Tobacco smoke is very disagreeable, causes heartburn and interrupts respiration. Great Taraxacum officinale chilliness after drinking creating. No thirst during fever. Thirst during sweat.

Chest - Pressure at chest. Shootings in chest and sides of chest. Jerkings in muscles.

Back - Tearing pain from ear down to neck. Sternomastoid muscle very painful to touch. Pressive jerkings and shootings in muscles of neck, throat and nape. Pressive and tensive shootings in back and loins, when lying down with obstructed respiration. Pressing, stinging in spine and sacrum with dyspnea. Vibration and quivering in right scapula.

Limbs - Muscular pains with shuddering and prickling in the muscles. Restless limbs. Limbs painful, tenderness of all limbs when touched. Tearing pains in limbs. Dull, joint pains. Fingertips cold. Pressive pains in loins. Heaviness of the legs, ameliorated by walking. Neuralgia of knee, better pressure. Jerking pain in calf (right) better on touch. Toes burning.

Sleep - Irresistible drowsiness after meals. Sleepiness in daytime and yawning while sitting. Sleepiness and going to sleep while listening to a scientific discourse. Vivid, unremembered dreams, frequent waking and tossing.

Skin - Stinging on skin. Unhealthy, pimply, sycotic skin. Eruptions over body and limbs, itching severely and appears to be a mixture of lichen and urticaria. Profuse night sweats, biting in skin with sweat.

Modalities - Better from touch. Better moving, walking, open air. Burning in throat is better by drinking. Worse while lying down, resting, at night. Worse from fat food.

Teeth - Toothache with drawing pain in carious teeth, extending to eyebrows. Pressive pains in teeth. Teeth set on edge as from acids. Flow of acid blood from decayed teeth. Blunt teeth. Hawking up of sour mucus, causing teeth to feel dull.

Tongue - Tongue, coated, mapped. Tongue covered with a white film. Tongue feels raw, comes off in patches, leaving red. sensitive spots. Tongue dry, loaded with a brown coating on waking in morning. Vertigo - Vertigo with giddiness and staggering when walking in the open air. Vertigo with unsteady gait, falls to either side. COMMENTS - The Treasury of Botany noted that “the bright-yellow flowers of Taraxacum open in the morning between 5 a.m. and 6 a.m. and close in the evening between 8 p.m. and 9 p.m. Hence this was one of the plants selected by Linneus to form his floral clock.” Cooper noted the case of an old Indian officer who, when in India, suffered from gallstones and was advised to take dandelion infusion every day. He did so and soon the symptoms left him and he remained free from them for over twenty years. Gastric and bilious attacks, especially gastric headaches. The headaches art: generally pressive. Pains in both splenic and liver regions. Jaundice with enlarged, indurated liver. Pressure in lower occiput after lying down. Debility, loss of appetite, profuse night sweats, especially when convalescing from bilious or typhoid fever. Restlessness of limbs in typhoid. Sweat between toes. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In gastric and bilious affections, Card-m.. Bry., Chel., Hydr., Lyc., Nux-v. (2) Mapped tongue, Ars., Nat-m., Merc., Ran-s. (3) Restlessness of limbs with tearing pains, Rhus-t. (4) Chel.- Tongue dry, yellowish with red edges, retains the imprint of the teeth. Epigastric pain, spreading to the lower corner of the right shoulder blade. Pressing sensation in the hepatic region. (5) Bry. - Dryness of the mucus membranes, acute, stinging pains, aggravated by movement. Intense thirst, stubborn constipation. (6) Nux-v. - Impatient, sleepy after meals, sensation of a weight in the stomach, constipation with empty urging. Compatible: Ars. - Night-sweats. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Liver - Pain in the region of liver and spleen. Liver enlarged and indurated. Sensation of heaviness in the liver region. Deficiency of the liver. Liver weakness. Chronic cholecystitis. Gallstones. Jaundice. Hepatitis with jaundice. Lungs - Cough after eating.

Kidneys - Bladder weakness. Frequent desire to urinate with copious urine. Urination with painless urging. Bedwetting during sleep.

Perspiration - Very debilitating perspiration, causing biting on the skin. Sweat on falling asleep. Profuse night sweats, mostly before midnight, when just going to sleep.

Temperature - Chill in open air. Chilliness after eating and drinking. Chilliness, shiverings, all over with pressive headache. Fingertips cold. Heat at night on waking, especially on face and hands. Heat without thirst, in face or toes.

name: Tarentula Cubensis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from tobacco smoking. Worse from cold drinks. Worse exertion. Worse at night..
constitution: Atasses. Anthrax. Bites,insect. Boils. Bubonic plague. Carbuncles. Chills. Chorea. Convulsions. Delirium. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Felon. Fever. Gangrene. Headaches. Intermittent, fever.Itching. Meningitis. Paralysis. Pruritus, vulvae. Scirrhus. Senile, ulcers.
keynote:
PHARMACY - tarent-c. Tarentula cubensis. Cuban tarantula. Mygale cubensis. Aranea peluda. N. O. Araneideae. Tincture of whole decomposed spider. Tincture of whole spider. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Atasses. Anthrax. Bites,insect. Boils. Bubonic plague.…
full:
PHARMACY - tarent-c. Tarentula cubensis. Cuban tarantula. Mygale cubensis. Aranea peluda. N. O. Araneideae. Tincture of whole decomposed spider. Tincture of whole spider. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Atasses. Anthrax. Bites,insect. Boils. Bubonic plague. Carbuncles. Chills. Chorea. Convulsions. Delirium. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Felon. Fever. Gangrene. Headaches. Intermittent, fever.Itching. Meningitis. Paralysis. Pruritus, vulvae. Scirrhus. Senile, ulcers.

HOMEOPATHIC - Tarent-c. affects the cellular tissues. It is useful in septic conditions, when incubation is slow, but further progress is rapid with alarming prostration, atrocious burning or sharp stinging pains, board like hardness of affected part and copious sweat. Intermittent septic chills. Severe types of inflammation and pain. Purplish hue and burning, stinging pains. Itching, especially about genitals. Diphtheria with intense fever and numb aching pains. Various forms of malignant suppuration. Gangrene. Bluish abscesses,painful. Felon. Carbuncles. Bubo. Bubonic plague, as a curative and preventive remedy especially during the period of invasion. Early and persistent prostration. Restless feet. Paralysis then convulsions. Tarent-c. is a remedy for the pain of death, soothes the last agony. MIND - Nervous restlessness. Sensitive to others. Anxiety. Excessive hyperesthesia. Hysteria. Lacks emotional control. Delirium due to pains. Agony of pains, compels the patient to walk on the floor for nights Keeps hands busy, picks fingers.

Head - Dull ache on top of head. Fullness in head. Headaches. Shooting pain through left eye across frontal region. Meningitis.

Stomach - Feels hard, sore. Loss of appetite, except for breakfast. Tendency to vomit.

Rectum - Diarrhea.

Back - Itches across kidney region. Female - Pruritus vulvae.

Limbs - Hands tremble, turgid with blood. Fidgety feet. Unsteady gait. Lungs - Spasmodic difficulty of breathing. Shattering cough, whooping cough.

Sleep - Drowsiness. Sleep restless, prevented by harsh cough.

Skin - Feels puffed all over. Pungent burning, stinging pains. Red spots and pimples. Purple discoloration. Carbuncles. Abscesses, where pain and inflammation predominate. “Senile ulcers.” Gangrene. Anthrax. Scirrhous of breasts.

Modalities - Better from tobacco smoking. Worse from cold drinks. Worse exertion. Worse at night.

Kidneys - Retention of urine. Urine hot, thick. Cannot hold urine on coughing.

Temperature - Pungent heat of surface. Vertigo - Dizziness after heat and hot perspiration. COMMENTS - Hering stated “The Mygale Cubensis, which may be called the Cuban Tarentula, also found in South Carolina and Texas is a larger spider of a dark brown color, less poisonous and covered with more hairs than the Tarentula Hispánica.” Tarent-c. seems to be a toxemic remedy, acting directly on the blood, and is in this way an analogue of Crot- h., Apis, Ars., etc. The bite is painless. The person is not sensible of it until next day. Then an inflamed pimple is found surrounded by a scarlet areola. From the pimple to some other part of the body a red erysipelatous line is seen, which marks the line followed by the spider over the skin after biting. The pimple swells, the inflamed areola spreads, chills and fever set in with copious sweat and retention of urine, the pimple becomes a hard, large. Exceedingly painful abscess, ending by mortification of the tissues over it and having several small openings. Discharging a thick, bloody matter containing pieces of tissue, fascia and tendons. The openings grow, run into one another, forming a large cavity. At this period the fever takes the intermittent type with evening exacerbations. In two cases in delicate children, the bite proved fatal, but the majority recover in from three to six weeks. A case of chorea in a girl of twelve was reported cured with Tarent-c. 6c. The movements were confined to the left side and occurred chiefly at night, when Tarent-c. was prescribed. Dr. Burt related the case of Don M. B. Aet. 72, good constitution, with an abscess in the back of his neck, whose burning, excruciating pain had completely banished sleep for six or seven nights. Fever, with great thirst and prostration. On examination, it was found to be anthrax, with all the accompanying train of symptoms. Burt gave Tarent-c., 6c one dose every two hours; after the second dose, the pain was greatly relieved, and that very night the patient was able to sleep through the whole night. Under the use of this remedy, the patient recovered without using any other, except Sil. to aid cicatrization. Carbuncle, even to sloughing with great prostration and diarrhea. Intermittent fever with evening exacerbation. Atrocious pains. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ars., Pyrog., Crot-h., Echi., Anthr., Bell., Apis. (2) in intermittents, Aran-d. (3) Carbuncle, Anthr., Lach., Sil. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Spinal, irritation. Spinal, sclerosis. Suffocation. Tonsillitis. Tumors. Twitching. Uterus, cancer. Uterus, neuralgia. Vertebrae, tumors. Vertigo. Violent, pains.

HOMEOPATHIC - The name tarantula covers a number of poisonous spiders, but in homeopathy, unless distinguished, it refers to Tarentula hispánica. Nunez instigated the proving and collected much outside information bearing on the action of the poison. “Tarantella” is a dance named from the city of Tarentum. “Tarantism” is a dancing mania, set up in persons bitten by the tarantula or in those who imagine themselves bitten. The cure is music and dancing. These symptoms give a keynote indication to this remedy. Affects the nerves, which are highly strung, producing remarkable nervous symptoms, hysteria with chlorosis, chorea. often reflexive from generative sphere. The heart, spine, respiration and right side are also prominently affected. Extreme restlessness, fidgety, hurried, must keep in constant motion even though walking aggravates. Music causes excitement. Rolls on ground from side to side or strikes vehemently with his feet or rolls the head and rubs it to relieve her distress. Chorea with arm symptoms. Irregular movements. Can run better than walk. Symptoms appear suddenly, with violence. Quivering, jerking, trembling, twitchings. Violent pains, neuralgias, as if thousands of needles were pricking. Joint pains. Headache with pain in uterus, throat with eye pains, face pain with stomach pain, pain in the ear with hiccough. Tickling, burning, scorching and numbness with prickling. Palliates the death pains and agony of dying process. Nervous phenomena, dysmenorrhea, spinal irritability. Bladder tenesmus. Constriction sensation. Deep septic conditions, abscess, evacuates pus rapidly. Noma. Emaciation, as if the flesh fairly fell off the bones, worse in the face. Cancer, fibrous tumors. Hysterical epilepsy. Intense sexual excitement, causing pain. Formication. Diabetes mellitus with great prostration and pain as if whole body were bruised. MIND - Adroit. Crafty, sly, cunning. Instability of intelligence. Obstinacy. Selfish and demanding. Very impatient and irritable with others. Hateful. Destructive impulses. Throws things away. Kleptomania. Desire to strike herself or others. Angry with despair. Discontented. Melancholy. Intolerant to any criticism. Averse to company, but wants someone present. Ungrateful. Conceited and deceptive behavior. Feigns fainting, insensibility. When there are no observers, there is no hysteria, when attention is directed to her. she begins to twitch. Suddenly changing moods, fancies or strength. Lacks emotional control. Erratic. Impulsive. Fits of nervous laughter then screaming. Moral depravity. Restlessness and compelled to walk. Tormenting and intense behavior. Anxious and full of fears. Erratic moods. Sometimes a sweet cheerfulness and gaiety, while at other times, anger, irritability. Quarrelsome, excitable, exhilarated or sad. Self-indulgence. Hysterical emotions. Intense sexual excitements, lasciviousness. Mania, very excitable. Sensitive to music. Dances up and down. Laughs, mocks, runs, dances, makes gestures and jokes. Cries and sings until hoarse or exhausted. Aversion to colors, black, red, yellow, green. Mental symptoms better in evening after eating. Refuses to eat. Delirium, mania, shrieking, singing, erotic mania. Stupefaction. Indisposed to talk. Sensation of being small (contrast to Aur., Plat., Stram.). Weeping, causeless, during sleep. Palliates the agony and pains of the dying process.

Head - Intense pain, as if thousands of needles were pricking into brain. Heavy pain in temples, extending to face and neck with nausea and impatience. Violent crushing headaches. Migraine, can’topen eyes, with tendency of head to incline backward. Fullness in head with throbbing carotids, better nosebleed. Burning heat in occiput with pricking and itching over whole body. Neuralgia in temples. Meningitis. Wants hair, brushed, pulledor head rubbed. As if cold water were poured on head and body.

Eyes - Itching of the eyes with thick tears. Stitching in eyes as sand or thorn. One pupil dilated, other contracted. Eyes are wide open spasmodically and staring. Photophobia. Squinting of eyes which remain open during epileptic attack.

Ears - Snapping, cracking in ears (right), with pain and hiccough. Noises, ringing as of bells, worse on waking in the morning. Singing, like a tea-kettle, in left ear.

Nose - Catarrh, dryness, burning, sneezing and bleeding, worse right side. Nosebleed better throbbing carotids and fullness in head.

Face - Acne in face since menopause. Fiery red, bloated. Expression of terror. Wrinkled. Pains in angles of lower jaw.

Mouth - Dry mouth and teeth. Tongue drawn backward, preventing speech. Pain in lower jaw, as if teeth would fall out. Grinding of teeth.

Throat - Tonsils greatly swollen, with offensive odor. Diphtheria both tonsils covered by a firm membrane, color of pearl. Vertigo - Vertigo after breakfast, with bad taste in mouth. Vertigo when fixing sight on any object. Vertigo at night, when descending stairs. Vertigo before or following epileptic attack. Vertigo, worse carrying burden on head, then spasms. Vision - Sees ghosts, faces, flashes. As if a cloud before left eye, before epileptiform fits. COMMENTS - Clarke recorded two cases of poisoning. The first was the case of a girl, three months old, who was bitten by a tarantula. She appeared at first uneasy, then exhibited dyspnea and complained. Showed signs of suffocation, vomited. She was agitated and convulsed. Music was played, movements of the limbs were set up, resulting in a profuse sweat, followed by sleep and complete recovery. Clarke also noted the case of Francis Mustek a peasant, who was bitten by a tarantula on the left hand about the middle of July as he was gathering corn. He went home with his companions but on the way fell as if struck by a stroke. Dyspnea followed and his face, hands and feet became dark. Knowing the remedy, his companions fetched musicians. When the patient heard their playing he began to revive, to sigh, to move first his feet, then his hands and then the whole body. At last getting on his feet he took to dancing violently with sighing so labored that the bystanders were almost frightened. At times he rolled himself on the ground and struck it vehemently with his feet. Two hours after the music began the blackness of his face and hands went off, he perspired freely and regained perfect health. Every succeeding year at the same season the pain and attending symptoms returned, but less violently and they could always be averted by music. But if the imminent paroxysm was not averted in time, he was found by his friends struck down as at first and was restored in the same way. Hysterical hyperesthesia. The least excitement irritates, followed by languid sadness. Great excitability of nerve endings. Fingertips are extremely sensitive. Sore and bruised feeling all over, worse moving about. Spinal irritation, slightest touch along spine causes spasmodic pain in chest and heart regions. Hypersensitive to the least touch. Neuralgias, particularly in the head, “as if thousands of needles were pricking to the brain.” Worse by noise touch, strong light. Better by rubbing head against pillow. Keynote better by rubbing. “Ends of nerves become so irritated. That some kind of friction is necessary in order to obtain relief.” Chorea (Ign., Staph.), most marked on right side. Characteristic unceasing movements, twitching, jerking, and dancing. Restlessness, particularly in the lower limbs, with desire to cry. Must keep moving about though all symptoms are worse walking. Farrington noted that “When there are no observers there is no hysteria, when attention is directed to her she begins to twitch,” and “cunning attempts to feign paroxysms of wild dancing." Mental symptoms in connection with sexual disorders. Sighing, yawning, laughing and crying. Joking and profound melancholy. Insanity. Better by music. Music at first excites then it subsequently relieves. Dark red or purplish coloration and swelling of skin and tissue. Septic boils that turn really blue and painful. Spider bites in general (Hyper., Led.). Periodicity, deep action returning annually on the date of the bite. Diphtheria tonsillitis, threatening suffocation. Apparent imminent choking. Cystitis. Septic and intermittent fevers. Constrictive headache with pain in uterus. P. C. Majumdar reported the case of a woman, 18, who had oppression of the chest, with a suffocating sensation. She had continuous jerking and movement of her hands. Foam at mouth. Complete insensibility. Profuse and delaying menses. Very sleepy. Hysterical epilepsy was diagnosed. Ign. 30c did nothing. Tarent., 200c, brought her out of the fit and restored her completely in a few minutes. C. M. Boger cured a case of irritative cough with Tarent. 30c. Mr. B.. 41, was sore all over, throat felt dry. Coughed when lying down at night and in morning after rising. Dry with tearing pain in chest. Excited by pressure of phlegm in chest. Felt short of breath for at least an hour after each coughing attack. Only better from smoking. Bad taste in the evening. Three doses cured. In Med. Ad., a case of hyperesthesia of the fingertips was mentioned. The patient, a woman, 33, could not dress herself without gloves. The irritation caused a sensation in the teeth as if set on edge by a strong acid. The pain was not in the fingers. Tarent, gave relief after Asar., Gels, and Sul-ac. had failed. Farrington related a case of typhoid in a child cured by Tarent. The child rolled its head and bit its nightgown. Apis, and Agn. improved. Tarent, slightly aggravated at first, then rapidly improved. RELATIONS - Tarent.’s action is similar to Ars. in many symptoms, therefore when Ars. seems indicated but fails, it is better to give Tarent. Antidote to: Lach. Antidotes: Puls., Mag-c., Mosch., Cupr., Chel., Gels., Bov., Carb-v. Compare: (1) Agar., Ars., Cupr., Mag. phos. (2) Kali-br. - Irritation of periphery of nerves better exercising and rubbing. (3) Chorea, Mygal.. Cimic., Agar., Stram. (4) Desire to jump, Stram., Croc., Nat-m., Stict., Asar., Agar., Hyos.. Cic. (5) Bores head in pillow, Bell. (Tarent, is more rubbing). (6) Croc. (7) As if occiput struck with a hammer, Naja. (8) Deep-in headache, Bac. (9) Extreme joy, Coff. (10) Unfortunate love, Ph-ac. (11) Ménière’s disease, ague, Chin-s. (12) Sees faces, Sulph. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Gastric symptoms, worse at onset of fever. Gastric disturbances, accompanied by pains in head, face, teeth etc. Bitter belchings, hysterical. Vomits all food eaten. Vomiting during pregnancy. Stools - Stools oily, black offensive, worse by washing head. Very dark, fetid, partly formed stools, containing much mucus, expelled with difficulty. Stools followed by smarting and burning in anus, but no tenesmus.

Abdomen - Violent burning in abdomen. Burning in hypogastrium with great weight, interferes with walking. Hepatic region painful to touch. Pain in hepatic region, with nausea and vomiting, worse before paroxysm of malaria. Sharp pain in umbilical region.

Rectum - Weakness of anal sphincter. Violent burning in abdomen and rectum. Burning pain with profuse, dark, fetid, bloody stools and violent urging. Severe constipation, not relieved by purgatives or enema. Constipation with involuntary passing of urine on coughing or any effort. Sensations - As if thousands of needles were pricking into brain. As of needles sticking into muscle of neck when touched. As of insects creeping and crawling. As if occiput were struck with a hammer. As of a hair in eye. As if lower teeth were going to fall out. As if heart turned and twisted around.

Male - Sensitive genitals. Extreme sexual excitement. Lasciviousness almost to insanity, worse sex. Prostatic ailments after masturbation. Seminal emission hot, bloody. Indolent tumors of testicles.

Female - Menses early. Profuse menstruation with frequent erotic spasms. Dysmenorrhea with very sensitive ovaries. Dysmenorrhea better during warm weather, when outdoors, worse during cold weather. Pruritus vulvae after menses. Leucorrhea alternating with bloody discharge. Leucorrhea of clear acrid, sticky lumps. Dry, hot raw, itching vulva and vagina, worse scratching. Great sexual desire. Violent nymphomania, worse sex. Sensation of motion in uterus like a fetus. Sensation of burning. Expulsion of gas from vagina. Strong bearing-down pelvic pains. Displacement of uterus. Neuralgia of uterus, with sadness and despair. Violent tearing pains in uterus. Fibroid tumors of uterus with bearingdown pains. Ovaries, sensitive to pressure. Cancer of cervix. Food - Loss of appetite. Refuses to eat. Food tastes sour. Mental symptoms better evening, after eating. Craving for sand or raw food. Craving for raw food during pregnancy. Desires highly seasoned food, salty things. Desires ashes, cuttlefish, smoking. Aversion to meat, bread. Thirst for cold water. Thirst often and for large quantities.

Chest - Panting with oppression of the chest. Sensations of oppression of chest when raising arms or lying on left side. Rheumatic pains in chest. Angina pectoris. Constitutions - Suited to nervous, hysterical patients subject to chorea disorders; to persons of foxy, mischievous and destructive tendency. Suited to chorea disorders when whole body or right arm and left leg are involved.

Heart - Diseases of heart, worse by wetting hands in cold water. Angina pectoris. Palpitations, precordial anguish. Trembling and thumping of heart as from bad news or fright. Sensations as if heart twisted and turned around. Heart takes sudden jumps. Pulse, hard infrequent, irregular. Heart suddenly ceases to beat, patient fears to die. Heart as if squeezed or compressed.

Back - Painfully sensitive spine, touch excites pains in chest, heart etc. Coccy- Tarentula hispánica godynia, better standing, worse slightest movement, touch. Tumors around vertebral column. Painfully sensitive spine.

Limbs - Multiple sclerosis with trembling. Chorea movements. Twitching and jerking. Extraordinary contractions and movements. Legs restless, impulse to walk. Can run better than walk. Numbness of legs. Weak legs, cannot plant them firmly, do not obey. Y awning with uneasiness of legs, must move them constantly. Festination. Kneeling difficult. Soles itching. Cold, moist feet and hands. Restless arms, keeps hands busy, picks fingers. Lungs - Attacks of suffocation, with crying, screaming and restlessness, must have fresh air, worse coughing. Panting with oppression of the chest. Cough when expectorating, gagging, fatiguing. Cough worse after sex, noise, better smoking.

Sleep - Sleepless before midnight from excitement. Sad dreams, with weeping.

Skin - Purplish skin. Ecchymosed spots. Cold spots or as of a cold matter flowing or dropping on part. Boils, burning and painful. Carbuncle. Deep abscesses. Helps evacuation of pus. Dry eczema (Ars., Sulph.). Miliary eruptions and furuncles, with diabetes. Itching, as of insects creeping and crawling.

Modalities - Better open air, sun. Better bright colors. Better from music. Better pressure, rubbing affected parts. Better relaxation. Better warm water, sweating, smoking. Better riding in a carriage. Motion improves headache but aggravates uterine pains and pains in coccyx. Worse from rest, touch, contact, motion. Worse noises. Worse seeing others in trouble. Worse damp, cold, washing head or putting hands in cold water. Worse after menses. Worse at night, evening. Worse periodically, yearly, at the same hour. Worse after sex: sadness, difficult respiration, cough, and general weakness specifically increased by sexual excitement.

Kidneys - Foul urine with sandy sediment. Incontinence on laughing, coughing etc. Diabetes mellitus. Polyuria with violent pains in lumbar region and paralysis of lower limbs.

Bladder - Bladder seems swollen and hard, during cystitis. Pains in region of bladder. Very painful, frequent urination, worse at night. Incontinence when coughing, laughing, or making any effort whatever. Urine foul, with sandy sediment. Causations - Ill effects of unrequited love, bad news, scolding, punishment, falls, sepsis.

Perspiration - Profuse excoriating sweat. Copious perspiration, worse after excitement.

Temperature - Alternate chill and heat. General heat with cold feet. Septic fever. Sweat profuse, excoriating. Intense chill all over before convulsions.

HOMEOPATHIC - Found in grapes, pineapple, sorrel and other fruits. Tart-ac. is an anti-scor- butic anti-septic, stimulating the mucus and salivary secretions. Extreme weakness. In evening feels very tired, can scarcely drag himself along. General bruised sensation, especially of lower limbs. Convulsions just before death.

Face - Face instantly became red as fire and having exclaimed that he was poisoned, became speechless, died on tenth day (drank 2 oz. in solution). Lips, turn brown and black on their inner edges. Constant dryness of lips, must moisten them continually. Burning of lips. Food - Excessive, very urgent thirst.

Mouth - Teeth set on edge. Brown and dry tongue. Taste, pasty in morning, ceases on eating.

Throat - Hoarseness and scraping in larynx. Burning sensation in throat and stomach as if on fire. Vertigo - Confusion in head, dizziness. COMMENTS - A proving by Nenning and some poisonings have furnished the pathogenesis of Tart-ac. One of the most marked symptoms was intense burning in throat and stomach, feeling “as if on fire.” Tongue brown and dry. Almost constant vomiting, vomited matter of deep green color. Feces coffee-ground color. Dullness andlassitude. Paralytic debility. “Weakness in the evening, can scarcely drag himself along.” Difficult respiration. Great weakness with diarrhea with dry and brown tongue. “Tearing pain on the soles of the feet, near the heel, which prevents him putting his foot on the ground after luncheon” (Phyt.). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Dyspepsia with copious secretion of mucus. Belchings. Nausea. Vomiting is repeated and almost continuous. Continued vomiting with burning in throat and stomach. Vomited deep green matter.

Abdomen - Pain around umbilicus and region of loins. Pinching below navel with emission of flatulence, cold feeling in abdomen.

Rectum - Many stools during night. Stools like color of coffee grounds.

Heart - Very weak action of the heart. Feeble pulse.

Limbs - Sharp pain in region of loins. Paralysis of thighs and legs. Tearing pains at soles, near the heel, which prevents him setting his foot on the ground after luncheon. Lungs - Breathing accelerated, then laborious and slow.

Sleep - Frequent yawning and stretching.

Modalities - Better in open air. Pasty taste is better after eating.

Temperature - General cold feeling, evening in bed.

CLINICAL - Allergic reactions. Anemia. Arthritis. Breast, cancer. Cancer. Chemotherapy, effects. Chills. Diarrhea. Dyspnea. Edema. Fatigue. Fever. Hair loss. Hypersensitivity. Hypotension. Hives. Kaposi’s sarcoma. Liver problems. Lung, cancer. Lung, disorders. Mouth, sores. Nail, discoloration. Nausea. Ovarian, cancer. Peripheral neuropathy. Radiation, effects. Rheumatism. Stomach, disorders. Skin, disorders. Tumors. Ulcers. Vertigo. Vomiting. Weight, gain.

HERBAL - The Taxol compound belongs to a family of compounds called Taxanes that are unique to the Yew species. During the Taxol studies, several yew taxanes in addition to the Taxol tanane were found to exert anti-cancer properties. Other Pacific Yew taxanes (also called diterpenes) are known by various names such as baccatin 111, brevitaxin, brevifoliol andcephalomannine, as well as variations of taxol compounds. Taxol is only one of hundreds of organic compounds in Taxus brevifolia. Taxol was originally approved for use as a treatment for ovarian cancer, ongoing research was showing its efficacy in other arenas such as cancers of the lung, breast, bladder, prostate, testes, esophagus, head and neck, cervix, and endometrium. Also used to treat Kaposi’s sarcoma and melanoma.

HOMEOPATHIC - The homeopathic indications for prescribing Taxol can be determined from the side effects of Taxol cancer therapy. Homeopathic potencies of Taxol maybe given to lessen the toxic side effects of the treatment. The following Taxol side effects are common for patients taking Taxol: Low blood counts. White and red blood cells and platelets may become decreased. Hair loss. Pain in the joints and muscles. Peripheral neuropathy, numbness and tingling of the hands and feet. Nausea and vomiting. Diar- rhea. Mouth sores. Hypersensitivity reaction with fever, facial flushing, chills, shortness of breath, or hives after Taxol is given. The following are less common side effects for patients receiving Taxol: Swelling of the feet or ankles (edema) .Liver problems. Low blood pressure. Darkening of the skin where previous radiation treatment has been given. Nail changes, discoloration of nail beds. Fever, chills. Shortness of breath, wheezing, difficulty breathing, closing up of the throat, swelling of facial features, hives. Allergic reaction. Redness or pain at the site of injection. Nausea. Vomiting. Diarrhea. Unusual bleeding or bruising. Black or tarry stools. Blood in stools or urine Extreme fatigue. Mouth sores, painful redness, swelling or ulcers. Yellowing of the skin or eyes. Swelling of the feet or ankles. Sudden weight gain. Signs of infection such as redness or swelling, pain on swallowing, coughing up mucus, or painful urination. RELATIONS - Compare: Taxus brevifolia (Pacific Yew) belongs to the botanical family Taxaceae, which is a small family with one main genus - Taxus. Species include Taxus baccata (European Yew), Taxus cuspidate (Japanese Yew), Taxus globosa (Mexican Yew) and Taxus canadensis (Canadian Yew). REFERENCES - Murphy.
