PHARMACY - thea. Thea sinensis. Chinese tea. Camellia thea. N. O. Temstromiaceae, Theaceae. Tincture or infusion of dried leaves and flowers. Trituration of Theine. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Delirium, tremens. Mania. Homicidal. Insanity. Insomnia. Kidney, disorders. Mania. Megrim. Nervousness. Neuralgias. Paralysis. Sleeplessness. Suicidal.

HERBAL - Tea contains an alkaloid, Thein, which is considered by some identical with caffeine, and both tea and coffee are used to stimulate the jaded faculties. The stimulation will enable persons to endure fatigue and get more enjoyment out of themselves than they could obtain by mere food. Coffee and tea are different in their effects though they may be alike in their chemistry. The after-effect of all stimulation is reaction, unless it is kept off by a repetition of the stimulant as the effect of the last dose wears off. The sign that the first dose of tea is wearing off is a nervous, restless, depressed, ill- tempered state, which is visible in persons who rely on tea, at about 5 p.m.

HOMEOPATHIC - Neuralgia and insomnia. All-gone, sinking sensation at the epigastrium. Nervous sleeplessness, heart troubles, palpitations and dyspepsia of old tea-drinkers. Sensitive kidneys. Sick head- aches. Allen noted it was antidotal to Tab. MIND - Nervousness and want of confidence. Great nervous excitability with exaltation of intellectual faculties. Ill-humored. Peevish. Disposition to quarrel at the most harmless speech. Nocturnal fright, suicidal thoughts. Temporary mental exaltation. Delirium with ecstasy, laughed incessantly, talked in rhyme. Delirium tremens. Mania. Suicidal and homicidal. Impulses to kill. Impulse to jump out of the window.

Head - Rush of blood to head. Sick headache radiating from one point. Sleepless and restless. Hallucinations of hearing. Cold damp feeling at back of head. Scalp tender can scarcely comb hair.

Eyes - Eyes are unusually bright. Dilated pupils. Neuralgia of eyes. Sight is dim, dark before eyes, fiery lines, sparks.

Ears - Neuralgic pains in cartilage of ears. Roaring in ears. Hallucinations of hearing.

Nose - Dryness, soreness of nose. Sensation at root of nose as if nosebleed would occur. Nosebleed before menses.

Face - Wild, distressed expression. Face is pale, with congested redness, flushed.

Mouth - Bitter taste in mouth. Much viscid saliva. Whole mouth cavity dry and sensitive. Tongue clean and pale. Tongue red, blistered, painful as if scalded. Teeth frequently decayed.

Throat - Scraping in larynx. Hoarseness. Diphtheria sore throat. Painless swelling of mucus membrane. Uneasy feeling in pharynx, as if obstructed by a foreign body. Vertigo - Vertigo with darkness before eyes, sudden in open air. COMMENTS - The symptoms are made up of observed effects of overdosing and some direct provings. A woman who was addicted to dri nking tea showed very pronounced delirium tremens indistinguishable from that caused by alcohol, though there was no alcoholism in the case. Another woman, who kept a pot of tea boiling on the stove and drank several bowls every day, developed both suicidal and homicidal mania, impulse tojump out of the window, to cut her baby’s throat or throw it downstairs. Thea 100,000c, Fincke, cured. A man who had been many years in the East and was used to one-story houses, on his return to the West had a curious impulse tojump out of the window, which he traced to tea-drinking and which disappeared when he left it off. Teste noted that the homicidal impulse appeared in the dreams of one prover, who was so far from being horrified by his dreammurders that he even took pleasure in them after awaking. The talkativeness of Thea, is one of its chief allurements. Among tea-tasters, who do not drink the tea they taste, but only hold it in the mouth a short time, yet long enough for the mouth to absorb some, there is sometimes developed what is known as tea-tasters’ paralysis, affecting mostly the lower limbs with loss of sensation of both upper and lower. A man, after drinking tea, had pain in his epigastrium going through to his back with a feeling as if he wanted to be sick and could not, better sitting down and stretching out. Thuj. 30c cured. Guernsey gave these as indications for Thea, “Nervous sleeplessness, heart troubles, of old tea-drinkers, palpitations of the heart, can’t lie down.” RELATIONS -Antidote: Thuj., Ferr., Kali-hp. - Material dosesfortea-taster’scoughAnridoted by: Beer.

Stomach - A sinking sensation at the epigastrium. Faint, gone feeling (Sep., Hydr., Olean.). Weakness about stomach. Sudden production of wind in large quantities. Nausea, and vomiting after eating. Vomits bile, when pain at its height.

Abdomen - Borborygmi. After lunch, stitch below ribs in paroxysms. Intestines relaxed. Liability to hernia.

Rectum - Swelling of lower end of rectum, with slight itching. Chronic relaxed bowels. worse by beer, better by port wine. Constipation. Sensations - As if on the verge of fainting. As if a foreign body in throat. As if the stomach hung down relaxed in the body like an empty bag. As if the weight of a sheet on the feet would crush the toes. Cold sensations are prominent, cold, damp feeling at back of head with pain spreading thence to eyes, also dryness and swelling of mucus membrane.

Male - Erections. Unnatural excitement.

Female - Soreness and tenderness in ovaries. Menses delayed, scanty with severe cramp-like pains. Uterine bearing down from beginning to end of period. Food - Very hungry, but little satisfies. Thirst, but every mouthful of cold water affects the head like a shock. Craves acids, lemons.

Chest - Oppressed and constricted. Fluttering in left side and feeling of suffocation.

Heart - Anxious oppression. Precordial distress. Palpitation, unable to lie on left side. Fluttering. Pulse rapid, irregular Thea sinensis intermittent.

Limbs - Paralyzed numbness of limbs. Joints of hands and feet tender. Nervous excitability in wrists, hands, and feet. Hand trembled violently. Restlessness of feet. Neuralgic pains in outer hamstrings. Sensation as if the weight of a sheet even would crush toes. Lungs - Edema of respiratory tract. Breathing increased in frequency and amplitude. Breathlessness on least exertion. Paroxysm of asphyxia. Cough is dry, severe and bloody expectoration.

Sleep - Sleepy in daytime, sleepiness at night with vascular excitement and restlessness and dry skin. Horrible dreams cause no horror.

Skin - Skin dry as if pores obstructed. Skin of fingertips peels from excessive dryness. Eruption of red, indolent pimples. Itching, crawling, prickling in different parts.

Modalities - Better warmth, warm bath, applying hand or warm clothes to occiput. Worse at night, from cold water, walking in open air. Worse after meals.

Compare - (1) Gone, faint feeling, sick-headache radiating from one point and pain in left ovary, Sep. (2) Averse to work, especially writing, Hydr. (3) Relaxed feeling in stomach. Ip. (4) Desire for acids, Verat., Sulph., Ant-c., Phos., Sabin. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Kidneys - Very marked increase of urine. Must pass water immediately after drinking tea.

Temperature - Intense coldness passing over whole head. Lowered temperature. Hands and face cold as marble. Beaded with chilly moisture. Excessive internal heat with flushes of heat on the surface, coming and going quickly. Disposition to perspire.

full:
PHARMACY - ther. Theridion curassavicum. Orange spider. Latrodectuscurassavicus. N. O. Arachnida. West- Indies. Tincture of the whole spider. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Anthrax, sheep. Bone, disorders. Decay. Menopause. Coughs. Dysmenorrhea. Eye-teeth, pains. Fainting. Headaches. Hysteria. Liver, disorder, abscess. Marasmus. Ménière’s disease. Nausea. Necrosis. Nose, catarrh. Ozaena. Photophobia. Pregnancy, sickness. Rickets. Scrofulosis. Seasickness. Spinal, irritation. Tetanus. Toothache. Tuberculosis. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ther. was introduced and proved by Hering in 1832. The spider is found in the West Indies, chiefly in the island of Curacao. It is about the size of a cherry-stone and is found on orange-trees. It is velvety black when young with antero-posterior lines composed of white dots, on the posterior of the body there are three orange-red spots and on the belly a large square yellow spot. The spider is very poisonous. It produces a highly sensitive, nervous condition with weakness, trembling, coldness, anxiety, faintness and easily excited cold sweat. Venom produces hypersensitiveness of the ***nerves. Sensitive to noise, which penetrates the body. It affects the teeth, causes nausea, chills and pains all over, strikes the painful parts etc. Nervous hyperesthesia. Noises seem to strike on painful spots over the body. Affinity for the tubercular diathesis. Tuberculosis, stitch high up in left apex (Anthr.). Where the indicated remedy does not hold long. Rickets, decay, necrosis. Vertigo, sick headache, peculiar pain around heart region, tuberculosis florida, and scrofula. Spinal irritation. Decay and necrosis of the bones. Bones feel broken. Rickets. Burning pains. Water feels too cold. Bounding internally, as of a child. Sense of duality. Effects of sunstroke. Hysteria during puberty and at menopause. Infantile atrophy, glands enlarged with marasmus. Nodes on various parts especially buttocks. Seasickness. Left side most affected. MIND - Restless, finds pleasure in nothing. Time passes too quickly. Sensitive to slightest noise. Startled by least thing. Confusion of mind, worse laughing. Insanity during menopause. Hysteria. Talkativeness and hilarity. Wantofself confidence. Aversion to work. Joyful during headache. Depression during headache. Weeping from toothache. Feels and looks as if dying, but hears and understands all that is said.

Head - Head internally hot, oppressed and heavy. Head feels thick, thinks it belongs to another, that she can lift it off or she would like to remove it. Migraine. Headache, felt during sleep, worse jarring, with nausea and vomiting, at menopause. Headache worse after stool. Cannot lie down with headache. Pain worse anyone walking over floor.

Eyes - Glittering vision, on stooping. Luminous vibrations before eyes. Blurred vision. Sensitive to light. Pressure behind eyeballs. Throbbing over left eye.

Ears - Least noise, even sound penetrates her whole body, especially teeth. Rushing in both ears like a waterfall.

Nose - Pain over root of nose. Ozaena. Chronic catarrh, yellow-green, thick offensive, discharge. Discharge is yellowish and offensive. Post-nasal catarrh (Puls., Thuj.). Sensations - As if her head was another strange head. As if vertex did not belong to her. Like a pressing pain in root of nose and about ears. As of a veil before eyes. As if something in esophagus were slipping towards epigastrium. Like labor pains in lower abdomen. As if a child were bounding in body. As if bones were broken and would fall asunder. As if dying.

Face - Pale. Jaws immovable in the morning.

Mouth - Mouth feels furred, benumbed. ***Froth before the mouth with shaking chill. Teeth feel as if cold water is too cold. Bites tip of tongue during sleep. Lockjaw, morning on waking. Remains open involuntarily, cannot close.

Stomach - Seasickness. Nausea and vomiting when closing eyes and on motion (Tab.). Nausea worse least motion, looking steadily at one object from noise. Nausea and retching better drinking warm water.

Abdomen - Violent burning in liver region. Abscess of liver. Pain in the groins after sex, motion and drawing up the limbs. Stinging pain on left side over anterior aspect of spleen.

Male - Gonorrhea. Prostate enlarged, sense of a lump and heaviness in perineum, worse at even step. Seminal emission during afternoon sleep.

Female - Hysteria during puberty, at menopause. Menses suppressed. Food - Constant desire to eat and drink but knows not for what. Craves oranges and bananas, acid fruits and drinks, wine, tobacco smoke.

Chest - Stitches high up in chest, back through apex of left lung. Pain in upper left chest (Myrt., Pix., Anis.). Pain in left floating ribs. Pinching in left pectoral muscle. Constitutions - Tubercular diathesis.

Heart - Cardiac anxiety and pain. Anxiety about the heart, sharp pain radiates to arm and left shoulder. Pulse slow with vertigo.

Back - Stinging pains. Spine is sensitive to pressure and jar, sits sideways in a chair to avoid pressure. Sensitiveness between vertebra. Causations - Seasickness. Washing clothes. Riding.

Limbs - Burning in upper arm. Restless feeling in hands, wrings them. Stinging from elbow to shoulder. Lies or sits with feet crossed, cannot uncross them. Lungs - Cough, jerks body together, head forward and knees upward. Too much air seems to enter the chest. Breathing difficult going up and down stairs, hysteria. Tuberculosis.

Skin - Stinging, stabs everywhere. Itching sensations. Sensitive skin on the thighs.

Modalities - Better from rest in horizontal position. Warm water improves nausea and retching. Warmth improves. Worse touch, pressurerai, leftside. Worseleastmotion, exertion, stooping, rising, walking, going up or down stairs. Worse sex, particularly groin pain. Worse on shipboard, riding in carriage. Worse from noise. Worse from cold, washing clothes, sunstroke. Worse closing eyes.

Kidneys - Increased urination, at night, does not pass much during day.

Temperature - Shaking chill with foam at mouth. Internal coldness. Cold sweat easily excited. Vertigo - Faints after washing clothes. Vertigo with nausea, worse stooping, kneeling. Vertigo with nausea and vomiting on least motion, worse when closing eyes. COMMENTS - Grimmer stated. “The orange spider poison can cure when indicated on the totality of its symptoms. Decay of bones, abscesses and cancer of the liver and lungs. It acts profoundly on the nervous system, producing extreme sensitivity to noise the vibration penetrating to the teeth.” Keynotes extreme sensitiveness to noise, worse by least noise, “sounds penetrate the teeth.” The sensitiveness extends to vibrations of any kind, jar of a step, riding in a carriage or in a boat. “Worse closing eyes,” especially in vertigo and symptoms of the head and stomach. Seasickness or sickness of pregnancy. Severe headaches, affecting the eyes, especially the left. The ears are highly sensitive. Intoler ance of light. Frequent cough, convulsive, head spasmodically jerked forward, knees jerked up to abdomen. Hallucinations of sight and hearing, luminous vibrations and rushing sounds. A kind of intoxication is induced, hilarity, talkativeness. “Time passes too slowly.” Burning pains and itching are common and a stitch high up in apex of left chest has proved a guiding symptom for Ther. in the cure of cases of tuberculosis. “Burning in liver region” led to the cure of abscess and even cancer of that organ. H. C. Allen noted it for spinal irritation and disease of the spine and other bones. Decay, necrosis and scrofulous disease of bones have all been cured with it. “In scrofulosis when the best remedies fail to relieve.” Chackravarti related a case of headache cured with Ther. Mr. B., 35, well built of bilious temperament, had for three months severe headache with nausea and vomiting like seasickness and shaking chills. Dullness and fullness in the head with throbbing beginning in occiput, preceded by flickering before the eyes. Head felt large and heavy. The pains began in the morning increase during the day and last until evening. Excessive irritation with loss of sustaining power. Worse from least overwork and motion, better by keeping quiet in horizontal position. Constipation, stools hard, small, dry. Ther. 3x was given, one drop in water twice daily. The pain was much better the next day and was gone in less than a week. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Aeon, (sensitiveness to noises), Mosch, (nausea), Graph, (more chronic effects). Follows well: Sulph., Calc., Lyc. (scrofula). Compare: (1) Aran- d. and Spiders generally. (2) Hemicrania worse closing eyes, worse noise, Sep. (But Sep. worse from noise is less intense). (3) Vertigo and faintness on closing eyes, Lach. (4) Headache, nervousness, hysteria. Tarent. (5) Stooping down, violent stitch high up in left chest, thence to back, Myrt-c. through to left scapula. (6) Time passes too quickly (too slowly Cann-i., Arg- n., Nux-m.). (7) Vertigo on closing eyes, Lach., Thuj. (on opening them, Tab., on looking up, Puls. Sil.). (8) Headache, worse lying down, Lach. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer. Phatak.

Dupuytren’s, contracture. Ectropion. Emphysema. Fibroids. Frozen, shoulder. Glands, enlarged. Glands, indurated. Indigestion. Indurations. Keloids. Lupus. Lymphatic glands, enlarged. Ménière’s disease. Old, age. Otitis, media. Otosclerosis. Painful, adhesions. Premature, aging. Rectum, stricture. Scar, tissue. Scleroderma. Senile, dementia. Stiffness. Strictures. Tabes dorsalis. Tennis, elbow. Tinnitus. Tumors. Urticaria. Uterine, tumors. Wounds.

HERBAL - Thiosinaminum belongs to the same chemical group as Urea. The colorless, bitter crystals are soluble in water, alcohol and ether.

HOMEOPATHIC - Thiosin. has been effective in curing adhesions, scars, lupus and enlarged lymphatic glands. It’s a dissolvent, externally and internally, for dissolving scar tissue, keloids. It has been used for tumors, enlarged glands, lupus, strictures, adhesions. Inflamed, swollen glands, adenitis. Ectropion, opacities of cornea, cataract, ankylosis, fibroids, scleroderma. Noises in ear. Tinnitus aurium, deafness. Gastric, vesicle and rectal crises. Strictures of rectum. Tumors of the uterus appendages. For tabes dorsalis, improving the lightning pains. Sensation of heat and burning in affected parts. Increases body weight and reduces glandular swellings. Dr. A. S. Hard suggested Thiosin. for retarding old age. MIND - Depression of spirits. Aversion to consolation. Moody, alternating moods. Alzheimer's disease. Senile dementia.

Eyes - Cataract of the lens or comea. Stricture of the lachrymal duct.

Ears - Ménière’s syndrome, vertigo. Noises in ear. Tinnitus caused by fibrous bands. Formation of fibrous bands impeding free movement of the ossicles. Otosclerosis. Suppurative otitis media. Thickened eardrum. Catarrhal deafness with scar thickenings. Deafness due to some fibrous change in the nerve. Adhesions of the Eustachian tube. Eustachian tube catarrh.

Nose - Allergies.

Stomach - Indigestion, flatulence of stomach and bowels, worse after eating. Pyloric stenosis. Stricture of esophagus. Vertigo- Arteriosclerotic vertigo. Ménière’s syndrome, vertigo. COMMENTS - The mustard seeds of Sin-n. are of a reddish-brown color. Mixed with those of Sin-a., they are crushed between rollers and subsequently powdered and sifted at least twice. A fixed oil is obtained by pressure from the residue left on the sieve. The powdered mustard is mixed with a considerable quantity of wheaten flour and a small quantity of turmeric powder. The Treasury of Botany noted that “The term ‘flour of mustard’ is not quite accurate, as the mustard seeds themselves contain little or no starchy material. The chemical ingredients are somewhat complex. Among them are a peculiar acid called Myronic acid, noticeable as containing a large proportion of Sulphur. When mixed with water and a peculiar substance called Myrosine, (analogous to albumen), also found in mustard seeds, yields a volatile Oil of Mustard. “This has no separate existence in the seeds, but is formed artificially in the manner just stated. This oil is very acrid and has been used as a rubefacient. The fixed oil before mentioned as existing in the seed itself has little or no acridity and has been used as a purgative and vermifuge.” Scar tissue and adhesions. Ringing in the ears. Tinnitus or deafness in elderly people from otosclerosis. The bones of the ears get calcium deposits. Scarred eardrums or eardrums that thicken and cause hearing difficulties. Chronic ruptured eardrums in children (Calen, acutely). Ménière’s disease Thiosinaminum (Chin-s.). Vertigo. Opacities of the cornea, cataracts. Torn ligaments, especially in the shoulder. Painful adhesions affecting mobility of a joint. Internal adhesions of the uterus, adhesions after surgery. Strictures of the urethra and painful urination. Dr. McCullogh found that it exerts a marked beneficial action on ear diseases accompanied by the formation of new connective tissue. He believed that this beneficial action was due to an increased pliability of this tissue. Its administration should always be accompanied by mechanical measures; better and more prompt results may be obtained in recent cases. McCullogh also noted a beneficial action on vertigo and better results may be obtained with it in the relief of tinnitus aurium than with any drug used previously. C. H. Pennoyer related the case of Mrs. C., 69, who had been ill for several years with gastric distress, sciatica, pains in hips down to knees, worse by motion. She had indigestion, flatulence of stomach and bowels, worse after eating. Pain in back. Inability to walk, much perspiration, depression of spirits and subnormal temperature. Her father had died at 69 of stomach trouble, mother at 58 of stricture of the bowel. Examination showed stricture of the rectum two inches above the anus, there being a tense fibrous band forming a ring opening, which would not admit the index finger. Bougies and mechanical measures failed to relieve. Weakness was so great, the patient would faint at stool. Nutrition improved under general treatment, but the local condition was unchanged. A year later the stricture was slightly increased. Thiosin. was then given, 2 grains, twice daily. The following year the patient was found to be much improved. Examination showed that the scar band had gone, the speculum could be introduced and the mucus membrane was normal in appearance, though not as elastic as a normal rectum should be. W. Spencer applied this property of ***resolving scar tissues in cases of tinnitus aurium “where the ossicles are bound down and the function of the tympanic cavity so much impaired by fibrous bands or adhesions.” In such cases he had encouraging success. Enlarged lymphatic glands have been reduced in the same way. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sil., Calen., Sinapis and Cruciferae. (2) Uterine tumors, Thlaspi. (3) Diuresis - also chemical. (4) Urea. Lup., Tub. (5) Scars. Sil., Graph., Fl-ac. (6) Affections of rectum, Nit-ac., Graph., Scirr. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer. Murphy. Phatak.

Abdomen - Flatulence. Internal adhesions after surgery, after hysterectomy, etc. Intestinal strictures.

Rectum - Stricture of rectum.

Female - Painful uterine adhesions, pelvic inflammation. Uterine tumors. Infertility- Food - Increased appetite.

Back - Tom ligaments in the shoulder. Frozen shoulder.

Skin - Wounds that are slow to heal. Wounds that form a lot of scar tissue. Scar tissues. Granulations, scars, keloids after burns, wounds. Inelasticity of the skin. Indurations. Urticaria. Lupus.

Kidneys - Strictures of the urethra and painful urination. Urine increased in quantity, no albumen or formed elements. Increased urination at night. ***Limbs - Locomotor ataxia. Stiffness of joints. Lungs - Accelerated respiration. Emphysema.

PHARMACY - thlaspi. Thlaspi bursa pas- toris. Shepherd’s purse. Bursa pastoris. Capsella bursa pastoris. N. O. Cruciferae. Tincture of fresh flowering plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

Liver, disorders. Metrorrhagia. Miscarriage. Nausea. Nosebleed. Ranula. Strangury. Urethritis. Uric acid, diathesis. Uterine, bleeding. Uterus, cancer. Whitlow.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany noted that Thlaspi is “A native of Europe, it has accompanied Europeans in all their migrations and established itself wherever they have settled to until the soil.” It does not refuse to grow in the poorest soils, but it luxuriates in the richest. Burnett noticed that it flourished best in the neighborhood of dunghills and the odor of the tincture is much suggestive thereof. Some have seen in the seed-vessel the signature of the shape of the uterus. Burnett found in it an organ remedy of vast importance. He said the tincture is the best thing to give for menses that have been checked, for uterine hemorrhages he preferred the potencies. Thlaspi bursa pastoris HOMEOPATHIC - Hemorrhagic and uric acid diathesis. Hemorrhages are profuse, periodic, blood dark, clotted. Uterine hemorrhage with cramps and expulsion of clots. Hemorrhage from uterine fibroid with aching in back or general bruised soreness. Bleeding fibroids. Bleeding between the menses. Tendencies to miscarriage. Bleeding at ovulation or postpartum hemorrhage of dark, red, oozing blood (Ham.). Passive bleeding. Hemorrhage with burning or a mild bladder problem. Uterine hemorrhages concomitant with bladder infections. Albuminuria during pregnancy. Kidney and bladder irritation. Kidney stone formation (Sars., Lyc.). Chronic cystitis. Craves buttermilk. The toes are affected along with cramping pain in stomach. Chronic neuralgia. Aching between scapulae. MIND - Impulse to walk far. Restless, goes from room to room. Agony because of pains. Spells of causeless weeping. Stupefied and dull, as if she had not slept enough.

Head - Headache, with great fullness. Frontal pain, worse toward evening. Pain from above eyes up over head to nape. Scaly eruption behind ears. Sharp pain over right eye, drawing eye upwards, behind right eye. Heaviness over eyes. Pressing pain in forehead. Stupefying pressing pain in forehead. Violent headache, lasting all night.

Eyes - Eyes puffy. Dusky eyes, shiny and with dilated pupils. Dull ache behind eyes on awaking in the morning with aching in nape. Blurred vision. Sensation as if eyes are swollen, as if the ball was pressed inward. Sensation as of dust in eyes, worse after sewing or using eyes.

Ears - Deafness and pain in left ear. Sensation as if something pushing in right ear. Spasmodic drawing from right ear to right lower jaw. Dry eruptions behind the ears. Small vesicles, with yellow points, above right ear. Scaly eruptions behind ears, with fissures in the fold. Sensation as of an insect entering the left ear, making buzzing noise, relieved by boring in ear with fingers.

Nose - Dull pain at root of nose. Gnawing pain in nasal bones. Soreness in nose, with tenderness on touch. Dryness of nose, preceded by sensations of bleeding. Bruised feeling each side of bridge, with bleeding from nose. Frequent nosebleeds. Nosebleed after nasal operations. Especially passive hemorrhage. Free discharge of blood and mucus from left nostril.

Face - Eyes and face puffy. Face feels parched and dry. Miserable countenance.

Mouth - Bitter, slimy taste with dryness of mouth. Taste like bad eggs. Scratchy feeling in the palate. Mouth feels raw, as if from smoking strong tobacco. Mouth cracked in right corner and sore. Upper lip cracked. Teeth sore on closing jaws. Gums sore, neuralgic feeling in teeth.

Throat - Hoarse in morning with slight sore throat. Soreness of upper part of throat. Swelling of throat and face, worse left side. Tonsils swollen. Dry throat on swallowing. Dryness of fauces, with sensation of con- striction of the throat. Dry sensation and scraping. Violent sore throat. Sensation as if the throat was laced together.

Stomach - Sick, faint feeling in stomach. Emptiness feeling in stomach. Cramping pain in stomach, toes hurt as well as stomach. Flatulence. Sour rising like heartburn. Attacks of nausea. Nausea so severe, could hardly raise head from pillow. Tobacco smoke, of which she was fond, now nauseates her. Nausea in the forenoon. Nausea with loathing of food. Vomited brown, sourish blood in the afternoon. Vomiting and purging, with great debility.

Abdomen - Flatulence. Pain between end of sternum and umbilicus like needles or an electric shock. Cramping pain, better bending over. Bloated after eating, with loud emissions of flatus; bowels feel as if drawn down and out.

Rectum - Passage of blood. Diarrhea mushy, brown, dark, urgent, and sometimes with nausea. Diarrhea yellowish color. Constipation. Slow and difficult stool. Obstinate slow stool with severe pressure and urging without effect. Hard, difficult, dry stool, leaving anus sore. Bleeding after hard stool. Troublesome itching and protrusion of hemorrhoids. Sensations - Sensation as of needles or shocks between end of sternum and umbilicus. As if neck and left shoulder would break with pain.

Male - Spermatic cord sensitive to concussion of walking or riding. Stitching in penis, running through to anus. Soreness of prepuce with intense itching or cold sensation (Agar.).

Female - Menses bright red and profuse. Menses too frequent and copious. Every alternate period very profuse. Menstrual blood stains indelibly. Leucorrhea before and after menses, bloody, dark offensive. Leucorrhea stains indelibly, smells foul, excites itching. Scarcely recovers from one period before another begins. Metrorrhagia. Cutting pain from side to side across pubes, worse by standing. Sore pain in uterus on rising. Uterine bleeding with violent uterine colic. Uterine fibroids with cramps and expulsion of clots. Sexual excitement. Food - Aversion to the sight of food. Aversion to potatoes. Craves buttermilk, juicy fruits. Oat cakes are eaten with a relish. Desire for bread and butter, which does not taste good. Nausea better after strawberries.

Chest - Pulsative pain in left chest. Pain, uneasiness, and pressure behind the sternum.

Heart - Feels large and sore, then throb- bings go up into back of neck. Stitching pains at the apex. Palpitations worse in the morning in bed. Palpitation ending with cough. Pain left side of apex.

Back - Continued pain in small of back. Morning backache. Wakes with violent pain between the shoulders. Weakness between scapula. Weakness between shoulders on rising. Breasts - Milky water from right nipple. Shooting pains in right breast. Causations - Suppression of hemorrhages or vaginal discharges.

Limbs - Weariness in lower limbs, can hardly stand. Drawing pain in left thigh like gout. Severe pain and stiffness in right knee cap. Tearing, gouty pains left leg, worse in forenoon. Strained pain in right shoulder. Gouty pain in arm. Tearing, gnawing pain from elbow to throat. Rheumatic pain in left arm and shoulder blade, extending to throat. Hands tremble when holding anything. Swelling of veins of hand and arm. Tearing, wrenching pain in left wrist. Redness around root of nails. Lame feeling in right forefinger. Pain in the periosteum.

Sleep - Restless tossing about. Frequent wakening. Sleeplessness. Sleepy after eating or falls asleep while eating. Confused and unpleasant dreams when asleep.

Skin - Skin dry, hot, even to burning.

Modalities - Better bending over. Better cold bathing, dampness, Better open air, rapid motion. Worse every other month. Worse toward night. Worse suppression of hemorrhages or vaginal discharges.

Tongue - Tongue and palate feel as if scalded. Ranula, caused enlargement of submaxillary duct. Tongue white, coated. Taste like bad eggs. Vertigo - Vertigo with sensation as if drunk. Dizziness in the forehead, like seasickness. Vertigo, worse rising. COMMENTS - “Shepherd’s purse,” said Gerarde, “stayeth bleeding in any part of the body, whether the juice or the decoction thereof be drunk or whether it be used poultice-wise or in both or any way else. In a clyster it cureth the bloody flux, it healeth green and bleeding wounds, it is marvelous good for inflammations new beginning and for all diseases which must be checked back and cooled.” Gerarde added that the decoction will stop diarrhea, blood-spitting, hematuria and all other fluxes of blood. Burnett noted it for the effects of suppressed uterine disease. Burnett observed it cause sexual excitement like Canth. It aided him in the cure of an inveterate case of gallstones, the origin of which he traced to the uterus. Dudgeon reported the case of a woman who had recovered from jaundice. She then had a peculiar discharge after the menses flux of a brownish-green blood which was attended with obscure abdominal pains. The cervix uterus was swollen and soft but not ulcerated. Dudgeon failed to cure this, but Rafin- esque of Paris, after trying other remedies, succeeded with Thlaspi. 6c, which had an immediate positive effect. Rafinesque then gave the tincture, and then again the 6c, and in a few weeks the cure was complete. Dudgeon, in an article on Thlaspi., quoted a case of Rademacher’s showing the action of Thlaspi. on uric acid excretion. A woman whom Rademacher had relieved ten years before of a large quantity of urinary sand, again presented herself; her abdominal cavity was full of water, extremely swollen and she was passing urine of a light red color with bloody sediment. Thlaspi. tincture, 30 drops five times a day, was given solely with the idea of stopping the hematuria. The result was a more copious discharge of urinary sand than ever before, the urine increased, the dropsy disappeared and the woman was cured. Dudgeon's own cases are no less striking. One such case concerned a woman, 76, who had rheumatic muscular pains in various parts and an abundant secretion of uric acid, which passed away with every discharge of urine. Sometimes small stones formed and there was much pain in their passage along the ureter, but generally it passed in the form of coarse sand, which formed a thick layer at the bottom of the utensil. This sand continued to pass after the cessation of the rheumatic pains, which lasted six or seven weeks. Puls., Pic-ac., and Lyc. had no effect. Thlaspi. 1c diminished the sand to an insignificant amount. Dudgeon also noted the case of a man, 57, who, in addition to other dyspeptic symptoms, had unusually large discharges of coarse uric acid, coming away in masses as large as a big pin ’ s head but without pain. Thlaspi lx stopped this. He also recorded the case of a woman, nearly 80, who suffered from the presence of a calculus in left ureter. She had previously passed much sand. Thlaspi. lx caused a great discharge of sand and a speedy relief of her pain. Dudgeon referred to a case of Harper’s illustrating the action of Thlaspi. on the bowels. An elderly woman had suffered for years from a copious discharge of mucus, pus, sometimes mixed with blood, sometimes nearly all blood, which passed from the bowels after each evacuation. She had been under high homeopathy, oxygen treatment and for a long time under Harper’s care, all without effect. He then gave Thlaspi. tincture in 5 drop doses and cured the case in a few days. Clarke, with Thlaspi. lx, saved a woman who had been curetted several times with little success from a further curetting, which was advised as being essential to the cure. Thlaspi. stopped the hemorrhages, restored the periods to their proper term and the patient immediately began to recover her strength, which had been drained to the last degree. There was no return of the trouble. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Urt-u., Croc., Trill., Mill. (2) Cruciferae, especially Sinapis. (3) Thiosin. - fibroma, uterine tumors. (4) Matth. - inspissated secretions, grows near sewage stream. (5) Kidney stones, Oci. (6) Uric acid, pain in shoulder, Urt-u. (7) Uterine hemorrhages, Trill., Vib., Ust., Senec. (8) Hemorrhages from bowel, Merc., Nit-ac., Sulph., Caps., Merc-c., Phos. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Liver - Gallstone colic, liver affection being secondary to uterine condition. Lungs - Accumulation of phlegm in lungs. Convulsive cough, relieved as soon as phlegm is loosened. Hemoptysis. Dry cough on lying down with aching under left breast. Cough with irritation behind sternum. Fits of coughing as if the sternum pressed inward.

Kidneys - Chronic cystitis. Kidney colic and stones. Urethritis, urine runs away in little jets. Frequent desire. Urine heavy, phos- phatic. Accumulation of gtave\,brick-dust sediment. Hematuria. Albuminuria during pregnancy. Dysuria and spasmodic reten tion, after forceps delivery. Dysuria in the elderly, with dribbling. Often replaces the use of the catheter.

Perspiration - Sweat profuse at night.

Temperature - Alternate chill and sweat during headache. All night chills, with wakefulness and slight diarrhea with swelling of tonsils. Chill at 9 a.m. or from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. Chilly when uncovering during fever. Chill worse from going into warm room during fever. Continued fever with quick pulse.

name: Thuja Lobbi
author: Murphy
constitution: ThujalobbiorRedCedaris atree which is almost 50 meters high and which originates from Alaska. From the heart-wood are separated out the Thuja plicines with antibiotic, as well as anti-fungal properties. These substances also exist in Thuja occidentalis. There is no homeopathic proving for this remedy, but Dano conducted a clinical proving with it in 1934. Thuj- 1. has emaciation and constipation.

full:
PHARMACY - thuj-1. Thuja lobbi. Red cedar of Alaska. Thuja menziessi. Thuja plicata. N. O. Coniferae. The tincture is prepared with the fresh leaves. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

HOMEOPATHIC - ThujalobbiorRedCedaris atree which is almost 50 meters high and which originates from Alaska. From the heart-wood are separated out the Thuja plicines with antibiotic, as well as anti-fungal properties. These substances also exist in Thuja occidentalis. There is no homeopathic proving for this remedy, but Dano conducted a clinical proving with it in 1934. Thuj- 1. has emaciation and constipation. Chilly and the limbs are cold. MIND - Anxious melancholy. Weeps and moans easily. Indifferent to everything except for his obsessions with his own suicide. Depressive neurotic condition. Psychosis from anguish. Lack of will-power. Personality problems with those around him. Hebephrenia. COMMENTS - If the development within the compass of homeopathic remedies is followed, according to Roy. Thuja lobbi can be situated on the line: Aur., Sep., Thuja lobbi. The tendency to suicide, which is characteristic of Aur. and the indifferent psychological disposition which characterizes Sep., can be anticipated in the development of a symptomatological picture for this remedy. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Tendency to suicide (Aur.) and indifferent disposition (Sep., Ph-ac.). REFERENCES - Julian.

name: Thuja Occidentalis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better on left side, drawing up limbs, crossing limbs. Better motion. Better pressure, rubbing, scratching. Better wrapping, warmth, air, wind. Better free secretions, sneezing. Worse from cold and dampness. Worse sun, bright light. Worse at night, closing eyes, from heat of bed, left side. Worse from increasing moon, moonlight. Worse at 3 a.m. and 3 p.m. Worse periodically, yearly. Worse touch, stretching. Worse after breakfast, after eating, chewing. Worse during menses. Worse urinating, sex. Worse after gonorrhea, after vaccinations, after suppressed warts..

Diarrhea. Dyspareunia. Dysmenorrhea. Ear, polyps. Emaciation. Epilepsy. Epulis. Eyes, inflammation. Eyes, tumors. Fatty, tumors. Feet, fetid. Flatulence. Fibroids. Fig, warts. Ganglion. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Hemorrhage.

full:
PHARMACY - thuj. Thuja occidentalis. Arbor vitae. N. O. Coniferae, Tribe, Cu- presineae. Tincture of the fresh green twigs. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies. Locally, forwarts and excrescences, tincture or cerate.

CLINICAL - Abdomen, distended. Anal, warts. Angina pectoris. Anus, fissure. Asthma. Balanitis. Bedwetting. Cancer. Catalepsy. Chorea. Clavus. Colic. Condylomata. Constipation. Convulsions. Cysts. Diarrhea. Dyspareunia. Dysmenorrhea. Ear, polyps. Emaciation. Epilepsy. Epulis. Eyes, inflammation. Eyes, tumors. Fatty, tumors. Feet, fetid. Flatulence. Fibroids. Fig, warts. Ganglion. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Hemorrhage. Hair, disorders. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Hernia. Herpes zoster. Ichthyosis. Intussusception. Joints, cracking. Leucorrhea. Miscarriage. Moles. Morvan’s, disease. Mucous, patches. Muscae, volitantes. Myopia. Nevus. Nasal, catarrh. Neck, stiff. Onanism. Ovarian, cysts. Ovary, pain. Ozaena. Neuralgias. Nose, catarrh, polyps. Paralysis. Pemphigus. Polyps. Post-nasal, catarrh. Pregnancy, imaginary. Prostate, disease. Ptosis. Ranula. Rheumatism. Rickets. Sciatica. Seminal, emissions. Sinusitis. Smallpox. Sycosis. Syphilis. Tea, effects. Teeth, decay. Tongue, ulcers. Toothache. Tumors. Vaccination, effects. Vaccinosis. Vaginismus. Vaginitis. Variola. Venereal, warts. Warts. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - Thuja was introduced to France from Canada during the reign of Francis I, and it now has an honored place in many gardens and shrubbery. The native habitat of Thuja is not without its importance in relation to therapeutics. It loves swamps, it is Hahnemann’s typical anti-sycotic and Grauvogl’s hydrogenoid.

HOMEOPATHIC - Thuj. is one of Hahnemann’s discoveries. Most of the remedies of his Materia Medica had been known in a fashion before his time, but practically nothing was known of the therapeutic properties of Thuj. until Hahnemann proved it. Old- school observers found in Thuj. an efficient hemostatic, locally applied, especially after tooth extraction. Hahnemann foundThuj. to be an antidote to the sycotic miasm, meaning the constitutional disease resulting from suppressed gonorrhea and having warty growths as its characteristic manifestation. Soft, spongy warts, emitting a fetid fluid with a sweetish odor something like herring brine. Warts that bleed readily and having the coxcomb or cauliflower form. Thuj. acts chiefly on the mucus membranes of genito-urinary tract intestines, skin, mind, nerves, glands, occiput and left side. Acts on skin, blood, gastro-intestinal tract, kidneys and brain. Wart-like growths on mucus and skin surfaces. Soft, exuberant, fungoid tissue, polyps, condylomata, warts, pediculated, black, suppressed. Spongy tumors, jig warts. bleeding fungus growths. Birthmarks. Moist mucus tubercles. Antibacterial action, as in gonorrhea and vaccination. Vaccinosis, never well since vaccination, neuralgia, skin troubles etc. Variola, aborts the pustule and prevents the suppurating fever. Suppressed gonorrhea. Crying babies with a sycotic taint from the parents. Complaints from moonlight. Burning, sticking, numbing, drawing or wandering pains worse warmth. Sycotic pains, tearing in muscles and joints, worse at rest, better in dry weather, worse damp humid atmosphere, lameness. Left-sided and chilly medicine. Great prostration. Rapid exhaustion and emaciation. Neurasthenia, prostatic weakness. The patient is exhausted and soft, body feels thin and delicate, frail. Deadness of the affected part. Sensation of lightness of body when walking. Flesh feels as if beaten off the bones. Edema about the joints. Pains keep extending from original site. Stitching, tearing pains in the glands as if they were being torn to pieces. Rheumatism. Paralysis. Jerking of the upper part of the body of spinal origin, chorea. Discharges are foul, acrid, musty, rancid or of sweetish odor. Oily, stools, skin, sweat. Trickling in urethra. Congenital inguinal hernia. Venous stasis. Aneurysm by anastomosis, swelling of the blood vessels. MIND - Introverted and private. Dullness of mind. Cannot concentrate. Speech slow, hunts for words. Hurried with ill humor, talks hastily, swallows words. Makes mistakes in writing and talking. Uses wrong words or omits words and syllables. Confusion in morning. Loses his way in well-known streets. Cretinism. Imbecility of mind and loss of speech after vaccination. Vanishing of thoughts while speaking. Disinclined to talk, worse on awaking mornings. Sadness. Aversion to life. Depression, feels isolated and alone. Aversion to company. Feels isolated and different from everyone, that they do not belong. Avoids the sight of people. Mental depression after childbirth (Sep.). Irritable, jealous, quarrelsome towards husband or mother. Self-contempt. Reproaches himself. Thinks she is ugly or unclean. Feels unlovable. Emotional sensitivity. Music causes weeping and trembling. When spoken to answers with tears and sobbing. Anxiety about salvation. Anxiety about health. Anger from contradiction. Overexcited, angry or anxious about trifles. Restlessness with ill-humor. Walks in a circle in room. Talks hastily. Fear of getting infections, diseases, germs. Despair of recovery. Fear of being incurable, of death. Thinks his blood is dirty or poisoned. Insane women who will not be touched or approached. Fear of the wind. Fear of strangers. Nervous, begins to twitch at approach of strangers. Mistrustful, secretive and paranoid. Fear of being discovered, and their secrets will be revealed. Full of hidden plans and secrets. Tells lies to hide real intentions. Manipulates others. Controls herself among strangers and doctors. Fanaticism. Indifference to opposite sex. Fear of getting venereal diseases. Religious fanatics. Religious aversion to sex (Puls.). Feels sex is Thuja occidentalis dirty, shameful, sinful. Sexual perversions. Immoral sexual behavior. Secret and hidden sexual activities. Many sex partners. Sexual desires excessive and strange. Fixed ideas and delusions, as if a strange person were at his side. Delusions as if soul and body were separated, as if something alive in abdomen (Croc.). Delusions, as if body were fragile, made of glass. Delusion as if being controlled by a stronger power. Imagines himself double or treble. Sudden impulse to kill herself. Time passes too quickly.

Head - Left-sided headaches. Pain as if pierced by a nail (Coff., Ign.). Pressing in vertex, as from a nail. Tearing, jerking pain. Headache, worse sexual excess or tea, better bending head backwards. Feeling of numbness in brain. Sensation as if parietal bones were being knocked to pieces. Heaviness of occiput. Boring through the temples. Meningitis. Neuralgia from tea (Sei.). Wants head wrapped up. Honey smelling sweat. White scaly dandruff. Dry hair, splits and falls out. Warts.

Eyes - Conjunctivitis after vaccination. Blood-red eyes, full of tears, stand open. Styes and tarsal tumors (Staph.). Eyelids agglutinated at night, dry, scaly. Burning and stinging of eyelids. Lids heavy as lead. Jagged iris. Ciliary neuralgia. Iritis. Acute and chronic inflammation of sclera. Chronic scleritis. Chronic keratitis, with excessive photophobia, Thuja occidentalis after vaccination. Small brown spots on cornea. Exophthalmos from tumors behind eyeball. Large, flat phlyctenules, indolent. Constant ache in eye, worse bright light. Feels as if cold air were streaming out of the head through eye, better when warmly covered. Photopsies, beyond visual field. Floating green stripes. Eye symptoms better warmth and covering.

Ears - Chronic otitis, purulent discharge. Watery, purulent, putrid otorrhea. Chronic otorrhea after vaccination. Ear discharge smells like putrid meat. Polyps. Cracking in ears when empty swallowing. Noise in ear as from boiling water. Inner ear as if swollen with hardness of hearing.

Nose - Warts on nose. Nose red and hot. Sinusitis. Chronic sinus infections. Chronic catarrh after measles, scarlatina, variola. Chronic catarrh, thick, yellow-green mucus, blood and pus. Coryza fluent outdoors, dry in room. Violent, sudden coryza. Dryness of nasal cavities. Painful pressure at root of nose. Pain in teeth on blowing nose. Soreness and ulceration of nostrils, worse pressure. Ulceration within the nostrils. Painful scabs in nostrils. Bloody scabs or briny odor in nose. Nosebleed, worse after being over-heated. Smell in nose as of fish-brine or sour beer.

Face - Pale, waxy, shiny, dark under eyes. Greasy skin of face. Light brown, freckles on face. B loated. Edematous erysipelas of face. Eruptions leaves livid spots. Lips pale, swollen, peeling off. Twitching of lower lip. Warts. Tumor on cheek. Blood vessels of face and temples distended. Netted with spider-like veins. Boring in malar bones (left), better by touch. Face aches. Burning heat and redness of face. Neuralgia from suppressed gonorrhea or eczema of ear. Cracking of joint of jaw.

Mouth - Aphthae, ulcers in the mouth (Bor.). Varicose veins on tongue and mouth. Mouth becomes dry while chewing food. Mouth as if filled with blisters. Mouth as if it has been burnt. Sweetish taste with gonorrhea. Taste as of rotten eggs, in morning. Teeth decay at the edge of gums, crumble, turn yellow. Gnawing pain in teeth, worse cold, tea and blowing nose. Gums, very sensitive and retract. Pyorrhea alveolaris. Drinks fall audibly into stomach.

Throat - Throat dry and rough. Polyps of vocal cords. Papilloma of larynx. Chronic laryngitis. Much mucus in throat, hawked up with difficulty. Painful swallowing. Sensations as if constricted when swallowing. Sensations as if a skin in larynx. Much mucus in throat hawked up with difficulty. Mucus tubercles in fauces.

Stomach - Cutting pain in epigastrium. Indurations in stomach. Sinking sensation in epigastrium before food, thirst. Flatulence, pain after food. Noisy swallowing, loud belchings. Gulping up of large quantities of acids. Eructations rancidor acrid. Eructations afford instant relief. Rancid belch- ings after fat food. Pressing in stomach, with retching, during menses. Vomiting of mucus, or of greasy substances. Stools - Stools gurgle or pop out, hard, oily, black, lumps. Painless, grass green stools, mixed with gushing water. Stools hurried, explosive, gassy, spraying. Tenesmus of stool with rigidity of penis. Hard stool followed by soft stool. Hard balls. Large, hard stool coated with blood.

Abdomen - Distended. Indurations in abdomen. Intussusception of intestines. Flatulence and distention, protruding here and there. Colic. Gurgling in bowels. Rumbling, flatulence, upper part drawn in. Movements in abdomen, as if something alive, without pain (Croc.). Soreness of navel. Cutting and squeezing in hypogas- trium. Ileus. Cutting, squeezing in hypo- gastrium, groin. Stinging as from needles. Hernia. Stitches in inguinal glands. Soreness of navel. Yellowish or brownish spots on abdomen. Herpes zoster.

Rectum - Constipation with violent rectal pain, causing stool to recede (Sil., Sanie.). Chronic diarrhea, worse after breakfast. Diarrhea after vaccination. Diarrhea periodically returning at same hour. Noiseless emission of flatus. Moisture oozing from anus, moist perineum. Ana/fissure, painful to touch. Ana/ warts. Condylomata at anus. Venereal warts. Red blotches at anus like fig warts. Swollen hemorrhoids, pain worse sitting with stitching. Hemorrhoids sensitive to touch. Burning pains at the anus. Burning in perineum. Perineal fistula. Perineum moist. Sensations - As if a strange person were at her side. As if under the influence of a superior power. As if soul and body were separated. As if whole body were very thin and delicate, as if its continuity would be dissolved, as if frail and easily broken, as if made of glass. As if a nail were pressing into vertex, as if a nail were driven from within outward in vertex. As if abdominal muscles were being pushed out by arm of a child. As if a living a animal were in abdomen. Legs as if made of wood when walking. As if lower limbs were elongated. As from flea bites.

Urine - Foamy urine. Split, small stream. Urinary stream forked and small. Discharge of glutinous moisture from urethra. Weak stream. Urine becomes Thuja occidentalis cloudy after standing. Urine yellowish or wine-colored. Urine dark red in morning. Urine deposits abrown mucus. Urine with dark, cloudy sediment, in rheumatism. Urine highly colored and of strong smell. Urine profuse, light-yellow. Urine bums, dribbles, foul, foamy. Vertigo - Vertigo as from motion of a swing. Vertigo everything seems tojump. Vertigo on closing eyes. Vertigo looking upwards or sideways. Reeling, as after turning in a circle. When rising from sitting; on stooping. Vision - Shortsighted. Diplopia. Amblyopia with blurring, better rubbing. Misty or obscured, with dilated pupils. Dim vision as from mist or veil, in open air, with confusion of head. Flickering vision. Sees flames of light like fire-flies. Sees clouds and streaks. Muscae volitantes. Streaks of light or sparks passing downward. Objects appear smaller. COMMENTS - Millspaugh noted that the American Arbor Vitae is a “spiry evergreen attaining a height of from 20 to 50 feet, though generally not above 40 and a diameter of about 10 to 20 feet through the greatest breadth of foliage. It assumes a conical form with such true lines as to appear ‘clipped.’ thus forming one of our most valued high-hedge trees. “It abounds in the northern zones of North America from Pennsylvania northwards. There it “often forms what are commonly known as cedar-swamps. It grows upon the rocky banks of rivers and in low, swampy spots, blossoming from May until June and maturing its fruit in autumn.” Teste remarked that in the period when the doctrine of signatures prevailed, the “Resinous callosities of the stems and leaves of Thuja might have seemed an indication that the plant was the specific for sycosis and warts.” Teste dismissed this idea, but he did ask whether resinous substances that have the power of modifying vegetable juices in a peculiar way may not affect the animal fluids in the same manner. He included Castoreum canadense in his Thuj. group and followed by giving an instance in which it acted on fig-warts. Castoreum canadense is the product of an animal that subsists on the bark of resinous trees. Hering described Thuj.’s action on fluids as “dissolution of fluids of the body, which become acrid, probably caused by Thuja perverting lymphatic secretions, disturbs digestion and sanguification.” He went on to discuss Thuja’s action in the vegetative sphere: “A surplus of producing life, nearly unlimited proliferation of pathological vegetations, condylomata, warty sycotic excrescences, spongy tumors and spongy pock exudates which organize hastily. All morbid manifestations are excessive, but appear quietly, so that the beginning of the diseased state is scarcely know.” Boenninghausen found Thuja both preventive and curative during an epidemic of smallpox. It aborted the disease process and prevented pitting. In veterinary practice, Thuja has proved curative in farcy and in “grease.” These clinical uses point to Thuj.’s affinity to vaccinations. No one has written more forcibly or lucidly on this than Burnett did in his book, Vaccinosis and its Cure by Thuja. “Arbor Vitae: nomen omen,” said Burnett on his title page. In his hands, Thuj. proved to be a tree of life to numberless sufferers from the vaccination miasm. By “vaccinosis” Burnett meant the disease known as vaccinia, the result of vaccination, in addition to “that profound and often long-lasting morbid constitutional state engendered by the vaccine virus.” Thuj. is homeopathic to this state, and therefore curative and preventive of it. Burnett made the observation, which Clarke confirmed, that the vaccination does not need to take in order to produce the vaccination miasm. Many people date their ill health from a so-called unsuccessful vaccination, so vaccinosis may exist apart from vaccinia. The anti-vaccinosis action of Thuj. is part of its anti-sycotic action, therefore vaccinosis is a sycotic disease. Burnett noted the case of an infant, ten weeks old, whom he was called to see as it was supposed to be dying. He found it ghastly white and in collapse. There was Thuja occidentalis nothing to account for this except that the baby had its wet-nurse changed two or three days before. The wet-nurse was questioned and declared herself quite well and looked it, but “her arm was a little painful.” She had been revaccinated in the Marylebone Workhouse the day before she took charge of the patient. Burnett found the vaccine eruption just turning into the pustular stage. He concluded that the infant was sucking in the vaccine poison with its nurse’s milk. He gave Thuj. 6c to both infant and nurse. The baby gradually improved the same day and the next morning, though still pale, was practically well and the vaccine vesicles on the nurse’s arm had withered. Burnett quoted a case of vaccine rash in an infant following the vaccination of its mother, who was nursing it. The effects of chronic vaccinosis are protean. Prominent among them are asthma, neuralgias, skin disorders, indigestion and constipation, warts and new growths of many kinds. Emaciation, brain damage, epilepsy and blindness. Hyperactivity, attention deficit disorder and autism. In these effects, a favorite method of Burnett’s was to give a course of twenty- four numbered powders, only three or four of them medicated with Thuj. 30c, one to be taken at bedtime. With the same prescription, he cured many cases of paralysis; his indications included paralysis of left side of body, very chilly, worse in morning, in wet weather and in cold. Burnett also found enlargements of the spleen to dissolve with these indications. The first case Clarke treated homeopathically was one involving new growths. There was a cluster of small warts on the forehead of a boy that had lasted eighteen months, following a cat’s scratch. Thuj. in small doses and tincture painted on permanently cured in three weeks. A gentleman, about 50, consulted Clarke about a wart on the right side of his head. He was then bald and the wart developed in the same locality soon after and has since remained. The patient had been twice vaccinated. Clarke gave him Thuj. 30c, twenty-eight powders, one in seven medicated, one at bedtime. In one month there was much reduction, Thuj. was repeated and in little over two months the wart was goift. Burnett suggested Thuj. for fatty tumors, which he regards as sycotic in nature. Thuja not only produces symptoms of the secondary stage of gonorrheal and vaccine affections, it also produces urethritis and a variolous eruption. Dudgeon reported acute urethritis with yellow discharge lasting altogether a fortnight as the result of chewing a Thuja cone. Goullon cured a lady who had a headache for a year. On waking, she felt as if a tight hoop enclosed her forehead, not passing away until noon. Eyelids heavy as lead. Thuj. lOx, one dose at bedtime, permanently cured. Robert Farley related the case of two children, age 5, who had what he graphically termed “urinary tantrums.” Two hours after being put to bed they would wake kicking, crying and refusing to answer a question. This lasted an hour or more. Asked if they wanted to urinate they would refuse to answer, strike at attendant, or even say “No.” Finally it was found that if they were taken up and put on the closet they would urinate and then go to sleep readily. One of the children developed signs of incipient inflammation of the left hip joint. The totality led to the selection of Thuj., which was given in the 200c. After the first night there were no more “tantrums,” and in two months the child was perfectly well. This child’s father had gonorrhea, treated by injection, some years before the patient was born. But the other child’s father had not had gonorrhea. In the latter case, which was exactly like the former, the cure was immediate, in the former case relief occurred on the second night. C. W. Roberts found Thuj. in five to seven drop doses at bedtime, to control nocturnal seminal emissions better than any other remedy. “Nocturnal seminal emission” is an emphasized symptom. Percy Wilde recorded the case of a young married woman who had a large epulis on her lower jaw, rapidly increasing in size, ulcerating on the surface, very painful and filling the mouth with an ill-smelling secretion. The entire tumor was removed by operation and also the subjoined bone. Three weeks later the tumor was as large as before and increased daily. Thuj. lx was then given. The growth stopped immediately, ulceration ceased, and the pain disappeared. In three weeks the gum was healthy and remained so permanently. Villers related a case of scalp tumor in a youth of seventeen. The tumor had existed for two years and had somewhat the appearance of a bean. It was situated about the posterior edge of the parietal bone, was devoid of sensation and the hair had disappeared from it, making it very conspicuous. Thuj. 30c was given, a dose every twenty days. In four months the youth was almost cured, entirely so in five months, and the hair grew again completely covering the spot. George Royal related a case of persistent cough cured withThuj. Miss X., 19, fair, had for three months a painless, dry cough. The irritation was only in the throat. There were six small growths at the back of her throat and one near the vocal cord. She had never had a cough before. She also had green, excoriating leucorrhea and menses that were a little too early. Thuj. 30c cured the growths and the cough in about three weeks. R. B. Johnstone offered some indications for Thuj. in hernia. He found it particularly useful for women with a sycotic history who have a tendency to left-side inguinal hernia after labor. When babies cry a lot, the umbilicus protrudes, growing red and sore, especially when the father has a sycotic history. Left inguinal hernia in infants, child cries all the time and is only quiet when the left inguinal region is relie ved from pressure or the thigh is flexed on the abdomen. Burnett recorded a case of lichen urticatus in a boy of 14, which came into his hands after a long course of treatment, external, internal and dietetic, at the hands of allopathic specialists without result. The rash came periodically in warm weather; the patient literally tore himself because of the irritation. The rash was worse on the left (vaccinated) side. Thuj. 30c was given in infrequent doses. The spots continued to appear for a week and then disappeared. The skin remained clear in spite of the patient indulging in all kinds of previously forbidden foods. Birthmarks and stains (Sep., Care.). Birthmarks and moles in children with a sycotic history. The skin is mottled and discolored, brown or red mottled spots, discoloration of the backs of the hands and feet. Tendency toward acne and greasy skin. Blood blisters. Spider hemangiomas. Benign tumor growths. Polyp formation, particularly on anus, rectum, or cervix. Severe left ovarian pains, sometimes burning, extend down thigh. Pains worse from any attempt at exercise, especially walking. Pains occur with every menstrual period and are generally worse before and during the flow. The pain compels the patient to lie down, but lying on the left side aggravates. Gonorrhea with yellow-green discharge. Vaginitis and cervicitis with yellow-green discharge (Puls.). Chronic sinusitis, yellowgreen or green mucus. White sinus discharge, with warts and a history of gonorrhea. Sweet smelling perspiration, sickly sweet. PHARMACY - Thymol. Thymolum. Thyme camphor. A phenol from the essences of many Labiatae, Lamiaceae or some Um- belliferae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Adenoma. Colitis. Diarrhea. Dyspnea. Enterocolitis. Fainting tendency. Hookworms. Laryngitis. Leucorrhea. Migraines. Neurasthenia. Sexual weakness. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - Thymol exists in the essences of certain plants belonging to the Labi atae family or to the Umbellifers. It is a phenol made up of para-isopropyl-metacresol. Thymol can be extracted from them by combining with alkaline lye (soda or potash). It is used therapeutically as an intestinal anti-septic and as vermifuge against tapeworm.

HOMEOPATHIC - The proving was conducted by Griggs, on eight pro vers, six males and two females, as well as one control using a placebo, in 1940-41. The experiment began by using 3x for two weeks, 2x for the next two weeks and lx for about ten days. The provings show an action limited to the sexual organs, producing a typical sexual neurasthenia. Thymol’s general action is on the stomach, genital organs and to a small extent, on the central nervous system. Genito urinary diseases. Pathological emissions, priapism and prostatorrhea. Nightly seminal discharge.

Head - Headache with sadness. Constricting pain in the temples, in women, ameliorated when lying down or from external heat. Bilateral temporal headache and at the occiput. Menstrual migraines.

Ears - Noises in the ears. Buzzing in the ears. Sound like bells. Temporary deafness.

Mouth - Salivation reduced when eating. Watery salivation with nausea. Ptyalism. Nauseating belchings.

(2) Canth. - Irritation and inflammation of the digestive, urinary and cutaneous mucus membranes. Intense burning in the digestive passages with frequent, compelling need to urinate. (3) Merc-c. - Burning pains in the pharynx, painful, frequent urination, urine comes drop by drop, diarrhea with tenesmus. (4) Ter. - Irritation of the digestive and urinary mucus membranes with tendency to hemorrhage. REFERENCES - Julian.

Blood - streaked leucorrhea. Glairy or membranous diarrhea. Hookworm disease (Chen-a.). General weakness with headaches. Constricting headache. Skin blue, cold. Spasmodic laryngeal cough. Excessive salivation with nausea. Frequent urination with compelling urging. Pains in the dorsal and lumbar region, spreading to the buttocks. MIND - Irritable, arbitrary, must have his own way. Uneasy feeling and agitation. Nervous agitation, loquacity, mental confusion. Bewildered state. Craves company. Morose, sad, uneasy. Energy gone.

PHARMACY - thymu. Thymus serpyllum. Wild thyme. N. O. Labiatae. Tincture of the whole plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Respiratory, infections. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - Thymus serpyllum belongs to the mint family; all the members have a marked action on the urinary organs and especially on the elimination of uric acid. It contains a volatile oil thymol, tannin, a gum and woody fiber. Thymol is a very powerful germicide, killing the germs of typhoid fever in thirty minutes.

HOMEOPATHIC - Respiratory infections of children, dry nervous asthma, whooping cough, severe spasms but little sputum. Ringing in ears with feeling of pressure in head. Burning in pharynx, sore throat worse empty swallowing, blood vessels distended, dark. COMMENTS - Small doses of Thymu. act as a sedative and contra-stimulant, the depressive action being preceded by a period of excitation. Large doses dull the nerves and produce motor incoordination and sleep. Animals poisoned by Thymu. sleep standing and are insensible to the prick of a pin. They have muscular contraction and tremors, vertigo and turning movements. Increase of diarrhea, vomiting appears, prostration is extreme, the skin becomes cold and death sets in with all the symptoms of a depressant position and with complete anesthesia. These final symptoms are due to the thymic acid, which is a camphor. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke.
