full:
PHARMACY - tub. Tuberculinum bovinum. Tuberculosis nosode. Tuberculinum bovinum of Kent. Tuberculinum of Koch. Nosode is prepared either from tubercular abscess or from a glycerine extract of pure cultivation of human tubercular bacillus. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Albuminuria. Allergies. Appendicitis. Asthma. Bedwetting. Bones, decay. Breast, tumors. Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia. Catarrh. Chilblains. Chilly. Colds. Cornea, opacity, ulceration. Coughs. Dentition. Diarrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspnea. Ear, infections. Edema. Emaciation. Epilepsy. Erysipelas. Erythema. Glands swollen. Hematuria. Hemoptysis. Headache. Heart, disorders. Hyperactivity. Influenza. Leprosy. Leucorrhea. Lungs, disorders. Lupus. Mania. Menses, early. Nephritis. Neurasthenia. Night sweats. Night, terrors. Paralysis. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Throat, sore. Tonsillitis. Tuberculosis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Clarke found no appreciable difference between the action of Tub. and that of Bac. His own impression was that they are practically identical and that one will answer to the indications of the other. The first provers were tuberculosis patients and only pathogenetic symptoms are recorded. Tub. 30c was used. Tub. affects the mind, lungs, head, occiput, glands and larynx. When symptoms are constantly changing and well-selected remedies fail to improve. Relapsing states. Patient always tired, motion causes intense fatigue, aversion to work, wants constant changes. Tubercular miasm. In tuberculosis where the symptoms are constantly changing and begin suddenly, ceasing suddenly or of obscure nature. Early stage tuberculosis. Always tired, motion causes intense fatigue. Increasing exhaustion and lowered vitality. Weakness, emaciation with good appetite. Rapid breakdown of health. General exhaustion. Nervous weakness. Neurasthenia. Fainting. Trembling, quivering. Epilepsy. Nervous children. Mentally deficient children. Tendency tocatch cold easily, on slightest exposure, which ends in diarrhea. Diarrhea in children running for weeks, extreme wasting, bluish pallor, exhaustion. Chronic, enlargement of the glands, adenoids. Enlarged tonsils. Kidney disorders, chronic cystitis. Bruised pain throughout the body. Bones painful. Formication. Skin affections, acute rheumatism. Arthritis. Clothes feel very damp. Very susceptible to changes of weather. Very sensitive mentally and physically. Sensitive to music. MIND - Changing moods. Dissatisfied and restless, always wants a change. Desire to travel, does not want to remain in one place long. Deep feeling of being unfulfilled. Romantic longing to find inner contentment. Wants to do something different or even to find a new doctor. Restlessness. Needs stimulating experi- . enees. Constant fight against boredom. Compulsiveness. Desire to break things. Impulse to run. Reckless. Every trifle irritates, worse when waking. Anxious. Anxiety during fever. Children awake screaming with restlessness. Whimpers when spoken to. Whines and complaints with very little ailment. Precocious children. Contradictory behavior, changing moods. Insomnia and sopor. Depressed, melancholy. Hopeless. Weary of life. Sensitive to music. Fear something will happen. Fear of animals, particularly averse to dogs and cats. Aversion to mental work. Confusion, everything in the room seems strange. Ritualistic. Superstitious. Mania and melancholia. Maliciousness behavior and destructiveness. Abusive. Fits of violent temper, wants to fight, throws anything at anyone even without a cause. Destructive fantasies. Desire to use foul language, curse and swear.

Head - Meningitis. Periodical headaches. Intense pain, as of an iron band around head. Deep violent head pains, tears hair or beats head with fist. Dashes against the wall or floor, worse motion. Shooting from over eyes (right) through the head to back of ear (left) or from right frontal protuberance to right occipital region. Headaches students, worse study or even slight mental exertion. Brain feels loose. Sensitive scalp. Plica polonica (Vine.).

Eyes - Sore, bruised eyeballs, worse turning them. Eczema of margins of eyelids. Meningitis with squint.

Ears - Persistent offensive otorrhea. Perforation in eardrum with ragged edges. Sticking pain from pharynx to ears. Great aching in ears and teeth. Tinnitus. Rushing in ears with heavy head.

Face - Old looking, edematous, pale. Black blisters on lips. Slight swelling and itching of lips. Aching in malar bones.

Mouth - Dryness, stickiness. Black blisters on lips. Grinding of teeth in sleep. Teeth sensitive to cold air. Sensation as if the teeth were all jammed together and there were too many teeth. Delayed dentition. Nose - Nose and lips somewhat swollen. Sweat on nose. Crops of small boils, intensely painful, successively appear in the nose.green, fetid pus. Watery pimples, which, suppurating, form scabs. Dryness of posterior nares. Soreness inside of nose. Colds ending in diarrhea.

Throat - Hoarseness, better talking. Enlarged tonsils. Hawks mucus after eating. Adenoids. Dryness of the posterior sinuses. Vertigo - Vertigo with obscuration of eyes, is obliged to lean on something. Vertigo with palpitations, nausea. Vertigo with headache, in morning, after dinner. COMMENTS - Generally a history of tuberculosis in the family. Suppressed acute infections. Tendency for sore throats, colds, and upper respiratory infections or bronchitis. Swollen glands and big tonsils. Sore throats, swollen glands, start losing weight. Recurring tonsillitis in children. Similar to Bac., but more chronic and more severe. Colds that go into the chest (Phos.). Asthma, associated with frequent colds. Intercurrent for severe, chronic lung disease. Lingering coughs, pneumonias. Coughs where well-indicated remedies don’t work. Rapid emaciation with a good appetite (lod., Cina.). Emaciation associated with lung diseases. Rickets. Fatigue, faintness, and profuse debility. Great weakness in the limbs, after dinner. Paralysis. Disturbed circulation, chills and flushes alternating. Extreme exhaustion with sweat. Night sweats and weight loss (Med.). Night terrors. Insomniafrom overexcited state and overactive mind. Children grind their teeth during sleep. “Shivering when beginning to sleep.” “Cold feet in bed.” Low vital heat. Fontanelles that fail to close. Hydrocephalus. Meningitis. Characteristic desire to hit their head against the wall. Pressure in the head. Insanity. Hair growth in unusual and new places (Syph., Thuj.). Ringworm, particularly in children (Bac.). Voracious craving for ice-cold milk. Desires sweets, chocolate, fats, smoked meat, pork, bacon, exotic foods and spicy foods. Craves variety in food. Diarrhea. Better in the mountains, in pine forests. Desire for open air, particularly with respiratory conditions. Better motion, activity, exercise (Rhus-t.). Worse cold, damp with cold hands and feet. Hyperactive children. Children seem to have two personalities, one very sweet, nice and apologetic, the other destructive, obstinate, and argumentative. Tantrums, behavioral problems. Can be snappy, irritable, peevish, over-reactive (Cham., when due to pain). Very intelligent, but learning disabilities. Too much energy, can’t slow down to learn anything (Med., because they can’t focus). Easily bored. Very excitable. Active and very restless. Always needs something new. Strong desire to travel. Sense that there is something missing (Calc-p.), but they don’t know what it is. Discontent. Passionate, driven and dissatisfied. Deep feeling of unfulfillment, emptiness. Very romantic, yearning and longing, pining. Falls in love easily and deeply, can be easily grieved (Nat-m.). Easily upset. Hard to please, capricious. Malicious, conscious intent to do harm or to disrupt their environment (Med. is unconscious, more confused). Characteristic desire to break things. Can bite or mutilate themselves. Insanity. Fear of wasting their life, their time, of not accomplishing something significant before they die. Fear of dying or despair over their recovery. Dislike of dogs and cats, severe allergies to cats. Nebel used Tub. in exactly the same way as Burnett; others have used Bac., on the indications Burnett laid down and with Burnett’s results. In 1892, Arnuphy began giving Tub. 6x and 8x trituration in acute and chronic tuberculosis cases, with encouraging success, but with undesired aggravations at times. These were avoided with 12x and 30x. In one case, originating in influenza, both apices were affected, the right one breaking down and abundant pleuritic effusion on the left side. Six weeks’ treatment with Tub. brought about recovery. When seen a year later, the patient was quite well except for retraction of the left side. Arnuphy frequently used Tub. for bronchitis, catarrhal pneumonia, lobular pneumonia, tubercular pleurisy, parenchymatous nephritis and influenza. He gave two cases of acute lobular pneumonia with characteristic symptoms and high temperatures quickly resolved by Tub. One case concerned a boy, 3, who received the 12x; the other was a man, 78, who suffered from chronic bronchial catarrh. The latter was taken with influenza, pneumonia developed and he was in a very serious state. Tub. 30x made an almost immediate change for the better and recovery followed. Arnuphy related that, in this case, an abundant perspiration took place (the skin had been dry) during the night and he observed this in all cases of pneumonia when Tub. acted favorably. Clarke found Tub. 30c, 100c, 200c and 1000c the best general antidote to the chronic effects of influenza poisoning. A curious use of Tub. was made by Jau- regg of Vienna in a case of insanity. He had observed that cases of insanity are always benefited by an attack of an acute infectious disease, especially if it is accompanied with high fever. The idea then occurred to him to utilize the fever produced by Koch's Tuberculinic injections. He tried it on some patients and though the favorable symptoms soon disappeared after the fever subsided, there remained a steady clearing of the confused sensorium. Insanity is very frequently a manifestation of the tuberculosis miasm and there is something more than a pyrexial power in Tub. RELATIONS - Vaccinosis may block the way of action of Tub. until Thuj. has been given. When Tub. fails Syph. often follows, producing a positive reaction. Compare: (1) Bac., Phos., Sil. (2) Tub-a., Form-ac. Stann., (3) Psor., Lach. (4) Teucr-s. - tuberculosis, garlicky odor of all secretions and breath. Complementary: Bac., Phos., Calc., Chin., Bry. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - All gone hungry sensation (Sulph.), which drives one to eat. Cramping pain in stomach. Belchings and sensation of fullness over stomach. Flatulent dyspepsia. Nausea with pains in umbilical region with diarrhea. Nausea before breakfast, with sudden diarrhea. Vomiting.

Abdomen - Inguinal glands indurated and visible. Drum belly. Spleen region bulging out, stitching pain in sides after running. Stitching pain in sides after running. Tympanites. Tabes mesenterica.

Rectum - Constipation, stools large and hard, then diarrhea. Chronic diarrhea with excessive sweat. Early- morning, sudden diarrhea (Sulph.). Brown, foul, watery stools, discharged with much force. Diarrhea of children running for weeks with wasting, exhaustion and bluish pallor. Tearing pain in rectum on coughing. Tearing in rectum on coughing. Sensations - As if the brain were squeezed with an iron ring. As if the teeth were jammed together and were too many for the mouth. Mucus in the throat of a tumor in the throat. Pressure in stomach going to throat as if the clothes were too tight. As if the clothes on the back were wet (Bac.).

Female - Burning in genitals. Amenorrhea. Menses too early, too profuse, long- lasting. Menses soon after childbirth. Dysmenorrhea, pains increase with the flow. Severe pain in breast at beginning of menses. Benign breast tumors. Retraction of nipples. Food - Loss of appetite, especially in morning. Aversion to all food, particularly meat. Ravenous hunger at night, driving out of bed. Craves alcohol, delicacies, sweets, cold milk. Strong craving for smoked meats and fats, bacon, ham, pork. Extreme thirst, day and night.

Chest - Heat in chest. Sore spot, pressure in chest. Sticking pain on both sides of chest in back. Constitutions - Tubercular constitutions. Lax fiber, low recuperative powers, very susceptible to changes in the weather. Mentally deficient children. Adapted to light complexioned. narrow-chested people. Coughs - Hard, dry cough during sleep. Hard, hacking cough with profuse sweating and loss of weight, rales all over chest. Cough with chill and red face, worse evening.

Heart - Heaviness and pressure over the heart. Palpitations on taking a deep breath after evening meal.

Back - Tension in nape of neck and down spine. Chilliness between shoulders or up the back. Pain in the back with palpitations. Sensation as if damp clothes on back. Breasts - Severe pain in breast at the beginning of menses. Breast tumors, benign. Retraction of nipples. Causations - Tuberculosis.

Limbs - Acute articular rheumatism. Hands and arms feel lame, unable to write or raise a cup or a glass. Fingertips brown. Sensation of fatigue in limbs. Cold feet in bed. Limbs feel weak or as if paralyzed worse dinner. Rheumatism. Pains in ulnar nerve. Wandering pain in limbs and joints. Lungs - Shortness of breath. Sensation of suffocation, even with plenty of fresh air. Longs for cold air. Asthma. Pneumonia after influenza. Tuberculosis. Deposits begin in apex of lung. Broncho-pneumonia in children. Profuse bronchorrhea. Hard, hacking cough, profuse sweating and loss of weight, rales all over chest. Dry, hard cough, more during sleep, worse dyspnea with chill and red face, worse evenings, worse raising arms. Thick, easy, profuse expectoration. Thick yellow or yellowgreen sputum. Mucus rattle in chest without expectoration.

Sleep - Insomnia and sopor. Overpowering sleepiness in daytime. Shuddering sensation on falling to sleep. Grinding of teeth during sleep. Night, terrors. Nocturnal hallucinations, wakes frightened. Screaming in sleep. Nightmares. Child wakes screaming. Awakes in horror. Night sweats. Poor sleep, restless, wakes early. Overpowering sleepiness in daytime. Distressing, vivid dreams. Dreams of shame. Dreams frightful.

Skin - Skin easily tanned. Dry, harsh, sensitive. Acne in tuberculous children. Ringworm. Measles. Psoriasis (Thyr.). Bran-like scales. Chronic eczema. Intense itching, changes places on rubbing, worse at night. Itching in cool air, better heat of stove. Itching worse undressing, bathing.

Modalities - Better open air, cool wind. Better dry mountain air, pineforests. Better dry, warm weather. Worse from close room. Worse change of weather, before a storm, cold, damp, drafts. Worse motion, slightest exertion, standing. Worse noise and music. Worse periodically. Worse after dinner, evening, night, when beginning to sleep. Worse on waking, early morning, after sleep, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Worse in the mornings, much purulent expectoration, sickness and nausea, loss of appetite, thirst, fatigue. Worse or better at seashore.

Kidneys - Must strain at stool to pass urine. Sticky urinary sediment. Bedwetting.

Perspiration - Clammy sweats. Sweat stains yellow. Offensive, of chest, axillae, palms, nose and feet. Profuse night sweats. Sweats from coughing, from slightest exertion. Sweats on hands, on upper parts.

Temperature - Remittent fever. Loquacious during fever. Profuse sweat, easy, cold, clammy. Sweat on upper parts, on hands, worse coughing, stains yellow. General chilliness. Chilliness between shoulders or up back. Chilly, at beginning of sleep. Chilly, yet wants fresh air. Shuddering like a chill seems to go from brain down spine. Heat on cheek of affected side in spots. Burning in genitals. Flushes of heat, worse eating. Wants covers on in all stages of fever.

PHARMACY - turq. Turquoise. Gemstone. Hydrous copper aluminum phosphate. CuA16(PO4)4(OH)8, 5H2O. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Backache. Cramps. Coryza. Cough. Diarrhea. Faintness. Fractures. Headache. Heat, flushes. Influenza. Injuries. Leucorrhea. Vertigo

HOMEOPATHIC - Injuries after falling from a height. Injuries to bones, fractures. Sharp pains. Internal or external squeezing pain. Sharp pains. Internal trembling. Accelerated pulse. Tension. Faintness on rising. Weakness, lassitude. Emaciation. Influenza. Worse in the morning, afternoon, 1 to 4 p.m., after midnight, 3 a.m. Worse from waking. Coldness in the morning, in bed. Heat flushes, at noon. Heat aggravates. Better from the moon. MIND - Fastidious. Industrious. Creative. Memory, active. Dullness, slowness of mind. Difficult concentration. Aversion to mental work. Forgetfulness. Discouraged. Cheerfulness. Excitement, exhilaration. Laughing, quickly followed by weeping. Alternating moods. Horrible news, sad stories, affect profoundly. Sadness. Grief. Homesickness. Weeping. Despair. Impatience. Irritability, waking aggravates. Irritability before menses. Confrontational. Censorious. Hatred. Angry, toward husband. Averse to husband. Aversion to company. Anxiety, during cough. Vivacious. Confidence increased. Amorous disposition. Clairvoyance. Foreboding. Tranquility. Relaxed feeling. Persistent thoughts. Delusion that she is betrayed. Delusion of being old. As if in a dream. Time passes too slowly, appears longer. Detached. Sensitive to noise, light. Starting during sleep. Restlessness.

Eyes - Dryness, irritation. Heaviness, tired sensation. Swelling. Scratching sensation. Pain, as if from sand.

Ears - Clear discharge. Noises, especially in the left.

Nose - Obstruction at night, wakes him. Obstruction, morning. Coryza in the morning, with fluent discharge. Clear discharge. Sneezing in the morning. Acute sense of smell.

Face - Discoloration, red flushes. Greasy. Wrinkled skin. Dry lips, posterior nares. Peeling, rough lips. Herpetic eruptions, painful, suppurating. Eruption on lower lip, around mouth. Acne, on forehead. Pimples.

Mouth - Metallic taste. Numb tongue. Pain, biting in the tongue. Roughness inside lip. Swelling gums.

Throat - Pain. Itching. Thick sensation. Voice rough. Vertigo - Vertigo with headache, during sleep. Vision - Acute or blurred vision. COMMENTS - One of the first gemstones to be mined, turquoise has long been prized for its intense color, which varies from sky blue to green, depending on the quantities of iron and copper within it. Turquoise symbolizes laughter, humor, confidence, and purpose. Turquoise is said to strengthen eyesight and even cure blindness. Strengthens and calms the mind and body. Stimulates tissue regeneration. Revitalizes blood, nervous system. It is said to be beneficial for circulation, bowel cramps and the chest area including lungs and respiratory system. Throat, lungs, asthma. Tones and strengthens entire body. Good for internal cleansing. Infections. Headache. High blood pressure. Anorexia. Teeth, jaw ailments. Hearing disorders. Like amethyst, it protects and detoxifies from alcohol, poison, pollution, x-ray/sun radiation. Induces enthusiasm. Encourages family bonding. Promotes trust, love, kindness and innocence. Empowers artistic traits. Provides discipline, attention and understanding. For fear, depression. RELATIONS - Compare: Amethyst. Amber. Ruby. REFERENCES - Murphy. Rowe.

Stomach - Appetite diminished, easy satiety. Appetite increased. Thirst. Tension. Noises, gurgling. Eructations at night. Nausea, with chill, headache. Vomiting.

Abdomen - Distension. Abdominal pain, better from diarrhea or vomiting. Cutting. squeezing, cramping pain, during diarrhea.

Rectum - Constipation, ineffectual urging. Diarrhea. Frequent hard or soft stool. Bloody stool. Flaky stool.

Female - Profuse clotted menses, frequent, too early, too soon, too short. Cramping pain in uterus, during menses. Leucor- rhea, lumpy. Itching vagina. Pain, burning vagina. Sexual desire increased, decreased. Foods - Aversion to meat, sweets. Desires alcohol, cold drinks, cold food, salt, pickles at night. Wine aggravates. Heads - Sudden headaches. Headaches in the afternoon, evening, on waking. Headaches, worse motion. Forehead pain, behind the eyes, extending to vertex. Temple pain, extending to vertex, forehead. Occiput pain, at night. Vertex pain. Dull pain. Piercing, penetrating pain. Squeezed pain in occiput. Expanded sensation. Sensation of swelling. Sensation of wet towel inside Turquoise head. Itching scalp.

Chest - Compressed sensation. Constriction. Eruptions, acne. Itching, evening. Pain in the ribs. Tingling. Tingling, side.

Back - Backache, worse draft of air, bending forward. Back pain, cervical, dorsal, under scapula, lumbar. Dorsal contraction. Lumbar, dorsal tension. Aching pain, cervical, extending to occiput. Cervical stiffness. As if neck gripped by a hand. Pain, swelling in the cervical glands. Pimples. Eruptions, acne. Breasts - Itching in nipples.

Limbs - Sharp pain in hip, thigh. Cramps in legs, hips, ankles, feet. Leg cramps at night. Leg weakness, descending stairs with trembling. Burning foot. Blotches, red eruptions. Dry eruptions. Echymoses. in lower limbs. Eruptions in legs, calf, knee, itching. Itching eruption in the forearm, shoulder, hands, palms. Numb finger, second finger. Electrical current sensation in arms. Stiff, tense shoulder. Lungs - Asthma. Difficult breathing. Dry cough. Night cough.

Sleep - Y awning, vehement, violent. Falling asleep difficult. Restless. Unrefreshing sleep. Sudden waking, after midnight, 1 a.m., 2 a.m.. 3 a.m. Difficult waking. Deep sleep. Vivid dreams. Dreams of cats, insects. Dreams of food, of water, of urinating. Dreams of houses falling apart, of falling, of injuries. Dreams of making purchases, of money, of servants. Dreams of being small, of being very tall, of growing large. Dreams of a man who looks like a woman.

Skin - Abscess. Echymoses. Eruption, pimples, worse warmth. Painful eruptions, red, sudden itching.

Kidneys - Urging to urinate. Pain before urination. Frequent urination. Feeble stream, slow, weak.

Perspiration - Scanty sweat.

full:

CLINICAL - Obesity. Plethora.

HOMEOPATHIC - Demesnes proved Tus-f., taking three drops of the tincture on the tongue. After first causing a disagreeable, spiteful mood, it set up in a few days an opposite condition, which lasted some time. A journey taken on the ninth day of the proving, which usually caused loss of weight, did not do so. Tus-f. has a peculiar sensation induced was as if a morsel of food lay at the bottom of the cardia and would not pass. Stoutness increased and plethora was added, later on the abdominal protuberance permanently disappeared. REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Tussilago Petasites
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Pains in pylorus worse by pressure. Lumbago worse standing. Drinking causes belchings. Worse from walking. COMMENTS - Kuchenmeister and five others took substantial doses. Most noticeable among the symptoms were a lumbago of very great severity. Tightnessofthechest. Headache shifting from one part of the head to another during two days. Pain about the pylorus. Urethritis with yellow discharge. Hansen gave the indication “Acute or chronic gonorrhea, yellow or white, thick discharge.” Crawling in urethra, jerking in spermatic cord and drawing in right testicle are additional symptoms of the proving. Rosenberg gave some experiences. The first concerned an extremely violent gonorrhea, penis swollen, painful, emission of urine extremely painful, mixed with blood, patient feverish and restless. Tus-p. was given in water. There was a great aggravation of all symptoms in thirty- six hours. The remedy was discontinued and marked amelioration followed. Resumed again, much diluted, rapid cure followed. The remedy was used externally as well in this case. A second case was a chronic ophthalmia, the result of gonorrhea “cured” with turpentine. Tus-p. restored the discharge and then cured. Rosenberg referred to a writer who said of the plant that if it is macerated in water, the water will not spoil even if kept for years. RELATIONS-Co/n/we.'(l)Tus-fa.orTus-f.- pylorus pain, plethora andcorpulency. (2) Pain in pylorus - Tus-f. is as if a morsel had lodged at bottom of cardia. (3) Lumbago, Ant-t. (4) gonorrhea, Thuj. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke..

HERBAL - Tussilago petasites grows in Central and Northern Europe. Tussilago means “cough-wort.” According to Green’s Herbal, it is “a genus of Compositae established for three or four species of Tussilago, which have the flower-heads partially dioeceous in racemes, sometimes branching into panicles. “The essential characters which separate them from the common Coltsfoot (Tussilago farfara) are very slight and the foliage is the same” (Treasury of Botany). Tussilago petasites grows on river-banks that are little trodden on. The roots are an admirable medicine in the worst kind of fevers with boils or buboes.” A medicinal plant, it was used as a diaphoretic in the middle ages. Its pharmacological action is sudorific, diuretic, emmenagogue and anti-asthmatic. It has been used for uterine cramps, coughs, hoarseness and urinary disorders.

HOMEOPATHIC - In 1847 it was the object of a fragmented homeopathic proving by Kuchenmeister and in 1960 of a pharmacological study by Karl Haas. A recent pharmacological study of the root extract revealed a product with antispasmodic action. Tus-p. has some action on the urinary organs and was found useful in gonorrhea. Affections of pylorus. Irritation of the urethra. Crawling in urethra. Gonorrhea, yellowish, thick discharge. Erections with crawling in the urethra. Inflammation and pain of the spermatic cord. Lumbar pain. Pains in the frontal sinuses.

Tus-p. restored the discharge and then cured. Rosenberg referred to a writer who said of the plant that if it is macerated in water, the water will not spoil even if kept for years. name: Ulmus Fulva

PHARMACY - ulm. Ulmus fulva. Slippery elm bark. Ulmus campestris. Red elm. Moose elm. N. O. Ulmaceae of the Urticaceae. Grows in the mountains of Canada and Pennsylvania. Pounded dried inner bark. Decoction of dried bark. Tincture of fresh bark. Historical close: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Boils. Burns. Chilblains. Constipation. Deafness. Hemorrhoids. Herpes. Inflammations. Malnutrition. Ophthalmia. Pain. Sore throats. Syphilis. Ulcers. Wounds.

HERBAL - Slippery elm is an herbal diuretic, emollient, and demulcent. A decoction of the viscous inner bark is used as a poultice for painful inflammations. It may be used as such in all cases of weakness, inflammation of the stomach, bronchitis, etc. The coarse powder forms the finest poultice to be obtained for all inflamed surfaces, ulcers, wounds, burns, boils, skin diseases, purulent ophthalmia, chilblains etc. It soothes the part, disperses the inflammation, draws out impurities, and heals speedily. The finely powdered bark makes an excellent gruel or food, and in addition possesses as much nutrition as oatmeal. COMMENTS - In a case in which the mucus membrane of the rectum was dry and extremely painful, Burnett relieved the sufferings with 20 drop doses of the tincture. Cooper mentioned that the triturated bark gives much relief as a snuff in old vascular deafness with tubal obstruction. He could not speak too highly of this remedy, and are confident there is nothing to equal it in the world for its mentioned uses. Inflammation in the bowels of infants and adults has been cured, when all other remedies have failed, by an injection into the bowels of an infusion of 1 oz of powdered bark to 1 pt of boiling water, used while warm. Slippery elm is also used in lozenges to relieve irritation of the pharynx. The food or gruel should be made as follows: Take a teaspoonful of the powder, mix well with the same quantity of powdered sugar and add 1 pt of boiling water slowly, mixing as it is poured on. This may be flavored with cinnamon or nutmeg to suit the taste, and makes a very wholesome and sustaining food for infants. REFERENCES - Clarke. Cooper. Murphy. Potter’s Cyclopedia.

The inner bark and the root contain similar properties, but the inner bark is preferred over the root, because stripping the bark does not kill the plant. It is reputed to enhance immune functions, increase energy and stamina. An ideal tonic forthose who are mentally, emotionally and physically exhausted from overwork or excessive stress. Helps against viruses, radiation, chemical toxins and chemotherapy effects. COMMENTS - Hank, age 53, suffered from partial urinary blockage due to an enlarged prostate for over two years. After drinking three cups of cat’s claw tea daily, using one teaspoon full of the powdered herb per cup. He reported that his symptoms dramatically diminished after three days. REFERENCES - Murphy.

CLINICAL - Asphyxia. Backache. Conjunctivitis. Eye, pains. Hangnails. Headaches. Palpitations. Sexual, excess. Styes. Tetanus. Vision, disorders.

HOMEOPATHIC - Upa. is obtained from a Strychnos and must not be confounded with Antiaris toxicaria, the concocted juice of which forms the "Upas antiar" poison of the Javanese. S. tieute is a climbing shrub. Pitet made a courageous proving of it, carrying it to the length of producing tetanic symptoms. Upa. produces tonic spasms, tetanus and asphyxia. A large proportion of the symptoms occurred in the head and eyes. A remarkable headache, “superficial drawing pain traverses left temple from before backward and ceases at outer angle of orbit, the part is hot and painful to touch.” Pressure in the eyes, feeling of a foreign body under the eyelids. Severe pains in orbits inflammation of the conjunctiva of the lids. Distorted vision. “Every morning weakness of the eyes with lachrymation, the lids being so heavy that they close involuntarily as if from drowsiness.” Drowsiness. Pressive and lancinating pains. Pain in the left side of the throat as from a splinter on swallowing. Pain in left Upas tieute sciatic nerve in left iliac fossa. Chiefly affects the left-side. MIND - Irritable. Disinclined for mental work.

Head - Dull headache deep in brain.

Eyes - Dull, sunken eyes. Pain in eyes and orbits with conjunctivitis. Styes.

Mouth - Herpes on lips. Burning on the tongue. Pain in mouth, as from a splinter (Nit-ac,). Sensations - As if the brain were rudely shaken. As if a foreign body in eye, as if sand in eyes. As if a splinter in throat on swallowing. As if a foreign body in esophagus preventing swallowing. As if an iron hoop around waist preventing breathing. As after sexual excess. COMMENTS - Keynote sensitiveness. Irritability, crossness, moroseness increased sensitiveness to cold, the least irritation brought on spasms, pressing in throat causing feeling of suffocation. Vertigo, ending in pressing headache. Twitching in brain and orbits. Pulsative headache with throbbing all over body. Great exhaustion after convulsive seizures. Itching in patella. Sexual function depressed. Distressing symptoms after sex, as occur after sexual excess. Left half of face red and hot, right half pale and cold. The tongue is coated white so thickly that it can be scraped off. Aversion to meat and eggs, the very thought of them causes nausea. Smell of manure in nose. Sallow complexion. Severe symptoms in the liver and from the right lung to the liver (cutting as with knives). RELATIONS - Antidote: Cur. Compare: (1) Upas-a., Ox-ac. (2) Upas when Bry. fails (typhoid). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Male - Desire increased with loss of power.

Chest - Sharp pain throughout right lung toward the liver, stopping breathing.

Heart - Violent palpitations, sensation of heaviness in stomach.

Back - Dull backache, as after excessive sex. Causations - Sexual excess.

Limbs - Hangnails inflamed, itching and redness of nail roots. Numb hands, feet.

Modalities - Better after rising. Better evenings, after dinner. Headache better in open air. Pain in left iliac fossa worse by touch. Throat worse pressure. Worse by motion, walking. Worse morning, afternoon and evening.

PHARMACY - uran-n. Uranium nitricum. Uranium nitrate. Uranyl nitrate. Solution in distilled water. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Anal, itching. Ascites. Backache. Bedwetting, nocturnal. Bronchitis. Constipation. Debility. Diabetes mellitus. Diabetes insipidus. Dropsy. Duodenum, ulcer. Dyspepsia. Edema. Emacia- tion. Enteritis. Gastric, ulcer. Glycosuria. Impotency. Insomnia. Malassimilation. Milk, secretion. Nephritis. Nephrotic, syndrome. Neuralgia. Ophthalmia. Peritonitis. Phosphaturia. Seminal discharges. Stomach, ulcers. Stomatitis. Styes. Ulcers. Urine, incontinence. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - Uran-n. belongs to the chromium group of elements. Uran-n. was proved by E. T. Blake, his monograph forms part of Hahnemann’s Materia Medica. Blake’s proving was suggested by the observation of an old-school experimenter, Leconte, who found sugar in the urine of dogs slowly poisoned with Uran-n. Blake was not very successful in producing sugar, but his proving is not any less valuable on that account and clinical use has filled out the picture. Uran-n. causes glycosuria and increased urine. Produces nephritis, diabetes mellitus and insipidus, degeneration of the liver, high blood pressure and dropsy. Its therapeutic keynote is great emaciation, debility and tendency to ascites and general dropsy. Excessive thirst, nausea, vomiting, excessive appetite. Dry mucus membranes and skin. High blood pressure. Burning in the stomach, gastric ulcer. Incontinence of urine. Burning in urethra while passing urine. Impotency with nightly emissions. Backache and delayed menses. Menses suppressed during diabetes. The left side was more affected than the right. MIND - Ill-humor, not feeling well all day. Depression.

Head - Head heavy on waking. Heaviness of head with general languor. Dull, heavy pain. Heavy, burning, in right side of vertex. Shooting from right orbit extending to occipital protuberance, in evening. Frontal headache. Dull aching in right temple. Pain in forehead, over left eye. Pain in left temple, with feeling as if he had taken cold. Severe pain, at posterior edge of right and left temporal bones. Aching at occipital protuberance. Fullness of head. Sensation of blood flowing to head, before eating. Neuralgia on posterior edge of left temporal bone.

Eyes - Styes in left upper lid. Edema of lower lids, worse than usual. Lids inflamed, agglutinated. Shooting from right orbit to occipital protuberance in evening. Pain over left eye.

Nose - Itching in nose. Left nostril stuffed. Dry coryza. Nostrils sore with purulent acrid discharge. Chronic scabbing of inner nostril.

Mouth - Painless ulcer with one elevated side in mouth, opposite left anterior upper molar, worse evening. Acid saliva. Ulcers in mouth, with copious salivation.

Throat - Hawking of tenacious mucus. Contracted feeling in throat. Vertigo - Vertigo, faint, flushing of upper part of body during menses. Vertigo, worse in evening. Vertigo with heaviness of head. Vertigo with debility and cold feeling. COMMENTS - Many cases of diabetes have been relieved orcured by Uran-n., usually in the lower potencies. Diabetes with excessive thirst, polyuria and dry tongue. Glycosuriais by no means an essential part of the indications for Uran-n. Diabetes concomitant with indigestion, belching, burping, and heartburn. Urine with bile and sugar in it, can smell fishy. Kidney disease with protein in the urine, nephrotic syndrome. Stomach ulcers. Very weak (Ph-ac.), debilitated, tendencies toward dizziness. One case, involving a married woman, was cured with 5 grain doses of Uran-n. 2x. She was weak and emaciated, vomited mucus mixed with blood and coffee-ground matter and passed dark, tarry stools, sensitive and tender over region of pylorus. Dr. Choudhury noted a case of diabetes in a middle-aged man. The patient had progressive weight loss, weakness, and great weariness in the legs with edema. His tongue was coated white, severely dry mouth. Pale, looked haggard with dark circles. Neither Chin, or Phos-ac. helped. Uran-n 30c cured. The patient needed no insulin after treatment. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Elemental relatives, gastro-duodenal affections, Chrom. and Kali-bi. (2) Diabetes, Phos., Ph-ac., Syzyg., Thyr., Lac-def., Lac-ac. (3) Sinking immediately after meals, Ars., Cina, Lyc., Sil., Staph. (4) Craves tea, Sei. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Mur- phy-

Stomach - Constant faintness at stomach, even after a hearty meal. Indigestion in afternoon. Dyspepsia, flatus after food, acidity, pain. Tasteless, putrid belchings. Sinking at pit, with acid eructations, flatulence and copious urination. Boring pain in pyloric region. Burning pain. Gastric and duodenal ulcers. Recurring hematemesis. Nausea and vomiting.

Abdomen - Abdomen bloated. Borborygmi. Flatus. Sharp colic with tenesmus and raw feeling in rectum. Enteritis andperitonitis with meteorism and great prostration.

Rectum - Borborygmi. Constipation. Urging in rectum and bladder. Soft stool, twice in one day. Anal itching. Sensations - As if blood were flowing to head. As if he had taken cold with headache.

Male - Complete impotence with nocturnal emissions. Organs cold, relaxed, sweaty.

Female - Pale, anemic. Menses suppressed during diabetes. Flushing of upper body during menses, with giddiness and faintness. Excessive flow of milk. Food - Malassimilation. Ravenous appetite. Eating followed by flatulence. Excessive thirst with intermittent vomiting or with emaciation (diabetes). Loss of appetite during menses. Craves raw ham, tea, sweets. Intense thirst from sensation of dryness in mouth and fauces. Excessive thirst at night.

Chest - Intermittent pain, radiating from left side to ensiform cartilage, worse fasting.

Back - Pain at lower angle of left scapula, worse deep inspiration. Tenderness of spine near and extending to kidneys. Breasts - Excessive secretion of milk.

Limbs - Stiffness in loins. White vesicles on arms and legs with red areolae, burn and itch. Lungs - Bronchitis with copious mucus expectoration and much emaciation. Chronic colds. Hydrothorax and congestion of lungs. Lung infiltrated with gray tubercle.

Sleep - Restless, with shivering and heat. Extreme languor, on rising from bed. Feeling as if he had taken cold. Great drowsiness and prostration during menses. Restless at night during menses. Sleeplessness.

Skin - White vesicles on hands and legs, with red areola. Burning and itching. Ecchymo- sis. Epithelioma. Lupus exedens.

Modalities - Better from deep breathing. Worse at night. Headache worse walking.

Kidneys - Contracted, gouty kidneys, with gastric disturbances. Sore pain in bladder region in evening. Acute nephritis. Diabetes insipidus and mellitus. Incontinence of urine at night. Nocturnal bedwetting. Burning in urethra, with very acid urine. Sugar in the urine. Copious urination in cold weather. Diuresis. Unable to retain urine without pain. Urine often excoriating. Urine greenish and smelling fishy. Urine pale, milky, with ammoniacal odour. Profuse, painful urination.

Cough - Cough with purulent discharge from left nostril. Cough with loss of appetite and great prostration.

Temperature - Shivering, alternating with heat, at night, with great restlessness. Shivering during day.

PHARMACY - urea. Urea pura. Carbamide. Urea nitrica. The chief solid constituent of the urine of mammals. White crystals. Trituration. Also tincture or solution of the nitrate, Urea nitrica. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Cirrhosis. Coma. Convulsions. Diabetes. Dropsy. Eczema, gouty. Gout. Kidney stones. Liver, cirrhosis. Pleurisy. Skin, disorders. Tuberculosis. Uremia.

HOMEOPATHIC - On general indications, Urea, has been used in medicine by both schools. Merck mentioned that it is diuretic and is used in cirrhosis of liver, pleurisy, kidney calculus. The failure of the kidneys to eliminate urea from the blood leads to uremic intoxication, delirium, convulsions and coma. Tuberculosis. Lumps. Enlarged glands. Kidney dropsy with symptoms of general intoxication. Albuminuria, diabetes, uremia. Urine thin and of low specific gravity. Constant urging, much sediment in urine. Intolerable sensa tion in abdomen, with burning skin. Gouty eczema. General uneasiness, felt ill, poisoned. Urea acted as a nervous tonic in tuberculosis patients. Urea is a hydrogogue diuretic in the treatment of dropsies. 10 grains every 6 hours.

Head - Head very dull, as if filled with a very heavy lump.

Eyes - Itching and profuse watering of eyes.

Abdomen - In right hypochondrium, a steady, dull sensation. Intolerable sensation in abdomen and burning of the skin.

Kidneys - Constant urging to urinate, beginning at root of penis. Profuse diuresis with rapid diminution of dropsy. Albuminuria, bloody urine, general dropsy. COMMENTS - Burnett used both Urea 6c and Ur-ac. 6c in gouty eczema, “where the gouty eczema has been the cutaneous outlet for the constitution.” Burnett gave Urea in gouty cases where the urine was thin and of low specific gravity, “it thickens the urine and gives great relief to the patient.” Allen cited from Mauthner two cases of kidney dropsy with symptoms of general intoxication in which Urea, 2 grains., divided into three doses and given two hours apart, cured brilliantly. Arthur Buch related cases of tuberculosis cured, on the plan originated by Harper of Nottingham, with Urea in 20 to 30 grain doses three times a day. Underthe treatment, lupoid nodules disappeared, tuberculous glands disappeared, tuberculous joints improved. No ill-effects of the treatment were noticed, “on the contrary, the action has evidently been in many cases that of a nervous tonic.” Villers examined the urine of an intensely neurasthenic woman, suffering from severe asthma and found 4.5 percent of urea instead of the usual 2.5. In order to find out the effect of Urea, on the healthy, he took for five days Urea. 15x., five drops thrice daily. He was then compelled to stop by the severity of the symptoms. He gave the same dose to a patient, a woman. She begged after a short time to be allowed to discontinue the medicine, as it affected her so painfully, causing constant urging to urinate, much sediment in the urine intolerable sensation in abdomen and burning of the skin. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ur-ac. - gout, gouty eczema, rheumatism, lipoma. (2) Urt-u., Tub.,Thyr. (3) Urin., Ur-ac., Thiosin., Urt-u. (4) Diuresis, Thyr. (5) Tuberculosis, Tub., Bac. REFERENCES - Allen. Boericke. Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - Old urine has a higher ammonia content that is more effective on skin disorders as eczema and psoriasis. To store urine for later use, one should pour it into a glass bottle and close it tightly. Keep the bottle in a cool, dark place for long periods of time. Side effects can include headache, diarrhea, itching and rashes, pain, fatigue, soreness of the shoulder, and fever. An increase in symptoms of the specific illness may also occur. COMMENTS - S. Mills Folwer mentioned the use of urine as a remedy for scurvy in the Civil War. In Andersonville prison the starving prisoners were dying by hundreds of scurvy and Mr. T. (who told the story) was one of the sufferers. His legs were flexed upon the thighs and the thighs upon the body in such violent contraction that it was impossible to extend them an inch and any attempt to do so was attended with shocks of pain as from an electric battery. He could only move on his elbows and rump. Within the stockade were growing two large turpentine trees. Of the pitch from these trees the patients would take enough to make their urine “clear and white as crystal.” The urine voided was allowed to stand until it began to sour, which took twelve to twenty-four hours. The patients then took a “good swallow” four or five times a day. They felt the good effect of every dose. The treatment cured Mr. T. and all his companions in misfortune who adopted it. RELATIONS - Compare: Urea., Urin., Urac. REFERENCES - Murphy.

HOMEOPATHIC - Urine is one of the most ancient remedies and can be used topically, internally and in homeopathic potencies. An important component of urine is urea, a commonly recognized antibacterial, antifungal, and antiviral agent. The Chinese treated wounds by sprinkling urine on them and the custom is widespread in the Far East. It is a major therapy in Ayurvedic medicine and was commonly used in ancient India. It is a custom in Yorkshire to wipe the baby ’ s tongue with its own napkin in cases of thrush. For pimples and blotches the natives of Barbados drink their urine and apply it locally. Soldiers in Germany would urinate in their boots so they wouldn’t get sores and blisters on their feet from long hikes. In Switzerland, for cases of ophthalmia in children, it is the custom to bathe the eyes in the children’s own urine. Taken internally urine is believed to stimulate the circulation and is valued as an active oxytocic. Anasarca, generally more marked in upper than in lower parts of body. Heaviness, heavy for work, having neither his usual life nor warmth in him. Loses her breath if she walks quickly, is obliged to stop. Used for multiple sclerosis, colitis, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis. Cancer, hepatitis, pancreatic insufficiency, psoriasis, eczema. Diabetes, herpes, mononucleosis, adrenal Urinum humanum failure. Allergies. Premenstrual syndrome, easy labor, mastitis. Cancer.

Head - Heaviness of head, worse on stooping.

Face - The face is very much swollen. Countenance pale, expression heavy and vague.

Stomach - Little thirst. COMMENTS - In the Brit. Med. Jour, of 1900 a number of instances of Western urine therapy were given. Cooper made some additions to these. Cooper had a case of a youth with crops of boils which nothing could remedy. He was recommended to drink a cupful of his own urine every morning for three mornings. Then after an intermission of three days to resume and so on until cured. He was cured on the ninth day. Cooper mentioned the case of a man who suffered very much from weak and inflamed eyes until he began to bathe his eyes in his own urine, which after a time cured him. A case of blackheads was cured in exactly the same way. This patient drank the urine when fresh. A case of chronic bronchitis was much relieved. This patient was deaf and misunderstood the doctor’s direction to bring some of his urine. He thought the doctor said “drink,” and acted accordingly. Urine also cured ague and urticaria. Allen under Urea, gave some symptoms observed on a man who, for a skin affection, drank the morning the urine he had passed the night before. The symptoms were severe, consisting of general dropsy, scanty urine and excessive weakness. Cooper also mentioned that a celebrated breeder of cattle and horses succeeded in getting his animals’ skin into an astonishing condition of fineness by giving them about a tablespoonful of old human urine with every meal. Kraft mentioned that urine has been used as a remedy for croup. These cures are to some extent analogous with nosode cures, as the patients drank their own urine, but Urin., Urea., and Ur-ac. are also medicines on their own account and rank with the sarcodes. The symptoms of uremia may be taken as a pathogenesis of Urin. for the use of the potencies. Urea cured kidney dropsy and Urin. produced it. The skin action of Urin. is remarkable in connection with its use in the dressing of leather, no substitute having been found for it in this. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Urea. - probably urine owes its chief effect to urea. (2) Ur-ac., Urt-u. REFERENCES - Clarke. Murphy.

Abdomen - Ascites. Fluid in abdomen and in parietes of chest and belly.

Rectum - Diarrhea.

Skin - Acne. Boils. Burns and skin rashes. Eczema. Scar tissues. Psoriasis. Wounds.

Kidneys - Urine scanty, thick, deep brown and very offensive.

PHARMACY - uro-h. Urolophus halleri. Round sting ray. N. O. Urolophidae. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Backache. Catarrh. Chilly. Cramping, pain. Cough. Delusion. Diarrhea. Fainting. Fibromyalgia. Flatulence. Hay fever. Herpes. Hot flushes. Itching. Nausea. Nightmares. Nosebleed. Osteomyelitis. Palpitations. Tinnitus. Trembling. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sting ray venom is a protein which is water soluble. Low concentrations cause heart changes associated with bradycardia, mild hypotension and vasoconstriction. Some degree of respiratory depression is noted and convulsions may also occur. The pain is immediate and severe. Pain is constant, pulsating or lancinating. The area is quite swollen and pale with a bluish rim, spreading around the wound. Local necrosis, ulceration and secondary infection are common. Bleeding may be profuse. Symptoms may persist for weeks to months after an injury including a dull ache and swelling which is better on elevation. Osteomyelitis can occur and amputation has been known to be necessary. The venom is associated with anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, frequent urination and salivation. Muscular cramps, tremors, paralysis of the affected limb. Fainting, palpitations, hypotension. Heart rate irregularities. Difficulty breathing, cough, pain on inspiration. Fever at night with copious sweating. Nervousness, confusion or delirium are also known to occur. Similar to Sep. Chilly, but can’t stand stuffy rooms, gets faint in a stuffy room. Very sensitive to weather changes. Needs a lot of sleep. Apt to get headaches. Worse in morning, better in evening. Worse from light or jar. Worse tobacco smoking. Less sensitive than Sep. Low backache (Sep.), better moving about, does not come back once he moves about. Likes a cushion in the back. Menopausal hot flushes. Palpitations, felt as if heart is pushing out. Fibromyalgia. Hay fever. Chronic nightmares. Dreams of being chased by spirits, of being lost in a house. Tired, self pitying patients. MIND - Difficult concentration. Dullness of mind, worse mornings. Confusion on waking. Forgetful. Memory weakness, for proper names. Indifference. Want of confidence. Sadness on waking. Indolence. Aversion to company. Disagreeable thoughts. Censorious. Anxiety, paroxysms. Attacks of anxiety. Fear of animals, snakes. Fear that something bad will happen. Restlessness. Hurried, impatient. Irritability. Shrieking during sleep. Suspiciousness. Talks to himself. Daydreaming. Clairvoyance. Delusion floating in air. Delusion being persecuted. As if in a dream.

Head - Fullness. Head pain, in the morning, on waking, in the afternoon, evening, at night. Headache, worse in the afternoon, at night. Dull pain in the forehead. Pulsating pains.

Eyes - Discoloration, redness, morning. Itching. Pain, burning, lids.

Ears - Pain in right ear. Stopped sensation. General noises, synchronous with pulse. Tinnitus. Ringing noises.

Nose - Catarrh. Sneezing in the morning. Nosebleed, worse in the morning.

Face - Eruptions forehead. Acne. Herpes on lips.

Mouth - Aphthae.

Throat - Pain, in the morning, on the right, better warm drinks. Sore or sharp pains. Scratching in throat. Sensation of swelling. Choking, constriction in throat. Lump sensation, worse on swallowing. Swelling of cervical glands.

Stomach - Stomach cramps. Noises, rumbling. Pulsation. As if something alive in stomach. Nausea during cough.

Abdomen - Distension, evening. Noises, rumbling. Cramping pain. Flatulence.

Rectum - Diarrhea, in the morning. Painless diarrhea. Flatus after dinner, during diarrhea. Sensation - Bubbling sensation. Lassitude tendency. Weariness, worse mornings.

Urine - Strong odor. Vertigo - Dizziness. Faintness tendency, worse in the morning. Vertigo on rising, on turning or moving the head. Vision - Blurred vision. COMMENTS - Margery Blackie wrote about using Sting Ray in her book Classical Homeopathy. She described patients who needed Sting Ray as “sallow, usually dark who have rather heavy rings around their eyes. They look tired, are chilly yet at the same time cannot stand a stuffy room. They are sensitive to all weather changes, but as a rule can stand real heat. They tell you of their need to sleep, how many hours they need, how they must have it or else they are no good at all. “They get a slight headache as with Medusa, and like a Sepia headache, but even duller. It usually starts in the morning, strangely enough is usually better in the evening, and is made worse by noise or jarring, rather like Sepia although to a much lesser degree. “In women, you think the patient must be Sepia. They come in looking pale and drugged and very tired, with rather dark rings. You think they are going to be Sepia, but their chief complaint is of lower backache and gradually they tell you (and Sepia of course also tells you) that it always improves if they walk about. A Sepia backache goes away if the patient walks about. The only difference is that with Sting Ray it does not come back, but in Sepia it always comes back when they sit. “This type of patient also gets quite a lot of palpitations, the men as well as the women. If the men have a tendency to faint, they think their palpitations has something to do with it. “The woman gets palpitations quite a lot but forgets it again if she is walking. The history is typically that if she gets bad palpitations, and has to go out because she has a very busy morning, by the time she comes back from shopping it is gone, which surprises her very much but which is a good symptom. “They are rather tired-out patients, but in no way so despairing or such martyrs as Sepia. Sepia can be real martyrs if they go on getting tired out and have a lot to worry them, especially if they have to look after various members of the family and will not accept any help that is offered to them. Sting Ray patients are much less like this, but they do get rather hopeless. “One of these patients, the best case I had seen, was a dark, tall, rather tired looking man who used to faint if he had to stand for long. He found it humiliating when he had fainted at two cocktail parties where he had to stand for a long time. He asked if I would give him something to stop him doing that. He had a headache and said that when it came, it lasted more or less all day. but was always better in the evening. These patients also tend to be a bit sensitive to tobacco smoke and I think that this is why he had fainted. “In one year, just after using Sting Ray the first time, I had two soldiers who fainted continually, especially if they had to stand for an injection. Both of them had fainted half a dozen times each within the last so many weeks. They had had a lot of injections and had had to stand for rather long. “One of them had taken part in the Queen’s birthday parade and had fainted. He had been held up between two other soldiers who had held him on his feet until he came round again, but he felt frightful. Both these men did well on Sting Ray and neither of them ever fainted again.” RELATIONS - Compare: Sep., Lach., Medus., Murx. REFERENCES - Blackie.

Male - Sexual desire increased.

Female - Profuse menses. Menopausal hot flushes. Sexual desire decreased or increased. Food - Appetite diminished. Extreme thirst. Thirst at night. Desires fruit, vegetables, meat, sweets, cinnamon. Aversion to meat.

Heart - Palpitations.

Back - Back pain, extending into lower limbs, lying ameliorates. Backache, worse before menses. Aching pains in dorsal region. Lumbar pains. Breasts - Pain in breasts, worse motion.

Limbs - Eruptions on the hands. Itching of hand, ankles. Cutting pain in foot. Soreness of foot. Swelling of ankles, foot. Tension in shoulders. Twitching, upper arm. Trembling, worse mornings.

Sleep - Restless sleep. Sleeplessness from worries (Ambr.). Waking too early. Waking after midnight, 2 a.m. to 4 a.m. Amorous dream. Chronic nightmares. Dreams of animals, of water. Dreams of being chased by spirits, of being lost in a house, of murder

Modalities - Better in evening. Worse change of weather, stuffy room. Worse periodically. Worse in morning, after midnight, at 3 a.m., at 9 a.m. Worse afternoons. Worse from light, noise or jar. Worse tobacco smoking.

Cough - Night aggravates cough. Morning cough. Violent barking, dry cough. Hoarse cough.

Perspiration - Night sweats. Profuse sweats.

Temperature - Chilly, lack of vital heat. Sensation of heat. Menopausal hot flushes.

full:
PHARMACY - urt-u. Urtica urens. Stinging nettle. Urtica dioica. The Common Nettle has similar if not identical properties. N. O. Urticaceae. Tincture of the fresh plant in flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, tincture and lower potencies.

CLINICAL - Agalactia. Ague. Allergic, reactions. Anemia. Arthritis. Bee, stings. Breastfeeding, disorders. Burns. Deltoid, rheumatism. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Edema. Erysipelas. Erythema. Gout. Gravel. Hemorrhages. Hemoptysis. Hives. Intermittents. Itching. Leucorrhea. Malaria. Menorrhagia. Phlegmasia dolens. Kidney, colic. Kidney, stones. Neuritis. Rheumatism. Shellfish, allergy. Spleen, disorders. Throat, sore. Uremia. Uric acid, diathesis. Urticaria, nodosa. Vertigo. Whooping cough. Worms.

HERBAL - In Sweden, nettles are regarded as a remedy for anemia. Fresh nettles are cooked and eaten like spinach for the purpose, or a nettle-tea is prepared from dry nettles. The juice of nettles with sugar is popular for hemorrhages of all kinds. Used in gravel and urinary disorders. Gerarde noted several other uses, including how nettle juice inserted into the nostrils stops nosebleed. He added that it is “good against inflammation of the uvula.” Useful in pleurisy, pneumonia, and whooping cough. “Being eaten,” as Dioscorides said, “boiled with periwinkles, it make the body soluble, doing it by a kind of cleansing faculty, it also provoke urine and expels stones out of the kidneys, being boiled with barley cream it is thought to bring up tough humors that stick in the chest.” Gerarde noted that “The leaves or seeds of any kind of nettle do work the like effect, but not with that good speed and so assured as the Roman nettle [U. Pilulifera].” Cooper reported that “A bundle of nettles applied to a rheumatic joint or part, has long been a favorite country remedy. A leaf of the nettle placed on the tongue and pressed to the roof of the mouth stops bleeding from the nose.” Gerarde mentioned its antidotal action for snakebites. It’s also useful for bee stings. An application of the tincture, even on the most sensitive parts of the face or eyelid, gives instant relief. In cases of stings about the eyes, the application may have to be repeated every five minutes and a compress must be kept on all night.

HOMEOPATHIC - Commonly known as stinging nettle, Urt-u. produces stinging or stinging, burning pains. First degree burns, used locally and given internally. Bee stings (Apis). Urticaria, associated or alternating with rheumatism. Antidotes ill effects of eating shellfish. Rheumatic and gouty pains and fever were all evoked. Gout and rheumatism associated with urticaria-like eruptions. Among the rheumatic pains a pain in the right deltoid muscle is very striking. Neuritis. The right side very much affected, but also the left hypochondrium (spleen). Uric acid diathesis. Bedwetting and urticaria. Kidney stones. Gout and uric acid diathesis. Spleen disorders.

Head - Headaches, worse over eyes. Headache with stitches in spleen. Dull aching in occiput and over eyes. Stinging pain in right parietal bone. Urticaria of scalp suddenly appearing.

Eyes - Eyes feel weak and sore. Pain in eyeballs as from a blow. Feeling as if sand were in eyes.

Throat - Burning in throat. Frequent hawking of frothy mucus causing cough, expectoration scanty, frothy. Vertigo - Headache with spleen pains. COMMENTS - Severe allergic reactions (Apis., worse heat), particularly food allergies (Lyc., Bry.). Urticaria, weals, welts, and hives (Apis., Puls., Nat-m., Sulph.). Allergic reactions to bites or stings (Apis., Led., Hyper.). Dermographia, red and itchy skin, easily marked. Bright red shiny rashes that itch and sting. Vesicles (Canth.). Burns (Canth.). Old burns that refuse to heal. Shiny sunburns with a stinging, burning pain (Calen.). Palliative for herpes, canker sores. Fever blisters with stinging (Nat-m., Rhus-t.). Burning and itching of the anus and vulva. Allergic vaginitis, vaginal lips are swollen, red and inflamed, especially if due to some dietary reaction. Regulates milk production. For reactions to the fresh stinging nettle plant. Intermittent fevers, malaria (Ars., Nat-m., Chin.). Enlarged spleen, painful, often associated with viral infections (Nairn., Cean.). Gout, used in tincture. Arthritis or gout, in packs on the joints. A woman who had no children for three and a half years and had nursed none of her children took a pint of hot infusion of the herb. Her breasts swelled, then discharged serum, followed by copious milk. Burnett may be said to have rediscovered Urt-u. as a remedy. The history of how he came to use it is one of the most fascinating passages of his works. Burnett’s tincture is made of the small nettle, Urt-u., which is the variety used in homeopathy. Burnett noted that the nettle springs up everywhere near human habitations. He noticed it flourishing more by the side of ditches that carry off fluid sewage, thus possibly living to some extent on uric acid. Burnett’s discovery of its fever action occurred when a female patient was cured of ague (which he had not succeeded in helping) by drinking nettle-tea on the advice of her herbalist. Urt-u. was useful to him in cases of the fevers of the East India, Burma and Siam. It also has a marked anti-gout action. Urt-u. causes fever as well as cures it, and one of Burnett’s patients was obliged to stop taking it: “It sets all my pulses beating, makes me terribly giddy, makes me feel as if I was going to topple (forwards) on my head and then a bad headache comes on and when I take it at night, it makes me very feverish.” When she took the dose in the morning she did not have the fever, and Burnett said, “The fever of gout generally comes on at night.” With Urt-u., Burnett cured severe cases of uremia, vertigo. Burnett used Urt-u. a good deal in spleen disorders and found patients under its use often passed large quantities of gravel. Burnett gave Urt-u. to a middle-aged, unmarried woman who had enlarged spleen and “who smelled so strongly of nettles that it almost nauseated me whenever it was my duty to examine her.” While taking it, she passed large quantities of gravel, but this did not attract much notice, as the woman was in the habit of passing considerable quantities of gravel with her motions. She had localized abdominal pain preceding such an occasion by a number of days. The painful spot, just under her spleen, she called her “gravel-pit.” Putting this and other points together, including the fever action of Urt-u., Burnett concluded that Urt-u. was a remedy for acute gout, which would cut short the attack “in a safe manner, namely, by ridding the economy of the essence of the disease product, its actual suffering producing material.” He usually ordered five drops of the tincture in a wineglass full of warm water every two or three hours. Under its action the urine became more plentiful, dark and loaded with uric acid. J. L. Nottingham noted two cases cured with Urt-r. The first concerned Mrs. W., 38, tall, slender, with auburn hair, who had eczema vulvae with violent itching and burning. She had swelling and thickening of her labia. Smooth, pale, dry appearance of the mucus surface. A dry, scaly, fissured appearance of labia majora and skin. Thirteen years before, she had a sinus from the right ovary emptying into the uterus. The husband had sycotic warts on the glans penis. Urt-u. lx relieved all the symptoms and removed sexual excitement induced by the itching and uncontrollable desire to rub. The second case concerned Mr. N., 21, who had swelling, stinging, and burning of his face, hands and feet with redness. Rubbing with a fingertip would leave a white line for some time. When out in the cold, damp, snowy air, his hands, feet and face became purple-red, puffed and stinging cold. Going into a warm room he had increased swelling, stinging, itching all over him, especially of hands and face. Urt-u. relieved in twenty-four hours. In four days he returned home better than he had been for years. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Dock leaves (Rumex obtus.) rubbed on the stung part lessen the pain, also the nettle’s own juice and the juice from the common snail. Antidote to: Apis (bee-stings). Antidotal to hemlock, mushrooms, quicksilver, henbane, serpents, and scorpions. Compare: ( 1 ) Apis, Medus., Nat-m., Lac-c. (2) Ric. - diminished breast secretion. (3) Bomb-pr., Rhus-t„ Chlol., Astac. (4) Puls. - urticaria. (5) Bol-lu. and Anae. - urticaria tuberosa. (6) Lyc. and Hedeo. - uric acid conditions. Form. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Nausea with burning in throat. Vomiting from suppression of nettle rash.

Abdomen - Chronic disease of large intestine characterized by large secretion of mucus. Sore abdomen, when lying. Burnett noted it for liver tumors. Breasts - Swelling of the breast with stinging, burning pains. Diminished secretion of milk after childbirth. Arrests the flow of milk after weaning. Causations - Ill effects of burns, beestings, eating shellfish, suppressed milk, urticaria.

Rectum - Diarrhea. Frequent urging. Small, painful stool. Stool scanty, a greenish- brown slime, with urging and tenesmus. Mucus mixed with white matter like boiled white of eggs. Ascarides with great rectal irritation. Intense itching of anus from pinworms. Hemorrhoids with raw burning in anus during and after stool. Sensations - Burning, stinging, itching and soreness are the principal pains. As from a blow in the eyeballs. As of sand in eyes. Muscles of right arm as if bruised.

Urine - like odor of the body. Favors elimination. Dysentery. Burning and itching of anus. Hemorrhages. Angio-neurotic edema. Profuse discharge from mucus surfaces. Very periodic. Ague. Headache with spleen pain, rush of blood to head, sore abdomen. Affects the breast glands, genitourinary organs, liver and spleen. Increases milk flow. In the case given in Allen, it caused swelling of the breasts and profuse flow of milk in a woman years after the birth of her last child.

Male - Itching and stinging of scrotum, keeps him awake. Swollen scrotum.

Female - Uterine hemorrhage. Acid and excoriating leucorrhea. Pruritus vulvae with stinging, itching and edema.

Chest - Sore feeling as from a blow to left side of chest. Intermittent soreness in right chest during day. Hemoptysis from least exertion of lungs. Constitutions - Gouty constitutions. Uric acid diathesis.

Limbs - Rheumatic pain in arms and ankles, worse right arm. Continuous pain in deltoid. worse rotating arm inwards, difficulty dressing. Acute and chronic gout. Gout pain in ankles, wrists. Raised, red, itching blisters on skin of hands and fingers. Stiff soreness on inside of left knee. Lungs - Hemoptysis after violent exertion. Whooping cough. Scanty expectoration, frothy.

Sleep - Drowsiness when reading.

Skin - Burns and scalds. Sunburn with intense burning, itching. Vesicles. Burn confined to skin. Hives with rheumatism, after shellfish, with pinworms. Itching, raised, red blotches. Nettle rash, worse every year in the same season, suppressed nettle rash. Rheumatism alternates with nettle-rash. Chickenpox (Dulc.). Urticaria nodosa (Bov.). Urticaria, burning heat with formication, violent itching. Erythema with burning and stinging. Prickly heat. Angio-neurotic edema. Herpes la- bialis with sensation of heat and itching.

Modalities - Better from lying down. Worse water, cool bathing. Worse cool, moist air, snow-air. Worse by touch, lying on arm. Worse yearly. Hemoptysis worse from violent exertion. Burning in skin is worse after sleep.

Kidneys - Hemorrhage from bladder. Urine suppressed. Strangury, gravel, disease of bladder and kidneys. Uric acid toxemia. Acrid urine causing itching.

Temperature - General heat in bed with soreness over abdomen. Fever of gout. Tropical fever. Sweatiness, at night with vertigo, with throbbing all over the body.

PHARMACY - usn. Usneabarbata. Tree moss. Old Man’s Beard. Tree-hair. N. O. Lichenes. Tincture. The fresh lichen is macerated in five times its weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cystitis. Headaches, congestive.

HOMEOPATHIC - Usn. is for some forms of congestive headache, sunstroke. Keynote bursting feeling, as if temples would burst or the eyes burst out of the sockets. Throbbing carotids. Head began to ache, soon could feel the blood press into the brain with domestic attentions he got to sleep and woke next morning uncommonly well. Pain over entire head or front head with feeling as if temples would burst or eyes burst out of sockets. COMMENTS - Anshutz wrote, “This article appeared in No. 284 of the U. S. Medical Investigator signed ‘M.D.’ In March 1878, I was cutting wood. I cut down a soft maple, the top was well loaded with moss. It attracted my attention, I viewed it closely. “I ate a little, about the size of a hickory nut, asltrimmedupmy tree .Myheadbegantoache. I cut off one log and had to go to the house. I could feel the blood press to the brain. My wife worked over me and I got to sleep. “Next morning felt well, never felt better. I did not think of the moss I had eaten. I went on a visit and was gone five days. On my return I went to my tree. The first sight of it reminded me of my headache. I gathered some of the moss and made a tincture. I soon had a case of headache to try my remedy on, it stopped at once. “ In the fall, about September, a load of young folks came to pick cranberries. Two of the young ladies had headache from riding in the hot sun. Both took the lounge. Now for my remedy. I put one drop of tincture in a goblet of water, gave a teaspoonful ordered another in fifteen minutes. The second dose stopped the pain. “A young married lady came on a visit to a relative - was having pains in her head. I was sent for, found her wild with pain. She said she had been subject to headache for five years, had got tired of doctoring. Gave her one drop in a cup of water, teaspoonful in twenty minutes, no more pain. “I put ten drops in a two-drachm vial of alcohol, directed her to take one drop when she felt her headache coming on. One year after she wrote her friend it had cured headache, sent thanks to me. “I could give many more cases where the pain is over the entire head or front head with a feeling as if the temples would burst or the eyes would burst out of their sockets. I have always used the tincture. I have not noticed any other effect from it, would like to see a proving.” RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Lyc., Glon., Bell. Bry. (2) Tillandsia us. Spanish moss. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - Burt, who proved Ust. on himself and others, introduced the remedy to homeopathy. It had been observed that pregnant animals feeding on maize affected with smut were very liable to abort. Roullin noted that shedding of the hair and sometimes of the teeth, occurred in animals and men, that mules that fed on it cast their hoofs, and that fowls laid eggs without shells. Ust. affects the female sexual organs, skin, hair and nails. The provings brought out a specific affinity for the reproductive sphere of both sexes, especially for the left ovary and uterus. Ust. congests the uterus and produces hemorrhages, generally passive or in clots, dark and watery blood. Flabby condition of uterus. Uterine hemorrhage, menstrual, post-partum and menopausal. Bleeding fibroids. Bearing down, as if everything would come from her. As of a knot in uterus, bowels, throat etc. Suppressed menses without cause. Vicarious menstruation, bleeding from the lungs and bowels, and bleeding between the periods with left infra-breast pain. Crusta lactea (Viol-t.). Prostration from sexual abuse. Warm room causes oppression and faintness. Excessively tired feeling. Loss of hair and nails. Tumors have been seen to disappear after its use. MIND - Great depression of spirits. Weeps frequently. Irritability, worse being asked a question or to repeat anything. Could not bear to see or talk with anyone. The day seemed like a dream. Restless sleep.

Head - Sticky secretion matting hair. Milk crusts. Vertigo with white spots before the eyes, at menopause, with profuse menses. Nervous headaches from menstrual irregularities.

Eyes - Weakness of eyes. Hot feeling on closing lids. Lachrymation in open air. Lids agglutinated in morning. Spots in vision.

Nose - Boil in right nostril. Dryness of nostrils in forenoon with dry feeling in skin. Rhinitis, bitter taste offensive odor noticeable to patient himself. Bright nosebleed, better pressure.

Face - Sudden pallor in face, when sitting, in evening. Burning of face and scalp from congestion.

Mouth - Bitter, thin salivation. Coppery taste in morning. Tongue coated in morning. Prickling in tongue with feeling as if something were pressing the roots upward with dryness of nostrils.

Throat - Dryness of fauces with burning dryness in stomach. Feeling as if there were a lump behind the larynx, which produces constant inclination to swallow. Left tonsil enlarged. Vertigo - Full feeling. Nervous headache from menstrual irregularities. Aching in eyeballs with much lachrymation. COMMENTS - Bleeding fibroids (Sec.). Tendency toward miscarriage and passing of dark blood (Sec.). Heavy, dark menstrual flow, debilitating. Alopecia after childbirth. Hurndall related the case of a small female dog that brought out many features of Ust.’ s action. About a fortnight before he saw the dog, she had aborted five fetuses at about the fifth week of gestation. Since then, there had been passive hemorrhage of dark clots. Moreover, the dog was a perfect specimen of alopecia, not having a hair of any sort on her body and only a little about the head. The cervix os of the uterus was soft, spongy. Great tenderness about the posterior parts when manipulating the hindquarters. Ust. 3x was prescribed, five drops three times a day. In two days the hemorrhage was completely arrested, tenderness reduced, spirits revived and general health improved. At the end of three months there was a nice coat of hair growing, which in due course became perfectly normal. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sec., Sabin. Sep. (2) Thlaspi, Zea-i. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Stomach - Cutting in stomach. Burning in esophagus at the cardiac orifice. Belch- ings, of sour fluid, of sour food. Vomiting of blood, passive, venous, accompanied by nausea, better by vomiting.

Abdomen - Pain as if intestines were tied in a knot. Colic pains, better by hard stools or constipation. Cutting in umbilical and hypogastric regions. Pain in right lobe of liver.

Rectum - Loose, soft, dry, lumpy, black stool with pain and rumbling in abdomen. Light-colored diarrhea. Constipated. Sensations - As if head were being lifted off. As if forehead would burst open. As if something were under root of tongue pressing upward. As of a lump behind larynx. As if intestines were being tied in knots.

Male - Irresistible desire to masturbation. Emissions, every night and when talking to a woman. Spermatorrhea with erotic fancies and amorous dreams.

Female - Menses, half liquid, half clotted, bright red, discharge of blood from slightest provocation. Profuse menses after miscarriage. Foul, yellow or brown leucorrhea. Vicarious menstruation from lungs and bowels. Menorrhagia at menopause (Calc., Lach.). Oozing of dark blood, clotted, forming long black strings. Uterine fibroids, bleeding. Hypertrophy of uterus, sub-involution. Cervix spongy, easily bleeding. Post-partum hemorrhage. Profuse lochia. Ovaries burn, painful, swollen. Acute ovarian pain, worse left. Pains shoot down thighs. Uterus feels drawn into a knot. Bearing down pains when child nurses. Food - Poor appetite. Thirst at night.

Chest - Aching, burning distress in sternum. Heat and pressure. Constriction with pain. Oppression along the sternum.

Heart - Palpitations. Sudden flying pains from the heart to stomach, arresting breathing.

Back - Pain in back extending to extreme end of spine. Pain in region of right kidney. Dull pain in lumbar region with great despondency and mental irritability. Bearing down in sacral region as in dysmenorrhea. Sensation of boiling water flowing along the back. Breasts - Pain under left breast, at margin of ribs, between periods, constant. Constitutions - Adapted to tall, thin women, at menopause.

Limbs - Sensation of boiling water along the back. Muscular debility. Clonic and tetanic movements. Muscular contractions, especially of lower limbs. Cutting in bones of right hand and foot. Rheumatic symptoms in arms, fingers and legs. Feet swollen in morning.

Sleep - Restless night with fever, troubled dreams. Difficult falling asleep, then unpleasant dreams. Sexual dreams without emission.

Skin - Dry, hot skin. Congested feeling in skin. Tendency to boils. Psoriasis. Eczema, copper-colored spots. Pruritus, sunburn. Painful, destructive disease of nails. Alopecia.

Modalities - Colicky pains better by constipated stool. Ovaries worse from pressure. Menorrhagia worse rising and motion. Abdomen and eyes worse by touch. Riding in carriage aggravates backache. Walking aggravates frontal headache, pain in left groin, pain in loins. Swelling aggravates pains in tonsils. Open air causes Ustilago maydis lachrymation. Worse from menopause. Worse motion.

Teeth - Looseness of teeth. Aching all day in decayed upper first and second molars.

Kidneys - Tenesmus of bladder and incon- " tinence of urine. Urging. Light-colored, high-colored, red, acid, scanty or increased urine. No desire, but uneasiness.

Temperature - Abundant sweat. Pulse at first accelerated then enfeebled. Chills running up and down back. Heat at night. Internal heat with vertigo.
