PHARMACY - uva. Uva ursi. Bearberry. Mountain box. Red berry. Bear’s grape. Arctostaphylos. Arbutus uva ursi. N. O. Ericaceae. Tincture or trituration of dried leaves and fruit. Tincture of fresh leaves gathered in autumn. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, disorders. Cyanosis. Cystitis. Dyspnea. Dysuria. Gonorrhea. Hematuria. Kidney, disorders. Kidney, stones. Nausea. Pyelitis. Urinary affections. Urticaria. Uterine, hemorrhage. Vomiting.

HERBAL - Uva ursi is a good kidney tonic (Equis.), it helps prevent the formation of kidney stones and tendencies toward bladder infections. A few experiments have been made with Uva ursi that have seemed to confirm its traditional reputation as an “astringent used to check excessive secretion of mucus, as in urinary and bronchial disorders and even in kidney stones.” The leaves are principally astringent, with which they combine mild tonic and soothing properties. It increase the flow of urine and particularly show their influence upon the uro-genital tissues. In chronic and sub-acute mucus discharges-such as catarrh of the bladder, leucorrhea, gonorrhea, and gleet it lessens the discharge gradually and giving tone to the parts. The tincture of the leaves may be used in chronic diarrhea and dysentery. Especially suited to an ulcerated condition of the bowels. Uva ursi has been used as a tonic and astringent in a bleeding stomach, bowels and kidneys. It is more soothing to the stomach than nearly any other astringent.

HOMEOPATHIC - Diabetes, gravel and strangury. Pyelitis. Kidney stones. Aching of the kidneys and bladder, congestion and ulceration of the bladder and prostate gland, involuntary seminal emissions, and incontinence of urine. Characteristic shooting pain from hip to hip. Chronic bladder irritation with pain, tenesmus and catarrhal discharges. Cystitis with bloody urine. Burning after the discharge of slimy urine. Slime passes with blood. Bladder symptoms are better lying on the back. Painful dysuria, with frequent but difficult discharge of thick, ropy urine of strong, pungent odor. Constant urging to urinate and straining, with discharge of blood and slime. Straining without any discharge at all, or only a few drops of urine. Cutting and burning pain in urethra, which is followed by discharge of blood. Dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, pulse small and irregular. Uterine hemorrhage. Cyanosis. Urticaria without itching.

Head - Slight vertigo and headache.

Nose - Fluent coryza with rawness.

Face - Flushing.

Throat - Hoarseness with pain in bowels, stopped up in throat, no appetite. Throat tickles, feels like coughing all the time, sore and bruised all over. Cough, nose raw and burning, cutting and burning on urinating. COMMENTS - Uva. should be remembered when there is a spasm of the bladder with straining and a discharge of pus, tenacious and clots of blood. It is recommended for hematuria, painful burning urine. Slimy or purulent urine. Calculi of the bladder. Dropsy, depending on disease of the heart or liver. Leucorrhea and lingering gonorrhea in females. In one cured case there were pains shooting through from hip to hip. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sec., Cann-s. (2) Arbin. - a crystallized glucoside of Uva, found also in Kalm., Gaul, and other genera of the family of Eriacee, given in doses of 3 to 8 grains with sugar three times a day. Used as a urinary anti-septic and diuretic. (3) Arctosphylos manzanita - acts on kidney and reproductive organs. Gonorrhea, bladder catarrh, diabetes, menorrhagia. Tincture of leaves. (4) Vacc-m., Huckleberries - dysentery, typhoid, keeps intestines aseptic and prevents absorption and re-infection. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Stomach - Weak, sick at stomach, sore all over as if bruised.

Chest - Uneasy tightness with a sensation of weight at the chest.

Kidneys - Pyelitis. Kidney stones. Frequent urging with severe spasms of bladder, burning and tearing pain. Urine contains blood, pus and much tenacious mucus with clots in large masses.

Bladder - Cystitis. Involuntary urination, green urine. Painful dysuria.

full:
PHARMACY - vac. Vaccininum. Cowpox vaccine. Vaccinia. Vaccinotoxinum. Lymph from cowpox vaccination pustule. Nosode. Trituration of vaccine matter. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Chickenpox. Conjunctivitis. Eczema. Keloids. Keratitis. Headaches. Hematuria. Herpes. Iritis. Leprosy. Malaise. Menorrhagia. Neuralgias. Nephritis. Nevus. Scars. Smallpox. Sycosis. Tumors. Vaccinosis. Whooping cough.

HOMEOPATHIC - Vaccinosis, smallpox and cowpox are inter-related diseases and the nosodes of each are available for the treatment or the prevention of manifestations of all three. The vaccine poison is capable of setting up a morbid state of extreme chronicity, named “vaccinosis” by Burnett. It may do this without causing the primary symptoms, when the vaccination apparently does not “take.” The symptoms of vaccinosis are protean and are, for the most part, identical with the symptoms of the sycosis of Hahnemann; vaccinosis is a sycotic disease. Leading features of the vaccinosis miasm include neuralgias, inveterate skin eruptions, chilliness, and indigestion with great flatulent distention. Vac. has skin eruptions, new growths, sycotic conditions. Restlessness. General malaise. Languor, lassitude. Tired all over with stretching, gaping feeling, unnatural fatigue. Child wants to be carried. Many persons faint when being vaccinated. Vaccinosis is related to whooping cough. An old-school observer vaccinated a child while they were suffering from whooping cough, and the whooping cough vanished. Burnett repeated the experiment in other cases with such success that he wrote to the journals to recommend it as a routine practice in the case of unvaccinated children. On the other hand, homeopaths have observed whooping cough immediately after a vaccination and have cured it with Thuj. 30c. MIND - Capriciousness. Confusion, she does not remember things at the time she wants them. Desired to be carried. Restlessness. Ill-humor, with restless sleep. Irritable, impatient, nervous. Crying. Disposition to be troubled by things. Morbid fear of getting smallpox.

Head - Eruption like crusta lactea. Frontal headache. Forehead and eyes feel as if split. Forehead felt as if it would split in two in median line from root of nose to top of head. Stitches in right temple. Prickling in left temple, as if going to sleep.

Eyes - Keratitis after vaccination. Tinea tarsi and conjunctivitis. Conjunctivae painfully sensitive. Weak eyes. Inflamed and red eyelids. Redness of eyes and face with small pimples on face and hands. Gauzy sensation before eyes in morning, cannot see well.

Nose - Full feeling of head with running at nose. Bleeding at nose preceded by a feeling of contraction above and between eyebrows, soon after eating meat. Sensations - As if forehead were split. As if head or over-exerted in lower limbs. As if bones of leg were broken and undergoing process of comminution.

Face - Redness and distention of face.

Mouth - Dry mouth and tongue. Tongue coated, dry yellow with papillae showing through coat.

Stomach - Aching in pit of stomach with shortness of breath.

Abdomen - Stitches felt in liver and spleen. Abdomen is bloated up with flatulence. Anns - Severe pains in left upper arm at vaccination mark. Rheumatic pains in wrists and hands. Keloids on re-vaccination marks.

Female - Menses rather profuse and too frequent. Food - Appetite gone. Disgust to taste, smell and appearance of food. Coffee tastes sour.

Chest - Stitch in left side of chest, anteriorly, under short ribs. Stitches in right side under short ribs, in front from right to left, then at corresponding place in left side, but from left to right, lasting five minutes.

Heart - Febrile action of heart, arteries.

Back - Backache. Aching pain in back, worse in lumbar region, extending around waist. Chill running down back. Twisting pain in lower back. Weakness in small of back coming on suddenly, ameliorated by lying down.

Neck - Swelling of neck under right ear (parotid gland), with sensation like being cut.

Limbs - Tearing in left thigh downward. Soreness of lower limbs, as if heated or . over-exerted. Legs ached immoderately, hardly able to get about. Break-bone sensation and a feeling as if bones were undergoing process of comminution (Eupper.). Twisting pains in both knees.

Sleep - Waked in middle of night by pain in forehead and eyes as if split and stinging in temples.

Skin - Hot and dry. Eruption like variola. Small pimples develop at point of vaccination with fourth dilution. Red pimples or blotches in various parts, most evident when warm. Eruption of pustules with a dark-red base and a round or oblong elevation, filled with pus of a greenish-yellow color, resembling varioloid, some as large as a pea, some less without depression in the center, coming with a round, hard feel in the skin (like a shot), very itchy.

Liver - A stitch in hepatic region, at margin of last lower rib, axillary line. Lungs - Short breath with aching in pit of stomach and pressure in region of heart. Whooping cough.

Kidneys - Nephritis with albuminuria, hematuria and dropsy, developed after vaccination.

Temperature - Fever with heat, thirst tossing about, crying, aversion to food. Chill with shaking. COMMENTS - Tingling, burning in skin over whole body, most intense in forehead skin and in lower and anterior portion of hairy scalp, which are tinged with a scarlet blush or efflorescence, similar to the immediate precursor of variola-like eruption. Garrison was consulted by a woman, 50 of a tubercular family. She had consolidation of both apices, had been losing flesh for three months, with severe night sweats. Almost constant, hacking cough with considerable expectoration at times. She was given one dose of Vac. 200c. In a week she reported that she had not had a severe coughing spell since the dose and for the last three days hardly any cough at all. She received one dose of Vac. a week, and at the end of six weeks returned to business. Vaccinating on a nevus in a child can destroy the growth by its inflammation and subsequent scarring. Frolich related the case of a child, age 6, who had well-developed nephritis seven days after vaccination with calf vaccine. The first symptom was puffed eyelids, then pain and swelling of the scrotum. On the fourteenth day, the urine contained blood, the inguinal glands were enlarged and tender, with slight edema of the legs. The urine contained blood and alumen for another month, when he recovered. Other similar cases have been observed. Burnett said the worse time of Vac. is the early morning. “Waked in middle of night by pain in forehead and eyes as if split and stinging in temples.” Vaccininum 6c in water, for one day with strict diet, repeated after eight days, acted as a preventive in six hundred cases. It treated many cases of variola and varioloid. Vaccininum 200c quickly relieved the severe symptoms of variola occurring in a child, aged six months. Two days before appearance of eruption the child had been re-vaccinated (after an interval of eight days) on a nevus near right nipple. Swallowing difficult through implication of tongue and fauces. Pustules, many of large size, scattered over scalp, face, body and limbs. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Thuj., Vario., Apis, Sulph., Ant-t., Sil., Maland. Compare: ( 1 ) In smallpox - Vario., Maland., Thuj., Ant-t. Sarr. (2)Nephritis - Apis, Merc-c. (3)Tubercu- losis - Bac., Tub. (4) Whooping cough - Dros., Thuj., Meph., Coc-c., Cor-r. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

PHARMACY - vacc-m. Vaccinium myrtillus. Bilberry. Whortleberry. Black whortles. Whinberry. Trackleberry. Huckleberry. Bleaberry. Hurtleberry. Vaccinium fron- dosum. N. O. Ericaceae, Vacciniaceae. CLINICAL - Arthritis. Cataracts. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysentery. Eye, disorders. Eyestrain. Glaucoma. Gout. Hemorrhoids. Indigestion. Macular, degeneration. Malaria. Myopia. Nausea. Night- blindness. Retinitis. Scurvy. Ulcers. Vaccinosis. Vision, disorders. Wounds.

HERBAL - The name Bilberry (by some old writers “Bulberry”) is derived from the Danish “bollebar,” meaning dark berry. Bilberry is a close relative of cranberry and the natural order is allied to the Ericaceae. Bilberries are used in making jams, preserves, liqueurs, and wines. The leaves can be used in the same way as those of Uva ursi. A decoction of the leaves or bark of the root may be used as a local application to ulcers, and in ulceration of the mouth and throat. A tea made of the leaves is also a remedy for diabetes if taken for a prolonged period. The fruits are astringent, and are especially valuable in diarrhea and dysentery, in the form of syrup. They are also used for discharges, and as antigalactagogues. It is helpful in scurvy and urinary complaints, and when bruised with the roots and steeped in gin has diuretic properties valuable in dropsy and gravel. Bilberry contains nutrients needed to protect eyes from eyestrain or fatigue, and can improve circulation to the eyes. It works by improving the microcirculation and regeneration of the retina. British Royal Air Force pilots during World War II, ate bilberry preserves before night missions as an aid to night vision. Clinical experience confirms that, when given orally, it improves visual accuracy in healthy people, and can help those with eye diseases such as pigmentosa, retinitis, glaucoma, and myopia. Cataracts and macular degeneration. Poor vision and night blindness. The dried fruit and tea has been used as a treatment for diarrhea and as a relief for nausea and indigestion. For mild inflammation of the mucus membranes of the mouth and throat. Stomach problems and irritated digestive tract.

HOMEOPATHIC - Vacc-m. is applicable to vaccinosis, malarial and dysenteric cases. Eye disorders. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Diabetes. Dr. A. H. Croucher, in an article published in the Homeopathic Review, gave cases of inveterate diarrhea cured by it. His experience has been repeatedly confirmed. Clarke always used it in the herbal tincture, generally giving 5 drop doses every four hours. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sima., Chin., Rheum., Merc. REFERENCES - Clarke. Murphy.

Worse from rest, standing, sitting, stooping, touch. Worse excitement. Worse fasting. Worse from open air, draft. Worse noon, evening, darkness, before midnight..

full:
PHARMACY - valer. Valeriana officinalis. Valerian. N. O. Valerianaceae. Tincture of the fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma, spasmodic, nervous. Bedsores. Clairvoyance. Coxalgia. Headaches. Heart, palpitations. Heels, pain. Hypochondriasis. Hysteria. Insomnia. Levitation, sensation. Menopause. Nervousness. Neuralgia. Sensitive. Sciatica. Sleeplessness. Toothache.

HERBAL - Valeriana officinalis is usually found in moist hedgerows or on the banks of ditches and streams. The peculiar fetid odor of Valerians is probably due to the presence of Valerianic acid. It is especially agreeable to cats, who become intoxicated with it. The Treasury of Botany noted that “Volatile oil of Valerian seems not to exist naturally in the plant, but to be developed by the agency of water.” Valerian root is largely relaxant and moderately stimulant. It is a mild stimulant to the circulatory and nervous system. It is an antispasmodic, laxative, diaphoretic and anthelmintic. A nervine and antispasmodic in cases of irritability, restlessness, hysteria, and nearly all forms of acute nervousness, insomnia, calming the brain, inducing quietude and sleep. The most valuable uses to which it can be put, are cases of nervousness, restlessness, and hysteria. If large doses are employed, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and hiccough, with frequent urination, result. If it is long continued, as state of low, melancholy and hysterical depression results. The heart’s action is increased, the temperature raised and formication of the hands and feet is complained of.

HOMEOPATHIC - Valer, first appeared in homeopathic medicine in Stapf s Additions, the article on it was written by Franz, and Hahnemann and Stapf were among the pro vers. Valerian produces over-sensitiveness of the nerves, spinal, genitourinary. Affects the mind, muscles, calf, heels, and Achilles tendon. Hysteria, over-sensitiveness, nervous affections. Lack of reaction, when apparently well-chosen remedies fail. Alternating symptoms. Mentalandphysi- cal dispositions change suddenly and go to extreme. Red parts turn white. Constant heat and uneasiness. Insomnia. Profuse sweat at night. Pains are darting, tearing, move outwards, are felt here and there or come and go, jump from one place to another. Epileptic fits. Paralysis and contraction of limbs, hysterical. Agitation of all nerves, jerks, twitches, trembling. Restlessness, impulse to move, cannot keep still. Weak, single parts, eyes, arms, wrists, popliteal etc. Globus hystericus. Illusions of vision, hearing, smell or taste. Slight injury causes spasms. Straightening out limb aggravates sciatica. Hysterical flatulence. Bedsores form soon in typhoid. Sensation of a thread hanging down from esophagus. MIND - Mental disturbances passing from one extreme of emotions to another, from the highest joy to deepest grief, from mildness to grumbling. Changeable disposition and moods. Impatience, passes quickly from one subject to another. Tremulous. Over-sensitiveness (Staph.). Irritable. Anger. Mad, raving, swearing. Hysterical spasms and disorders generally. Wriggles or squirms about. Inclined to faint. Hysteria, dreads being alone and especially in the dark. Hallucinations at night. Erroneous ideas, thinks she is someone else, as if all around were strange and disagreeable. Delusions of animals, men. Feels light, as if floating in air.

Head - Headache, which appears suddenly or in jerks. Fullness as from rush of blood to head. Pressive headache. Headaches, better moving about, worse sunshine. Moving eyes aggravates headache. Sensation of great coldness. Pressure in forehead. Bending head back aggravates pain in occiput.

Eyes - Swelling and painful sensibility of eyelids. Myopia. Brightness and light before eyes in a dark room, vision sharp. Sparks before eyes. Objects seem too near eyes. Wild look.

Ears - Otalgia with spasmodic drawings. Jerkings in the ears. Hyperesthesia. Earache from exposure to drafts and cold. Nervous noises. Tinkling and ringing in the ears. Illusions of hearing, imagined he heard the bell tinkle.

Nose - Violent sneezing.

Face - Pain appears suddenly and jerks. Muscles twitch. Cheeks red and hot in open air.

Mouth - Rancid, greasy taste. Bitter taste on tip of tongue. Tongue thickly coated. Nausea felt in throat. White blisters on tongue and upper lip, painful when touched. Toothache with shooting pain.

Throat - Choking in throat-pit on falling asleep, wakes as if suffocating. Pharynx feels constricted. Sensation as if a thread were hanging down throat with salivation and vomiting. Nausea felt in throat. Vertigo - Vertigo on stooping, feels light, as if floating. Head confused, as after intoxication. Intoxication and dizziness with absence of ideas. Whirling in head when stooping forwards. COMMENTS - Franz wrote that it was the custom among women in Germany to take Valerian almost as frequently as coffee. He attributed much of the nervous suffering, then prevalent, to this practice. “There is scarcely a remedy,” he said, “which communicates its primary as well as secondary action to the organism with more intensity than Valer.” He referenced his own eye symptoms, which were both severe and remarkable, though he had no tendency to anything of the kind before. His symptoms were excited at intervals for four months afterwards, the cause was frequently unknown, showing the deep action on the organism. Franz recorded burning, smarting and pressure in the margins of the eyelids, which seemed sore and swollen. There were also hallucinations of hearing and of sense. “Imagines she is some one else and moves to the edge of the bed to make room.” “Anxious, hypochondriac feeling, as if the objects around him had been taken from him, the room appears to him desolate, he does not feel at home in the room, he is compelled to leave it.” “As if in a dream.” “The many inveterate spasms of the stomach and abdomen. The incurable cases of hysteria and hypochondriasis. Moral disturbances, passing from one extreme of emotion to another. From the highest joy to the deepest grief from leniency. Kindness and mildness to grumbling impatience, obstinacy and quarrelsomeness from a sinking of the vital forces. A painful craving for stimulants to the greatest liveliness and extravagance and vice versa.” In Franz’s opinion, tedious convalescence after nervous fevers, and paralysis and contractions of the limbs, were owed less to the original intensity of the disease than to the Valer, with which the patients had been dosed. They were only saved from worse effects because Valer, was frequently given in combination with one or more of its antidotes. Franz noted that the first and most rapid effect of Valer., which precedes any after symptoms, is an acceleration of the pulse and congestion of the head. Symptoms of the upper and lower limbs alternate frequently. Principally produces symptoms at noon Valeriana officinalis and early afternoon, and the hours before midnight. The abdominal symptoms are particularly felt in the evening. Disturbed digestion. Fetid tallow taste before dinner. Flat, slimy taste early in the morning, on waking. Nausea begins in umbilical region, rising into pharynx. Darting, tearing pains that come and go. Pains appear suddenly. Tearings, cramps, better morning. Constant heat and uneasiness. Restlessness. Nervous irritation, cannot keep still. Tissot recommended Valer. for epilepsy. Nash cured a severe case of sciatica in a pregnant woman based on the symptoms, “pain worse standing and letting the foot rest on the floor.” She could stand with the foot resting on a chair or lie down in comfort. Hering said it met “Nervous disorders occurring in excitable temperaments. In hypochondriasis it calms the nervousness, abates the excitement of the circulation. “It removes the wakefulness, promotes sleep and induces sensation of quietude and comfort. Sadness is removed in globus hystericus in all asthmatic and hysterical coughs. Nervous palpitations, profuse flow of limpid urine. Red parts become white.” RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Bell., Camph., Cina, Coff., Puls. Antidote to: Merc., abuse of Chamomile tea.

Stomach - Weak stomach and digestion. Sense of something warm rising from stomach and causing suffocation Cramps in stomach. Foul belchings, like bad eggs. Heartburn with gulping of rancid fluid. Nausea with faintness. Child vomits curdled milk in large lumps after nursing after mother’s anger.

Abdomen - Abdomen inflated and hard. Hysterical cramps. Spasms, cramps in bowels after food and at night in bed. Flatulence. Draws abdomen in involuntarily.

Rectum - Ascarides. Hemorrhoid pain from worms. Painful borings in rectum. Bubbling pressure above anus in region of coccyx. Loose evacuations, greenish, papescent, and bloody stool. Thin, watery diarrhea with lumps of coagulated milk, with violent screaming in children. Discharge of blood from anus. Sensations - Pressure of hand or covering with hat causes icy coldness on vertex. As if flying in air. As if eyes would be pierced from within outward. As if smoke in eyes. As if a thread were hanging down throat. Like lead in limbs. Lightness in leg. As if strained in right ankle. As if bruised in outer malleolus of right foot.

Male - Creeping and drawing in of penis, as if it had gone to sleep.

Female - Menses late and scanty (Puls.). Neurasthenia of sexual organs. Food - Voracious hunger with nausea, as if from navel.

Chest - Sudden stitches in chest and liver from within out. Eruption of small, hard nodosities on chest. Constitutions - Hysterical women who have taken too much chamomile tea. Nervous, irritable, and hysterical subjects in whom the intellectual faculties predominate and who suffer from hysteria and neuralgia.

Heart - Stitching in heart with quick, small and weak pulse.

Back - Lancinations in left lumbar region above hip, worse when standing and especially when sitting, than when walking. Rheumatic pains in the shoulder blades. Causations - Injuries, slightest injury causes spasms.

Limbs - Rheumatic pains in limbs. Heaviness. Sciatica, pain worse standing and resting on floor (Bell.), stretching limbs, better walking. Pain in heels when sitting. Crampy pain, electric-like shocks in humerus (left), wakes from sleep. Constant jerking. Tensive pain in the calves, worse crossing legs. Cramps in biceps (right) while writing. Cramps of hands and feet prevent sleep. Pain from calf to heel. Legs feel light after walking. Lungs - Choking in throat on falling asleep. Wakes as if suffocating. Spasmodic asthma, convulsive movements of the diaphragm. Obstructed respiration and anguish in chest.

Sleep - Sleeplessness with nightly itching and muscular spasms from excitement, worse on waking. Cannot sleep before midnight. Insomnia, during pregnancy and menopause. Di sturbed sleep with tossing and anxious, confused dreams.

Skin - Skin too dry and warm. Painful eruptions. Eruption of small nodosities, at first red and confluent, then white and hard.

Modalities - Better after a meal, after breakfast. Better after sleep. Better changing position, walking about, motion. Rubbing helps cramp in calf. Worse from rest, standing, sitting, stooping, touch. Worse excitement. Worse fasting. Worse from open air, draft. Worse noon, evening, darkness, before midnight.

Compare - (1) Asaf., Ign., Croc., Castor. (2) Am-val., Zinc-val. - in neuralgia, gastric disturbance and great nervous agitation. Insomnia. Feeble, hysterical nervous patients. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy-

Kidneys - Much straining and prolapsed rectum during urination. Urine increased and more frequent in nervous women. Urine contains a white, red or turbid sediment.

Temperature - Chilliness, generally begins in neck and runs down back. Body ice cold with nausea and vomiting. Sensation of icy coldness (Helo., Camp., Abies-c.). Heat predominates. Fever composed of disagreeable heat only. Long lasting heat, often with sweat on face. Sudden gushes of sweat, mostiy on foreñead.

HOMEOPATHIC - Valium is used in the treatment of anxiety disorders and for short-term relief of the symptoms of anxiety and panic. It is also used to relieve the symptoms of acute alcohol withdrawal. To relax muscles, to relieve the uncontrolled muscle movements caused by cerebral palsy and paralysis of the lower body and limbs. Used to control involuntary movement of the hands (athetosis), to relax tight, aching muscles, and to treat convulsive disorders such as epilepsy. Loss of muscle coordination. Uncontrolled movements of body, including the eyes. Tremors, vertigo, dizziness. Increased sensitivity to touch and pain. Confusion. Depression. Anxiety. Over- stimulation, rage, seizures. Drowsiness, fatigue, light-headedness. Unusual tiredness or weakness. Slow heartbeat. Low blood pressure. Headache. Blurred vision, double vision. Hallucinations. Yellowing of eyes and skin. Skin rash, sleep disturbances. Changes in salivation. Slurred speech and other speech problems. Nausea. Difficulty urinating, or inability to hold urine. Constipation. Changes in sex drive. MIND - Mental confusion. Dullness of mind. Memory loss. Disorientation. Slurred speech and other speech problems. Depression. Anxiety. Delirium tremens. Agitation. Overstimulation and rage. Paradoxical reactions such as acute hyper-excited states. Unusual excitement, nervousness or irritability. Feelings of suspicion or distrust. False sense of well-being. Abnormal thinking. Behavior changes, including aggressive behavior, bizarre behavior, decreased inhibition, or outbursts of anger. Hallucinations. Delusions, holding false beliefs that cannot be changed by facts. Loss of sense of reality.

Head - Headache.

Eyes - Blurred vision. Diplopia. Nystagmus. Yellow eyes. Sensitivity of eyes to light.

Ears - Increased sense of hearing.

Mouth - Changes in salivation. Watering of mouth. Dryness of mouth. Slurred speech. Ulcers or sores in mouth.

Throat - Sore throat. Laryngospasm and pain in throat or chest. Ulcers or sores in throat. Vertigo - Fainting and dizziness. COMMENTS - Withdrawal symptoms, similar in character to those noted with barbiturates and alcohol have occurred following abrupt discontinuance of valium. Convulsions, tremors, abdominal and muscle cramps, vomiting and sweating. REFERENCES - Murphy.

Stomach - Increased thirst. Hiccoughs. Nausea and vomiting.

Abdomen - Abdominal cramps.

Male - Changes in libido.

Female - Changes in libido.

Heart - Fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat. Bradycardia. Cardiovascular collapse. Hypotension.

Limbs - Muscle spasms, weakness. Ataxia. Staggering. Dysarthria. Tremors. Tingling, burning, or prickly sensations. Trembling or shaking. Venous thrombosis and phlebitis at the site of injection. Lungs - Increased bronchial secretions. Coughing. Depressed respiration. Dyspnea. Hyperventilation.

Sleep - Sleep disturbances and stimulation. Insomnia.

Skin - Skin rash, itching. Urticaria. Jaundice. Unusual bleeding or bruising.

Kidneys - Incontinence. Urinary retention.

Perspiration - Increased sweating. Rectum - Constipation.

Temperature - Fever and chills.

PHARMACY - vanad. Vanadium metallicum. Vanadium metal. (At. Wt. 51.2). Burnett used the soluble ammonium salt. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Addison’s disease. AIDS. Anemia. Anorexia. Arteriosclerosis. Atheroma. Blindness. Brain, softening. Bronchitis. Bulimia. Cachexia. Cancer. Colds. Constipation. Debility. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Emaciation. Eye, disorders. Fatty, heart. Growth, retarded. Hysteria. Immune, weakness. Indigestion. Liver, disorders. Malnutrition. Metabolism, disorders. Osteoporosis. Paralysis. Pneumonia. Raynaud’s syndrome. Retinitis. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Thyroid, disorders. Tonsillitis. Tuberculosis. Vertigo. Warts. Weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Vanad. has never been subjected to the test of a homeopathic proving but something of its effects upon the human body are known from its accidental absorption by workers. It is an ingredient in some black pigments and of a black, permanent ink. Workers become debilitated. They contract a dry, hard, almost convulsive cough, with hemorrhage. The temperature becomes elevated with a diurnal maximum. Diarrhea sets in soon, and flesh and weight is lost rapidly. They are very apt to go from this state into genuine tuberculosis and die. These symptoms suggest it as a remedy in the early stages of tuberculosis. It agrees with the general characters of that disease, namely the cough, prostration, fever with daily rise, emaciation, hemorrhage and diarrhea. Vanad. also affects the liver with a degenerative process. Its action is that of an oxygen carrier and a catalyzer, hence its use in wasting diseases. Increases amount of hemoglobin, also combines its oxygen with toxins and destroys their virulence. It also increases and stimulates phagocytes. It is a remedy in degenerative conditions of the liver and arteries. Anorexia and symptoms of gastro-intestinal irritation. Tremors, vertigo, neuro-retinitis and blindness. Anemia, emaciation. Cough dry, irritating and paroxysmal, sometimes with hemorrhages. Irritation of nose, eyes and throat. Acts as a tonic to digestive functions and in early tuberculosis. Degenerative states with brain softening. Tuberculosis, chronic rheumatism, diabetes. Cold hands and feet. Raynaud’s syndrome. Degenerative conditions of liver and arteries. Fatty degeneration of the heart and liver. Arteriosclerosis, sensation as if heart was compressed, as if blood had no room in the aorta. Deeply pigmented patches on forehead in liver disorders. Profound weakness. Emaciation and weakness. MIND - Restlessness. Gloomy. Yielding, easily influenced. Crying easily over trifles. Fears of failure, criticism, being opposed. Anticipation. Fears of being late. Hysteria and melancholia. Mood alternating. Manic depression. Psychosis. Anorexia alternating with bulimia.

Head - Headaches. Brain softening.

Eyes - Neuro-retinitis and blindness. Opacity. Arcus senilis. Paralysis of optic nerves. Amaurosis.

Mouth - Teeth problems. Tongue green.

Throat - Tonsillitis and sore throats, coughing up small, greenish-yellow, bitter mucus. Thyroid problems. COMMENTS - Burnett told how he came to use Vanad. through reading the result of some experiments on animals in which the Salts of Vanadium produced “true cell destruction, the pigment escaping, the liver being hit hardest.” Burnett had at the time a case of “fatty liver, atheroma of the arteries, much pain corresponding to the course of the basilar artery, large, deeply pigmented patches on forehead, profound adynamia.” Vanad. restored the patient, who was seventy and at eighty he was “hale and hearty.” Marc Jousset told of experiments with salts of Vanad., chiefly the meta-vanadate of sodium, by Lyonnet and others. Animals poisoned by intravenous injections rapidly develop Cheyne-Stokes respiration with little or no action on circulation or blood. Cachexia. These clinical observers gave Vanadates to two hundred patients, suffering from neurasthenia, tuberculosis, chlorosis, chronic rheumatism, etc. It produced in nearly all cases increased appetite, strength and weight. The amount of urea was also increased. They regard Vanad. as “an energetic stimulant of nutrition,” and probably an oxidant stimulating organic combustion. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ars., Phos. Am- c. (2) Vanad. - fatty degeneration of liver. (3) fatty degeneration, Phos., Ars. (4) Addison’s disease, Adren. (5) Tuberculosis, Tub., Bac. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Rectum - Constipation. Diarrhea.

Female - Premenstrual symptoms. Menses scanty or absent. Pain in ovaries. Worse at ovulation. Lactation problems. Food - Loss of appetite. Anorexia. Bulimia. Disturbed fat and glucose metabolism. Retarded growth. Desires licorice, sweets. Weak digestion.

Heart - Fatty degeneration of the heart. Arteriosclerosis. Hypertension. Sensation as if heart was compressed, as if blood had no room in the aorta. Bursting pain. Constriction sensation.

Limbs - Chronic rheumatism. Sciatica. Restless and itching legs. Paralysis. Osteoporosis.

Skin - Pigmented patches. Warts.

Liver - Fatty degeneration of the liver. Lungs - Dyspnea, tiredness, weakness. Pneumonia and bronchitis. Cough dry, irritating. Colds with sneezing. Tuberculosis.

Kidneys - Addison’s disease. Albumen, casts and blood in urine.

Blood - Anemia and nutritional problems. Chest - Anxious pressure on whole chest. Sore chest. Dreams - Dreams of being late, of futile efforts. Dreams of paralysis.

PHARMACY - vario. Variolinum. Smallpox nosode. Trituration of matter from smallpox vesicle. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Backaches. Chill. Eczema. Fevers. Headache, occipital. Herpes zoster. Nausea. Neuralgias. Pustules. Shingles. Smallpox. Testicle, swelling. Ulcers. Vaccinations, ill effects.

HOMEOPATHIC - The Vario, nosode is prepared from lymph from a smallpox pustule. It has proved as an efficient preventive against smallpox and vaccinial infection. Vario, is used for bad effects of vaccinations. Seems to be efficacious in protecting against, modifying and aiding in the cure of smallpox. Vario, was Burnett’s chief remedy in shingles, it generally, as he expressed it, wiped out the disease, eruption and pain as well. It will also cure neuralgia left by herpes. Vario, has aborted many cases of smallpox and has proved an efficient preventive against smallpox contagion and vaccinosis infection. The keynote symptoms of Vario, are the defining symptoms of smallpox. Severe cold, chill, chilly creepings as if cold water were trickling down the back, violent fever with extremely hot skin, with or without high pulse. Violent headache. General aching in the muscles worse in back, occiput and legs. Nausea. Pain in epigastrium. Pain in limbs as if in bones. Severe backache. There may be rash or there may not. Calcareous deposits in the blood vessels, spinal cord. etc. MIND - Delirium with fever. Morbid fear of smallpox. Fear of death. Wild excitement and begging to know if he was to die. Variolinum

Head - Crazy feeling in the brain. Headache with icy coldness of feet and hands. Pain in occiput.

Eyes - Inflamed eyelids. Green vision, on rising.

Ears - Deafness.

Mouth - Tongue protrudes during sleep. Foul, metallic taste. Breath horribly offensive. Sensations - As if a band tightly encircled head. Crazy feeling through brain. As if throat were closed. As of a lump in right side of throat. Like streams of ice-water running down back.

Throat - Throat very sore, painful swallowing. Deep purplish crimson pharynx and fauces, with gangrenous appearance. Sensation as if throat were closed. Sensation of a lump in right side of throat. Diphtheria with horrible fetor oris. COMMENTS - Nonspecific shingles (Rhus- t.). Neuralgic pains without defining char- acteristics. Tendency to herpes, or acutely for herpes zoster or simplex. Acne, with yellow pus, leaving scars and large pock marks (Calc-s.). G. M. H. recorded the experience he had concerning Vario. 6c given to the mother and children of a family, one of whose members was taken with smallpox and removed to an isolation hospital with his mother to nurse him. The patient (who did not receive Vario.) was dangerously ill for a month. Neither the mother who nursed him nor any of the other children caught smallpox. Vaccines were sent by the government, and all the family were vaccinated, but it did not take with any of those who had taken V ario., although the vaccination was repeated. Moreover, G. M. H. himself, who had taken a dose of Vario., submitted to vaccination, but “although four thorough inoculations were given, they healed up immediately and did not even itch or smart.” A school of two hundred children were “internally variolated” with Vario. (100,000c, Swan) on the evening of February 18th and the morning of February 19th. Of two school mistresses, one was not at all affected, the other was ill for two days in bed. On February 21st many of the children were ill, by the 23rd, all except forty were. The symptoms were the usual preliminary symptoms of smallpox, and later, Swan found pustules on many. After the varioloid had passed off, but before the patients had recovered their vitality, twenty-three children were vaccinated without Swan’s knowledge. All but one took and had terrible ulcers on the arms and had to be remedied by Vac. (100,000c, Swan). RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Maland., Thuj., Ant-t., Vac., Sarr. Compare: (l)Herpes, Mez., Rhus-L, Ars., Vac. the same action. (2) Maland. - the morbid product of the grease of the horse, a prophylactic of smallpox and a remedy for the ill-effects of vaccination, chronic eczema following vaccination. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Stomach - Odor nauseates. Wants to regurgitate food. Vomiting of milk immediately after drinking it.

Abdomen - Tympanites, pouting upwards, looks pregnant.

Male - Enlargement of testicle. Hard swelling of left testicle from a contusion.

Back - Excruciating backache. Pain as if back were broken, worse by motion. Terrible pains in back on right side of spine. Pains from back, shift to abdomen.

Limbs - Aching in legs. Muscular rheumatism, worse on motion. Tired all over with restlessness. Wrist pain. Lungs - Oppressed breathing. Asthma. Troublesome cough, with serous and sometimes bloody sputa. Cough with thick viscid, slimy, bloody mucus, smelling bad. Feeling of a lump in right side of throat.

Skin - Hot, dry. Eczema of palms. Herpes zoster. Shingles and pains that follow. Eruption of foul pustules. Ulcers look scooped out. Profuse, bad-smelling sweat. As of bugs crawling under the skin.

Modalities - Worse from motion. Worse after vaccinations.

Temperature - As of cold water trickling down the back. Violent chill. Hot fever with intense, burning, radiating heat.

full:
PHARMACY - ven-m. Venus mercenaria. American scallop. American clam. Pelecy- poda class, living along the Atlantic Coast of America, France and Southern England. Tincture of the mollusc, plus an equal part of a trituration at 1/100 of the shell. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Amenorrhea. Arthritis. Flatulence. Headaches. Indigestion. Mania. Migraines. Schizophrenia. Weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ven-m., the American scallop, is a bi-val vular mollusk. The proving, after asuggestion by D. M. Foubister, wasconducted by Raeside in 1961-62 on nineteen pro vers, plus seven controls during three terms, one dose morning and evening for fourteen days, using the 30c in first term, 12c in second term, and 6c in third term. The third term produced most of the symptoms. Ven-m. is above all a remedy with cephalic action. For migraine headaches, accompanied by a host of digestive and urinary manifestations. Migraines of digestive origin. Increased frequency of urination. Frontal and occipital headache, predominantly on the right side, pains of a heavy sort, worse early in the morning and especially in the afternoon. Headache accompanied by vertigo, nausea, vomiting. Furred tongue, flatulence, diarrhea. Frequency of urination, especially during the day. Scalp and skin of the face and limbs itchy. Predominantly right sided. Sometimes there is a pseudo influenza, weakness at 10 a.m., extreme chilliness from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m. Sensation of contusion when pressure is applied. MIND - Lack of co-ordination of thoughts. Dull mood, state of indifference and lack of concentration. Sensation of boredom with fear ofcryingfor no reason. Exaggerated irritability from noise and people. Mania. Schizophrenia. Feels cut off from the world. Drunk feeling in the morning.

Head - Frontal, dull headache, behind the eye to the right with nausea, especially in the afternoon. Occipital headache on the right side, also in the afternoon. Migraines of digestive origin. Frontal and occipital hemicrania of the right or left side with nausea and feeling as if the head were being held tightly. Headache, aggravated in the afternoon, by exercise, ameliorated by sitting quietly in the dark and in the late evening.

Mouth - Soreness of the left lower lip and corner of lips. Blister on the lips. Tongue coated, furred. Cold feeling in the mouth and throat. Teeth sensitive to hot and cold, especially on the upper left jaw. Nerves - Incoordination of the mind and body when writing.

Throat - Pain on right side, spreading to the ear, aggravated by swallowing with dryness, chill and swollen glands. Constriction in the pharynx and larynx. Boil on the neck. Vertigo - Vertigo on rising after sitting for a long time, worse when ever tired, ameliorated by pressure. COMMENTS - Ven-m. in one single dose of 30c or repeated once is a remedy both for attacks of migraine and for complaints based on migraine headaches. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Calc. - digestive complaints with acrid-smelling stools, nausea and headache, chilliness. (2) Iris. - headache around the right eye with gastric complaints, burning and heartburn. (3) Lyc. - meteorism, constipation, depression, aggravated from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. Complementary: Care, is complementary. REFERENCES-Julian.

Stomach - Dyspepsia. Stomach ulcer. Nausea after eating with headache and vomiting. Flatulence all day long. Pressing stomachache with nausea, ameliorated after eating. Heaviness in the epigastrium, feeling of a stone in the stomach, aggravated by menses and at night.

Abdomen - Abdominal pains around 9 p.m. like menstrual pains. Muco-membranous enterocolitis. Flatulence and rumbling in the morning.

Rectum - Slight diarrhea or stubborn constipation with no desire to go to stool.

Female - Amenorrhea. Menses painful, especially at onset, for 2-3 hours. Menstrual pain ameliorated by heat and lying down. Depressed on first day of menstruation. Food - Desire for cold food, thirsty for cold water, ameliorated in the evening. Food tastes metallic.

Chest - Tender around the sternum. Constitutions - Allergic, psoric and sycotic types, tending towards a cancerous state following severe self- intoxication.

Heart - Short stabbing pain in the heart.

Back - Arthralgia and muscle pain with stiffness in the back and nape of the neck on waking.

Limbs - Pain and paresthesia of the limbs. Cramps, heaviness, itching of the arms and legs. These pains are ameliorated by movement. Pains in the hip, knee and ankle joints. Right knee swollen, hot and painful. Muscle pain. Arthritis. Arthrosis.

Sleep - Sleep disturbed, waking at 2 a.m. Dreams of spiders. Dreams of violence, ending in death. Dreams of death and disease.

Skin - Itching eczema. Prurigo simplex. Itching of the limbs, ears, back and face. Urticaria on the left hand. Boils and eruptions on the face.

Modalities - Better from movement. Worse on waking, in morning, in afternoon. Worse from noise.

Kidneys - Persistent pain in the right kidney on waking up. Fleeting pain in the left kidney. Frequency of urination by day. Urine turbid, frothy with a fetid odor. Frequent need to urinate.

PHARMACY - verin. Veratrinum. Veratria. Veratroidia. Viridia. Melanthiaceae. An alkaloid obtained chiefly from seeds of Saba- dillaandrootsofVeratrum album. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Cohc. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Dysuria. Esophagus, stricture. Intestines, catarrh. Jaw, snapping. Neuralgias. Pain. Paralysis. Spasms. Spine, neuralgia. Tetanus. Twitch- ings. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Verin, is both a paralyzer and a great pain producer. It causes a sensation like electric streams in nerves, shooting Veratrinum pains like electric-shocks in veins, muscles and joints. Verin, causes tetanus, which Farrington distinguishes from the convulsive action of Nux-v. in that Verin, causes purgation and vomiting with the spasms and that general paralysis does not take place from exhaustion as with Nux-v., but from devitalization of the muscles. In large doses, it causes violent sneezing and great gastro-intestinal irritation, vomiting, purging and symptoms of collapse. The pulse is rapid, small and irregular and often involuntary muscular tremors come on. A peculiar creeping and prickling sensation in skin generally accompanies these symptoms. Externally applied to the unbroken skin it has no marked action. If rubbed on with some fat, it passes through the epidermis and causes first irritation and then paralysis of the ends of the sensory nerves and producing a prickly and creepy sensation, succeeded by numbness. This effect is produced whether applied locally or taken internally. Brunton noted this irritating action in the sensory nerves is also observed if it is inhaled through the nose, where it causes violent sneezing, which also occurs after absorption through the stomach. COMMENTS - Subsultus tendinum, fibrillary twitchings are marked. Startings and tremors occur in limbs previously affection by paralysis or pain. The pains are tingling, sparkling, prickling, burning. Twitching of facial muscles. Snapping, closure of lower jaw. Drawing pain along the spine. Shocks in head. Sensations of oppression in head, suffocation of boiling water running over the back. As if a stream of warm air or drops of hot water issued from various parts. As if a frozen atmosphere around feet to knees or cold water poured on them. “Dull pain afterwards burning in lower part of spinal column, followed by pain in bowels and prepuce, accompanied with jerking in lower limb.” RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Coffee mixed with a little lemon-juice. Compare: ( 1 ) Sabad., Aeon., Con. REFERENCES-Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - verat. Veratrum album. White hellebore. White-flowered veratrum. N. O. Melanthacae of the Liliaceae. Alps and Pyrenees. Tincture of the rootstocks collected early in June before flowering. Historical dose: All potencies, first to thirtieth potency.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Anemia. Anguish. Anasarca. Angina pectoris. Asthma. Bronchitis. Cholera. Colic. Collapse. Coma. Constipation. Convulsions. Coprophagia. Coughs. Cramps. Deafness. Debility. De- hydration. Despair. Diarrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Eclampsia. Emphysema. Epilepsy. Esophagus, stricture. Fainting. Fevers. Gastric, catarrh. Head injury. Headaches. Heatstroke. Hernia. Hydrocephalus. Hy- drophobia. Hysteria. Influenza. Insanity, religious. Intermittent fever. Intussusception. Labor, constipation. Lips, cracked. Liver, hyperemia. Lockjaw. Lungs, edema. Mania. Measles. Melancholy. Meningitis. Menstruation. Neuralgias. Nyctalopia. Paralysis. Peritonitis. Pernicious fevers. Pneumonia. Pregnancy, imaginary. Ptosis. Rheumatism. Salivation. Scarlatina. Shock. Sleep, whining. Spleen, swollen. Strokes. Sunstroke. Throat, sore. Toothache. Typhoid fever. Vertigo. Water brash. Whooping cough. Yellow fever.

HERBAL - In his Helleborism of the Ancients, Hahnemann showed that Verat. was the principal agent used at Anticyra and other places in Greece to produce the evacuations which were regarded as an essential of the “cure.” Spring was deemed the most favorable season and autumn the next. The herbal treatment was employed in diseases including “mental derangements, epilepsy, spasms of the facial muscles, hydrophobia, ptyalism of the pancreas, diseases of the spleens, goiter, hidden cancer,” etc.

HOMEOPATHIC - Verat. profoundly affects the mind, nerves, abdominal, heart, blood, blood vessels, respiration, vertex and diges- tive system. Fainting, from emotions, least exertion, slight injury with hemorrhage after stools, vomiting. Progressive weakness and emaciation in acute diseases, whooping cough, ague, etc. Sudden sinking of strength. Paralysis after debilitating losses. Profound prostration, collapse with extreme coldness, blueness and weakness. Post-operative shock with cold sweat on forehead, pale face, rapid, feeble pulse. Cold perspiration on the forehead with nearly all complaints. Vomiting, purging and cramps in limbs. Profuse, violent retching and vomiting. Breath, tongue, cold as ice. Effects are violent and sudden. Copious evacuations, vomiting, purging, salivation, sweat, or urine. Excessive dryness of all mucus surfaces. Burnings. Blood seems to run cold, blood sepsis, pyemia. Carphology. Tonic spasms or cramps in chest, bowels, hands, fingers toes, soles of feet with diarrhea. Convulsions caused by religious mania or excitement, also of children. MIND - Melancholy with stupor and mania. Head hangs down, sits brooding in silence, wants to be alone. Sits in a stupid manner, notices nothing. Sullen indifference. Amativeness. Haughtiness. Remorse. Busy restlessness. Deceitful, never speaks the truth. Despair about position in society, feels very unlucky. Delusions of impending misfortunes. Malingering. Anguish, fear of death. Imaginary diseases. Thinks herself pregnant. Nymphomania, embraces everybody even objects. Kisses everybody, before menses. Puerperal mania. Religious mania. Despairs of her salvation. Imagines the world on fire. Prays, curses, shrieks in turn. Frenzy of excitement, shrieks, curses. Cursing, howling all night. Insanity. Violent mania alternates with silence and refusal to talk. Sings, whistles, laughs. Runs from place to place. Delirium with violence, driving to madness, loquacity or lewdness during pain. Mania with desire to cut and tear things (Tarent.). Aimless wandering from home. Talks about the faults of others or scolds. Swallows his own excrement.

Head - Cold sweat on forehead in all complaints. Sensation of a lump of ice on vertex. Violent pain driving to despair, better cold. Headaches with nausea, vomiting, pale face, diarrhea, diuresis. Vertex itches during headache. Rubs forehead. Contracted features. Neck too weak to hold head up. As if cold wind blowing through head. Hair bristle, painful.

Eyes - Surrounded by dark rings. Eyes dull, clouded, yellowish. Staring eyes, turned upwards without luster. The eyeballs are turned upwards. Pain, as if the eyeballs were bruised. Lachrymation with redness. Dry, heavy lids.

Ears - Shootings in ears. Pressure and constrictive sensations in ears. Alternate sensation of coldness and heat in ears. Deafness, as from obstruction in ears. Humming with sensitiveness to noise. Roaring in ears, especially when rising from a seat.

Nose - Icy coldness of tip of nose andface. Nose grows more pointed. Smell before nose. Nosebleed from right nostril, only at night in sleep.

Face - Face very pale, blue, collapsed, cold. Features sunken. Deathly pale, on rising, bluish, pinched or distorted, frowning cold, terrified look. Cheek red (left), as if burnt. Tearing in cheeks, temples and eyes. Jaws cramp on chewing. Lockjaw. Lips blue, hang down.

Mouth - Dry in center not relieved by water. Salty saliva. Water tastes bitter, like peppermint. Toothache, teeth feel heavy as if filled with lead. Grinding of the teeth. Tongue, cold, pale, cool sensation as from peppermint. Speech lisping, stammering or as if tongue too heavy.

Throat - Hoarse, weak voice. Loss of voice. Dry, scraping or roughness. When drinking water, it seems to run outside, not going down the esophagus. Vertigo - Vertigo, especially when walking. Vertigo with cold sweats on forehead with loss of vision, sudden fainting. Vertigo from opium, abuse of tobacco and alcohol. COMMENTS - Copious discharges, stools, vomiting, urine, salivation and sweat. Discharges drain the tissues. Exhausting discharges, causing vertigo, blackness before the sight, fainting and collapse. “Rapid sinking of forces, complete prostration, cold sweat and cold breath.” Useful for collapse with icy cold sweat (Carb-v.). Fainting from emotions, from the least exertion, from retching, or from stool. Sinking feeling during hemorrhage. “Skin blue, purple, cold, wrinkled, remaining in folds when pinched.” “Face hippocratic, nose pointed.” “Hands icy cold.” “Face and legs icy cold.” “Coldness of the whole body.” “Coldness running over whole body soon after taking it.” “Continued rigor in back and over arms.” “Cold feeling in abdomen.” Coldness predominates in fever, but there is also “heat and redness of face and hands.” “Feeling of internal chill ran through him from head to toes of both feet at once.” Cold sweats, especially on the forehead. Cardiac debility, following acute diseases. Thread-like pulse. Low blood pressure. Blood loss, hypovolemic shock. Faints in morning, face red when lying down or sitting up, deadly pale, hands cold, clammy. J. S. Mitchell considered it one of the best heart stimulants in homeopathic doses. Dryness and burning felt in the nose, mouth, palate, and throat. Pneumonia. Tickling deep in trachea and bronchials. “Tickling in chest, as if it would provoke cough in middle of sternum.” Severe dehydration (Chin.), often associated with heatstroke or sunstroke. Sun headaches or sunstroke. Extreme hunger, craving for cold food and refreshing things. Craves unripe fruit, ice cold drinks, ice cream (Phos.). Great thirst for ice-cold water, during both the chill and heat of fever. Copious stools. Cholera (Camph. and Cupr.). Rice-water stools. Watery diarrhea in infants. Green vomit, stool, or urine. Characteristic diarrhea, frequent, greenish, gushing, mixed with flakes. Cutting colic with cramps commencing in hands and feet and spreading all over. Prostrating after fright, worse least movement with vomiting, cold sweat on forehead during stool followed by prostration. “Violent vomiting with profuse diarrhea.” Characteristic constipation without desire. Large, hard stools, in round black balls from inactive rectum. Frequent desire felt in epigastrium. Painful constipation in infants, children, and women after confinement. Cramps, convulsions, can be tetanic with lockjaw or epileptic. The eyes are particularly convulsed or the lids paralyzed. There may be vanishing of sight, sparks before the sight, or night-blindness. Neuralgic pains, dysmenorrhea, or migraines, accompanied by diarrhea, vomiting, cold sweat, fainting or prostration. Delirium and prolonged sleep during fever. Violence in delirium. “Fury: tears his clothing, bites her shoes to pieces and swallows the fragments, cursing, stamping, wants to run away, makes a great noise.” Mental alienation. Insanity. Delusions of personal identity. Exalted, religious or sexual mania. Puerperal mania. Nymphomania, mania for kissing everybody. Delusion that she is pregnant, and she gets physical symptoms from it (pseudocyesis). Destructive mania. Despair and hopelessness, “bowed down with great grief.” Hahnemann said that it has the power “to promote a cure of almost one-third of the insane in lunatic asylums (at all events as a homeopathic intermediate remedy).” One of the symptoms taken by Hahnemann from Grading is “He swallows his own excrement.” Goullon verified this in a case of his in which a child had a craze for eating its own feces or dung lying in the street. Verat. 2c. three times daily, cured in a month. E. F. Watts had the case of Mrs. C., who had severe nervous headaches for years. Any over-exertion, like riding or working on hot days, would excite them. They frequently began in occiput, settling sometimes in one eye, sometimes in the other. Spig. and Sil. gave no relief. One day. Watts noticed that the brow contracted and the eyelids nearly closed with the intensity of the pain. Verat. was given and relieved at once. Gee cured, with one dose of Verat. 200c, the case of Mrs. L., a widow, 43. She had sciatica for four years. Pain sharp, transient, darted upwards and downwards and from both sides to center. Heat, worse “the cooler the better.” Cold sweat with the attacks. Headache from both temples to base of brain, worse by heat. Vertex itched during attacks. Pain compelled her to move about, but no better from motion. RELATIONS-Antidotedby: (Poisonous doses) Strong coffee, Camph. (pressive pain in head with coldness of body and unconsciousness after). Aeon, (anxious, distracted state with coldness of body or burning in brain.), Chin, (other chronic disorders from abuse of Verat. e.g., daily forenoon fever.), Staph, (most cases. Teste). Antidote to: Ars., Chin., Cupr. (colic), Op., Tab., removes the bad effectsofopium and tobacco. Compare: ( 1 ) Chin., Verin. - alkaloid from seed of Sabad. - electric pains, electric shocks in muscles, fibrillary twitchings. (2) Cho. - cramps in calves. (3) Camph., Cupr., Ars., Cupr-ar. - intermittent, cold, clammy sweat. (4) Narc-po. - gastro-enteritis with much griping and cutting pain in bowels. Fainting, trembling, cold limbs, small and irregular pulse. (5) Trychosanthes - diarrhea, pain in liver, dizziness after every stool. (6) Agar-em. Agar-ph. Follows well: Ars., Am., Chin., Cupr., Ip., Camph. (cholera), Am-c., Carb-v. Bov. (in dysmenorrhea with vomiting and purging). Lyc. and Nux-v. in painful constipation of infants. Followed well by: Puls., Aeon., Bell., Cham., Rhus-t., Sep., Sulph. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Mutphy.

Stomach - Painful, burning at pit of stomach. Hiccough after hot drinks. Cold water brash. Copious vomiting with nausea, aggravated by drinking and least motion. Vomits or belches froth. Violent retching. Nausea while eating, cannot get food down without retching. Cold feeling in stomach. Gastric irritability with chronic vomiting of food. Vomiting, worse drinking and least motion. Great weakness after vomiting.

Abdomen - Sinking and empty feeling. Cold feeling in abdomen. Epigastrium painful. Pain in abdomen preceding stool. Painful retraction of abdomen during vomiting. Abdomen sensitive to pressure, swollen with terrible colic. Cutting colic as if bowels were twisted in knots with cramps in limbs and rapid prostration. Peritonitis. Intussusception. Reversed peristaltic action. Sensation as if hernia would protrude (Nux-v.). As if hot coals in abdomen.

Rectum - Diarrhea from drinking cold water on hot days. Constipation from inactivity of rectum with heat and headache. Constipation of babies and when produced by very cold weather. Large stools with much straining until copious and forcibly evacuated, followed by great prostration. Evacuations of cholera morbus and true cholera when vomiting accompanies the purging. Cholera morbus. Cholera infantum. Stools, thin like ribbon, flat. Watery, green, odorless or colorless (rice water) stools, or in large masses with straining, until exhausted with cold sweat. Sensations - As if he had a bad conscience or had committed a crime. As if she would have to fly away. As if in a dream. As if head would burst. As if heat and cold at same time on scalp. Hair as if electrified. Distress over heart and epigastrium. As if something alive running from stomach into throat. As from ravenous hunger, pain in stomach. As of knives cutting bowels. As of hot coals in abdomen. Sinking, empty feeling in abdomen. As if pregnant or in throes of childbirth. As of knives cutting bowels. Electric pains occur in various parts.

Female - Menses too early, too profuse, suppressed. Dysmenorrhea with coldness, purging, cold sweat. Faints from least exertion. Menorrhagia with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. Nymphomania, before menses, from disappointed love, unsatisfied passion in lying-in women. Eclampsia. Puerperal mania. Food - Thirst for cold water, but is vomited as soon as swallowed. Craves ice water, wants everything cold or sour, drinks, juicy fruits and salt. Voracious appetite, gnawing hunger in spite of nausea and vomiting. Averse to warm food. All fruits disagree, causing painful distention. Potatoes and green vegetables disagree. Better eating meat and drinking milk.

Chest - Spasmodic contraction of muscles of chest. Oppressed chest, with pain in side during an inspiration. Sensation of fullness in chest, which induces frequent belchings. Constitutions - Suited to the extremes of age, children and old people. For lean, choleric or melancholy persons. Young people and women of a sanguine or nervo-sanguine temperament. People who are habitually cold and deficient in vital reaction. Persons of gay disposition, of fitful mood. Anemic persons.

Heart - Palpitations with anxiety and rapid audible respiration. Visible palpitations with chorea. Weak, cutting at heart. Intermittent, feeble, slow, thready pulse. Intermittent action of heart in feeble persons with some hepatic obstruction. Tobacco heart from chewing. Blood runs like cold water through veins.

Back - Neck so weak, child can scarcely keep it erect, worse whooping cough. Pain crampy between scapulae better motion. Bruised feeling in sacral region. Causations - Post-operative shock. Shock of injury. Ill effects of fright, disappointed love, injured pride or honor. Suppressed rashes. Opium, tobacco, alcohol.

Limbs - Brachial neuralgia, paralytic and bruising pain in arms. Fine burning in arms, right to left. Arms feel full and swollen. Tingling in hands and fingers. Feet icy cold. Cramps in calves during stools. Sciatica, pains like electric flashes in legs, must sit up and let legs hang down out of bed. Soreness and tenderness of joints. Difficulty in walking, like paralysis from debility. Pains in feet or knees as if heavy stones were tied to parts, must move about. Lungs - Air seems too hot. Asthma, worse in damp, cold weather, better bending head back. Tickling down throat into lungs. Rattling in chest. Much mucus in bronchial tubes that cannot be coughed up. Coarse rales. Chronic bronchitis in the aged (Hippoz.). Continuous violent cough with retching, worse cold drinks. Neglected whooping cough with complication. Barking cough with belchings, worse warm room. Involuntary urination with cough. Cough on entering warm room from cold air (Bry.). Hollow cough, tickling low down with blue face. Urine escapes when coughing.

Sleep - Wakes at night trembling. Starts as if frightened. Yawning. Nocturnal sleeplessness with great anguish. Sleep, long, uninterrupted, heavy, too profound. Sleeps with the arms passed over the head. Dreams with frightened waking and a fixed idea that the dream is true, of quarrels. Dreams are anxious, of being bitten by a dog and cannot escape, of being hunted of robbers.

Skin - Blue, cold, clammy, cold as death. Skin flabby and without elasticity. Wrinkling of skin of hands and feet. Cold sweat. Skin feels scorched. Dry tetters. Measles, tardy and pale. Nettle rash. Scarlatina in hot weather.

Modalities - Children feel better when carried about quickly. Better from warmth, covering, hot drinks. Better lying, walking. Better eating meat, milk. Worse from drinking, cold drinks. Worse wet, cold weather, change of weather. Worse at night. Worse exertion, touch, pressure. Worse before and during menses. Worse before, during or after stools. Worse fright, during pain. Worse injured pride or honor. Worse opium, tobacco chewing.

Kidneys - Scanty, red brown urine. Thick, greenish, suppressed, involuntary during cough.

Temperature - Chill with extreme coldness and thirst. General coldness, icy, on vertex, nose tongue, mouth, limbs, sweat. Internal heat with cold surface, when drinking. Fevers showing external coldness only.

HOMEOPATHIC - Cooper gave a few observa- tions for Verat-n. The plant, he said, has much the same botanical characters as Verat, but the flowers are dark-colored. It is native to Austria and Siberia. Verat-n. has headaches, protracted menstruation. Tinnitus aurium.

Head - Constant headache when attempting to move or exert the brain. Fierce headache threatening acute mania. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Ears - Constant buzzing of left ear for two weeks with tenderness of meatus and intense sensitiveness of the head to the motion of an omnibus with beclouding of the brain and pain in nape of neck.

Female - Period continually returning, sometimes light-colored and slight in quantity and sometimes profuse with weak feeling in back.

name: Veratrum Viride
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from rubbing, lying with head low. Better eating. Pain in head better by pressure. Closing eyes and resting head helps vertigo. Worse from raising up, lying on back. Worse cold, sunstroke, going from warm to cold. Worse morning, on waking, evening. Worse after confinement. Motion aggravates, sudden motion causes faintness and blindness. Walking causes blindness. Lying down aggravates headache, breathing..

Esophagus, spasms. Erysipelas. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hiccoughs. Hyperpyrexia. Influenza. Malarial fever. Measles. Meningitis. Menses, suppressed. Muscle, pains. Orchitis. Pneumonia. Proctalgia. Puerperal, convulsions. Pue
