HOMEOPATHIC - Proved in 1970 by Boffa and Dupin on 14 subjects, 7 men, and 7 women. The heart, blood and blood vessels were chiefly affected. Sleepiness during daytime. Chilly. Worse left side. Nerves. Throbbing pains. Throbbing headache. Heavy sensation in eyes. Dazzling when raising eyes. Dryness of mouth, with pasty tongue, on waking in morning. Dry mouth before menses. Menses with small, very dark clots or with big red clots. MIND - Pessimism. Nervousness. Irritability. Disposition to contradict. Impatience. Anxiety. Dreams of death.. Food - Intense thirst for cold drinks.

Heart - Palpitations of heart at night, worse lying on left side.

Limbs - Spontaneous ecchymoses on arms. Painful heaviness in legs, worse walking, better raising legs. Veins of thighs distended. Marbled, mottled appearance of thighs.

Modalities - Better during menses. Better gentle motion. Worse warm, damp weather, warm room, heat. Worse left side, pressure. Worse evening. Worse before menses. RELATIONS - Compare: Vip., Lach., Naja., Aran-ix., Buth-aust. REFERENCES-Julian.

name: Vipera Berus
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Worse from letting limbs hang down. Worse by pressure. Worse change of weather, from cold touch. Worse yearly..
constitution: Bites. Goiter. Hemorrhages. Jaundice. Liver, enlargement. Menopause. Multiple neuritis. Nosebleeds. Paralysis. Paraplegia. Phlebitis. Poliomyelitis. Senility, premature. Tongue, swelling. Varicose veins.
keynote: PHARMACY - vip. Vipera berus. German viper. Vipera torva. Pelias berus. Adder. Vipera communis. Common Viper. European Viper with other varieties, especially the Red Italian Viper. N. O. Ophidia, family, Viperidae. Dilutions of the venom. Historical dose: All…
full:
PHARMACY - vip. Vipera berus. German viper. Vipera torva. Pelias berus. Adder. Vipera communis. Common Viper. European Viper with other varieties, especially the Red Italian Viper. N. O. Ophidia, family, Viperidae. Dilutions of the venom. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Bites. Goiter. Hemorrhages. Jaundice. Liver, enlargement. Menopause. Multiple neuritis. Nosebleeds. Paralysis. Paraplegia. Phlebitis. Poliomyelitis. Senility, premature. Tongue, swelling. Varicose veins.

HOMEOPATHIC - The effects of bites by the common viper and related species have been collected and have furnished the data for homeopathic prescribing. The venom of common German Vipera torva affects the blood and blood vessels, leading to hemorrhage and inflammation of the vessels. Allen related the case of a gold beater who found the veins of his right arm become exceedingly swollen and painful, so that he could no longer work or let his hand hang down. Vip. cured immediately. A case quoted from Med. Adv. of varicose veins of the popliteal space with the sensation as though the leg would burst and a nervous, fidgety condition of the feet which kept them in constant motion, was cured with Vip. 30c. The bursting feeling appears to be at the root of this characteristic. A keynote for Vip. in cases of phlebitis and varicose veins is “Worse on letting the limb affected hang down,” as if it would burst with fullness. The region of the vessel affected is inflamed and sensitive. Swan said Vip. was a remedy for all forms of nosebleed. Vip. affects veins, causing inflammation and ahemorrhagic tendency. Inflammation of veins with great swelling. Cardiac dropsy. Bursting sensation, enlargement of liver. Special action on kidneys and induces hematuria. Edema of glottis. Goiter. Ailments of menopause. Paralysis, ascending, paraplegia of foot. Multiple neuritis. Poliomyelitis. Temporary increase in reflexes, paresis supervenes, a paraplegia of the lower limbs extending upwards. Resembles acute ascending paralysis of Landry. Vip. has a chronic and periodic action, the symptoms return annually for years.

Eyes - Eyes are dark yellow, red, inflamed and watery, staring, sunken. Pupils are dilated or left dilated, right contracted. Paralysis of lids, dropped over eyes. Vision is dim, dim in left eye, lost in right.

Nose - Nosebleed with vertigo, while nursing the child.

Face - Excessively swollen. Lips and the tongue swollen, livid, protruding. Tongue dry, brown, black. Speech difficult. Food - Appetite lost. Thirst with moist tongue, for cold drinks.

Mouth - Scorbutic line on gums. Tongue swollen, brownish-black, protruding. Lips, blue, swollen. Speech difficult.

Throat - Swelling like goiter. Edema of glottis. Closure of throat so that she could swallow only water and milk. COMMENTS - Vip. patients resist the cold badly. The parts may be paralyzed and ulcers and gangrene follow. Worse from letting limb or part hang down. Sensation as if something ran up the thigh occurred in the bitten limb in one case. In one case there was sweat over the whole body except the bitten limb. Leonard gave Vip. to a woman suffering from menopausal hemorrhage, flow red with dark clots, excessive to prostration and faintness. She had a small uterine fibroid. A few doses relieved and the excessive hemorrhage did not return. He also noted the case of a woman nursing a child a year old who was much prostrated by hemorrhage lasting several weeks, not profuse, but continuous: Nosebleed nearly every day, weaning brought no relief. Chin. 200c did no good. Vip. 100,000c cured in three doses. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Hemorrhage of fluid blood, Sanguis. (2) Worse hanging down limbs, Calc., Alumn., Am-c., Sabin., Thuj. (3) Pelius berus. Adder. - Prostration and fainting, faltering pulse, skin yellow, pain about navel. Swelling of arm. tongue, right eye with giddiness, nervousness, faintness, and sickness. Compression of chest, could not breathe properly or take a deep breath, aching and stiffness of limbs, joints stiff, collapsed feeling, great thirst. (4) Ser-ang. - heart and kidney diseases. Failure of compensation and impending asystole. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Digestion slow. Pain in epigastrium, worse pressure. Nausea with shuddering with attack of faintness. Retching with suffocative sensation. Vomiting after milk of all food and drink.

Abdomen - Excruciating pain in the epigastrium, worse pressure. Violent pain in enlarged liver extends to shoulder and hip, jaundice with fever.

Female - Menopausal hemorrhage, flow red with dark clots, not profuse but continuous with prostration and faintness from nursing the child.

Chest - Oppression with anxiety with violent efforts to breathe and swallow. Veins of chest and abdomen thick and hard. Swelling of chest as far as umbilicus after bite on face.

Back - Sticking in kidneys. Pain in loins.

Limbs - Patient is obliged to keep the limbs elevated. When limbs are allowed to hang down, it seems as if they would burst and the pain is unbearable. Shuffling gait caused by paralysis of foot. Varicose veins and acute phlebitis. Veins swollen, sensitive, bursting pain. Blue lower limbs. Severe cramps in lower limbs.

Sleep - Disposed to yawn. Sleepiness and heaviness with inability to sleep and also almost constant necessity to change the position. Sleeplessness from pain. Restless at night.

Skin - Livid. Boils, carbuncles with bursting sensation, relieved by elevating parts. Ulcers. Gangrene. Skin peels in large plates. Lymphangioma.

Modalities - Worse from letting limbs hang down. Worse by pressure. Worse change of weather, from cold touch. Worse yearly.

Liver - Violent pain in enlarged liver with jaundice and fever, extends to shoulder and hip.

Kidneys - Strangury. Involuntary urination. Urine is increased, suppressed, dark yellow, as in jaundice. Hematuria. Ineffectual desire.

Temperature - Temperature is diminished, resists cold badly. Chilliness with cold sweat, with rigidity and clammy sweat, then fever. Fever of irregular type intermittent fever. Sweat after vomiting.

full:
PHARMACY - vise. Viscum album. Mistletoe. N. O. Loranthaceae. Viscaceae. Tincture of ripe berries. Tincture of bruised leaves. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Ankylosing spondylitis. Arteriosclerosis. Asthma. Aura epiléptica. Cancer. Chorea. Deafness. Dupuytren’s disease. Dysphagia. Endometritis. Epilepsy. Hypertension. Labor pains, slow. Lumbago. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Migraine. Neuritis. Orchitis. Osteoporosis. Otorrhea. Ovaritis. Raynaud’s syndrome. Retained placenta. Sciatica. Spasmodic paralysis. Spleen pain. Throat, sore. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - Viscum Album’s active principle is viscotoxin, a mixture of acetylcholine and choline. Viscum is a chlorophyllous plant, which grown on various trees (apple, poplar) and forms large bunches. It is gathered in August and September, before the fruit ripens. The leaves are then blanched and dried quickly in hot air and stabilized. In the middle ages, it was used as an anti-epileptic. Hypo-tensor and diuretic. Anti-tumors, by external use, as for papilloma, due to the necrotizing properties of the viscotoxin. Viscine is most abundant in the mistletoe of the apple-tree, Visco-resin in that of the oak and acacia, excites the sexual appetite. The mistletoe of the hawthorn possesses like all the rest, but in a higher degree, the contractile properties of Sec. on the uterus in uterine inertia. That of the oak has a remarkable anti-epileptic power on horses. According to Laville, all mistletoes are useful in epilepsy and rabies. A breeder had a very fine stock which became epileptic at four or five years old. He cured them with a tincture of the fresh leaves bruised in a mortar.

HOMEOPATHIC - The first homeopathic symptomatology was established by Proll, Stager, Schier and Black during the second half of the 19th century, using the mother tincture and low potencies. Proell made a proving of the tincture and the symptoms developed resembling an epileptic aura and petit mal, which had the additional epileptic feature of recurrence they recurred frequently for two years. Vise, affects the nerves and female sexual organs. Lowered blood pressure. Dilated blood vessels but does not act on the centers in the medulla. Pulse is slow due to central irritation of the vagus. The symptoms point to rheumatic and gouty complaints, neuralgia, especially sciatica. Epilepsy, feels a glow that rises up from feet to head. Chorea and metrorrhagia. Chorea from fright. Symptoms like epileptic aura and petit mal. General tremor as if all muscles are in fibrillary contraction. Neuralgia. Paresthesia. Rheumatism, tearing pains. Rheumatoid condition ameliorated in fresh air and by the movement. Gouty. Sciatica with otorrhea. Spinal pains from uterine causes. Feeling of lightness as if floating on air. The brain is swaying around the inside the skull. Congestion in the head with headaches and vertigo. Blood would not clot and wounds would not heal. Bleeding of bright red blood from the uterus. Valvular disease with disturbances in sexual sphere. Rheumatic deafness. Asthma. Hypertensive albuminuria. Nausea at the sight of the bottle containing the medicine to be taken. Pruritus. Burning cold under the right shoulder. MIND - Apathy, sadness. Lack of optimism liveliness. Irritable, sad, morose. Restless, nervous, thoughtless, shakes with impatience. Unable to carry out intellectual activities. Thoughts keep turning to past events, for hours on end. Obsessive persistence of thoughts. Sensation of strength, optimism, gaiety, desire to undertake anything, full of ideas for the future. Hallucinatory psychosis. Extremely sensitive to noise. Fear of telephones.

Head - Feeling as if whole vault of skull were lifted up. Sudden throbbing in vertex. Headache, especially at the forehead, temples andparietalbone,can spread to the whole heat. Dull, heavy aching, numbing and congestive, beating or hammering.

Eyes - Blue rings around eyes. Ocular neuralgia. Conjunctivitis. Mydriasis, ocular neuralgia, conjunctival irritation. Double vision. Bad focusing, eyes weep through fatigue.

Ears - Deafness from cold. Buzzing and stopped-up feeling in ear. Hypersensitive to noise. Whistling, buzzing. Hears heartbeat. Sclerosis of the ears.

Nose - Catarrh in the nose and pharynx. Catarrhal congestion of the mucus membranes with discharge of a watery or purulent liquid. Purulent rhinitis. Polyps. Nosebleed.

Face - Facial muscles in constant agitation. Countenance suffused. Lips livid. Face hot and flushed.

Mouth - Lips cracked. Dryness of the mouth. Mouth suddenly fills with saliva. Unpleasant taste on waking tongue coated to tip with ochre-yellow fur. Tongue sore. Buccal mucus membrane is as if tanned. TeetWehattered.

Throat - Throat dry, burning with sticky discharge. Sensation of constriction around the neck. The feeling of a lump in the throat disappeared in one female prover. Vertigo - Vertigo, persistent after epileptic attack. Sensation of lightness, as if floating on air. Severe attacks of vertigo totters and has to hold on to the furniture. Vertigo occurs on rising from movement, by moving the head quickly, tends to fall backwards. Vertigo never occurs when lying down. Vertigo when looking out of a window. COMMENTS - Two women took Vise, to procure abortion. Every muscle save those of the eyes became paralyzed, as did also the intestinal tract. They could not swallow and died of starvation in consequence, the bowels being obstinately constipated. The muscles of speech were also paralyzed. A boy, 14, ate some berries, soon after began to feel giddy and then became insensible. He was found with suffused countenance, lips livid, conjunctiva injected, pupils slightly dilated and fixed, pulse slow and full, bounding, breathing slow, stertorous. On pricking the soles the feet were quickly drawn up. Then, cold applications aroused him, when he began to talk incoherently, had spectral illusions and was inclined to be violent. In a pamphlet on “Viscum Album” Dr. George Black of Torquay put together most of the facts relating to this plant including four new provings, by himself and three female provers. Black removed with Vise. 3c lumbago from chill, tearing pain, wants something to press against it. Lumbago, right, extending to right buttock, worse by slightest movement. Pain in sacral region, unable to turn either side, worse slightest movement, “pain of a terrible clutching nature, as if her vitals were affected.” Cooper gave great relief with Vise, in “old spinal irritation pains.” He also named “spinal symptoms due to uterine causes” as indicating it. Rheumatism, “the weight of my body on the joint causes it to be very sore,” excessive perspiration. Sciatica associated with otorrhea. Burning pain from center of left buttock to inner ankle, heel as if red-hot coal applied, leg feels heavy as lead. In addition a number of cases of catarrhal deafness with noises in the ears were cured or greatly improved. Belcher gave to a girl, 17, suffering from chorea, 5 drop doses of a tincture of leaves and berries. On the second day he was called to see her and found her suffering as if under the influence of an opiate. Black also quoted William Huber’s experiences with Vise., the first case was of retained placenta with constitutional symptoms after miscarriage at sixth month. Expulsion rapidly effected by Vise. 3c. A man, 22, robust, fair took a chill from traveling in ice-cold wind. Got a drawing, tearing pain in left lower jaw, lasting some hours. Succeeded by loud buzzing and stopped-up feeling, ending in complete deafness of that ear. Vise. 3c cured. Metrorrhagia following suppression from working in water. Sciatica left side, cured with Vise. 3c. Rheumatism from wading ill-shod through great tracts of snow, cured with Vise. 3c. Hydrothorax (right) from chill with shooting in spleen, cured with Vise. 4c and 3c. John Wilde made a tincture of the bruised leaves and gave 5 drop doses to a boy, 14, who had chorea affecting face and limbs. There was improvement in two days and in a few weeks a complete cure. A boy, nine, strumous with tendency to skin disease, was affected with chorea after a fright. He was completely changed in expression, speech quite inarticulate, look idiotic. The movements continued at night and the boy was worn out for want of sleep. Vise., 1 to 2 drop doses, did no good. The dose was then increased to 15 drops. Improvement set in at once and a perfect cure was effected, the doses being diminished after a time because soreness of the tongue and redness of the conjunctiva were set up. C. M. Boger related a case in which persistent vertigo after epileptic seizures, lasting a month at a time, was cured with Vise. 100,000c. Huber used the 3x and 6x. He considered it applicable to all kinds of rheumatism, acute and chronic, especially when characterized by tearing pains in cases occurring in winter, the result of exposure to sharp winds and in cases of rheumatic deafness. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Chin. Compare: (1) Sec., Conv., Bry., Puls., Rhod. (2) Guipsine - active principle - exalts the hypotensive properties of Viscum. (3) Hed. - Intercranial pressure. (4) Bry. - Vertigo in the morning on rising, prickling pains, aggravated by movement, great thirst, dry constipation, menses copious with brown blood. (5) Bell. - Neuro-vascular congestion, fear of imaginary things, hypersensitivity and hyper-exicitability of the senses, pulse strong, irregular, menses too early with bright red, hot blood. (6) Aran-ix. Follows well: Aeon, (rheumatism). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Julian.

Stomach - Gastritis. Heavy sensation, feeling of a stone in the stomach. Squeamish before breakfast and dinner. Heartburn, cutting pain in the stomach, ameliorated by eating and belching. Nausea ameliorated by vomiting.

Abdomen - Feels as if someone were dragging her down from the waist. Sore about waist. Violent rumbling and painful distention of the supra-umbilical region, ameliorated by expelling wind and leaning backwards. Colitis. Chronic pancreatitis.

Rectum - Feeling of constriction of the anus with empty urging. Feeling of not having emptied the intestine completely after stool. Stools soft, watery or thick, frothy, stinking, explosive, bulky with nightly urging, forcing him to get out of bed. Stools hard and dry. Pruritus and burning of the anus with splinter-line pain. Bleeding hemorrhoids.

Male - Libido increased or diminished. Disturbed libido. Violent, painful erection. Atonic discharge of seminal fluid. Cramping pain in the prostate. Prostatitis.

Female - Menses too early, copious with bright red blood and very painful. Menorrhagia. Chronic endometritis. Metrorrhagia. Atonic, post-partum hemorrhage. Hemorrhage with pain. Blood partly clots and bright red. Menopausal complaints (Lach., Sulph.). Pain from sacrum into pelvis with tearing, shooting pains from above downwards. Ovarian pain, especially left. Retained placenta (Sec.). Food - Felt starving at supper-time. Appetite ravenous.

Chest - Angina pectoris. Nervous dyspnea with feeling of constriction in the chest.

Heart - Hypertrophy with valvular insufficiency, pulse small and weak, unable to rest in a reclining positions. Low blood pressure. Failing compensation, dyspnea worse lying on left side. Weight and oppression of heart, as if a hand were squeezing it, ticking sensation about heart. Inflammation of the coronary arteries. Feeling of tightness of heaviness. As if the heart is being squeezed by a hand. Heartbeat irregular. Agitation and fibrillation. Pulse accelerated or slow with fear of death. Palpitations in the chest, throat and upper part of the abdomen. Palpitations during sex.

Back - Lumbago from a chill, wants someone to press against the back. Stiffness and muscular pains in the nape of the neck, thoracic cage and back. Torticollis. Sensation of a burning coal under the right shoulder. Causations - Chill, wetting. Fright. Suppression of menses.

Limbs - Chorea-like movements of the arms and legs. A glow rises from the feet to the head, seems to be on fire. General tremor, as if all muscles were in state of fibrillary contraction. Dropsy of limbs. Sciatica. Drawing, tearing pains in the arm. Pains alternate in the knee and ankle with shoulder and elbow. Periodic pains from sacrum into pelvis, worse in bed with pains into thighs and upper limbs. Tearing, shooting pains in both thighs and upper limbs. Cannot keep legs still. Sensation of a spider crawling over back of hand and foot. Itching all over. Compressing pain in feet. Raynaud’s syndrome. Walking, bending is painful. Burning sensation in the feet. Lungs - Dyspnea, feeling of suffocating when lying on leftside. Stertorous breathing. Asthma, if connected with gout or rheumatism. Bronchial asthma, connected with gout or rheumatism. Glottal spasms and rattles in the bronchi. Painful, frequent cough, scanty, gray or yellow sputum. Spasmodic cough.

Sleep - Falls asleep late, wakes early. Sleeps, despite exhaustion and after drinking coffee. Troubled dreams of war, bombardment.

Skin - General itching and tingling with no apparent cause, ameliorated in the evening and by perspiration. Formication along the arms. Pruritus, senile and vulvae.

Modalities - Better by counter-pressure, resting quietly, walking in the fresh air. Worse by slightest movement. Worse winter, cold, stormy weather, becoming chilled while hot, heat. Worse in bed, lying on left side. Worse suppression of menses. Worse mental effort. Worse tobacco.

Kidneys - Urinary tenesmus and copious urine. Bladder paralyzed. Involuntary passing of urine as a result of an irritating cough. Urine is turbid and evil-smelling. Urine milky after standing. Bedwetting.

Temperature - General shivering followed by sudden hot flush towards the head and feeling of anguish.

CLINICAL - Blood, clots. Cancer. Cerebral, thrombosis. Colds. Coughs. Diarrhea. Food, poisoning. Sinusitis.

HERBAL - The wasabi plant is native to Japan, and is traditionally found growing in or by cold mountain streams. The earliest cultivation of wasabi in Japan dates back to the 10th century. The grated rhizome, or above-ground rootlike stem, has a fiery hot flavor that quickly dissipates in the mouth, leaving a lingering sweet taste, with no burning sensation. The roots have a strong penetrating odor, which can clear the head and bring tears to the eyes, when inhaled or ingested. Wasabi is valuable medicinally for its antibacterial properties, and anti-inflammatory action. It has been used for coughs, colds, sinusitis and diarrhea. It is a powerful digestive stimulant, and removes toxins from the body. As a member of the cruciferous family, wasabi contains the same cancer-fighting isothiocynates as its cabbage relations. Researchers believe that the substances in cruciferous vegetables help prevent cancer by helping the body eliminate excess hormones such as estrogen, thus reducing the risk of hormone-related cancers such as breast and prostate cancer. Scientists have recently found that a component of the plant inhibits the formation of blood clots and cerebral thrombosis. The plant has exhibited strong antioxidant properties. Research also found that wasabi contains substances that suppress the growth of stomach cancer cells. It has also been used as an antidote to fish poisoning. RELATIONS - Compare: Ars. REFERENCES - Murphy.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Angina pectoris. Body, odor of offensive. Constipation. Coms. Diarrhea. Earwax, excessive. Glaucoma. Gout. Hair, rapid growth, loss, grows darker. Hemorrhage. Hemorrhoids. Hernia inguinal, femoral. Indigestion. Miscarriages. Nosebleed. Rheumatism. Infertility. Vertigo. Whitlow.

HOMEOPATHIC - The hot, chlorinated saline springs of Wiesbaden contain 8.176 grams of solids to each liter, and of these Nat-m. makes up more than seven grams. The baths, which constitute the chief part of the treatment, are extremely stimulating. The baths, combined with drinking the water, generally determine at the begining of the cure certain phenomena of saturation which disappear on temporary suspension of the treatment. The most common of these is a saburral state of the stomach and a feeling of fullness and tension in the whole abdomen. Passive or atonic gout, these cases usually pass through a period of aggravation before improvement sets in. Torpid and rheumatisms, the douche being employed as well as the bath. Paralysis, muscular and tendinous contractions. Sprains in complete anchyloses. Stiffness from old fractures. Gunshot wounds which are slow to heal. Modalities - Better by nosebleed, by hemor- rhoid flux. Worse during menses. Frequent urination worse from coffee. V ertigo worse lying in bed. COMMENTS - Constantin James noted, “Abdominal plethora and portal obstruction are relieved.” By the artificial congestion which they set up in the venous plexus of the rectum they have for a constant effect the disengorge- mentof the viscera under the diaphragm and the prevention of stasis in their parenchyma. Pelt observed the effects of drinking the water and excessive bathing. Magdeburg observed the effects on eight very healthy persons. The stimulating, congestive and évacuant effects mentioned by James appeared in the provings. Blood rushes to the face. Vertigo when lying in bed and vertigo which causes falling. Hemorrhages occur from anus and nose which relieve other symptoms. Fermentation occurs in the abdomen and there is great exhaustion after diarrhea. Hemorrhoid flow occurs with better of abdominal plethora. In one case nosebleed occurred persistently for six weeks, at the end of which a weakness of vision bordering on blindness was cured. During the menses there is great weakness, also constipation. A number of remarkable symptoms appeared in reference to the skin and nails. The hair grew rapidly and became darker. Nails also grew rapidly. Corns and callosities dropped off. Berridge cured with Wies. 200c a Miss B., 21 of a soft corn between the fourth and fifth toes of right foot. There was burning and shooting pain. Itching with the sweat. The sweat on the diseased parts made a brown stain. The urine stiffened linen. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Nat-m. Corns, Ferr-pic. (2) Callosities, Ant-c. (3) Hair turns darker, Jab., Piloc., Wild. REFERENCES - Clarice.

The first impression of the bath is delicious, this is succeeded by sensations more clear and distinct: a slight degree of excitement, at times luminous sparks before the sight, a finer blood seems to flow to the brain(Puls.). “One would like to remain in the bath, but something unusual and strange warns you that it is time to get out.” Wildbad is chiefly for disorders of the spinal cord, more then half the patients being paraplegic. Sensation as if the brain were over-filled. Gnawing, sinking, empty sensation. Pain as if sprained. Sensation of looseness in the joints, ankles loose, knees loose, the bones seem as if they did not fit. Teeth seem too long. In one pro ver the hair, which had been greasy, became dry and the beard became of a darker color. Desire to stretch.

HERBAL - Withania somnífera is an important herb used in Ayurveda, the traditional Indian medicine. A native of India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, the name comes from the peculiar odor of this herb, smell akin to that of a sweaty horse. It is an erect branched shrub with a greenish or lurid yellow flowers. In India, it is akin to ginseng in other parts of the orient, both are touted for their longevity enhancing and sexually stimulating properties. The shoots and seeds are also used as food and to thicken milk in India. It is said to work mainly on the reproductive and nervous systems coupled with rejuvenating qualities. Tumors, inflammation (including arthritis), and a wide range of infectious diseases. Regulates blood sugar, which aids in suppressing sugar cravings. It is commonly used to increase vitality, recover from chronic illnesses and pain management for arthritic conditions.

HOMEOPATHIC - According to B. Gan- gooly, M.D., from Calcutta, India, in the Homoeopathic Recorder, vol. 37, 1922, With-s. has been employed successfully in all cases of debility. Nervousness. HOMEOPATHIC - Wye. was introduced and proved with the fresh root or the tincture, on seven men and two women, by Selfridge. The first proving gave Wye. a definite and important place in throat disorders. Those symptoms make up the first pathogenesis. Wye. has marked effects on the throat and has proven an excellent remedy in pharyngitis, especially the follicular form. Irritable throats of singers and public speakers. Throat feels swollen, epiglottis dry and burning. Constant desire to swallow saliva to relieve the dryness yet affording no comfort. Swallows with difficulty. Hay fever symptoms, itching in posterior sinuses. Prickling, dry sensation in posterior sinuses, sensation as if something were in nasal passages, an effort to clear them through the throat affords no relief. Burning sensation in bronchial tubes. Dry, hacking cough, caused by tickling in epiglottis. Useful also in hemorrhoids. MIND - Nervous, uneasy, apprehensive of calamity. Depressed. Incapacitated for mental work. Averse to company. Impatient and quarrelsome.

Head - Rush of blood to head. Sharp pain in forehead. Severe headache.

Ears - Itching in right ear. Pain in left ear. Eyes - Itching in left inner canthus.

Nose - Hay fever symptoms. Sensation as if something in nasal passages.

Mouth - Feels as if scalded, sensation of heat down esophagus. Itching of the palate.

Throat - Hot, dry throat. Constant clearing and hemming. Dry, posterior sinuses, no relief from clearing. Throat feels swollen, epiglottis dry and burning. Difficult swallowing. Constant desire to swallow saliva. Uvula feels elongated. Tendency to get hoarse talking or singing. Vertigo - Dizzy. COMMENTS - Nonspecific hay fever, characteristic itching of the upper palate. Hay asthma, allergic asthma. A history of hay fever going to the lungs, or asthma caused by hay fever treatments or decongestants. Kent used this as a prophylactic hay fever remedy. Tough, ropy saliva. Belching alternating with hiccough. Pain over left ovary, shooting down to knee. In one case, menses, which had been in abeyance since confinement a year before, remmed with much pain. Hale noted several cases from Selfridge. The first concerned dry asthma in a woman who had several attacks promptly relieved with Wye. The second case noted the effectiveness of Wye. in chronic follicular pharyngitis with dryness of pharynx and burning in epiglottis. In the third case, Hale found Wye. to be successful in a case of severe epidemic influenza. Clarke had a case reported to him in which a boy had been kept awake many nights by a persistent, dry, hacking, nervous cough. Wye. 30c cured in one dose. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Arum, Sang., Lach. (2) In throat affections, Arum-d., Caust., Hep., Stict., Rumx., Pen., Phos., Sulph. (3) Tough, ropy saliva and headache, Epip. (4) Sensation as if something indigestible eaten, Abies-n. (5) Scalded mouth, Ran-s. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy-

CLINICAL - Anemia. Anorexia. Burns. Cancer. Chronic fatigue. Debility. Dermatitis. Emaciation. Heart, problems. Hemaphila. Hemorrhages. Infertility. Leukemia. Mastectomy, pains. Memory, weak. Ovaries, atrophy. Psoriasis. Purpura. Radiation, dermatitis. Skin tumors. Sterility. Sun, exposure. Testes, atrophy. Vitality, low. Warty growths. Weakness. X-ray, poisoning.

HOMEOPATHIC - Roentgen noted that repeated exposure to X-rays produced skin lesions often followed by cancer. Changes take place in the blood lymphatics and bone marrow. Its homeopathic action is centrifugal towards the periphery of the body. The stock comes from the potency lc of this irradiated alcohol. The proving on X-ray was conducted by Fincke in 1897, on ten provers, using 6x. This was repeated by W. B. Griggs on two male and one female provers, and published in the Homeopathic Recorder in 1952 using the 30c and 200c potencies. X-rays have the property of stimulating cellular metabolism. Arouses the vitality, mentally and physically. Useful for syndromes of deficiency of certain elements present in the blood. Leukemia. General debility. Chronic fatigue and a sick feeling. Unexplained weakness. Low vitality and anemia. Discharges, gray, white withjelly-like lumps. Psoriasis. Corresponds to burns, that refuse to heal. Distressing pain. Sexual glands are particularly affected. Atrophy of ovaries and testicles. Infertility. X-rays brings to the surface suppressed symptoms, especially the psoric and sycotic due to mixed infections. For cancer patients submitted to treatment by radiation. X-rays, cobalt. For patients submitted for therapy by immuno-suppressors and all anti-tumor chemotherapy. MIND - Sadness. Aversion to company. Memory, weak. Sleepy. Irritable, desire to kill, especially before and during menses. Abdomen - Heaviness and fullness in lower abdomen, distended. Flatulence with ineffectual desire for stool.

Head - Sticking pains in different parts of head and face. Ringing in head. Sensation of fullness in the head. Pain in the forehead, occiput, temples, extending to the neck. Better by hot compresses on the forehead.

Eyes - Painful to the touch. Eyeballs sore. Sensation in right eye as if bulging. Bearing down of eyelids. Eyelids heavy and sleepy.

Ears - Sensation of fullness, noises in the ear, buzzing. Sore pain in cartilage of left ear when pressing it, later in right ear. Pressing outward in ears. Buzzing in right ear with pressure extending to temples. Intermittent noise as of deep steam-whistle in left ear.

Nose - Nasal congestion, odor of sulphur vapor.

Face - Red, smooth eruption on right side of face. Dull pain in right upper jaw. Paralytic feeling in right cheek. Stinging pains in different parts of head and face.

Mouth - Bad taste in the mouth. Tongue dry, rough, sore. Teeth discolored, graygreen color.

Throat - Throat painful on swallowing. The pharynx has gray-green mucus, discomfort and cramping pain on swallowing. Sensation of narrowness in the throat. COMMENTS - Dr. John B. Campbell, one of Fincke’s original provers, discovered the great value of this remedy in rousing the reactive vitality of the system, both mentally and physically. In doing so, it brings suppressed symptoms to the surface in persons laboring under a combination of Hahnemann’s miasms. This is particularly helpful in deep-seated constitutional ailments, sycotic in character, which often terminate in malignant disease, especially cancer. Useful for conditions lacking presenting symptoms. When well selected anti-psoric remedies (Calc., Med., Psor., Sep., Sulph., Syph., or Tub.) fail to relieve completely. When well-indicated remedies fail with a history of exposure to radiation. Tends to bring out old suppressed eruptions or discharges (Sulph.). Non-specific chronic fatigue and weakness. Sores that fail to heal. Neuralgias after mastectomy. Extreme thirst and dryness of the mouth. X-ray burns, whether of the bone or skin. History of exposure to x-rays. Radiation sickness. Weakness after radiation treatments (Sol.). Dr. King developed an x-ray burn on his left hand. Eighteen months later, seedy warts appeared. Caust. finally helped, so he believed that Caust. may potentially be another antidote for x-rays. RELATIONS - Antidotes: Nux-v., Sulph. and the dynamic potencies of the remedy. Compare: (1) Cadm-s., Care. - Cancer patients, weak immune system. (2) Electr. - Sugar of milk saturated with the current. Anxiety, nervous tremors, restlessness, palpitation, headaches. Dreads approach of thunder-storms, heaviness of limbs. (3) Magn-ambo. Magn-arct. Magn-aust. (4) Merc. - Desire to hurt, even those dear to him, agitated, confused. Tongue covered with a yellowish coating and retaining the teeth imprints. (5) Phos. - Bleeding of bright red blood, frightened, hypersensitive, afraid of the dark an of storms. (6) Sec. - The limbs are cold with paresthesia, hemorrhaging of black blood, aggravated by the heat, ameliorated by the cold. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy-

Stomach - Nausea with a sick feeling. Nausea and vomiting with profuse sweat after immense stool. Sick feeling in stomach.

Rectum - Diarrhea, constipation and anal itching. Green stools.

Male - Lewd dreams. Sexual desire lost. Sterility. Re-establishes suppressed gonorrhea.

Female - Menses profuse or lacking. Menses dark green one day. Pain darting upward in region of left ovary. Flushes of heat, better afternoons and evenings. Food - Anorexia, aversion to food. Can eat plenty but does not enjoy it. Desire for sweets.

Chest - Thorax painful, palpitations. Contraction of chest at night relieved by belching. Sensation of drops of water trickling down on inside of chest.

Heart - Extra systole on coughing or crying. Pain in the precordial region. Noises from the heart prevent him from sleeping on the left side.

Back - Lame and stiff in back. Aching whole length of spine. Cramping pains in the back and lumbar region in the morning, on walking. Soreness in small of back.

Neck - Painful stiffness of the neck, on lifting the head from the pillow. Sudden “cricks” attack first one side of neck, then the other, worse on getting cold. Aching pains in left side of neck.

Limbs - Rheumatic pains. Trembling of the limbs. Generalized pains in the limbs, sciatic neuralgia. Sensation of electric current at the limbs. Lungs - Cough caused by palpitation, in evening. Cough in the morning with green sputum. Grayish expectoration.

Sleep - Sleepy with headache. Sleepy all the time with chronic fatigue. Sleepy, but unable to sleep for some hours after retiring.

Skin - Skin is discolored, pale, sclerous, cold. Skin dry, wrinkled. Hyperkeratosis of the skin. Warty growths. Radiation dermatitis. Chronic itching eruptions. Papular, vesicular, itching eruptions. Dry, itching eczema. Psoriasis. Palms rough and scaly. Erythema around roots of nails. Painful cracks. Nails thicken. Ingrown nails.

Modalities - Better from hot applications. Worse from cold, open air. Worse movement. Worse afternoon, evening and night, when in bed.

Kidneys - Oliguria, tenesmus of the bladder. Retained urine. Kidney colic with vomiting. Clutching pain from left kidney to bladder.

Blood - Decreased leucocytes and platelets. Leukemia. Hypochromic anemia. Hemorrhagic syndromes. Hematoma, tendency to hemorrhage, purpura. Breasts - Nerve pains after mastectomy.

Temperature - Chills as soon as beginning to sleep, running up back, preventing sleep. Chilly while undressing in warm room. Chilliness on moving or from draft. Perspires easily. Profuse perspiration on getting into bed, keeping him awake. Night sweats. Spells of fever, perspiration and weakness.

full:
PHARMACY - xan. Xanthoxylum fraxineum. Prickly ash. Xanthoxylum americanum. Toothache tree. N. O. Rutaceae. Tincture of fresh bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - After-pains. Amenorrhea. Aphonia. Asthma. Cholera. Coccyx, pain. Colic. Dyspepsia. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Earache. Fibroids. Flatulence. Headaches. Hemiplegia. Hoarseness. Hysteria. Injuries. Insomnia. Jaw joint, pain. Levitation. Menstruation, painful. Nausea. Nerves, injured. Nervousness. Neuralgia. Neurasthenia. Ophthalmia. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Toothache. Ulcers.

HERBAL - Xan. belongs to the Rutaceae and has a vulnerary action (Ruta.). Xan. contains Piperin. Rafinesque was the first to investigate Xan., which was known to him as “a great article in the Materia Medica of the Indians,” who use the root bark in decoction for “colics, gonorrhea, syphilis inward pains toothache, ulcers, etc. It is a great topical stimulant,” he continues, “changing the nature of malignant ulcers.” T. C. Duncan, recounting reminiscences of his boyhood, said, “There was another remedy that set my youthful mouth and stomach on fire and that was Prickly Ash. You wanted to open the mouth to let the cool air get in.” This warmth is felt as a warm glow through the entire system with a sensation in the nerves as if gentle shocks of electricity were passing through the body.

HOMEOPATHIC - Xan. exerts its influence on nerves, female sexual organs, respiration and left side. Its action is on the nervous system and mucus membranes. Injury to nerves. Neurasthenia. Pricking sensation, shocks as from electricity. Numbness of left side. Paralysis, of single parts. Hemiplegia. Insomnia. Occipital headache. Neuralgic and rheumatic disorders, especially in patients of spare habit and nervous, delicate organization. Increases mucus secretion of mouth and stimulates the secretion from all glands with ducts opening in the mouth. Poor assimilation, emaciation. Indigestion from over-eating or from too much fluid. Painful hemorrhages, after-pains, dysmenorrhea. Sluggish capillary circulation. Mucus membranes smart as from pepper. As if floor were soft like wool, on walking. Injury to nerves. Grinding, shooting, radiating, sudden pains, neuralgia. Many pains are radiating, some are sudden, arouse from sleep and cause the patient to catch her breath. Pains are excruciating, unbearable and are accompanied with red, hot face, but the heart pains causes pallor. MIND - Nervous, frightened feeling. Mental depression. Did not care if she lived or died. Abdomen - Some pain in right side below ribs. Griping pain on waking in morning. Colic pain in right iliac region. Rumbling with soreness on pressure. Flatulence.

Head - Feels full. Weight and pain on vertex. Pain over eyes, throbbing pressure over nose, pressure in forehead, head seems divided, ringing in ears. Occipital headache. Sick headache with dizziness and flatulence. Throbbing headache, pain as if top of head would fly off. As if head is divided into two parts. As of a tight band around.

Eyes - Watering of eyes and nose. Lachrymation, pain in lid of right eye. Eyes bloodshot with red margins and feel as if full of sand. Dull, heavy, grinding pain in left eye. Ophthalmia. Eyes twitched, pupils dilated. Vision blurred, as if looking through blue lace. Objects seem a long way off.

Ears - Ringing in ears. Loud noise in right ear, as of a valve constantly opening and shutting. Dull pain in right ear. Darting pain under and back or right ear.

Nose - Fluent coryza. Right nostril seems filled up, discharge of dry and bloody scales of mucus. Discharge of mucus from nose with congested feeling, as if it were about to bleed. Slight nose-bleed. Dryness of both nostrils. Numbness throughout left side of body, division felt in nose.

Face - Hot flushes over face and head. Face much flushed. Pallor even to lips with heart pains. Neuralgia of lower jaw. Pain in right jaw-socket.

Mouth - Peppery taste in mouth, fauces and throat. Burning and dry feeling in mouth and tongue. Ptyalism, tongue coated yellow. Tongue seemed to alternately expand and contract. Dryness of mouth and fauces. Pharyngitis (Wye.).

Throat - Aphonia. Hoarseness with husky feeling in throat, obliged to clear throat frequently. Throat dry, very difficult to talk. Peppery taste in mouth and throat. Feels hollow. Pain and soreness in right side of throat. Throat felt as if in a vice. COMMENTS - Xan. belongs to the Rutaceae and like Ruta, has a vulnerary action, as Clarke discovered in the case of Miss X., 28, who injured her right ulnar nerve at the elbow by repeatedly striking it against the edge of a bath while washing some articles. For two months she had to keep the arm in a sling. A few weeks after that the arm was swollen. Some eight months after the injury Clarke saw her. The pain centered in the ulnar nerve where it crosses the inner condyle of the humerus, though there was pain above and below as well. Clarke gave Ruta 30c, which gave some relief to the pain and relieved a frontal headache to which the patient was subject. The arm becoming less well, Clarke gave Xan. 12c four times a day. This made a distinct improvement in the arm and also relieved a dysmenorrhea to which Miss X. was subject. After treatment with various potencies of Xan. the nerve lost its sensitiveness and the patient could use her arm freely. In one of Cullis’ provers, Miss D. (there were six provers, three of them women, all took the tincture), the entire left half of the body became numb, the left half of the head being sharply divided in sensation from the other half. These symptoms with the many head pains and fullness in the head, give the correspondence in hemiplegia in which Xan. has been given with success. Two additional provings on women appear in C. D. P. In these provings 20 to 100 drop doses of the tincture were taken and symptoms of great severity were produced. Both provers had severe dysmenorrhea pains with increased and anticipating flow. The symptoms in each case roused the prover from sleep with pain and suffocation, the pain being confined to head, heart, throat and pelvis. Many of the pains were radiating from above right eye over head from right ovary down thigh and in other directions. Left-sided numbness was present in one, who also had symptoms of levitation and disordered sensation. Cullis, who had success in cases of dysmenorrhea and amenorrhea, related several cases, including that of Miss A., 25, brunette, who had menstrual irregularity since commencement, would go three, four or five months and then her sufferings were excruciating. When she came under treatment had no menses for two months. Xan. 1c was give, 5 drops thrice daily. Menses appeared in three days and were painless. Miss B., fair, nervous, had menses suppressed by getting feet wet, being then a weekovertime.Xan.lx,5 drops every three hours, brought on menses the next day. P. C. Majumdar cured a case of uterine fibroid with Xan. 3x. An emaciated, feeble, wrinkled woman, 56, widow, had been advised by allopaths to have an operation for tumor. Menstruation hadceasedfifteen years before. It had been profuse and painful and preceded and followed by leucorrhea. She had neuralgic pain in right ovarian region, a hard nodular tumor size of a small orange, painful on deep pressure. Fetid, yellowish white discharge from vagina. Nervous, depressed, lazy and sleepy even in daytime. Appetite poor, disgust for food. Xan. 3x was given night and morning. In a week the pain was better and discharge less. In four weeks Majumdar found the patient a changed person. The tumor was much softer and reduced by half. In six months the tumor had gone and the patient was quite well, Xan. having been taken intermittently all the time. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Gnaph., Cimic., Staph., Mez., Pise. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Dyspepsia from excessive eating and drinking. Feeling of fullness of pressure in epigastrium, fluttering. Intense burning and stinging in esophagus with slight nausea. Empty belchings with slight taste of ingesta. Nausea with headache, with sense of oppression at stomach.

Rectum - Constipation in morning. Griping and diarrhea. Dysentery with tympanites, tenesmus, inodorous discharges. Epidemic dysentery. Cholera collapse stage. Sensations - As if top of head would be taken off by flashes of throb-like pain. As if bewildered with pain in back of head. Feeling of looseness of brain. Eyes as if full of sand. As if walking on wool. As if sunk deep in bed. As if body expanded.

Female - Menses too early and painful. Menses thick, almost black. Leucor- rhea at time of menses. Leucorrhea with amenorrhea. Neuralgic dysmenorrhea with neuralgic headaches, pain in back and down legs. Ovarian neuralgia with pain in loins and lower abdomen, worse leftside, extending down the thigh, along genito-crural nerves. After pains (Arn., Cupr., Cham.). Food - Very thirsty, drank much at a time. Unusually hungry. No appetite. Anorexia.

Chest - Oppression of chest. Constitutions - Suited to women of spare habit, nervous temperament and delicate nerves. Neurasthenic patients who are thin, emaciated, poor assimilation with insomnia and occipital headache.

Back - Very severe pain in cervical and upper sacral region. Back of neck numb. Dull pain from nape to right scapula. Causations - Injury to nerves. Wetting (getting feet wet). Suppression of menses.

Limbs - Numbness of left side, impairment of motion. Paralysis of left side following spinal disorders. Hemiplegia. Left arm numb. Neuralgic shooting pain, as from electricity, all over limbs. Anterior neuralgia (Staph.). Sciatica, worse hot weather. Pain in nape, extending down back. Lungs - Shortness of breath. Constant desire to take a long breath, oppression of chest. Dry cough, day and night. Cough, slight hacking in spells, only in open air.

Sleep - Continued gaping, drowsiness. Hard and unrefreshing, dreams of flying. Sleeplessness in neurasthenics. A dream of suffocation woke her.

Skin - Measles, dullness, bewilderment, drowsiness and want of sufficient development of the eruption. Old, indolent ulcers.

Modalities - Better from drinking ice-water, vomiting. Better lying down. Headache is better by cold water and in open air. Neck pain is better by pressure and by throwing head back. Worse from sleeping, in morning, 4 a.m. Worse dampness, getting feet wet. Worse suppressed menses. Worse by moving head suddenly.

Kidneys - Urine at night and next morning scanty and high-colored. Profuse, lightcolored urine, nervous women.

Temperature - Slight chill accompanied by death-like nausea. Frequent chills with pains in limbs, nausea. Typhoid fever in stage of collapse. Sense of heat all over veins, flashes of heat from the head to foot.

HOMEOPATHIC - Xero. should prove curative in eczema conditions, poison oak and early typhoid states, etc. MIND - Dull, cannot concentrate. Forgets names. Dyslexia. Writes last letters of words first. Misspells common words. Bewildered. Loss of consciousness.

Head - Feels full, stuffed up, pain across forehead and above eyes. Great pressure at root of nose. Pulsating headache.

Eyes - Painful, as if sand, smarting, Hard to focus for close work. Eyes sore, burn.

Nose - Stuffed, tightness at bridge of nose, acute nasal catarrh.

Face - Bloated, morning. Puffy eyes.

Throat - Stitching pain upon swallowing. RELATIONS - Compare: Rhus-t., Anae. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Feels full and heavy. Belchings sour offensive, an hour after luncheons and dinner. Vomiting at 2 p.m.

Abdomen - Intestinal flatulence. In morning, rumbling with desire for stool.

Rectum - Constipation, stools hard, small lumps. Difficult, soft stools with much straining. Much flatus. Bearing- down pain in rectum.

Female - Bearing-down sensation. Vulva inflamed with furious itching. Increased sexual desire with ovarian and uterine pains and leucorrhea.

Back - Feels hot from sacrum to scapulae. Heat deep in spine. Backache, extending down legs. Pain over kidneys.

Limbs - Limbs feel stiff (Rhus-t.). Muscular lameness, trembling. Inguinal glands and behind knees swollen. Pain in knees. Lungs - Posterior sinuses raw, discharge thick, yellow mucus. Sneezing. Trachea sore, lumps feel constricted.

Skin - Skin rough and cracked, feels like leather. Dermatitis, especially around knees. Inflammation resembling poison oak. Erythema with vesication and intense itching, stinging and burning. Blisters, little lumps.

Modalities - Better application of hot water. Better in morning. Better moving affected part. Worseapplication of cold water. Worse in afternoon and evening.

Kidneys - Difficulty retaining urine, dribbling when walking. Frequent urination.

CLINICAL - Abscess. Adenitis. Buboes. Colitis. Crohn’s disease. Encephalitis. Erythema. Gastroenteritis. Influenza. Ileitis. Meningitis. Parkinson’s disease. Plague. Septicemia.

HOMEOPATHIC - According to Fortier-Ber- noville, it is Barishac who proposed Yersin for the treatment of grave or a typical forms of influenza. Severe form of influenza of pulmonary type with hyperthemia, respiratory troubles, soft thick, rosy expectorations, presence of sub-crepitant rales in the base of lungs. Mesenteric adenitis. Acute entero-colitis, gastro-enteritis with lesion of ilium. Acute enteritis of young children. Crohn’s regional ileitis. Influenza of gastro-intestinal form. Pseudo-typho meningitis of milkmen. Meningitis syndromes of influenzal origin. Encephalitis lethargica. Parkinson’s disease. Severe toxic, infectious states, either cutaneous (bubo) or pulmonary. Septicemias accompanied with icterus and hepatic abscess. Acute toxicosis of babies. Lymphoid terminal ileitis of Arnulf and Buffart. Nodulous erythema. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Tub-a., Bapt., Pyrog. (2) Mimosa Púdica - thoracic pain, dry cough, irritation of naso-pharyngeal and laryngeal mucus, frequent irritating stools with colic, better by not bath. (3) Amorpho- phallus Ri vieri - general ill feeling with great weakness, gastro-intestinal troubles with weakening diarrhea, fetid stools. REFERENCES - Clarke. Julian.

full:
PHARMACY - yohim.Yohimbinumcoryanthe. Yohimbe bark. N. O. Rubiaceae. A crystalline alkaloid obtained from the bark of the Y ohim- beha or Yumbehoa tree of the Cameroons. Trituration. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aphrodisiac. Diuresis. Hyperemia. Impotence. Menorrhagia. Neurasthenia. Palpitations. Priapism. Urethritis. Sexual, neurasthenia.

HERBAL - The natives of West Africa discovered a potent aphrodisiac in the bark of the Yohimbeha tree, and from this an active principle. It is a powerful stimulant of the genital function in males. Excites the sexual organs and acts on the central nervous system and respiratory center. An aphrodisiac, used in physiological doses, but contraindicated in all acute and chronic inflammations of abdominal organs.

HOMEOPATHIC - Useful for priapism and congestive states of the sexual organs. Menorrhagia. Hyperemia of the milk glands, stimulates breast-feeding. In animals Yohim. causes increased liveliness and cheerfulness, hyperemia of the conjunctiva, heat and redness of the ears and of the nose also in dogs. MIND - Intense agitation with trembling.

Head - Agitation with flying sensations of heat in face.

Face - Sensations of heat, heightening the color. Food - Appetite almost completely disappeared.

Mouth - Disagreeable, metallic taste. Copious salivation. Tongue covered with a yellow coat.

Stomach - Nausea and eructation.

Abdomen - Flying heat sensations in abdomen.

Rectum - Intestinal hemorrhage. Bleeding hemorrhoids. Stools frequent, liquid, black and bilious.

Male - Sexual neurasthenia with impotence. Priapism. Strong and lasting erections in the morning without increase of desire. Enlargement of testicles and epididymis.

Heart - Heart beats more intense and more frequent, pulse, normally 80, became 108. Flying sensation of heat in heart.

Back - Flying heat sensations in back.

Limbs - Hands trembled, could scarcely write, writing was illegible.

Sleep - No sleep all night. Sleeplessness. Thoughts of events of whole past life keep him awake.

Kidneys - Urine clean abundant, foamy, no trace of albumen, had to rise three times in the night. Urethritis.

Temperature - Rigor intense heat, waves of heat and chilliness, tendency to sweat. COMMENTS - Lambreghts related the case of a young man, 28, “thin, anemic, nervous and partially impotent,” who took a 5 mg. tablet one morning, another in the evening and a third the following morning. The symptoms were so severe that he discontinued the herb in spite of a certain amelioration of the sexual neurasthenia. Yohim. set up symptoms of fever, disordered the digestion, caused agitation and tremors and increased the action of the heart. Eulenburg used Yohim. in 10 drop doses of a 1 percent solution and “in cases of neurasthenic impotence with excellent result.” RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Erections - Canth., Pic-ac., Phos., Graph., Canth. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Fear of heights, ladders. Fear of narrow spaces. Dreams of heights, falling, ladders. Dreams of mountains, volcano, water. REFERENCES - Scholten.

full:
PHARMACY - yuc. Yucca filamentosa. Bear grass. Agavaceae. N. O. Melanthacae, Lili- aceae. Tincture of root and leaves when not in flower. Tincture of flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Biliousness. Coryza. Diarrhea. Flatulence. Headache, temporal. Post-nasal catarrh. Throat, granular.

HOMEOPATHIC - Yuc. was proved by Rowell and four others in the 30c. Farrington gave these Yuc. indications: biliousness with pain going through upperpart of liver to back. Diarrhea which contains an excess of bile. Much flatus passed by rectum. Frequent passage of flatus and of watery, yellowish-brown stools. Dull ache in center of liver. Abdomen sensitive. As with many liver disorders, there is chilliness, cannot bear to be away from the fire. Face sallow. Bilious symptoms with headache. Frontal or temporal headache with frequent flushing of face. Bad taste in mouth. Tongue coated yellow and taking imprint of teeth. The tongue is usually a bluish white. MIND - Despondent and irritable. Irresolute. Disinclined to study. Mind wanders, uses wrong words. Unable to remember anything read. When others talking to him, hears but doesn't seem to understand.

Head - Headaches frontal, heavy, pressing, throbbing. Headaches as if top of head would fly off. Temporal arteries throb. Sensation of cold air blowing on left side of scalp.

Eyes - Dark rings under eyes. Eyes feel hot and inflamed. Itching and smarting left eye, left inner canthus. Dull pain over left eye.

Ears - Pain behind right ear, 6:30 p.m. Very sensitive to least noise.

Nose - Nose red. In evening, right side of nose constantly running, left dry. Profuse, bloody, watery discharge. Coryza. Sensation as if something hung down from posterior sinuses, cannot get it up or down.

Face - Pale, flushed, burning, yellow. Momentary aching in zygoma, recurring several times. Pain in jaw joints. Food - Appetite increased, food relished, lost.

Mouth - Bad odor from mouth. Taste as of rotteneggs(Arn.). Back of mouth dry. Yellow tongue yellow, coated, taking imprint of teeth (Merc., Podo., Rhus-t.).

Throat - Tonsils dark red, not sore. Pharynx seems covered with granules is dark red. Stringy, greasy-looking mucus back of throat. Sensation as if something hanging down from posterior sinuses. RELATIONS-Antidoted by: Cocc. Compare: ( 1 ) Constriction in heart, Lil-t. (2) Biliousness, Bry. (3) Tongue imprinted with teeth, Merc., Podo. (4) Blue tongue, Gymn. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Aching and sharp pains in stomach. Region of stomach sore and sensitive.

Abdomen - Deep pain in right side over liver, going through back. Abdomen bloated after dinner and feels sore. Rumbling. Colic. Crampy pains in abdomen after breakfast. Throbbing, painless, right side about twelfth rib. Much flatus emitted, odorless.

Rectum - Constant desire for stool. Sudden, violent tenesmus, followed by discharge of wind, which relieves the pain. Diarrhea following pains in abdomen. Stools are watery, copious, thin, yellowish brown with smarting at anus. Stool yellowish brown with bile. Tenesmus after stool. Sensations - As of something hanging down from back of sinuses. As if cold air blowing on left side of scalp.

Male - Burning and swelling of the prepuce with redness of meatus. Gonorrhea (Cann-s.). Erections, all night long but no emissions, cannot study, mind runs on sexual subjects.

Chest - Constriction in whole chest and in heart. Pain in upper intercostal muscles.

Heart - Constriction in heart. Momentary aching in heart region. Visible throbbing in arteries of hand. Pulse full and heavy, a little irregular.

Back - Constriction of neck muscles, seems to draw head backward. Tight feeling around neck, evening, had to take off collar. Severe pain in left scapula, at 9 p.m. Backache.

Limbs - Crampy pains in knees. Sore, crampy pains in muscle of back of left leg, just above ankle, as if sprained. Lungs - Hard, rattling cough.

Sleep - Very sleepy in the evening. Restless night. Lewd dreams.

Skin - Erythematous redness.

Modalities - Griping pain is better bending forward. Worse by noise. Worse motion, pressure.

Kidneys - Circumscribed edematous red swelling, raw sensation around meatus. Irritable bladder, frequent urination. Burning when urinating. Urine increased, high specific gravity.

Temperature - Coldness of scalp, left side, as if cold air blowing on it. Coldness, cannot bear to be away from fire. Restless and feverish. Hot, feverish. Face sweats, evening.

HOMEOPATHIC - Zinc-ar. affects the lumbar region and lower limbs. Chorea. Numbness, right arm then left, better when writing. Lumbar pain, worse from exertion, sitting, jarring or standing. Occipital pain. Blue vision. Burning in bladder. Anemia. Neurasthenia. Weakness, enervation, exhaustion, prostration, infirmity. Profound exhaustion on slightexertion. Slight exertion aggravates. Soles ache when tired, better pressure. Worse exertion, ascending stairs. Weakness, in acute diseases. Weakness and infirmity from nursing the sick. Ailments from night watching. Desires to walk. Worse from 10 a.m. and 3 p.m. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Modalities - Toothache is worse by touch. Worse in evening. Worse by motion, ZINCUM ARSENICOSUM

HOMEOPATHIC - Hale used Zinc-br. on its double indications for teething children who suffer intensely from pain in nerves of head and face. Pains which throw the children into a state of stupor alternating with wakefulness. Hale used the 3c and 6c potencies. REFERENCES Clarke.

PHARMACY - zinc-chr. Zincum chromatum. Zinc chromate. Chrome. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

HOMEOPATHIC - Zinc-chr. acts upon the ears, nose, throat and left side. Aching, gnawing, grinding, pain or wandering in shocks. Catching stitches that impede motion. MIND - Aversion to work.

Head - Inward pressure in spot on bregma. Throbbing temples.

Eyes - Vision wavering.

Ears - Throbbing behind the ears.

Nose - Bad odor within nose. Blowing of pus and blood and scabs.

Mouth - Metallic taste in mouth.

Throat - Shooting pain from larynx (left side) up through tonsils into ear. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Abdomen - Cannot tolerate her hands on abdomen.

Female - Dryness of vagina with sense of a coming sickness, 10 to 12 a.m. Food - Indefinite craving, knows not for what. Aversion to even thinking of food.

Heart - Cutting at apex, at night.

Back - Gnawing and grinding below and above left scapula.

Limbs - Feet sore. Cramps of gnawing, grinding pain in toes, at night. Lungs - Cough from tickling in throat-pit. Expectoration, sweet, loose, but had to be swallowed or tough with constant spitting spells.

Modalities - Worse from motion. Worse lying on the back. Worse washing the head.

Head - Congestion to head.

Face - Face suddenly changes color.

Rectum - Constipation. REFERENCES - Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - Zinc-i. has been proved by American pro vers, producing some well- defined symptoms, including splinter-like pain in throat. A cough from tickling in the throat and the more he coughed the worse the tickling became. A peculiar tingling in right side of face to vertex with tension in skin of the part. Undulating pain at border of right free ribs, extending to third rib on same side. Coldness in stomach and bowels with tendency to perspire. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Splinter pain in throat, Hep., Arg-n. (2) The more he coughs the worse it tickles, Ign. REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Zincum Metallicum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better while eating. Betterfree discharges and appearance of eruptions, menses. Better rubbing, scratching. Better motion, hard pressure. Better warm, open air. Worse from exhaustion, mental or physical. Worse after eating, after wine. Worse sweet things, milk. Worse from noise. Worse suppressed eruptions or discharges, menses. Worse between 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. Worse being heated, touching anything cold, being touched. Worse approach of storms which causes chills..
